title: improve: speed up large-buffer test assertions
body:
Related: #188777, #188823

## What Problem This Solves

RFB, borrowed-file-descriptor, and avatar-cache tests spend seconds recursively comparing large byte arrays.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. These focused tests run faster with complete-byte integrity and every existing lifecycle assertion retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native `Buffer.equals` with failure labels at seven comparison sites. The avatar expectation uses an identically sized Buffer, which remains a Uint8Array, and native equality rejects missing or non-byte-array results. No new helper or production change.

## Evidence

Three successful serial before and three after runs **per file**, against frozen base `e279b64ffe86578edff6c72cd39f98893a0e5ff2`, with the same host, private frozen dependencies, runtime, task temp roots, and caches:

| File | Median wall before → after | Gain | Median Vitest before → after | Median case-body sum before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `rfb-probe.test.ts` | 29.83 → 4.33 s | 85.5% | 26.73 → 1.360 s | 24.620 → 0.766 s |
| `file-descriptor.test.ts` | 9.86 → 2.18 s | 77.9% | 8.36 → 0.672 s | 7.746 → 0.053 s |
| `user-profiles.avatar-cache.test.ts` | 16.64 → 9.05 s | 45.6% | 14.49 → 6.830 s | 9.667 → 2.246 s |

Every after wall time is below every before wall time for its file; no file was dropped. All runs passed the original 18/8/5 cases. Cold setup is retained, including the first avatar baseline's 36.6-second worker preparation and the first RFB baseline's runtime staging. Case-body and CPU reductions support the matcher mechanism; wall time also includes runner/cache noise.

- **Mutation proof:** flipping the last observed byte at each conversion failed the intended assertion, including both avatar rows; a separate RFB truncation control also failed. Eight full-file mutation runs produced exactly eleven intended failing case executions. Real sockets/files/SQLite reads still ran; no mutation mocked the asserted behavior. All mutations were restored byte-for-byte before final proof.
- **Retained behavior:** the 8 MiB native write/backpressure, both queued callbacks, peer FIN, paused-reader terminal response, final tail, abort sibling and cleanup; independent expected descriptor SHA/size, onChunk digest, source and seeded target cursors, source exhaustion, borrowed ownership and all six mutation/platform rows; 33 persisted 512 KiB avatars per row, the 16 MiB cache pressure, current-reader checks, warm zero-read accesses, cold one-read reload, deferred promise identity, and lifecycle cleanup. No behavior, case, row, timeout or repetition was deleted/reduced.
- **Causal work count:** the same ten complete comparisons remain: one 8,388,626-byte RFB value; descriptor windows of 1,048,578 / 1,048,580 / 1,048,576 bytes; six 524,288-byte avatar values. These seven sites compare the same 14,680,088 bytes without Vitest's recursive byte-property matching. Native I/O and cache-pressure work remain.
- **Final focused proof:** 71/71 tests across the three targets plus `src/gateway/desktop/rfb-preauth.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-database-backup-engine.test.ts`, and `src/state/user-profiles.avatar-worker.test.ts` passed after restoration. Scoped native typecheck, type-aware lint, format, diff, conflict, line-cap/max-lines, assertion-safety, test-LF, timeout-race and mock-export ratchets passed.
- **Exact budget:** test LF **537 → 537**, production LF delta **0**. The native tracked test census remains **6,314,647**; scalar **6,320,000** plus **194 unchanged grants totaling 26,651** gives ceiling **6,346,651**. Effective-cap delta = actual-LF delta = **0**; inherited slack remains **32,004**. No scalar/grant edits. Manifests, lockfile, installed-module metadata and pinned runtime metadata hashes remained unchanged.
- **Simplify:** eight lines replaced by eight lines, entirely in the existing tests; no new helper, fixture owner, production seam or configuration.
- **Independent review:** isolated Codex P0–P2 autoreview of the complete local candidate against the frozen base, with intact targets/owners/helpers (195,863 prompt bytes). Machine status `scoped-clean`, `report_produced: true`, exit 0, no findings; one pass. Committed head `8b25cd2f75581f97d88bc0ece1c8e58c71667531` is byte-identical to the reviewed candidate. The empty reviewer sandbox did not rerun tests.
- **Overlap:** exact-path and basename open-PR searches before work returned no hits. Prior-mechanism PR file lists were read and do not overlap these targets. The six exact-path/basename searches were repeated immediately before publication, again with no hits.
- No failed normal benchmark runs, discarded trials, retries or observed flakes. The metric parser initially assumed seconds and was corrected for Vitest's millisecond duration output using the same raw logs; the original parser and all measurements/mutation logs are retained.
- Discovery's historical CI file case-duration sums were 24.263 / 9.542 / 10.290 seconds respectively; these are not wall times or candidate CI measurements. Fresh exact-head PR CI is the broad gate. No broad local suite or SDK build was run, and no live Gateway or Team state was changed. Parent source review and native landing are complete.

<details>

`timeout 900 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test <target> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`

title: feat(automations): preview impact before changing default models
body:
Related: #188761

## What Problem This Solves

Changing a default model can leave existing automations blocked by model policy or account/runtime compatibility, with no warning at the point of change.

## User Impact

Models and Agents settings show automation impact before changing the primary model, and ask for confirmation when enabled jobs have blockers or unknown compatibility. CLI and agent callers can inspect the same read-only result. Existing overrides, account ownership, permissions, schedules, and expired work are not changed.

This is an advisory metadata preview—not proof that inference, fallback attempts, tools, or delivery will succeed. Missing personal/native observations remain unknown. CLI models set preserves offline save behavior when assessment is unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

One cron-owned assessment reuses scheduled model selection, account-route availability, and runtime checks. The UI, CLI and automation tool share it instead of maintaining separate compatibility rules. This is the agreed preview-and-guidance first stage; bulk editing automation overrides remains deferred. No migration or new configuration option is required.

A recorded account constrains only its own provider. An inherited default moving to another provider selects credentials/runtime live, so preview reports that case as **unknown**, not incompatible. Model policy still applies.

## Evidence

### Current landing candidate

Head **80cc97b6aefe91c5fe5de26e8e5846c69b97eaf8**, rebased onto main **197872027df6c2fbc56f0318e305b6008429b5ad** on November 14 after confirmed conflicts. Only generated validator/prompt artifacts conflicted; canonical regeneration resolved them. No feature behavior, tests, dependencies or limits were changed. Main’s utility-model controls, read-only GitHub identity view and OAuth status owners were preserved.

- **Fresh affected proof:** 153 core/domain/catalog/CLI/Gateway/prefix tests across 10 files pass (206.34s). Core and Cron test types, scoped lint/format, validators, six prompt snapshots, protocol registry/native determinism/introduction-train, line-cap and exact test allocation checks pass.
- **Fresh UI proof:** 231 owner/consumer tests across 17 files pass, as do 4 impact/recovery browser tests and 2 real-Gateway tests. All three relevant UI type leaves pass. Fresh current-source runtime and production UI builds were used. Cancel preserves config/jobs; acceptance changes only the default. The wire sequence is cron.modelImpact, cron.modelImpact, config.patch. Scheduler disabled; no live inference.
- **Review reuse:** the November 12 complete three-pass P0–P2 local autoreview found no actionable findings against base 1ca34955022cadc5900793cebeab6c89a2a652ba, with complete coverage and final source verification. It covers the unchanged authored feature delta. This is a mechanical rebase, not a new behavior revision; overlapping main integrations were separately inspected and tested. No new hosted-review verdict is claimed.
- **Test cost:** +1,490 literal test LF lines; the current 400-line allowance plus a 1,090-line feature allocation covers the exact growth. Coverage protects distinct selection/account, private-session visibility, transport, cancellation and config-only acceptance boundaries. No shared limit or unrelated debt adjustment.

### Current CI qualification — not merge-ready

[Run 43620176288, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176288) completed on the exact candidate: 82 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs, four failing root jobs and the failed aggregate gate. Security-fast and the observed security reviews passed. The current-head control-ui-performance check passed; the earlier local build’s eight budget warnings are not being presented as a failing hosted performance gate.

Three root failures reproduce identically on untouched main197872, with the relevant failed source inputs unchanged through CI base989f4a6d1e4096461fc6c4fbae993f56f3b02a6e and tested merge70be73c291ba56aef59d48e96b91f7fb997bfb2a:

- [Baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176288/job/132524321376): mock-exports rejects the worker diagnostics mock of worker-request-delivery-report.runtime.js. Clean-base replay fails identically (10.79s).
- [Node small-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176288/job/132524322828): the wrapper closure test misses worker-request-delivery-report.runtime.ts. Clean-base replay fails identically (25.38s). Both worker defects enter through main #199034.
- [UI1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176288/job/132524322062): the 390px new-session model-picker gap is 46px against a 32px bound. A fresh clean-base production-UI replay reproduces exactly; the 1440px case passes (16.05s).

**Unresolved required failure:** [UI4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176288/job/132524321831) exhausted its 20-minute action budget. All 152 completed modules passed, but the splash suite and three later suites were incomplete. The final active splash case had only just started; its presence in the timeout artifact does not establish a defect in that case. Focused splash replay passes 19/19 on both clean base and candidate. All 156 selected test files are unchanged, but adding this PR’s automation suite changes 21 UI4 shard members, so an effect from test redistribution has not been excluded. Two scheduled-main UI4 runs passed. Shared runner load is a hypothesis, not established attribution. **This timeout does not yet qualify for the inherited-only landing exception.** No CI limit, baseline, ignore rule, retry or gate bypass was used to obtain green.

The optional [shared OpenClawKit dead-code check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620176193/job/132530524874) also reports OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError as unused. The relevant native sources and scanner are unchanged by this PR; no native repair is bundled here.

No upstream credential-acceptance, live scheduled execution or WebKit proof is claimed for the feature.

<details><summary>Prior qualification retained for unchanged inputs</summary>

The November 12 head 3a8fdc135e9c9a2041b03f7f8c6da79199d36a3b had 193 CLI/tool/Gateway/prefix tests, 16 domain/runtime tests, 26 catalog tests, 137 UI-owner tests, 4 mocked-browser tests, 2 real-Gateway tests and 10 models-set E2E tests passing. Models-set used ordinary current-source runtime preparation, without skip-build or stale-dist reuse (230.79s). The earlier preparation attempt was interrupted by a Gateway restart before tests; its resumed supported run completed successfully.

Two temporary negative controls failed through the real preview boundary: restoring the old provider blocker, and dropping the provider argument that preserves a recorded runtime on its own provider. Both controls were restored byte-for-byte; the final domain suite passed. Synthetic loopback transport is not upstream-provider proof.

The five prior bot-authored commits, including two merge-resolution repairs, were consolidated with an exact tree-equality check before the November 12 rebase. Human attribution was retained. The old missing deep-research client preparation blocker is gone on these bases.

The previous run43309903161 failed three UI shards. Main now includes #198016’s account-menu animation repair, #198341’s fresh-visit setup change and #165504’s sharding mitigation. title: fix: cancelled workspace binding waits for unrelated session writes
body:
Closes #188771

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cancelled workspace preparation remaining stuck at final binding when an unrelated session write holds the database queue.

## User Impact

Cancelled binding can reject without waiting for the unrelated writer. Writes that have already entered still settle before their owner releases custody. No schema, permission, durability, or configuration changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the preparation source's cancellation signal alongside its source assertion into final binding, then use the existing shared-store reservation and canonical writer FIFO to remove only waiting work. Final authority checks, source-assertion metadata, and durable ownership reconciliation before rollback remain intact; this does not race the entire commit or release source custody early.

Simplification retained the existing queue owners rather than adding cancellation state or a new writer. Against the pinned base, production grows by 16 lines and the two test files by exactly 181 lines. The separate 181-line allocation is necessary to cover the distinct canonical/shared-store waiting paths and the opposite contract—an entered write must finish and persist its result. The shared budget scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reused exact-patch proof from the original implementation/verification session at base `ac3fdf3662b67da941c12289a9423b75003b1000`. All eight supplied implementation/test blob hashes match in this draft candidate.
- The real registered-project/source-custody/native-admission regression reproduced on reported revision `899e74744d88f39ea864d969d9bf204e9c18b9e4` and the pinned base. Both final canonical/shared-store regressions were red on the original production source and green with this patch.
- Complete `server.worktree-preparation.test.ts`: 7/7 passed, 39.83 s wrapper wall time; new cases 3.128 s and 3.097 s. Four affected sibling files: 36 tests passed in 61.21 s wrapper wall time, including entered-write settlement and persisted-value verification.
- Production core, Gateway-server test leaf, and config-cli test leaf typechecks passed. Six production files and both changed tests passed lint before the final timeout-signature correction; Gateway-server typecheck and the full 7-case suite passed after that correction. Final corrected-signature lint/format have not been rerun here.
- Fresh bound Auto Review of the complete nine-file candidate against the pinned base, with intact production-owner context: no actionable findings at the helper's default **P0-only** threshold. This is source review, not broader-priority or executed-test proof. The earlier patch-only review's missing-context limitation was addressed by the context-complete pass.
- `git diff --check` and staged diff check passed. Prior runtime proof used Debian 12 x64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15, and Vitest 5.0.5. This preparation sandbox had Node 24.20.0 and no dependency installation; unchanged runtime tests were not rerun there.

**Draft / outstanding gates:** No full-suite, CI, isolated live Gateway/model flow, PostgreSQL, or lease-expiry qualification is claimed. Full format/lint of the final signature, unused-file proof, and the executable test-line ratchet remain unrun in this preparation workspace. CI timing is not yet available. This PR is intentionally draft; ready-for-review and merge are not requested.

Use the existing auth JSON-to-SQLite migration owner to admit the real synthetic API-key and OAuth profiles. Require both complete warning messages, including the selected billing routes and profiles, so missing credentials cannot produce a false pass. Keep the unique Decision-selector case.

title: fix(feishu): recover transient sends without duplicate messages
body:
Supersedes #104322, thanks @litang9.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Feishu messages when a create or reply request encounters a transient network or server failure, including a lost response after acceptance.

## User Impact

Text, cards, and uploaded-media messages recover with up to two retries using the same UUID, preventing duplicate posts within Feishu’s deduplication window. Uploads and CardKit entity creation retain their existing transient-failure behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Message create/reply now share one request assembler that supplies a UUID before the first attempt. The existing Feishu request owner delegates scheduling and canonical network classification to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/retry-runtime`; transient recovery is opt-in only for these UUID-bearing requests. Existing rate-limit handling, sender authority on every attempt, durable dispatch accounting, withdrawn-reply fallback, and streaming without a message receipt remain covered.

The shared outbound delivery queue does not provide this per-request recovery: ambiguous sends require reconciliation before replay. The repair belongs at the UUID-bearing Feishu HTTP request boundary.

Production LOC: **net -2**. Consolidating duplicate create/reply assembly in ordinary and streaming sends and combining fulfilled/rejected business-error classification offsets the new behavior. Tests: **net +125**, allocated specifically for transport loss, cancellation, upload non-replay and retry policy. Documentation: +4 lines.

## Evidence

- Baseline `70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643`: four new registered-adapter/real-Lark-SDK loopback regressions failed on `ECONNRESET` after fixture acceptance (direct text, thread reply, card, uploaded media). The source owners remain unchanged on the newer main inspected before publication.
- Fixed: **120 tests across six focused files passed** using the repository wrapper with one worker. The final transport suite passed 29 tests, including stable serialized UUID/content over two HTTP attempts with exactly one fixture acceptance, per-attempt dispatch accounting, sender retirement preventing a second POST, and one failed upload followed by the existing link fallback. Retry policy covers HTTP 408/425/5xx, fulfilled/rejected 230049, canonical transport codes and permanent failures. Streaming still updates/closes after recovery without a message receipt.
- Local wall time: first consumer batch (five files, 91 tests) 21.09 s; final retry/transport batch (two files, 46 tests) 57.09 s, including 35.66 s of runtime-worker preparation. The transport test execution was about 8 s; real SDK HTTP and durable delivery settlement require this boundary. The exact-head [extension CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146098127/job/124371966446) passed: test step **240 s**, whole job **329 s**. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146098127) completed successfully.
- Feishu production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, assertion safety, mock-export ratchet, exact test-line allocation, documentation link audit (0 broken links), and `git diff --check`: passed. Initial typecheck setup lacked generated SDK declarations; after preparation, the final check passed.
- `pr-simplify`: completed; one message request owner replaces the duplicate assembly paths.
- Final local **autoreview**, base `70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643`, complete local candidate, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings. Review ran independently and did not execute project code.
- Dependency inspected: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.76.0` accepts `data.uuid` for both create and reply and performs one POST per invocation. Official [create](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/CreateMessageReqBody.Builder.html) and [reply](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/ReplyMessageReqBody.Builder.html) contracts document at most one successful send per UUID within one hour.
- Proof limit: loopback simulates provider acceptance/deduplication; no new authenticated Feishu delivery was run. The original PR contains separately dated live-provider evidence. Contributor code was read only with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`; it was never checked out, installed, built or executed here.

Contributor credit is preserved for both commit-author identities from #104322: litang9 and Alex Tang.

title: fix(anthropic): preserve global exec restrictions in partial agent overrides
body:
Supersedes #124275, thanks @Yigtwxx

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a latent policy-inheritance defect where the Claude CLI callback silently requests an implicit native-tool permission bypass when a partial agent exec block discards restrictive global settings.

## User Impact

This is defense in depth. **Current launchers already strip or replace the implicit bypass**, including non-live plugin execution, manual compaction, exact-tool/side-question execution, and node execution. There is no user-visible change to those launchers and no migration or new approval gate.

The documented callback cases do change: global `mode: "deny"` or `security: "deny"` plus an empty/ask-only agent block no longer yields `bypassPermissions`; a security-only agent block also retains a global `ask: "always"`. Explicit agent modes and explicitly configured Claude permission arguments retain precedence. Any future route that trusts the callback therefore inherits the configured global restrictions instead of permissive defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing exec-policy owner to layer defaults, global settings, then agent settings. A supplied mode determines both policy fields; supplied legacy fields clear an inherited mode and replace only those fields. Missing fields inherit. Explicitly configured overrides remain intentional overrides; this does not impose a new maximum-restriction policy.

The production delta is **+1 line**: the SDK export of the existing helper. The adapter is line-neutral because it removes its duplicate policy reconstruction and reuses that helper. There is no additional dead production code in this owner to delete safely. Other SDK exports and implementations are unchanged. Existing policy-helper tests now exercise the SDK export directly.

### Before/after configuration matrix

`D` = default `security: full, ask: off`; `G` = normalized global policy; `A` = a complete agent security/ask pair or explicit agent mode; `P` = a partial agent block (including empty/non-policy blocks). `N(P,D)` fills missing fields from defaults. `Layer(G,P)` normalizes modes first and preserves unspecified fields from G. `bypassPermissions` is derived only when the final mode is `full`, subject to the existing explicit-argument/compaction checks and later launcher filtering.

| Global exec policy | Agent exec policy | Callback before | Callback after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unset | Unset | D | D |
| Unset | Partial P | N(P,D) | N(P,D) |
| Unset | Full A | A | A |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Unset | G | G |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Partial P | N(P,D) | Layer(G,P), inheriting omitted fields from G |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Full A | A | A |
| Restrictive | Unset | G | G |
| Restrictive | Partial P | N(P,D), potentially dropping restrictions | Layer(G,P), retaining unspecified restrictions |
| Restrictive | Full A | A | A |

For `full/off`, Layer(G,P) equals N(P,D). A legacy `full/on-miss` policy instead retains `on-miss` when omitted; the callback still projects mode `full` unless an explicit agent field changes that projection.

Examples of the changed row:

| Global | Agent | Before callback policy / implicit bypass | After callback policy / implicit bypass |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode: deny` | `{}` or `ask: off` | full/off / yes | deny/off / no |
| `security: deny, ask: off` | `host: gateway` or `ask: off` | full/off / yes | deny/off / no |
| `security: full, ask: always` | `security: full` | full/off / yes | full/always / no |
| `mode: ask` | `ask: off` | full/off / yes | allowlist/off / no |
| `mode: deny` | `mode: full` | full/off / yes | full/off / yes |

## Evidence

- Base: `a1d1da77f8e80c2c4ace3445d507597201fd2f78`; candidate: `6408000f6ad7f19e9b3c5641d6bb42dae7093259`.
- Red before: fresh/resumed callback regressions fail for six inheritance combinations on main; 30 other tests pass. Green after: all 32 Claude shared tests and both SDK policy tests pass.
- Claude shared file: 2.51 seconds including transform/import/setup; the complete two-shard focused command took 175.41 seconds with a cold compiled-worker rebuild. The matrix replaces an existing table; its net 35 test lines have a separate allocation record protecting global inheritance and explicit overrides.
- Format and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final-head security autoreview: Codex, P0/P1, scoped-clean, no actionable findings, with unchanged policy owner and launcher/consumer source supplied. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Capped rootless Podman (4 CPUs / 8 GiB): all 578 tests across 13 consumer files pass (232.82 seconds), including approval readers/policy, prompt-prefix stability, Codex config/side-question/conversation/MCP App consumers, Muse, Policy, and Anthropic sibling mappings.
- Full build passes (4 minutes 15.2 seconds), including SDK declarations and export verification. Production extension, extension-test, and core typechecks pass.
- Type-aware lint passes on the two Anthropic files (8.26 seconds) and both core/SDK files (5.35 seconds). SDK export registration check passes.
- Existing SDK-helper file: 169.06 seconds with 99% in cold transform/setup; assertions are synchronous and do not add a process or server fixture. Required PR CI passed on this exact published head: [CI run 41145533104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41145533104). The compact check job took 303 seconds; extension bundle jobs 2 and 3 took 374 and 333 seconds. These are whole-job CI times including other files; per-file CI timing was not available from the retrieved logs.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the maintainer fallback used completed autoreview plus one hosted ClawSweeper request. The hosted review was still in progress at merge and remains advisory.
- No authenticated Claude/model execution is claimed. Prior investigation verified actual process argv with a synthetic Claude executable; the current change targets the callback contract. Contributor code was read only, never checked out or executed.

title: fix: keep Windows managed updates alive when the task stops
body:
Related: #169844

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Scheduled Task updates can kill their own helper when stopping the Gateway, leaving the Control UI at **Activating**, no terminal result, and the task disabled.

## User Impact

This draft keeps the managed update helper alive through the task stop while retaining cleanup of ordinary Gateway children. **Blocked on merging and releasing [proc-safe#31](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/31), then updating this dependency:** the declared dependency and lockfile intentionally remain at 0.4.2; its released API cannot run this integration. All 24 required checks now pass on native head `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, but that PR is still unmerged: `roboclaw-bot` has only READ permission in proc-safe and cannot land it. A maintainer with merge permission must merge it first. Then publish the paired native package, update the shipping dependency/lockfile, and revalidate before marking ready. No native merge commit exists to reference yet.

Already-installed affected updaters need one [manual npm, pnpm, or Bun hop](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d514bf8157581542d8a3d55747a4e898e5124bb2/docs/install/updating/update-methods.md#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) from outside the Gateway to a fixed release. The installed driver owns the first handoff, so downloading a candidate cannot repair it. The documented service refresh restores the task definition and enabled state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the task-launcher Job and inner command Job permit explicit breakaway, and only the Scheduled Task managed update helper requests it. Kill-on-close stays enabled and ordinary children remain contained. The existing runtime staging owner retains the matching spawner outside the installation being replaced; stdin/stdout and optional JSON IPC still reach the existing lease, cancellation, recovery and terminal owners.

The proc-safe launcher PID differs from the helper PID. The current handoff already verifies and settles the helper independently of its launcher. Mapped staged native files can remain for existing stale-directory cleanup after process exit; no new cleanup store or protocol is added.

## Evidence

- Spawn selection and outer/inner Job regressions fail on base and pass with the fix. Retained-runtime tests cover loading the copied public spawner after removing the source installation, executable validation, and process creation identity.
- Production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting and docs links pass against the paired API, locally pinned to proc-safe PR commit `ec55427cacc83115f80b42750dc2aea28e470991`; the temporary dependency/lock changes are excluded from this PR.

Prior interrupted run completed 43 native lifecycle, 27 launchd recovery, 25 systemd recovery and 6 engine cases before termination. Initial full lifecycle batch: 79 passed, 4 failed, 5 skipped. The four existing profile-notice cases reproduce host `fs.watch` EMFILE and subsequent cleanup assertions on the base as well; no timeout, retry, skip or assertion relaxation was introduced.
- Test allocation adds exactly 204 net regression/support lines for spawn, nested Job permission and retained native runtime boundaries. The shared ratchet still reports 1,036 lines of inherited debt after this allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- pr-simplify completed: existing staging and handoff owners retained, the FreeBSD-only stage export replaced without an alias, and non-service Windows staging remains independent of proc-safe. Net production growth: 47 lines; tests/support: 204 lines. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- [Native Windows CI](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/actions/runs/41144054731): all four x64/ARM64 × Node22/24 jobs passed at `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, including native Node/Bun main-thread/Worker Job, pipe/EOF, JSON IPC and strict OS-argv proof. The native production/API bytes match the locally tested commit. All 24 required native-PR checks, including every other platform, have now completed successfully. Windows Scheduled Task/Control UI package-upgrade, failure/recovery and cancellation E2E remains unrun here. Crabbox rejected Windows before allocation; it was not retried. No full-symptom closure is claimed.

title: fix(plugins): plugin MCP accounts cannot be signed out and reconnect after reinstall
body:
Related: #165951

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-declared MCP accounts (Granola-style connectors) can be signed in from the plugin page but never signed out, and uninstalling then reinstalling the plugin silently reconnects the previous account.

## User Impact

User impact: a connected account on a plugin's page now has **Sign out** (with confirmation), and uninstalling a plugin removes its saved MCP sign-ins, so a reinstall starts signed out. A server under `mcp.servers` with the same name and URL keeps its credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway only had `mcp.authLogin`, and `openclaw mcp logout` resolves only `mcp.servers` entries, so plugin-declared servers had no sign-out path. The connected-account **Edit** action opened Settings → MCP, which does not list plugin-declared servers.
- New operator-admin `mcp.authLogout { serverName }` resolves the exact connection `mcp.authLogin` signs in (`resolveOperatorMcpOAuthConnection`) and clears it through the existing OAuth store owner. Running MCP clients read tokens per request, so their next call needs a new sign-in.
- Clearing can wait up to 30 seconds for the credential lease while another sign-in or refresh holds it. The caller's live authority (request authority plus `operator.admin` scope) and request signal are passed into the credential write and checked again at write admission, so a caller who loses authority during that wait clears nothing. Uninstall cleanup passes its own `beforePersistentApply` authority the same way and stops on loss instead of reporting it as a storage warning.
- The plugin page replaces the dead-end **Edit** on connected accounts with **Sign out**; the result is re-read from `plugins.inspect` rather than assumed. A confirmation that fails to open shows an error on the account row and leaves the account connected.
- The credential store key is derived from the server name and URL, both of which come from the plugin, so a reinstall found the old row. Plugin uninstall now clears the operator and requester OAuth rows for the plugin's declared HTTP MCP endpoints, as removing a configured server already does. Endpoints are read during uninstall preparation, before files are removed. A storage failure while clearing becomes an uninstall warning rather than failing a committed uninstall.
- No stored format or schema changes: existing `mcp_oauth_stores` rows are read and cleared through the existing owner, and rows for other servers are untouched (asserted in the tests below).
- Accepted edge case: if two installed plugins declare the same MCP server name and URL, uninstalling one clears the shared sign-in; the other plugin shows **Sign in** again.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI in headless Chromium, with a synthetic OAuth MCP server and a local plugin declaring one HTTP OAuth MCP server. Before: installed release 2026.10.9 (`7975404`). After: this branch built with `pnpm build` and `pnpm ui:build`. Sign-in went through the real browser callback; uninstall and reinstall went through `openclaw plugins uninstall/install` against the running Gateway.

**Connected account — before:** only **Edit**, which leads to a page that does not list the server.

![Before: connected plugin account offers only Edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/734e8107-6bd9-4b7c-ad1a-bcf855a646bc)

**Connected account — after:** **Sign out**, with confirmation.

![After: connected plugin account offers Sign out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e439663d-a485-4cea-b013-d9c812937ab8)

![After: Sign out confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abf7b16a-fe7d-4f45-b584-bd63215ff8d3)

**After uninstall, reinstall and enable — before:** still **Connected** to the old account.

![Before: reinstalled plugin is still connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/684f4734-42bc-4852-8f0e-45119869a2dd)

**After uninstall, reinstall and enable — after:** signed out.

![After: reinstalled plugin starts signed out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b1c2365-65fd-4afd-87d9-fca48294f668)

Stored credential readback from the Gateway's `mcp_oauth_stores` row for the plugin server:

| Step | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in from plugin page | tokens present | tokens present |
| Sign out | no control | tokens cleared |
| Uninstall, reinstall, enable | tokens present | tokens cleared |

The browser run above predates the authority follow-up commit; that commit changes only revocation behavior and the dialog failure path, which the tests below cover.

Focused tests:

- `src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts`: 38 passed, including a case that signs a bundle-declared connector in through the browser callback, rejects read-only and unknown-server logout, then signs out without touching another connection's credentials.
- Permission loss during logout (same case): with the credential lease held by another owner, an admin connection sends `mcp.authLogout`, loses `operator.admin` while the handler waits, then the lease is released. The request fails and the saved tokens remain. Without the authority wiring this step fails: the logout succeeds and clears the tokens.
- `src/plugins/management-uninstall.mcp-oauth.test.ts` (new, 5 passed): management uninstall (enabled and disabled plugin) and CLI uninstall clear the plugin's operator and requester rows and keep an unrelated server's row; these fail with the clear call removed. Uninstall cleanup whose authority ends while it waits for the credential lease rejects and keeps the tokens; this fails without the authority wiring. A configured server with the same endpoint keeps its sign-in.
- `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.mcp-auth.test.ts` (8 passed) and `plugins-page.test.ts`: confirmation gating, sign-out request, authoritative refresh, error retention, and a confirmation that fails to open (error shown, no logout request, account still connected). The confirm-dialog mock keeps the real module exports; `check-test-mock-exports` passes.
- Also passed: gateway method descriptor/since/list tests, `connect-hello` scope test, existing uninstall and inspect suites, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files, `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.

Gaps: no real Granola account was used. Settings → MCP still has no **Sign out** for `mcp.servers` entries; `openclaw mcp logout` covers those. Locally, `server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts` needs `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1` on hosts that set `HTTP(S)_PROXY`; without it, existing cases in that file also fail with "could not reach the sign-in service" because the loopback fixture is sent through the proxy.

title: fix: stop GitHub publication from delaying cloud workspace settlement
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud workspace settlement waiting on GitHub network publication after the workspace has already been accepted.

## User Impact

Cloud sessions can finish syncing their changes and accept subsequent work without waiting for GitHub. The original publication receipt completes through the existing lifecycle sweep. No schema, credential, personal-confirmation, retained-disk, or durability-policy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture both turn-bound and queued session requests under the accepting claim, preserving their immutable snapshots before handing publication to existing recovery. Queued requests can reuse an already-published, owned, correctly attributed exact snapshot without another push; unrelated head drift still refuses and preserves previously recorded effects. The existing remote-head reader moves into the recovery owner to keep the executor within its line limit.

## Evidence

- Hosted-review limitation: [ClawSweeper run 41144371719](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41144371719) stopped before review at its input-safety gate, so it produced no verdict. The historical manifest retained only the first of two finding identities: the preexisting diagnostic-redaction fixture at `src/gateway/github-publication.test.ts:403` in base blob `96b09cf5b0a75a94af05d93f8e03c1583d11ca1a`. A subsequent scan-only reproduction used the canonical pinned scanner with verification enabled, the complete committed range, actual review template/context, and decision schema. All two newly emitted records were attributed to that same unchanged synthetic fixture in the base and head blobs, through PLAIN and HTML decoding. Source inspection confirms reserved-domain, fixture-marked test data. These are reproduced records, not recovery of the missing historical second identity. The external review-service hold remains untouched: no scanner exemption, policy edit, model execution, or held-review retry was performed, and local review/CI are not represented as hosted-review success. OpenClaw's current maintainer policy treats hosted ClawSweeper as advisory; landing still requires its ordinary native local-review, CI, security, ownership, and branch-policy gates.
- Red/green handoff regression: the base performed 47 Git/GitHub commands where only the 14 pre-handoff commands were expected. The repaired handoff and claim-held sweep add none. Existing restart coverage still reports the result once.
- Real Git regression: three queued requests publish the accepted contents with one push and one PR, preserve later dirty-file edits, and retain frozen snapshots across preparation retries. The missing session snapshot and duplicate-request failures were reproduced before repair.
- Main publication suite: 22 passed; boundary suite: 34 passed. Runtime/history/personal coverage exposed one personal-head-drift receipt regression during development; it was repaired, and the final targeted head-drift and real-Git queue cases both passed. The subsequent observer extraction preserves the same command arguments, decoding, and authority-wrapped runner.
- Final targeted lint (7 files, 293 rules), formatting, Gateway-methods TypeScript check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Canonical autoreview via the restricted OpenClaw engine, P0–P3: no actionable findings in the full candidate against `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`. Reviewed snapshot is committed as `3359972b4dc49ce6f2605e5addd5b6b3ab2c61b3`. Its completed review predates the hosted scanner refusal; the published head retains the identical tree `8031b7a192ecffbe000a1c19d9ed0eb7669e2da7`.
- Test-line ratchet remains **1,026 lines over its inherited ceiling**. This change adds exactly 37 test lines and a matching 37-line allocation; both totals rise equally, and the shared baseline is unchanged. This is not claimed as a passing ratchet.

Proof ran in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.22.1 containers with real Git/SQLite and synthetic GitHub responses. The 23 optional PostgreSQL cases and live cloud/GitHub publication flow were not exercised. Exact-head [aggregate CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143173993/job/124364732824). The inherited local test-line debt above describes the pinned authoring base; the hosted merge-tree ratchet passed without changing this PR or raising its baseline. Current attached-check inventory: **55 success, 67 skipped, 1 neutral; no failed or pending checks**. CI seconds are not yet available.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and simplification</summary>

- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 27.58 seconds command-runner wall time.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 85.76 seconds, including cold worker compilation; the new real-Git scenario itself takes about 4.2 seconds. Real Git is necessary here: the old synthetic transport did not advance HEAD and could not expose queued-request snapshot reuse failures.
- Final targeted repair proof: 2 passed in 59.41 seconds, including worker compilation.
- Against the pinned base: production +111/−74 lines; tests +51/−14 lines; allocation +2 lines. The inline publication/report loop disappears; the existing writer and lifecycle sweep remain the only state and scheduling owners. Growth preserves the previously uncaptured session-request path and exact queued-request outcomes.

</details>

Related: #94893

## What Problem This Solves

Jetson operators lack a discoverable starting point for adapting the Linux installation to their board.

## User Impact

Readers can find Jetson preparation and diagnostics, then follow the maintained Linux installation, headless service, remote-access, backup, and local-model guides. This does not certify particular boards, images, or GPU inference workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the useful, vendor-neutral hardware guidance from #118594 in a 67-line page instead of duplicating the generic Linux workflow. Remove the unverified compatibility table, blanket native-prebuild guarantees, model-capacity recommendations, unconditional swap/power tuning, and repeated installer/onboarding commands. Current onboarding already attempts to enable lingering; the page routes failures to the existing service runbook. NVIDIA owns board/JetPack selection and hardware tuning.

Runtime production LOC: +0/-0. Docs/navigation/glossary: +72; regression: +14; its separate test-line allocation: +2. The necessary growth makes this new entry point discoverable; the proposed guide is reduced from 240 to 67 lines. No unrelated deletions or runtime changes.

title: feat: onboard personal channel users without external sign-in
body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

## What Problem This Solves

A token/password-authenticated single-user Gateway cannot establish a personal channel identity when its only profile is shared Owner, leaving personal session creation dependent on an external sign-in provider.

## User Impact

An authenticated administrator can explicitly create a person and bind a verified channel sender without Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, or another proxy. Shared Owner stays separate. An explicitly assigned role can delegate session-only authority without granting channel-owner status or global operator write access.

This is a draft for local testing. Real channel end-to-end acceptance remains unverified; do not treat the passing local fixtures as live Discord or Slack evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add administrator-gated `users.create` using the existing profile writer, then reuse `users.linkChannelIdentity` for the exact `(channelId, accountId, senderId)` binding. Carry limited personal authority with the existing verified requester identity, independently of command ownership, and retain the original binding and current policy during queued recovery.

Default roles, display names, message text, and login-name role assignments do not delegate these session scopes. Conflict protection, account qualification, shared-Owner exclusion, access policies, and live revocation checks remain in place. No database schema change or automatic identity migration is introduced. Profile names are not unique keys, and repeated `users.create` calls create distinct people; setup and recovery are documented in [User model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ccb547a8062a35564f527c87708ce9baf5b647ae/docs/concepts/user-model.md#onboard-without-an-external-sign-in-provider).

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing onboarding method through registered Gateway dispatch before implementation: `users.create` returned `unknown method`.
- Onboarding/authority/recovery suites: **95 tests passed** in 139.14 seconds including compilation. They cover unauthorized creation, shared Owner exclusion, conflicting links, exact account matching, forged/asserted contexts, default-role non-escalation, multi-user behavior, demotion, unlinking, and queued recovery. The Discord and Slack host-ingress fixtures invoke the real `sessions_create` tool and verify persisted personal creator attribution, without owner fallback.
- Protocol/discovery/prompt-stability consumers: **56 tests passed** in 79.23 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, touched TypeScript lint/format, protocol registry, generated-validator consistency, native protocol generation, documentation configuration examples/links, diff checks, and the scoped test-line allocation check passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) covered the local candidate against base `1d6f75fd`. No concrete implementation defect was reported; its outstanding P2 finding is the missing real-channel acceptance proof.
- **Pending:** real verified channel turn → model tool invocation → new session under the personal profile's session-write authority. The QA credential broker could not be reached through any existing authenticated Convex launcher. No live Discord or Slack test turn ran, and no production identities or permissions were changed. The requester explicitly asked to publish this draft for local testing.

### Local testing

1. Start an isolated token/password-authenticated Gateway whose profile directory initially contains only shared Owner. Add the explicit `sessionWriter` role from the documented setup; preserve any existing multi-user defaults.
2. From the authenticated administrator connection, call `users.create` with `{ "displayName": "Local tester", "role": "sessionWriter" }`; save the returned `profile.id`.
3. Independently verify the channel sender's immutable ID and configured account, then call `users.linkChannelIdentity` with that personal profile ID and the complete identity tuple. Do not bind shared Owner.
4. From that sender, submit a fresh, normally admitted channel turn explicitly requesting a new independent session. Verify the actual `sessions_create` trace and the stored human/profile creator ID. It must be the new person, not `gateway-owner`; administrator/global-write operations must remain unavailable.
5. Check a different account with the same sender ID, then unlink or demote the person. Confirm those paths cannot retain or regain the old session-write authority. Inspect existing profiles/links before retrying any uncertain creation or binding operation.

Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Repository-only worker sessions repeatedly transfer and reimport previously accepted file changes at every checkpoint.

## User Impact

Later checkpoints can transfer only the new delta without losing cumulative recovery files, deletions, executable modes, symlinks, or worker commits. No configuration, schema, retention, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing checkpoint owner validates the last accepted parent, retains the original pinned source, and supplies immutable blob identities to the existing Git import worker. Entire checkpoints are reused only when file, publication, and Git-history identities match; the stable turn claim still receives a recoverable ref. Startup captures do not become acknowledgments.

## Evidence

- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354205/job/124356640588) fails with 6,314,212 lines against a 6,313,199-line ceiling (1,013 excess). Read-only counting of its main parent `a03f8f6aeed34fffb9ed5e4dc4e12b4df20b8aff` gives 6,314,037/6,313,024 (the same 1,013 excess). This PR adds 175 test lines and exactly 175 allocated lines, preserving the inherited debt; no shared baseline was raised. The aggregate CI gate is therefore not green.

Acceptance rule: with an accepted 256 KiB changed blob and a small second-turn delta, the second Git import must remain below 16 KiB without retransferring the old blob; an unchanged follow-up must perform zero imports and preserve the accepted revision. New Git history and publication snapshots must not be skipped. Count/byte evidence is owner-boundary proof, not a live-provider latency benchmark.

- Tested snapshot: `b46605be3c990dea5aeded3096eebc8610639daf`, against `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`. The committed diff matches the reviewed/tested snapshot exactly.
- Final focused owner, real node HTTP transfer, ref-mutation, and staging suites: **52 tests passed in five files**, 76.26 seconds (80.21 seconds including the repository wrapper). Earlier repository startup/node sync coverage also passed in the four-file, 50-test run before the mechanical ref-helper move. CI seconds are not available yet.
- The original base rejects the incremental payload at the pinned-base check. The fixed two-turn fixture imports **263,529 bytes initially, then 1,580 bytes**, reuses the old 256 KiB blob, and performs **zero imports/no revision change** for an unchanged follow-up. Coverage includes restart reads, stale/missing parents, closed authority, deletions, symlinks, executable mode, empty worker commits, and changed/unchanged publication identity.
- Targeted TypeScript checking of both changed test roots and their production closure, type-aware lint on all 11 changed TypeScript files, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation audit: 16,170 internal links checked, zero broken.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. **Autoreview / Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3**, reviewed the complete local change against the pinned base: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. The reviewer did not execute tests in its sandbox. The first review was invalidated by concurrent formatting; this result is the completed review of the final frozen snapshot.
- No live cloud allocation or model-driven latency benchmark was run; the evidence is real storage/Git/HTTP boundary behavior. Broad/platform validation belongs to PR CI.

Simplification: the existing Git-ref owner now serves both ordinary checkpoint publication and reused claim aliases; there is no second store/cache or new serialized format. Production delta: **+239/−102 lines (net +137)**. Test delta: **+206/−31 (net +175)**; a dedicated 175-line allocation covers the new reconstruction/identity/transport regressions without changing the shared baseline.

Contributor credit: Galin’s [S5 source commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/8c2d1d7a98f6299d6cc08126244efdd178d4c6f9) informed this bounded extraction, rederived against current main.

title: fix(workers): recover interrupted stops without a Gateway restart
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cloud worker can remain stuck stopping until the Gateway restarts when Stop is interrupted before its final workspace-save claim is recorded.

## User Impact

User impact: background recovery can finish saving and releasing the same worker without a Gateway restart. Offline workers retain their final-save obligation until reconnection; recovery never replays input or allocates a replacement. Existing claims, moves, and replaced attachments remain protected. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime sweeps previously skipped draining placements without a claim. Enroll those placements through the existing guarded workspace-recovery owner, then let normal pending-result recovery finish the save. Proven worker loss still records that unresolved changes are unverified.

This adapts the interrupted-drain portion of S4 to current main: `retainDrainingWorkspace` already owns the donor's proposed enrollment helper, so no second helper or recovery path is introduced. Retained-disk changes and provider-outage containment are deliberately excluded.

## Original implementation evidence (head `96b6dd8017c43d3171b46bae82ffb5f94aabd46d`)

- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141200382/job/124356088673) fails with 6,314,125 lines against a 6,313,100-line ceiling (1,025 excess). Read-only counting of its main parent `3111c36da03ae2932fffbac605628cbc5b66d525` gives 6,314,049/6,313,024 (1,025 excess). This PR adds 76 test lines and exactly 76 allocated lines, preserving the inherited debt; no shared baseline was raised. The aggregate CI gate is therefore not green.

- Regression reproduced on base `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`: no pending final-save claim after a runtime sweep; proven worker loss remained draining.
- Corrected recovery suite: 37 tests passed, including actual temporary-file apply through the real placement/pending-result owners, offline retry, unchanged claim ownership, stale/replaced attachments, no replay/allocation, and proven-loss reporting. File wall time: 65.23 seconds (67.57 seconds including wrapper); native-worker compilation dominates the cold run. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Final combined recovery, admission, Move, and targeted-recovery suites: **80/80 tests passed across 4 files** in 96.96 seconds (99.53 seconds including wrapper).
- Scoped typecheck, two-file lint, and three-file formatting passed in a task-isolated rootless container with frozen dependencies and normal supply-chain gates; `git diff --check` also passed. Provider/tunnel I/O is fixture-backed; no live cloud-provider or model run was performed.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 review found two test-fixture issues, both corrected. Local autoreview (Codex/GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3) reviewed the complete final local snapshot against the pinned base with the unchanged ownership contracts supplied: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Reviewed commit `53c250e17f5feabda51186b0731547c5796556bd` and managed publication head `96b6dd8017c43d3171b46bae82ffb5f94aabd46d` have identical trees; the latter adds publication attribution only. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; [the hosted review is already queued](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188805#issuecomment-6535207498), so no duplicate request was posted.
- Simplification: reuse the current enrollment and pending-result owners; no new state, schema, replay logic, or provider machinery. Delta: production +21/−2; tests +92/−16 (net +76, separately allocated for these regressions); documentation +1/−1.

Contributor credit: adapted from Galin Iliev's S4 source commit `9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27` at his request.


## Final review correction — October 31

Fresh independent P0–P3 review found that runtime recovery still required current launch compatibility before enrolling a claimless interrupted drain. An exactly attached worker with an older launch dialect remained draining without its final-save claim. The correction uses exact attachment ownership; the existing final-save owner still owns runtime qualification, save and teardown. No execution is resumed.

- The added stale-dialect case fails on the published production code with zero pending results instead of one, then passes with the one-line correction. The final six interrupted-drain/ownership controls pass (40.84 seconds including the runner).
- Full recovery suite: 36 passed, two failed. Both failures are the existing startup/runtime pending-result retirement cases; both reproduce identically with the production file restored to the prior published version (87.50 seconds). They retain an active pending claim rather than the asserted failed placement. Their underlying cause remains unresolved; this is not claimed as a fully passing suite or a fix for those failures.
- Gateway test typecheck, two-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. The dedicated allocation is now exactly 84 net regression lines; shared scalar unchanged.
- Fresh canonical autoreview / Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, reviewed the complete corrected candidate. Its only finding was the old INDEX version of the repaired gate; it explicitly judged the working-tree repair correct with no additional actionable findings. Staging the exact reviewed changes resolved that INDEX-only finding. The run itself is not labeled scoped-clean.
- Simplification: one existing predicate changed; the existing file-save test table gains one case, with no new state or recovery path.

Published correction: `f0bedeb8628874a266a1f0cdd43f71b289e417a4`, tree `5ca0b969ad8ba6d9a5ea05a5c0346ed11d9bae4a`. Current-head CI is pending; earlier failed CI remains historical evidence.

title: fix(workers): refresh platform certificates before Linux enrollment
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Linux cloud workers can fail TLS bootstrap when a provider injects certificates that have not yet been registered in the system trust store, including workers started from a cached image.

## User Impact

Linux enrollment registers available platform certificates before downloading artifacts or launching the node. Non-root images need noninteractive sudo for `/usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates`; a failed refresh stops enrollment with repair guidance. Runtime-only preparation and non-Linux targets are unchanged. Certificate verification is not disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the trust refresh to the existing enrollment owner, where both cold and cached starts pass. The certificate-update subprocess receives none of the private setup, download, or worker-Codex environment values. Existing supervised trust inheritance is reused rather than duplicated.

The production change is +20/−1 lines in one existing file; no new configuration, SDK contract, or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real Linux trust proof: a network-isolated Node 24.22.1 Debian container executed the actual generated enrollment command with `/usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates` unchanged and a local HTTPS endpoint signed by a newly installed, unregistered CA. Fresh and cached-runtime enrollment both fail on the pinned base with curl certificate-verification exit 60, then complete with exit 0 on the published source. Existing settings remain byte-for-byte identical; fresh enrollment downloads one fixture artifact and cached enrollment downloads none. This uses a synthetic node package to observe launch, not a live Azure worker or model run. A direct production-generator harness was used after the broader supplementary test runner hit compiler process limits; no test or resource safeguard was disabled.
- Data-model review clarification: this patch changes no stored fields, config shape, schema, or migration. The actual cached-runtime/settings preservation above covers the touched startup path; it is not claimed as a full released-version upgrade campaign.
- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41140850963/job/124355019451) reports 6,314,124 lines against a 6,313,099 ceiling (1,025 excess). Its main parent `b39e2d09329cc81b09cf55980a2506623236ea59` already had 6,314,049/6,313,024 (the same 1,025 excess). This PR adds 75 test lines and exactly 75 allocated lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. The aggregate CI gate remains red on that inherited debt.
- Baseline regression: the three Linux cases fail on unchanged production code; the macOS negative control passes.
- Fixed candidate: all 32 enrollment tests pass in a secretless Node 24.22.1 container using the repository test runner (23.38 s wall time). Coverage includes root/non-root registration, cached runtime preparation, rejection before artifact download after refresh failure, credential isolation, and existing bootstrap behavior. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Targeted type-aware lint: no problems in both changed TypeScript files. Repository formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Targeted compiler validation of both changed files and their dependency closure passes through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, retaining the extension graph’s ambient declarations.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`, P0–P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable.
- The 75-line net test allocation covers generated guest-shell execution at the real enrollment boundary. OS command paths are mapped to isolated fixtures; no host certificate store or live cloud machine is changed. This is not a live Azure-provider proof.

Original platform-trust work by @galiniliev, extracted and narrowed from [9501dfaa8de](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27).

title: fix(android): preserve accepted work when ending Talk
body:
Closes #188134

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted agent work being canceled when an Android phone user taps End Talk.

## User Impact

End Talk stops listening and playback while accepted work continues and its answer remains available in chat. To cancel work instead, say “cancel” before ending the call or use the chat run’s existing Stop control.

Realtime detachment requires a Gateway advertising `talk-session-close-disposition`; older Gateways retain their legacy aborting close. Other clients’ Stop behavior is unchanged. No new setting, permission, protocol field, or UI control is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending an audio conversation should not silently discard work the agent already accepted. Reuse the phone’s existing capture-cleanup path, which already detaches during backgrounding and mode changes, rather than maintain a separate abort override for End Talk. Native Talk keeps its existing accepted-work behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual Android `NodeRuntime` and relay WebSocket boundary on base `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`: the updated regression failed with **expected detach, observed abort** specifically for End Talk.
- With the fix, `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **131 tests**: all **112 TalkModeManagerTest** cases and **19 RealtimeAgentCoordinatorTest** cases, with zero failures, errors, or skips. These include End Talk/mode-change close requests, capture retirement, native accepted-work preservation, explicit abort, legacy capability behavior, and voice cancellation. Gradle completed in **47 seconds**.
- Gateway `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts -t "settles close disposition"` passed **9 selected scenarios** in **84.75 seconds** overall. This exercises the real close/admission/history owners with fixed inference/provider fixtures: detach leaves accepted work running and publishes its answer; explicit/default abort cancels it. It also covers work completed before close, spoken replacement, a second consult, and uncertain transcript append outcomes. The 13 unrelated cases were filtered, not claimed passing.
- Android `:app:ktlintCheck` passed (**17 seconds**); production and test Kotlin compiled as part of the focused Gradle run. Both changed docs passed MDX and formatting checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent **AutoReview**, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium reasoning, **P0–P2**, reviewed the complete local candidate against the pinned base with relevant unchanged lifecycle/cancellation context: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Only an American English spelling correction followed. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable within this task’s permitted source/skill scope, so the documented fallback route was used; hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR for review; its review is pending.
- Simplification: removes the phone-only close-disposition override and its unused plumbing. Production Kotlin **+2/-8**; regression test **+4/-4**. No new state or parallel lifecycle owner.

**Proof limits:** this is Android runtime/WebSocket and isolated Gateway boundary proof, not a newly installed physical-phone call or live-provider audio test. No rendered UI changes are included. Broad PR CI is separate from these focused passing checks.

Reported by @jeffjhunter in #188134. Prepared at the request of @RomneyDa.

title: fix(test): prevent Usage snapshot reuse deadline flakes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Usage snapshot-reuse regression test can fail when worker preparation crosses the request's real 15-second deadline.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The test continues to check pagination, filtering and publication invalidation with every existing assertion retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

A deadline-expired publication read correctly returns a partial snapshot, and the next filter correctly loads it again. This test assumed that read always completed. It now controls only `setTimeout` and `clearTimeout` for the snapshot-reuse case, with real timers restored during cleanup. Separate tests retain the deadline and partial-reload contracts.

The historical CI trigger was not observed. This fix addresses the demonstrated deadline premise; it does not claim a cache-identity defect or attribute one to an introducing commit.

## Evidence

title: docs(gateway): clarify HTTP check gaps during lifecycle transitions
body:
Related: #187171

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway supervisors can mistake expected HTTP-check gaps during startup, shutdown, or in-process restart for a wedged process.

## User Impact

Operators get an explicit contract for connection refusal before bind and after transport closure, including while the same PID remains alive. Combine HTTP checks with process/exit information, bounded startup/restart grace, and the process owner's shutdown budget; a living PID does not justify indefinite grace. No runtime or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the documentation alternative explicitly offered in #187171 and recommended by [its review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187171#issuecomment-6485949796): define pre-bind/post-close refusal windows and bounded supervisor grace. The documentation change is complete for that scope. It does not promise continuous HTTP availability or change listener ownership; any such runtime contract remains a separate maintainer decision.

The checks share the Gateway HTTP transport. The later listening summary is not the bind timestamp. Existing projection-startup guidance and endpoint semantics are preserved: health 200 means HTTP liveness, startup remains 503 while starting or draining, and startup 200 is not readiness. Traffic still uses readiness and normal admission. No universal numeric timeout is prescribed.

## Evidence

Source inspection at candidate base `00bfbf1f7ca54b0da62a10cc0d33323f3559dc02` confirms transport ownership, bind/close order, same-process restart, endpoint semantics, and delayed startup logging.

Isolated Debian 12 Bookworm / Node 24.22.1 measurements compared actual npm **2026.10.5** (`1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`) with source-built main **2026.10.9** (`d3c0ab1fc65a0dc0350a2f661835b05e2ea0c0f2`). | First completed HTTP responses: health 200 / startup 503 / ready 503 | 5.072 / 5.075 / 5.074 | 4.418 / 4.419 / 4.418 |
| Later `http server listening` summary | 5.306 | 5.688 |
| First completed startup 200 / ready 200 | 5.836 / 5.836 | 6.376 / 6.417 |
| Transport close interval / process exit (code 0) | 7.545–7.565 / 8.124 | 7.505–7.526 / 7.710 |

title: fix(sandbox): sandboxed turns fail with "Aborted" when Podman is slow to answer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sandboxed turns fail before any model runs, showing only "Your request couldn't be completed.", when the Podman engine takes more than 5 seconds to answer `podman info` on a busy host.

## User Impact

User impact: on a busy Podman host, sandboxed turns wait for Podman to answer instead of failing. If Podman really is unresponsive for 30 seconds, the run error names the Podman command that hung and what to check, instead of a bare `Aborted`.

Accepted tradeoff: a truly hung Podman now takes up to 30 seconds to fail a turn instead of 5.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every sandboxed turn on the Podman backend first runs `podman info`. That probe had a 5-second timeout, while every other sandbox engine control call (container lifecycle, Docker target checks, quiescence, persistent exec control) allows 30 seconds. On a busy shared host, `podman info` can wait several seconds on storage locks while the engine itself is healthy. The probe's abort then surfaced as an untyped `Aborted`, which became the turn's `SandboxProvisioningError`.

This aligns the Podman probe with the 30-second engine-call budget. A timeout now becomes an error that names the command, such as `podman info`. Non-timeout failures are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Production incident (team gateway, 2026-10-30):** 62 `SandboxProvisioningError: Aborted` turn failures in one log window, across more than a dozen sessions plus a cron job. They came in two bursts: 19 in the 17:00 UTC hour and 30 in the 21:00 UTC hour. The diagnostics timeline shows each failing turn spent about 5.0s in `attempt.setup.sandbox.backend.runtime_info` before aborting. That matches the old `SANDBOX_ENGINE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000`. The host had about 180 running sandbox containers at the time.
- **Regression tests** in `src/agents/sandbox/docker.test.ts` use a fake clock. One checks that a slow-but-healthy `podman info` (12s) still resolves; the other checks that the timeout error names the command. On `origin/main`, both fail: the first rejects with `AbortError: Aborted`, the same failure seen in production. With this change, both pass.
- **Real-subprocess check** against real Podman 5.7.0, through a PATH shim that delays only `podman info`:
  - base, 8s delay: `failed after 8011ms: AbortError: Aborted`
  - fix, 8s delay: `ok after 8567ms {"machine":false,"rootless":true,...,"version":"5.7.0"}`
  - fix, 40s hang: ``Podman did not answer `podman info` within 30s. Check that Podman is responsive on the Gateway host (for example, `podman info`), then retry.``

  The wall-clock times above include the shim's `sleep` keeping the output pipe open after SIGTERM, which is an artifact of the shim.
- `pnpm test` passed for `docker.test.ts` (19 tests) and the sandbox consumer tests `podman-runtime.mounts`, `podman-upgrade`, `docker-backend`, `dependency-template` and `docker.config-hash-recreate` (81 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the touched files also passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P2): scoped-clean, no findings.
- **CI repair (2026-11-02, `74c83914a6de795b72d64b5c43b2ed9f96fd4d12`):** the original CI run `41137380276` failed only the test-line ratchet. Added `config/test-lines-allocations/podman-startup-timeout.txt` for exactly the 51 net regression-test lines needed to protect slow-but-healthy probes and actionable timeout diagnostics. Both tests and all assertions are unchanged; the shared scalar is unchanged. No rebase or main integration was performed.
- **Fresh repair verification:** all six sandbox files passed again, 100/100 tests, in 63.27s wrapper wall time. Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of the complete local candidate against `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b` was scoped-clean, with no findings; the reviewed tree is the committed repair above. Earlier typecheck and real-Podman subprocess evidence is reused because production and test source did not change in this repair.
- **Ratchet proof:** the actual checker passes on the pinned merge composition of main `b1e0c9a24eba640d983e08fec4c0d6f90b8ca00b` and the repair: 6,389,782 test lines, ceiling 6,401,323, slack 11,541. The historical branch snapshot still contains 1,042 lines of inherited debt; that failure remains recorded rather than being hidden by a scalar raise or unrelated test edits.
- **Exact-head CI:** [run 41407402471, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41407402471) completed all 64 jobs. The repaired test-line ratchet and `security-fast` passed. Only the extension-boundary test and its aggregate failed; all other CI jobs passed or were skipped. The failure reports a private Baseten runtime import in `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts`. Both that offender and `test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` are byte-identical between actual main baseline `b0fdadd6b3448af5e23c45794465d48d97944fbe` and tested merge `33abecb7200ea30f385840a4babd826c8dd2e654`; the complete merge delta contains only the three reviewed Podman paths. Automatic classification is `unknown` because no main job name matches; this independent source-bound attribution supports the native inherited-failure route, not a claim of green CI. No rerun, re-push, or unrelated repair was used.
- **Gap:** I did not run a full isolated Gateway turn under induced Podman contention. The proof covers the probe at the subprocess boundary.

Not in this PR: the host-side cause of the contention (many concurrent sandbox containers and Podman jobs on one box) is an operational issue for whoever runs that host.

body:
Supersedes #127116, thanks @rrmars.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing token counts for streamed `byteplus` and `byteplus-plan` responses when the endpoint requires an explicit usage request.

## User Impact

BytePlus streaming turns request final token counts so those counts can reach turn accounting. No configuration change or migration is needed. Explicit model-level streaming-usage overrides retain precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both provider IDs now declare support through the existing plugin manifest contract, matching Volcengine. The shared transport already requests and parses final usage chunks; no new runtime branch is needed. BytePlus documents `stream_options.include_usage` as defaulting to false in its [Chat API reference](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/modelark/chat-api).

The simplification pass retained only the two capability declarations and extended the existing manifest test. Executable production code: +0/-0. Production metadata: +14/-0; no equivalent dead or duplicate code exists in this owner to remove safely. Tests: +7/-8 (net -1). Direct JSON import removes redundant file reading/parsing; no test-line allocation or baseline change remains.

## Evidence

- On main `d107cb81b327fc4654dbbaa9f21beba0cf2fc57a`, the updated manifest regression fails on the missing `providerRequest` declaration: 1 failed, 3 passed. With this fix: 4 passed. Command: `pnpm test extensions/byteplus/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Final regression wall time: 12.83s red, 11.15s green (Vitest 6.59s; transformation dominates). The original cold baseline took 58.47s. The [final-head extension CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138293887/job/124346605101) took 106s including setup. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on phones, the screen shown while a new session is being created uses a different header and menu button than the chat it turns into, so the header visibly changes when the session opens.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7195c458-7296-47ac-9cc4-88adafeb33c1)

User impact: from the moment you press Start on a phone, the session shows the same header it will keep: the round, outlined menu button, the title placeholder and the Panels/⋯ capsule. Before the Gateway accepts a new session, the pending screen has no mobile panel host, so its header fell back to the squeezed desktop chat header. ## What Problem This Solves

A Windows-node command submitted through Code Mode can remain pending without returning native output, an exit status, or an actionable failure, even when discovery and native Codex session listing succeed.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is for remote Windows commands to return their actual output and exit status, or a truthful denial, timeout, cancellation, or unknown-outcome result.
