Issue #176315 reports this failure with a Linux Gateway and native Windows node running OpenClaw 2026.10.4. The failing owner has not been identified, so this draft deliberately does not propose a speculative repair.

The next step is one bounded, harmless absolute-path `codex.exe --version` probe in an isolated paired environment, using normal supported approvals. Correlate the Code Mode bridge request with exec entry, preparation, approval disposition, node invocation, native process completion, terminal-result acceptance, and Code Mode continuation. Only then select the smallest fix at the responsible boundary.

## Evidence

- Read the report and complete comments, traced the execution and result-return owners, and compared release `383c124cc32f` with inspected main `76985e4c31c4`.

Similar symptoms do not establish a shared cause or prove that this report is fixed.

title: fix(ci): prevent mobile release output-cap test flakes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent mobile release CI test failures when output-limit termination interrupts the process-tree fixture's PID publication.

## User Impact

Developers get reliable native process-cleanup evidence. Release execution behavior stays unchanged.

title: fix(codex): avoid missing native binaries during automatic selection
body:
Closes #90587.

Supersedes #127303, thanks @rajmp999.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes first-message failures when automatic Codex selection finds its npm launcher but no native app-server binary, including Linux RISC-V64.

## User Impact

Automatic selection can use the built-in OpenClaw harness. Explicit and prepared pinned Codex choices retain native ownership and report an actionable error. Custom commands, environment overrides, socket transports, worker-hosted app-servers, and source-built native executables remain eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check actual binary presence at the Codex supports boundary using the existing managed resolver. The official npm launcher can throw before spawning on an unsupported platform, so spawn ENOENT alone misses the reported failure. Another platform allowlist would duplicate the existing mapping and reject valid native builds or remote connections. Unsupported is returned without a declared fallback; the existing selector already distinguishes implicit/auto selection from explicit ownership. Version and handshake validation stay at startup.

The earlier extraction and shared command-source wrapper are removed. The final production delta is +58/-14 (net +44), confined to two existing owner files; tests add 49 lines and docs add 8. There is no equivalent dead code in this owner to remove without deleting supported behavior. The necessary net growth comprises the managed-local-stdio eligibility guard and actionable error (+16 plus one import), the actual-presence query over existing candidates/PATH (+20), and synchronous bounded launcher recognition (+7 net, including imports). This reuses the existing platform map, singleton, package resolver and native recognition, with no new module, cache, setting, core or SDK contract. Synchronous filesystem recognition is needed by the synchronous selection contract; it reads only the existing two-byte shebang prefix. Worker-hosted configuration keeps binary validation with the worker; unplaced local attempts retain existing startup validation.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on main `81cf32d99769`: the new missing-native case returns supported; the other 36 harness tests pass. Final repair: all 37 harness and 32 managed-startup tests pass (69 total, 55.56 seconds including cold compilation). The regression preserves custom/env commands, WebSocket/Unix, live worker config and a native PATH fixture under Linux/RISC-V64 simulation.
- Real production selector probe is red on the base (selects Codex) and green on the final head: implicit selects OpenClaw; explicit and prepared pinned Codex reject; configured transports remain eligible. Selection contract tests (26) and prompt-prefix stability tests (14) also pass.
- Final-head focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh final-head autoreview through P2, including full frozen resolver/selection context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm build` passes on final head `1123b4d3831f69d9df2859a6defa2ecca42c8da5` in a rootless container capped at 4 CPUs / 8 GiB (3m 28.9s), using the supported `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352` setting. Cgroup OOM events: zero. Earlier attempts exceeded the cap before that build-owner heap setting was applied.
- The completed build passes an isolated host Gateway turn with private state/home, free loopback port 41019 and native Codex artifacts fault-injected absent. No runtime override or authored request-transport parameters were used. Trace-only instrumentation observes `selected=openclaw reason=implicit_plugin_unsupported_openclaw`; the Gateway process makes a POST to the Responses request boundary, receives a fixture response and returns `PR127303_PROVIDER_BOUNDARY_OK` with CLI status `ok`. The Gateway process and port are confirmed closed afterward. No Team Gateway action was taken.
- Live limitation: no task-scoped provider credential was available. The successful boundary proof uses a synthetic noncredential marker and an intercepted transport, not authenticated model inference. Physical RISC-V hardware remains untested. The native-missing regression and real selector negative control fail on the base, so a preexisting route-based OpenClaw choice cannot satisfy this proof.
- Contributor code was read via GitHub only and never checked out or run. Every replacement commit credits Raj Muppala <54062691+rajmp999@users.noreply.github.com>.

Final-head [CI run 41136992196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41136992196) completed: 35 jobs passed, 27 skipped. The only root failure is [test-lines](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41136992196/job/124342346729); `openclaw/ci-gate` fails downstream. Its tree was reconstructed and verified.

title: improve: show gateway commit and build time on About
body:
Original author: Chris Eckert (@ceckert). This is his #180353, rebased onto current `main` so it can land; that branch's managed workspace became unusable during its base refresh, so it could not be updated in place. The branch carries his `Co-authored-by` trailer, so the squash commit credits him.

## What Problem This Solves

Members can see the connected Gateway version but cannot identify its running commit or build time when diagnosing a possibly stale deployment.

## User Impact

Settings → About shows the Control UI and the connected Gateway as two separate sections, each listing version, commit (with copy) and UTC build time; the Control UI section also shows its branch. A member can tell whether the Gateway they are connected to includes a fix without assuming the browser bundle matches it. Missing provenance is omitted; a disconnected Gateway shows its version as unavailable. Host diagnostics and update operations remain restricted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing authenticated hello payload and About page rather than adding another version endpoint or screen. The Gateway reports `server.commit` and `server.builtAt` from the build provenance it captures once at startup, so a later checkout change does not relabel the running Gateway. No changes to `system.info` or `update.status` authorization.

The UI adds no new CSS. Both builds render with the existing Settings facts grid (`.settings-kv`) and the shared `CopyButton`, replacing About's bespoke copy state machine and its styles. `about.css` shrinks versus `main` (6,235 → 4,962 bytes), so the Control UI CSS budget check, which allows no growth while `main` is over its cap, passes.

Rebase notes (relative to #180353): `main` now owns build provenance in `readBuildProvenanceForModuleUrl`, so the Gateway build time is read from that record (`resolveRuntimeServiceBuiltAt`, normalized to ISO, unparseable values omitted) instead of a second build-info reader. About strings live in the deferred `en-about` catalog, and the hero keeps `main`'s Support link. The mocked Gateway carries commit and build time through `main`'s `control-ui-mock-scenario` module.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway handshake (in-process Gateway server, real WebSocket connect, device paired with member scopes `operator.sessions.read`/`operator.sessions.write`, production-shaped `build-info.json`): hello returned `server.commit` (short SHA) and `server.builtAt: "2026-10-30T21:00:00.000Z"`; `system.info` → `missing scope: operator.read`, `update.status` → `missing scope: operator.admin`. This closes the "isolated real Gateway/member handshake" gap listed on #180353.
- Unit: About view/page tests (both sections' facts, copy controls, localized UTC build time, omitted facts and unavailable Gateway), `connect-hello.update-scope` (member hello carries commit/builtAt, update details still omitted) and `version` tests pass.
- Browser (Playwright Chromium, production bundle, mocked Gateway, member scopes): `about.e2e` (both sections' facts, Gateway commit copy, zero `system.info`/`update.status` requests, no horizontal overflow at 375px) and `build-info-unicode.e2e` pass on the current head after merging `main`.
- Current head: UI typecheck, formatting and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, P1) on the earlier rail layout: scoped-clean, no findings. Not rerun on the reuse-only layout.

### Screenshots

Production-bundle captures of the reuse-only layout (desktop, 390px, dark) were inspected in the landing session: both sections render with the standard Settings card and facts grid, and the copy button takes the Settings 44px touch size on mobile. They are not embedded here because this publication route cannot upload images; the earlier rail screenshots from #180353 no longer match and were removed.

Contributor credit: Chris Eckert (@ceckert) authored this change: he identified the member-access gap and requested extending the existing About page. Design review: Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski).

Fixes `openclaw update` refusing an already-current npm installation with legacy config that Doctor can repair, unless the operator also supplied `--channel`.

Already-current updates skip candidate admission. title: fix(memory-core): keep fallback diary entries out of context
body:
Supersedes #126642, thanks @HsienW.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed dream narrative's placeholder can enter later dreaming prompts and displace a useful recent diary entry.

## User Impact

Recent continuity context keeps useful diary entries while fallback history stays visible in `DREAMS.md`. Existing placeholders are excluded without a migration or user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the exclusion in the current diary reader, before the recent-entry limit, and share the fallback sentence with its writer. The original PR conflicts with the diary-owner extraction, so this replacement re-implements the fix on main and extends the existing empty-completion regression through the next narrative request.

The exact standalone diagnostic sentence is intentionally treated as a placeholder regardless of its writer; entries containing additional prose remain eligible. Origin markers for future writes would leave existing placeholders affected.

Production LOC is net zero: the shared constant and reader filter are offset by consolidating the redundant return branch in diary-section creation. Test LOC is also net zero: symlink read/write checks share one fixture, and file/directory permission checks share the existing/new-workspace cases. Their assertions are retained. **Landing remains coordinator-owned:** current-head CI and the normal landing gates must pass. Earlier-head checks are not approval of this new head; no CI rerun was requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Runtime-image integrations need ready capacity without a connected browser, without unavailable policy blocking cleanup or restart destroying and replacing existing ready workers.

## User Impact

The configured default profile keeps runtime-only workers ready and refills after claims. Restart preserves compatible reserve identities while demand is reconstructed. Disabling capacity drains unused workers without interrupting attached sessions or extending finite deadlines. Ready workers incur running-machine charges until deletion is confirmed.

Standing demand reuses the existing pool and environment inventory. Image preparation contains runtime artifacts, not repository contents or credentials. Repository claim/startup and credential authority are supplied by the landed prerequisites. Browser-driven repository demand and empty-workspace activation retain their existing paths.

Demand observation cannot disable expiry or physical cleanup. Pending reconstruction preserves inventory but grants no provider I/O. title: fix(macos): avoid startup crashes from invalid custom Gateway hosts

Closes #187602

## What Problem This Solves

Invalid saved custom Gateway hosts can crash the macOS app at startup or endpoint refresh. Configuration errors can also become stuck as ownership failures after the host is corrected.

## User Impact

The app displays an actionable IPv4 configuration error and recovers after host-only correction without silently choosing another Gateway, rewriting settings, or enabling unsupported IPv6 binding. Genuine ownership conflicts remain blocked. No new configuration, dependency, database schema or state owner is introduced.

Scope decision, 1 November: keep this PR focused on endpoint crash safety and configuration recovery. The first-launch updater/runtime-pin ordering failure discovered during validation is a separate repair task; it is not claimed fixed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing endpoint owner validates custom IPv4 binding before URL construction and publishes failures through its unavailable state. The process manager distinguishes retained ownership conflicts from recoverable configuration errors, preserving background activation intent.

title: feat(workers): start repository sessions from runtime image reserves
body:
Related: #188656, now merged as `a4b07c63b60cf3a971c824064c82946c530e1686`. This PR now targets **main**. History-preserving refresh `75275a543acd67edc3e6ec353aff0c73d15d1a2c` merges that exact main into the existing image branch; it does not land this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Repository integrations need to separate reusable runtime capacity from each session's repository access and checkout.

## User Impact

Integrations selecting image-only capacity can claim a compatible runtime worker, or provision one cold, then restore the repository under the current request's authority. Image preparation does not read repository contents or obtain GitHub credentials. Unsupported profiles fail before allocation. Native, paired-device, and repository-capacity preparation retain their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image and empty-workspace preparation have distinct source, claim, and cache identities. Dispatch selects runtime-only intent without repository preparation inputs; repository startup retains the original host-side credential reader, including admission and current-authority checks. Live profile checks reach allocation and claim, and retries settle stored intent rather than selecting a changed profile.

Rejected, unallocated image requests are terminalized so reconciliation cannot later allocate them. Uncertain provisioning and cancellation retain their existing ownership. Repository authority, native credential return, required-profile admission, and sessions.create caller handling are supplied by the landed prerequisite, not duplicated here.

The image delta adds no standing-demand/refill policy, retained-disk feature, heartbeat, packaging feature, database table, live configuration change, or production test hook. Production growth remains 130 lines; test growth is 1,025 lines with matching allocations of 586 + 326 + 113. Node/transfer and managed-profile fixtures are shared.

## Evidence

### Current main conflict refresh

Tested tree: `4ca284c6ee331f5ead63a56c21758d18537e16b3`. First parent: previous image head `428a4576808c07fc5f1582755bcadf08d9a6dc21`; second parent: exact main `a4b07c63b60cf3a971c824064c82946c530e1686`.

- Five squash-related textual conflicts were reproduced. Every incoming conflict file was byte-identical to the already integrated authority source. Resolution preserves **all 17 image-delta files byte-for-byte**, including RPC repair `92fa442b0ea78784434b9a87f4f780f8c32f94f1`; the complete path set against main is still exactly those 17 files, with no extra base-relative edits.
- **95 tests across six files passed**, in **158.87 seconds**: the meaningful 54-case RPC/image/managed authority suite plus 41 focused runtime-artifact/bootstrap cases for the changed upstream package inputs. These use real local Git, admission, checkpoint and fixture-package effects; no full production package rebuild ran.
- Targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Normal attributed commit hooks remained enabled. Existing independent P0–P2 reviews remain applicable to the unchanged image delta; the mechanical resolutions and complete base-relative source preservation were inspected directly.
- The frozen dependency graph is unchanged. Parsed multi-document lockfiles are semantically equal—the textual changes only reorder entries. The root manifest only adds upstream's `runtime-artifacts` export; workspace manifests and package versions are unchanged. Tests use independently frozen read-only fs-safe 0.27.0 dependencies and private generated outputs in secretless Node 24.22.1 containers. No parent mutable dist/cache, live cloud, or live credentials were used.
- The previous `428a…` CI result remains previous-head evidence. Natural CI on this new publication is still required; no workflow rerun was requested.

### Actual authority and checkout effects

- **App mode:** native JWT signing verified by a local HTTP server, synthetic installation credential issuance/revocation, authenticated Git HTTP checkout through NodeWorkerWorkspaceRuntime, and actual SQLite/bare-Git checkpoint storage and transfer. Unauthorized/revoked/reassigned callers cannot issue credentials or perform Git I/O; revocation after authorized issuance prevents checkout. Recovery restores accepted state, excluding unaccepted old-node files.
- **Managed PAT/OAuth:** actual private-profile reads and HTTP credential verification, authenticated checkout and checkpoint restoration. Positive claim/cold controls succeed; denied callers cause zero verification and zero Git/node effects; caller retirement stops checkout. OAuth recovery re-enters current policy and rejects a forbidden fresh caller. The plugin is never asked for a managed bearer.
- **Actual sessions.create:** allowed RPC verifies the managed identity exactly once and checks real file contents. Policy revocation, source replacement, Stop, and caller retirement retain zero-verification/zero-node-command assertions. Runtime allocation asserts image intent without a credential reader. No fixture-only admission is fabricated.

### Retained provenance and compatibility evidence

- Exact prerequisite `b062896364982a2838139025c0497d6e5bfb7712`, tree `2b96a7360603b237e4d4b3facbaff778c25f3cdf`, was integrated through `e56379f…` and tree-identical merge `94fdd2b3…` before its squash landing. That image tree `6455ab40de45e201e3044bcd88d7f146a284a298` passed the 54-case suite in 136.38 seconds with independently frozen inputs.
- The prerequisite owner completed the installed stable upgrade on exact `b062…`: agent schema 25→39, state schema 20→36, configuration, 14 plugins and retained checkpoint proof, with teardown confirmed. That is prerequisite-owned evidence, not a new installed-binary run on this image refresh; no active-worker reconnection is claimed.
- RPC repair `92fa442…`, tree `949676825692d904ecad4b4f32e7c60a03e9850f`, reproduced the [original failing CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41162152493/job/124422139825): one failed/nine passed on `7594c433…`, versus ten passed on exact parent `c6ceb4ae…`. Removing the fixture-only identity call from runtime intent creation preserved actual startup admission. Its 54-case repair run, static checks and ratchets passed; one test line and one allocation line were removed. Those ratchet totals remain historical input-bound evidence.
- Earlier identity/selection, canonical registry, refused-intent reconciliation, and prior-reader revocation negative controls remain recorded. The older 106-case/seven-file run omitted the RPC suite and is not presented as proof of that former failure.
- Released `v2026.10.9` (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`) used v1 project-shaped worker records, including empty local workspaces. Runtime-image identity is new capacity metadata, never authorization. This image slice changes no worker SQL table or settings schema. The earlier schema20→state36 synthetic-record spot-check is retained only as prior-head evidence.

Current-head CI and root-owned landing gates remain. title: improve: safely reuse qualified offline compositions
body:
Related: #188661, now landed. This follow-on targets **main** and preserves exact prerequisite `f3bdcadb948e1b873b59066cbd0994192da50a42` in its history. Its effective change against reviewed main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081` is exactly the five qualified-reuse files.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated offline compositions rehash every dependency payload, while skipping verification of a mutable donor or Docker's `app/` input would admit stale or changed bytes.

## User Impact

Release tooling can opt into qualified dependency reuse and an archive-bound image recipe without changing the strict defaults. Reuse receipts explicitly report partial input verification; neither mode replaces Linux target acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

A trusted, digest-bound receipt from a prior strict composition qualifies the dependency manifest, not the current donor. Reuse still checks complete topology, modes, sizes, link targets/containment and package manifests, then verifies the actual selected copies against that inventory. Unselected payload bytes are not rehashed, and partial receipts cannot qualify another reuse. No caller-written operation report serves as authority.

The landed composition owner's repairs are retained: builtin-named npm dependencies use package lookup and nearest-ancestor deduplication, and legitimate implementation files under paths such as `src/node_modules` are copied and verified. Those prerequisite fixes are not reintroduced as independent owners here.

The optional `--image-input archive` recipe checks the receipt-bound archive/manifest and the small admission inputs without rehashing all of `app/`. Docker copies the archive, checks its exact SHA-256 inside the build, and only then extracts it. The existing finalizer remains the single lifecycle owner. Directory recipes and full-inventory verification remain the defaults.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev. Relative to main, this adds no cache, competing operation-report owner, dependency, lockfile or tool pin. Net production growth remains 176 lines. The scoped allocation is still exactly **140** for the **+140** test-line delta; the shared scalar was not changed.

## Evidence

- Published head `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a` preserves tested commit `63593cf109f5737ed238603dec0f1c73d583553c` and tree `dcc577f3532a53cb300ee278b730e4947adc7060`. The exact prerequisite was merged history-preservingly in `aa52afa9975e8cfe3b8eecaec51bf3418a3ae214`. Four squash-lineage conflicts were then resolved against main only after proving all four main-side blobs equal the reviewed prerequisite. No rebase or age-only refresh was performed.
- **53 relevant tests have passing main-context evidence:** 32 composition, 14 bundled-link helper, 4 offline dependency-planner and 3 Docker-digest tests. The first main-context run exposed a test-fixture clone that traversed unavailable unrelated history in a partial checkout. The fixture now clones the real runtime commit at depth one; that case and the four planner tests passed in a focused 59.19s follow-up, including 41.66s cold worker compilation. Unaffected passing cases were reused rather than blanket-rerun. The complete pre-main integration run also passed all 53 tests in 78.46s.
- Builtin-name admission is exercised through the real composition fixture using an npm package named `fs`. Restoring the old lookup makes composition fail with `openclaw requires fs`; the repair passes while retaining nested versions. The existing implementation-file tamper case still fails with the old copy filter and passes with the repair. Genuine first strict receipts, relocation/tampering, partial-receipt rejection, CLI archive admission and native-finalizer boundaries remain covered.
- Fresh main-relative scripts, tooling-test and extensions-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint reported zero warnings/errors; formatting, normal isolated commit hooks and diff checks passed. Frozen dependencies were reconciled only in the task-owned isolated installation; shared caches were unchanged.
- **Fresh main-relative ratchet passed:** 6,315,807 test lines, ceiling 6,347,775, slack 31,968. The earlier 1,042-line overage was measured on the pre-main snapshot and is not stamped onto this checked main-based tree. No allocation was inflated to hide it.
- Fresh independent local autoreview of the final five-file candidate against main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. The final candidate was committed unchanged. The dirty local ClawSweeper checkout required the documented autoreview route. The [earlier hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188678#issuecomment-6533057882) also found no actionable defects; it is prior-head evidence, not a current-head approval.
- Retained real offline Podman admission proof remains source-bound to the unchanged Dockerfile: the archive-input stage consumed the original archive despite changed `app/` bytes; archive tampering failed checksum verification before extraction. No broad rebuild was repeated solely for metadata or ancestry changes.

<details>
<summary>Retained archive-consumption trace — unchanged Docker stage</summary>

Successful admission and container readback, while mutable `app/` contained different bytes:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: OK
archive bytes consumed; mutable app excluded
```

After changing that archive while retaining the expected digest:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: FAILED
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
```

The maintained build step orders checksum verification before extraction with `&&`; the tampered build exited 1. This is archive admission proof, not full release-image qualification.

</details>

**Current-head CI is green:** the [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41148539662/job/124382281583) passed for `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a`; final readback found no failed or running checks. Full release-image acceptance remains target-owned. Receipts retain `compositionOnly: true`, ABI/libc `requires-target-acceptance`, and lifecycle `target-required`. No live cloud operations were performed.

## User Impact

title: fix(skills): selected project skills are missing from the $ picker and slash commands
body:
Related: #187813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills from a selected project's `skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are missing from the Control UI `$` picker and slash commands, both in the New session composer and in existing project sessions, even though the agent's runtime skill catalog includes them.

## User Impact

User impact: in the New session composer, selecting a registered project shows that project's eligible skills in `$` and `/`, switching projects or back to the agent workspace replaces the list, and a picked project skill is actually invoked on the first turn. Existing project sessions (Control UI, and channel sessions such as Telegram) list and invoke their project skills too. Precedence, allowlists, eligibility and sandbox containment are unchanged; clients that could not create a session in a project never see its skills.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New session preview:** `commands.list` accepts an optional `projectId` (not combined with `sessionKey`). The Gateway resolves it through the project registry, admits the root with the same session-creation authorization and sandbox containment as `sessions.create`, repeats that admission right before responding, and passes the root to the existing skill loader as the execution root. The composer sends its selected project; the UI command cache and stale-request ownership are keyed by project, and a pending slash refresh is retired when agent, draft or project changes.
- **Invocation:** reply-path consumers (explicit `$` references, slash and tool dispatch) derive the session's execution skill root with the same resolver as the runtime catalog, so a listed project skill is also invocable.
- **Existing sessions:** a session with an execution root (spawned cwd or managed worktree) reads its own `commands.list` instead of the agent-scoped startup command catalog; sessions without a project keep the startup catalog. A republished catalog retires the session's cached copy.
- **File host:** one shared resolver keeps registered and cloned project roots Gateway-owned through preview, creation, invocation and the runtime snapshot, including for agents whose workspace is served by a paired node (File Transfer). The `workspace:<agent>` pseudo-project keeps the agent workspace's own host, using the registry's source classification.

Overlap: #187869 by @yy19971996 independently makes the same session invocation-root change in `chat-commands.ts`; this PR includes it because the preview-to-invocation flow needs it, and uses the same option names so either PR rebases cleanly onto the other. Credit to @yy19971996 for that work. #155867 is untouched.

## Evidence

Control UI New session with project **alpha** selected — both project roots listed:

![New session $ picker with project alpha selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/595a6a70-3327-4437-a45f-c24f2b47ac1a)

After switching to project **beta** — alpha entries gone:

![New session $ picker after switching to project beta](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44910848-9df9-493b-a4cd-75a196247f62)

Back to the agent workspace — project entries gone:

![New session $ picker back on the agent workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ddac3a-3606-4640-9673-1e4c9e68e3ce)

Existing alpha session `$` picker:

![Existing alpha session $ picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2925aaff-bfee-4799-9f0a-18b3d59502c3)

Project tool-dispatch slash command answered without a model turn:

![Project tool-dispatch slash command reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/866d1e9c-df09-4e57-8b88-7a963a390bb8)

Cache retirement in the shipped Control UI (project session, Library activation succeeds, metadata refresh fails at the transport, a stale in-flight catalog read is released): reopening `$` fetches the fresh catalog once and shows the new pin, and an unrelated session keeps its cached catalog:

![Project session $ after Library activation shows the fresh pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6112db15-87aa-4d22-8846-f8d39c245aa3)

![Unrelated session $ still served from its own cached catalog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3daff8ae-14f8-4877-9829-de357640839a)

- Focused unit/boundary suites: 250 passed across command discovery, the `commands.list` handler, protocol, runtime preparation and the New session/chat composer, plus the affected re-runs for each later change. Each fix has a regression that fails with the fix reverted, including a new one for invalidating every cached command variant of a session (Library activation, failed metadata refresh, late in-flight read, unrelated session unaffected).
- Real Control UI + Gateway flow (isolated Gateway, synthetic fixtures, fixture model): render and select both project roots, switch projects and back to the workspace, start a session and confirm the first turn carries the explicit skill instruction, open `$` in the created session, and run a project `command-dispatch: tool` slash command without a model turn.
- Shipped Control UI cache scenario (production bundle, visible Library controls, transport-level failures at a mock Gateway): see the screenshots above.
- Authority (real Gateway, trusted-proxy identities, `gateway.roles`, synthetic projects): `commands.list` with a `projectId` returned the project's skills to an administrator and to a member whose role allows the agent. A device granted only `operator.read`, and a role whose agents exclude the target agent, received only the agent catalog. While a slow discovery was in flight, removing the project returned `UNAVAILABLE` ("Project access changed while preparing its commands"), a config patch removing the role's agent access returned `UNAVAILABLE`, and revoking the operator's role closed the connection before any response; no project skills were disclosed. Tightening the agent's sandbox mode mid-discovery was not exercised because that setting requires a Gateway restart.

The no-Gateway-path-read claim rests on the node read policy and the observed catalogs, not a per-request node trace.

title: feat: build Linux images from offline runtime packages
body:
Related: #188651 (landed prerequisite); #188678 (qualified-reuse follow-on). This PR targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Release tooling needs to turn a portable OpenClaw package and qualified Linux dependencies into installed image assets without rebuilding the package or resolving dependencies online.

## User Impact

Operators can compose and verify Linux/x64 image inputs offline while preserving bundled payloads and importer-relative dependency versions. The default Docker source-build route remains unchanged.

**This is composition, not Linux runtime qualification.** ABI/libc acceptance, entrypoint, provider identity, and runtime-export checks remain target requirements. The installed-assets stage finalizes without networking; shared later image stages can still require network access for OS/operator tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing archive inspector, installed-dependency planner, package lifecycle, and Docker graph rather than introduce another installer. Full input/output inventories bind the handoff, portable bundles retain their bytes, and promoted plugin dependencies use their declared importer instead of unrelated root development packages. Root production dependencies keep root ownership. Private implementation trees inside dependency packages are preserved while installed dependency placement remains planner-owned.

The shared resolver distinguishes declared npm packages from identically named Node builtins, including ancestor deduplication. Codex's fs-safe importer is aligned with the root's already-approved 0.26.15 pin. Qualified reuse and archive-bound optimization remain separate in #188678; this does not import the runtime-artifact API feature.

Net growth against integrated main `65acdfd629e3555f3c876e3fe887d548633e1863` is 1,127 non-test lines (including documentation/configuration) and 833 test lines. Separate allocations cover 798 composition/archive/ownership/tamper/lifecycle/digest lines and exactly 35 shared resolver regression lines. Existing baseline debt and the shared scalar are unchanged.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev.

## Evidence

- History-preserving main integration in `d69cf9304cd093585bdf7fb006f2b6922d90e41b` retained both executable-entry declaration sets. Subsequent cherry-picks import only reviewed shared fixes `d4e71ba4a3154f0d3a2e45ff9d7a018bfbbdce30` and `79daa9c3c9563b43f6538dae0faf90a85bc59c56`; their six resulting file blobs match exactly. Reviewed integration head: `ce39deacdc7fa0fbabaeb241924be495bb4525ab`.
- **221 tests across seven affected files passed** after integration in secretless, network-disabled Linux isolation (179.09s): shared bundled links, offline/bootstrap artifacts, composition, tarball inspection, Docker digest classification, and plugin manifest contracts. This includes relocated builtin-name package cycles, nested versions, source-link preservation, missing-package/source-boundary guards, importer ownership, and the real native-prebuild/finalizer boundary.
- Frozen dependency reconciliation passed all 1,727 supply-chain entries. Codex resolves fs-safe 0.26.15; Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 remain unchanged. Tooling-test, composition, and affected Gateway-test typechecks; targeted lint/format; the direct dependency pin guard; and diff checks passed.

title: feat: export and install offline worker runtime artifacts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Image-preparation tools need a supported way to export the installed OpenClaw worker runtime and install transferred archives without enrolling a node. Prerequisite #188651 is merged; this PR targets main.

## User Impact

Tool authors can use `openclaw/runtime-artifacts` to qualify bundled plugins and export canonical offline node/worker archives. Crabbox's lazy CLI API installs verified local archives without a logical lease, forwarded credentials, npm, lifecycle scripts, or plugin activation. Bundle enrollment needs matching Node and tar; explicit npm installations and repository setup retain npm/npx/Corepack where applicable. Existing remote npm installations retain their lock/reuse behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public entrypoint composes existing artifact producers, joins both before cleanup, and returns build, archive and digest identities. Bundled qualification uses a detached inspection registry. Local transfer is an adapter in the existing installer, not a second installer. Only `./runtime-artifacts` is added to package exports; declarations and documentation are included.

History-preserving integration retains upstream root/Codex fs-safe 0.27.0 and the source-inspection worker-boundary fix in #188870. The lock was regenerated with pinned pnpm; dependency graph and integrity data match upstream, with canonical ordering differences only. The `/node-runtime-dependencies/` artifact ignore and accurate troubleshooting prerequisites are restored. Read-only cache verification remains separate in #188671.

## Evidence

### Current source, tests and review

- Published head **`ee479a542b773fead85d101d915f8b21d3521853`** has reviewed tree **`d175c65ee19fcaaf087c1f49e808efac8916c38f`**. Authored source merge **`842de317b317a604492c4a5d10277e8a6d28f5fa`** preserves parents `ef8db05f` and main `ece4ca85af0e0ffa7cc619522b9e8b7e40b08da9`.
- Both conflicts retain upstream repairs: the shared Gateway logger fixture exactly matches main; rollout tests preserve upstream targeted notification delivery and final no-read assertion, plus coarse directory timestamps, warm-cache reuse and controlled watcher-loss coverage. Real rename/unlink and exact membership oracles remain. No production scanner fence, sleep or weaker assertion was added.
- **60 focused tests pass**: API 5, Gateway scope consumers 30, Workboard 2, rollout 20 and offline installer 3 (126.24s wrapper). Withholding only the three final notifications fails the original membership oracle; restored source passes. This is controlled notification evidence, not an observed kernel-watcher cause.
- Targeted types, six-file type-aware lint (293 rules; zero warnings/errors), formatting, whitespace checks and normal hooks pass. Exact accounting: **6,321,781 / 6,352,142**. Rollout allocation is **16** net lines beyond integrated upstream; API **332** and Workboard **7** remain unchanged. No baseline, scalar or checker waiver.
- Fresh independent **P0–P3 autoreview is scoped-clean** for the complete 22-file delta against `ece4ca85`, with 13 complete unchanged owners. No actionable findings; final source verification passed, and the committed tree matches the reviewed staged tree.

### Canonical package build and recovery

- Linux x64 / Node 24.22.1, source **`842de317b317a604492c4a5d10277e8a6d28f5fa`**, actual build **`2026.10.9-842de317b317-2026-10-31T04-58-16.446Z`**.
- Full maintained runtime-only selected-Codex build completed in **6m 38s**, including UI, runtime postbuild, stamps and CLI metadata. A Gateway restart interrupted packaging afterward. Source, clean-input stamps and process settlement were verified; canonical postpack restoration reconciled the interruption. Supported package-only continuation reused the completed build without skipping any package checks.
- Canonical packaging passed in **98.34s**; tar preflight/extraction, npm 11.19.1 finished-archive inventory and distribution import graph all passed (**39s** integrity check). Public registry metadata and lock-pinned native input preparation used secretless isolation. Shared dependency installs were not modified.
- Canonical tarball: SHA-256 **`17cc2b32561fd72f3a1fa817d9817c55bb23ddf7f3409ac5797b9bdd5f54fb12`**, **111,178,480 bytes**.

### Actual installed-package public API boundary

- The canonical tarball was installed into a **fresh standalone npm consumer**, with normal preinstall/postinstall lifecycle and declared dependencies (**14.21s**). Its npm lock's tarball integrity matches the canonical finished-archive receipt. Raw extraction alone lacks ordinary npm dependencies; that setup failure is not counted as a product failure or successful proof.
- The proof imports bare **`openclaw/runtime-artifacts`** from that installed consumer and asserts its resolved URL is inside the installed package. Both qualification and export receive the real installed package root—not the source checkout. The installer is imported from the **same installed package's** `dist/extensions/crabbox/cli-runtime-api.js`; no descendant verifier code participates.
- With networking disabled, plugins-disabled and Codex-enabled selections each qualified and exported bundle-mode node/worker archives, then installed into fresh worker homes. Both real CLIs printed **`OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (842de31)`**. Installed agent schema **39**, fs-safe **0.27.0**, manifest digest and worker archive digest matched receipts. Installation plus CLI: **9.485s / 8.851s**; complete installed-package round trips: **97.83s**.
- The canonical input already bundles Codex, so the two selection receipts have different `enabledPluginIds` but identical exported node bytes. This proves both configuration paths; it does not claim a minimal Codex-free distribution.
- No enrollment state, logical lease, forwarded credentials or cloud allocation. Fresh receiver homes and owned build namespaces were removed. The installed producer and immutable exports are retained for the separate verifier lane.

<details>
<summary>Installed-package export identities</summary>

- Node archive, both selections: `b2c9a747f20d1d0f940e2836aef1d57f93ee8f812e64964fd12b9734d96f0c1b` — 293,213,073 bytes.
- Node manifest: `32efb5e97a141773a7fea076660c5065863bb7b4f3579ef0c0e4b0ef33110106`.
- Worker archive: `8d1d25c625cb31392ae493dfea1f3782084a90ba1a0e23f20b1194868024fbe1` — 22,863,074 bytes.

</details>

### Separate source-dist and earlier evidence

- The earlier **90.25s source-dist** export/install run remains valid separate evidence: its producer was the built checkout, not the npm-installed canonical package. Its node archive hashes (`a93c96e4…` core, `339ff4c3…` Codex) are not substituted for the installed-package exports above.
- Prior `49968f5` and `d4b533` build evidence retains its original identity. Source `49968f5` passed 78 focused tests. Upstream #188870 repaired the generated worker import boundary without weakening its guard; the original case ran and passed, while the earlier all-skipped run was not passing proof. The cross-test-contamination claim remains withdrawn.
- [CI job 124416178578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160183562/job/124416178578) reproduced on `9d193015` as **2 failed / 283 passed**. The coordinated owner fixture repair from `5b08bece` made the identical eight-file invocation pass **285/285**. Main now supplies the complete logger; this PR retains diagnostics save/enable/restore and the original closure/admission/card-list assertions.

### Scope and separate verifier

- Current-head CI and native landing remain maintainer-owned. No manual hosted CI rerun or merge was performed by this session.
- Separate #188671 owns read-only verification. The installed-package export set above is the final artifact handoff for its current-source no-effect controls. This PR's successful installation does not substitute for that verifier proof.
- Full release/declaration packaging, live Codex execution, Azure, macOS and Windows remain separate proof. Packaging here is runtime-only. Archive/manifest identity does not certify every installed payload byte or grant live execution authority.

title: fix: keep older commentary before unrelated chat input
body:
Closes #188641

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: older commentary can appear below an unrelated user message when its original prompt is outside the loaded history page.

## User Impact

User impact: retained progress stays with its original conversation turn instead of looking like a response to a newer request. This changes presentation only; it does not rewrite saved history or require configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recover the missing input boundary from retained output belonging to the same run. Saved-stream materialization and the live renderer share that recovery decision; the renderer preserves its existing steering, independent-turn, and forwarded-activity rules. Genuinely unanchored activity keeps its existing fallback. A run's own projected output does not become a recovered ceiling, keeping continued replies and their working indicator in the same run frame.

The patch changes only two production files. Added tests, their allocation record, and newly added code comments were removed at the requester's direction; existing tests are unchanged.

## Evidence

[Before/after browser screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188658#issuecomment-6532221191).

- Chromium with the production UI and mocked Gateway startup/preamble replay: full-window control unchanged; paged history changed from **answer → unrelated prompt → old commentary** to **old commentary → answer → unrelated prompt**. Saved messages remained ordered; no browser errors. No browser state was assigned directly.
- Construction-time proof: reproduced the production-function defect on base `7d9677ce36db4aeea2ce36a3bb78588829e80933`; temporary materializer and live-renderer regressions failed before their fixes and passed afterward. Independent review through P2 identified an independent-turn boundary issue, which was reproduced, fixed, and reviewed clean. Those temporary tests are not retained in this PR.
- After the requested cleanup, five existing suites passed **201/201 tests**. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, formatting, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- CI regression: [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41120933487/job/124287655261) exposed an existing continued-answer frame test failure on `b628e2effbbbe2c3cb845b60ec0b1f1a8e5c997a`. Recovered bounds incorrectly stopped at the same run's native projected tool-result boundary, splitting its working frame. The repair excludes same-run messages from that ceiling.
- After the CI repair, four existing suites passed **158/158 tests**, including all 38 cases in `chat-transcript-message-index.test.ts`. Standalone checks passed for original materializer/live paged-input ordering, independent notice/automation boundaries, and the run's own projected boundary. UI typecheck, oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed; fresh independent review through P2 was clean. No tests or comments were added for this repair.

Limitations: the browser proof uses deterministic Gateway fixtures, not a live model. The exact event sequence from the originally affected private tab remains unconfirmed. No live Gateway installation was changed for proof.

Thanks @hannesrudolph for the report and deterministic reproduction.

title: feat(workers): preserve repository authority during dispatch and recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional repository policies need caller-bound admission throughout worker preparation, checkout, and authenticated recovery, whether placement begins from chat or session creation and regardless of GitHub credential type.

## User Impact

Deployments opt in with `gateway.repositoryIntegration`. Missing or revoked admission refuses worker source access; omitting the integration preserves native behavior. Required repository placement retains the original session-creation caller after acknowledgment. Automatic required placement does not request setup scripts, consistent with its existing worktree behavior.

Native owners retain credential issuance, managed-profile reading/rotation, and cleanup. The feature introduces no schema or checkpoint-format migration; the integrated upstream base includes agent schema 39. **Fresh installed schema-25→39 configuration/checkpoint preservation passed on the published source**, using the maintained private runtime-package profile described below. This is offline checkpoint recovery, not worker reconnection or full release-distribution acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

One lifetime-bound integration owner supplies policy; existing identity, dispatch, and worker owners enforce it. Managed PAT/OAuth profiles enter policy admission before refresh/profile reads without asking a plugin for their bearer. Native/App paths retain their issuer and guarded return value. Dispatch forwards the original reader; source owners compose caller, policy, and dispatch lifetime checks. The redundant reader wrapper was deleted.

Session creation passes its native caller-bound reader through an internal preparation option. Existing retention and source-custody owners retain post-acknowledgment work. No chat admission is fabricated, and no wire field or additional issuer is introduced. Host credential callbacks remain excluded from node transport.

Published head `b062896364982a2838139025c0497d6e5bfb7712` has the exact source tree of tested candidate `b4358540899f6cbad387b302ae7dd35b88179ede`: `2b96a7360603b237e4d4b3facbaff778c25f3cdf`. History is preserved, including exact main `510e1687e965c1a5e2c372f6622704c88448fb5b` and #188922. The sole current-main conflict retains the canonical upstream logger. Reviewed fixture correction `1420553393074da1a7434cb06011be929d9a6032` preserves required shutdown joins and real connection-identity resolution. No guard, timeout, or test-line budget was relaxed; shared Workboard diagnostics credit is not duplicated.

## Evidence

- **Published-source installed upgrade:** the real `v2026.10.9` baseline (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`) produced the repository session and revision-3 checkpoint through actual dispatch/editor RPCs. Its preserved pre-Doctor snapshot was restored into an isolated copy with exact hashes and database integrity checks: agent schema 25, global schema 20. The genuine stable package was installed and its CLI version checked, then the exact b062 candidate installed over the same prefix/config/state with networking disabled. Installed `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check --non-interactive` created backups and migrated agent 25→39 and global 20→36. Both resulting database versions were independently read back.
- **Preservation oracles:** Gateway, model, and plugin configuration remained equal; agent configuration differed only by the existing heartbeat migration, whose disabled job was verified through `cron.list`. All 14 plugins observed active in the baseline remained active through actual `plugins.list` RPC. Session identity and the exact repository/base/manifest/checkpoint reference and revision survived. With zero connected nodes and failed/offline placement, public `sessions.files.get` returned the original edited bytes, absent from the Git base. SHA-256 remained `823ca7b910bb25c9299516a968a823fb1b06f20a10cb685c33e2cd8ee66133cd`. This proves stored-checkpoint preservation and offline reads, **not active-worker recovery, reconnection, or move-to-Gateway behavior**.
- **Package scope and integrity:** the maintained packer built fresh with `--runtime-only --bundle-plugin codex`; no partial-build `--skip-build` was used. This private profile retains runtime CLI/Doctor, core plugins, configured Codex, and schema metadata while omitting SDK declaration promises and unrelated isolated external-plugin builds. Canonical inventory, normalization, and tarball-integrity checks passed. Installed build identity is `2026.10.9-b06289636498-2026-10-31T05-24-57.798Z`; package manifest declares agent 39/global 36. Tarball SHA-256: `01d5ceead1f6955103033e3dbc04fd6e314c41017f7b721c2b7b68d5227451c7`. Proof receipt SHA-256: `6084cc8b1d7ec77573948c86f28a955422e3ef91c158d3c83d1c06b5bbc3ec09`. This is not complete release-distribution or SDK/declaration acceptance.
- **Isolation and recovery:** public-registry preparation used task-owned caches and a separate dependency prefix. Actual stable/candidate installation, Doctor, Gateway, and RPC acceptance ran offline in disposable Node 24.22.1 containers with synthetic credentials and a TLS-validating local GitHub/Git fixture. An initial offline cache miss was retained, then the independently prepared cache was used for the complete offline install-over. The earlier full-distribution attempt timed out after 900 seconds. A later retained build lock was released only after documented descendant/namespace-custody verification; normal locking and signature/integrity checks remained enabled. All owned test containers and Gateway processes are stopped, build ownership released, and source checkouts clean. No live Gateway, shared dependency install, cloud allocation, or real credential setup was changed.
- **Current boundary proof:** all five actual `sessions.create` controls and both diagnostic-enabled Workboard terminal hooks passed on b435, whose source tree exactly matches b062. The creation path exercises `handleGatewayRequest` → required preparation → coordinator → native dispatch/Git/checkpoint effects after the RPC ACK, plus revoked policy, changed caller scope, replaced source, and targeted controller Stop. This is in-process RPC proof, not WebSocket/model proof; Stop coverage uses the real controller owner, not public `sessions.abort`.
- **Startup CI repair:** the exact failing [compact-small20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161544452/job/124420328494) group reproduced one failure, 47 passes, and one skip on pinned Bun. The fixture still expected early release before the intentional required-join repair in #188920. Corrected assertions retain HTTP resources and keep rollback unsettled until cleanup is released. The same group then passed 48 tests with one existing skip. Restoring the old shutdown owner makes the new held-process assertion fail. Four shutdown controls also passed. After the #188922 integration, all 12 startup and five creation tests passed together.
- **Handshake CI repair:** [compact-small2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161544452/job/124420325618) exposed a fixture mock missing `resolveRepositoryConnectionIdentity`, causing actual hello to return `UNAVAILABLE`. The partial mock retains both native identity resolvers and mocks only remote enrichment. ## What Problem This Solves

Cloud workers using bundle installation still need registry access to assemble their node runtime on the destination.

## User Impact

Bundle profiles install preassembled runtime dependencies without invoking npm or package lifecycle scripts. Explicit npm profiles retain destination-native installation, project locks, fallback, and reuse.

Cross-platform bundle deployments must prepare matching OS/CPU dependency inputs; a missing target fails with a preparation hint instead of silently falling back to npm. Cached-runtime verification pins the manifest and build/platform identity and probes the CLI; it does **not** hash every installed payload file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical producer packages the installed dependency graph and qualified target inputs, keeping selected plugin dependencies at their installation owner. Enrollment verifies and extracts authenticated archives into private staging before publication. Producer caches distinguish execution mode and installation mode. Only bundle runtime enrollment uses Node-only prerequisites: repository seed/setup and npm enrollment retain npm, npx, and Corepack preparation, preserving the original contract from #170796.

This is the first runtime slice of the requested packaging split. Public artifact APIs, read-only cache verification, and Linux composition remain separate dependent changes. Existing npm dependency ownership, locks, credential isolation, and timing behavior are preserved. Package input validation is shared with the dependency collector; no second installer, durable state owner, database schema change, or profile migration was introduced.

## Evidence

title: fix: scheduled runs fail after unrelated channel reloads
body:
Related: #188530 covers caller-turn custody separately; this change does not modify that boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled work failing after unrelated channel configuration reloads, and known pre-effect policy refusals stranding an occurrence until a later slot.

## User Impact

Unrelated channel reloads leave valid scheduled work active. Relevant policy changes can re-admit genuinely unstarted work under fresh authority. Work that may already have performed effects, including model-resolution hooks, is not replayed by this policy retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled events compare effective policy using canonical runtime/source snapshots for the selected agent, trusted creator and delivery channels, including shared channel policy and activation. Live source/job and per-effect authority checks remain. The existing event owner retains the same occurrence, with its existing two-readmission limit and 100/200 ms backoff. A typed lifecycle refusal before operation acquisition returns the existing mailbox receipt to the existing FIFO drain.

Execution and registered hook dispatch consume existing custody. This includes `before_model_resolve`, the only registered hook dispatched by the logical entry/setup modules before native candidate preparation, alongside the existing bootstrap and reply-hook barriers. Treating a registered model hook as possible work conservatively gives up policy retry even if that handler happened to be pure. No hook-runner semantics, second retry queue, persistence, configuration option or FIFO/coalescing behavior changed.

## Evidence

- Seven original regressions are red on integrated main `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1` and green with R6. The committed registered-hook regression is red on incoming `67533beaef03f344b1386afa081c1b5096919afa`, observing two persisted filesystem appends. Whole-PR test lines remain **−1**; all cases remain, and a redundant fixture setup readback is still covered before effect and after settlement.
- Targeted format, typecheck and correction-file lint pass. Full-PR local lint retains the handoff `max-lines` finding: 735/700, with unmodified integrated main also above the cap at 712/700. The existing GitHub Actions advisory size policy is unchanged; no cap, baseline or suppression changed. Focused suites used the pinned CI Bun runtime in isolated, network-disabled rootless Podman, limited to 4 CPUs/8 GiB and one test worker.

It assessed source and did not independently execute tests. The native correction review resolves `R6-HOOK-REPLAY` and retains the incoming NEEDS WORK evidence.

title: fix(macos): preserve shortcuts pressed while the dashboard opens
body:
Closes #187486

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes New Session and Command Palette shortcuts silently disappearing when pressed while the macOS dashboard is opening.

## User Impact

With the updated Mac app and Control UI, the first ⌘N or ⌘K waits for the dashboard's listeners instead of requiring another keypress. Older shared-credential UI bundles retain their historical document-load delivery and open-only search fallback; this does not retroactively repair delayed startup in already-built older bundles.

**Validation status:** The native delayed-listener regression is red on the comparison base and green on this exact head. A newly supplied November 1 packaged-app trace covers actual guest ⌘K during an induced startup delay, followed by the native event and visible palette after import of the current UI. This is supplied Mac-run evidence, not a new native run by the publisher, and the six-second delay is test-only. The required CI gate and completed Periphery report builds passed; inherited local matrix/SwiftLint failures remain disclosed below. The completed November 1 exact-head review inspected the supplied startup captures and public observer fixture, accepted them as sufficient shipped-entry-point proof, and reports no actionable findings. The code and head remain unchanged; human maintainer review and any merge decision remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dashboard controller remains the ordered command-queue owner, and the shell remains the listener-readiness owner. The HTML boot script declares pending readiness before deferred startup; native dispatch observes readiness for every authentication mode. An absent protocol is accepted only for legacy non-browser-identity documents, never an explicit false value. No retry timer, second queue, or replay mechanism was added.

The existing 120-second document-load timeout throws; it is not a delivery fallback. Legacy compatibility uses the explicit undefined-only readiness probe and the existing cancelable-toggle/open-search fallback.

## Evidence

Tested head: 6ddf6c2900bb885d519eb849bf2cd2c48806564b.
Comparison base for native red proof: c0c068e1ecd9ec78a75ad6847e032f4d0f5b1241.

### Packaged-app startup trace — induced delay (November 1)

[Capture, fixture, and provenance supplied by @PollyBot13](https://gist.github.com/PollyBot13/2e4a03665ea2001157c9d2ede5ba0ec8), also linked in the [public proof supplement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188646#issuecomment-6556083073). The supplied run used the unmodified packaged app built from the tested head in a credentialless macOS 26.6.2 Tart guest and a loopback test Gateway.

Only a copied UI HTML module entry was replaced with a test fixture that waits six seconds before importing the reported byte-identical current UI module. **This is a deliberately induced startup interval, not a naturally observed six-second boot and not a production source change.** The fixture observes native events and polls readiness; it does not synthesize events, call preventDefault, or assign readiness.

The supplier reports closing the dashboard and delivering actual guest ⌘K with the packaged app foreground. The pending frame shows the reopened dashboard still loading with readiness=false; the delivered frame shows the command palette open after UI import. The visible overlay records:

| Observation | Time relative to copied HTML fixture |
| --- | ---: |
| HTML readiness=false | 0 ms |
| Begin importing current UI module | 6005 ms |
| Native toggle-search event observed (overlay label: native-command-palette) | 6296 ms |
| Poll observes shell readiness=true | 6308 ms |

**Sampling limit:** Readiness is polled every 20 ms. The sampled ready=true row appearing 12 ms after the event is not evidence that dispatch preceded the actual readiness assignment. No precise key-down timestamp is claimed. This visual startup trace is for ⌘K; the existing native regression covers both commands and the authentication matrix, while the earlier loaded-app captures cover ⌘N/⌘K with current and older UI bundles.

**Pending — dashboard reopened, UI import held, readiness=false**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture with import delayed and readiness false](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fa80f44-d6ed-4462-8c51-ca10c1bb751a)

**Delivered — current UI imported, native event recorded, command palette visible**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture after import with native palette event and visible palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d726217-8c8d-43b0-9696-4a1e3ae629fb)

<details>
<summary>Capture provenance and artifact verification</summary>

Execution and binary-identity measurements are supplied provenance, not a publisher-run native reproduction. The record identifies packaged executable SHA-256 3a2e8dbf17495e0e0e7c538477bd0a11be6a7c3850ea2cf9e1fe4577d3f0c462 and original current UI index SHA-256 670eab030f346e3931a4b4874abc279179fd891e848472ec885b7879c1b39b72; the current JS module was reported byte-identical. Those binaries are not included in this packet for independent comparison here.

The five manifest entries in pr188646-roboclaw-proof-handoff-20261101.zip were verified; archive SHA-256 471a5e8d45303902a5104715d4b67d36b7b0062c34b76228532fec9a541907d7. The public gist's README, two SVGs, and delayed-boot.js were fetched and matched the supplied packet byte-for-byte. The fixture was inspected as source, not executed here. Both SVGs contain only the original embedded PNG; those PNG bytes were extracted unchanged, visually inspected for sensitive content, and attached above. The screenshot overlay is part of the supplied live capture, not a new annotation added during publication.

</details>

### Native execution

Requester-supplied evidence from a separate credentialless Tart macOS VM: macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4, Node 26.12.1. The logs were inspected here, not rerun on this Linux host.

title: fix(workers): retain runtime chunks loaded through optional aliases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A worker bootstrap archive can omit a required runtime chunk when it is loaded through an optional aliased loader with a literal template path.

## User Impact

Extracted worker runtimes keep these required chunks and start successfully. Ordinary relative path arguments do not become mandatory imports. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing bounded distribution scan to collect literal-call candidates for conservative chunk retention, removing the unused Node-loader detection callback and the second root-bundle scope scan. Nested dependency scanning and strict required-import validation retain their existing owners.

The deliberate tradeoff is conservative retention: an ordinary call referencing an existing local file may keep an extra chunk. It does not make missing ordinary path arguments fail archive creation. This is the standalone scanner slice of the runtime-packaging work, not the offline installer.

## Evidence

- Secretless Linux/Node 24.22.1: 36 bootstrap artifact tests and 28 package-scanner tests pass, 9.60 seconds total through the repository runner. The regression executes the extracted archive, not just a helper.
- With the original bootstrap resolver from base `1bdc2908bce9c23766307aee629c006062b16af2`, the new optional-loader regression fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the omitted chunk. With this change it passes. Existing malformed-ownership, missing-import, ordinary require, and path-containment cases remain covered.
- Targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors. Tooling and Gateway-other test typecheck leaves, formatting, normal commit hooks, and `git diff --check` pass. Full distribution build and broad CI remain PR-CI proof; no measured startup-speed claim is made.
- Independent autoreview covered P0–P3 over base `1bdc2908bce9c23766307aee629c006062b16af2` to the final candidate committed as `b0fcfc106f20d6199fe38136e73b01c2fca47bb2`: scoped-clean, with no remaining findings.
- Simplification removes the superseded detection API; net production growth is one line. Regression growth is 17 lines with a scoped allocation. CI seconds pending.

Source work: @galiniliev’s [runtime-packaging commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/0b084c6aabe75c24c914b7a8f6fec329b83c381f).

title: feat: prepare selected Linux Sandbox disks without snapshots
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected Linux Azure Sandbox disks cannot be used for prepared workers when snapshot capture is disabled.

## User Impact

Users can select `settings.azureSandboxDiskId` on an `azure-sandbox` profile and prepare its project before enrollment with `warmImage: false`, provided a Linux target and machine class are selected. The machine class may come from the profile or placement; original profile settings still supply the idle timeout for activation-based refill. Existing profiles and image keys without a selected disk are unchanged. This does not introduce retained-disk recovery, snapshot receipts, or changes to disk permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the provider’s existing preparation eligibility owner for both discovery and provisioning, validate and forward the selected disk, include it in preparation identity, and retain the configured prepared-worker idle timeout. No new preparation manager, persistence schema, or recovery path is added.

Source implementation by @galiniliev, extracted from `63fda88754e` with the required selected-disk parser/allocation and provisioning prerequisites from `7d630e25`.

## Evidence

- **Placement-sizing regression:** the final JSON-valid classless fixture fails on published head `1d5e73655e3256480e3986c6a0fab6d51d51fbf1`: the idle callback returns `undefined` instead of `3600000` (1 failed, 13 passed; 14.88 s wrapper wall time). On repair head `728476bf495eff394b6d2c71a4a969049f8b21db`, all 14 prepared-image cases pass (15.02 s wrapper wall time). Configured and placement sizing both exercise real provider preparation before enrollment, selected-disk allocation, idle policy, disjoint disk identity, and no snapshot capture. Missing effective class and non-Linux preparation remain ineligible.
- **Consumer proof:** 97 additional unchanged provider, profile, and Gateway prepared-pool-maintenance cases passed; 111 relevant tests total. The four-suite run took 91.64 s including cold compiled-worker preparation, and the final changed suite was replayed after correcting the fixture to omit class rather than store an undefined JSON value. Its test-case time was 5.255 s, mostly existing custody cases; configured/placement selected-disk cases took 34/9 ms. [Current-head CI and applicable security requirements passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41125448438). Per-file CI seconds were not separately measured.
- **Static checks:** final targeted typecheck, type-aware lint (0 warnings/errors), formatter, normal commit hooks, documentation discovery, and `git diff --check` passed. One SDK declaration-preparation attempt exited 13 with an unsettled top-level await; a bounded isolated retry completed. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recent-message previews in the macOS menu stay on “Loading preview…” or show old messages when a session submenu is reused.

## User Impact

User impact: reopening can retry a cancelled preview without reconnecting the Gateway. Fresh cached messages are projected immediately; expired previews show Loading while the existing asynchronous load refreshes both retained views. **Open for maintainer review; current-head native compilation and all 20 focused tests passed. New supplied interactive proof shows cancellation/reopen recovery and expired-cache Loading → recovery in the unmodified final-head debug app, including compact and expanded previews.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the submenu, hosted views, existing cache, and one cancellable load per submenu. The latest supplied candidate makes the existing UI-only cache/loader main-actor owned so configuration can synchronously project fresh cached content or Loading before menu tracking. Network requests remain asynchronous; the existing limiter, timeout, cancellation checks, and Gateway/session ownership remain intact. No polling or additional cache implementation.

The [public proof record and five original captures](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/ddf3f53a5e5841a3d3baab233168c96787520baf/README.md), also attributed in the [requester's PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188635#issuecomment-6559951418), address the interaction gap identified in revision 4. title: improve(test): speed up installed Gateway benchmark tests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed-package benchmark tests spend most of their time repeatedly preparing the benchmark CLI.

## User Impact

Faster test feedback, with no product behavior change. This is the scoped test-health optimization requested by Peter Steinberger.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `runNodeScript` worker-argument callback instead of hardcoding the TSX preload. The selected executable stays the same: Bun executes TypeScript natively, and Node receives the helper-owned TypeScript loader with its normal private transform cache. All fixture runtime state remains independent.

The real benchmark CLI, production diagnostic functions, native processes, HTTP/WebSocket requests, CPU profiles, and outer settlement still run. No assertions, cases, repetitions, CPU work, deadlines, runner policies, or production code change. The test shrinks by two lines; the effective test-line ceiling decreases by exactly two.

## Evidence

Original benchmark/review base: `6b4a37495dbe5beccdbead95d673cc3d9c2e964a`. Original approved substantive head: `82fde45e900ffff76fd1202e3ee43bf5dc4fcc19`. The mechanical rebase below preserves that test blob and patch exactly.

Three before and three after samples per runtime, using the same checkout, frozen private install, and owned temporary/cache namespace:

```sh
timeout 600 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test test/scripts/bench-gateway-installed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

The Node comparison additionally sets `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` for both sides. Every run passed all 10 Linux cases; the existing Windows-only case remains platform-excluded.

| Runtime | Before wall samples (s) | After wall samples (s) | Median before → after | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default pinned Bun | 55.79, 49.57, 48.25 | 12.93, 12.16, 12.19 | 49.57 → 12.19 s | 75.4% |
| Node | 60.89, 62.37, 62.92 | 34.99, 33.88, 33.07 | 62.37 → 33.88 s | 45.7% |

| Median metric | Bun before → after | Node before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vitest duration | 48.22 → 10.76 s | 60.77 → 32.05 s |
| User CPU | 37.94 → 15.51 s | 58.03 → 44.12 s |
| System CPU | 7.04 → 4.27 s | 7.49 → 6.60 s |
| Maximum RSS | 933.9 → 942.7 MiB | 946.2 → 581.8 MiB |

The unchanged Linux workload creates 13 independent installed-package fixtures, starts 17 controllers, and runs 34 fixture Gateway launches plus 34 descendant forks. Bun's unnecessary TSX preloads fall from 17 to zero. Node retains a TypeScript loader through the shared runtime owner. The default 9-launch cohort, 18-launch ABBA order, acknowledgment/request order, native profile samples/output, failure slots, cancellation liveness, and joined cleanup remain covered by the original assertions. No test helper changed.

Profiling separated imports from child startup: Vitest attributed approximately 99–100% of the original duration to test bodies; the dominant preparation happened inside spawned controllers. With the same pinned Bun executable, profiled CLI help startup measured 3.06 s with forced TSX; native help without the profiler measured 0.25 s. The Node profile attributed 1.58 s to synchronous esbuild work and 0.22 s to module compilation in a 3.04 s controller import. Real profile acquisition retains the original 60 ms CPU workload. Node remains above 30 seconds because this proof still executes the native CLI/process/profile composition.

Additional validation passed:

- 75 owner/sibling tests across `test/helpers/run-node-script.test.ts`, `src/infra/runtime-worker-url.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/bench-gateway-startup.test.ts`.
