- Test-line, line-cap, timeout-race, and mock-factory ratchets. The original scalar accounting was stale. Upstream #188620 corrected that prior census error; the current same-tree base/candidate comparison below supersedes those historical counts. No debt or headroom is invented or defended.
- `pr-simplify`: existing owner reused, no new helpers/cache/state, production delta 0 and test delta −2 lines.
- Original isolated Codex autoreview, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no findings. Reviewed the local delta against the base above, committed unchanged. Helper source SHA-256: `ea4d3415094d50a670f28a1ee092e928a9dbcf7327103014c3a9f909d9a6ef17`. Review snapshot diff SHA-256: `ac72d4e7d0ff7843666de771a837a33d86acbfcc606f0cbd05d75853805410b7`. The reviewer inspected supplied source and did not independently execute tests.

### Mechanical conflict repair and current census

- Parent-approved substantive head `82fde45e900ffff76fd1202e3ee43bf5dc4fcc19` was first mechanically rebased to `a8b489b3bf69c5bac1b6d5289ba2552130ca7275`; r3 refused before dispatch on a new scalar conflict. Parent's 19:18 ruling authorized integrating the already-landed upstream correction. Current repaired head: `9053277dcf2650563eab290d679567ce76b16c9e`, captured current main `d5c013995b33b9879a48a71678fc32be929bcc68`.
- Upstream **#188620** (`6941b99db5206045d1508a9717990f1f80999486`, Peter/GitHub) corrected the prior stale census and excessive scalar cut from #188561, restoring **6,284,794 → 6,287,506** with zero headroom. This external correction is inherited main history, not new funding or a performance/campaign gain claimed by this PR.
- Compare base and candidate in the **same captured current tree** through the native check-only owner: scalar **6,287,506 → 6,287,504**; tracked test LF **6,307,449 → 6,307,447**; effective cap **6,307,449 → 6,307,447**. Exact LF delta **−2** equals effective-cap delta **−2**. Base and candidate slack are both **0**; no inherited debt or slack is added or excessively removed.
- All **152 current-main grants totaling 19,943** remain byte-identical. No pruning, folding, new allocation, minification, or extra funding.
- Exact original approved test blob preserved: `a085c8723dc546867b26f9bcd38f83b31d407687`. Old/new test-patch SHA-256 identical: `743e8686a10d14ce5052418f142d0011f22f6d85ea0b681920d4a71d03bb6573`. No helper, production, assertion, fixture, case, repetition, timeout, or runner policy changed.
- Fresh affected proof passed: **10 target cases on pinned Bun + 10 on Node + 75 owner/sibling cases**, with the existing Windows-only target case platform-excluded. Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap, timeout-race, mock-export, and native same-tree census checks passed.
- Parent approved reuse of the original complete isolated P0–P2 source review and original 3-before/3-after measurements **per runtime** only because the substantive test patch is identical. The **37.38s/75.4% Bun** and **28.49s/45.7% Node** reductions remain observations on the original benchmark snapshot, not new rebase or CI timing claims.
- One leased push published this actual conflict repair after proof. Fresh exact-head CI/security/required reviews were enforced and passed at merge; original-head runs are historical evidence only. No rerun, synthetic push, extra review request, or security waiver.

Discarded attempt: fixture runtime-hash reuse plus a controller bytecode-cache setting produced 53.65, 49.97, and 50.83 s (median 50.83 s versus 49.57 s baseline), so it was removed. The pinned test runner disables that bytecode cache. An initial external temporary typecheck config could not resolve `@types/node`; setting its correct repository type roots fixed the setup, and the final scoped check passed. Neither is claimed as a product repair.

Limitations: Linux proof only; no Windows/macOS qualification or new coverage-percentage claim. All installations, homes, ports, and processes were synthetic and task-owned. No live installation or Gateway was accessed. Original-head [CI run 41109879203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41109879203) is historical provenance only; it does not qualify the repaired head. Parent review of the exact substantive head and authorized patch-identical repair is complete; native live exact-head CI, security, and required-review admission passed before merge.

Merged exact requested head `9053277dcf2650563eab290d679567ce76b16c9e` as `f4c7eb489a1f115c8e344d3bbcaf80756924d995`. Native PR-owned worktree/branch cleanup and completion recording succeeded. Original benchmark metrics remain historical snapshot observations; no new CI speed claim. ## What Problem This Solves

The dist artifact ownership suite repeats a complete nested-directory scenario and copies unused compiler installations before rejecting a retained lock. This target was assigned after main CI [41071928241 / job 124118721726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41071928241/job/124118721726) measured the file at 66.267 seconds.

## User Impact

Faster test execution with the same artifact ownership contracts. Production artifact and lock behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing launcher that forwards to the installed native compiler for the four lock-refusal cases. Keep nested-directory coverage in the stronger symlink scenario instead of replaying the same complete scenario for canonical `src`.

The test file changes by **-3 lines**; production and shared-helper changes are **0**. The conflict repair lowers captured main’s scalar from **6,284,797 to 6,284,794**, preserving all **152 current-main allocations totaling 19,943**. Tracked test LF decreases **6,307,404 → 6,307,401** and the effective cap decreases **6,304,740 → 6,304,737**. Main’s existing **2,664-line deficit is preserved**, not hidden or funded. The native check-only ratchet accepts this non-growth change under its inherited-debt policy; no grant was pruned, folded, or enlarged. The original reviewed snapshot’s zero-slack 6,306,007 total remains historical evidence below. PR #150246 was rechecked: none of its 709 files overlap the target or inspected helpers. The separate native PR baseline-fixtures lane is untouched.

## Evidence

Same checkout, Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, pinned Bun test backend, private frozen dependencies, task-owned temp/cache, serial samples. Every sample used:


title: chore: update mature dependencies without breaking compatibility
body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw misses maintained dependency releases because several eligible upgrades fail existing build, approval, or native-artifact contracts.

## User Impact

Refresh compatible provider, browser, discovery, native, mail/media, and tooling dependencies without silently changing approval, desktop-permission, or telemetry behavior. No configuration migration is required. Native platform CI and the deliberate holds below remain explicit; this is not a vulnerability-free-graph claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixed audit: **2026-10-30T15:45:38Z**. Inclusive publication cutoff: **2026-10-23T15:45:38Z**, including introduced transitives. Preserve inherited newer pins, existing exceptions, and supported contracts; no unapproved identity/edge downgrade.

The refresh covers direct npm, Cargo, Ruby, Swift, and tooling dependencies plus two targeted security transitives. Five candidate updates were deferred during CI repair (details below). Already-open Dependabot Action updates are not duplicated.

Eight updates needed deeper qualification: tsdown 0.23.2, Muse 1.4.12, CUA 0.37, Chrome MCP 1.12, Lobster 2026.10.1, Crabline 0.1.31, body-parser 2.4, and ctutils 0.4.4.

- Rolldown changed region labels to module-ID comments. Share the small reader across consumers while preserving real-comment/source-and-symbol provenance, ambiguity rejection, and all-mappings-before-write.
- Handle Muse's new approval-feedback error while retaining deny, interrupt, failure, and terminal cleanup.
- Refresh verified CUA native admission hashes with the SDK; preserve permissions and routing.
- Forwardport the three existing Chrome renderer/session, Lobster AOT-validator, and Crabline static-codec contracts instead of dropping patches. Patch count and behavior remain unchanged.

### Highlighted upstream changes

- **OpenAI 7.39 → 7.43:** Realtime large-message/reconnect and lifecycle fixes, plus reduced long-log processing work. Breaking-minor Decisions types were checked against actual consumers. [7.40](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.40.0), [7.42](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.42.0), [7.43](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.43.0).
- **Google GenAI 2.30 → 2.31:** consistent mid-stream SSE/drop errors and additive Live-context/function-result support. [Notes](https://github.com/googleapis/js-genai/releases/tag/v2.31.0).
- **Anthropic 0.135 → 0.137; Vertex 0.21 → 0.22:** unknown-SSE-event passthrough, tool-definition compatibility, sensitive-header and literal-replacement fixes without the 1.x authentication migration. [0.136](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.136.0), [0.137](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.137.0).
- **CUA 0.36 → 0.37:** target-focus, untitled-X11-window, sibling-menu refusal, and recovery-hint fixes. SDK and native artifacts were qualified together; no live desktop-control proof is claimed. [Notes](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0).
- **Chrome MCP 1.12:** upstream snapshot timeout/filtering, frame waits, and Lighthouse improvements with the existing ownership repair retained. Real Chromium/OOPIF and packaged stdio flows qualify the port.
- **Native runtime/discovery:** mdns-sd 0.21.6 fixes browse/resolve backpressure deadlocks and multicast retries; Tokio 1.54.1 and Tauri patches address I/O, timers, and Linux runtime errors. [mdns-sd](https://crates.io/crates/mdns-sd/0.21.6), [Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692), [Tauri opener](https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/pull/3565).
- **Compatible parsing/security transitives:** fast-uri 4.2.3, body-parser 2.4.0, ctutils 0.4.4, without a new override.

These are upstream claims unless consumer proof below demonstrates an OpenClaw effect; updating an SDK does not expose every new upstream feature automatically.

## Evidence

The following qualification was supplied by the dependency-updater loop before current-main reconciliation; the merge-head proof is recorded separately below.

- Full `pnpm build`, updater bridges, bundled assets, SDK declarations, Control UI, core/extension typechecks, targeted lint/format/budget checks: passed.
- Red/green updater-provenance and Muse approval-lifecycle regressions; installed wrapper/AOT/packaging, real isolated Chromium, CUA artifact/client/result, and actual HTTP middleware consumers: passed.
- Frozen pnpm/independent npm installs and native Cargo/Swift locked resolution; Ruby frozen installs and actual consumer imports: passed.
- Rust workspace 148 tests, Watch engine 13, Go readonly tests/build/vet/module verification, Fastlane 17, Swift protocol 7, Python skills 27: passed. Replays/duplicate shard summaries are not added to a grand total.
- Correct application-lock document, introduced publication dates, package identities and dependency edges audited. No age violation or unapproved downgrade; Cargo/Ruby/standalone npm audits also pass. No new override, freshness exception, public peer floor, or patch behavior.
- Independent local review covered the initial checkpoint and complete compatibility/port delta, scoped-clean P0–P2. All 114 final source hashes match reviewed bytes.

### Known gaps and deliberate holds

- Workflow guards: **186 passed, one inherited serial UI-inventory mismatch**, reproduced on the exact baseline. No unrelated assertion was relaxed; aggregate is not green.
- Native Apple/GTK/Windows application proof remains for platform CI. This host lacks desktop development libraries; locked metadata/protocol tests are not app-build proof.
- Chrome initial attachment can have empty loader IDs: old-UID reuse after recapture fails on both prior patched 1.11 and this 1.12 port. No weakened guard or forced reload.
- **Copilot stays 1.0.25:** 1.0.26 removes pre-create/pre-resume restrictions while native remote export/steering remains. No supported equivalent deny contract was established.
- **Coordinated migrations held:** Anthropic/Vertex 1.x changes authentication/API/request contracts; OTel 3 lacks a compatible Jaeger propagator; MXC 1.x replaces the consumed sandbox API/wire contract.
- Convex broker needs a supported credential-store review route. Exact Mailauth/Crabline pins retain older undici/nodemailer/re2js rows; MSAL 7 is outside the current Azure identity range. No blanket security override or vulnerability-free claim.

title: fix: preserve Usage creator focus when switching metrics

Switching Usage between tokens and cost replaces creator tables and rows, losing the focused creator control.

## User Impact

Creator controls keep focus and an expanded More section stays open when switching metrics. Refreshed creator totals, labels, selection, and actions stay current. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give each creator table a stable Solid component boundary and key its rows by the existing opaque creator identity. Remove the helper-call rendering path that rebuilt tables; live row accessors update refreshed snapshots without another state owner. Production LOC is unchanged; two regression tests add 141 net lines to cover metric-switch retention and refresh/reordering/More transitions. No effects, caches, controllers, styles, or markup changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-source targeted suite: 27/27 tests across creators, creator selection, and Usage view; 3.36s Vitest / 7.13s wrapper wall time. CI seconds are not available at publication. Full UI production and UI-pages test types, scoped lint/format, controller/line/test ratchets pass.

## What Problem This Solves

Package-lock generation fails against registry mirrors that publish only SHA-1 metadata, even when the same package version already has a reviewed SHA-512 pin in the pnpm lockfile.

## User Impact

Operators can generate npm installation locks through these mirrors without weakening the archive-integrity requirement or changing selected package versions. Conflicting strong hashes, ambiguous pins, and local-artifact validation remain errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the one existing SHA-512 constraint for the exact package identity into the generated lock. This is a standalone extraction of the registry-mirror fix from the runtime-packaging work; it does not enable offline runtimes or change worker provisioning.

## Evidence

- Secretless Linux container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependencies: all 94 generator tests pass (13.69 seconds through the repository runner; 12.43 seconds Vitest).

- Review repair: normalization is private, with no injected test pin map. Missing/ambiguous pins, wrong versions/identities and strong-hash conflicts are tested through `generateNpmPackageLock`; existing local-tarball validation remains covered.
- Targeted formatting, oxlint (0 warnings/errors), root-scripts typecheck, normal commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(cua-computer): prevent Linux registration from freezing Gateway startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway startup freezing while an explicitly enabled CUA Computer plugin registers on Linux. The reported incident spent 201,369.1 ms in registration.

## User Impact

CUA registration selects its Linux native artifact without generating a full diagnostic report on the Gateway thread. Pinned package versions, SHA-256 verification, explicit plugin enablement, macOS/Windows handling, lazy SDK loading, and desktop authorization remain intact.

Restricted or unrecognized procfs mappings produce the existing unsupported-platform diagnostic with `unknown-libc` rather than guessing an artifact. The SDK's separate resolver on lazy first native use remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The artifact verifier now reads the loaded GNU or musl library from `/proc/self/maps` instead of synchronously calling `process.report.getReport()` solely for its libc header. Removing that cast also removes exactly one stale assertion-safety allowance; no budget was raised.

## Evidence

- Four production-path registration fixtures (GNU `libc.so.6`, GNU `libc-2.31.so`, musl loader, and unknown mapping) fail on base `484cb468ccb7b3c85a35058d287c8b41e1400e24` at the diagnostic-report call, and pass with the candidate without calling it. Registration forwards the accepted artifact record.
- Candidate registration, artifact, Doctor, and driver-client checks: **5 files / 44 tests passed**. Targeted typecheck, lint, format, assertion-safety, pinned per-file ratchet, test-line ratchet, and whitespace checks pass. Net test-line delta is **−2**; production source **+9**, assertion allowance **−1**. Existing artifact and authorization owners are retained.
- Fresh independent installed autoreview of the complete candidate through **P3**: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewed snapshot is committed unchanged at `6b55c501d0446d5b8027fd2ce2163bf77afbfe8f`.
- Exact-head [CI 41100652095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41100652095) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Original [CI 41090146657](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41090146657) remains failed; its obsolete assertion allowance is fixed by the current head. No rerun or empty push was requested.

### Built Linux Gateway registration

The actual built Gateway became ready with CUA explicitly enabled. Registration completed in **44.6 ms**, with `loadFailedCount=0` and `registerFailedCount=0`. The verifier selected `@trycua/cua-driver-linux-x64-gnu@0.36.0`, read both native artifacts through its SHA-256 owner, and emitted no driver diagnostic. Registration generated **zero diagnostic reports**. Independent readback checked the emitted CUA module, build identity, observer, artifact reads, and successful registration trace.

One separate startup diagnostic report came from `@openclaw/fs-safe` libc detection during terminal-upload cleanup recovery, before CUA verification. The observer captured its actual stack; it is outside this registration repair. The first harness's stronger zero-total-report assertion failed on that unrelated call and is not represented as passing. A fresh startup-only proof on the same completed build passed the required registration-path contract.

Proof used local rootless Podman, Node **24.22.1**, isolated synthetic state, no production credentials, no published or host-network ports, and no desktop operations. Every container was capped at **4 CPUs / 8 GiB**, under the exclusive loop lock. The maintained `pnpm build:runtime` owner completed in **103.5 s** using explicit **5,120 MiB** heaps and compiler concurrency **1**; measured peak cgroup memory was **6,908,080,128 bytes**, with **zero OOM events**. Build metadata identifies the exact PR head. No source build budget or automation definition changed.

Earlier build attempts failed during setup, including an 8 GiB OOM; those are not product failures or passing proof. No cold-start/base timing comparison or measured 201-second improvement is claimed. The serving Gateway was untouched. Task containers were removed.

title: fix(ui): composer pickers and buttons look disabled in dark themes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in dark themes, the composer's pickers (model, reasoning) and buttons (attach, permission, microphone) look disabled at rest, most visibly in Absolutely dark.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4b567cfa-6b05-415a-be54-2a4f1b7d8b84)

## User Impact

User impact: resting composer controls read as enabled in every built-in dark theme. They are only slightly lighter than before, not bright, and stay clearly above the disabled Send. Light themes are essentially unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Built-in dark themes lift the composer surface well above the page canvas, but its controls kept canvas-calibrated ink (`--muted` for labels, the translucent `--icon-interactive` for glyphs). On the lifted surface those inks lost contrast, while the disabled ink is computed from the composer surface itself. The result was inverted: in Claw dark the `+` sat below the disabled Send, and in Absolutely dark the shield, chevrons and provider glyph sat below it (3.35:1 vs 3.81:1).

The composer now derives three inks from its own surface as ordered Oklab steps of `--text`: labels 75%, resting glyphs 62%, disabled 50% (`base.css`, consumed in `composer-surface.css`). Oklab keeps the steps perceptually even in light and dark. Beacon keeps its deliberately stronger `--muted` ink. Popovers and the pickers above the new-session composer are unaffected.

- Light themes: labels within about ±0.6, glyphs about 0.5 darker, disabled near 3:1. Beacon unchanged.

title: fix: show recovery steps when Doctor repair is interrupted
body:
Related: #178359, #182683, #187900.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can leave a managed Gateway paused after forced termination, or after cleanup refuses an unsafe restart, without explaining how to recover it.

## User Impact

Doctor now prints recovery steps immediately after stopping its managed Gateway, before repair admission and original-state capture. Admission, cleanup, and restoration failures also report the recovery steps. Operators must let Doctor and its repair children exit, resolve storage or cleanup failures, and successfully finish repairs before starting the service.

Forced termination still cannot execute a finalizer. This change does not claim to fix the reported I/O stall or the unreproduced native LaunchAgent activation failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Graceful signal handling already settles admitted work and restores the service. The remaining gap was diagnostic: the only early message was “Stopped…”, and cleanup could fail before the restoration-specific error logger. The existing maintenance owner now reports those failures, using one recovery message from its exit module. Native authority, child settlement, prior enablement, and restoration ordering remain unchanged. Windows continues restoring its temporary Scheduled Task disable before activation; the existing guarded `gateway start` command can enable an interrupted task after safe recovery.

Simplification kept the existing error boundaries and removed the narrower restoration-only logger. No new recovery state, background restarter, schema, dependencies, or options. This does not duplicate #188472's requester-maintenance-scope repair.

## Evidence

- **RED on main `b19c8c7ccc915b55d3a2d90fbbd03c7e1e6f41b2`:** the registered Commander command, real `doctorCommand`, health flow, and maintenance owner reached a deliberately blocked original-capture boundary after a synthetic managed-service stop. Forced termination left only “Stopped…” in output, with no recovery command. Native service/database I/O were fixture adapters; this is not native-service proof. Existing owner regressions also failed for missing early guidance and missing unsafe-cleanup guidance.
- **GREEN:** the same registered-CLI capture/termination proof retains the repair-children, `doctor --fix`, status, and start instructions before termination. Final focused maintenance settlement, signal/process, and systemd-identity suites passed **61 tests**. An additional **22** revalidation and **10** Windows compensation cases passed before moving the identical formatter to the exit module; their lifecycle inputs did not change.

title: feat: gate personal instructions on private session audience
body:
Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps automatically selected personal USER.md content and canonical personal-instructions chat operations out of shared or unverified initial audiences, without replacing the existing human-profile registry, Settings editor, or session profile-selection rules.

## User Impact

This review proposal contains three bounded improvements:

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the selected personal file. The final common filter also withholds personal-marked/origin hook entries. Shared defaults and existing allowlists remain intact.
2. The personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set operations with known group/channel origins or execution targets. Both actions return content; both are checked before file access or mutation.
3. Initial delivery also requires committed host sharing facts: an existing creator-private **Draft**, no public share, and a canonical creator matching the selected profile (bootstrap) or authenticated editor (chat tool). Shared/read-only/suggest, foreign-creator, and unverified audiences withhold the overlay or direct chat operations to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**. Distinct delegated origin and execution sessions must both qualify. A direct label alone is insufficient.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** Session selection remains assigned human owner, otherwise authenticated human creator; a new sender does not replace it. The authenticated editor remains separate from that selection. Canonical aliases and immutable creator stamps stay with their existing owners.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** These checks cover initial loader delivery and the canonical file handler's response/write boundary. Admission is not retained through every provider submission, tool-history append, or native thread. Widening an already-used private conversation can expose prior context or generated responses. Generic file/shell/native capabilities, inferred-to-file confinement, Knowledge/LCM audience admission, and retained history remain unqualified. Trusted administrators/host access are not hostile tenants. This is proposed narrowing for owner review, not upstream design acceptance. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small admission composes the existing profile catalog and retained session-sharing facts; no second registry, cache, SQL schema, configuration, public SDK contract, or model-supplied identity/audience argument is introduced. The existing public-share fact now participates in the internal sharing projection and its invalidation. Bootstrap checks after reads and hooks; the personal-file owner composes audience checks with its existing requester/role/agent and safe-writer pre-mutation assertion.

Author simplification retains the existing profile/file and session-facts owners. title: improve(update): reduce POSIX package backup cleanup overhead
body:
Related: #184658 (supporting research only; this does not diagnose or close the native Windows delay).

## What Problem This Solves

POSIX npm updates do avoidable work while removing the previous installed package during final cleanup.

## User Impact

Updates driven by a version containing this change spend less work retiring package backups, without changing configuration or migration requirements.

The installed updater owns this cleanup: installing the fixed candidate cannot accelerate an already-running older updater. Native Windows uses a different activation path and is not covered. The measured improvement below is for one cleanup phase, not total update time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing admitted SQLite reader for one artifact's removal rather than opening a new journal connection for every removed entry. Every callback still reads the current journal record and checks object identity and live executor authority. Each read releases its snapshot; the retained connection closes on success or error before settlement or archival.

There is no cached authorization decision, reduced check frequency, deferred cleanup, or deadline change. Shared removal cadence, Windows compensation, updater-runtime retention, and terminal-output ordering remain unchanged. This isolates a POSIX-only cost found while supporting DonnieFi's investigation, not a competing Windows repair.

## Evidence

The following commands and measurements were executed by Codex in Mert Başar's isolated Linux/WSL2/Docker environment. RoboClaw verified the source transfer and reused those receipts; it did not rerun or claim independent execution of the tests.

Measured baseline: `a0f10e38dea4244cfb22ad3f63139ef540e51587`. Original measured candidate: `d64336801477b849cb019c4bf721eedfdc5a6c3a`. The transferred candidate files match their recorded SHA-256 values.

### Qualified cleanup measurements

**Node 24.22.1**, five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, fresh process and fixture for each sample, the same committed **2,000-file / 40-directory** workload, warm/uncontrolled filesystem caches, no profiler in this series.

| Retirement metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 2,324.893 ms | 1,704.147 ms (−26.70%) |
| p95/max wall time | 2,499.576 ms | 1,858.149 ms |
| Median process CPU | 2,464.444 ms | 1,886.597 ms (−23.45%) |
| p95/max process CPU | 2,739.229 ms | 1,981.209 ms |
| Journal connections opened/closed, each sample | 2,091 / 2,091 | 35 / 35 |
| Journal preparations, each sample | 8,343 | 2,178 |
| Fresh current-record reads, each sample | 2,084 | 2,084 |

No recorded median/p95 metric regressed by 20% or more. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum, not a robust tail estimate. The original stronger preparation-scaling criterion is only partly met: the existing per-read journal-mode preparation remains. Total preparations are not constant.

The workload exercises real publication/retirement owners with private synthetic trees and an inert recovery-runtime fixture. It does not measure whole-update latency or establish a Windows/macOS improvement.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible workload and focused-test receipt</summary>

With supported Node 24.22.1 selected on PATH, the committed opt-in measurement entrypoint is:

```sh
OPENCLAW_BENCH_RETIREMENT=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/package-update-journal-retirement.perf.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Recorded focused-suite output:


The three added journal cases passed: intervening committed intent, replaced journal inode, and scope-end disposal. The four skips are existing macOS-only non-root ownership cases. Existing SQLite-owner proof covers snapshot-lock release and writer visibility. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and patch checks passed on the donor candidate.

</details>

### Packaged CLI boundary and retained limits

- Published stable **2026.10.8 → candidate** completed with matching build identity and durable run, readiness HTTP 200, preserved synthetic durable conversation, and intended incognito cleanup. This is compatibility proof; cleanup in that first hop still belongs to the old installed driver.
- A **candidate-driven explicit replacement** completed with update/status exit 0 and durable `succeeded/finished`. CLI `packageActivation.phase` was `complete`. Function coverage bound to the original driver PID **84** recorded **3 executions** of `createAssertionReader`. This is execution coverage, not a CPU profile.

The optional external autoreview helper **did not run**, because transmission of unpublished code to its configured service was not authorized. No clean result from that tool is claimed.

title: fix(pr): resume reviews after interrupted checkout writes
body:
Related: #181316

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a native PR review cannot resume when an interrupted checkout leaves a tracked file with bytes matching neither recorded endpoint.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly preserve the unexpected file and resume the existing review without discarding its history or changing its workflow binding. No app UI or CI workflow changes. Automatic recovery still refuses unknown bytes, including empty files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one operator-selected salvage operation to the existing checkout owner. It qualifies current official-main tooling under the original PR lock, backs up the exact unknown file and review preimages, and atomically restores only that working file from its recorded source. The original bound workflow still validates and completes the transition.

The initial scope is a detached review journal and a regular file present in both endpoints. It does not reset the checkout, change HEAD/index/journal/binding, accept arbitrary replacement content, or grant merge authority. Other writers must be quiescent during repair. This is a separate tooling prerequisite; it does not alter the iOS contributor's patch.

## Evidence

- Original read-only reproduction: the retained review rejects its unexpected zero-byte file. - Actual native wrapper entry: **4/4 passed**. An older admitted workflow refuses the interrupted state; current qualified recovery uses the real helper; then the unchanged older binding resumes ordinary replay. title: fix: Home button stops opening after a failed run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking the Home icon does not open Home when session attention replaces the icon with a warning, question, or approval indicator. Stale child-failure details can also make the navigation button look like an unrelated error.

## User Impact

User impact: Home stays recognizable and clickable regardless of session failures. Run/queued/unread activity and draft/outbox badges remain; session attention keeps its existing session and Inbox surfaces. No configuration or data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generic session-row renderer puts an interactive attention tooltip inside the Home button. That tooltip stops click propagation. title: fix: unblock agent sessions after a Gateway owner dies
body:
Related: #183052, #182984

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent sessions remaining unavailable for a full database integrity scan after the previous Gateway owner dies, including during startup admission. Two healthy 35 GB Team database opens blocked sessions for 15 and 21.6 minutes.

## User Impact

A matching dead-owner lease on Linux now takes QUICK admission, including after interrupted startup. A subsequent successful checkpoint and clean stop seal that QUICK receipt, so the following ordinary restart also avoids the full scan. Revoked validation, dirty receipts without matching dead-owner provenance, replaced files, prior corruption, live peers, and explicit maintenance policies retain full verification or refusal. Known FULL requirements survive interrupted verification in the existing lease status. Failed recovery QUICK checks fall back to FULL. No configuration or database schema migration is needed.

QUICK omits full index consistency checking. Its receipt remains distinct from FULL. Seal identity, journal, expiration, final-close, and refusal checks remain in effect; normal SQLite access, Doctor, and later full verification retain corruption detection.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite WAL recovery preserves committed writes after process death. Treat matching dead-owner provenance as process death instead of corruption evidence, and recheck provenance after opening the file. The existing admission facts and clean-close seal owner carry a distinct successful recovery-QUICK receipt across clean restarts. Ordinary maintenance QUICK checks never mint that receipt. This avoids moving the outage to the next deploy and adds no background-check owner or persistent store.

## Evidence

- The original regression fails on the original main base: same-boot recovery runs a full scan instead of zero. The extended regression also fails on reviewed commit `623776c93bd` (replayed after rebase as `89edda72c85`): after QUICK admission and clean close, reopening runs another full scan. With the receipt/seal fix, the extended regression passes.
- Red/green command: `timeout 180s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.integrity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'quickly admits matching killed owners'`. Exercises real SIGKILL, native worker admission, session creation, WAL preservation and rollback, interrupted admission, dirty receipts, provenance mismatch, failed QUICK falling back to FULL, and clean restart after retiring process proof. It verifies no extra scan and no false FULL receipt on restart.
- Rebased onto `6f098f501e6959d7688334a781a91c6964e044a0` before verification. All 174 tests across eight focused owner/consumer files passed in 122.25 s, including shared-state admission, seal rejection/expiration, ordinary QUICK/FULL policies, and native crash recovery. Final restart-regression replay passed after simplifying receipt publication. Targeted state/SQLite typecheck, changed-file lint/format, docs link audit (16,144 links; zero broken), and `git diff --check` pass. Broad checks ran in PR CI; the unrelated failures and landing blocker are recorded below.
- Existing native-execution file: 42 tests, 48.5 s summed test time; lease-integrity file: 27 tests, 18.8 s; lease-owner file: 13 tests, 0.98 s. These existing real process/worker fixtures prove crash, custody, and restart behavior; no extra fixture file is needed.
- The final staged candidate against `6f098f501e6959d7688334a781a91c6964e044a0` received scoped-clean P0–P2 autoreview with full admission/seal context. The review finding about interrupted known-FULL checks is fixed and covered by lease-status tests; earlier index-only findings were resolved by staging the complete candidate. Static review is separate from executed tests.
- After the retained-FULL change, 22 focused lease/native recovery cases passed, covering record/completion, stale required-FULL reclamation, revoked/replaced proof, and the crash/clean-restart regression.
- Net test line delta: **0**; the existing crash regression and lease tests replace superseded assertions. No test file or persistent store was added. Simplification uses the existing admission/seal owners; production delta +65 lines, test delta 0.
- [Exact-head CI run 41069077227, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41069077227) finished with 66 successful jobs, 26 skipped jobs, two failing test jobs and their failing aggregate gate. The automatic failure table classifies both jobs as unknown because main uses different shard names. Independent attribution now covers all five assertions: the two replay-cohort signatures match [scheduled-main job 124089265185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41063477930/job/124089265185) and reproduce on baseline `6f098f501e6959d7688334a781a91c6964e044a0`; their focused expectation repair is separately owned by #188398. All three refusal-product copy expectations (bio, cyber, misalignment) also reproduce on that baseline. The completed misalignment-only replay failed at the same terminal assertion (1 failed, 3 skipped, 87.78 s total): detailed review text was expected, but the generic failure summary was received. This completes the earlier timed-out baseline gap. The reproduction baseline has no R1 patch; inspected test, fixture, replay and copy-owner inputs also match the CI main parent and tested merge. Native inherited-failure evidence is prepared; these results remain failed CI.

title: fix(update): keep the plugin lifecycle lease alive while finalize blocks the main thread.
body:
Related: #188335
Related: #182476

## What Problem This Solves

Update finalization and repair can lose the plugin lifecycle lease when synchronous work blocks the main thread for longer than five minutes.

## User Impact

Plugin finalization can finish through a long main-thread stall without failing solely because its lease-renewal timer could not run. This does not remove the underlying stall or repair plugin versions left behind by an earlier core rollback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable the existing worker heartbeat in the shared native plugin lifecycle lease owner. Finalize/repair, native Doctor, and plugin install/update holders receive the same fix, including nested work, while existing durable ownership checks, cancellation, and joined release remain in place. Standalone async metadata leases keep their existing behavior; artifact cleanup already uses a worker heartbeat.

The runtime acquiring the lease needs this change; a candidate cannot retrofit an already-running older updater. No backport is included.

## Evidence

Published head: `11f3c8fbfb5523e4585aaca392d3cbbf1769a753`. Both required product proofs now pass. Exact-head CI run [41072554012](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41072554012) remains green; a fresh same-head GitHub GraphQL read returned 150 terminal checks with no failures or pending checks. The canonical watcher refresh hit HTTP 503 before attachment; no CI rerun or push was requested.

- RED at `db5d331f07c686187240075f7e798c9e89d3aaa5`: the real one-second lifecycle lease expired after a 1.5-second parent `Atomics.wait`, with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`, `reason: expired`, `expiredByMs: 505`, and `renewalTimerLateByMs: 1170`.
- Fixed [Node CI failure in checks-node-changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41068750223/job/124107799042): its publication fixture advanced only the parent clock by four seconds while the worker kept real time. It now blocks the parent for 1.5 seconds with a one-second lease during publication and after maintenance closes, retains `assertOwned()` at both boundaries, and verifies persisted expiry advanced. The cross-process cache fixture also uses real time: its old `NODE_OPTIONS` clock preload was deliberately not inherited by the heartbeat worker. All contention and cache-handoff assertions remain.
- GREEN on Node: publication file **30 passed** (18.68 s test / 24.61 s wrapper), lifecycle owner/refusal files **22 passed** (39.80 s test / 52.37 s wrapper). The latter includes real cross-process startup/cache handoff and native worker cleanup; these independent-clock/process contracts need this boundary. An initial whole-file run encountered an inherited shared-temp build lock; isolated `/tmp` rerun passed without changing that lock.
- GREEN on pinned Bun: publication file **30 passed** (25.25 s test / 31.72 s wrapper), lifecycle owner/refusal files **22 passed** (27.06 s test / 31.68 s wrapper). Existing cancellation, revoked authority, killed-owner recovery, durable pre-publication checks, release/reacquisition, and cache handoff remain covered. Tests used isolated HOME/state, sticky `/tmp`, repository wrappers, and bounded timeouts.
- Targeted format, type-aware lint, staged test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. `pr-simplify` removed the obsolete fixture clock machinery. Against the merge base: production +2 lines, docs +6, and **17 fewer test lines**; no test-budget allocation remains. Exact-head CI completed successfully in run 41072554012.
- Fresh Codex `autoreview --engine codex` covered the complete final candidate against `db5d331f07c686187240075f7e798c9e89d3aaa5`, including the state lease, heartbeat and publication owners, at P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The committed patch at `11f3c8fbfb5523e4585aaca392d3cbbf1769a753` matches that reviewed candidate. The reviewed source diff is unchanged; the required product proofs now pass below.
- **Real installed CLI RED/GREEN:** the private five-second grant and 7.5-second parent stall reached `openclaw update repair` at its real plugin-finalize boundary. With only native worker renewal removed, repair failed `finalize:plugins` with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST` (2,802 ms expired at the product check). With the worker enabled, the same owner renewed during the block, repair exited 0, and 3,869 ms remained on the durable lease afterward. The harness verified release before any next product command, preserved the fixture's canonical record/package/manifest, and successfully ran its installed CLI ping. Strict source comparison confirmed the two private owners differ only by the existing heartbeat option; the shortened grant is common to both.
- **Published stable to exact uninstrumented candidate:** the installed `openclaw@2026.10.9` updater performed `openclaw update --tag file:<candidate> --yes --json` successfully. Both versions are 2026.10.9, but the build changed from published commit `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` to this exact head. Before any subsequent candidate Doctor or Gateway command, the identity helper compared all **17,156 application files** against the frozen candidate, required a changed build ID, and verified tarball SHA-256 `9e3220fded1b7bbe063daea421136af86f7ce189d7139c1679aaae600fd0de0a`. This candidate retained the normal five-minute lease and has no fault instrumentation.
- **Upgrade survival:** the canonical configured-plugin-installs survivor runner passed Matrix's npm record/payload integrity and installed CLI inspection, automatic migration and state survival, then `/healthz` 200, `/readyz` 200 (`ready=true`, no failing components), and `gateway status --require-rpc`. The RPC server reported the exact candidate build ID. Startup took 21 s; health/readiness/status phases took 1/1/2 s. Readiness also recorded CPU degradation under the four-CPU test cap.
- These product proofs used rootless Podman with four CPUs and 8 GiB per container, at most two concurrent loop containers, private HOME/state/temp directories, no credentials or published ports, and H-owned source/artifacts. The one prepared Crabbox request queued and was stopped/reconciled before the explicitly authorized local fallback. Initial setup refusals were preserved and corrected only in private harness setup/layout/permissions; none was counted as RED. The production Gateway/state were untouched. Native Windows and external provider/channel APIs were not exercised. Both required product proofs and maintainer evidence review are complete; native landing remains subject to current head, CI, security, review and writer gates.

<details>
<summary>Separate rollback-plugin finding (not changed here)</summary>

A separate audit of this PR's base found that a package-only core rollback could leave newer npm plugins; that follow-up is not changed or revalidated here. `src/plugins/update-installed.ts:102` enters plugin transactions, which commit at `src/plugins/install-transaction.ts:169-173` without an outer deferred transaction request. The updater does not retain those transactions at `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.ts:216`, and publishes the canonical install records at `:435`.

`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-rollback.ts:430` rolls back only the core package transaction. Compatible databases stay in place at `:354-356`; restoring config snapshots at `:472` does not revert the canonical plugin index. A failure before index publication can instead leave old records beside newer package bytes. Full-state recovery is explicitly deferred at `:143-149`.

A separate fix should retain the existing deferred plugin install transactions and the matching prior index/config publication state through outer activation verification, then restore owned prior plugin artifacts and records under the lifecycle lease before restarting the prior core. It must preserve live authority checks and avoid reverting later independent plugin changes. This is a source-audited finding, not a rollback runtime reproduction.

</details>

## Credit

Thanks to @patosullivan for #188335 and @yyds-xxxx for #182476. Implementation and review direction: @steipete.

The Crabbox wrapper suite repeatedly copies thousands of immutable compiled files into temporary checkouts, adding filesystem work to a test priced at 173 seconds in the CI timing inventory.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Sharing immutable compiled fixture files removes repeated byte copies while preserving existing coverage. The corrected passing samples do not demonstrate a wall-time speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share compiled entrypoints and chunks with hard links, falling back to the existing copy operation when links are unavailable. Each checkout retains its own paths and cleanup ownership. Reuse the same fixture construction for the setup executable.

Production code, test cases, assertions, timeouts, and platform conditions are unchanged. Test lines decrease by six. The scalar is lowered to the exact tracked total, 6,295,757; the previous scalar already contained slack.

## Evidence

`test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts`, same host, command, and one worker. Only successful runs enter the medians:

| Version | Observation | Wall (s) | Vitest (s) | Filesystem output (blocks) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1 | 250.75 | 248.93 | 20,468,480 |
| Before | 3 | 201.48 | 199.38 | 20,071,616 |
| Before | 4 (detached original base) | 193.67 | 189.89 | 4,291,008 |
| **Before** | **Passing median** | **201.48** | **199.38** | **20,071,616** |
| After | 1 | 199.79 | 197.95 | 3,779,112 |
| After | 2 | 205.93 | 204.18 | 8,492,360 |
| After | 3 | 205.36 | 203.56 | 3,920,600 |
| **After** | **Passing median** | **205.36** | **203.56** | **3,920,600** |

The corrected passing-baseline wall median is **201.48 s**, versus **205.36 s** after: **3.88 s slower (1.9%)**. Vitest medians are **199.38 s → 203.56 s**, **4.18 s slower (2.1%)**. These observations do not establish wall-time savings. Ranges overlap (before 193.67–250.75 s; after 199.79–205.93 s), and host load and cache conditions vary; there is no guaranteed CI saving. CI has not yet retimed this change.

Failed observation, preserved separately and excluded from successful-run medians:

| Version | Observation | Wall (s) | Vitest (s) | Outcome |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Before | 2 | 288.30 | 286.16 | 1 failed, 283 passed, 1 skipped; exit 1 |

The failure was `transports verified source and dependencies (provider=blacksmith-testbox, shallow=false, scenario=transport)`: the fixture's local `git clone` exceeded its unchanged 10-second deadline (`ETIMEDOUT`, `SIGTERM`, observed 11,132 ms). Source inspection places this failure in fixture setup before wrapper invocation. The same case passed in original baseline observations 1 and 3, the added original-base observation 4, and all three after runs. The cause remains unresolved; a passing replay is not a repair. ## What Problem This Solves

CI Git policy tests spend seconds waiting through TERM grace periods that their assertions do not depend on.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The focused CI Git policy tests run faster while retaining real Git, real signals, and descendant-extinction checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor an explicit `realDrain: false` in the existing test harness and use it for base-policy and workflow-sanity checks. Unspecified options retain the old real-clock/cancellation defaults. The owner still sends TERM/KILL and must prove extinction before retry, output consumption, or publication.

Native grace coverage stays in `test/scripts/ci-platform-checkout.test.ts`, including `preserves checkout ownership and fixture isolation (Linux=$linux, $scenario)` and `waits for legal slow tree startup before cancellation`. All real-Git shallow-history and publisher cases remain. No tests or assertions are deleted; no production code, timeouts, runner settings, timing baselines, or allocation files change.

The publisher already shares an immutable Git seed. Real-Git ancestry cases cost roughly 0.1–0.5 seconds each locally; the dominant avoidable cost was repeated five-second grace waits plus their process polling. Remaining file cost comes from 115 expanded cases executing real workflow policies and native subprocess/Git boundaries.

## Evidence

| File | Phase | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Median |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ci-git-owner.test.ts` | before | 71.69 / 70.04 | 89.32 / 87.46 | 93.27 / 91.15 | 89.32 / 87.46 |
| `ci-git-owner.test.ts` | after | 54.64 / 53.06 | 54.48 / 52.86 | 54.13 / 52.46 | 54.48 / 52.86 |
| `ci-linux-git.test.ts` | before | 39.55 / 37.54 | 38.69 / 36.62 | 39.13 / 37.00 | 39.13 / 37.00 |
| `ci-linux-git.test.ts` | after | 32.84 / 31.43 | 33.97 / 32.19 | 33.72 / 31.93 | 33.72 / 31.93 |

**Owner wall median: 89.32s → 54.48s, saving 34.84s (39.0%).** Sibling control: 39.13s → 33.72s, an observed 5.41s difference with unchanged effective options.

These are Linux measurements with the repository's default runner and `--maxWorkers=1`; cells contain wall / Vitest seconds. All three samples are retained. Host load varied; the unchanged sibling is a control, and its observed difference is not attributed to this change. CI's existing timing catalog prices these files at 180s and 101s respectively; new CI timing is pending.

Representative per-test medians:

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| drains the base action's 30-second exact fetch before deepening | 10.922s | 0.686s |
| workflow sanity retains 30-second fetch deadline | 5.966s | 0.743s |
| base policy stops before availability/retry on cancellation | 5.541s | 0.460s |
| base policy stops before availability/retry on cancellation during timeout drain | 5.445s | 0.409s |
| workflow sanity never recovers or publishes after fetch cancellation | 5.563s | 0.431s |

title: fix(ui): mobile web composer stays one line while the keyboard is open
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat composer in the mobile web UI does not grow while typing when the phone keyboard is open. It stays at a single line and scrolls, so you can only see the line you are typing. The New Session page already grows.

## User Impact

User impact: on the mobile web UI (not the iOS app), a draft in an existing chat now grows to three lines while you type, then scrolls inside the composer. The conversation above stays visible. Desktop and narrow desktop windows keep their existing line caps.

## Why This Change Was Made

An open portrait phone keyboard shrinks the chat pane below 320px. A short-pane rule meant for nearly closed panes then held the editor to one line. The mobile composer now sets its own three-line cap, which takes precedence over that rule and also replaces the six-line cap used on full-height phones. The measured pane limit can still lower the cap when the pane really is too short. Landscape phones and nearly closed panes keep their existing one-line rules.

## Evidence

Real Control UI build, mock Gateway, touch-enabled mobile viewport. The editor is focused at full height and the viewport is then shrunk to simulate the keyboard, with prose typed word by word.

**Before** — 360 × 372 with the keyboard open: three lines typed, one visible.

![Before: mobile composer stuck at one line with the keyboard open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ca50a91-f971-49cf-84d3-7c0408aa85b4)

**After** — the same state: the draft grows to three lines.

![After: mobile composer shows three lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0882d452-ac26-4382-a0eb-22a7b4fc8589)

**After** — past three lines the composer scrolls and keeps the typed line visible.

![After: mobile composer scrolls past three lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f0bc091-3c28-42b5-aeb9-003172b1ae0a)

- New `composer-height.e2e.test.ts` case, at 360 × 372, 390 × 400 and 390 × 844. Every keystroke checks that the height follows min(lines, 3). Past three lines it scrolls with the typed line visible, the composer stays inside the viewport, and clearing the draft returns it to one line.
  - Against `main` it fails in all three cases: the editor stays at 36px when the draft is 60px at 360 × 372 (keyboard open), and it reaches 108px instead of stopping at 84px on taller panes.
  - With the fix it passes in all three cases on every run (four full runs).
- `composer-height`, `chat-composer-size`, `chat-composer-redesign` and `mobile-new-conversation` e2e: 25/25 pass.
- `chat-footer-layout` and `chat-responsive` browser tests: 77/77 pass. This includes the short-pane test that keeps the non-mobile composer at one line.
- `chat-composer-height` and `chat-composer-mobile` browser tests: 25/25 pass. This includes the narrow desktop window still stopping at six lines.
- Jitter check: a frame-by-frame probe sampled the composer, textarea and last message at every rendering opportunity and again after each paint. It ran at 360 × 372, 390 × 400, 430 × 480 (keyboard open) and 390 × 844 (keyboard closed) across focus, keyboard open/close/reopen, typing word by word, Shift+Enter, 40 backspaces, select-all delete, a 30-line paste, typing at the top of a scrolled draft, clear and blur, for `main` and this branch.
  - With this branch, no painted frame shows a bounce. The textarea, composer edges, thread scroll and draft scroll never reverse direction. The draft never scrolls backwards while appending or moves while typing at the top, and its overflow style never flaps. The focus/blur reveal animation is monotonic.
  - A one-frame lag between composer growth and transcript scroll appears only in pre-ResizeObserver samples. It is corrected before paint, on `main` too. This branch's lower cap also removes `main`'s one sampled frame where a 30-line paste briefly put the composer 28px over the last message.
  - Every flag on this branch also appears on `main`.
  - The regression test now also samples every frame while typing and asserts the draft never shrinks and the composer's bottom edge never moves (12/12 in the file pass; the three mobile cases still fail on `main`).
- Pre-existing, unchanged by this PR, follow-up: on an instant viewport shrink, one task-boundary sample shows the transcript with a different last-message element and a stale thread height before the shell catches up. It is identical on `main` and never visible in a frame sample after the first.
- stylelint, oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.

Not covered: a physical phone or a real on-screen keyboard. The keyboard is simulated by shrinking the viewport, which matches how `interactive-widget=resizes-content` resizes the app.

## What Problem This Solves

Suggested tasks open as a large card floating over the top-right of the transcript, separate from everything else that waits above the composer. Its start button also uses a darkened copy of the accent, so it doesn't match Send when a custom accent is set.

## User Impact

User impact: a suggested task now lives in the stack directly above the composer, next to queued messages and the progress card.

- **Closed**, it's one quiet row: a muted lightbulb, the title and repository, a `1/2` pager when there are several suggestions, a plain accent-text **Start** action with its options arrow, and dismiss.
- **Open**, it reads like the question panel: the full title, the summary, and the instructions with their folder and a copy button. The footer carries the same small primary button the question panel submits with, nearest the composer.
- **On narrow screens** the closed row keeps only the title, position and dismiss. Opening it reveals paging and a full-width start button just above the composer.
- **When starting fails**, the card stays open. The lightbulb becomes a warning, and the error and recovery actions (Retry, choose a repository, Cancel) appear in the footer.
- The filled start button uses exactly the same fill and text color as **Send**, including custom accents. Its menu still offers a new session, a new worktree, or this session.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b28c92fc-e5c6-4d38-974a-31db2110ca36)

## Why This Change Was Made

- The tray renders in the composer's footer content, beside session suggestions. That content is shared by the built-in composer and plugin composer companions. The conversation's top-right gutter now holds only Details notices.
- The closed row uses the queue and progress card's surface and `--chat-stack-*` geometry. The open card mirrors the question panel's header → content → action-footer order, so the primary action always lands nearest the composer. The card is bounded at `min(30rem, 62dvh)`, and only its content scrolls.
- One start action, two weights: closed it is `btn btn--sm` with transparent ground and accent text, so the row stays quiet; open it is `btn btn--sm primary`, the question panel's Submit, with Send's hover step. The old lightness clamp and fixed white ink are removed, so a custom accent's computed ink applies to both.
- Copy moves next to the instructions it copies, and the instructions are shown in body text rather than a monospace block. The duplicate eyebrow and path boxes are removed.
- The disclosure state belongs to the tray, so paging keeps it. Starting a task doesn't open the card, but a failed start keeps it open until the user retries or dismisses.
- The open content is a flex column. A grid there sized its rows before the scrollbar appeared, which let a rewrapped long summary overlap the instructions and cover the copy button.
- Styles live in `composer-task-suggestions.css`, loaded by the lazy tray module. A new `Start` string was added to the English catalog.

## Evidence

Screenshots were captured from the real bundle against a mocked Gateway with synthetic data. They'll be attached in a follow-up body edit.

- `chat-flow.task-suggestions.e2e` + `chat-startup-priority.e2e` (13 tests, real bundle). The row renders inside `.chat-footer__context` and is closed by default. Opening it shows the summary, folder, prompt and copy, and moves Start to the footer. The footer's Start and its options trigger match Send's rendered fill and ink at rest and on hover, with `#da7756` and `#ffffff` accents. The menu opens above its trigger. Long summaries stay reachable, and copy and Start pass Playwright's trial-click hit check at 1280×720, 390×720 and 900×500. The draft is kept in all three start modes.
- Unit: `chat-task-suggestions` + `chat-pane-task-suggestions` (38 tests). These cover disclosure ARIA wiring, disclosure kept across paging, no opening while starting, a failure keeping the card open, the closed row's short label with its full accessible name, and Start moving from header to footer.
- Capture pass at 320 px and 1280 px with two suggestions, in both the plain failure and repository-chooser states: dismiss stays inside the row.
- `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt and `ui:i18n:verify` are clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2). On the first layout, the first pass found one P2, later fixed, and the second pass was scoped-clean. On the redesign commit the result was scoped-clean; the final weight-only refinement reran the suites above.

title: feat(ui): compact context from the composer usage popover
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The prompt-budget popover beside the composer showed how full the context was but had no way to act on it: compacting meant opening **View context** and finding the button in the side panel.

## User Impact

User impact: the context-usage popover now has a secondary **Compact** button on its **View context** row, vertically centered with the link. It stays outlined at every usage level (the context ring already signals the warning), explains why it is unavailable while a run is active, shows progress while compacting, and keeps the popover open so the budget updates in place when the Gateway reports the compacted session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The side panel's Compact button becomes one shared control used by both surfaces, so they share one request owner, labels and disabled states instead of two copies. The control also reads the pane's existing compaction status, so a compaction started by the runtime or from the other surface shows as in progress in both places.

How it behaves in each popover state:

| State | Compact |
| --- | --- |
| Viewer cannot compact (no admin scope, catalog session, participation blocked, disconnected) | hidden; the row is pixel-identical to `main` |
| Normal usage | outlined secondary |
| Fresh usage at or above 85% | outlined secondary; the ring stays the warning cue |
| Approximate (stale) totals | outlined secondary |
| Run active | disabled, title "Available when the current run finishes." |
| Compacting (this request or a pane-tracked compaction) | spinner + "Compacting", disabled, `aria-busy` |
| Narrow/mobile widths, light/dark, plan-billed sessions | same row, above the separator and any quota tray |

The popover deliberately stays open after the click: the budget bar, percentage and button emphasis above are where the result shows up.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- Copy moved from the lazily loaded `chat.sessionDetails.contextCompact*` keys to `chat.composer.contextUsage.compact*`, which the popover already loads eagerly, so the label can never render before its catalog. The unused `contextCompact` ("Compact session") key goes with them. Foreign locales pick up the new keys through the locale refresh workflow.
- Shared outlined button styles move to the boot chat stylesheet. The side panel keeps its sizing and its existing filled warning style (it does render filled at 95% on `main`), now scoped to the panel; its header renders pixel-identical before and after.
- In the popover the outline is lifted 1px (`margin-top: -2px; padding-top: 2px`) so it centers on the line it shares with View context: both labels share one baseline and the button box centers on the label (measured in Chromium, asserted in the browser test).
- The popover row was already 26px tall, so adding the button causes no layout shift.

</details>

## Evidence

Before → after: 95% fresh usage, dark theme, 1280px. Real Control UI build with a mocked Gateway; synthetic session data.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the popover offers only View context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71f98ea6-23fa-485c-a8b5-3bc2f81e388f) | ![After: an outlined Compact centered on the View context row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d74434a-3367-491b-af6f-24470b08d6ab) |

<details><summary>Other states (after)</summary>

| Normal usage (42%) | Stale totals (~95%) | Compacting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Outlined Compact at 42% usage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a90f65a6-18c1-4263-a1ad-bc788861201b) | ![Outlined Compact when totals are approximate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90a3088e-65a9-4966-a40a-551c885b11fe) | ![Disabled Compacting button with spinner while the popover stays open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fda52d4-1639-491a-8c03-33947c348919) |

| Light, 95% | 390px dark, 95% | 390px light, 42% |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Light theme with outlined Compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67080031-24bf-4d80-aedd-c66a2bb82393) | ![Mobile dark popover with outlined Compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8b3a9f0-79c7-4269-b12a-1d58b18756ff) | ![Mobile light popover with outlined Compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/645a6df6-6ac1-43af-a665-99909e21a5d3) |

Context panel header with the shared control (pixel-identical to before):

![Context panel header with Compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83bace9b-06df-4e93-a6d7-d3f4d6d7185b)

</details>

- **Unit (jsdom):** state matrix (hidden, normal, warning, stale, run active, disconnected, pane-tracked compaction), never filled at any usage level, and one request per click while pending, popover open throughout. Existing panel test (busy until the request settles, current callback) still passes on the shared control.
- **Browser (Chromium):** at 1280 and 320px with 95% usage, Compact is outlined, shares the View context label baseline, centers on it, and keeps the 26px row; a real click keeps the popover open, shows Compacting, then returns to Compact.
- **Control UI E2E** (`session-context-breakdown.e2e.test.ts`, mocked Gateway, built UI): new scenario opens the popover at 95%, clicks Compact, asserts the `sessions.compact` request, the disabled Compacting state and an untouched draft, then resolves it and sees 21% while the popover stays open. The existing panel flow passes; its old assertion that the popover had no Compact button was updated.

On the first commit the dead-export scan failed only on pre-existing unused exports that no changed file referenced on `main` (`reply-tool-authority-inbound.ts`, `artifact-download-grants.ts`, `session-html-preview.ts`, `session-progress-card.ts`, `participant-colors.ts`, `motion/spring.ts`, `chat-composer-width-ref.tsx`).

title: feat(baseten): support joey-1 decision model
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Baseten users cannot select joey-1 for native typed decisions even though it shares the existing System One protocol.

## User Impact

Users can select `baseten/decision-models/baseten-joey-2b-latest` as their Decision model for text/JSON Boolean probabilities, choices, and rubric scores. The primary chat model is unchanged. This adapter does not support images; probabilities are estimates, not safety or action-authorization guarantees.

## Why This Change Was Made

The vendor documents joey-1 on `POST /v1/systemone`, not chat completions. One manifest row extends the existing decision owner and its allowlist; no new provider, transport, core tool, configuration option, or runtime implementation is introduced. The row declares the hosted 16,384-token per-question limit and supported option bounds. Documentation shows selection, current vendor-listed pricing, and limitations.

Primary sources checked October 30, 2026:
- [Baseten supported models and protocol](https://docs.baseten.co/inference/model-apis/decision-models)
- [System One API fields, limits, and response](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/inference-api/system-one)
- [Base Labs joey-1 model card](https://huggingface.co/baselabs/joey-1)
- [Launch announcement](https://www.baseten.co/blog/decisions-for-a-penny-introducing-joey-1/)

## Evidence

All published-head evidence below targets `c24717c401ffab2358077254ef4d0bf36df3431d`.

- Red on base `358300de55eb5612328a33ab5ee2d9359e6e3427`: joey mixed-rubric transport returned `unsupported-input`, and the decision-only catalog case lacked the manifest row. After adding the row, both pass.
- Focused Baseten tests: **36 passed**, 3 files, 11.94 seconds wrapper wall time (10.27 seconds Vitest). Extension production/test typechecks, targeted oxlint, formatting, docs MDX/config examples, and `git diff --check` passed. An initial package-boundary typecheck hit existing test-support `rootDir` errors; the canonical production/test lanes passed.

- The supplementary A–K live run **failed overall** on Google (`streamFn(...).result is not a function`) and Copilot (tool metadata sentinel assertion); it had 69 passed and 26 skipped tests. Those provider/test paths are unchanged by this additive Baseten metadata PR. This is successful Baseten proof, **not** a claim that the broader live suite is green.
