title: improve(ui): mobile sheets move with iOS-style springs, flicks and swipe-to-dismiss
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0fb3ffc-670f-446e-a5e0-ab2c33ba9de8)

## What Problem This Solves

Mobile sheets in the Control UI do not move like the iOS sheets people expect: the Panels sheet fades in place, disappears instantly on close, ignores flicks, snaps between heights without easing, and cannot be swiped away. The Inbox and Filter & sort sheets cannot be swiped down at all.

## User Impact

On phones, the Panels sheet, the Inbox and Filter & sort sheets, the navigation drawer, in-sheet pages and the Details/Panels switch now share one iOS-style spring. Sheets slide up and back down, follow the finger, carry a flick's momentum into the next height, and close with a downward flick, a pull past half their minimum height, or a tap outside. Slow drags still leave the Panels sheet at exactly the height you chose. Reduced-motion users keep instant changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Motion now has one owner in `ui/src/lib/motion/`:

- `spring.ts` solves Apple's duration/bounce spring in closed form and reduces it to a compact CSS `linear()` easing (13 stops, within 0.3% of the solver). `base.css` exposes it as one `--motion-sheet` token (`441ms linear(…)`) that every sheet, drawer, picker page and segmented-control transition reuses; a unit test keeps it generated from the solver.
- `gesture.ts` holds the WWDC18 fluid-interface physics: release velocity over the last 100 ms, momentum projection with the scroll-view deceleration rate, and rubber-banding.
- `chat-mobile-host-release.ts` decides where a released Panels sheet rests; the runtime then swaps in a one-off spring curve that starts at the finger's speed.
- `sheet-dismiss.ts` gives the sidebar bottom sheets swipe-to-dismiss and an animated tap-outside dismissal.

Closing keeps `hidden` and `inert` as the immediate source of truth for focus and accessibility. `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` lets the hidden sheet finish sliding out, with the Panels launcher still visible. A sheet settling into the dock stays above the conversation until it arrives, so collapsing no longer drops it behind the chat. Live drag geometry is written to the sheet itself instead of the whole region, following the Vaul note that inherited custom properties restyle every descendant per frame.

**CSS budget.** The total Control UI CSS gzip budget was already exceeded on `main` (308,922 B against a 308,526 B cap), so any growth fails `control-ui-performance`. After consolidating to one motion token, reusing the existing page-reveal rule for push motion, logical `inset-inline-start` for the segmented thumb (no RTL rules) and native `visibility` interpolation for the drawer backdrop, the change adds 279 B gzip / 1,344 B raw (down from about 530 B gzip). Raw stays under its cap. @vyctorbrzezowski approved exceeding the gzip budget, so `totalCssGzipBytes` moves to 309,265 B (measured 309,201 B plus the 64 B build variance) with an approval note.

Accepted limits: engines without `allow-discrete` exit transitions (before Safari 18 / Chrome 117) still hide the sheet instantly, as they do today. An open panel tool or Details page stops presenting the moment the sheet closes, so it slides out with an empty body; keeping that content presented through the exit needs a closing state in the pane owner and is left as a follow-up. Escape and programmatic closes of the sidebar sheets stay instant.

<details>
<summary>Research: sources and what each one decided</summary>

| Source | What it established | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Apple: SwiftUI `Spring`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/spring) | Duration/bounce ↔ mass/stiffness/damping; `Spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.3)` → stiffness 157.9, damping 17.6 | Solver parameterization; unit test reproduces Apple's numbers |
| [Apple: `spring(duration:bounce:)`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/animation/spring(duration:bounce:blendduration:)) | Perceptual duration; bounce 0 is critically damped; springs preserve velocity when retargeted | Bounce 0 for sheets; velocity hand-off on release |
| [WWDC23 “Animate with springs”](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10158/) | Springs are the only curve that stays continuous with an initial velocity; use perceptual duration, not settle time, for UI timing | Gesture releases start at the finger's velocity |
| [WWDC18 “Designing Fluid Interfaces”](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2018/803/) ([implementation notes](https://github.com/nathangitter/fluid-interfaces)) | Project momentum with `UIScrollView.DecelerationRate.normal`; relative velocity; rubber-band at boundaries | `projectDistance`, close decision below the minimum, overscroll resistance |
| [Apple HIG: Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) | Resizable sheets rest at detents (medium ≈ half, large), resize by grabber or content | Dock/expanded detents; flicks step one detent |
| [Ionic iOS modal animation](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-framework/blob/main/core/src/components/modal/animations/ios.enter.ts) | iOS sheet presentation reproduced as `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` over 500 ms | Fitting target for the spring's pace |
| [Emil Kowalski: Building a drawer component (Vaul)](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/building-a-drawer-component), [Vaul constants](https://github.com/emilkowalski/vaul/blob/main/src/constants.ts) | Velocity flick (0.4 px/ms), 25% close threshold, damped overdrag, avoid per-frame inherited custom properties | Flick and dismiss thresholds; drag geometry on the sheet element |
| [Chrome: CSS `linear()` easing](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/css-ui/css-linear-easing-function) | `linear()` approximates springs with enough stops | One stop per frame from the closed-form solution |

**Fit study.** A grid search over Apple's spring space against the Ionic/Vaul iOS curve found the best match at bounce 0 and a 0.29–0.30 s perceptual duration (≈1.5% RMS of the travel distance over 600 ms). SwiftUI's default 0.5 s `.smooth` spring measured noticeably slower than iOS sheets, so the PR uses 0.3 s with no bounce. Critically damped springs never overshoot from rest and only overshoot when a release is faster than the spring's natural frequency, which is how momentum earns a little settle without any bounce at rest.

</details>

### How it moves

![Spring versus previous curve and the iOS curve; spring launched at release velocities](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41e35193-ea6a-4aeb-b5fc-ffad458f8d1b)

![How a released sheet decides where to rest](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdf99895-d1f6-4799-8b47-c32804e67246)

## Evidence

**Panels sheet, before (left) and after (right).** Same script, same touch input via Chrome DevTools Protocol, 390×844 mobile emulation. Steps include flicks, a slow drag past the top, close, and slow-motion replays with page animations at 20% speed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0034b4c1-abf7-41f5-a93f-5a8a2aa524f9

**Navigation drawer and Filter & sort sheet, before and after**, including swipe-down dismissal, a choice page, and tap-outside.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50afa312-b9c9-417f-99f5-f0c35508fe10

Before: flicking the grabber up stops where the finger lifts.

![Before: flick up leaves the sheet where the finger lifted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/266c6e28-0990-4962-bb40-6253b906abad)

After: the flick carries the sheet to the expanded detent.

![After: flick up settles on the expanded detent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e00d32fa-326e-41fa-b299-b944abc327aa)

Before: 120 ms after tapping ✕, the sheet is already gone.

![Before: sheet vanishes immediately on close](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f59c03a5-c4b1-4600-837c-1ab078a9d83b)

After: 120 ms after tapping ✕, the sheet is sliding away.

![After: sheet slides down on close](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51356edd-4e4b-4914-8348-da535d0efc5e)

**Measured motion.** Visible sheet height sampled every animation frame, before versus after:

![Measured visible height per frame for seven scenarios](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/690f131c-b692-4729-a1d9-9ddf2883bf2b)

**Tests**

- New `ui/src/e2e/mobile-sheet-motion.e2e.test.ts` (8 cases): spring entrance and slide-out exit with the launcher still visible; flicks through dock → expanded → dock → dismiss; slow releases keep their height and only close past half the minimum; header-space drag with tappable controls and the sliding segment thumb; push/pop direction for Details pages; Filter & sort swipe-down, spring-back and tap-outside; reduced motion stays instant. Five of these cases fail on `main` (no spring, no flick detents, no exit, no swipe).
- Unit: `spring.test.ts` (Apple's documented coefficients, monotonic critically damped curve, velocity hand-off, iOS-curve fit, CSS token sync), `gesture.test.ts`, `chat-mobile-host-release.test.ts`.
- Regression: 18 existing mobile and panel E2E suites (Inbox sheet, shell geometry, session menus, panel layout, side-panel clearance, pull requests, details, outbox, owner filter, and more), sidebar/details browser suites, and related unit suites pass. `mobile-inbox-sheet` now asserts the shared spring's duration (< 500 ms) instead of the old 240 ms curve, and the layout test helper treats a sheet that is sliding out as already closed.
- WebKit (Playwright 2370): open, expand, restore, flick up/down, flick-dismiss and close all animate (9–18 intermediate frames each) and reach the expected end states, confirming the `allow-discrete` exit in Safari's engine.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, `oxfmt --check`, `check:control-ui-controllers`, `git diff --check`, `test/scripts/control-ui-performance.test.ts`, and a local `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against the merge base (passes with the new cap: total CSS gzip 308,833 → 309,112 B).
- After the CSS consolidation, 12 mobile/panel E2E suites (59 tests, including all 8 new motion tests) pass again.
- Gesture tests are timing-independent: flicks dispatch input with explicit timestamps and slow placements pause before lifting, so CI load cannot turn a flick into a slow release. The shared Details test helper now ignores a sheet that is already `hidden` while it slides out (this fixed `session-progress-live-placement` on the first CI run). Both suites pass repeatedly locally.
- `chat-stream-runtime-budgets` › “commits a streamed delta burst…” failed once in CI; it also fails 2 of 3 local runs on the unchanged merge base (`92f70af`), so it is a pre-existing flake unrelated to this change.
- Local autoreview (shared helper, Codex engine, P0–P2, merge-base with `origin/main` → `8236d31`, before the CSS consolidation): no actionable findings. The reviewer saw the diff without the surrounding pane-owner and popover lifecycle code and did not execute tests.

**Not verified:** a physical iPhone in Safari or the native iOS app; captures use Chromium mobile emulation and Playwright WebKit. Drag cost on low-end phones was not profiled.

title: improve(ui): let session links accept typing while the page loads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a session link showed a "Loading…" placeholder where the composer belongs until the Gateway connected and the session route resolved, so anything typed in that window was lost.

## User Impact

User impact: a session link's composer accepts typing from first paint — click or tap into it right away instead of waiting behind "Loading…". Focus stays with the operator, as in the chat composer, so nothing is auto-focused. What you type survives every loading frame and lands in the session's composer with its caret, and pressing Enter early sends the message once, after the session has opened through the normal checks. Text never reaches a session the link didn't open: a missing or inaccessible session, or navigating elsewhere first, means nothing is sent.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/376d76b6-162d-4ec7-b5b4-3fb68e268d26)

## Why This Change Was Made

- The static boot frame (`ui/index.html`) now holds a real textarea in its composer slot. A small inline script owns its keys before any bundle loads: Enter only records intent (Shift+Enter, IME commits, touch Return and the saved send shortcut follow the chat composer). The loading text moves above the composer and hides once there is a draft.
- `app/boot-composer.ts` keeps that one element across the Solid connecting splash and the in-shell route skeleton, restoring focus after each move. It retires on any pushed or history navigation, so a draft can't follow the operator to another session.
- The route's chat pane adopts the draft only after the route loader has resolved the session — after connect, the session lookup and its access checks. A saved draft for that session stays first and is never auto-sent.
- An early Enter becomes a *queued submit* in the chat composer. It is sent through the same `submitDraft` admission the send button uses, once the composer's own loading hold (route verification, outbox scope) clears; any edit withdraws it. The same rule now covers pressing Enter in the real composer during those holds, which previously inserted a newline.
- The boot composer paints the chat composer's surface color and mirrors its geometry, including autogrow and the narrow and mobile editing forms, so the handoff doesn't move the frame or the text. A composer that mounts already focused on mobile no longer animates up from a compact form nobody saw.

Accepted edge cases: on touch devices Return inserts a newline (as in the chat composer), so an early send waits for the send button. Placeholder copy in the static frame is English, like the existing "Loading…".

## Evidence

Before — the composer slot is a "Loading…" placeholder, and typing goes nowhere:

![Before: Loading placeholder over the composer slot while the session loads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0357a713-c5e4-4b14-b373-c5f1051c8780)

![Before: after loading, nothing typed earlier was kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f5cf8b5-d750-4d90-8ed7-c0b27c9394c9)

After — the composer accepts typing while the session loads, and the session opens with that draft in place:

![After: typing into the composer while the session loads, on the chat composer's surface](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51b92de4-25f6-424b-ae9c-6b691d829f72)

![After: the session's composer holds the early draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d8900ad-6cd7-4ae7-919d-d4e9de989da5)

- New `ui/src/e2e/chat-boot-composer.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, real bundle): the boot composer is not auto-focused; typing during connect and route hold, then Enter, sends exactly one `chat.send` only after `sessions.resolve`; an unsent multi-line draft keeps its text, focus and caret; a 90-frame recorder proves every animation frame through the handoff shows one composer at one size with the whole draft (desktop and iPhone emulation); a missing session never sends and the draft doesn't follow navigation.
- Updated `chat-snapshot-route` e2e: Enter while route authority is pending is held, then sent once after it settles.
- Unit: `boot-composer.test.ts`, queued-submit cases in `chat-composer-actions.test.ts`, and skeleton accessibility checks.
- Geometry sweep at 1280/820/400 px and iPhone 390 px, light and dark, typing continuously across frame swaps: no lost characters, no page errors, zero non-input CLS, and boot and chat composer frames identical at handoff (single and multi-line).
- 27 related Control UI e2e suites pass locally (splash pixel parity, loading geometry, cold/warm boot, outbox, reconnect, drafts, mobile). `boot-module-boundaries` placement-recovery cases fail identically on unmodified `main`.
- Performance (`scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`, built bundles, 21 interleaved base/candidate pairs, untraced): first contentful paint 44–48 → 40–44 ms, static shell unchanged, CLS unchanged. Shell and composer readiness are bimodal on this host in both builds (chat ready with the shell ≈260 ms, or shell ≈160 ms then chat ≈300 ms); the mode split was 8/21 vs 11/21 and within-mode times match. Startup JS gzip is unchanged (−5 B); the HTML document grows by ~1.1 KB gzip (inline styles and script) and chat boot JS by under 1 KB gzip.
- PR CI's first run caught that auto-focusing the boot composer moved focus away from model pickers, question docks and route-readiness flows (6 UI e2e files); the third commit leaves focus to the operator and those files pass locally. `chat-widget-retention` (live widget handoff) fails identically on unmodified `87facf07` locally.
- Local autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, max priority P2, branch `87facf07..HEAD`): first pass found one P2 (keep the caret through the handoff), fixed in the second commit and covered by the e2e caret check. The re-review raised one P2 about an IME composition open at the exact moment of handoff; declined: a CDP IME probe across both the connect and route handoffs shows the composing text is committed into the session composer and typing continues (`hello にほ` → `hello にほん`), so only the candidate window restarts — rare and recoverable, and documented in `boot-composer.ts`.

title: fix(ui): mobile shows two pills for one PR after publishing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the mobile Control UI shows two pills for one pull request ("#N +adds −dels" and "PR published") after a PR is published from the session.

## User Impact

User impact: on mobile web, a single PR keeps a single pill that moves through its lifecycle — **Publish PR** → **Publishing PR…** → **#N** → the PR pill with its draft/open/merged state and checks. Sessions with several PRs still show one pill per PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication pill stayed eligible whenever a publication result was retained, even after the PR snapshot listed the PR that receipt created. A published receipt now folds into the listed PR it names (matched by repository and number), so the PR pill continues the lifecycle instead of a second pill appearing. While the snapshot catches up, the receipt pill already shows the PR number, so the swap is visually continuous. Verification failures and other recovery states stay on the publication pill. On mobile, dismissing that PR also retires its receipt (matching the desktop row), and the mobile Details root drops the now-redundant "Review publication" entry. Desktop surfaces are unchanged.

## Evidence

Mobile web, 393×852, dark theme, mocked Gateway via the Control UI e2e harness.

It fails on `origin/main` (`expected 'PR published' to contain '#4321'`) and passes with the fix.
- New e2e `hides a published PR's single mobile pill without reviving its receipt`: fails with the receipt-retirement hunk removed (the receipt reappears as a pill), passes with it.

title: fix: child session activity ring freezes during startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: newly spawned child sessions show a frozen activity ring while their workspace is being prepared.

## User Impact

The activity ring animates from accepted startup through execution. Real turn, global-lane, and recorded capacity waits still show a paused ring labeled **Queued**. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued presentation was inferred from execution not having started yet. A visible worktree child can spend several seconds preparing its checkout before that marker is set. Project accepted preparation as active instead, retaining explicit wait facts for queued presentation in both RPC-backed and native runs. Execution clocks, admission, cancellation, and scheduling are unchanged; no CSS is changed.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4279f410-ff62-4118-ba9d-bd37c8d267d2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/c2164b84-64f5-4746-ae9d-2b5227a27789)

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway + Control UI, a deterministic local model, and a visible managed-worktree child with a real 10-second checkout setup script:

| Child-row observation | Before | After |

| Startup ring | `session-glyph__ring--queued` | `session-glyph__ring` |
| Computed animation play state | `paused` | `running` |
| `getAnimations()` play state | `paused` | `running` |

[Proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188147#issuecomment-6517274933).

- Startup regressions failed on the base for the intended queued-vs-running mismatch, then passed with the fix.
- CI run `41014664978`, head `43cb1e45118b72dc5854974afbf7eea9e8e514b4`: complete failed-job logs contain exactly two failed tests, both stale startup-consumer expectations. Corrected accepted `chat.send` to expect running, and gave the metrics fixture an actual global-lane wait/resume. A source audit also corrected describe/list coverage to distinguish active preparation from genuinely queued follow-up input. No production code changed in this repair.
- Fresh validation reran the previous 62 affected tests plus all three additional consumer suites: **86 tests across 7 files passed** in the bounded same-order replay (151.00s command wall time, including 98.99s cold unit-shard compilation and a 46.84s Gateway shard). New-head CI seconds are not available yet.

The exact same command/order then passed all 86 tests. That same interrupt test passed in the original exact-head CI log (681ms). No SQLite lock repair is claimed; the original failure is retained rather than relabeled as a fix.
- Fresh targeted Oxlint passed for all three repaired consumer files; `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-test Gateway-server and Gateway-methods typecheck graphs, targeted format, and `git diff --check` passed. The original `pnpm build` proof still covers the unchanged production code.
- Independent local autoreview of base `c49e07385f8d176` to the original working-tree candidate, P0–P2, with intact lifecycle context found one stale lane-wait fixture, corrected before publication. The later ClawSweeper P2 consumer-contract finding is addressed by this update.
- Simplification: removed execution-start-as-queue inference, no new production state; production net −3 lines, regression tests net +9 lines. The separate nine-line allocation preserves explicit startup, queued-input, and lane-wait/resume contracts without adding another test harness.

title: fix(ui): attachments get extra top-left padding in the resting mobile composer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: attachment chips in the mobile chat composer sit with extra top and left padding (8px further right and 7px further down than in the expanded composer) whenever the composer is in its resting one-line layout.

## User Impact

User impact: on phones, attached files and images line up with the composer's controls and keep the same position whether or not the draft is being edited, instead of floating inside a second inset.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/82ae50ec-a50a-4179-9ddc-453ae6825a89)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/00f62d3e-1c9a-4356-bf91-2b93c3cb3194)

## Why This Change Was Made

The resting mobile composer (`data-mobile-composer="true"`, `data-composer-editing="false"`) pads its surface `7px 8px` for the bare input row. The attachment rail in the composer lede already carries the editor inset plus the remove-button hit slop from `composer.css`, so the two insets stacked. The reply/context strip in the same lede already cancels that row padding; the rail now does the same. Desktop and the editing state are unchanged (no row padding there).

CSS budget: main is already over the fixed total-CSS gzip ceiling, so `control-ui-performance` allows at most 64 B of growth. A first revision that named the row inset as custom properties cost +90 B and failed that check; the rule now uses literal values and measures +37 B total CSS gzip vs main (`pnpm ui:build`, same compressor as CI).

title: fix(ui): user messages span the whole chat column after resizing message width
body:
Related: #178226 (exposed this regression)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: your own chat messages (and other participants' messages) stretch across nearly the whole transcript column whenever a chat message width is saved, which now happens on any composer border drag, arrow-key resize or double-click since #178226.

## User Impact

User impact: after widening or resetting the message width from the composer border (or in Settings → Appearance), user and peer bubbles stay right- or left-aligned at their normal size, `min(900px, 68%)` of the reading column, exactly as they look with no saved width. Assistant replies, tool rows and activity still fill the wider column, as before. Mobile and bubble-mode layouts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A saved width sets `--chat-thread-max-width` to the chosen width and `--chat-message-max-width: 100%` on the chat pane so agent content fills the widened column. The base `.chat-group` column cap also read that token (`var(--chat-message-max-width, min(900px, 68%))`), so participant bubbles lost their own cap and became as wide as the column. Before #178226 a saved width only came from Settings, so this was rare; border resizing made it the common case.

The participant cap now keeps its default proportion and treats the token only as an upper bound: `min(var(--chat-message-max-width, 100%), 900px, 68%)`. Role-specific caps for assistant, tool and reply groups, the mobile 82%/88% rules and bubble mode's 88%/94% overrides are untouched. Forwarded agent messages stay on the assistant column, matching their unsaved geometry.

## Evidence

Screenshots: real Control UI against the mock Gateway with synthetic data, 1920×900, light theme, after dragging the composer border wider (saved width). Cropped to the chat pane.

Before (current main):

![Before: user bubble spans the widened column](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/562e06de-4b4c-48ff-815e-466c2996e9dd)

After (this PR):

![After: user bubble keeps its default share; assistant text fills the widened column](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e27e7416-a0ed-400a-a12d-bac08b487c09)

- **Real flow regression (new e2e):** `composer-layout.e2e` opens a chat with a long user message and an assistant reply at 1920×900, drags the composer border wider, and asserts the saved width widened the column by more than 200 px, the assistant text still fills it (wider than 980 px), and the user bubble equals `min(900px, 68%)` of its group. Fails on main (user bubble at 1.47× its cap, i.e. the full column), passes here. Test 2.0 s, file run 15.7 s including the shared UI build.
- **Component regression:** `chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx` now checks the viewer bubble keeps its default share in default, saved and narrow modes at 1440/1024/390 px, LTR/RTL, shared/direct, light/dark. Desktop cases fail on main (`expected 1294 to be close to 900`), all 8 pass here (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 6.1 s wall).
- Sibling suites pass unchanged: `chat-responsive.browser` (full file, 6.2 s, includes the configured-width tool/composer case), `chat-image-loading.browser` (5.0 s), `chat-composer-width.browser` (4.1 s).
- `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, stylelint on touched files, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Local AutoReview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, branch mode, P0–P2): scoped-clean.
- Not changed: the composer border drag preview only sets `--chat-thread-max-width`, so during a first drag beyond 980 px assistant text stays at its unsaved 980 px cap until release. That is pre-existing and independent of the bubble fix; user bubbles are now consistent between preview and saved states.

## Contributor credit

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

title: fix(ui): mobile composer loses its top padding while the keyboard is open
body:
octopool: pr_view served from shared cache (hit); freshness is not confirmed by this cache hit
Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

Related: #161134, #152608

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the mobile chat composer intermittently loses its top padding while focused with the iOS Safari keyboard open, so the draft sits against the composer's top edge.

## User Impact

User impact: on phones the draft keeps the same padding inside the composer whether or not the keyboard is open, regardless of keyboard type, QuickType bar or Safari toolbar state. Desktop split panes between 161px and 320px tall also keep the normal editor padding (14px of height moves from the transcript to the composer). Panes of 160px or less, such as a landscape phone keyboard or a nearly closed split, keep the existing compact layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat conversation's short-pane step (`@container chat-conversation (max-height: 320px)`) removed the input-row padding and shrank the editor inset to 2px. A portrait phone keyboard leaves a conversation pane of roughly 300–340px, so small changes in the visible viewport flipped the composer across that step.

The 320px step now keeps its footer and gap trims and caps the editor at one line through the existing line-cap formula, which includes the editor's normal inset. Removing the inset moves to a 160px step. Only nearly closed panes reach it, including the landscape keyboard case that #161134 trimmed for. A full-inset composer overflows that 150px landscape viewport by 1px.

## Evidence

iPhone 15 (WebKit), composer focused, keyboard open (302px conversation pane):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: draft placeholder pressed against the composer's top edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92b4eecc-c4ad-4dda-8dd1-4f028f7d6af2) | ![After: draft keeps its normal top padding](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff52f353-27e3-47e8-aa42-e4e4d81d1742) |

- **Regression test:** the new `chat-footer-layout.browser.test.ts` case measures text inset from the composer top while a pane goes from 340px to 300px. On the base it fails at phone and desktop widths (13px becomes 3px); with this change it passes. It also checks that the short pane still caps the editor at one line.
- **Browser tests:** `chat-footer-layout.browser.test.ts` and `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` passed (77 tests).
- **Control UI e2e (bundled build):** 33 files and 151 tests passed. These include `mobile-shell-geometry` (keyboard open/pan/dismissed, landscape keyboard at 150px, a 94px desktop pane) and `chat-footer` (248px and 200px canvases with notices, queued input and Details). They also cover composer size/layout/height/redesign/picker/readability, `chat-responsive`, `chat-loading-geometry`, split and rail panes, question flow, inline approvals (`exec-approvals-dirty-target-switch`), attachments (`chat-attachment-read-lifecycle`), PR/CI/progress notices, native plugin UI and outbox recovery.
- **Real-browser sweep on built UI, base vs. this branch:** WebKit with the iPhone 15 profile, portrait, focused composer, visual viewport from 260px to 659px, with and without a 24px caret pan; WebKit landscape from 120px to 361px; Chromium desktop with the conversation frame from 94px to 420px, both empty and with a multi-line draft. On the base, the text inset drops from 13px to 3px once the pane falls below 320px. This branch keeps 13px in every portrait state (panes from 202px to 601px). The composer fits and actions stay reachable in every state that fit on the base, and panes of 160px or less match the base.
- **Static checks:** stylelint, oxlint, oxfmt check and `tsgo` (ui-chat test shard) all passed.
- **Review:** local autoreview (Codex, branch against `origin/main`, P0–P2) at `5f8482d` reported no findings.

Tradeoff: landscape panes from 161px to 320px tall (for example, landscape with Safari toolbars and no keyboard) keep the landscape editor's normal 10px padding instead of 2px, which leaves about 26px less transcript there. The composer and actions still fit.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ui): Details "View all" and "Show more" links hover with a square background
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: hovering **View all processes** / **Show N more** (and the other Details "Show more" text links) in the session Details pane paints a square background box.

## User Impact

User impact: Details "View all" and "Show more" links behave like text links: hover brightens the text and adds no background. Row-style controls (process rows, subagent summary, automation rows, stop buttons) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `.chat-details button:hover` rule paints `--surface-hover` on every Details button, including the text-link buttons whose own hover only changes color. Each link's hover rule now outranks that shared background and brightens the text instead: `.chat-details-processes__view-all` (new hover rule), `.chat-details__more` (existing color hover, now with `background: none`), and the Automations `button[class]:hover` (restates its transparent background).

## Evidence

title: feat: allow scoped operators to manage their automations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators with write access cannot ask an agent to create and manage their own automations without Gateway administrator authority.

## User Impact

Adds `operator.cron` for authenticated agent-turn automation access, implied by `operator.write`. Users can schedule and manage jobs within the existing conversation/account ownership boundary without receiving `operator.admin`. Cron-only access does not grant chat, general write, or global scheduler administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing requester grant and job ownership checks instead of treating every scheduler caller as an administrator. One runtime-method mapping covers creation, job management, history, and scratch access. Scheduled runs preserve the initiating operator scopes. Direct/global scheduler APIs, privileged binding, live revocation, and tool restrictions retain their existing checks.

Signed requester transports preserve private scoped-creation provenance without promoting it to local-owner or management authority. No new state owner or storage schema is introduced. The config baseline is regenerated for the accepted scope.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto main `f8fe5864ab3aab29ffeab8b98fef51d3014e5349`; current head is `01d2a7a7edda96784c97de77f5af43040223cfbc`. The only rebase conflict was the generated configuration checksum, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. `git range-diff` confirmed the feature and regression patches were unchanged by rebase. `pnpm config:docs:check` and `git diff --check` pass. All 145 focused post-rebase tests pass across scope implication, Gateway auth config, signed creator transports, Cron policy, and persisted scheduled continuation.
- [Rebased-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152994878) exposed two failures, repaired in the current head: the contained-symlink test now accepts the earlier symlink refusal while still requiring denial; `usage.cost` no longer gives a freshness TTL to a refreshing lower-cache result. Two cost-handler regressions fail before the fix and pass after it for single-agent and all-agent reads, without increasing timeouts. The cost repair reuses the existing cache completeness predicate (production +2 lines; no new owner).
- CI repair validation: all 6 skill-read tests and all 44 cost/cache/consumer tests pass; formatting and diff checks pass. An independent P0–P2 review of all three repair files found no actionable issues. [Current-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154293835) on `01d2a7a7edda96784c97de77f5af43040223cfbc`, including all Android and PostgreSQL lanes, changed Node shards, clean-install type/lint checks, and both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks. The [real Gateway quarter-backfill regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154293835/job/124398236592) passed in 10.809s on that head. Local full Gateway E2E setup, core typecheck, and lint preparation failed because the shared installation had fs-safe 0.26.13 versus lockfile 0.26.15 (missing native-asset pin/export); the shared installation was not modified. Those local environment failures are retained separately from the passing clean-install CI evidence.
- Red/green regressions for scoped creation and signed requester grants. Both `operator.cron` and `operator.write` pass real token mint/verification, production in-process dispatch, owned-job persistence, foreign-conversation/account refusal, and revocation during validation before persistence. Refused mutations leave storage unchanged; no local-owner or management authority is added.
- Reproduced the five stale CI consumer assertions and updated ingress/rejected-manager expectations without weakening their security checks. All 205 consumer tests and 9 transport tests pass. Scope implication, config, scheduled-scope preservation, grant/token, and prompt-stability suites also pass.
- Before this rebase, core/source-test typechecks, focused lint/format, config checks, line-cap/test-line ratchets, and diff checks passed. Main `f0586d2e3e0d73c` was integrated only for a generated-config conflict; affected checks were rerun. These are prior-head results, not current-head clean-install evidence.
- Pre-rebase local independent P0–P2 reviews of the implementation and the consumer/signed-effect repair found no actionable issues. The unchanged signed-token implementation was unavailable to the implementation reviewer; its changed regression tests and grant owner were reviewed.
- [Pre-rebase exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41003845653) on `3eb0998e661ed1fd7681c0cfb01b16799cc552e0`, including both Android lanes, all PostgreSQL lanes, changed Node shards, and required aggregate checks. The earlier Android emulator-setup failure did not recur.
- [ClawSweeper's completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188090#issuecomment-6514958472) of current head `01d2a7a7edda96784c97de77f5af43040223cfbc` has no actionable findings and no remaining before-merge items. CI was still pending when that review completed and is now green.
- Gap: no live-provider Gateway turn or full WebSocket signed-request test was run. Proof uses production admission, dispatch, and Cron storage with mocked model execution.

<details>
<summary>Validation cost and change size</summary>

All changed test files were exercised with `--maxWorkers=1`; wall times include compilation/setup:

| Suite | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Creator authority context | 38.20s |
| Gateway auth config | 6.03s |
| Scheduled operator continuation | 75.80s |
| Signed runtime identity | 7.03s |
| Fresh operator admission | 9.52s |
| Gateway Cron policy | 18.75s |
| Scope implication | 1.07s |
| Chat, requester authority, authenticated connection consumers | 53.37s combined |
| Signed/embedded/CLI creator transports | 53.20s |
| Authenticated connection consumer after assertion simplification | 24.17s |
| Skill-read CI repair (6 tests) | 47.17s |
| Cost freshness and cache consumers (44 tests) | 80.09s |

Transport execution itself takes about 14s; most wall time is compilation. The existing scheduled-continuation suite exercises real persistence/restoration and authority lifecycle, which helper-only tests cannot prove. The successful pre-rebase CI run's start-to-final-update window was 1,417 seconds (23m37s). The current-head CI run took 1,522 seconds (25m22s), including setup and parallel jobs; neither is summed runner time.

Production delta against integrated main: +65/-24 lines. Tests: +376/-73 lines. The original 284-line allocation covers distinct admission, signed final-effect, and continuation-scope regressions; the CI cost-cache repair adds 19 test lines in an existing suite. No shared test scalar was raised.

title: fix(test): align clone retries with concise failure notices

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The test continues to protect live clone-recovery guidance, session-row diagnostics, durable failure context, preserved project intent and successful retry in both worktree modes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main #187883 deliberately separates concise display copy from retained diagnostics. The existing retry cases still expected the diagnostic in display content. They now assert the exact concise notice and independently check the original cause and run ID in the durable transcript event; no test case is removed or assertion weakened to ignore the failure.

These are unresolved local cleanup gaps, not claimed passing evidence or causal fixes. No deadline or assertion was relaxed. The complete CI-matching Bun replay passed.

title: fix: transcript reads fail after concurrent database preparation
body:
Related: #184511.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes transcript reads failing with a physical-owner validation error when database preparation completes ahead of a queued read.

## User Impact

Queued reads use the current validation receipt for the same physical database. Revocation and foreign-file checks remain in force; no retry, schema, configuration or permission change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker captured a validation receipt before awaiting read admission. A preceding writer can renew that receipt during the wait, leaving the real worker with revoked proof. Capture now occurs inside the existing admitted operation, after its predecessors settle. The owner is byte-identical on guest-stack head a17fcb30 and main base 8da85beb, establishing an inherited race rather than a membership change.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, the original filtered-sharing file passed 10/10 in three separate runs on each side (30/30 on a17fcb30, 30/30 on main 8da85beb); those passing replays alone did not establish a fix.
- A deterministic owner-bound regression warms a real worker, holds the next admission, renews the same file's writer validation and releases the read. It fails on main with the exact CI error, `Session reader validation does not match its current physical owner`, and passes with this repair. The test does not replace worker execution or returned data.
- Node 24 owner, schema-freshness and original filtered-sharing suites passed 27/27. Core and affected test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. SQLite T1 calls remain 168 → 168. Main's test ceiling is unchanged: 6,283,332 lines against 6,329,653 allowed.
- Combined scoped wall time was 129.98 s, including compiler preparation and real-worker lifecycle. The new owner case took 25.719 s; it boots/joins the real native worker to prove receipt transfer, which a mocked result cannot establish. Hosted CI timing remains pending.
- Independent AutoReview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, full changed modules plus admission/physical-owner context) reported scoped-clean. It did not execute tests. Simplification retained the existing admission owner and moved the existing capture; production net growth is one line, with one 51-line boundary regression and no new state or helper API.
- No CI rerun or dispatch was requested. The historical CI attempt was not instrumented, so the controlled reproduction proves this pre-existing mechanism, not the exact scheduling of that attempt.

### CI typecheck correction

The first head's CI caught a missing `databaseAgentId` in the new regression input. The follow-up binds the request to the fixture's actual database agent; production behavior and the demonstrated admission repair are unchanged. Node 24 reader tests passed **7/7** after this correction, and the actual owning `tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json` leaf, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Prior 27-test and independent source-review evidence remains scoped to the original production move; one exact-head re-review is requested for the corrected head. No test deadline, check or ceiling was relaxed.

### Current exact-head build gate — 2026-10-30

The corrected head `bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6` has [clean exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055#issuecomment-6513913355), with no Before-merge items or findings, and its typecheck failure is cleared. [CI run 40998529819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819) is blocked by [build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340): the bundled root-help renderer timed out after **120,000 ms** in `scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.ts`. This leaves `openclaw/ci-gate` red.

One bounded local `pnpm build` at this exact head passed under verified Node **24.22.1**, with isolated HOME/config/state: total build phases **3m 30s**, startup metadata **4.22s**. The previous [6c62e05e build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40994523700/job/123864788070) also passed; the only source delta to the corrected head is the regression input binding, not production code. The later main build passed too, and no intervening repair in the helper or root-help owner was found. These passing controls do not establish a causal fix for the failed hosted build. The timeout remains **unattributed / unreproduced locally**, not waived or labeled green. No CI rerun, dispatch, no-op push or timeout increase was used. The PR remains unmerged under the requested green-only gate.

### Bounded root-help timeout audit — 2026-10-30

The [failed bundled root-help child](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340) reached its **120,000 ms budget, 120,008 ms elapsed**, on Node 24.22.1. The hang remains **unattributed**, not established as inherited or a shared flake.

Read-only run-creation window: **2026-10-29 04:18:24Z through 2026-10-30 04:18:24Z**. Logs were observed October 30 at **04:22:31Z–04:29:38Z**, not backdated to the creation cutoff. All 24 completed scheduled-main runs returned in that window were inspected. The other-PR sample selected the latest six completed non-cancelled distinct branches per four-hour bin, from at most 100 returned candidates per bin, excluding the guest stack and its two repairs. This is a bounded sample, not an exhaustive incident-rate estimate.

- Main: **0 matching timeout hits / 24 readable log misses**; 23 target jobs succeeded and one was cancelled after metadata completed.
- Other PRs: **0 hits / 3 readable executed-job misses**; **33 skipped target jobs** do not count as executions.
- **No unresolved read gaps.** Initial job-list 502s were recovered through the attempt jobs API, reconciling both pages against total counts.
- Successful main metadata phases: **23 samples, min 2.95 s / median 3.75 s / max 6.59 s**. Other-PR phases: **3 samples, 3.23–3.79 s**. These enclosing-phase durations are not individual-child measurements and do not justify increasing its deadline.

The failed job actually built synthetic merge **c87bcb9ca45e19b2f986840c500a471837028fbb**, with main parent **acb102d176c49d7df4360edb58e7b3fc1b490c9e** and PR parent **bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6**. The previous and corrected PR heads had different hosted integration bases. The prior passing local build was the raw PR head, not this synthetic merge; it cannot exclude a base/composition effect. This audit did not replay the exact synthetic merge locally.

At that executed merge, renderBundledRootHelpText imports the root-help bundle and calls outputRootHelp with fresh isolated HOME/state/workspace and a fixed synthetic config. Root help assembles command descriptors rather than registering live command runtimes. The repository-owned runtime-emitted import graph, erasing type-only imports, visited **1,582 eager source modules** without reaching either changed file. The dynamic legacy-plugin loader requires a nonempty external-plugin list; the isolated render uses bundled assets, not user-installed legacy plugins. Resolution gaps were confined to external fs-safe/proc-safe packages, whose boundaries were inspected; this is not a complete native/bundled runtime trace. The production delta adds no imports or top-level initialization: it moves validation capture inside an already-invoked admitted reader operation. **No causal path from this repair to the help hang was found.**

Existing [#147932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147932) states a live-config fast-path scope; [#187644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187644) explicitly changes exit-code diagnostics, not timeouts. Neither provides a proven repair for this hang. With no matching comparison timeout, no reproduced original hang and no demonstrated cause, no speculative owner patch, timeout increase, rerun/dispatch, empty push or chase rebase was made. The requested green-only landing remains blocked and is escalated to the requesting maintainer.

title: fix(ui): completed turns scatter work across many Worked disclosures
body:
Related: #183267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completed dashboard turns scatter their work across many **Worked** disclosures, leave work recorded after the answer hanging below it, and split tool-result images out of their tool group, since #183267 changed the completed-turn presentation.

## User Impact

User impact: a completed dashboard turn again shows one **Worked for X** disclosure above the answer, holding the preamble, commentary, reasoning and tool activity in their original order. Work recorded after the answer sits above it, tool-result images stay with the tool that produced them, and speech bubble view keeps its single activity disclosure instead of wrapping it in a second **Worked** row. The stored transcript stays intact; existing live-turn, search and handoff boundaries are retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

#183267 by @Marvinthebored replaced the single completed-turn rollup with per-envelope splitting (`chat-work-chunks.ts`), so narration became visible between one **Worked** disclosure per work stretch. The single rollup was a deliberate design by @vyctorbrzezowski, and replaying real transcripts (Anthropic, OpenAI, Codex and agent API runs) at `ad55c5e`, `e7f0546` and current main showed the split presentation also introduced regressions, listed below.

This is a forward change that restores the earlier presentation in the files #183267 changed, rather than a revert commit. It removes the splitting module, its tool-card envelope bookkeeping, the split-fragment action/footer/terminal-status fields and the per-stretch timing, and restores the rollup's session timing and the earlier test expectations (including the three e2e expectations later adapted in `8c05667`). Later unrelated main work is kept: #186323, the published-PR handoff split (`4d50f6c`), grouped work without failed counts (`210b364`), cached row display facts (#186512), the video widget lazy-import wait, and the empty-group guard from #186499 for provider voice groups. The `presentationOwnsFooter` clauses from #186499 and #186681 go away with the fields they guarded. The test-line scalar returns the 2,089 lines #183267 added.

<details>
<summary>Regressions observed on main that this restores</summary>

1. Empty **Worked** rows before answers that carry (empty) OpenAI reasoning.
2. With **Show thinking**, inline reasoning moved into a collapsed **Worked**.
3. With tool calls hidden, stacks of empty **Worked** disclosures.
4. Work recorded after the answer rendered between the answer and its footer.
5. Speech bubble view wrapped the activity summary in **Worked**: two clicks, summary hidden.
6. Turn duration lost after switching sessions in one pane.
7. Per-stretch browser previews showed stale or duplicate tab previews.
8. Live turns split and regrouped.
9. A pre-handoff receipt became its own reply with a second header and footer.
10. Reply jumps expanded unrelated disclosures, because fragments shared persisted IDs.
11. Duplicate narration previously hidden in the rollup became visible.
12. `collapseCompletedTurnWork` ran 5–10x slower.
13. Narration containing Markdown characters disabled splitting, so that envelope's narration merged while plain narration split, out of order with its tool calls.
14. Tool-result images (for example `view_image` frames) split out of their tool group into standalone assistant rows.

</details>

## Evidence

Screenshots: real Control UI against the mock Gateway with synthetic data, 1100 px, light theme. Before is current main (`589348d`), after is this branch.

**Flat completed turn with narration between tool calls and a test run after the answer**

Before:

![Flat completed turn on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02af3fbf-bbdb-468f-8de6-7bdebb3f5e27)

After (collapsed):

![Flat completed turn with this branch, collapsed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94c3132e-d59b-4602-b58a-3a6109231075)

After (expanded):

![Flat completed turn with this branch, expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/398fe288-42b6-475d-a6f4-4409eb6a7904)

**Speech bubble view, same turn**

Before:

![Speech bubble view on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95e8384c-27cf-4f4c-a46e-d24d45dcb1aa)

After:

![Speech bubble view with this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef8aebc4-b832-4b85-9c4d-021ea82a8ab7)

**`view_image` tool result with two frames**

Before:

![view_image turn on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e158c7c-d514-4064-9b4c-2e39d5cd8045)

After:

![view_image turn with this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb176141-56d9-4c97-acc7-63d5603defc0)

Tests:

- New regressions in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` (Markdown and plain narration stay in one ordered rollup, tool-result images stay in their tool group, post-answer work moves above the answer, bubble mode gets no rollup) fail on main's presentation code and pass here (4/4 red on `589348d`, green on this branch).
- `chat-bubble-activity.e2e` now asserts no `.chat-work-group` in bubble view and one activity disclosure that opens the tool summary in a single click.
- `vitest.ui` over `ui/src/pages/chat` and `ui/src/lib/chat`: 629 files passed.
- Mock-Gateway e2e over every `ui/src/e2e/chat-*` suite: 1046 tests passed. The 17 `*.real-gateway` suites failed at setup in this shared worktree (Gateway entrypoint/plugin build not prepared; no assertion ran) and are not passing live-Gateway evidence. The original PR CI also skipped its real-Gateway lane. `chat-loading-geometry` hit a transient artifact lock and passes on rerun. `chat-stream-runtime-budgets` (delta-burst commits) and `chat-outbox-migration` (v3 Blob migration) fail identically on current main `589348d` in a side-by-side rerun, so they are not caused by this change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`: pass.
- Local autoreview (branch mode, base `589348d`, P1): no actionable findings.

## Review repairs and current validation

Independent review and the subsequent full CI identified these additional cases in the proposed rollup, now fixed:

- A terminal error or aborted tool envelope recorded after an answer stays visible, outside completed work.
- A freshly opened pane restores elapsed time only when its loaded completed reply matches the session metadata. Cached projections retain that timing, and switching session, agent or Gateway cannot borrow another turn's recap.
- A completed assistant answer containing both text and tools retains assistant ownership, visible text and reply/copy actions. Ordinary assistant messages reuse their prepared display text instead of sanitizing it again.
- Legacy mixed forwarded narration retains its tool grouping and sender-owned file links. An explicitly completed forwarded answer (`final_answer` or `stop`) keeps its visible answer and actions.

The existing presentation, recap and message owners implement these repairs; no additional state owner or compatibility path was introduced. Focused regressions fail on the uncorrected PR head and pass with the repairs. The terminal error/abort cases were relocated into the existing grouping suite to reuse its history assertions and keep the thread test file within its line cap.

Focused repair validation: 283 tests passed across the chat owners and progress suite. The latest grouping and action refinements passed 205 affected tests across seven suites, plus UI and UI-test typechecks and targeted lint/format checks. Both CI failures reproduced locally before repair. Explicit forwarded-answer cases also fail on the original PR grouping and pass with the final implementation. After the test-only relocation, both terminal cases were again confirmed red on the uncorrected presentation and green with the fix (1.22 seconds wrapper wall time for the green run). Line-cap and test-line ratchets pass without raising their baselines (6,280,129 test lines against a 6,326,480 ceiling). Fresh independent reviews of the initial repairs and the final CI repair delta returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Full PR CI run 41003470362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41003470362) passed on head `12eef1abf280e31b008795e8c90eb16e9d1c1362`. Its tested merge `9ddca045716bc844e7084eec72314375cdb863a8` includes #186061; the merged source preserves per-message timestamps, Reply controls, hover/touch behavior, and main's grouped-message CSS.

## Risk and coverage

This changes how completed-turn content is grouped, so failure visibility, reply actions, run ownership and cached timing are the main regression risks. The focused tests exercise those boundaries. The screenshots above use the real Control UI with a mock Gateway and synthetic messages; they are not live-Gateway proof. Earlier broad test results above describe the original implementation and are not relabeled as runs on the repair commit. No successful real-Gateway run is claimed.

title: fix(daemon): avoid repeated Windows scheduler engine drift warnings
body:
Supersedes #167827, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.
Fixes #167778.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Windows service drift warnings when Task Scheduler exports `UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine=true` for an otherwise healthy Gateway task.

## User Impact

Status and Doctor stop treating this known scheduler-populated value as an unexplained edit. Real launcher and account changes still appear, and replacement/publication checks continue protecting the engine value from silent loss. No migration or user action is required; native Windows execution was not independently repeated here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing comparison owner accepts only the known `true` value during reporting, alongside its existing `false` default. It retains strict comparisons when a replacement command or prepared XML is supplied. Account aliases already use SID equivalence from #169481.

This independently reimplemented replacement adds five production lines, two documentation lines, and 28 regression-test lines. There is no equivalent dead or duplicate code in this owner to remove safely. The separate 28-line test allocation covers the reporting regression, a real launcher-drift control, and publication protection; the shared baseline scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Base: current main `c633ec6376e1ce6cdf6268f98d1c86eb9395b074`. The new reporting regression fails with `unknown-edit` for `Settings.UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine`; the other 15 cases pass.
- Fixed: `pnpm test src/daemon/service-audit-schtasks.windows.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 16 cases, including launcher drift, mismatched/unresolvable account identities, omitted defaults, and engine-change rejection during publication. Local wall time: 41.03 seconds (Vitest: 38.45 seconds, mostly initial compilation; individual new cases: 23 ms and 21 ms). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41254801185) passed in 475 seconds overall.
- Consumer proof: `pnpm test src/daemon/service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts src/daemon/service-definition-backup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 105 tests in 30.12 seconds wall time.
- Targeted service test typecheck, changed-file Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad CI and the combined security/CI gate passed before native landing.
- Autoreview: Codex, local candidate against `c633ec6376e1`, P0–P3, `scoped-clean`; no accepted findings. The subsequent test-allocation correction matches the measured 28-line growth.
- Task Scheduler I/O is synthetic in the focused tests; native Windows registration and a live Windows CLI run were not performed. The contributor's Windows observations remain separately documented in #167827. Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` only and was never checked out or executed on this host.

Configured output budgets now use `max_tokens` on Alibaba compatible-mode endpoints. Coding Plan, OpenAI, unrelated proxies, and explicit `compat.maxTokensField` overrides retain their behavior. No configuration migration or operator action is needed.

The original host-normalized attribution behavior is preserved. Tests: +41 lines; the separate 41-line allocation covers the serialized-request regression and two existing budget expectations.

## Evidence

title: fix(slack): keep progress editable after native stream failures
body:
Supersedes #141170, thanks @shannon0430.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Slack progress freezing when native streaming expires or rejects an update during a running turn.

## User Impact

Later progress continues through ordinary draft posts and edits. The final answer is delivered once, and the temporary fallback draft is removed after successful delivery. Native user Stop requests remain respected. No configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Slack progress renderer and draft lifecycle after the native transport fails. Keep the original native message as history rather than reconstructing and rewriting its full contents. Native completion and queued-turn cleanup retain their existing owners.

This is a focused reimplementation on main, with contributor credit in the commit. Production delta: +23/-16 (net +7) in one owner; duplicate draft-activation expressions were removed. The small growth connects transport fallback and queued cleanup without a new projection, state store, or configuration option. Regression tests add 69 net lines, covered by a scoped test-line allocation for the real dispatch/SDK failure cases.

## Evidence

- Base: `e44b8f449184ccc3fc57ddf46cb3b88ff3b30da4`. Three regressions first verified the injected Slack rejection, then failed on the missing progress edit on unchanged main (10.44 seconds wall time).
- Green: `pnpm test extensions/slack/src/delivery-trace.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 122 passed, 15.17 seconds wall time. Real dispatch and Slack SDK buffering; only Slack client I/O is mocked. Covers rejected starts, `message_not_in_streaming_state`, a stream timeout, later progress edits, cleanup, single final delivery, and existing Stop/human-boundary behavior.
- Focused typecheck, three-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41250503853) passed in 451 seconds wall time (no failed jobs).
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local snapshot against the base above with transport/draft/lifecycle context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Its sandbox did not execute tests; the surrounding dispatch caller was inspected separately.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. No live Slack API or production Gateway test was run; proof is the mocked-client production-path harness.

title: fix(images): report returned settings separately from requests
body:
Supersedes #140357, thanks @NianJiuZst.
Supersedes #140995, thanks @ericcaiwx-star.
Related: #140295.

## What Problem This Solves

Image generation reports requested size, quality, and format as applied even when the provider returns different settings or leaves them unknown.

## User Impact

Completed image results now separate `details.requested` hints from per-image `details.outputs`. Output dimensions and format come from the saved bytes, and quality appears only when the provider reports a concrete value. Completion text reports these observed settings too. Consumers of the former top-level hint fields should use `requested` or `outputs` instead. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared image-result owner stops inferring applied settings from requests or pre-submission normalization. The Codex parser retains concrete returned quality and identifies returned image bytes; batch filenames retain that format. Missing, `auto`, or unrecognized quality stays unknown, and heterogeneous outputs retain their own settings.

This covers both contributors' reporting fixes without a new result-helper module. The superseded image branch of the shared geometry formatter was deleted; its remaining video-only path preserves video behavior. Production delta: +53/-30 (net +23). The remaining growth supplies per-image facts and their completion text. Test delta: +73, with a matching scoped allocation for the two distinct reporting/wire-parser regressions and the strengthened existing batch fixture.

## Evidence

The new cases add no sleeps or external calls.

Successful shared-shard logs sum provider case times to 9.237 s and parser case times to 0.018 s; these are not standalone per-file command wall times. The optional local full-tree test-line ratchet hit the 60 s host timeout; the scoped allocation exactly matches the +73 test-line delta, and the CI ratchet passed.

The final review includes the array-access typing/lint corrections and strengthened batch fixture. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; its single hosted review was automatically queued for this head. It is advisory; local autoreview supplies the completed independent review.

title: feat(knowledge): share person-scoped project knowledge between agents
body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

Related: #186066 (parent #186050; prerequisite #186065). Complements #188494 without duplicating its USER.md/bootstrap changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Proposes person-scoped project Knowledge sharing between two explicitly authorized agents without granting a scoped specialist an ungranted personal space.

## User Impact

With the documented restricted embedded-runtime profile, A and B can publish/read the same project record revision and evidence. Personal record bodies, IDs, titles, record counts, evidence, standing indexes and automatic-recall candidates remain outside the specialist’s enabled retrieval paths. Revocation is persisted and rechecked for warmed leases/references and after restart.

**Permission/upgrade proposal:** verified direct requesters now need an explicit person/agent grant rather than falling back to agent-private or conversation knowledge. Existing records are not migrated or reclassified automatically. Unprofiled legacy audiences keep their legacy partitions and cannot traverse person-space directories. This is a reviewable proposal, not a claim of upstream architecture acceptance.

**Required boundary:** the qualified profile allows exactly eight Knowledge record/evidence tools, disables automatic workspace bootstrap/code mode/tool search, and excludes raw filesystem/execution/admin/cross-session history and globally numbered Knowledge History/Recent/revision APIs. Those history sequence identifiers are not represented as private activity counts. Workspace-file import is excluded; person-bound `knowledge_attach_file` also refuses host-workspace reads. Broader tools, bootstrap inputs, providers and native harnesses require separate qualification. There is no OS tenant-isolation or erasure claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse host-minted memory audiences and live authority. The authority owner separately attests requester provenance: unattributed system execution derived from a session owner/creator cannot become a person binding. Genuine roots and validated continuations retain the fact; the existing private recovery snapshot preserves it without turning older/unclassified execution state into a requester.
- Reuse named agent-store membership and the Knowledge registry/publication lane. An operator-only grant selects one store-local space per `(profileId, agent)` against the current binding. No union search or model-controlled store/scope selector.
- Resolve tools, provider search/get/health/candidates, evidence and standing indexes through the restrictive principal. Reuse the scope-key owner for storage/index/receipt/evidence paths and include the partition in standing-index cache identity.
- Check the original administrator inside the registry SQLite transaction, after lock admission and immediately before a permission write; grant changes are compare-and-set.

Knowledge remains the durable record/evidence/publication owner; LosslessClaw remains the conversational-history/compaction owner. No private LCM database reads, new memory owner, SQL table/migration, runtime config option or paid service. No new UI grant controls or USER.md owner/selection changes. The author simplification pass retained one storage/publication owner and replaced duplicate directory selection with the existing scope-key helper. Necessary growth covers grant state, requester provenance and owning-boundary regressions; the separate test-line allocation does not raise the shared baseline.

## Evidence

- Current published head: `ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4` (42 files); source base: `fbb9bc44e8c60c2e756ddcdd9f859e8d123d4065`. The previously interrupted publication request `0318e1bf-be47-41e7-a2b2-6028e5d303a8` is verified published; it was not replayed. Retained `28600ce5` 41-file production-patch artifact: 107,164 bytes, SHA-256 `fc37ea7735df87df46a81ca319e373c3c6ed3b4353c53a0e3591720089f134e5`. Follow-up to previously reviewed `c3044466`: eight files, 23,883 bytes, SHA-256 `a3d7a41b6feab2169abbcd7c6219ccb52243c1ef5b9d35cff781df9bd1379571`. No merge or deployment.
- Genuine red → green for two follow-up defects: (1) native space publication previously returned a published receipt with Git pending / “Unsafe Git content path.” Canonical `spaces/<64 lowercase hex>/` now reaches normal Git completion; exact record/evidence/descriptor bytes and replay are checked, while malformed partitions, traversal and unsupported scopes remain denied. (2) a real registry worker committed revocation, then lost its reply and exited; a warmed provider incorrectly returned the old record on the original client. Worker loss/uncertain permission settlement now invalidates the cached snapshot and reconciles durable authority before further access.
- Final Git/recovery/person-auth consumer run: **66 tests in six files passed**, two Vitest shards, **507.27s wrapper**, including source-runtime preparation. Five Knowledge suites: person-project, git-history, stores, conversation-grants and maintenance. Real isolated Gateway cases: shared-owner **25.050s**, verified-person **23.091s**. The verified-person flow uses synthetic trusted-proxy authentication through the actual host profile producer and obtains distinct canonical P/Q identities with `users.self`. Q has its own identically named space grant and direct session; successful empty list/null record/empty grep and denied evidence reads distinguish partition isolation from a generic authentication failure. Outgoing deterministic model requests are checked for absence of P’s private/project sentinels.
- Both Gateway cases verify the same project ID/revision/hash/evidence across agents, **committed Git receipts**, excluded-tool execution denial, read-only and missing-grant parity through WebSocket and both HTTP endpoints, revocation, and persisted denial after the Gateway PID changes. This qualifies the documented restricted profile with deterministic model I/O—not a live identity provider or live inference.

<summary>Sanitized terminal evidence from the final Git/recovery consumer run</summary>


The committed tests contain the exact negative assertions and use synthetic data only. These excerpts omit ANSI formatting and lifecycle/build noise; they are not a live-provider capture.

</details>

- The subsequent hosted-review P3 diagnostic repair adds an actionable administrator recovery path using the existing operator-only `person_grants` / `person_grant` operations and documented page. No access rule changed. After that diagnostic-only change and binding the test’s original Worker event method, all **five native person tests passed again (53.97s wrapper)**. The Gateway evidence above precedes only those narrow diagnostic/test-cleanup deltas; it is not relabeled as a fresh whole-flow rerun.
- Original requester-provenance/recovery regression coverage remains applicable: owner-derived system authority cannot mint a requester profile; marked and older/unclassified recovery state stay distinct. The six-file authority/principal/worker/recovery/admitted-context/audience run passed **138 tests**; the corrected HTTP dependency/provenance suite passed **27 tests**, and **14 prefix-stability tests** passed. - Fresh static gates passed after all follow-up edits: targeted production and changed-test tsgo leaves extending repository configurations; type-aware lint for six changed TypeScript files; formatting for seven follow-up code/docs files; staged test-lines ratchet; `git diff --check`. Measured net test growth/allocation: **1,142 lines**. The final Gateway consumer run rebuilt the source runtime; the earlier full build’s inherited nonfatal UI CSS-budget warning is not claimed fixed. Unchanged documentation link set was previously audited: 16,196 links, zero broken.
- Independent narrative review inspected all **39 files at c3044466** and found the now-fixed uncertain-revocation P2. A separate final six-file follow-up review traced Git publication/replay, snapshot recovery and authenticated P/Q boundaries, verified all six resulting file hashes, and found no remaining P0–P2 findings in that delta. A diagnostic-only follow-up independently verified the existing operator operations, authority and documentation target, with no P0–P2 findings. The final test method-binding lint cleanup and measured allocation adjustment are mechanical follow-ups. These reviews did not independently rerun the reported tests. Native Auto Review failed internally without a report: **no native-helper-clean or whole-current-head clean verdict is claimed**.
- Compatibility lane: five separate OS processes exercised production registry seed → grant → cold read → revoke → cold revoked read, preserving existing membership/conversation/maintenance/schema/manifest/operational bytes except additive person-grant metadata. This is a **candidate-created legacy-shaped fixture**, not stable-created data. Public latest `openclaw@2026.10.9` contains no Knowledge implementation across 14,109 archive paths; `@openclaw/knowledge` returns 404. Therefore a supported stable binary could not seed an existing Knowledge fixture. Stable→candidate upgrade remains **unqualified**, not waived or passed.

### Committed installed Knowledge–LosslessClaw qualification

The current head includes [the runnable opt-in fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4/test/knowledge-lossless-continuity.e2e.test.ts) and its [documented invocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4/docs/plugins/knowledge/stores-and-access.md#installed-context-engine-continuity-qualification). The remote fixture SHA-256 is verified as `7a920aec36ffd8eb6d56c02c454acc0b988534606de20901eec4c07001d3f3bf`, matching the tested artifact. ```

Final maintained-fixture result: **1 passed**, **66.106s case / 72.45s Vitest / 271.16s wrapper**, including source-runtime preparation. Default invocation separately reports **1 skipped** (44.31s wrapper). Final targeted types, type-aware lint, formatting, test-budget and diff checks passed. The current allocation is **1,560** justified lines; 1,142 above describes the retained earlier production follow-up, not the current total. Review caught an unbounded publication-observation wait in the initial fixture; existing settlement/cancellation helpers now bound it, and the follow-up review confirmed that correction.

```text

PASS actual public context-engine compaction: 1260 -> 915 tokens
```

This materially supplies the bounded installed save/compact/restart/history/evidence and named fault-point evidence requested by #186065. It uses synthetic data, real Gateway/plugin/disk boundaries and deterministic model I/O—not live-provider inference, a live identity provider or a complete supported-harness matrix. The continuity fixture uses the shared-owner profile; distinct authenticated P/Q person isolation is established by the separate Gateway tests above. The interruption is **after publication**, not a mid-transaction crash. The outage result is the observed **client timeout**, not fail-fast or terminal provider recovery. No private LCM database reads or new history owner are used.

The latest-stable Knowledge-record producer comparison is **not applicable to that package**, because the inspected latest stable does not ship Knowledge; it is not a passing upgrade result. The five-process candidate-created legacy-shaped fixture above is narrower persistence evidence. The earlier native-compiler setup failure was recovered through a task-local, source-bound producer/consumer run; the actual pre-PR comparison below now passes.

### Actual pre-PR Knowledge producer → candidate reader

A task-local rerun now passes using the **actual production Knowledge service/registry/storage workers** at producer `fbb9bc44e8c60c2e756ddcdd9f859e8d123d4065` and candidate source bytes verified against `ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4`. This is a native owner/data compatibility proof with synthetic host-authority fixtures, **not** a full Gateway binary upgrade or live-authentication qualification. No shared installation or existing user state was reset. The producer/candidate lockfile, workspace configuration, package manifests and package implementations were identical, allowing sequential reuse of the already-owned frozen dependency graph; the actual old Knowledge implementation was checked out separately and executed by its own supported test wrapper.

```text

Candidate ce0ad040 source: 1 passed; 0.679s case / 43.30s Vitest / 45.55s wrapper; PID 166700
Private record: revision 1; hash fbc02465bb811b572f5505fa724422c5fb5dc34e8b0541f536841b23d8c934b6

PASS shared membership main/research and existing read-only conversation grant retained
PASS unprofiled legacy owner/research/granted conversation reads; isolated conversation remains isolated
PASS identical mutation retry receipts, including existing Git commits; one record per partition
```
