SQLite file bytes are not represented as immutable: normal read/index bookkeeping can write operational state. Registry comparisons use its production owner after worker shutdown. The one new empty person-grant snapshot field is explicitly asserted empty and excluded only from the old-shape comparison; all legacy facts remain equal. A first observation compared a cold store's documented unknown count (`records: null`) with the producer's already-open count. That fixture-stage mismatch is retained as setup evidence; the corrected run compares the **entire** snapshot after the same exact reads/counts, with fresh task-owned old-produced state. No production compatibility workaround or ignored expected value was added.

The verified-requester grant requirement is still the intentional documented permission proposal. This proof does not reinterpret a missing person grant as data corruption or automatically migrate private records into a person space.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the native old-writer/new-reader comparison</summary>

Use two independently owned source checkouts at the exact refs above, with each checkout's normal frozen dependencies (or an equivalently verified, privately owned graph reused sequentially). Save the driver below as `extensions/knowledge/src/prepr-compat-recovery.test.ts` in both. Use an empty, absolute, task-owned path for `PROOF_DATA`, outside both checkouts. The same driver is copied unchanged; its SHA-256 is `7f504aa8bd92986ed26b05444316a0ae21f3efac786e21d142303966854847a9`.

```

The producer creates synthetic records through the old service; the candidate cannot manufacture the expected receipt because it loads the producer's exported views, metadata and file hashes. The test overlay is qualification-only; it is not a production change or ordinary CI download.

```typescript
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { randomUUID, createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { readFile, writeFile, mkdir, readdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { createKnowledgeService } from "./service.js";
import { StoreRegistry } from "./store-registry.js";
import { hostApi, operatorContext, toolContext } from "./test-support.js";

const phase = process.env.KNOWLEDGE_COMPAT_PROOF_PHASE;
const root = process.env.KNOWLEDGE_COMPAT_PROOF_DIR!;
const sharedKey = "agent:main:discord:channel:shared-compat";
const isolatedKey = "agent:main:discord:channel:isolated-compat";

async function contentHashes(dir: string, prefix = ""): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  const result: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (entry.name === ".git") continue;
    const rel = prefix + entry.name;
    if (entry.isDirectory())
      Object.assign(result, await contentHashes(path.join(dir, entry.name), rel + "/"));
    else if (entry.isFile() && !entry.name.includes(".sqlite"))
      result[rel] = createHash("sha256")
        .update(await readFile(path.join(dir, entry.name)))
        .digest("hex");
  }
  return result;
}

it.runIf(phase === "produce" || phase === "consume")(
  "reads actual pre-PR Knowledge state through the candidate native service",
  async () => {
    await mkdir(root, { recursive: true });
    const exportPath = path.join(root, "producer.json");
    const baseline =
      phase === "consume" ? JSON.parse(await readFile(exportPath, "utf8")) : undefined;
    const ids = baseline?.ids ?? { shared: randomUUID(), isolated: randomUUID() };
    const stops: Array<{ stop(): Promise<void> }> = [];
    const host = hostApi(path.join(root, "fixture"), {
      agents: ["main", "research"],
      stores: { work: { agents: ["main", "research"] } },
      policy: { operatorRead: true, writesEnabled: true },
      extra: { registerService: (service: { stop(): Promise<void> }) => stops.push(service) },
    });
    const service = createKnowledgeService(host.api);
    const owner = toolContext(host.api, "main"),
      research = toolContext(host.api, "research");
    const admin = operatorContext(host.api, ["operator.admin"]);
    const chat = (key: string, id: string) =>
      toolContext(host.api, "main", {
        kind: "conversation",
        agentId: "main",
        sessionKey: key,
        sessionId: id,
      });
    const shared = chat(sharedKey, ids.shared),
      isolated = chat(isolatedKey, ids.isolated);
    const inputs = baseline?.inputs ?? {
      private: {
        requestId: randomUUID(),
        title: "Existing private record",
        type: "note",
        body: "Synthetic pre-PR private bytes.",
        source: {
          text: "Synthetic pre-PR private evidence.",
          attribution: "Compatibility fixture",
        },
      },
      conversation: {
        requestId: randomUUID(),
        title: "Existing conversation record",
        type: "note",
        body: "Synthetic pre-PR conversation bytes.",
        source: {
          text: "Synthetic pre-PR conversation evidence.",
          attribution: "Compatibility fixture",
        },
      },
    };
    let snapshot, privateReceipt, conversationReceipt, privateRead, conversationRead;
    try {
      if (phase === "produce") {
        privateReceipt = await service.save_page(inputs.private, owner);
        conversationReceipt = await service.save_page(inputs.conversation, isolated);
        expect(privateReceipt.git?.state).toBe("committed");
        expect(conversationReceipt.git?.state).toBe("committed");
        const before = await service.stores_snapshot({}, admin);
        const granted = await service.stores_grant(
          { expectedRevision: before.grants.revision, sessionKey: sharedKey, access: "read" },
          admin,
        );
        expect(granted.outcome).toBe("applied");
      } else {
        privateReceipt = baseline.privateReceipt;
        conversationReceipt = baseline.conversationReceipt;
      }
      const args = (id: string) => ({ id, metadataView: "full" as const, includeEvidence: true });
      privateRead = await service.record(args(privateReceipt.id), owner);
      conversationRead = await service.record(args(conversationReceipt.id), isolated);
      expect(privateRead.record).toMatchObject({
        id: privateReceipt.id,
        revision: privateReceipt.revision,
        hash: privateReceipt.hash,
        body: inputs.private.body,
      });
      expect(conversationRead.record).toMatchObject({
        id: conversationReceipt.id,
        revision: conversationReceipt.revision,
        hash: conversationReceipt.hash,
        body: inputs.conversation.body,
      });
      expect(privateRead.evidence).toEqual(
        expect.arrayContaining([
          expect.objectContaining({ verified: true, excerpt: inputs.private.source.text }),
        ]),
      );
      expect(conversationRead.evidence).toEqual(
        expect.arrayContaining([
          expect.objectContaining({ verified: true, excerpt: inputs.conversation.source.text }),
        ]),
      );
      expect((await service.record(args(privateReceipt.id), research)).record).toEqual(
        privateRead.record,
      );
      expect((await service.record(args(privateReceipt.id), shared)).record).toEqual(
        privateRead.record,
      );
      expect((await service.record(args(conversationReceipt.id), owner)).record).toBeNull();
      expect((await service.record(args(privateReceipt.id), isolated)).record).toBeNull();
      expect((await service.records({}, owner)).total).toBe(1);
      expect((await service.records({}, isolated)).total).toBe(1);
      snapshot = await service.stores_snapshot({}, admin);
      if (phase === "consume") {
        expect(process.pid).not.toBe(baseline.pid);
        expect(privateRead).toEqual(baseline.privateRead);
        expect(conversationRead).toEqual(baseline.conversationRead);
        expect(snapshot).toEqual(baseline.snapshot);
        expect(await service.save_page(inputs.private, owner)).toEqual(privateReceipt);
        expect(await service.save_page(inputs.conversation, isolated)).toEqual(conversationReceipt);
        expect((await service.records({}, owner)).total).toBe(1);
        expect((await service.records({}, isolated)).total).toBe(1);
      }
    } finally {
      await Promise.all(stops.map((entry) => entry.stop()));
    }
    // Inspect registry metadata only through its owner, after native worker shutdown.
    const registry = new StoreRegistry(host.stateRoot);
    let durable;
    try {
      durable = registry.snapshot();
    } finally {
      registry.close();
    }
    const legacyDurable = Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(durable).filter(([key]) => key !== "personGrants"),
    );
    if (phase === "consume")
      expect(
        Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(durable).filter(([key]) => key === "personGrants")),
      ).toEqual({ personGrants: {} });
    const hashes = await contentHashes(path.join(root, "fixture"));
    if (phase === "produce") {
      await writeFile(
        exportPath,
        JSON.stringify({
          pid: process.pid,
          producerRef: execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim(),
          ids,
          inputs,
          privateReceipt,
          conversationReceipt,
          privateRead,
          conversationRead,
          snapshot,
          legacyDurable,
          hashes,
        }),
      );
    } else {
      expect(legacyDurable).toEqual(baseline.legacyDurable);
      expect(hashes).toEqual(baseline.hashes);
      await writeFile(
        path.join(root, "consumer.json"),
        JSON.stringify({
          producerPid: baseline.pid,
          producerRef: baseline.producerRef,
          consumerPid: process.pid,
          candidateRef: "ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4",
          privateId: privateReceipt.id,
          privateRevision: privateReceipt.revision,
          privateHash: privateReceipt.hash,
          conversationId: conversationReceipt.id,
          conversationRevision: conversationReceipt.revision,
          conversationHash: conversationReceipt.hash,
          evidencePreserved: true,
          metadataPreserved: true,
          legacyAudiencesPreserved: true,
          replaySameReceipts: true,
          contentFiles: Object.keys(hashes).length,
        }),
      );
    }
    console.info("Knowledge pre-PR compatibility", {
      phase,
      pid: process.pid,
      privateRevision: privateReceipt.revision,
      conversationRevision: conversationReceipt.revision,
      contentFiles: Object.keys(hashes).length,

  },
  120_000,

The repeatable opt-in fixture and its non-authorizing transport observer are prepared locally for the next source publication; **they are not yet part of current head ce0ad040**. title: fix(update): preserve config edits during plugin finalization
body:
Related: #189778

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin finalization aborting an update with “config changed since last load” when another writer edits config during package or plugin work, including same-version repairs.

## User Impact

Unrelated edits survive finalization. Already-applied changes succeed; owned-field conflicts or repeated concurrent writes produce a warning with `openclaw plugins doctor` / `openclaw doctor --fix` guidance instead of failing the core update or preventing Gateway recovery. Existing ownership, path, validation, and I/O refusals remain enforced. A plugin may remain unavailable until repaired.

This fix is **not yet released**. The separate Windows Gateway recovery repair is on main in #189647 (`ed79334f`), also not yet released. Leave #189778 open until release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalization previously replaced config against a hash captured before awaited plugin work. It now reapplies only its changed fields to fresh config using the existing config lock, five-attempt retry, and plugin publication/index rollback owner. The planning baseline is retained before in-memory channel restoration. Authority refusals propagate unchanged; warning settlement rechecks authority after rollback.

The original report does not identify the concurrent writer. Same-version convergence can run while the Gateway is online; the regressions exercise ordinary concurrent config edits without claiming to reproduce the reporter’s exact writer or Windows update.

## Evidence

- **Include/env retry invariant:** every attempt [reads a fresh snapshot and merges its write options](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L904-L955). The retry loop [reuses the prepared snapshot only for attempt zero](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L976-L1015). The snapshot owner [returns newly captured env restoration, include hashes/targets, and plugin metadata](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/io.snapshot.ts#L601-L610). The writer [selects the include boundary from that snapshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L324-L348) and [restores authored env references](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/io.write-values.ts#L35-L81).
- The [extended production-path persistence test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts#L302-L382) switches include destinations and changes the env value during the first commit. It proves the retry preserves the root `$include`, root and included env references, the old include byte-for-byte, concurrent values in the new include, and install-index rollback after exhaustion. No secrets are inlined and the include is not flattened or clobbered.
- The extended case fails with the original base finalization code (`603106d1a96a`: include conflict) and also fails when only the stale `envSnapshotForRestore` is retained (one commit attempt instead of the required successful second attempt). Both temporary controls were restored. The complete persistence suite passes: **17 tests**, 31.08 s Vitest / 32.98 s wrapper. Final formatted retry cases pass: **2 tests**, 39.99 s / 42.21 s including cold worker compilation.
- Targeted CLI-update test typecheck, focused oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Earlier unchanged-source proof covers 101 focused persistence, authority, finalizer, config-fence, and degradation cases; another 19 consumer/authority cases passed after the fixture correction.
- Fresh independent **Codex autoreview, P0–P2**, base `603106d1a96a` through the final local candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The committed patch matches that candidate. Existing hosted ClawSweeper review found no code defects.
- Simplification retains the existing lock/retry/rollback owners. Production grows by 99 net lines; 177 net test/fixture lines cover distinct finalization contracts, including 50 additional lines extending the existing retry test. No test-only production seam, new schema, persisted format, public config/SDK contract, dependency, or config option is introduced. Persistence proof uses real config/include/index writes; a cheaper mocked layer cannot establish these guarantees.
- Exact-head [CI run 41252307222](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41252307222) is fully green on `17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, the aggregate CI gate, and current dependency/security guards. Zero failures and zero pending checks. Prior-head CI remains historical evidence only.
- Installed latest-stable-to-candidate Windows upgrade and real Gateway/model proof were not run. External package/service/provider operations are stubbed in local finalizer composition. This limitation remains disclosed; no installed-upgrade or live Gateway claim is made.

title: fix(update): recover repeated Git download interruptions
body:
Related: #189643. Supersedes #184452, with thanks and commit credit to @duyufansh2008.

## What Problem This Solves

Git updates still fail after two interrupted fetches, and an initial transactional clone has no automatic transport retry.

## User Impact

Update fetches and clones get at most four attempts with 1s, 5s, and 15s backoff. Discovery and dry-run probes retain one retry. Attempts share the original timeout and cancellation scope; each retry logs a warning. Authentication, certificate, integrity, and uncertain-cleanup failures stop immediately.

This must be present in the installed updater; a new candidate cannot repair an older updater already running. #189643 remains open pending its sanitized Git stderr; this addresses the transport-failure class without claiming that report's cause is established.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared retry policy and the existing transactional clone owner. Each failed clone settles and removes its private staging before another attempt. Cleanup warnings stop retries, and current update authority is checked immediately before each native clone command. Retry classification uses native stderr before diagnostic-tail truncation.

Numeric transfer progress and unrelated upgrade-harness changes from the contributor PR are excluded. Existing stage/activity presentation remains. Package managers continue to own package/tarball transport retries; whole installs are not replayed.

Simplification: no new downloader, parser, persistent state, or lifecycle owner. Net growth is 52 production lines and 245 test lines; the separate test allocation covers real HTTP recovery plus cleanup, cancellation, authority, timeout, and permanent-error regressions.

## Evidence

- Native Git HTTP regression is red on main `603106d1a96a6fd65868372fc4d8601c8789aac8`: truncating a pack response produces exit 128 / curl 18. With this patch, two truncated packs are followed by a successful third clone; commit identity, file contents, and absence of partial staging are verified. Backoff waits are injected in this functional fixture; the retry-owner tests verify the clock and remaining budget.
- 73 focused tests pass across retry, command diagnostics, transactional clone, native Git HTTP, dry-run, and update-timeout suites. Native recovery takes 232ms of test time; the final 40-test HTTP/clone rerun takes 7.63s wall time. No full suite or release build ran on the review host.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2: the complete production/test delta against the base above and the subsequent test-only lint repair were separately scoped-clean, with no actionable findings. Full owning transaction/process context was supplied for the production review.
- Formatting and whitespace checks pass. [CI passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41248890463) on `8266f8c4771fc80249671445a8433be5eeaa509c`, including production/test typing, lint, affected tests, guards, docs, and the aggregate gate. Primary run elapsed time: 24m01s. CI supplied the lint/type qualification after local preparation rejected the shared dependency layout.
- Full latest-stable installed-CLI upgrade and a real requester/executor revocation during native clone backoff were not run for this rewrite. The [hosted advisory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189818#issuecomment-6550213783) has no code findings and asks for those proofs before merge; the parent approved landing: real-owner revocation and the latest-stable installed-upgrade matrix are deferred to the next deep pass and are not merge blockers for this narrow retry wrapper with regression coverage. The callsite unit test verifies rejection after awaited work, and native HTTP tests prove allowed recovery. Contributor fork upgrade results are not claimed as proof of this branch. No config, schema, dependency, or publication protocol changes.

title: fix(daemon): preserve trailing backslashes in Windows launcher arguments
body:
Supersedes #140180, thanks @SebTardif.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows Gateway launcher arguments swallowing the following argument when a quoted value ends in a backslash.

## User Impact

Windows launchers preserve trailing backslashes and argument boundaries, and service inspection reads their generated commands correctly. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing quoting helper now doubles backslashes before the closing quote and escapes backslashes beside embedded quotes according to [Microsoft's native argument rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments). Readback reuses the existing Windows argument parser; strict inspection still rejects ambiguous CMD/CRT quoting.

Production delta: **−5 lines**. Removed the separate empty-value quoting branch and superseded daemon parser mode in favor of the existing native parser. Tests add 34 lines, with a scoped allocation for the serialization table, service-reader regression, ambiguity rejection, and native cmd.exe case. The contributor's broader legacy working-directory parsing changes are outside this focused repair.

## Evidence

- Base: `4778b0ae3ca1fb63c4a750e6e2164f2bbb2d4a05`. The production-generated command parsed the trailing-backslash argument, `SENTINEL-NEXT`, and `< NUL` as one argument. Five serialization-table cases failed; generated service inspection failed with “ambiguous working directory.”
- Fixed: **89 passed, 7 platform skips** across seven focused test files, including quoting, native parsing, service readback, restart helpers/logs, and CLI shims. Total wall time 60.61s; daemon tests 2.80s with a warm compiler cache (cold transform overhead 36–41s). Native Windows cases skip on Linux; this PR CI plan skipped the Windows lane, so actual cmd.exe execution remains an explicit coverage gap. The new native case is registered for Windows test runs. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41248044822) passed in 487 seconds (including runner setup and broad checks); both required CI-gate reports passed at the reviewed head.
- Targeted source/test typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad proof runs in PR CI.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host. Shared autoreview reviewed the final local candidate against the base above, including full native parser, renderer, strict reader and native test context: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. Hosted ClawSweeper review follows the maintainer fallback route.
- Reimplemented from trusted main. Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed. Native service registration and a live Gateway are not part of local proof.

title: fix: prevent context overflow during long tool turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long tool-heavy turns can exceed the model window before turn-end maintenance runs. In the Contributor PRs cron incident on 2026-10-31 20:28–20:30Z, request 7 reached **1,000,188 tokens against a 1,000,000-token window**. The surfaced “Auto-compaction failed” label did not establish that compaction had run.

## User Impact

Hard context-window admission now runs by default at provider request boundaries, using conservative projected context and the existing 20,000-token reserve floor (capped for small windows). The optional soft threshold retains its disabled default and configured reserve. Unsafe replay or unsettled tools still prevent recovery compaction; surfaced overflow messages now identify a mid-turn window overflow. Manual compaction is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead policy decision: a request already projected beyond the model window guarantees a 400 and cannot advance the turn. Reuse the existing provider-bound estimator, boundary signal, and compaction/retry owner instead of sending that request. title: fix(exec): keep Windows POSIX shell approvals one-shot
body:
Supersedes #140127, thanks @PrisonBreakPB.
Related: #139917.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows operators can save reusable execution approvals for inline POSIX shell commands even though those shell carriers should remain one-shot.

## User Impact

Inline `sh -c` and `bash -c` commands on Windows, including package-manager and dispatch wrappers, no longer mint reusable rules. Repeated or changed payloads continue to require approval. Script-file and durable positional-carrier approvals retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persistence collector unwrapped carriers and then analyzed POSIX shell payloads with the Windows cmd/PowerShell parser. Exclude POSIX shells from that fallback after the existing script and positional handling, matching the one-shot carrier policy on POSIX hosts.

Security review: this only narrows future approval generation. Current main already hashes argv and cwd, so this repair does not claim that approving one command grants arbitrary later payloads. It prevents deriving reusable rules with the wrong shell grammar. Direct commands and cmd/PowerShell approvals remain bound to their inner argv; changed arguments still prompt. Existing saved rules are not revoked or migrated; operators can review and remove previously saved carrier rules through the approvals controls. No schema or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced against main `edc86dd18f36a84126ced2ea35d3f9be61ec1615` using the real shell evaluator and persistence decision owner: five Windows POSIX-shell cases failed because they returned an inner-executable rule; 51 other tests passed. No contributor code was checked out or run.
- After the fix: `pnpm test src/infra/exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts src/infra/exec-allow-always-persistence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 75 tests. Coverage includes direct/nested POSIX wrappers, Linux/macOS carrier policy, repeated/changed payload approval misses, and argv-bound cmd/PowerShell/direct-command controls.
- Changed-file suite: 1.87 seconds wall time on the passing run; two-file orchestration including cold worker preparation: 45.61 seconds. The [CI changed-node lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41246822393/job/124672159185) passed in 287 seconds total (228 seconds running its broader test shard).
- Focused TypeScript check, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Final autoreview: full collector/planner/wrapper context supplied; P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewed the final local snapshot committed as `cac1b153266d753a53ee3259d31854556b866827` against the main commit above. Native Windows execution and a full Gateway/model approval round trip were not run; explicit Windows evaluator paths ran on Linux with synthetic executable fixtures.
- Simplification: production LOC +0 (6 added / 6 removed), including removal of the inaccurate inline-shell persistence example. Tests +41 lines; the dedicated test-line allocation covers the platform regression and native-wrapper controls without changing the shared baseline.

title: feat(database): capture externally quiesced SQLite migrations
body:
## Problem

An external controller that has already suspended a local Gateway cannot produce an exact SQLite migration capsule until it stops that Gateway. An existing filesystem archive cannot establish that a live suspension covers both the archive and exact database images.

## User Impact

Controllers can capture an already-suspended local Gateway without stopping it or transferring suspension ownership. The mode creates its own filesystem archive and exact SQLite images; restore remains restricted to a new private staging tree. Capsules contain private credentials and retained operational state and must be protected accordingly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing local-state, source-preserving archive, snapshot, and restoration owners. The bounded suspension adapter authenticates to the selected local backend, verifies physical owner/process identity and zero write custody, renews only the original controller suspension, and joins pending renewal during cleanup. It never resumes or stops the controller. Offline behavior stays unchanged; this slice introduces no schema or retention change.

title: feat(database): capture exact SQLite migration capsules
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary portable backups intentionally sanitize delivery/recovery state. They cannot serve as exact original-state capsules when moving a stopped SQLite installation to a disposable host for database migration.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw database migration-capture capabilities|create|restore`. Operators retain exact native SQLite/configuration images with a verified filesystem base and restore only into new private staging. This does not import PostgreSQL, start services, resume database ports, or change ordinary backup sanitization.

Creation requires stopped writers, state-relative databases, valid pinned configuration, and an output outside live state/configuration roots. Unsupported PostgreSQL sources and external roots fail explicitly. The manifest digest is a producer receipt, not a substitute for operator custody of this sensitive capsule. The operator must bind a fresh base archive to the same stopped source generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the offline state owner, existing recovery-store discovery, verified SQLite publication, archive admission, and matched shared/local credential owner. Restore admits every artifact before creating staging, overlays only private regular staged files, removes explicitly missing database families, and cleans failed staging. The manifest-pair guard permits installations that have shared state but no local credential database.

This is the smallest coherent offline create/verify/restore slice of [Galin's capture change](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/2c4173934ae1074ecca1b1f48eb13410c143d603). [Source-preserving archive acquisition #189638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189638) and [PostgreSQL companion profiles #189685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189685) are merged. [Externally quiesced capture #189802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189802) remains a separate, dependent PR. The new capsule orchestration is necessary to combine existing owners; no new database/state manager or alternate recovery implementation is introduced.

## Evidence

### Combined companion admission

Integrated landed main `4fb684e294e27aed927548aaf64d2a7b8ba4696f`, retaining both ordinary companion selection and this PR's internal SQLite-only restore option. The combined guard checks typed PostgreSQL anchors as well as export candidates at **both** capture-base admission and SQLite-only restore admission, before output/target creation. Ordinary companion restoration and a zero-anchor SQLite-only companion remain accepted.

Both regressions were reproduced through genuinely verified archives on the combined unguarded code: creation and restore incorrectly returned `ok` rather than rejecting. No malformed-fixture failure was credited. After the two-condition repair, **50 tests across three affected files pass**, including the positive sibling cases, exact state/credential promotion, alias/tamper handling, archive completeness, and both physical-source refusal paths. Vitest 273.93s; complete wrapper 436.36s including 140.054s worker preparation and joined cleanup. The new capture-base and restore checks executed in 162ms and 33ms; the zero-anchor profile control took 90ms.

Core production, commands-test and infra-test typechecks pass. Source-backed type-aware lint passes all four touched files; formatting and diff checks pass. The exact **354-line** allocation gate passes (previous 292 plus 62 justified net lines for these independent admission paths and their positive control). No shared scalar, timeout, assertion, schema, authority or durability policy was weakened.

Fresh independent autoreview against pinned landed main completed final source verification with **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. It reviewed the selected source/patch and complete supplied admission owners; it did not execute project code or independently validate omitted dependency implementations. The prior complete credential-owner review remains separately recorded below.

The main integration carries the already-landed state-schema-37 migration. Earlier CLI evidence remains bound to its original source, not relabeled as new-head execution. The requested latest-stable and promoted-authority proof is now complete as detailed below; current-head CI and hosted reassessment remain pending.

### Latest-stable offline round trip and final protected authority — passed

Executed a complete new runtime built at clean integrated source `2335c6a6bed1d65d4c7f5a02b8aee6dc62927547` in [dependent PR #189802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189802), which contains this PR's exact published dependency `23b25e002c40e7c88e3b53a230a4a7e0abe4a8b1`. This is explicitly **offline exact-SQLite proof**, not PostgreSQL companion proof or externally quiesced capture: the real command supplied `--base-archive`, no suspension IDs or `--externally-quiesced`, and the capture receipt contained no quiescence record.

1. Published npm **OpenClaw 2026.10.9**, independently resolved as latest stable, initialized absent databases and created/read a session through its real Gateway and CLI. Candidate Doctor upgraded that actual stored state. The candidate loaded the retained session, settings, shared authentication, and user file; schema **37** and `worker_environments.resource_receipt_json` were asserted.
2. Two distinct real Ed25519 clients received tokens through Gateway handshakes and native token-cache owners. **Both first performed protected `agents.files.set` writes**, proving the forbidden-client test was not a client that had never been authorized.
3. A real controller revoked one device before capture. Its device-token-only protected request was rejected with `device_token_mismatch`, **zero authenticated-handshake callbacks**, and an independent file witness unchanged: bytes/SHA-256, inode, size, nanosecond mtime and ctime.
4. After accepted work settled through the existing ready/non-drain suspension and the disposable Gateway stopped, the built CLI ran **backup create/verify → offline migration-capture create → migration-capture restore** into fresh staging. The capsule included the native local credential database. Exact configuration and user-file bytes matched; explicit disposable-tree promotion retained the old source separately.
5. Both transported identities and both cached bearer values loaded through the real local credential owners. A real Gateway then started on the **promoted restored SQLite authority** and loaded the stable-created session. The allowed client successfully performed the protected file write. The client revoked before capture was refused before authenticated dispatch, with the independent file witness unchanged.
6. The controller then revoked the remaining allowed client **against the promoted authority**. Its cached device-token-only write was also refused before authenticated dispatch with the same unchanged-file oracle. This proves final protected effects and denial, not just credential-row admission.
7. All three owned Gateway stops and final worker/fixture cleanup joined. **1/1 passed: 79.932s test, 86.48s Vitest, 100.01s complete repository wrapper; exit 0.** No live user installation, database, or non-public endpoint was used.

**Exact snapshot semantics:** restoring SQLite restores captured authority. This proof does not claim that a source revocation occurring after capture survives rollback. It proves a revocation present at capture and a new revocation against the activated restored owner.

**Source applicability:** parent `23b25e0` and executed `2335c6a` have identical backup/restore, credential rebinding, device identity/token, protected file-handler, and schema-upgrade owners. The capture module differs by PR5's reviewed suspension adapter; this execution selects the normal offline branch over the same owners, with both export/nonempty-anchor guards preserved. Parent inspection checked the actual introduced diff and proof fixture, not only the result summary. No claim is made that the full PR3 and PR5 trees are identical.

**Reproducibility/binding:** complete `pnpm build:runtime` stamps bind clean head `2335c6a`; build input signature `f9ec5de26145decf70e67f6e00d9c5122fd54a1575e986d2a6be5fbc71c0da17`, runtime-postbuild signature `48d845aa6a45b8d7a63a961277550192d17986378d75db0155589df7bda2cbd6`, executed entrypoint SHA-256 `9b04b8104f537ec5b85f62a0d67cc34d348dcc347116c908b08639c0066f83e2`, proof fixture SHA-256 `09afc4c3c93a7e07ad35524be795fa15ac8b8afe6c5dd3527b81da871b0a0980`. The retained disposable fixture uses `createOpenClawTestInstance`, the actual CLI and Gateway, and independent filesystem observations; no mocked auth or private credentials are included here.

**Earlier attempts retained:** two schema-36 attempts exhausted the unchanged 60-second Gateway startup deadline under heavy I/O and were not credited as final proof. The first schema-37 attempt hit the fixture's unchanged 3-second child-cleanup deadline. The passing fixture settles accepted work with the existing bounded suspension before each normal stop; all stop receipts passed. No Gateway readiness, cleanup, RPC timeout, lease heartbeat, authority check, or product code was weakened. Later success is not claimed as a product fix for those setup/timing failures.

### Earlier source-bound proof

- **Real alias regression:** the owner captured a canonical state root while restore compared the caller's lexical path. The alias case failed with the expected logical-path rejection before the repair. Both sides now use the existing canonical identity resolver.
- **Real absent-credentials regression:** complete independent review found a valid shared-without-local-credentials capsule that failed during rebinding. The actual create/restore case failed before the fix. Rebinding now requires the local image declared by the admitted manifest, not a filesystem existence guess.
- **Earlier offline integration:** all **5 cases pass** through actual archive/capture/restore owners and native SQLite, including queued delivery intent, daemon pins, private socket credentials, workspace bytes, promoted credential admission, state/output aliases, missing local credentials, and artifact/manifest tampering before target creation. Wrapper 388.99s including worker preparation and cleanup. The two physical PostgreSQL-refusal cases also passed, including the stopped-store fast path.
- **Landed prerequisite integration:** the pinned main commit containing #189638 was merged to provide a clean base for the dependent quiesced PR. No conflicts or feature production edits were needed; the three production modules and their existing owner contracts remain byte-identical, with matching feature patch ID. All **9 tests across three files** pass on the combined tree: five capsule cases, WAL/DELETE source-preservation cases, and both physical PostgreSQL-refusal cases; complete wrapper 53.50s. Core typecheck passes. The live CLI result remains explicitly bound to its earlier clean source, not relabeled as a new-head run.
- **Checks:** core production and commands/services test typechecks passed; final repair's commands-test typecheck and source-backed lint passed. Production/test formatting and diff checks passed. Documentation link validation checked 16,194 links with zero broken. That earlier revision allocated 292 governed lines; the combined candidate's exact 354-line allocation is verified above.
- **Review:** full committed-context independent review included the unchanged credential owner and identified the missing-local issue. Fresh repair review completed source verification with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Earlier incomplete reviews are not credited as clean. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable, so the documented local-autoreview/hosted-review fallback applies.
- **Real built CLI proof:** runtime build completed at clean source `3710860d6c54c01eae89b4479bf9aad55b9c7e5b`. A disposable, uniquely profiled instance exercised capabilities → ordinary backup creation/verification → exact capsule capture → staging restore → exact witness-row read and promoted credential-owner admission → tamper refusal before target creation. All four stage markers passed; 1/1 proof test passed in 11.455s, with the full test wrapper and joined cleanup finishing in 50.50s. The build and runtime-postbuild stamps both bind the executing source; no installed Gateway or user database was accessed. The disposable proof harness was removed after settlement.
- **Prior setup failures retained:** the first CLI attempt selected the default service during runtime preparation; the corrected-profile attempt then exhausted its unchanged 600-second command deadline while building bundled plugins. Neither was product proof. Separate standard runtime preparation completed successfully before the passing run; no publication guard, heartbeat, or product deadline was weakened.

Historical cold Node runs hit startup/no-output or outer command limits. Later Bun passes do not establish fixes for those timing failures. No live installation or real user database was used.

title: fix(feishu): avoid repeated card replies after Gateway restarts
body:
Supersedes #139396, thanks @SebTardif.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Feishu approval cards and cancel or invalid-action notices when a completed card callback is redelivered after a Gateway restart.

## User Impact

Completed callbacks remain suppressed across restarts for the existing 15-minute window. Failed direct sends can retry. Persistence remains best effort: a database failure is logged and in-memory dedupe continues. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the callback map with the existing SQLite-backed channel replay guard, bounded to 1,000 cached entries and 10,000 persisted entries per account. A separate callback namespace in the existing plugin database preserves the message dedupe budget and its 24-hour window. Synthetic commands keep their downstream message dedupe and failure suppression.

The old callback timer/map implementation and the single-use target/cache wrappers disappear: production +44/-45, net **-1 line**. Regression coverage adds 50 test lines; the dedicated test-line allocation covers restart, expiry, failed-send retry, and the asynchronous in-flight boundary. The handler suite joins the existing process-based database-worker test lane so it exercises the real SQLite broker.

A crash after an external send succeeds but before its completion is committed can still allow redelivery; this uses the existing best-effort replay contract.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main base `bed4f71b73658b9a2b20c40b7245471c871a3883`: complete a cancel callback, reload the handler, replay the same callback; the new regression fails because two notices are sent instead of one. The current-main handler still had the same memory-only callback path when inspected.
- After the fix: `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/bot.card-action.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/dedup.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **35 passed**, 3 files, 66.32s wall time including cold worker preparation. The callback suite uses real SQLite, closes its database and clears replay memory before redelivery; cancel, approval, and invalid notices remain suppressed, then become eligible after 15 minutes. Failed sends retry and successful retries survive reopening.
- Package typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/feishu/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passed after declaration preparation. Targeted type-aware oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244450076) passed: 61 jobs total, 33 non-skipped jobs, 4,048 cumulative job-seconds and 444 seconds wall time. The hosted baseline ratchet passed; its local run reached the 90-second host limit.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate against `bed4f71b73658b9a2b20c40b7245471c871a3883`: Codex, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Review included the replay-guard and persistent-store owners; it did not execute tests. Local ClawSweeper had no installed CLI; the existing hosted review receipt was already queued, so no duplicate request was posted.
- Contributor source was read only with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. This is an independent implementation on main with verified human coauthor credit.

No live Feishu tenant or production Gateway restart was used. Sends are observed at the production handler boundary with external delivery mocked; signature verification and HTTP transport are unchanged. The production Team Gateway was not modified.

title: fix(fal): reject generated media downloads containing error documents
body:
Supersedes #139191, thanks @Yigtwxx

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fal image and music generation returning corrupt assets when a successful download contains an error document or an empty body.

## User Impact

Malformed downloads now fail with a fal-labelled image/audio error. Valid media, MIME fallbacks, size limits, download deadlines, and fal's deadline-only timing remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fal download owners now use the existing binary-response validation contract. Music forwards the reader's idle-timeout option so enabling validation does not shorten fal's existing download budget. Image downloading stays in its generation loop; removing the single-use download wrapper, intermediate result, and redundant image counter offsets the added validation: production +37/-37, net 0.

The shared contract rejects JSON/text MIME types and empty bodies, and rejects wrong media families for audio. Nonempty media-declared or untyped bodies retain the existing shared-reader trust contract.

## Evidence

- On current main `7b29a23da2a6`, eight new provider-entry-point regressions fail because invalid downloads resolve as successful assets; 48 controls pass. Fixtures include JSON, problem JSON, HTML, an empty image/audio body, and a music response labelled as an image.
- With the fix: 58 fal tests and three shared music-asset tests pass. The MiniMax sibling suite passes all 27 tests. A fake-clock control proves valid fal audio can pause 31 seconds without acquiring the shared reader's default 30-second idle timeout; the image suite checks the missing-MIME fallback and dispatcher release.
- Focused source/test typecheck, type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, the test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. A package-boundary typecheck initially lacked generated SDK declarations; the final focused source check includes the repository's ambient declarations.
- Local fal lane: 11.45 seconds for both files; shared helper: 1.38 seconds. The final music-only rerun took 39.10 seconds, almost entirely compiler preparation; the fake-clock control itself took 3 ms. MiniMax: 41.24 seconds. The CI extension shard passed 105 tests across six files in 44.54 seconds (112 seconds including job setup).
- Shared autoreview (Codex), local candidate against `7b29a23da2a6`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The subsequent change only removed a Promise executor's implicit return to satisfy lint. The pr-simplify pass removed the private image download wrapper and redundant counter.
- Regression growth is 68 test lines, covered by the change-specific allocation; these exercise the two affected provider boundaries and preserve MIME/timing behavior. Production net LOC is 0; docs +4 and allocation +2.

These tests execute the independent main-based implementation with synthetic network responses; no paid fal call or live channel send was made. Covered by merged [#189768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189768), `7b29a23da2a6e787eca43c757bbc489f83d5b682`. This duplicate is closed without merging.

Fixes standalone service relay artifacts unexpectedly retaining the database preflight handler graph after the host worker pool began importing its child registry.

Found in scheduled full [run 41238866951](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41238866951), head `8100edf85a07788d5ffc08c6496ed3238860c6ca`, job **node compact small42 / 124648552421**. Introduced by [a805746632d1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a805746632d1c38534cdad037350d2f38dec34f3) (#189722).

## User Impact

Changes production build/import behavior: one-shot helpers exclude child-only read handlers. Startup metadata still retires its native child before Gateway admission; no schema, retention, config, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the single startup-metadata retirement predicate at the pool effect and remove the registry policy wrapper and host-to-child value import.

## Evidence

The covering main commit passed the same two emitted-artifact cases and all three original-order cancellation, reuse, and native-retirement cases locally. Its CI gate passed in [run 41243178904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41243178904). The conflict was detected before any merge request for this PR was sent.

Two exact service-relay runtime/worker artifact cases and three original-order cancellation, reuse, and startup-metadata retirement cases. Existing emitted-file and native retirement assertions remain unchanged. Production +3/-12 lines; no test edits.

The accepted l182 repair has red-before/green-after focused proof, scoped TypeScript, typed lint, format, whitespace, and independent canonical Codex autoreview (P0–P2, scoped-clean, no remaining findings). The reviewed source snapshot was based on `8088fcd1f416851087eafbe4d356689f749a449d` and matches accepted commit `f65a663d1c92`; mechanical splitting preserves that delta. The complete accepted source delta is unchanged; source freshness and exact-head native review are checked before landing. Only the focused proof above is replayed here; PR CI supplies broader exact-head coverage. Local runtime is Linux/Node 26; CI runtime coverage remains separate.

Simplification and test audit: the change uses existing owners, removes superseded machinery where applicable, and preserves the independent assertions.

Requested by @steipete

title: feat(cli): accept bounded stdin model prompts
body:
Supersedes #139221, thanks @Zundar

Related: #139208, #189301

## What Problem This Solves

Pipelines cannot send one-shot model prompts through stdin without putting the text in process arguments or creating a temporary prompt file.

## User Impact

`openclaw infer model run --prompt-stdin --json < prompt.txt` and the `capability` alias accept up to 1 MiB of UTF-8 input. Exactly one of `--prompt`, `--prompt-file`, or `--prompt-stdin` is required. Invalid input fails before inference. The selected provider still receives the prompt; no configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

#189301 (a5d66ef1) added bounded file input, but its landed command does not read stdin. This small follow-up extends the existing prompt-selection owner and reuses the shared byte-stream reader and UTF-8 decoder before the unchanged local and Gateway paths.

The simplification pass retained one input selector and extended the existing file-input test table. Production grows by 14 lines; there is no equivalent dead or duplicate code in this owner to remove safely. Tests grow by 56 lines for stdin boundaries, errors, and conflicting sources, with a separate regression allocation.

## Evidence

- Base: `e67e538d68acec33e87fce6a6717fade04da1b10`; the affected owner and tests are identical on checked main `6b7aa2be9d99705e5b02d22a182d61b1792077e3`. Nine stdin regressions fail on the unchanged command with unknown `--prompt-stdin`, while both file-input cases pass. The fixed command passes all 43 model-run cases.
- Final focused run: 102 existing CLI cases, 43 model-run cases, and 14 prompt-prefix stability cases passed. Total wall time: 39.19 seconds; the two CLI files took 11.75 seconds together, including under one second of model-run test execution. The first cold model-run run took 43.86 seconds including shared compiler preparation; its actual tests took about 2.3 seconds.
- Real bounded streams cover exactly 1 MiB, UTF-8 split across chunks, byte-count overflow, malformed UTF-8, whitespace, read failure, and rejection of conflicting sources without consuming stdin. Provider and Gateway I/O use fixtures; no live-provider run is claimed.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. The local repository-wide test-line ratchet exceeded its 60-second cap; [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41241343378) passed that gate and all selected jobs for `04dad42dc434` in 415 seconds wall time (807 summed Node-test job seconds).
- Shared autoreview of the complete local candidate that became `04dad42dc434`, against `e67e538d68ac`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected supplied change/source context but did not execute tests or independently inspect the unchanged stream/decoder helpers.
- Contributor code was read only using GitHub and was never checked out or executed. Human commit credit: `Co-authored-by: Zundar <37469922+Zundar@users.noreply.github.com>`.

title: fix(scripts): explain recovery when boundary preparation fails
body:
Supersedes #139551, thanks @ylcn91.

## What Problem This Solves

Boundary preparation failures during lint report an exit code without a recovery step.

## User Impact

Contributors now see `pnpm install` suggested when dependencies changed. The failure still stops lint and reports the preparation exit code. No runtime, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the contributor's useful conditional guidance in a compact message. Production LOC: +1/-1, net 0; no execution changes. - Local autoreview of the complete local change against the main SHA above, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189758#issuecomment-6549064173) also found no actionable defects.

title: feat(cron): let human owners manage and transfer automations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation owners cannot manage or hand over their schedules from the Automations page without administrator access.

## User Impact and Design

The editor gains an Owner selector beneath Agent. Administrators and the current human owner can edit or transfer an automation; other humans cannot modify it. Agent-created jobs retain separate conversation-scoped capability checks.

A transfer pauses the automation, cancels active occurrences, and retires captured execution authority. The recipient cannot silently use the previous owner's credentials. Trusted human-creator records supply the initial owner without rewriting audit provenance. Ordinary edits, force-run, or transferring back do not satisfy the requirement for fresh execution-authority capture.

The Gateway owns authorization and retirement; the UI reflects its decisions. Human ownership, immutable creator provenance, and agent/session capability stay separate. Host-command, session-routing, tool and approval restrictions are preserved. Requested by @VACInc.

## Review Repairs

Initial five findings repaired in `9b34a698` (original `3de16314`):
- Private `ownerTransferPending` distinguishes actual transfers from legacy app-only recovery.
- Pending transfers are blocked before isolated/main/named-session dispatch; only fresh private authority capture clears the guard.
- Profile-directory reads obey visibility, attachment and Gateway lifecycle admission.
- E2E inventory, direct run/remove commit-guard assertions and keyboard navigation are updated.

The active-execution finding on `156ed1d1` is repaired in **`49f55e04`**: the existing committed-mutation cancellation owner now cancels when human ownership changes, including force-runs of already-paused jobs. Explicit-disable cancellation remains intact, while display edits and unchanged ownership do not cancel. This adds two net production lines, not another revocation mechanism.

## Current Candidate and Proof

Published head **`be693bc6c568c5c5778925a324844710410173b1`** has exactly the tested `49f55e04` tree. Rebased onto `7232a8de67eff527b3f5764987312f2424beda94` as requested; the rebase tree matched an independent integration oracle. Upstream Memory/hovercard fixes were preserved, not replaced with obsolete assertions. Human credit and authored repairs were retained.

- **Final-head CI passed:** [run 41253288557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41253288557). Pre-merge full check snapshot: **100 success, 66 skipped, 1 neutral, zero failed or pending**. Both real-Gateway E2E shards passed, including the active-transfer scenario.
- **Active transfer red/green:** on `156ed1d1`, both enabled/paused scheduler cases fail because cancellation never arrives, and the real Gateway/browser run incorrectly completes successfully after transfer. With `49f55e04`, scheduler **3/3 pass** and real-Gateway/browser **1/1 passes**.
- The browser proof first executes a real file-write tool through a local HTTP model with a synthetic credential. It then holds another model response during a force-run of a paused job, transfers ownership, and releases an attempted write. The run terminates with the transfer cancellation reason, the file does not exist, and no further provider request occurs. Former-owner denial, recipient edits, and isolated/shared recovery failures remain covered. No paid/external model or real credential is claimed.
- Local repair timings: scheduler 0.641 s test / 50.61 s wall including worker preparation; browser 6.827 s test / 55.42 s Vitest wall. The existing browser boot is reused. **41 net test lines** are allocated for the distinct in-flight boundary; no new suite or timeout increase.
- Targeted lint, formatting, canonical Cron and UI-E2E typechecks, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of the repair is **scoped-clean**. Simplification retained the existing cancellation owner.
- **Latest-stable upgrade passed:** [run 41251264471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41251264471), baseline **2026.10.8**, pinned package/workflow `156ed1d1`, both `base` and `cron-scheduled-authority` scenarios successful. Package integrity and npm install acceptance also passed. This is explicitly pre-repair-head evidence: the only later production change is post-commit active-run cancellation; schemas, migration, persisted fields, recovery and startup are unchanged. Current-head cancellation behavior is separately proven above. No image publication or deployment.

### Retained earlier proof and disclosed gaps

- Scheduler/session/fallback/store **44/44**, including legacy creator backfill, app-only recovery, transfer back, persistence and fresh-authority recovery. Four behavior regressions fail on original base `fd55221c` and pass with the fix; ownership UI likewise fails on the base.
- Gateway policy **21/21**, ownership UI **1/1**, E2E inventory **14/14**, production types/lint/build passed. Earlier lifecycle suite **33/34**: the cold lazy-render failure reproduced on untouched original base. A separate cold local rebased run timed out before Gateway readiness; the subsequently expanded red/green scenario reached the actual behavior, and final-head CI passed. Neither setup failure is counted as passing proof.
- Notice fixture repair preserves requester/foreign-job nondisclosure and write denial. Upstream Memory/hovercard expectations are retained; no production permission relaxation.
- An earlier local-review migration suggestion was declined because an unmerged, undeployed intermediate revision is not a shipped compatibility contract. Released stored-data compatibility is covered by the upgrade and legacy tests above.

## Visual Proof

Actual source UI, same synthetic fixture, Chromium 1440×1000, before original base and after `a58a740`; this UI is unchanged by the rebase and cancellation repair. Both sanitized captures were inspected, attached in the originating chat, and uploaded in [the proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189749#issuecomment-6549285963). Both images were also verified rendering at 1440×1000 in the actual GitHub PR page and those rendered screenshots inspected. Visual gate complete.

![Before: automation editor without human owner selector](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d7dd878-df73-421c-b7c4-5c5352c6f449)

![After: human Owner selector directly below Agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d3e8f5-c4b6-459c-9fd5-278f8ad72980)

**Final-head ClawSweeper review complete:** [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189749#issuecomment-6549030790), reviewed `be693bc6` at 2026-11-01 00:06 UTC. No findings, no before-merge items, ready for maintainer review. No live Gateway, deployment, or user automation was modified.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

title: chore(deps): refresh mature dependencies through the Oct 29 cutoff
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Qualifies maintained dependencies with a seven-full-day cutoff instead of letting an older blocked landing prevent the next daily audit. This PR retains the October 31 sweep and contains the November 5 catch-up, integrated with current `main` only for real conflicts.

## User Impact

Refreshes provider SDKs, ACP adapters, HTML/Markdown processing, media, QA, native mobile tooling, Rust TLS helpers and release tooling. No configuration migration or user action. Updates that showed a regression or a downgrade are deferred rather than forced. No claim that dependencies are vulnerability-free or that every ecosystem is current.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **November 5 audit:** `2026-11-05T04:30:52.133Z`; inclusive cutoff **`2026-10-29T04:30:52.133Z`**; audit baseline `bca996c12f55`. Every introduced version, including transitives, is at or before the cutoff. An earlier 9m40s-later working cutoff was superseded; zero introduced versions fall in that gap.
- **October 31 audit** (`2026-10-31T16:54:00Z`, cutoff `2026-10-24T16:54:00Z`) remains historical; its ACP app-builder migration, Matrix 44 patch carry-forward, TypeBox accumulator generator repair and oxlint 1.89 source fixes stay in the branch.
- No new release-age exception, override, patch, cast, lint disable, weakened assertion or gate change. The only override edit repins the existing `codex-acp>@openai/codex` 0.164.0 pin to the new adapter version.

### Researched highlights

- **entities 8.1.0 → 9.0.0** ([release](https://github.com/fb55/entities/releases/tag/v9.0.0)): faster HTML decoding upstream. OpenClaw only uses the unchanged synchronous `decodeHTMLStrict`/`decodeHTMLAttribute`.
- **OpenAI 7.43.0 → 7.45.1** ([7.44.0](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.44.0)): delegation/cache controls and stream action-check reuse; the breaking Live Decision union change has no OpenClaw consumer.
- **axios 1.21.0 (override)** ([release](https://github.com/axios/axios/releases/tag/v1.21.0)): restores Fetch in runtimes that reject implicit `cache: 'default'`; proxy/multipart fixes.
- **ACP:** Claude adapter 0.95.0 → 0.99.0, SDK 2.1.0, Codex adapter 2.3.0 ([releases](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/releases)): ACP error codes, subagent model reporting, usage-limit error kept after compaction. SDK 2.1 adds an initialization gate; the startup test fixture now initializes before session traffic (null/empty-ID assertions unchanged).
- **Fastlane 2.241.1 → 2.241.2** ([release](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/releases/tag/2.241.2)): fixes GHSA-m67f-ghvw-j7qp (spaceship), GHSA-gqqf-9mh3-3578 and GHSA-hqmj-jmgc-wmwp; identical dependency map. Android and iOS bundles and the workflow version checks move together.
- **Gradle setup action v6.4.1** ([release](https://github.com/gradle/actions/releases/tag/v6.4.1)): security fix in dependency submission (OpenClaw uses setup-gradle; no direct exposure claimed).
- **Rust:** ctutils 0.4.7 (constant-time hardening on Thumb-1/RISCV32), openssl-probe 0.2.2, tauri-plugin-deep-link 2.6.3 / single-instance 2.5.5 (rust-ini compile fix). **Go:** golang.org/x/net 0.62.0.
- **Sandbox CLI 4.10.0 → 4.11.1** (release tooling): only `@vercel/sandbox` 3.9.0 → 3.9.1 changes in its standalone lock; the materializer's pinned lock hash and integrity assertions are updated.
- Also: marked 18.1.2, LINE 11.4.0, AWS SDK 3.1159, Mistral 3.4.0, MCP ext-apps 2.1.0, Google auth 11.3.2, music-metadata 12.3.2, ONNX 1.31.1, PostCSS 8.5.32, qs 6.17.1, tsdown 0.23.3 (existing `rolldown-plugin-dts` 0.28.8 override unchanged; no resolved downgrade), wrangler 4.155.0, TypeScript nightly 20261028.

### Deferred (rechecked today)

- **mailauth 8.0.4:** downgrades `commander` 15.0.0 → 14.0.3 and `undici` 8.11.2 → 7.30.1; main's 7.3.1 kept. joi 18.3.1 is now age-eligible but mailauth pins joi 18.3.0 exactly.
- **CUA driver 0.38:** native artifact digests differ from the accepted manifest. **oxfmt 0.75 / oxlint 1.90:** formatter/linter parity failures. **Convex broker 1.48:** standalone qualification not done.
- **croner 11** (DST/startAt semantics), **minimatch 11 / path-to-regexp 9** (transitive majors), **Matrix 45** (patch re-port), **Solid vite-plugin next.52** (compiler/runtime skew), **TanStack virtual-core 3.19.8** (known picker regression), **Codex 0.165** (harness requalification), **tsrs 0.20**.
- **swift-collections 1.7.5:** eligible, but native macOS qualification is blocked: the cloud worker has no prepared darwin/arm64 runtime. Other Swift/Android graphs were inventoried; parent-capped Swift transitives and Dependabot-owned Gradle/Actions groups are unchanged.
- **ClawHub CLI 0.24.1:** would drop the scoped undici override and downgrade undici. **vercel 65.7.0:** large bundled-builder jump without release notes.
- Separately owned: OpenTelemetry 3 (#189667), Anthropic/Vertex 1.x (#189697), Copilot SDK (#189703), MXC (#167292).

## Evidence

- **Lock audit (pnpm, off-host native resolution):** lock `af4214be…` (then `5d50f435…` after main's vitest patch-hash change; no new package identities): 115 new npm identities, all ≤ cutoff, no unknown dates; 3,722 matched dependency edges, zero downgrades. Cargo/Bundler/Go/npm standalone locks were regenerated natively; every changed crate, gem and package has an exact registry timestamp and checksum ≤ cutoff.
- **Native/standalone age proof vs main `6cdd1c7a`:** 93 introduced identities (crates 15, Linux Tauri 34, WatchRTC 1, gems 4, Go 1, vercel-cli 38), all published ≤ cutoff with matching registry checksums/integrity.
- **Off-host Linux proof (corrective tree `561d1e1b`, commit `8db64e64`):** frozen install; protocol generation; package-contract 64 passed/3 skipped (fixture now copies `release-context.mjs`/`release-version.mjs`); TypeBox 15/15; ACP startup 15/15; CUA artifacts 5/5; Codex recovery 12/12; IMAP watcher 55/55; manifests/HTML 9/9; formatter/Bun parity; Rust gateway-client + node-host 106/106; Fastlane frozen load in both graphs; Sandbox CLI materialized at 4.11.1; focused oxlint on touched production files clean. Some results were recorded on intermediate trees that differ only in later unrelated fixture/pin files.
- **Main integrations** (each only for an actual conflict; main made no dependency-manifest change in any of them):
  - `bca996c12f55`: generated predicates, Postgres bridge worker, qa-lab manifest, lock; main-introduced `no-lonely-if`, `no-div-regex` and predicate findings fixed at the source.
  - `15bec5ab81c2`: workflow-guard fixture; main's equivalent fix (#193170) adopted verbatim.
  - `fcac16691153`: lock conflict from main's vitest patch-hash change (#190823); lock regenerated natively off-host, tree `94719e97` reproduced locally byte-for-byte.
  - `6cdd1c7ac3b2`: generated gateway predicates; regenerated with the branch generator (locked typebox 1.4.3 / esbuild 0.28.2 / oxfmt 0.74.0), `gateway:validators --check` clean; the only difference from main is the counting-reducer rewrite.
- **Prior head `9701478` CI (historical, superseded):** two failures. (1) `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` test-lines: over by 4 with net +84. Off-host on the merged tree with main `fcac1669`: this branch is over by **29** with net +84, and main `fcac1669` itself is over by **29** with net 0 (main passes only under the non-increasing rule). The overage is main's, not this PR's; allocation credit equals exact growth. (2) `control-ui-performance`: base and candidate both exceed the absolute startup-JS cap; main's own run measures 92404 B against the 90815 B cap and passes only because growth is +0. That run showed candidate +400 B over base with +2 raw bytes; off-host on the merged tree with main `fcac1669`, `ui:check-performance:base` passes with **−3 B** (92398 → 92395 B).
- **Current head `67d2fce7`** (tree `2c500d48`) PR CI run 41992904186 attempt 1: **failed** — 174 jobs passed, 16 skipped, `security-fast` passed; the only failed leaf is `checks-node-compact-small-7` (job 127130169542), plus the `openclaw/ci-gate` aggregate. That leaf fails `test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` › *Windows CI partitions* because `vitest.cli.config.ts` is shared by both Windows partitions. Scheduled main run 41994726590 (job 127135526377, `ba75cf71`) fails the identical case and assertion. The cause is main's 558e2f3a (#185917); every input of that test is byte-identical between main and this PR. The prior-head test-budget and performance failures no longer appear.
- **Test-line budget:** net growth vs current main `6cdd1c7ac3b2` is +84 (TypeBox counting cases, ACP SDK 2 fixture/setup, packaging fixture imports), recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/deps-mature-20261031.txt` per [writing-tests](docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md#cost-budget); shared scalar unchanged. These run inside existing focused files; no new processes or timeouts.
- **Review:** exact-head autoreview of `67d2fce7` against main `6cdd1c7a` at P0–P2: no findings. The earlier corrective-tree review (`561d1e1b`) was also clean; an earlier independent review's mailauth-downgrade finding is fixed by the deferral.

title: test(skills): consolidate project skill picker test fixtures
body:
Related: #188663

## What Problem This Solves

The project skill picker tests added in #188663 repeated the same Gateway, paired-node and UI catalog setup across several files. That made the routing and admission contracts harder to read and maintain.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Tests only: no product, protocol, config or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Moves the repeated paired-node skill workspace setup into one small shared fixture.
- Keeps each host-routing check with the code that owns it. The Gateway `commands.list` test keeps the preview checks. The created-session catalog check now lives in the skill discovery test, which compares that catalog with the reply-path loaders, including their node roots.
- Folds duplicated project-scoped UI catalog cases into the existing owner-replacement and session-catalog tests.

The distinct regressions from #188663 stay covered:
- authorization, admission and recheck before disclosure;
- sandbox, node vs Gateway file host, and workspace pseudo-project;
- precedence, allowlist and invocation;
- stale responses, cache invalidation and unrelated sessions.

Across the five touched test files, cases go from 89 to 88 and lines from 1827 to 1717 (net −110). The UI "never sends projectId with a sessionKey" case is folded into the session-catalog test.

## Evidence

- **Focused suites, before and after:**
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/commands.project-skills.test.ts`: 2/2 passed.
  - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-commands.test.ts`: 22/22 before, 21/21 after.
  - `ui/src/pages/new-session/composer.test.tsx`: 58/58 passed.
- **Discovery test:** `src/skills/discovery/chat-commands.discovery.test.ts` has two existing allowlist failures. They reproduce identically on the unchanged base and on this change; their loader cause is unproven and they are not addressed here. The other 5 cases pass.
- **Other checks:** `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass.
- **Mutation spot checks:** temporarily breaking each retained product guard failed a retained test. The checks covered authorization, recheck, sandbox containment, routing, precedence, the command allowlist, invocation, catalog parity and the UI cache/stale-response guards. Two mutants on redundant guard layers survive on both the original #188663 tests and this change, so this change introduces no coverage loss. The creator-role sandbox input path remains untested, as before.
- **Timing:** local wall times were dominated by host load and are not a performance claim.
- **Review:** an exact-candidate review of this head found no actionable issues.
