title: feat: offer a disclosed compatible copy for supported mixed-track recordings
body:
Part of #180550.

## What Problem This Solves

Some mixed-track recordings have usable video and stereo AAC audio but cannot be prepared because an additional unsupported APAC track would be lost.

## User Impact

After **Compress to fit**, eligible attachments offer **Create compatible copy** with a separate disclosure and confirmation. The copy omits the additional APAC track and its spatial information, re-encodes video and retained audio, and is neither lossless nor spatially equivalent. **Download original** retains the unchanged source while the attachment remains in the draft. Nothing uploads or sends automatically.

**Draft proposal, not merge-ready:** implementation and draft publication were authorized by @vyctorbrzezowski and @TheAngryPit for human review. This does not establish final fidelity-policy acceptance, real Apple APAC support, a completed device matrix, or a diamond evaluation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing bounded worker, serialized queue, attachment-read lifecycle and Solid preview rather than introducing another preparation pipeline. Eligibility is exactly one decodable video, one decodable two-channel AAC track and one additional unsupported audio track identified by its container sample entry as APAC. Only known BT.709/sRGB SDR profiles qualify.

The worker revalidates the precise omitted track ID after consent and checks exact utilized/discarded inventories. A small ISO-BMFF header audit accounts for track IDs that Mediabunny's audio/video projection can hide. Within this compatible-copy path, all other track loss remains refused. MP4 forces H.264/AAC; WebM forces VP9/Opus, including AAC-source audio. Removal and draft replacement invalidate pending consent/results; retries cannot broaden consent.

Preserves the owners from #172844 and #179007. It does not take over #180319's retained-error notices, #180298's picker discovery or #172163's post-upload playback.

## Evidence

Base: c9405cd28d98d909548e383f101636e497e42e1c; Mediabunny 1.62.1. Proof below is for this independent candidate, not the earlier parent-session implementation.

- **77 focused tests passed** across seven attachment/worker/policy/inventory files: 3.46 s Vitest, 4.66 s wrapper wall. Three new consent/draft regressions failed on the baseline and pass with the fix. Strict refusal controls cover unavailable codecs, unsupported video, no usable AAC, unapproved/hidden track loss, HDR/unknown color, malformed inventory and existing bounded output/cancellation behavior.
- **Three production-build browser E2Es passed**, 26.49 s total; test callbacks 13.42 s. The new 10.91 s case exercises real encoding, the rendered loss disclosure, Cancel/remove/reselection, byte-exact original download, draft and other-attachment preservation, unmuted completed playback and a nonzero stereo waveform. Earlier browser attempts failed during diagnostics in the fontless container; task-local fallback-font configuration allowed the unchanged existing tests to pass. No guards or assertions were weakened.
- The existing New Session partial-paste cancellation and preview-URL cleanup E2E also passed (1 selected case, 1.24 s callback; 10 unrelated cases filtered out).
- A pinned-base production UI run reproduced refusal of the same synthetic input. The built worker independently changed from refusal to offer/confirmed conversion.
- **Actual WebM conversion, Linux Chromium 156.0.8078.4:** 745,204-byte input to 164,616-byte output under a 524,288-byte budget; actual VP9/Opus, video/webm, .webm. Native capabilities were H.264/VP9/Opus encoding available, AAC encoding unavailable; AAC decoding worked. No custom codec was installed in the application.
- Decoded source/output each retained 180 frames and all four colored edge markers at 320×180. Audio markers were 0.52/5.52 s and visual flashes 0.5/5.5 s in both: 20 ms offset and no measured added drift at 10 ms resolution. Parsed duration 6.037333→6.04 s; decoded output audio ended at 6.0535 s. Known SDR metadata remained BT.709/sRGB. These meet the proposed numerical tolerances for this synthetic fixture, not an accepted cross-device qualification.
- UI production, UI chat-test and UI E2E-chat typechecks, focused lint, CSS lint, formatting, i18n baseline/verify, controller guards, documentation links, test-line budget and whitespace checks passed. One unchanged Solid reactivity warning remains in the existing context-copy callback.
- Author test-audit/simplification applied. Net change is +290 production lines and +416 test lines, plus docs/provenance. Growth supplies the complete-inventory/consent/recovery path and distinct worker/lifecycle/browser proofs; no new service, dependency, configuration or test-only production hook. The scoped test allocation records exactly this regression growth; the shared scalar is unchanged.

### Review and qualification gaps

- Native autoreview at P0–P3 refused the complete staged candidate because the added MP4 binary cannot be reviewed. **No independent review was produced.** The binary remains in scope; no alternate reviewer/host was used to bypass the refusal. Named Comment Sicko and independent source-blind validation were not performed. Human draft review is requested; no diamond claim.
- The purpose-generated fixture has an unknown sample entry labeled APAC, **not genuine Apple APAC**. Provenance and SHA-256 are beside the fixture. Genuine consented/redistributable Apple APAC remains required; the private original is not requested.
- **Real MP4/H.264/AAC output remains unqualified** in this environment. Controlled branch tests are not natural AAC-encoder availability or successful MP4 output.
- Physical iPhone/iPad Safari, macOS Safari, the existing WKWebView Control UI host and Windows Chrome/Edge need consenting operators/access and matching fixtures. Native composers, HEVC/HDR handling, human listening and final tolerance/merge-versus-release gate agreement remain open under the umbrella. No hardware reservations or platform support guarantees are claimed.
- Initial exact-head checks at 19bda08ee197aabf097c23c9070547605241c1fa: 5 passed and 63 skipped/neutral. The broad CI preflight and ci-gate were skipped on this draft, so this is **not broad CI proof**. ClawSweeper acknowledged receipt; no review result is claimed.

### Before and after

All three uploaded images are publicly readable and match the inspected local SHA-256 bytes. The published tree matches the tested staged tree exactly; commit parent is the pinned base above, and both required human coauthor trailers were verified.

Pinned base c9405cd2 refuses the synthetic mixed-track fixture. This candidate offers explicit loss consent, then a bounded copy with original recovery. Captures use synthetic data and Chromium mobile emulation, not a physical Apple device.

title: fix(agents): skip credential retries for missing models
body:
Supersedes #138943, thanks @teddytennant.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes wasted credential attempts when a provider explicitly reports that the requested model is unknown, missing, or retired.

## User Impact

Assistant failures for absent models advance directly to the configured fallback, or surface the error when no fallback exists. Authentication, quota, account-access and plan failures still allow profile recovery. Ambiguous not-found responses retain their existing behavior. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing run failover policy now handles affirmative model absence alongside its certificate-error exception. Consolidating duplicated profile-decision parameter declarations keeps production LOC unchanged (+30/-30). Tests grow by 70 lines, with a dedicated allocation for the recovery regression; docs grow by six lines.

This is a maintainer-authored replacement so the contributor branch was only read with `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff`, and was never checked out or run. Both human author identities from the original commit metadata are credited; machine authors are excluded.

## Evidence

- On main `5bbed787a731`, the two new missing/unknown-model regressions failed: the real assistant-failure handler and model-fallback runner attempted profiles 0, 1 and 2 before fallback. Six profile-specific/ambiguous controls passed.
- After the fix, the assistant-failure suite passes all 36 tests. Each explicit absence now reaches fallback after profile 0, without advancing credentials; the table includes separator variants, Gemini missing models, Ollama retirement and model deprecation. The no-fallback case surfaces the missing-model error.
- Focused policy, prompt-failure, attempt-normalization and prompt-prefix stability suites also pass (84 tests). The final assistant suite took 48.45 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation, with under two seconds of test execution. Broad proof and CI timings come from PR CI.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, docs link audit and `git diff --check` pass. Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) is scoped-clean after fixing its concrete format-coverage findings.
- [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41235798270) passed, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate` and test-line ratchet. The two changed-test CI jobs took 298 and 244 seconds, including their setup and other selected tests.
- Proof uses synthetic assistant errors and isolated test state; no live vendor or Gateway was run. The production Team Gateway and its state were untouched.

title: fix(whatsapp): resume reconnect when last-route writes stall
body:
Supersedes #139161, thanks @SebTardif.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp reconnect and shutdown can wait indefinitely when a last-route persistence write stalls.

## User Impact

User impact: WhatsApp can reconnect after a stalled route write instead of waiting forever. Teardown gives pending writes 15 seconds, warns on timeout, and continues closing the listener and transport. The underlying writes remain active; a locked store can still delay persistence until it recovers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `raceWithTimeout` helper only at the connection teardown boundary, without an abort signal, so shutdown retains its drain window. Normal message processing continues to track every route write and report persistence failures.

The same owner now shares its duplicate raw WebSocket fallback and lets `clearInterval` handle absent timers directly. Production delta: +13/-15 (net -2). Regression-test delta: +69/-2 (net +67); the dedicated 67-line allocation covers stuck-write reconnect/shutdown, slow successful shutdown, and synchronous fallback behavior. No new timeout helper, configuration, schema, or dependency.

## Evidence

- Base `5bbed787a731a2bda8b780d1f1eb198f619762de`: the new fake-timer reconnect and shutdown cases both fail because teardown is still unfinished at 15 seconds; the other 26 cases pass. The same unbounded await is present on newer main `8186cba2d875`.
- Fixed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 29/29 pass; final warm run 10.36 s wall (Vitest 7.99 s, under 1 s test bodies). Reconnect actually closes the old transport and installs its replacement; shutdown waits for an early-finishing write.
- Final P0-P2 Codex autoreview against the base above: scoped-clean, no actionable findings; reviewed the complete local candidate plus timeout, persistence-producer, and socket-cleanup source. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the initial hosted ClawSweeper dispatch is already queued, so no duplicate request was sent.
- Focused format, whitespace, lint, and targeted source/test typecheck pass. Exact-head [PR CI run 41235549508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41235549508) passed all 33 selected jobs in 482 seconds. The changed-code test job took 344 seconds for its shared selection, not this file alone. The test-line ratchet passed in CI after the local whole-repository scan hit its 60-second cap.
- This is controller-boundary proof with controlled socket/store completion, not a live WhatsApp transport or real SQLite-lock experiment. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

title: fix(update): hand foreground Gateway recovery back to systemd
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Failed updates can leave systemd recovery blocked by a foreground Gateway holding the service's state directory, while the update report labels an unverified readiness check as “not serving.”

## User Impact

Managed recovery now gracefully stops the verified foreground owner, waits for its exit, and restarts through the installed service. Native restart permission, config, and live-authority guards run before shutdown. Other supervisors, reused PIDs, and unverifiable owners are preserved. Reports distinguish unverified readiness from independently observed current health.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guarded service restart owns the handoff for both the candidate CLI invoked by older updaters and retained-service recovery. Preserved CLI recovery prepares its service-targeted restart intent after foreground ownership settles. No detached Gateway fallback is introduced.

The original spawning command remains unproven. Source inspection of beta.4 and main found managed recovery using the service manager; compile-cache exec/spawn alone does not explain a cgroup escape. This PR repairs the demonstrated recovery and reporting gaps without attributing that launch to an unverified path.

## Evidence

- Final-head [CI run 41240685941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41240685941), attempt 1, completed successfully on `fc9a21c540010e0fa708b6731a38965ea1e6e3d7`. All three PostgreSQL conformance lanes and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed; there were no failed jobs.

- The real CLI recovery regression failed before the fix and passes afterward. It also covers shutdown settlement and preservation of another supervisor, a reused PID, and an owner protected by newer config.
- 74 service integration cases, 16 retained-owner cases, and 15 restart-intent cases passed. Report/progress suites passed 159 tests; four affected output-consumer cases passed.
- Targeted CLI/update and infra typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, docs content sanity, and diff checks passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final staged change against `64e2da31a4fa`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Complete owning guard implementations were supplied after the initial pass identified a context gap.
- CI identified an unchecked error cast in the new signal handler. Reusing the existing errno classifier fixes the assertion-safety ratchet; four handoff cases, targeted typecheck/lint/format, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review of that correction passed.
- Hosted review identified a P1: a non-root caller could signal a same-account foreground owner before a system-scope restart was refused. Recovery now resolves the native target and reuses `assertSystemdServiceActionAllowed` before SIGTERM, rechecking live authority after discovery. The permission case failed before this repair. Six Linux cases now use real child processes, start identities, SIGTERM, liveness, and shutdown waits; other supervisors, reused PIDs, newer config, missing permission, and revoked authority preserve the child. Owner discovery and manager transport remain simulated. The final service suite (74), intent suite (15), and retained native suite (16) pass; the two stale queued fixture mocks found by the broader run were repaired by restoring the inherited implementation in `finally`.
- Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review of the permission repair: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The unchanged native permission/authority owners were supplied in full.
- Blacksmith Testbox capacity queued and the task lease was stopped. Live systemd/WSL2 and a published-driver upgrade were not exercised; the regressions are the available behavior proof.

The service integration fixture had 54 identical failures on base and candidate because native discovery escaped its mocks. Aligning discovery with its actual isolated user-unit fixture restored the suite without weakening production checks. The 156-line test allocation covers the handoff/report regressions, real process effects, permission/authority refusals, and fixture work needed to validate them.

Timing: the final permission-repair service suite took 38.55s and the intent suite 11.36s of Vitest time (170.61s wrapper with runtime preparation); retained native tests took 9.89s. The original combined recovery suites took 83.19s of Vitest time, with the two updated intent mock cases subsequently passing in the 27.91s intent suite; report/progress checks took 59.39s including compilation, and affected output consumers took 127.59s including runtime preparation. CI duration is recorded by the attached workflow.

Landing review found and reproduced one further P2: user-unit activation could refuse a conflicting system owner after the foreground process had already stopped. Recovery now calls the existing activation-ownership guard before SIGTERM and rechecks live authority after inspection. The real CLI regression failed on the previous head because its child had been stopped. The full service suite passed 75 cases; after a mechanical test typing correction, the ownership-refusal regression and all 16 retained native restart cases passed. Scoped lint, targeted typecheck, formatting, assertion safety, test-line allocation, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete incoming range (base `64e2da31a4fa`, head `0bd847410fb1`) identified that P2; the final correction against `0bd847410fb1` is scoped-clean at P0–P2 with complete permission/ownership/authority source supplied. No actionable findings remain. The added 16 test lines protect the new refusal case using a real child and the native restart owner; native manager I/O remains simulated.

title: fix(copilot): update Copilot SDK to 1.0.26 while keeping isolated turns remote-denied
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Security gate open, not ready to land.** SDK 1.0.26 has no supported way to deny remote export and steering per session before create or resume. If an operator's runtime is launched with remote enabled by default, the runtime enters remote setup inside `resumeSession`, before the post-resume deny in this PR can run. The details and options are under "Security gate" below. A maintainer decision, or an authorized credential to probe the authenticated case, is required before merge.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Copilot plugin is stuck on `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.25 because 1.0.26 removed the `remoteSession: "off"` session option OpenClaw used to keep isolated turns (isolated completions and settled-tool finalization) out of Mission Control export and remote steering.

## User Impact

User impact: Copilot runtime users get SDK 1.0.26 / bundled Copilot CLI 1.0.103. With OpenClaw's default runtime launch, isolated Copilot turns keep remote export and steering off from create/resume through the prompt. If the deny RPC fails, or wedges until the run is cancelled, the isolated turn fails before any prompt reaches the model. Ordinary Copilot turns are unchanged: they never pinned remote off. Operator runtimes launched with remote enabled by default are not equivalently protected yet (see the Security gate).

## Why This Change Was Made

Version change: `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.25 → 1.0.26, plus its 8 platform packages, in `extensions/copilot/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. 1.0.26 is the newest release outside the repo's 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` (published 2026-10-22T16:38Z). 1.0.27 (2026-10-27) and 1.0.28 (2026-10-28) are still inside that window.

Upstream highlights:
- [v1.0.26 release](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/releases/tag/v1.0.26): "Updated the bundled Copilot CLI snapshot to 1.0.103". [Compare v1.0.25...v1.0.26](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/compare/v1.0.25...v1.0.26): `f2b720c8ec` and `f527e6134f` (SDK snapshot for CLI 1.0.103).
- `docs/features/remote-sessions.md` now describes remote sessions as read-only history export, not remote control. The `enableRemoteSessions` client option and the create/resume `remoteSession` option are gone; the 1.0.26 client no longer sends either. `session.rpc.remote.enable/disable` and `session.remote_steerable_changed` remain. The generated RPC contract documents `remote.disable` as "Disables remote session export and steering."
- `session.sendAndWait` now first tries a new `session.sendAndWait` completion RPC. It falls back to `session.send` only when the runtime answers JSON-RPC MethodNotFound (-32601).
- New host APIs: `allowCreatingNewSessions` (denied by default), `host.setSessionCreationPolicy` and host authentication. OpenClaw does not use them.

The change: right after create or resume, and before the first send, isolated completions and settled-tool finalization call `session.rpc.remote.disable()`. If that method is missing or rejects, the turn fails closed. In isolated completions the call runs inside the existing completion deadline and cancellation boundary. In settled finalization it is raced against the run's abort signal. In both paths the existing cleanup disconnects the session and releases the pooled client. The catalog-lifetime fault peer now answers unsupported RPCs with MethodNotFound, as a real runtime does, so the SDK's fallback is exercised. It also asserts the exact unsupported set.

## Security gate

All probes below ran on the real bundled runtime with a temp home, an isolated synthetic session, a BYOK synthetic provider and no GitHub auth.

- **How the runtime decides.** Remote mode at create/resume is computed in the runtime with no auth input. An explicit per-session request wins, and otherwise the runtime falls back to its launch default, set by the `--remote` launcher flag. This flag is the only default source I found: the `remoteSessions` setting had no effect in five config locations. The bundled `copilot-runtime` accepts `--remote`, `--no-remote` and `--no-remote-export`, and rejects unknown flags.
- **OpenClaw's default launch** (bundled runtime, no connection args) resolves remote off at create and at resume. That includes resuming a session first created with `"on"`, and resume completes normally. With this launch, nothing remote happens before the disable call.
- **Runtime launched with `--remote`** (for example an operator `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` wrapper):
  - On 1.0.25, `remoteSession: "off"` kept create and resume off, and resume completed in about 12 s.
  - On 1.0.26 (and on 1.0.25 with the option omitted), create reports `remoteSteerable: true` and resume of a persisted session blocks inside the runtime for more than 180 s, before the post-resume `remote.disable()` can run.
  - With auth, remote export or steering could begin inside that resume. That would be a regression against the 1.0.25 per-session contract. Fresh local review rates it P2: "Enforce remote denial before resuming isolated sessions".
- **No supported per-session pre-create/resume deny exists in 1.0.26.** `--no-remote` did not override an explicit `"on"` on 1.0.25. I did not check whether it can override a `--remote` default.
- **Options for a maintainer decision:**
  1. Launch isolated and finalization clients through the public `RuntimeConnection.forStdio({ path: <packaged copilot-runtime>, args: [] })`, so they always start with remote off. This changes behavior for operators whose `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` or default-connection overrides currently also apply to isolated turns.
  2. Reject isolated turns on non-packaged runtime launches before create/resume. This also removes a currently supported operator configuration for isolated turns.
  3. Hold the bump until upstream provides a per-session pre-create/resume deny.
  4. With an explicitly authorized GitHub credential that has Copilot remote-session access, run the authenticated probe (synthetic history only) to check whether a `--remote` runtime exports or accepts steering before the deny.

Holds:
- Not taking 1.0.27/1.0.28: they are still inside the strict 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` at the audit time (2026-10-31T16:54Z, cutoff 2026-10-24T16:54Z).
- Settled finalization has no pre-send deadline of its own. A wedged deny is bounded by the run's abort signal, as the existing resume call already is.
- No change to ordinary (non-isolated) attempts.
- Each isolated turn makes one extra RPC round trip before its first send.

## Evidence

- Real-runtime integration (`harness.detached.integration.test.ts`, real SDK 1.0.26 runtime, synthetic provider endpoint):
  - Isolated completion and settled finalization record `["remote.disable", "provider", "disconnect"]`, and `session.start.remoteSteerable` is `false`.
  - When disable rejects, both turns fail with only `disconnect`, and no request reaches the provider.
  - When disable never settles, isolated completion fails at its 200 ms deadline and settled finalization fails on abort. Both disconnect, and no provider request is made.
  - **Red** with the deny wiring removed: `expected [ 'provider' ] to deeply equal [ 'remote.disable', 'provider' ]` and `promise resolved … instead of rejecting`. **Red** before the abort bound: the wedged-deny test times out (120 s). **Green** with the fix: 8/8 in the file.
- `catalog-lifetime.test.ts` (ClawSweeper P2 on `c8137c9`):
  - **Red** on the candidate: test timed out at 120 s with session-controller cleanup still pending. The fault peer answered `session.sendAndWait` with -32603, so the SDK never fell back to `session.send`.
  - **Green** after the peer repair: 1/1 in 1.7 s with every existing lifecycle assertion (session.error → detach → Code Mode cancellation → host closure), plus `expect(peer.unsupported).toEqual(["session.sendAndWait"])`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/copilot/harness.detached.integration.test.ts extensions/copilot/harness.test.ts extensions/copilot/src/attempt.test.ts`: 51/51 and 89/89 pass.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

title: feat(anthropic): migrate to Anthropic SDK 1.x
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Upgrade the Anthropic and Vertex SDKs to their eligible 1.x releases without silently changing authentication, request versions, or supported sampling behavior.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. API keys remain in `X-Api-Key`; OAuth/setup-token, Copilot, Foundry bearer and Mantle credentials remain bearer-authenticated; Vertex retains Google authentication. Custom temperature on older Claude models, streaming, tool calls, caching, thinking, refusals and error handling retain their existing contracts. Missing credentials still fail before network access.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `@anthropic-ai/sdk` **0.137.0 → 1.3.0** across root, AI package, Mantle and the existing shared pin; `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` **0.22.0 → 1.1.0**. The existing Vertex-specific Google auth 11.3.1 override follows the upgraded parent. No new override policy or release-age exception.
- SDK 1.x defaults to API version `2026-10-21` and bearer API keys. Use its documented custom-header support to preserve the existing `2023-06-01` API and `X-Api-Key` contract, matching OpenClaw's fetch transport. Credential layers now merge case-insensitively so caller overrides replace rather than duplicate credentials.
- Vertex SDK 1.x copies the version header into `anthropic_version` and strips the header. Explicitly retain `vertex-2023-10-16`; Mantle retains `2023-06-01`.
- SDK request types no longer contain temperature. The request builder explicitly models the supported pinned-version field, without a cast.

### Upstream research and holds

Audit instant: **2026-10-31T16:54:00Z**; inclusive cutoff: **2026-10-24T16:54:00Z**. These are the newest qualifying releases: SDK 1.3.0 published October 23 at 23:31:47.897Z; Vertex 1.1.0 at 13:13:08.611Z. Registry integrity matches the generated lock. Application lock audit: 1,749 package identities before/after, only these two replacements, no other dependency-edge changes or downgrades after normalizing the intended upgrade.

Authoritative sources: [SDK changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/sdk-v1.3.0/CHANGELOG.md), [Vertex changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/vertex-sdk-v1.1.0/packages/vertex-sdk/CHANGELOG.md), [API migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21).

Upstream highlights: 1.0 changes API version/authentication and role-specific message types; 1.1–1.3 add administrative endpoints and message threads, repair tool-runner behavior, and adjust endpoint query handling. Published tarball comparison confirms the SSE parser and error classes are unchanged; OpenClaw's `messages.create(...).asResponse()` / `Stream.rawEvents()` path remains supported.

**Hold: adopting API version `2026-10-21`.** It rejects sampling parameters even on models that previously supported them, with no equivalent replacement, and Bedrock supports it only for Claude 4.7+. Adopting it would remove supported behavior and needs a separate product decision. This PR upgrades the SDKs using their supported explicit-version/header APIs instead.

**Unchanged:** desktop runtime pruning still names SDK 0.132.1, already stale before this migration; its owner's re-audit is outside this change.

## Evidence

Candidate: `c21aae8f1971b0ef916237d204153995e9b36bef` (base `1df551011c87ddab2b6e6edb316682cd8a9de1f2`).

- Native `pnpm install --lockfile-only` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed. No hand-edited lockfile.
- Real-provider wire regressions: replacing only the provider with base code while retaining SDK 1.3 produced **4 failing / 1 passing** tests (version/auth contract failures); restoring the migration passed. The added missing-key regression also passes.
- Focused AI provider, transport/error parity, SSE and lazy-import tests: **85 passed**, plus the final missing-key regression (**86 unique**). Final affected fixture rerun: 6 wire tests and 11 Mantle tests passed.
- Complete Anthropic Vertex + Bedrock Mantle consumer tests: **100 passed across 11 files**. The Vertex wire test uses the real SDK and Google OAuth client with synthetic credentials, verifies endpoint rewriting, body version, bearer header and sampling. Mantle wire proof uses the real SDK.
- Caching, context-management, thinking binding and Anthropic transport siblings: **133 passed**; prompt-prefix stability: **14 passed**. **333 unique passing tests** total, not counting reruns twice.
- Core/extension production and package/extension test typechecks: passed, including final changed sources.
- AI package runtime + declaration build: passed. Both touched provider packages compile to JavaScript; package-boundary typechecks passed. An exploratory declaration emit that included the unchanged Vertex test-support file reported TS2883; the production runtime emit and package-boundary checks pass.
- Standalone oxlint and pinned-Bun analyzer: passed on touched core/extension files, with the repository's **CI parity comparison** enabled. Final oxfmt/Bun format parity, `git diff --check`, and test-line ratchet passed. No lint/test suppressions or new unsafe casts.
- Independent **autoreview / Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2**: full migration with complete relevant source context and final repair delta both **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Review did not execute tests; execution evidence is listed separately. Simplification removed cast-based test scaffolding in favor of real typed clients/streams.

Timing: final AI batch 52s wrapper wall / 36s Vitest; extension batch 678s / 626s (91% transform); sibling/prefix batches 764s wrapper. Individual new wire tests are subsecond; CI timing remains pending. Earlier overloaded-host attempts timed out during declaration preparation and test transformation, before assertions; completed recovery checks above replace those incomplete attempts without weakening gates.

**Remaining evidence limits:** no authenticated live Anthropic, Vertex or Mantle call and no real-model Gateway E2E was run—task environment exposes none of their credentials. Wire/consumer proofs use synthetic external I/O. Hosted CI and required repository/security review remain pending; no merge or auto-merge requested.

title: feat(voice-call): opt in to Twilio account call recording
body:
Supersedes #138861, thanks @DCastile.

Related: #138842

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who have already arranged consent cannot request a Twilio recording through the Voice Call plugin.

## User Impact

Set `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.twilio.record: true` to record every outbound call made with that configured Twilio account. Recording stays off when omitted or false and does not affect inbound calls.

**Consent warning:** recording starts at answer, without an automatic announcement or consent prompt. Obtain all required participant consent before calling; leave the setting off unless consent is arranged for every outbound call. Twilio owns audio storage, access, retention, deletion, and recording charges. OpenClaw does not download audio or retain recording links in call status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass Twilio's existing `Record=true` parameter through the existing call-creation owner for both notify and conversation calls. Account configuration keeps this operator-controlled. The replacement deliberately limits the original proposal to Twilio-hosted recording; callback persistence, retained recording URLs, and per-call tool inputs are outside this change.

Simplification removed duplicate status-callback URL initialization. Production TypeScript grows by six lines; the manifest grows by eight lines for the required opt-in schema and consent help. No equivalent dead code was found to remove safely. The generated config budget grows by one authorized setting (4912 → 4913). The separate 64-line test allocation covers the carrier-request regression and runtime/manifest schema acceptance and rejection.

## Evidence

- Red before: on baseline `c9405cd28d98d909548e383f101636e497e42e1c`, the new runtime regression failed because the serialized Twilio Calls request omitted `Record=true` (13.71 seconds including harness).
- Green after: 113 tests across `runtime.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, and `providers/twilio.test.ts`; 18.80 seconds Vitest duration, 27.04 seconds including harness. Covers both outbound modes, true/false/omitted settings, account isolation, and strict boolean validation in both schemas.
- Focused Voice Call package typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting, docs MDX validation, config-baseline regeneration, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview against the pinned baseline, covering all authored source/docs changes at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper CLI was unavailable; the hosted review route is requested when ready.
- Exact-head [CI run 41232950860](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41232950860) passed, as did Security Review and the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. CI workflow elapsed time was 476 seconds (including scheduling and shared setup).
- No live or paid Twilio call was made. Carrier I/O uses synthetic fixed responses; live recording, audio retrieval, and Twilio billing were not exercised.

title: feat(backup): add PostgreSQL local companion checkpoints
body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL installations need local restart checkpoints without exporting and later rolling back their live database rows.

## User Impact

`openclaw backup create --local-companion --verify` captures local files, fixed-local credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors. Verification and staging restore work while PostgreSQL is offline; activation reconnects to the same stores/namespaces and current rows. `restore --local-companion` also works through `--from` and refuses ordinary archives before extraction.

**This is not disaster recovery.** All portable families must select PostgreSQL. Local files roll back; PostgreSQL rows do not. Stop the Gateway before activation, keep the matching database available, and do not run original/restored installations concurrently with the same credentials. Legacy-audit migration inputs and saved PostgreSQL export directories are refused. Source-preserving capture keeps row IDs and may retain free-page bytes; it is not a secure-deletion export. Ordinary backups retain exports, online capture, sanitization, and fresh-namespace recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest profile/anchor inventory lets the existing verifier reject store/namespace mismatches, sidecars, and undeclared exports offline. Existing credential owners preserve fixed-local credentials and rebind them to the matching anchor. Generic acquisition remains owned by #189638, now landed on main as `f33e48e6720fe0b7b8ba2801096f532275cd08a5`. This PR targets main and contains only PR6 changes; the squashed dependency is not duplicated in its diff.

Adapted from [Galin's source commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/be31051c80993015e53a8ec4fc98e5e6c62e846e), with contributor credit retained. No externally-quiesced capture API, PostgreSQL import/rollback path, new production manager, or competing state owner is added.

## Evidence

### Main integration after PR4 landing

Merged pinned main `f33e48e6720fe0b7b8ba2801096f532275cd08a5` into the existing publication lineage after the stacked PR automatically retargeted to main. Resolved only six duplicate preservation-option hunks in two files, retaining the reviewed companion behavior. The main-targeted diff is exactly the 19 PR6 files, with no PR4-only test/support/allocation delta. `backup-create.ts` is byte-identical to the Diamond-reviewed version; snapshot planning retains main’s existing weak-owner-map allocation helper instead of the equivalent local helper.

Inspected relevant main authority changes: pairing wait-observation labels, worker-identity detection (not the operator client path), and an early refusal to issue a token for a missing paired device. Token verification/revocation and the companion credential-restore owner are unchanged. The original actual Gateway/PostgreSQL and stable-upgrade evidence remains bound to its recorded source, not relabeled as a new-head execution.

Affected gates: **66 tests passed in 7 files / 2 shards** (capture and ordinary controls, archive completeness, credential promotion, source aliases, pairing worker, weak-map contract); wrapper 133.64s, native preparation 71.00s. Core and infra test typechecks passed; targeted type-aware lint had zero warnings/errors; formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of committed `f0d71193a94d178b486623b929b9b2a63ae3f7f4` against pinned main completed source verification with the full PR6 delta and 18 frozen owner contracts: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It did not independently rerun tests or live PostgreSQL. New exact-head PR CI is required. No product scope or test-budget expansion was added for this integration.

### Integrated production CLI / Gateway / PostgreSQL

Built through the supported owner at exact source `399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e`; all build stamps/build-info matched. The subsequent merge `6818508e3090855e6478358b3897f62f323ac4e4` changes exactly two inherited test/support files and their allocation. At Diamond-reviewed head `9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a`, all production inputs were byte-identical to that tested runtime. The later main integration is qualified separately above; no fresh live PostgreSQL run on the new head is claimed. PostgreSQL 17.11 ran only in a disposable task-owned container/database; no live user state or Gateway was touched. No model inference is claimed for this authentication/RPC boundary.

1. Two distinct clients authenticated with native device tokens and exercised protected device-pairing RPCs. The built CLI captured `backup create --local-companion --verify` while the Gateway ran: one matching PostgreSQL anchor, zero export capsules.
2. **After capture**, the admitted administrator used `device.token.revoke` on the second client and changed a real PostgreSQL-backed label to `current-after-capture`.
3. Stopped/joined Gateway and PostgreSQL; confirmed PostgreSQL connection refusal. Built CLI offline verify and `restore --local-companion` returned `ok:true`. Promoted only the task-owned restored tree, with both services stopped. Read-only whole-row hashes/counts matched for two native identities, two tokens, and one native exec socket credential; the PostgreSQL anchor matched exactly.
4. Restarted the **same database** and a new Gateway on the restored tree. The captured allowed token authenticated and completed a protected rename. The captured token revoked after capture was rejected with `AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH` during connection authentication, **before its attempted protected rename**. An independently admitted read proved the forbidden label was never written. The post-capture label survived activation; the store anchor and every non-system namespace matched. No PostgreSQL import, new namespace, or rollback occurred during companion restore.
5. Stopped/joined all task services. The expected negative authentication message is evidence, not a failed test.

Sanitized terminal results; successful proof commands exited 0:

```text
BOTH_DISTINCT_DEVICE_TOKENS_AUTHORIZED_BEFORE_CAPTURE
CHECKPOINT_CREDENTIALS_ANCHOR_NAMESPACE_WITNESS_RECORDED
BUILT_CLI_COMPANION_CAPTURE_VERIFIED
POST_CAPTURE_REVOCATION_AND_CURRENT_ROW_COMMITTED
POSTGRES_CONFIRMED_OFFLINE
backup verify: ok=true profile=local-companion

OFFLINE_PROMOTION_EXACT_CREDENTIAL_ROWS_SOCKET_SECRET_SAME_ANCHOR_OK

```

### Latest-stable existing-data compatibility

Installed actual latest stable `v2026.10.9` with the maintained installer in a separate task prefix, isolating released dependencies from this checkout. Its real Gateway/public SDK produced a paired identity/token, protected rename, and nondefault timezone. On the **same state without resetting/reseeding**, current Doctor migrated shared schema 20 → 36 and the native credential store; original identity/token whole-row hashes matched. The original token authenticated to the exact candidate Gateway, read the retained setting, and completed a protected rename. After the supported SQLite → PostgreSQL port, that same released credential authenticated against PostgreSQL and read the retained setting.

```text

LATEST_STABLE_CREDENTIALS_SETTINGS_PROTECTED_EFFECT_AFTER_UPGRADE_OK

```

Stable had no PostgreSQL/native-client-store selection: this proves actual stable SQLite/native-credential upgrade, followed by a supported port **before** capture, not stable PostgreSQL migration. First Doctor invocation hit its outer command budget after migration; state was reconciled before idempotent resumption, which completed. No product watchdog was weakened.

### Automated proof and finding disposition

- Hosted tuple-inference P2 fixed with named fields, no casts/suppressions. Combined infra test typecheck passes.
- Actual baseline-failure logs classified: relocated errno cast replaced with existing `hasErrnoCode`; duplicated PRAGMA site replaced with existing read-only helper, preserving both guards. Generated assertion baseline pruned through its owner (one obsolete allowance removed); dialect sites decrease 3 → 1. Both ratchets pass. Test-line CI already passed: 328 governed lines plus two inventory lines explains the review's +330 surface. Unique allocation remains 328.
- **Post-PR4 integration run: 45 tests passed / 3 files**: source-preservation WAL/DELETE, companion capture, full archive completeness. Wrapper 170.02s, native preparation 106.55s, Vitest 39.19s; combined infra typecheck/diff checks pass.
- Repair run: **59 tests / 3 files passed**, wrapper 385.03s including 219.92s preparation; targeted type-aware lint zero warnings/errors, formatting/diff checks pass. Earlier unchanged-consumer evidence: 17 focused tests plus alias regression, covering credential promotion, remote/offline refusal, identity/namespace/profile/sidecar/export damage, ordinary WAL and mixed-engine controls. Synthetic anchors are not counted as real PostgreSQL proof.
- The inherited `resource.sock` failure is fixed by #189638 and integrated without duplicating the patch. Personally inspected exact test-only diff and owner evidence: 241 passing tests / 16 consumer groups, original-base red controls, real CLI round trip, clean independent review.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed the full feature with frozen credential owner context and fresh follow-up repair review; source verification completed and no actionable findings remained. The dependency's full review is also clean. No pending runtime proof was credited by those reviews; the actual evidence above now closes that gap.

### Remaining observations and accepted limits

Prior head `494226b9` CI's compact-small-18 failure is the now-integrated missing broker socket repair. Its separate copied-harness E2E failed with retryable `Model runtime changed before this turn started`; that fixture does not exercise backup/restore. No fix or baseline attribution is claimed for that observation; current-head CI must be inspected. Initial final-flow setup gave two clients identical silent-pairing metadata, so the owner correctly pruned the superseded client before revocation. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository-only cloud sessions need an explicit way to keep their original disk authoritative between turns instead of copying a workspace checkpoint to the Gateway after every result.

Depends on #189437, now landed as `4e4342b9f82de8e7159a73f280948f8def7ecb7f`. This PR now targets **main** and preserves the actual landed lifecycle, disk-I/O, immutable publication and Move prerequisites. Related: #188796.

## User Impact

Operators can opt in through `workspaceDurability: { mode: "retained-disk", computeWindowSeconds: 3600 }` on a supported dedicated managed-node profile. Omission and explicit mirrored mode are unchanged. Existing allocations and pending mirrored results retain their recorded policy; changing a profile does not convert them. The original disk is authoritative, so unpushed changes can be lost after confirmed disk loss rather than recovered from an older initialization checkpoint.

**Move to Gateway** captures current files and private Git history before retiring the original resource. Stop, archive/delete cleanup, other Move targets and implicit forks refuse instead of discarding or reconstructing the bound disk. Explicitly pinned historical snapshots remain usable. This PR does not allocate infrastructure, deploy or adopt a controller, or claim live cold-boot/model acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing allocation owner records capability- and receipt-gated policy before provisioning. Initial source/accepted-checkpoint hydration runs once; the native placement transaction publishes active placement and exact disk authority together.
- Ordinary result settlement preserves durable metadata, transcript/tool custody and claim release without per-turn mirror capture. Explicit input prepares the original retained runtime before claiming execution, including after a Gateway build change during an open compute window. Passive result recovery cannot open a new compute window.
- Fixed-lease/image reserves and legacy idle reclamation do not operate on retained allocations. Existing lifecycle, placement and result owners remain authoritative: no new schema, disk manager or parallel checkpoint-ref owner. The implicit-disk guard lives in the current canonical ref leaf; explicit accepted parents, immutable aliases and fork refusal retain their owning paths.
- Generated configuration changes are exactly the approved selector, mode and compute-window entries: core **2586 → 2589**; channel **4003** and plugin **4934** are unchanged. Canonical generation produced the files; removing exactly those three entries in memory reproduces landed core and combined hashes. Separate test allocations are **613 + 268 + 62 + 12**; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Current Candidate and Integration

Signed head **`3e8dbd332ee8375e0790ba0a99ac5c5ebc806e60`**, tree **`0cddb69e3a7dc976006ca02064efc0d7e30c6007`**. Final child delta: **50 files, +1557/−130**, including production **+464/−75** and tests/support **+995/−33**.

The initial native baseline `710b6ced` preserved original hosted `5a74d0a` and actual landed S8 `4e4342b9`, resolving 31 exact conflicts with bound blob evidence. Its signed ten-file fixup carried the qualified consumer/build-recovery fixtures, canonical checkpoint guard/history cutover and generated metadata. Both landed S8 fixture adapters and the readiness-poll owner were preserved.

Main then landed #190506, making three unused retention schemas private. The PR initially exposed an older base/merge projection and no CI attachment. One documented same-head close/reopen preserved the branch and source; a fresh main fetch identified the real single-file conflict. Native baseline **`3e8dbd33`** now preserves published **`9a0ac0da`** as first parent and actual main **`f82a3d34`** as second parent. It retains the three private declarations and S9’s used durability-schema export; no published-ancestry rewrite, unsigned override or signature exemption was used.

**49 of the 50 final child blobs exactly match reviewed `9a0ac0da`.** The remaining file differs only by those three main-owned export-keyword removals. The complete introduced path set and added/removed lines are unchanged against the new base. Removing S9’s unchanged seven-line selector from that module reproduces current main exactly; all five selector consumers remain. The previous independent review and unchanged behavioral proof are reused explicitly, not claimed as newly executed.

## Evidence

### Current integrated source

- On reviewed `9a0ac0da`, **37 tests across five files passed**, three routed shards, **148.20s runner / 148s wrapper**: 21 configured activation/disk-settlement/capture cases, eight caller-authority cases and eight configuration cases. The capture proof exercises both frozen-alias recovery and unchanged initialization files through real Git/HTTP/state owners, including implicit-read/fork refusal. Provider, pairing and external transport inputs remain synthetic.
- On that integrated source, core, Gateway-other, agents-sessions and config-CLI typechecks passed. CI-mode type-aware lint of **41 TypeScript files** reported **zero warnings/errors**; canonical formatting of **42 recognized files**, whitespace, generated-config check and two-file MDX checks passed. Static wrapper **89s**. Test-line ratchet: **6,381,639 ≤ 6,395,421**.
- Independent canonical **P0–P3 autoreview** covered all **50 paths plus 14 unchanged owner contexts** on `9a0ac0da` against actual S8 main: **one pass/attempt, 305,839 prompt bytes, scoped-clean, exit0, no actionable findings**. HEAD, index bytes/tree, complete diff and 62,467 tracked file hashes were unchanged. This is static supplied-evidence review, not independent tests or live-provider proof; other unchanged integration contracts not supplied are not claimed as reviewed.
- Current `3e8dbd33` conflict composition passed **all eight schema cases**, **509ms Vitest / 1.61s runner**, plus core/config-CLI typechecks, one-file CI type-aware lint, formatting, canonical config-baseline check, whitespace and ratchet **6,381,641 ≤ 6,395,441**. Total affected-check wrapper **24s**. No test/assertion/schema/runtime behavior changed, and no second full review or duplicate 37-case run is claimed.
- Exact-head [CI 41327789200, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41327789200) is **in progress** on `3e8dbd33`. GitHub now reports the PR mergeable; required current-head checks remain enforced. The previous `9a0ac0da` had no CI attachment and is not claimed as a passing run. No CI rerun or workflow dispatch was used.

### Prior proof retained at its original scope

- [Native run 41239118043](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41239118043) qualified exact hosted `5a74d0a`: **54 cases / six files, no skips or failures, 149.92s** under its unchanged 600-second envelope. All 43 bound hashes matched before/after, wrapper and command exited0, and the lease settled with independent no-host cleanup. This covers configured allocation, retained readiness/revocation, disk settlement, capture, Move and exact pending-result recovery—not live provider adoption.
- Signed `b3d904be` repaired three reproduced CI defects through execution-effect assertions, lexical routing and the exact test allocation. Its **18 cases passed in 241.20s**, with scoped types/lint/format/ratchet. Those repaired blobs are preserved. Joined qualification retained **739 focused passes** in their individual scopes; overlapping 72-case sequencing evidence is not added again. A historical broad stall and incomplete Goal wrapper remain nonpasses; seven affected Goal cases passed separately.
- Qualified `bfb7e35c` completed maintained runtime preparation in **248s**, then the three destination-authority cases in **86s** under the separately admitted 600s/180s envelopes. This is historical source-bound runtime proof, not a newly built current package. It was not replayed for cosmetic freshness.
- The original open-window negative control reached stale-build/runtime-refresh recovery but its fixture replaced the initiating error with a reconciliation sentinel; classifier rejection and wrapper1 remain recorded. Later fixed native proof is separate. Earlier interrupted local batches and failed CI remain failed, not converted into passes by a later run.

### Installed compatibility and remaining limits

The lifecycle prerequisite qualified exact `0b2a51db` installed latest-stable → shared-state39 preservation, actual decoder, repeated Doctor and cold serving-process requirements using recovered [run 41315369261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41315369261), followed by verified native cleanup and post-cleanup rehash. Settings, old NULL-retention rows, placement/pending rows and durable session identity were preserved. Its outer transport exit143/reporting BrokenPipe remain failed; independent post-volume inventory was unexecuted, with owned volume deletion established by the checked EXIT trap. The absent optional repository predecessor table remained unexercised. See #189346.

S9 adds no schema migration and does not reinterpret legacy policy. Current mirrored-default and configured activation cases supplement that dependency proof; **no exact-current-S9 installed activation package, live retained-provider cold boot, real-model flow or controller deployment is claimed**. Those final feature/deployment acceptance boundaries remain separate. The stale hosted review on `b87036a` predates the later authority and installed-prerequisite evidence; its lack of a concrete source finding is not treated as live acceptance.

title: feat(diagnostics-otel): migrate to OpenTelemetry 3
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Move the diagnostics exporter to the age-qualified OpenTelemetry SDK 3 without breaking existing propagation or collector settings.

## User Impact

Configured trace, metric, and log exports, sampling and span limits, resource attributes, and generation-private flush/shutdown behavior are retained. Deprecated `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=jaeger` still reads and writes `uber-trace-id` and `uberctx-*` baggage; no cross-service header migration is forced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adopt [SDK 3.0.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/releases/tag/v3.0.0), [experimental 0.300.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/releases/tag/experimental/v0.300.0), and [API 1.10.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/releases/tag/api/v1.10.0). Logs API moves into `@opentelemetry/api`; `sdk-trace` replaces `sdk-trace-base`. Follow the [3.x migration guide](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/blob/v3.0.0/doc/3.x/migration-guide.md).
- **There is no compatible published Jaeger propagator.** Upstream [removed it in #7077](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/pull/7077); its last 2.12.0 release requires API <1.10. W3C TraceContext is not wire-compatible. A plugin-owned adapter preserves the shipped default-header behavior, baggage encoding, and tracing suppression, with fixtures also executed against upstream 2.12.0.
- SDK 3 private tracer providers stop reading sampler/span-limit environment variables. Preserve that documented contract explicitly; leave exporter configuration and lifecycle ownership with their existing owners.
- SDK Node 0.300.0 becomes a plugin **test-only** dependency. Root and `packages/ai` get development API 1.9.1 pins so Mistral's optional SDK 2 peers remain compatible, without new peer overrides or changes to public peer contracts.

### Versions and holds

- Plugin API **1.9.1 → 1.10.0**; context/core/B3/resources/metrics **2.12.0 → 3.0.0**; logs SDK **0.223.0 → 3.0.0**; protobuf exporters and SDK Node **0.223.0 → 0.300.0**. Replace trace-base 2.12.0 with trace 3.0.0; remove standalone API Logs and Jaeger from the plugin.
- Audit **2026-10-31T16:54:00Z**, inclusive cutoff **2026-10-24T16:54:00Z**. All **25** introduced package identities were published October 20. The native multi-document lock audit found no new non-OTel identities, age violations, or downgraded edges of unchanged parents. Frozen installation passes; release-age exclusions are unchanged.
- Hold semantic conventions at **1.43.0**: 1.44.0 was published **2026-10-28T20:49:19.974Z**, after the cutoff.
- Retain Mistral's SDK 2 optional peers and the existing core 2.12.0 override, narrowed to major 2. Both Mistral 2.7.0 and age-qualified 3.2.0 require resources/trace-base ^2.9 and exporter ^0.220. Do not silently remove `@openclaw/ai` public peers. The inherited Mistral exporter ^0.220/0.223 peer warning remains; new OTel API peer violations are resolved.
- Related, not incorporated: [#184661](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184661) (generic cache usage attributes) and [#158145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158145) (content-capture stall). Their behavior-owning hunks are untouched; shared import/test edits may need normal integration.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension diagnostics-otel`: **13 files, 149 tests passed**, 8m12s wrapper wall / 446.52s Vitest. Covers real OTLP receivers, propagation, resources, sampling, TLS, external ownership, and restart flush/shutdown.
- Final SDK-peer isolation: four real-consumer files rerun, **48 passed**, 515.60s wrapper wall / 447.83s Vitest. These are a subset of the 149, not additional unique tests.
- Jaeger: five fixtures pass against both the local adapter and upstream 2.12.0; a temporary identity assertion verified the actual upstream class was substituted.
- **Passed:** native plugin npm-runtime build (3 entries); extension production/test and final root-E2E typechecks; changed-extension and final root-E2E standalone oxlint/pinned-Bun diagnostic parity (zero warnings/errors); oxfmt/Bun formatting parity; frozen install; test-line ratchet; `git diff --check`; docs links (16,194 checked, zero broken).
- Native **Node ESM** smoke passes SDK 3 public entrypoints, private tracer resource/force-flush/shutdown, stable Logs API, context manager, and all three OTLP exporter constructors without a bundler. This is not a Gateway/model-turn proof.
- **Current-head CI is green:** [run 41231060684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41231060684), **181 successful, 69 skipped, 1 neutral** check results; no failures or pending checks. `openclaw/ci-gate`, `security-fast`, and security-sensitive review report success for `2b57294febc1552db62d910dfa1bd0b77c09c891`. No CI rerun, merge, or auto-merge was requested. Test-specific CI seconds were not collected.
- **Installed-plugin Gateway E2E remains unproven.** Local setup refused before tests: `Cannot verify that test preparation is separate from managed Gateway artifacts`; no checkout artifacts were rebuilt. The configured Blacksmith Testbox fallback was stopped after more than ten minutes of local source-capsule preparation, still in `git update-index --refresh`, before remote allocation/run. No lease ID, Actions URL, or remote test result was produced. No provider fallback or guard bypass was used.
- A repeated extension-boundary declaration prerequisite hit its unchanged 300-second timeout before lint. Retain the earlier passing extension parity result; do not call this prerequisite failure a product failure or passing proof. Task-owned interrupted artifact claims were recovered only after checking their recorded processes and descendants had stopped.
- Independent **autoreview / Codex, P0–P2**: terminal **scoped-clean, no findings**, complete candidate against `1df551011c87ddab2b6e6edb316682cd8a9de1f2`, including final source verification. It checked upstream contracts statically, not test execution/publication dates. Published head has the same source tree as the reviewed implementation commit.
- Simplification retires plugin use of the old trace-base shim, API Logs, and Jaeger packages. Necessary adapter/configuration growth: **+171 net production TypeScript lines, +100 net test lines**. The separate 100-line regression allocation protects the removed dependency's wire contract; the shared test ceiling is unchanged.

title: fix(talk): settle retained persistence before shutdown deadline
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Talk persistence blocking Gateway shutdown until SIGKILL. The reported production stop on October 31, 2026 at 17:57 UTC stalled for 84 seconds.

## User Impact

Accepted Talk work gets time to finish, then cooperative cancellation and time to settle before the shutdown deadline. Completed writes remain committed, and uncertain deliveries keep their existing non-replay settlement rules. Work that ignores cancellation is reported as retained cleanup rather than silently discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained owner waited for all accepted work to become idle before aborting its signal. Work awaiting that abort therefore blocked its own cancellation. Talk now opts into two phases, each capped at 30 seconds and a quarter of the remaining process cleanup budget, leaving at least half the budget for subsequent teardown. Sandbox registry and worktree run-end owners retain their existing behavior.

Digest delivery is a concrete production candidate: accepted intents can queue behind channel sends, but their attempt signal previously did not observe the retained owner's cancellation. It now combines both signals and uses the existing delivery/receipt paths. The exact inner promise from the production incident remains unidentified. Escalation gives cooperative work a settlement opportunity that SIGKILL loses; a second timeout retains custody and reports incomplete cleanup.

## Evidence

- Base reproduction: the original Talk close probe remained un-aborted and pending after 85 seconds of virtual time. The compact committed regression fails on base for pending Talk drain, and the digest regression fails because owner abort is not propagated; both pass with the fix.
- The Talk close regression uses a four-second process cleanup budget and verifies graceful completion, abort-only settlement before the deadline, explicit retained failure for ignored abort, and an unconfigured retained scope continuing to wait without aborting.
- Focused validation uses one timeout-wrapped file per invocation with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and `--maxWorkers=1`. Unchanged persistence settlement tests cover committed writes, lost acknowledgments, uncertain delivery and marker retries. All **102 cases across nine files passed**: Talk close, digest owner, unchanged voice lifecycle/digest retry/digest source, sandbox authority, worktree run-end, shared async work, and the isolated Gateway voice shutdown integration. Changed-file command wall times: Talk close **50.23 s** (46 s initial compiler/import setup; test bodies below 1 s), digest owner **9.44 s**. The exact-head CI workflow completed in **1,479 seconds**; its inherited failures are detailed below.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Net test lines: **-3**; production growth is limited to escalation, its retained-error classification, and digest abort wiring. Overlapping retry/expiry test setup was folded while preserving its assertions.
- CI repair: the first run exposed a Talk-to-shutdown import cycle and missing budget modules in the native wrapper inventory. Timeout recognition now belongs to the existing shutdown classifier; the wrapper inventory includes both budget leaves. The import-cycle guard reports **zero cycles**; **45 repair cases across four files passed**, including all **35 extracted wrapper/import cases**. The repaired Talk close command took **42.63 s**, including compiler preparation; the wrapper proof took **36.82 s** because it checks extracted dependency contexts. The final exact-head run completed, with only the independently attributed UI baseline failures below.
- Fresh autoreview **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, against base `a31d9039928ca8fc9055e25e940fd0a4136c51b4` and the full staged candidate committed at `7c841c6cd33504cb6bb74bd41f24fdccd616a1bd`. No actionable findings.

- Exact-head [CI run 41231792441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41231792441) retains two inherited UI failures. The retained-diff loading assertion matches [scheduled main job 124620417465](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41229387066/job/124620417465), and the healthy cloud-disk badge assertion matches [main job 124620417504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41229387066/job/124620417504), with identical cases, lines, and expected/actual values. Shard numbers differ between runs. The complete UI tree is identical between the tested merge and its protected-main parent; both tests and mock fixtures also match scheduled main source. All **98 jobs are terminal**; all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and `security-fast` passed. These two UI jobs and their aggregate gate remain failed. Native inherited-failure admission preserves that red verdict and must verify all other checks, security, review, and live writer authority.

Requested by @steipete

title: fix(update): stale recovery captures have no cleanup path
body:
Fixes #189642

## What Problem This Solves

Old recovery and Doctor captures can occupy gigabytes while update status calls them ambiguous or incomplete and points back to itself, without a usable retirement command.

## User Impact

Status and cleanup now use one capture inventory. Status gives an exact cleanup preview command for historical captures; confirmed cleanup can retire superseded incomplete sets through the existing `--include-unmanifested <path>` option. Sealed orphans keep their existing explicit retirement route, and Doctor keeps its documented retention rule, including the newest sealed copy.

Incomplete sets need a later successful update with recorded Gateway readiness and no pending recovery before the new explicit route is offered. Unsealed run-owned copies also require verified supersession. Running updates, unresolved failed sealed originals, unreadable history, and unverified successors remain protected. Real cleanup still requires the Gateway to be stopped and confirmation (or `--yes`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The released inventory gap is already partly fixed on main. The remaining split was status's separate capture discovery/classification and cleanup's exclusion of historical incomplete directories. Reuse the capture inventory and existing retirement safeguards instead of introducing a pruning command or deletion owner. Status skips payload byte counting and shares one ledger snapshot with recovery diagnostics.

Merged #189249 removes fresh producer-owned failed Doctor attempts; it deliberately does not retire historical captures. This PR covers that remaining path. Open #188868 owns runtime/database-snapshot custody and #169515 owns secondary Git-cleanup diagnostics; neither duplicates this fix.

## Evidence

- Landing verification: incomplete standalone `doctor-*` sets were explicitly Doctor-owned before this PR ([base source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/110d1f0dc699df6df51333bcf34ae779bd222806/src/commands/update-capture-cleanup.ts#L190)). Current eligibility requires `latestVerifiedStartedAt > directory.mtimeMs` and no pending recovery ([source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5/src/commands/update-capture-cleanup.ts#L212)). Doctor acquires exclusive state-maintenance ownership before its original-capture hook ([admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5/src/commands/doctor-maintenance-state.ts#L243)); cleanup acquires that same owner before selection/removal ([retirement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-retirement.ts#L205), [lock](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5/src/commands/doctor-sqlite-maintenance-lock.ts#L168)). Active Doctor custody therefore blocks removal even for an old-looking partial capture; no additional guard or head change was needed.
- Landing verification reran the capture-cleanup, explicit-selection, and Doctor-retention suites: **39 passed**, **60.94 seconds wall**. Fresh shared **Codex autoreview P0–P2**, complete range `110d1f0dc699df6df51333bcf34ae779bd222806..d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5`, is **scoped-clean**, zero findings, with Doctor admission/lock/retirement source context. Static review only; no additional live upgrade claim. Exact-head CI run 41233606965, attempt 1, remains successful.

- Final exact-head [CI run 41233606965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41233606965) is **green** for `d1d10d8380fba6e0cae502a052639e71edd3cbf5`, including all PostgreSQL conformance shards.
- Regression is RED on the original inventory owner: the historical incomplete set remains `unmanifested-update-capture` despite a verified successor. Fixed-tree regression uses real ledger records and cleanup handlers to prove read-only preview, actual removal, and preservation with unverified success, pending recovery, and the newest Doctor original.
- Focused capture/status/explicit-selection suites: **60 passed**, 55.02 seconds wall. Final source: **36 passed** across capture/status/Doctor-retention files, 60.02 seconds wall (including worker preparation). The earlier explicit-selection suite contributes 28 additional tests with unchanged inputs.
- Targeted production/test types, lint, formatting and diff checks pass. A broader automatic-cleanup consumer run reached its 120-second bound after nine passing tests; the command was interrupted and is not claimed green. Remaining consumer coverage is left to PR CI.
- CI caught an incomplete Doctor history mock and an obsolete closed-mock debt entry. Completed the conservative fixture; the repository owner pruned exactly one obsolete entry. Four focused Doctor recovery tests, targeted types/lint/format and the mock-debt check pass. No production change was needed.
- The unchanged fresh-preview refusal tests caught missing sealed metadata on the new warning shape. Restored `runId` and `manifestPath` for sealed warning entries; the same two cases are red before and green after, with seven status checks also passing (60.97 seconds wrapper wall). Incomplete sets expose no sealed locator. Targeted types/lint/format pass; the repair received a clean Codex P0–P2 review.
- Addressed the other hosted P2: releasable warning entries no longer compete with a genuine failed baseline. The superseded case is red before the fix; all 27 status cases pass after it (44.01 seconds wrapper), including an unresolved-orphan negative control. This preserves #188021's recovery-guidance intent.
- Fresh independent shared **Codex autoreview, P0–P2**: primary candidate against `110d1f0dc699`, fixture repair against `a462ae796f6f`, sealed-metadata repair against `5a49d18c74c8`, and resolved-warning repair against `eb86d7d05eb0` are all **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Context included the relevant owners and consumers. The reviewers did not execute tests or live upgrades.
- `pr-simplify`: removed status's separate directory discovery. Reused existing per-path selection, live-store/reference checks, confirmation and final-effect ownership checks. No new store, public option, protocol or dependency. Production +89 lines; regression +150 lines, exactly allocated for this behavioral boundary and its preservation controls.
- No full build, live Gateway change, installed stable-to-candidate upgrade, or physical Windows multi-GB cleanup under this focused-only task. CI supplies broad proof; those platform/upgrade limits remain explicit.
