title: feat(plugins): let policy hooks list authorized tool names
body:
Supersedes #137880, thanks @Colton-Harris.
Related: #137872

## What Problem This Solves

Policy-bound prompt hooks can test a known tool name but cannot discover the finalized tools available to their turn, forcing generic policy plugins to maintain a duplicate catalog.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can select tool-specific prompt guidance from the current turn's authorized names. The optional `toolAuthority.list()` method supports feature detection on older hosts; existing plugins need no changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing canonical snapshot through its current authority owner. Enumeration returns frozen, sorted, deduplicated names only and uses the same host/dispatch checks as `allows()`. This accepts the narrow SDK addition proposed in #137880 without a new factory, catalog, export subpath, or configuration option.

### Security review

- The embedded runner supplies names only after applying prompt-hook restrictions; CLI and harness callers likewise supply their finalized surface. Enumeration reads that same snapshot, never the registry, configuration, or another turn's tools.
- No descriptions, schemas, parameters, handles, or execution capability are exposed. Frozen strings already returned are data, not continuing authorization.
- Every call revalidates the existing host and dispatch lifetime. This preserves the current authority contract; the separate `hookInvocation` capability still owns each handler's result lifetime.
- Ordinary hooks do not receive this capability. Tests cover excluded tools, empty and differing turn surfaces, immutability, host revocation, and dispatch completion after a timeout.
- This is additive and source-compatible: the method is optional, and existing `allows()` consumers remain unchanged. The SDK impact policy requires ecosystem inventories for removals and incompatible changes; neither applies here.

## Evidence

- On main `f2e870edfcaecb7721821eed4b949892522e1cf9`, the focused hook suite failed 3 regressions because enumeration was absent; 43 existing tests passed (46.72 seconds).
- With the fix, `pnpm test src/plugins/hooks.phase-hooks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 46 tests (38.66 seconds including cold compilation; wrapper wall time 41.25 seconds). The scope regression uses the real embedded tool filter and production hook runner with independent expected names.
- Targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and core production plus plugin/platform test typechecking passed. Typechecking ran in a rootless container capped at 4 CPUs and 8 GiB; broad runtime proof belongs to PR CI.
- Local autoreview of the full candidate against `f2e870edfcaecb7721821eed4b949892522e1cf9`, including unchanged authority/caller context, completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The committed candidate is `a408c1ed61fe4c9d61cd65e1fec65da631aab698`.
- Simplification kept the implementation inline and avoided the proposed extraction. Production delta is +6 lines (+4 runtime, +2 type); these implement the method and its public contract, with no safe dead-code offset in this path. Tests add 75 lines with a dedicated allocation; docs add 8 lines.
- Contributor code was read only through GitHub and was never checked out or executed. No fresh live Gateway/model run was performed; no Team deployment or live-state change was made.

Contributor credit: Co-authored-by: Colton Harris <colton@opspot.ai>.

title: fix(update): restore Windows Gateway after verification failure
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Windows update can leave its Gateway stopped after post-update verification fails, including a same-version npm reinstall. Related: #189620.

## User Impact

The updater re-enables its owned Scheduled Task and retains recovery until final Gateway readiness is verified. Recorded data risks still block startup. The running updater must contain this fix; installing a newer candidate does not replace an older driver already running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Autostart enablement was incorrectly counted as a Gateway start, suppressing the final restart. Failure reporting could also settle the Windows task recovery handle before final recovery. The existing finalizer now retains the handle through readiness, and the recovery owner restores the suspended task under the existing service-ownership guard before activation. The rollback sibling uses the same distinction. Final task-settlement errors retain the initiating update failure and add the native recovery error.

No new recovery owner or state is introduced. Two same-version failure cases exercise the real finalizer, recovery owner, task suspension, and readiness verification with synthetic native I/O. Their 26 net test lines plus one corrected activation-fixture line have a dedicated 27-line allocation. Production growth is 19 net lines; regression growth is 27 net lines. No CHANGELOG changes.

## Evidence

- Both same-version regression cases fail on base `d224ff6b39b8`. The final recovery file passes all 28 tests: 32.95 s Vitest / 35.10 s wrapper; the new cases take 481 ms and 455 ms. Exact-head CI passes the same 28 tests in 15.79 s Vitest / 17.22 s wrapper. Existing data-risk controls still refuse startup.
- The final post-update file passes all 94 tests: 92.29 s Vitest / 129.65 s wrapper including compiler preparation; exact-head CI passes all 94 in 61.47 s Vitest / 63.40 s wrapper. These existing composed files exercise real finalization and state recovery; the added coverage does not create another full-product boot.
- [Original CI run 41229659564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41229659564), head `b18fb2384659`, exposed PR-caused failures in `checks-node-changed-1` and `checks-node-changed-4`. The Windows lifecycle failure reproduced locally: final task-disable failure replaced `restart-unhealthy` with `post-update-failed`. The finalizer now routes settlement rejection through the existing failure handler. Both ordering failures came from a restart mock that did not report actual activation; the corrected fixture requires Doctor → restore → activation attempt → start. No inherited-failure exception is claimed for these failures.
- The repaired lifecycle case and its enable-failure/success siblings pass locally. The full local lifecycle run reached its 180 s outer command budget during later tests. Exact-head CI passes the complete file: 25/25, 115.77 s Vitest / 117.87 s wrapper.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview, GPT-6.1 Sol / medium, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed the complete final staged candidate against `d224ff6b39b8`, source tree `44f98074bc5b5e7c386cfcad25fd95cec3487b5f`, committed as `9f6c22bf100e`, with the service, recovery, native command, Windows task, and terminal owners supplied as context.
- Format, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet pass (6,347,935 lines / 6,372,728 ceiling). Local typecheck/lint are blocked by the worktree's pre-existing externally linked dependencies; that shared installation was preserved. [Exact-head CI 41231222201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41231222201) passes final typecheck/lint and broad proof on `9f6c22bf100e` (including all three PostgreSQL conformance lanes). No inherited-CI exception is used.
- The bounded native Windows attempt did not produce a runnable test environment. AWS Crabbox `cbx_0333da1894a0` reached SSH in 4m 5s, but its image had unsupported Node 24.19 and no dependencies; runner hydration lacked registration permission. Supported Node 24.22.1 and the exact runtime/regression/allocation source blobs were verified in the guest, then [frozen dependency installation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_feb780c2c10309f3c3e125453c0e524e) lost remote workspace ownership renewal. Neither the native regression nor native allocation check reached execution. The lease is confirmed released. **The regression through real finalization is the accepted proof for this landing; native Windows and latest-stable upgrades remain unverified.** The report's initiating verification/restart errors remain redacted, so this does not claim to diagnose those errors or close #189620.
- Additional local service-reassignment controls failed during fixture setup: four cases expected `before.stopped: true` but received `false` at `update-command-service-recovery.test-support.ts:401`, before invoking the changed recovery path. One bounded diagnostic reproduced that precondition failure; its temporary assertion was restored. The pre-stop owner and fixtures are unchanged by this PR. The host/filter refusal remains unresolved, and these four cases are **not** counted as authority proof. The passing 10-case Windows owner suite and source revalidation inspection are the available evidence.

Its CI attribution question is resolved above. Existing Windows authority controls pass all 10 tests, including lost authority before restore and compensation. The retained handle still runs service identity/fingerprint revalidation and executor checks at native mutation; the repair adds no alternate authority or new state. Additional native/upgrade proof remains the explicit gap above, rather than a new landing requirement.

title: fix(ui): mobile sheet goes blank while it slides out after closing
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski. Follow-up to #188162.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0fb3ffc-670f-446e-a5e0-ab2c33ba9de8)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on phones, closing the Panels/Details sheet while a tool (Files, Browser…) or a Details page is open blanks the sheet before it slides away, so an empty grey panel animates off screen.

## User Impact

The sheet now slides out with the content it was showing, like an iOS sheet. Closing still takes effect immediately for focus, screen readers and the conversation layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

#188162 made the sheet itself animate out, but the pane owner flipped every content consumer to "closed" at the same instant, so panels and Details pages hid on the first frame of the exit. The pane owner (`ChatPaneSidePanels`) now has a short `exiting` state:

- `close()` still sets `open = false` at once, so the sheet becomes `hidden`/`inert`, focus returns, and the conversation reclaims its space immediately.
- While the sheet slides out, the presented layout and Details/page content keep treating it as shown (`open || exiting`), so the last panel or page stays painted.
- After the exit (`--motion-sheet-duration`, including a gesture release's own spring), the owner finishes the close: content hides, a transient menu destination returns to its saved destination, sheet height resets, and companion observer visibility syncs. Reopening mid-exit cancels the pending close; reduced motion and session changes skip it.

Reopening exposed a related bug on `main`: the hidden sheet's `visibility` transition started from `hidden` when it reopened, so Side chat's opening focus was refused for that frame (a reopen after the sheet had fully closed never focused Side chat; main's E2E only passed because it reopened mid-exit). The sheet is now visible at once on open and stays visible until its exit ends (`visibility 0s` on open, the exit duration on close). Reopening mid-exit also counts as a new Side chat opening.

This replaces the launcher-only CSS rule from #188162 (−8 lines of CSS). Minified builds serialize the token as `.441s`, so the duration parser accepts both `s` and `ms`.

## Evidence

Files open, 60 ms into closing (animations slowed to 25% for the capture), 390×844 Chromium:

Before: the sheet is already empty while it slides away.

![Before: the closing sheet is empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68b3b5a7-9f47-413e-998a-66ce18d18593)

After: the Files panel slides out with the sheet.

![After: the Files panel stays in the closing sheet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee4d1869-d73a-4c30-9a85-cfd0181142ac)


- New E2E case in `mobile-sheet-motion.e2e.test.ts`: the Files panel and a Details › Outputs page stay visible 60 ms into the exit and are hidden after it; reopening mid-exit keeps the sheet open with its page. It fails on `main`.
- Existing motion cases (spring present/dismiss with the launcher retained, flick detents, slow placements, header drag, push/pop, Filter & sort swipe, reduced motion) pass.
- `chat-session-companion-focus` (15/15, including the 390 px reopen case that failed on the first CI run) and `mobile-sheet-motion` (8/8) pass together; `boot-module-boundaries` › cloud target, which failed once in CI, passes locally and is unrelated.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base`: total CSS gzip 309,345 → 309,329 B (−16 B), raw −87 B.
- `chat-mobile-environment` and `chat-panel-layout` E2E suites pass (14/14 together with the motion suite); a wider 15-suite mobile/panel batch passed apart from those two, which had timed out under host load and passed on rerun.
- Unit: `chat-pane-sidebar-view`, `chat-pane-panel-toolbar`, `chat-pane-mobile-composition`, `chat-details-mobile-content` (17/17).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`.

title: fix(doctor): migrate auth profiles on PostgreSQL stores
body:
Related: #189587

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` rejects every auth-profile migration on PostgreSQL stores with “Auth profile backup differs from the planned source,” which can prevent a pre-start Doctor from allowing the Gateway to start.

## User Impact

User impact: PostgreSQL installations can migrate legacy auth profiles after saving a verified backup containing the original credentials and rotation state. SQLite keeps its existing snapshot verification. The candidate Doctor contains the repair; the installed updater needs no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup owner selects the physical store backend. PostgreSQL uses the existing exact export, and Doctor validates the captured portable database rather than the local anchor. Existing identity and source-row checks still run before rewriting. A changed source refuses migration and preserves the credentials.

This replaces #189587 with the backend decision in the backup owner. Thanks to @ceckert for the report, initial fix, and PostgreSQL reproduction. Chris Eckert and steipete retain co-author credit.

## Evidence

- Main source at `712ff412ee77` still takes the SQLite-only backup path. History and open-PR searches found no existing fix.
- 76 focused SQLite tests passed across auth alias migration, alias preservation, and Doctor auth-profile migration (114.50 seconds including two Vitest shards).
- Core and Doctor-test typechecks, focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `pnpm build` passed (301.1 seconds).
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2, against base `712ff412ee77` and the final local source snapshot: complete, no actionable findings. Full Doctor, export/backup owner, auth reader, and SQLite regression context supplied. Source review only.
- The new PostgreSQL regressions verify the matched exact backup and its original credential rows, then verify canonical migration. A changed-source case preserves the rotated credential and refuses migration. Both mixed-engine owner arrangements are covered and explicitly registered in canonical conformance CI.
- The first CI run exposed a fixture config omission in the four new PostgreSQL cases ([failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41228979593/job/124619300676)). The fixture now passes the real database configuration, matching the production Doctor caller; backup verification is unchanged. Doctor-test typecheck and an independent Codex P0–P2 review of this correction passed.
- PostgreSQL execution is CI-only here. The focused Blacksmith Testbox allocation queued and was stopped before its payload ran. Baseline-red execution and a published-stable-to-candidate CLI upgrade have not been obtained.

- Corrected head `5bbaab011190`: all four PostgreSQL regressions passed in [shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41230577132/job/124624140309), with both actual backup verification and credential-preserving refusal assertions executed. File time: 25.14 seconds; case times: 2.13–2.63 seconds. All three PostgreSQL shards, the aggregate gate, and the full [fresh CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41230577132) passed on exact head `5bbaab011190e376e0526490022d3cc12df2e583`.

Simplification: the replacement needs no Doctor backend adapter or extra whole-store fingerprint scans. Production delta is +38 lines; the 135-line regression allocation protects credential migration and refusal across the two database owners. No schema, retention, dependency, or permission changes; no CHANGELOG edits.

title: feat(backup): preserve source artifacts for internal captures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal filesystem captures need to read SQLite state without changing the source WAL index or recovering rollback journals in place.

## User Impact

No new CLI flags or changes to ordinary backups. This adds the internal `createBackupArchive({ preserveSourceArtifacts: true, ... })` mode for isolated migration/checkpoint capture processes. Default backup sanitization and compaction, archive format, and PostgreSQL `online: true` capture remain unchanged.

The internal mode preserves row IDs by skipping compaction, so free-page bytes can remain in its archive. It still applies the existing row-level sanitizers and is not a secure-deletion export.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup owner applies the existing artifact-preserving read scope during planning as well as private SQLite acquisition. Legacy audit reconciliation is refused before it can take a source write lease. Acquisition uses verified private images and preserves row IDs. No companion profile, anchor inventory, CLI, or quiescence API is included.

The hosted review's P2 fixture finding is repaired at the shared backup scratch owner: drain fixture state, retire idle state readers and the retained native broker, then remove the case directory. Failed custody settlement retains the directory. The regression starts cold with a short fixture prefix so a long-socket-path fallback cannot mask the deleted-socket failure. Production behavior is unchanged by this repair.

Extracted and adapted from [galiniliev's source commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/be31051c80993015e53a8ec4fc98e5e6c62e846e), with contributor credit retained.

## Evidence

### Changed preserving mode through the production CLI consumer

This is additional evidence for the **changed mode**, distinct from the ordinary CLI compatibility run below. The existing stacked consumer in [PR #189685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189685) executed its built CLI while a disposable Gateway and PostgreSQL 17.11 were running:

```text
node dist/index.js --profile <isolated-profile> backup create
  --local-companion --verify --no-include-workspace
  --output <owned-checkpoint.tar.gz> --json
exit: 0
localCompanion: true
verified: true
```

The original native command and terminal receipt, successful build log, clean build stamps, capture output, witness implementation and retained archive were independently inspected—not inferred from PR6's rating. Runtime source was `399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e`; both build stamps and build-info identify it. The [comparison to integrated consumer head `9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e...9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a) changes only three test/support/allocation files, so the tested production inputs remain identical.

The call chain was personally checked: [CLI option/action](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a/src/cli/program/register.backup.ts#L25-L48) → unchanged `backupCreateCommand` option forwarding → [archive owner selecting `preserveSourceArtifacts: true`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a/src/infra/backup-create.ts#L286-L298) → the preserving planning scope and private SQLite snapshot acquisition. The private-acquisition/row-ID block is byte-identical to this PR, as are `sqlite-snapshot.ts`, `sqlite-readonly-location.ts`, `sqlite-snapshot-staging-owner.ts`, `artifact-preserving-state-reads.ts`, `commands/backup.ts`, and the lockfile. The two archive modules as a whole are **not** claimed identical: PR6 adds profile/anchor inventory and its own destination policy.

The retained 953,531-byte archive has SHA-256 `7f149851302acccaeef09415c98c367b534135db960240dd81dcb7e3929f259c`. Its unique manifest reports `local-companion`, one PostgreSQL anchor and zero export capsules; it contains both the shared-anchor and fixed-local credential SQLite images. A separate read-only audit extracted private copies and matched whole-row hashes/counts against the original capture-time witness: **2 device identities, 2 device tokens and 1 native exec socket credential**, with the same anchor store/engine/namespace. No credential values are published. Retained final-effect receipts additionally show offline verify/restore, a successful allowed protected RPC after activation, and rejection before effect of a client revoked after capture.

This qualifies actual production-consumer selection/acquisition and a usable archive. PR6's credential-retention policy is not attributed to PR4, which retains its existing sanitizers. The exact-base WAL/DELETE fingerprint, row-ID and sanitization oracles below remain the detailed preservation proof; this retained consumer run is not mislabeled as a new before/after WAL measurement. No new public API or service rerun was introduced for this evidence audit.

### Original-base, invariant and compatibility proof

- **Exact original-base red:** Ran the final regression against unchanged production code at `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7` in a separate checkout, copying only the regression and corrected fixture helper. title: fix(anthropic): report automatic Claude CLI compaction
body:
Supersedes #138010, thanks @zijunl.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing compaction completion reports when Claude Code automatically compacts a CLI-backed conversation.

## User Impact

OpenClaw's existing compaction event consumers can observe successful automatic Claude compaction. Manual compaction keeps its existing status lifecycle. Claude Code still owns its saved history; this mapping does not create a durable OpenClaw summary or independently repair transcript replay/accounting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic mapper on main drops `system/compact_boundary` records before inspecting them. Map only the documented streamed `compact_metadata.trigger: "auto"` boundary to the existing successful completion event. Manual boundaries remain excluded to avoid duplicate completions. The [Anthropic event contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkcompactboundarymessage) defines this record.

The replacement keeps the fix in the Anthropic producer, removes its redundant null-return branch, and reuses one completion projection. title: fix(ui): image viewer arrows stop at message boundaries within a turn
body:
Related: #152027, #153198, #154051

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the image viewer, Left/Right arrows, the previous/next buttons and swipes stop at the edge of the opened message, even when the same assistant turn shows more images in its other messages. In replies that interleave text and images, the arrow order could also disagree with the order the tiles appear.

## User Impact

User impact: opening any image in an assistant turn lets you step through every image in that turn, in transcript order. Navigation still stops at the turn boundary (the next user message, a divider or a forwarded session), the same boundary the expanded video player already uses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Images were scoped to the opened message's image list, while expanded videos already followed the transcript's turn projection. Images and videos now share that projection (the video-only module is renamed) and one membership helper. Each message contributes its images in rendered order: in-order replies place unpositioned transcript images above the body, so those come first. Sibling images load with their own message id, matching the cache scope of their tiles. Membership is built only when the viewer opens; the transcript render path is unchanged.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

title: fix: long fenced replies can stall the Gateway after a leaked tool call
body:
Related: #186601, #181696; #186605 addresses the separate assistant-visible sanitizer owner.

## What Problem This Solves

A long fenced reply after a leaked plain-text tool call can block the Gateway while every cumulative partial snapshot reparses accumulated Markdown. This targets the snapshot projection attributed in the R11 freeze, rather than the separate assistant-visible text sanitizers.

## User Impact

Settled tool-call snapshots retain literal fenced examples without repeatedly parsing the entire reply. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing two-entry snapshot reuse discarded its settled ranges whenever an appended chunk contained Markdown delimiters. Carry the existing fence scan with each reuse anchor and inspect only appended candidates. An unfinished prose tail preserves earlier proven fence verdicts; candidates in the unresolved tail still use canonical scrubbing. Content-block changes, uncertain ownership, and custom resolvers retain their existing invalidation rules.

This removes repeated snapshot-parser work without adding a parser or another cache owner. Production delta: +32 lines; test delta: 0 lines. The existing loose call-count test is replaced with a byte-budget regression and exact comparison of every projected snapshot.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

**Maintainer product/SDK and security decision requested:** please assess the optional public shape, initial Control UI-only scope, and rejection once multiple people steer a turn. Reuse the private profile, reply snapshot, participant, admitted-run and plugin-lifetime owners. Match the exact agent/session/run and host-issued operator authority. Recheck identity and invocation in the final synchronous effect admission after awaits; resource/owner policy remains independent. Preserve synthetic-ingress rejection and original-client liveness without restoring ingress execution context around plugins. Steerers never replace the requester; ambiguous turns fail closed. No new store, config, protocol or OAuth mapping. Already-dispatched work cannot be retracted.

Pinned main `a5b6c876b9c5d806a7808a970333d3aba609b8a6` retains the gap. Bounded searches and patch comparisons found no duplicate factory fix:

### New protected-effect runtime qualification

The current E2E launches the **built Gateway through its real CLI as a separate owned process**. Public `system.info.pid` must equal the child PID and differ from the test process. A real TLS proxy forwards WebSocket traffic to the Gateway; trusted-proxy authentication/device admission remain separate from profile roles. | --- | --- |
| Personal administrator | Three model requests drive read → consume result/draft → completion. One real HTTP read and one draft POST. Service persists `.eml` with `X-Unsent: 1` and verified profile ID; sender absent, independent owner true. |

| Second participant during preparation | Second human `chat.send` steers a shared session. Test-plugin RPC probes the original captured guard and confirms the existing several-participants error without reading process-private maps. Final guard refuses: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |

title: fix(chat): keep preparation failures visible in chat history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Control UI/Team chat turn that fails during preparation, before the agent run starts, shows no reply and leaves nothing in chat history. Examples are sandbox setup failing, the state lease being lost, or preflight compaction being aborted.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions
- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ce8a3e10-2215-49f3-aaec-9ba55c3a7b27)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/91df71ac-780f-4e4a-81b9-e7e64a4507f2)

## User Impact

User impact: when a turn fails during preparation, chat history now keeps a failure notice that says what went wrong and what to do next (for example retry, `/compact` or `/new`), and the session is marked as failed. A client that reloads, reconnects or missed the live event sees that notice instead of an unanswered message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply preparation (memory flush, preflight compaction, sandbox setup) returns a failure payload instead of starting the agent runtime. The Gateway only broadcast that payload as a live chat error. No runtime lifecycle existed for the run, so nothing recorded its terminal state and history kept only the user message. In the observed incident the turn went through the queued follow-up path. There, the rejected payload reached the Gateway only as a `failed` batch completion carrying a plain error string.

The chat.send dispatch-error lifecycle owns failures that happen before the runtime starts. It now records them as the run's terminal lifecycle error:

- **Direct path:** a returned error payload from an unstarted run is persisted immediately through the existing `allowUnstartedFailure` writer gate.
- **Queued path:** a rejected follow-up carries its user-facing notice on the failed completion, and turn adoption records it through the same owner.

The returned notice is stored as the run's failure notice in history, so the persisted copy matches what the live client saw. For runs that did start, the runtime lifecycle remains the only terminal writer.

<details><summary>Follow-up (not changed here)</summary>

Preflight compaction and the pre-run memory flush run inside the same turn preparation that provisions the sandbox workspace, so a sandbox or lease failure can surface as `preflight compaction failed: Aborted`. Decoupling compaction from sandbox provisioning is a design change with its own tradeoffs, and this incident alone does not justify it. This PR makes the failure visible; the decoupling is left as a separate follow-up.

</details>

## Evidence

- New real-WebSocket regression `src/gateway/server.chat-preparation-failure.test.ts`. It runs against a real Gateway with the preflight-compaction failure payload, covers both the **direct** and **queued follow-up** paths, then reads `chat.history` from a fresh connection.
  - Base: the direct case fails; history ends with the user message and has no failure entry.
  - This branch: both cases pass. History ends with the `run-failed-before-reply` notice "This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it. Try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session.", and the session row is `failed` with the run id.
- End-to-end check before the rebase, using a scratch Gateway and a fake model provider. Preflight compaction was forced to fail on the real reply path, which routes the turn through the queued follow-up runner. On base, `chat.history` ended with the user message; on this branch it ended with the failure notice above.
- After rebasing onto current `main`:
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.
  - `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.
  - The regression's queued case passes.
  - The direct case hit the Gateway test RPC timeout on the first `chat.send` because the shared test host was saturated (load average 50–90, cold Gateway start of about 9 minutes). It passed before the rebase. CI is the clean rerun.
- Local review: autoreview (codex), branch mode against `origin/main` at P1, returned scoped-clean with no actionable findings.
- The live incident was inspected read-only on the affected host. Turns failed with sandbox-provisioning `Aborted`, lease-lost or watchdog errors, and session history ended in consecutive user messages with no reply or error entry, matching the red behavior above.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix: recover exited Windows lock owners after EPERM
body:
Supersedes #138697, thanks @Barry-886.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows stale-lock recovery remaining blocked when an exited owner’s PID still returns `EPERM` from the signal-zero probe.

## User Impact

Windows can recover locks whose owners are proven absent or exited by the existing native process identity reader. Live owners, protected or unreadable owners, and unavailable native inspection remain protected. POSIX behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already consults native identity in `isPidAlive`, but `isPidDefinitelyDead` returns early on Windows `EPERM`. Let that case reach the same existing native evidence instead of introducing another PowerShell/CIM query. Native access denial never means absence. Existing start-time checks still handle PID reuse; lock age alone never authorizes reclaiming a live owner.

Production delta: **+3 lines**, after removing the duplicated native-result branch from the same liveness owner. Regression delta: **+25 lines**, with a matching test-line allocation for the five distinct Windows owner outcomes. No dependency, state format, or public configuration change.

## Evidence

- Base `050238fdbdb0816d03f01588dbc6a3eced999f3b`: the new regression failed for both absent and retained-exited Windows owners (`expected false to be true`); live/protected/unavailable controls passed.

title: fix(workspace): interrupted refresh_base permanently wedges the session sandbox workspace
body:
Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions
- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ce8a3e10-2215-49f3-aaec-9ba55c3a7b27)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/13e44c7b-8097-45d4-9e4f-c9c19569b34e)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's sandbox workspace stays stuck forever when `github_publish` `refresh_base` on a branch far behind its base is interrupted by a turn deadline.

## User Impact

User impact: an interrupted base refresh now finishes on a later turn instead of wedging the session; later turns no longer fail sandbox workspace setup (lease lost, stall watchdog, quiesce abort) while the refresh is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

A base refresh deliberately keeps its pending receipt and paused runtime until both the canonical worktree and the sandbox projection accept the refreshed files. When a projection pass was stopped mid-application, workspace recovery treated the base-refresh journal like an ordinary reconciliation and restored the files it had already applied. Every later turn therefore restarted the whole projection application from the old files within its own deadline. On a large real repository one application pass costs several minutes (patch creation dominates), so it was interrupted again each time and the session could never run, including the `refresh_base` that would have resumed it.

Recovery now keeps the already-applied files for base-refresh refs and only clears the stale journal. The next pass reconciles the remaining difference toward the same staged result, which is idempotent for files that are already refreshed. Ordinary (non-base-refresh) journals still roll back exactly as before.

Accepted edge cases:
- A pass stopped in the middle of writing one file leaves that file for the next pass to reconcile toward the staged result rather than restoring it first; the staged result and receipt are unchanged, so the next pass converges.
- The first pass on a very large refresh is still long; this change makes progress durable across turns but does not make patch creation itself faster.

## Evidence

- Regression test `resumes an interrupted base refresh from the files it already applied` (`local-workspace-projection.test.ts`, real Git + SQLite): stops the projection pass at acceptance, then stops the next turn before it writes, then lets a third turn finish.
  - Red on the base (fix reverted): `expected 'original\n' to be 'refreshed\n'` — recovery rolled the applied refresh back.
  - Green with the fix: the refreshed bytes survive both stopped turns and the third turn accepts the refresh (`base_commit` advanced, `pending_ref`/`pending_target`/`journal_json` cleared). Whole `local-workspace-projection.test.ts` suite: 71 passed, 1 skipped.
- Real-repository run (scratch harness, not committed) on a copy of an OpenClaw checkout refreshed across a large base gap: attempt A was stopped at projection acceptance after ~228s with the refreshed files applied; attempt B was stopped again before writing and kept them (14s); attempt C completed the refresh in 25s and cleared the pending receipt. Without the fix, recovery restores the pre-refresh files (the red test above), so each later attempt repeats the full multi-minute application.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on touched files.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Problem

Each automation row in the session details sidebar showed more than the automation itself: under the name and schedule it repeated the last meaningful run result (clamped to two lines), a muted "Checked 14m ago" freshness line, and a "Check failed" marker after a failed run. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI sessions sidebar header (owner picker such as "My sessions", the status filter, and the collapse button) scrolls out of view when the session list is scrolled, so filtering or collapsing the sidebar first requires scrolling back to the top.

## User Impact

User impact: the sessions sidebar header stays pinned at the top of the sidebar while the session list scrolls, on desktop and in the mobile navigation drawer, in light and dark themes. Pages and Online panels are unchanged.

title: fix(memory): reclaim archived legacy reindex shadows
body:
Supersedes #136327, thanks @NianJiuZst.
Closes #136284

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained disk usage when Doctor has already archived a legacy memory database but old `.tmp-<uuid>` reindex shadows remain beside it.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` can reclaim shadow families older than 24 hours after the primary has a regular `.migrated` archive and no primary or primary companion remains. Live indexes, configured import sources (including aliases), current-format shadows, young families, symlinks, and unresolved recovery state are preserved. Removal failures are recoverable warnings.

Eligible files appear in Doctor's preview and migration backup inventory. Every cleanup path also reports each file to stderr before deletion, including automatic Doctor migrations without a backup capture. Freshly archived databases wait until the next Doctor invocation. The candidate contains this repair; the installed updater needs no new protocol. This uses the existing SQLite sidecar migration and does not alter schemas, configuration, search results, or runtime cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main (`f1c935770852`) recognizes only `.memory-reindex-<uuid>` in runtime cleanup and requires a live primary for Doctor import discovery. Archived legacy families therefore never reach either cleanup path. This replacement keeps retirement checks and cleanup with the existing Doctor migration instead of porting the larger proposal or widening runtime deletion.

The filesystem helper shares the sidecar suffix declaration with import/archival and keeps Doctor enumeration dependency-light. Production +131/-8 (net +123), tests +88/-1 (net +87), docs +13, and a separate +87 test-line allocation. The necessary growth covers archived-location discovery, conservative family checks, backup inventory, preview, and truthful failure reporting; no equivalent dead production path could safely be removed.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged main owner: both default and configured archived-path cases fail because Doctor returns no detection; unresolved recovery preservation passes.
- Final affected migration and backup-inventory suites: 44 tests passed in 27.90 seconds including worker preparation (24.06 seconds in the test runner). Ten declaration/dependency-closure tests also passed; their import graph is unchanged by the safety corrections.
- Additional regressions failed on the first candidate when a configured recovery alias lost its target and when removals had no pre-deletion report. Both pass with the final guard and reporting; the reporting test verifies each file still exists when reported.
- Targeted memory-core typecheck, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The initial leaf typecheck lacked generated SDK declarations; it passed after the repository's normal lint preparation generated them.
- Final local autoreview against `f1c935770852`, Codex, P0-P2: `scoped-clean`, no remaining findings. Configured-source alias preservation and the automatic path without backup capture were addressed with physical identity checks and an unconditional pre-deletion report, respectively. Full sidecar, backup, and automatic/exclusive migration orchestration context supplied; the reviewer did not execute project code.
- Earlier candidate [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41215006725) failed in the PostgreSQL update-cohort restore test: a global namespace snapshot expected three schema rows but received two. Matching main jobs passed, so baseline attribution remains unproven. That test disables plugins and is unchanged here; a passing later run is not claimed to repair it.
- Contributor source was read through PR view/diff only and was never checked out or run. The replacement was independently implemented from main. Tests use synthetic isolated filesystem/SQLite state through the public Doctor migration boundary; a complete published-updater/CLI upgrade was not run on the production host. Broad proof is delegated to this PR's CI.

Human contributor credit is retained in the commit: `Co-authored-by: NianJiuZst <180004567+NianJiuZst@users.noreply.github.com>`.

title: fix(ui): dim mobile browser chrome with the navigation drawer
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #189474. On a phone, opening the navigation drawer dims the page behind a `rgb(0 0 0 / 44%)` backdrop (`.shell--mobile-nav .shell-nav-backdrop`). The browser chrome did not dim with it. `theme-color`, and the document canvas Safari shows behind its status bar and toolbar, kept the undimmed page color, so the top and bottom bands looked lighter than everything between them. Measured on an iPhone capture with Absolutely dark: the dimmed page was ≈`#101010`, the bands `#1b1b1a`.

The backdrop is deliberately `position: absolute` inside the app canvas: Safari fades fixed backgrounds into its chrome on its own. That means the bands follow `theme-color` and the `html`/`body` background, not the scrim.

## Fix

- The shell reports the open drawer to the system chrome owner. `app-host` passes `{ contentCanvas, navScrim }` to `syncControlUiSystemChrome`; `navScrim` is true when the committed shell has `shell--mobile-nav` and `shell--nav-drawer-open`. The positional `contentCanvas` boolean became this object, and the owner keeps the last committed value for theme and breakpoint resyncs.
- While `navScrim` is set, the owner publishes the surface color composited behind the 44% scrim to `theme-color` and `--control-ui-system-chrome-background`. Closing the drawer restores the surface color. The scrim opacity is a named constant next to the composite, with a comment pointing to the backdrop rule.
- The document canvas uses one owner-toggled class, `control-ui-system-chrome-canvas`, set when the exposed narrow route canvas (`/new`, `systems`) or the drawer backdrop differs from the page surface. It replaces the media-scoped `control-ui-content-canvas` rule, so total CSS shrinks. `control-ui-performance` allows no CSS growth on main; the first push failed it by adding a second rule (+117 B raw).

## Impact

With the drawer open, the top and bottom bands match the dimmed page in every built-in theme, and they return to the page color when it closes. Nothing changes when the drawer is closed or on desktop.

The bands switch at the start of the drawer's 441 ms fade instead of animating with it. The `theme-color` meta cannot transition, and I kept `body` in step with it.

## Evidence

Drawer open, 393×852, with iPhone safe areas emulated. The top and bottom bars are painted from the published `theme-color`, standing in for Safari's tinting, which Chromium does not do:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absolutely dark | ![before absolutely dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7bee2be-e652-4e82-ad62-3194904505d9) | ![after absolutely dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43c19af1-47d1-4e3a-b6b5-49f4c56aa192) |
| Claw light | ![before claw light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5a462e2-6945-4f04-b3ba-372957144ca0) | ![after claw light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d976dd1-5916-45ea-b4ba-987e4ebcb06b) |

Published `theme-color` with the drawer open: `#1f1f1e` → `#111111` (Absolutely dark), `#f4f4f4` → `#898989` (Claw light).

- **Regression (red on base, green on fix):** `theme-typography.e2e` ("keeps system chrome with the mounted route…") now checks that the `html` and `body` backgrounds equal `theme-color` in every state. It also opens the drawer and expects the dimmed page color, closes it from the backdrop and expects the page color, then opens it again. On base it failed at the drawer step (received `#f4f4f4`, expected `#898989`). The earlier states, now also checked on `html`/`body`, passed on base.
- **Green on the current head (Chromium, bundled UI e2e):** theme-typography, theme-surfaces, theme-background, theme-boot, mobile-shell-geometry, mobile-chat-header, mobile-sidebar-session-menu and app-chrome-interaction: 8 files, 58 tests. Unit tests: `control-ui-presentation.test.ts` 5/5, updated to the new call signature and class name only.
- **Checks:** oxfmt, stylelint and oxlint on the touched files, plus `pnpm tsgo:ui`.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` at `fb0087b` (before the CSS consolidation), max priority P1, came back `scoped-clean` with no findings. The reviewer noted that it did not receive the unchanged source.

Not covered here: I have not checked this on a real iPhone in Safari.

title: fix: Doctor leaves literal quotes in macOS service credentials
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor leaves macOS gateway and node service credentials unusable when their generated env file contains unintended literal outer double quotes.

Supersedes #103845, thanks @lonexreb.

Related: #103804.

## User Impact

Interactive `openclaw doctor` identifies affected keys, retains a private backup, and removes one outer quote pair after explicit confirmation. Other env text stays byte-identical and values are never displayed. Restart the named service afterward; correct inherited shell values before reinstalling.

Quotes can be intentional data, so `--yes` and noninteractive runs cannot approve this repair. Native macOS service startup and a latest-stable upgrade were not exercised; local proof uses synthetic files and a real POSIX shell on Linux. The Team Gateway was untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main's writer already preserves clean input correctly; it also faithfully preserves existing literal quotes. The original quote-introducing boundary remains unconfirmed. This is recovery for existing files, with lossless runtime reads retained.

The existing service-file owner inspects generated shell literals, backs up the original at mode 0600, and publishes through the existing atomic writer under the owning gateway/node operation lock. Confirmed repair runs after schema admission and the update offer, before Doctor maintenance captures the launcher fingerprint; later health checks only diagnose. Multiline values, escaped apostrophes, unrelated entries, and files changed during the prompt are preserved.

Production delta: +109 lines. Removed the duplicate macOS warning dispatcher/list in favor of the existing collector; further deletion would remove unrelated behavior. Remaining growth implements the missing inspection, consent, backup, and repair path. Test delta: +151 lines, covered by a dedicated allocation for these regression contracts. No dependency, schema, config-option, or changelog changes.

## Evidence

- Regression on main base `2e705304cb39`: 5 failures / 14 passes, because Doctor neither reports nor repairs the seeded corruption. The same regression file passes all 19 tests with the fix, including repair after schema admission and before maintenance, diagnostic-only maintenance, gateway/node profile selection, real shell values, retained private backup, noninteractive refusal, and prompt-time file replacement.
- Startup tests: 7 passed. These two focused files completed in 44.27 seconds including worker compilation; the regression file's warm Vitest shard took 2.50 seconds, including import/transform time.
- Existing flow/update tests: 103 passed. An initial combined command hit its 120-second limit during the next service-writer shard; it is not counted as a passing complete run.
- Real generated wrapper + current value encoder: clean input stays clean; existing outer quotes reach the child process unchanged. No service installation or contributor code was run.
- Codex autoreview against `2e705304cb39`, P0–P2: identified schema admission ordering in the prior staged snapshot; resolved in `953b61ef77b4`. The reviewer explicitly found the corrected working-tree ordering sound and established no additional P0–P2 defects. The committed correction matches that reviewed working tree. Native macOS and stable-upgrade gaps remain explicit.
- Existing service-writer ordering: 8 passed; launchd service-file tests: 17 passed (75.56 seconds including worker compilation; test time about 28 seconds total). Targeted Doctor typecheck, changed-file oxlint/format, the mock-export ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The ratchet initially required isolation annotations for the new external-boundary mocks; those annotations are included in the correction. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41213186289) succeeded for `953b61ef77b4` (about 17 minutes elapsed for the complete workflow; per-file CI seconds are not reported).

title: fix(ui): close mobile session sheets when switching sessions
body:
## Problem

On mobile web chat, sheets and panels carried over between sessions:

- **Entering a session reopened its saved desktop layout.** The mobile host's default `open` state came from the session's saved sidebar layout (`layout.open` or a non-conversation main panel). Any session last used on desktop with Files, Terminal, or a similar panel open came up on mobile with that sheet covering the conversation.
- **Returning to a session reopened the sheet you had left open.** Chat keeps a parked pane for each session (`chat-pane-cache`). A parked pane kept `mobilePresentation.open = true`, so going back to that session showed the old sheet again.

Desktop is supposed to restore each session's panels, and it still does.

## Solution

All changes are in the pane's mobile presentation owner (`ChatPaneSidePanels`):

- **Default closed on mobile.** A mobile session now starts on its conversation. The saved layout still decides what opens on dashboard routes (`routeFace === "dashboard"` or `dashboardExpanded`), so dashboard links keep showing their board, the same exception native mobile already makes in `restorePaneSidebarLayout`.
- **Forget the sheet when a pane is parked.** `presentedChanged(false)` calls `forgetMobilePresentation()`, so the next render resets that pane's mobile presentation.
- **Keep explicit opens.** `navigateMobileHost` now applies the session reset before it records the request. Without this, a panel opened for a new session before that session's first render (an agent `ui.command`, a buffered panel toggle) would be thrown away by the reset that follows.

Nothing changes in the saved per-session layout or in desktop presentation.

## Evidence

- New unit test `chat-mobile-host.test.ts` › "enters each session closed on mobile while desktop keeps the saved open panels": fails on `main`, passes with the fix. Removing the `navigateMobileHost` scoping line also makes it fail, so that line is required.
- New browser e2e test `ui/src/e2e/mobile-session-panel-persistence.e2e.test.ts` runs at 390 px (mobile) and 1280 px (desktop), with two sessions that both have a saved open Files panel:
  - **Mobile:** session A opens closed. Files is then opened by hand. Session B opens closed, and returning to A is also closed.
  - **Desktop:** both sessions restore the open Files panel.
  - **On `main`:** the mobile case fails on the first session.
  - **Without the park reset:** it fails on the return to A.
- `mobile-panel-auto-open.e2e.test.ts` still passes, so agent-driven panel opens on mobile web keep working.
- 114 chat-pane, mobile, sidebar-region and board unit test files: 1288 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, the `ui-chat` and `ui-e2e` test typecheck lanes, oxlint, oxfmt, `format:docs:check` and `git diff --check` all pass.
- Local autoreview (branch vs `origin/main`, P2): scoped-clean.

Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/panels.md` now describes the mobile behavior and limits per-session panel restore to desktop.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ui): match mobile browser chrome to the session chat surface
body:
## Problem

On narrow screens (iPhone Safari), the status-bar band at the top and the band behind Safari's bottom toolbar are a different shade than the chat. Measured on a real iPhone capture with the Absolutely dark theme: chat `#1f1f1e`, bands `#1b1b1a`. Every built-in palette has the same mismatch (e.g. Claw light `#f4f4f4` chat vs `#f8f8f8` bands).

Cause: `syncControlUiSystemChrome` publishes `--bg-content` for every narrow chat-like route (`shell--chat`), both into `<meta name="theme-color">` and into the `html`/`body` canvas Safari shows in the safe areas. The mobile session workbench (`.sidebar-region--mobile-host`, `--chat-surface: var(--bg)`) paints `--bg` over that canvas, so the chrome no longer matched what it borders. Only `/new` and `systems` still leave the shell's `--bg-content` canvas visible at the edges.

The generic mobile `.content` rule also adds a 4px top inset above the session workbench. Desktop chat has none. That inset showed the shell canvas as a thin strip under the status bar. It was hidden only because the band above it was the same wrong color.

## Fix

- `app-host` marks the narrow layout as exposing the content canvas only for chat-like routes without a mounted session workbench (`content--workbench`). Session routes now publish `--bg`, the surface they paint. `/new` and `systems` keep `--bg-content`. The flag and its root class are renamed (`chatShell`/`control-ui-chat-shell` → `contentCanvas`/`control-ui-content-canvas`) to match that meaning.
- theme-color now receives resolved colors (`resolveThemeColor`) instead of raw palette expressions. Named themes derive `--bg` with `color-mix()`, which was being written verbatim into the meta tag.
- The narrow session workbench drops the generic 4px mobile top inset (`padding-top: 0`, as on desktop chat), so its header meets the system chrome without a seam. My first version painted the workbench instead. `theme-background.e2e` rejected that because it put an opaque layer over shell theme artwork, so the inset is removed and nothing is painted.

## Impact

The top and bottom browser bands on mobile session chat now match the chat surface in every built-in light and dark theme. Desktop, settings, `/new` and `systems` publish the same chrome colors as before; only the format changed (resolved hex instead of `color-mix()`).

## Evidence

Synthetic fixture captures, 393×852, iPhone safe areas emulated (`--safe-area-top: 59px`, `--safe-area-bottom: 34px`):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |

title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping retries after execution timeouts
body:
Supersedes #137274, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.

Related: #137215.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes overlapping executions when a cron job times out but its original runner continues past the retry deadline.

## User Impact

Timeout retries remain enabled and wait for the original execution to settle. Late completion preserves the single recorded timeout outcome. No public API, configuration, or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker-owned finalizer now retains the active receipt while recording the timeout, then finishes only that receipt after the underlying execution settles. The scheduler owns the subsequent refresh, and startup recovery reuses the recorded outcome.

The older settlement module was removed by #169946, so this is an independent repair of the current owner. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

## Evidence

- On main `028723cde2165962d8489b2548e74efaf18e6de3`, the initial fake-timer reproduction started the runner twice while the first execution remained held. The final one-shot and recurring regressions both fail on that unmodified main because the active receipt is prematurely released.
- With the repair: 102 tests across seven focused cron files passed (63.22s total command wall time). After the final scheduler-wake adjustment, all 40 affected tests in the watchdog, receipt-finalization, and worker-finalization files passed again (69.35s including compilation). The regressions preserve retry eligibility with rejected or stalled cleanup, fence execution until settlement, and retain one timeout plus one successful retry. Recovery coverage confirms no second accounting pass after restart.
- The initial CI found six TypeScript narrowing errors introduced by this repair. The correction makes the receipt required at the shared recovery operation; an explicit type check of the worker module passes, as do all 25 tests in the affected watchdog/recovery suites. The earlier local test-import graph did not reach that worker module. Changed-file lint, formatting, assertion-safety, max-lines and whitespace checks passed. The local test-line ratchet exceeded its 120s host budget; its exact-head CI check passed. The allocation records exactly 115 added regression lines.
- Fresh autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) found no actionable findings on the final staged tree `94b655267fb466152564e47e4407e291333cd26c`. A fresh P0–P3 review of the type correction also found no actionable findings. These were static reviews; runtime proof is recorded separately.
- Compatibility: no schema, stored format, migration, or status-enum change. Existing legacy-history recovery and receipt admission/retirement tests passed; the new restart regression preserves job settings and history while settling a recorded timeout. The advisory hosted review requests a latest-stable upgrade run; that operational proof was not run under this task's focused-test-only host constraint. The storage-boundary proof covers the changed lifecycle, with that limitation explicit.
- Candidate: `23805358a80b237f122c1452ed48c28744d6a1d6`. All required exact-head CI passed in [run 41213153484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41213153484), including production/test types, baseline ratchets, tests, lint, and security checks. Merged as `7caee827c5be71496b5f3ab8dcc6eee559b7db83`. No production Gateway or live state was modified.

<details>
<summary>Scope and tradeoff</summary>

Production net +43 lines; regression tests net +115; allocation +2. Removed obsolete host mixed-deferred batch splitting and unused finalizer options in the same owner, plus the superseded marker-retirement recovery fallback. The remaining growth carries execution settlement into the worker-owned receipt lifecycle and preserves accounting idempotency; the zero-growth target was not reached.

A runner that never settles keeps its own job fenced. Failed asynchronous receipt settlement logs a warning and leaves the receipt for startup recovery rather than admitting overlapping work.

</details>

title: fix(ui): keep the mobile composer open while a draft waits
body:
## Problem

On the mobile Control UI, typing a message and then leaving the composer (tapping the transcript, a header button, etc.) collapses it to the one-line resting capsule even though there's an unsent draft. The draft gets cut off on one line, and the +, permission, context, model and effort controls disappear until you tap back into the editor.

The cause: the resting one-line layout in `ui/src/styles/chat/composer-mobile.css` (and the `data-composer-layout="single-line"` textarea reset) applied whenever the composer wasn't being edited, without checking whether a draft existed.

## Solution

Built on the restored in-composer layout from #189454. While editing, the composer is the full surface with its controls row inside it, below the text. At rest, it's the one-line capsule.

- `chat-composer-mobile-interaction.tsx` now owns one presentation fact, `mobileResting`: the mobile composer is resting only when it isn't being edited **and** its visible draft is empty.
- `chat-composer-view.tsx` sets `data-composer-resting` on the shell from that fact, and also drives `data-composer-layout="single-line"` from it, so the textarea reset follows the same rule.
- `composer-mobile.css`: the existing one-line rules are keyed on `[data-composer-resting="true"]` instead of `[data-composer-editing="false"]`. This is a straight selector swap with the same specificity and no new rules.

With a draft waiting, the composer keeps the full editing surface, with the controls row inside it. An empty composer still rests as the capsule. `data-composer-editing` and `onComposerEditingChange` still report real editing, so keyboard handling and mobile-host panel suspension don't change. Nothing from #189264's raised toolbar comes back.

CSS size: 309,275 B gzip / 1,598,970 B raw, slightly below main (309,341 / 1,599,255), so the budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI at 390×844 (touch, DPR 2) on the current head. Current main is the "before". The flow types a draft, then taps the transcript:

| Before (main): draft collapsed to one line, controls hidden | After: draft keeps the open composer, controls inside | After: empty composer still rests as the capsule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f8c716d-3dda-4937-a2a3-31cf6ec2a452) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e86be545-6813-4a03-97c0-f7e25e98734a) | ![after empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35ef5433-f9e8-4408-9aa0-be3f8cdb6100) |

States recorded by the same Playwright flow:

| | `editing` | `layout` | toolbar |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before, draft waiting | false | single-line | hidden |
| After, draft waiting | false | none | inside the composer |
| After, empty draft | false | single-line | hidden |

Tests:

- New real-pane browser test `chat-pane-keyboard.browser.test.tsx` › "keeps the mobile composer open while a typed draft waits". It types into a real pane and blurs, then checks three things: the composer is not single-line, the controls are shown, and they sit inside the input surface. Then it clears the draft, blurs and checks the composer rests on one line with the controls hidden. **Fails on main** (`expected 'single-line' to be undefined`) and passes with the fix.
- `chat-composer-mobile.browser.test.tsx`: two tests that measure the resting one-line capsule now use an empty draft (attachments only, or none), so they keep exercising that capsule.
- `chat-pane-keyboard`, `chat-composer-mobile` and `chat-composer-height` browser suites: 29/29 pass.
- Mocked Control UI e2e: chat-composer-redesign, chat-model-controls, chat-composer-picker-layout, chat-mobile-latest-clearance, chat-attributed-identity, new-session-page.instant-thread, chat-composer-focus, composer-layout, chat-composer-pointer-activation, question-flow, chat-mobile-environment, chat-composer-accessory-focus, mobile-new-conversation and composer-draft-store. 96/97 pass. The one failure is the desktop (1100px) WebKit case of the picker layout. It's a local environment failure: the host's egress proxy blocks WebKit from loading the local test server, and the failure screenshot shows only "Secret egress proxy refused the request." The Chromium case of the same test passes. CI's WebKit lane covers it.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `pnpm ui:build && pnpm ui:check-performance` are clean.

The published branch already had history, and the publisher never force-pushes it. So current `origin/main` is merged in rather than rebased onto. The PR diff against main is only the five files above.

title: fix(whatsapp): stop group replies to unrelated phone-number digits
body:
Supersedes #137490, thanks @elbourne12345.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp replies in mention-required groups when unrelated order IDs, longer numbers, or scattered digits happen to contain the bot's phone number.

## User Impact

Group messages containing ordinary numbers stay as context without waking the bot. Mention the bot using WhatsApp's native mention picker or a delimited `@15555550123` / `@+15555550123` token. title: fix(ui): restore the two-bolt Ultrafast look as one icon
body:
## Problem

#184760 replaced the Ultrafast indicator (two stacked `zap` icons with a `drop-shadow` gap) with a single `zapDouble` SVG. That made it one icon, but changed the look: softer rounded bolts, a different overlap, and a white-mixed palette.

## Solution

Keep `zapDouble` as a single SVG, but rebuild it from the original geometry:

- **Front bolt:** the regular `zap` polygon at the old 2px/4px offset. The viewBox is `27.43 × 30.86`, which is the old 16×18 box in zap units.
- **Rear bolt:** a precomputed path made from the stroked `zap` outline minus the front bolt and its old `-0.8px/-0.6px` gap. The separation is real transparency, so it works on any background. It needs no mask, no `id`, and no background-colored outline. The rear bolt has `stroke="none"` because the stroke is already baked into its outline.
- **Colors:** the icon now carries the original theme-aware mixes as its own defaults: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 60%, var(--muted))` for the rear bolt and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 75%, var(--text-strong))` for the front. `--icon-secondary` and `--icon-primary` remain overrides. The unchecked speed option still mutes the icon. The checked option resets both vars to `initial`, so it falls back to the icon's own colors. The composer trigger no longer needs any color CSS.

The unused `SOFT_ZAP_PATH` is removed. Raw CSS shrinks compared with `main`. An earlier head grew it by 129 B and failed `control-ui-performance`; moving the colors into the icon fixed that.

## Evidence

Screenshots, including mobile at 390×844: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189443#issuecomment-6544631018

- **Visual comparison:** a temporary Control UI e2e scenario (mock Gateway, session `fastMode: "ultrafast"`, dark and light) rendered the composer trigger and the effort/speed menu. It also rendered a same-page comparison of the pre-#184760 two-icon composition, current `main`, and this PR, at 1×, 2× and 5×. This PR matches the pre-#184760 shape and colors in both themes.
- **Mobile:** a scenario at 390×844 and 3× scale rendered the gauge badge with this PR's icon and with `main`'s. The thinner stroke used by the badge is not visible at this size.
- **Current head:** a re-check found the trigger and the checked option both resolve to the intended mixes. Dark: rear `rgb(210 112 116)`, front `rgb(252 130 130)`. Light: rear `rgb(151 79 67)`, front `rgb(150 60 45)`. 2/2 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files.

title: feat: prepare retained repository disks for explicit operations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explicit repository operations could not prepare a paused retained disk, and an interrupted Move requiring a newer worker runtime stayed held even when the original disk remained intact.

Depends on #189346, now landed as `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`. This PR targets **main** and preserves the actual landed authority, current-disk I/O, Move and lifecycle prerequisites. Related: #188796.

## User Impact

Selected publication snapshots remain immutable: retries neither wake the disk nor recapture later edits, and preserve the landed checkpoint-alias recovery path.

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Ordinary mirrored sessions and turn admission are unchanged. This child adds no schema, config selector, queue, manager, provider allocation or public protocol. Failed wake preserves durable Move custody for retry; it never substitutes an older mirror or replacement disk. No deployment or controller adoption is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Editor preparation stays inside session/workspace exclusion and precedes result claiming. Downloads retain read authority through preparation and every byte window.
- Move intent and result custody own wake before quiescence. Already-quiesced Move capture does not refresh its native owner. One exact-disk/result predicate serves host refresh admission, native validation and settlement; mirrored Moves, other targets and replaced disks remain refused.
- Runtime refresh preserves the original epoch, disk, pending result and placement. Current requester authority reaches awaited installation and the receipt-writing effect; revocation grants no new turn or input replay.
- The implementation removes a separate pre-drain wake path and reuses existing lifecycle, result and queue owners. Separate measured test allocations are **546** for consumer/recovery contracts, **4** for the Stop fixture isolation/assertion repair, and **6** for the required fixture-contract repair; the shared scalar is unchanged.

The provider readiness module is again byte-identical to landed main and adds no child production delta. The subsequent fixture-only CI repair is recorded below.

Vitest **339.55s**, wrapper **362s**; cold transformation accounted for 75% of Vitest time, including a 139.225s worker compilation. The exact failed typecheck reproduced both TS2741 errors before repair and passed afterward. Both affected materialization/publication-handoff files passed **28 cases**, Vitest **268.56s**, wrapper **276s**. Scoped CI-mode lint, formatting, whitespace and ratchet **6,378,997 ≤ 6,393,537** passed in **96s**.

title: fix(discord): serve live mentions ahead of recovery backlog
body:
Supersedes #121204, thanks @emeric-dandelion-cult. Human commit-author credit is retained for @gloss-dandelion-cult.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live Discord mentions wait behind old ambient messages after Gateway recovery because each old message must finish preflight before the channel lane advances.

## User Impact

Recent native bot mentions take priority over pending recovery chatter, while ambient messages still reach normal preflight and history recording. A live turn can start before the remaining ambient context is recorded. Active claims and retry backoff can still delay a mention. Pattern-only mentions, replies without a native bot mention, and DMs retain their existing scheduling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ingress drain now accepts an optional pending-message priority predicate. Discord prefers guild messages with a native bot mention sent within the last 15 minutes. Snapshot order stays stable within each priority, and original indices retain retry eligibility. Normal claim validation and access policy still own delivery. There are no new configuration settings or schema/retention changes.

Production delta: **+15 lines** (+30/-15). Simplified redundant dispatch return-type plumbing in the same drain owner; remaining growth supplies the priority hook and Discord predicate. This replaces the proposed pre-claim expiry/inventory machinery with scheduling only, preserving ambient history.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `94a2a5463910d8d614c9f56719cfbc45ae4c28f8` through the raw Discord handler, real durable queue, dispatcher and real preflight, with channel lookup held at the external I/O boundary. Three old ambient rows precede a newly admitted native mention. The regression fails on main: the next preflight is old row `1001` instead of live mention `2000`.
- With the fix, the live mention follows the already active row and precedes the remaining ambient rows. All three ambient history entries are retained; only the addressed message reaches the processing seam. The regression takes about 0.4 seconds. This is isolated boundary proof; no live guild, model, delivered reply, or production latency benchmark was run.
- Focused ingress, recovery, drain-lane and monitor-scheduling suites: **42 passed across 4 files**, 35.85 seconds including runner overhead. After the final ordering simplification, both changed suites passed again: **28 tests**; per-file wall times 6.33 seconds (drain lanes) and 13.22 seconds (Discord recovery), including import/transform overhead. A new owner regression checks priority FIFO and preservation of retry backoff.
- Discord package typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false`), targeted type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. After correcting the raw event type to Gateway MessageCreate, all 60 focused Discord listener/ingress/recovery tests pass (43.20 seconds including runner overhead). Broad typechecks/build/tests are delegated to PR CI on this production host.

Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; hosted ClawSweeper automatically picked up this PR when it opened, so no duplicate review request was sent.

The accepted Stop replacement test waits out a 15-second drain because its idle replacement fixture is retired only after awaiting Stop.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

title: fix: stop retrying exhausted unadopted channel messages
body:
Supersedes #124337, thanks @karmafeast.

**Withdrawn: this narrow replacement is unsafe without the broader cancellation cutover. Nothing was merged.**

## What Problem This Solves

The proposed shared-owner change bounds genuine pre-adoption abandonment, which still bypasses retry exhaustion on main.

## User Impact

No shipped change. The proposal would also dead-letter explicitly cancelled queued messages at the retry threshold because reply cancellation still reaches `onAbandoned`. It must not be deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared drain's direct abandonment release increments attempts but never consults the existing failure disposition. The proposed handoff fixes that defect, but retaining the drain's `onCancelled` callback is insufficient: `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` drops it, and `abortSessionControllerInput` invokes abandonment during explicit cancellation. Shared debounce, dedupe settlement, and channel-owned lifecycle wrappers also need a complete cancellation contract. That broader cutover is outside this task's bounded shared-owner-only takeover scope; #124337 is not being ported wholesale.

The useful part remains the shared retry-policy handoff and its exhaustion regression, conditional on completing cancellation propagation. Deliberate queue-cap drops remain the separate scope of #182252.

## Evidence

- **Original defect confirmed on main:** Telegram's production ingress monitor and SQLite queue, with a 25-hour-old message and seven prior failures, left the failed ledger empty after the eighth abandonment on `c504abf10afa`. The determining shared owner was also unchanged at `338de6d69998`.
- **Proposed fix:** the same Telegram regression passed; all 23 Telegram ingress tests and 38 shared drain/retry-policy tests passed. Wall times: 46.18 and 42.83 seconds, including worker compilation. Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- **Introduced regression reproduced:** a separate focused probe used real `createChannelIngressDrain` → `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` → `enqueueFollowupRun` → `clearFollowupQueue`, with the existing drain policy `maxAttempts: 1, deadLetterMinAgeMs: 0`. title: fix(telegram): show typing while detached children work
body:
Supersedes #134148, thanks @samiralibabic.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram looks idle after a requester yields while its detached child is still working.

## User Impact

Telegram keeps showing typing on the originating account, chat, and topic while an announcement-producing child runs. Quiet children and `typingMode: never` stay silent. Completion, errors, abort claims, requester reset/deletion/rebinding, revoked authority, and Gateway replacement stop further typing. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Gateway lifecycle typing/keepalive owner rather than adding Telegram progress hooks, a second controller, reference counts, or another expiry policy. Registration retains its original requester capability and a predicate over the canonical requester session identity and delivery state; the existing guarded transport rechecks those facts immediately before each send. A route changed before preparation is rejected, and the target is never redirected to a replacement session or chat.

The bridge is cosmetic and best effort, with the existing configured cadence and command timeout budget. It applies to currently registered public-completion children; it does not reconstruct typing after a process restart or expose internal/collector work.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged main production code: registered active children produced zero typing sends (expected originating routes); the same regression passes with the bridge.
