title: feat: hand repository disk custody to Gateway worktrees
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The existing Move-to-Gateway path still tried to reconcile a disk-authoritative repository as a mirror. It refused before a usable local handoff, and interruption recovery needed to distinguish an unimported disk from an already-bound managed worktree before releasing the original resource.

Depends on #189263, now landed as `38978c421475789e9daefda87c98dd8c450ef7c0`. This PR now targets `main`; the verified child-only comparison contains the same 37-path durable Move/handoff and retirement change.

## User Impact

For an already-bound, active exact repository disk, the existing authorized `sessions.move` operation can now hand work to the Gateway:

`draining Move → pending result/original receipt → fresh export → verified local worktree binding → repository custody retirement → exact-resource cleanup → local placement`

Private Git commits and working files survive. A staged index or unavailable history still refuses a lossy export. Missing/replaced disks do not fall back to an old mirror, clone-only reconstruction, or automatic replacement.

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Paused-disk preparation and final activation are separate. No schema/version change, new queue, manager, config option, or public protocol is introduced; the lifecycle owner’s shared-state v39 reservation is untouched. No deployment or cloud allocation is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Existing pending-result fields retain the fresh export and original immutable resource receipt. The repository owner gains an exact-claim retirement operation; the existing Move and environment owners keep cleanup and completion.
- Before local binding, recovery captures the current original disk again. It can resume an interrupted unbound import only when its HEAD matches the fresh export; unknown local commits still refuse.
- After local binding, recovery never recaptures or reapplies files. The managed worktree/session binding is the handoff receipt; original cleanup and pending-result release resume independently.
- Caller, session generation, writer, exact attachment, and publication exclusion remain enforced. In-memory recovery now preserves its actor/session/writer authority across its own workspace binding, rather than rejecting that binding.
- Claimless restart recovery no longer tries to close worker-tool state for a local claim; worker-owned closure remains unchanged.

Simplification reused the existing Move state, pending result, repository store, managed-worktree binding, and cleanup operations. No additional handoff schema was needed. The production growth covers the two real ownership transitions and crash recovery; 334 net test/helper lines are separately allocated for the actual Move entry and distinct interruption boundaries.

## Evidence

### Current main integration

Signed candidate **`82b400ee1a4a6a2fde04eb00344a2ee29cdda053`**, tree `cf6a958f8aec5444da2b8fbca1cb1468c345d7d3`, preserves original published `f9176e034c0b9efd38065b31c8e09dac8ca5b53b` ancestry and integrates actual landed S6/main. Native conflict resolution preserved the qualified child content and all landed prerequisite repairs, including retained capture aliases. The 37-path delta remains **+1,184/−305**, with the identical stable patch ID; only three inventory blobs incorporate independent main additions. No signature override, recreated PR, or unsigned prerequisite side-history was used.

- **25 current Move/recovery cases passed in two files**: 96.14s Vitest, 98.06s wrapper, including compiler cleanup. These overlap the prior 122-case integration proof and are not added to that count. Real Move, disk export, Git/native stores, restart boundaries and incognito/revocation cases exercise the newly combined capture/result owners.
- Current core and Gateway test typechecks, CI-mode scoped type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), canonical format, whitespace and test-line ratchet passed. Existing 334-line test allocation and shared scalar are unchanged.

An initial preparation attempt named a nonexistent context file and did not run a review; it was corrected to the actual teardown owner on the same route.

### Earlier implementation and repair proof

Earlier reviewed candidate **`f9176e034c0b9efd38065b31c8e09dac8ca5b53b`**, tree `4b62f52276f0a500bd7509ce6bd6f97467398c93`. It preserves the original Move implementation `0efab5aabb8c4f566195e025bea43a69f8d69769` and adds the owning CI repairs below:

- Reproduced the original authorized `sessions.move` failure: `A disk-authoritative repository cannot accept a mirrored checkpoint`. The same entry now reaches local placement with private HEAD and disk-only bytes intact.
- **13 Move scenarios passed**: normal completion; interruption at intent, import, before export, captured artifact, local binding, before/after cleanup, pending release, and reconciliation; revoked authority; in-memory success and revocation. Real Git, native stores, local node workspace/HTTP transfer, lifecycle barriers, and the real environment cleanup owner are used. Provider destruction and GitHub identity are explicitly synthetic.

title: feat(workers): recover retained disks through exact lifecycle intent
body:
Related: #188796
Depends on #189350 (durable disk Move), above #189263 (current-disk IO), #189106 (disk authority), and #189019 (exact resource receipts). Those prerequisites have landed; this PR now targets `main`.

## Problem and solution

A retained cloud disk needs durable pause/resume intent and exact-resource recovery. A lost provider reply or Gateway restart must not allocate a replacement, extend a work window, discard cleanup custody, or treat resumed compute as a usable worker.

The existing environment writer records immutable acquisition policy and lifecycle operation ID/action/expected claim revision. The provider queue retains the original receipt and operation. **Persisted resume intent is custody, not authority:** maintenance observes pending resume without replaying it; only a fresh authorized wake or same-key creation retry can reopen compute. Pause and lost-reply settlement keep their existing owners.

Crabbox translates the generic contract into Linux Azure Sandbox capability, identity, policy, and independent readback checks. Pending readiness is polled without starting or renewing compute; closed windows still require explicit recovery. Runtime admission stays fenced until the original node reconnects and its current bundle is verified. Unknown observations preserve custody; explicit deletion remains pending until exact-resource stop confirms it.

**Activation remains off.** No profile default, idle-sweep selection, workspace mirroring, disk-authority activation, controller adoption, or Crabbox dependency/release change. Released Crabbox cold-boot readiness is not claimed.

## Internal integration contract

- `createWithRequest` persists explicit retained policy before allocation. A fresh same-key retry revalidates caller/source authority, recovers the original receipt and operation, and resumes provisioning admission.

title: fix(msteams): send channel files to the team SharePoint site
body:
Supersedes #136274, thanks @a-tokyo.
Related: #136271

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Microsoft Teams channel file sends fail without a manually configured SharePoint site, and a central configured site can leave team members unable to open the file card.

## User Impact

Standard channels can send files to their own team's SharePoint site without setting `sharePointSiteId`. Explicit sites keep precedence. Group chats and private/shared channels still require an explicit site; no config migration or new option is introduced.

Discovery uses the existing `Sites.ReadWrite.All` application grant and the existing `ChannelSettings.Read.Group` RSC grant in the documented Teams manifest. No new permission scopes are requested. Microsoft documents these grants for [site lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/site-get?view=graph-rest-1.0) and [channel lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/channel-get?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both file-send paths now resolve the team's actual site through the existing guarded SharePoint Graph request owner. Cold references resolve the AAD group through the existing identity owner and regional SDK client. The site cache holds at most 500 account/tenant/bot/team entries; channel type is checked before using a cached parent-team site.

This is a small reimplementation of the useful fix, omitting the proposed folder option and extra Graph scope. The old require-site-only helper and its obsolete unit test are removed. Production grows by 113 lines for discovery, bounded caching, and the regional metadata operation; no equivalent dead production code was found to remove safely. Regression tests grow by 196 lines, with a matching test-line allocation for the two delivery entry points, cache isolation, cancellation, and audience/explicit-site contracts.

## Evidence

- Main baseline: `447e14d02460342af4fe2c98dbd5475b15b938d2`. The new regression failed in both public send entry points at the original `sharePointSiteId is required` error before production edits.
- Green: six focused sibling files, 82 tests (11.37s Vitest; 13.09s wrapper). Final changed test files: 33 tests (37.27s including cold worker preparation; 39.42s wrapper). The six new cases consume 40ms total test time. Discovery, upload requests, and final file-card assembly run together against synthetic external I/O; team/account interleaving verifies cache separation.
- Focused typecheck and typed lint passed; formatting, three-file MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed. The initial CI run passed all behavioral, type, lint, docs, and security jobs; its baseline job found a new test mock that did not preserve exports. That test-only defect is corrected, and the exact failed mock-export check now passes locally. The corrected six-case regression passes (7.84s Vitest / 9.63s wrapper). Final-head [CI run 41199827659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41199827659) passed on `ad71ec8e5ca71ff7bd1ffbfd001fb7d1f4795b00`, including the previously failing baseline checks.
- Shared autoreview completed at P0–P3 with `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings, against the full local candidate based on `447e14d02460342af4fe2c98dbd5475b15b938d2` (committed unchanged as `a1b7b58ccff0e60f0f7e44818abb1b85e14b6ac4`). This was a static review, with unchanged SDK, handoff, timeout, and identity sources supplied as context. A separate P0-P3 autoreview of the export-preserving test correction and exact three-line budget increase also completed scoped-clean; production is byte-identical in correction ad71ec8e5ca71ff7bd1ffbfd001fb7d1f4795b00.

title: feat(memory-wiki): allow owner-scoped bridge reads in shared vaults
body:
Supersedes #129191, thanks @igs-rogenlo.

## What Problem This Solves

Agents sharing a global wiki cannot restrict imported bridge notes to their owners without also separating the native wiki into per-agent vaults.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into `plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.bridge.ownership: "owner"` so non-sandboxed agents retrieve their own bridge notes while native wiki pages stay shared. The omitted setting and explicit `"sandboxed-only"` preserve today's behavior; sandboxed reads never widen.

Owner mode hides bridge pages without matching ownership, including unowned pages and calls without a resolved identity. CLI calls resolve the default agent unless `--agent` is supplied. This filters wiki query results, not filesystem access or compiled prompt digests; native aggregate pages remain shared. Existing configurations need no migration or action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing plugin-owned visibility filter and validate one optional enum in its runtime and manifest schemas. Delegation and public SDK additions from the original proposal are outside this minimal replacement. Main's `vault.scope: "agent"` separates the entire vault and does not cover this shared-native-pages scenario.

The simplification removes the one-use bridge-page predicate in the same visibility owner. Production TypeScript is **−3 lines**; manifest schema/help is **+8 lines**, for **+5 production/config lines** overall. Tests are **+43 lines**, allocated in a dedicated test-line record for the tool-level regression and independent schema boundary. Generated config artifacts add exactly one plugin leaf (4911 → 4912); core/channel counts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red before repair on main `447e14d02460`: owner-mode `wiki_search` returned another agent's bridge page; runtime schema rejected both new enum values. The original two-file run had 3 expected failures and 40 passes (50.60 seconds wall time).
- Green after repair: `pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.reads.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.path-lookup.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.abort.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query-reader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **64 passed, 6 files**, 46.77 seconds wall time including cold worker preparation; test execution about 2 seconds. PR CI succeeded at the same head: [run 41198930094](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41198930094), all 32 executed jobs passed; the changed-test job took 273 seconds including setup.
- The regression executes the real `wiki_search` and `wiki_get` tools on a synthetic temporary vault, checking omitted/legacy/owner settings, sandboxed and non-sandboxed calls, shared native pages, unowned bridge pages, unresolved identity, and CLI-style default identity. Existing memory-provider seams remain mocked; no live Gateway/model or stable-upgrade run was performed on the production host.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `config:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check`, staged test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad compiler/test proof is delegated to PR CI.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete candidate against `447e14d02460`, including query/config/tool context: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. The [requested hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189336#issuecomment-6543110134) completed with no code findings and asks for broader trusted-runtime and fresh/stable-install evidence. Review addressed by the maintainer ruling: the one optional field preserves defaults and sandbox restrictions; focused red→green proof and exact-head green CI are sufficient. Broader runtime/upgrade runs are not required for this change and were not performed. Applicable security review and `openclaw/ci-gate` have passed.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` only and was never checked out or executed. Human credit from both commit-author identities is retained; agent co-authors are excluded.


Upgrade note: existing configs without `bridge.ownership` validate unchanged and retain current sandbox-inferred visibility; the [runtime and manifest schema test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/34ac5c06226d9239b9a8ddacbe3703df3bd0e176/extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts#L25) covers the omitted field, and the tool regression covers unchanged default visibility.

title: fix(feishu): preserve durable final reply and card delivery

Supersedes #130580, thanks @zw-xysk.
Related: #114517.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Feishu final replies falling back from durable delivery when they include reply targets, threads, structured cards, or message-sending hooks.

## User Impact

title: feat(cli): read bounded model prompts from files
body:
Supersedes #120598, thanks @shad0wca7

Related: #140244

## What Problem This Solves

Automation must put large or sensitive one-shot model prompts in process arguments, where operating-system limits can reject them and process inspection can expose them.

## User Impact

`openclaw infer model run --prompt-file ./prompts/judge.txt` and the `capability` alias accept a UTF-8 file instead of `--prompt`. The file must stay inside the invocation's current directory, with symlinks and hardlinks rejected and a 1 MiB limit. The existing local and Gateway model-run paths receive the resolved text without adding a chat transcript. The selected provider still receives the prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the file at invocation time through the existing fs-safe root owner, then use the existing one-shot execution paths. Exactly one prompt source is required; invalid input fails before inference. This replacement adds one CLI flag and no configuration or Gateway protocol fields.

Production growth is 10 lines for input selection, the existing bounded reader call, and capability discovery. There is no equivalent dead code in this owner to remove safely; reusing fs-safe avoids a new file reader. Tests grow by 79 lines, with a dedicated allocation for the input-boundary regressions.

## Evidence

- Base: `3f8bff35bba2625b13a4c83e741e2320878de395`. The final eight prompt-file regressions all fail against the unchanged main command because the flag is unsupported, then pass with this change.
- Focused tests: 102 existing CLI cases, 33 model-run cases, and 14 prompt-prefix stability cases passed. The model-run file took 36.31 seconds including cold transformation (6.17 seconds on a cached run); prefix stability took 22.83 seconds.
- Real filesystem inputs cover a 140 KB UTF-8 prompt, both command names and execution transports, absence of input from CLI output, and missing, empty, oversized, escaping, symlinked, and conflicting input. Model/provider and Gateway I/O use fixtures; no live-provider run is claimed.

title: fix(reply): avoid sending blank attachments in normalized replies
body:
Supersedes #128580, thanks @sunlit-deng.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes broken replies when blank media metadata causes an empty attachment attempt, either instead of a text reply or after a valid attachment.

## User Impact

Replies with only blank media send their text normally, and mixed media lists send only real attachments. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original duplicate-text defect is already fixed by #129230, and #128372 preserves singular attachments when plural metadata is blank. Current main still passes whitespace media through its loose-payload normalizer to media senders.

Reuse the existing nonblank-string predicate for both media fields at that normalization owner. Empty strings, whitespace, and null entries are dropped before consumers choose dedupe or delivery; valid strings retain their original bytes, duplicates, order, and precedence. There is no new dedupe path.

Production delta: +3/-5, net -2 lines, replacing the local string/length predicate with the shared predicate. The 21-line test allocation covers two regressions at the public normalization-to-media-delivery boundary; the contributor's large proof runner is not ported.

## Evidence

- Baseline `bc82773a72ebe20a3f8c916998b3cfcbc7b00d78`: both regressions fail. A whitespace singular URL invokes the media sender instead of sending text; a mixed list invokes it for both the real image and a whitespace attachment.
- After: `src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts` passes all 33 tests (0.587 seconds total Vitest duration). The new cases exercise `createNormalizedOutboundDeliverer` through `sendTextMediaPayload` and inspect transport callbacks.
- Focused reply-builder, inbound-dispatch, direct-DM, and outbound-contract suites pass (65 additional tests); message-action execution and subagent-completion suites pass (73 additional tests).
- Targeted Plugin SDK/channel TypeScript, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation is provided by this PR's CI; per-file hosted CI seconds are not separately available yet.

title: fix(acp): keep completed run conversations resumable
body:
Related: #106696.

Supersedes #107366, thanks @henkterharmsel.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost conversation history and missing asynchronous results when a parent continues a completed ACP run-mode child.

## User Impact

With acpx and a harness that supports loading or resuming sessions, a follow-up to the same child key keeps its recorded conversation, including after a runtime restart. An asynchronous follow-up returns its result to the current parent once. Completion releases workers; reset and deletion prevent reuse. Persistent ACP children retain their existing delegated completion behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already retains the necessary metadata. Reuse the persisted-handle lookup after completion and let the existing one-way completion owner return the new result. Keep live-task, caller, and persistent-parent completion exemptions. Remove the obsolete private metadata-based helper and redundant metadata overlay.

This independently implements the useful behavior without porting the large proposal or adding state, capabilities, configuration, dependencies, or retention policy. Production code shrinks by 20 lines. Unsupported harnesses and previously deleted legacy metadata retain their existing behavior; #106696 remains open for those cases.

Regression tests grow by 215 lines, with an exact per-change test-line allocation: the real Gateway custody regression replaces the earlier mocked ACP return case and proves three distinct allowed/revoked/replaced outcomes. Docs grow by 2 lines; test routing and allocation add one line each.

## Evidence

- Red on main `2464bd85e0bc2927701c3147bf3dfc6993daaae3`: real acpx over stdio with a synthetic ACP agent returned a different backend session ID and forgot the first turn after completion/restart. Green: unchanged backend ID, history `["first", "second"]`, worker release, and deletion cleanup. The owner suite passed 5/5 (46.87 s command wall; continuity case 4.24 s). Its process cost protects real protocol/restart behavior that a helper test cannot establish. Runtime siblings passed 33/33.
- The production `createSessionsSendTool` regression is also red with main's routing source: accepted input reports `delivery.status="skipped"`. With the fix it returns pending, closes the invocation, then admits exactly one complete result to the original parent through the real Gateway service and completion custody. Device revocation or parent lifecycle replacement while the result is delayed prevents parent execution. All 3 custody cases pass (final Vitest duration 13.13 s; case test time 8.17 s; prior standalone command 24.69 s). Only model execution is synthetic; dispatch, final admission, profiles, authority, sessions, and SQLite remain real.
- [Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41191364263) caught a persistent-ACP scope regression. The repair retains that existing completion exemption; the exact failed coordination file passes 43/43 (77.49 s Vitest duration). Its existing integration cases are needed to protect other child modes. `test:ci-failed` could not retrieve escaped job logs; direct supported job-log retrieval identified the failure, and the exact file was run locally. No inherited-failure exception is claimed.
- Directed send policy 27/27, result consumers 8/8, remaining ACP interaction contract 1/1, and prompt-prefix stability 14/14 pass. Targeted plugin/agent-tools typechecks, lint, format, and diff checks pass. Broad proof runs through current-head PR CI; job timings are available in its check logs.
- Fresh Codex autoreview at P0–P2 confirmed the production custody test and found only the stale indexed persistent-parent regression, explicitly repaired in the reviewed working tree. That repair is included in the merged commit and matches the reviewed working-tree source. No additional P0–P2 source defect was found. The earlier missing completion-owner finding is also addressed.
- No contributor code was checked out or executed. These proofs use isolated synthetic state and a synthetic ACP agent, with no credentialed Claude/Codex/Cursor or external-channel smoke. No production Gateway or state was changed.

Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193101040) passed all 72 jobs. Whole-shard CI durations: `checks-node-changed-1` 251 s, `checks-node-changed-3` 248 s, and `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` 246 s. The [refreshed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189273#issuecomment-6542095798) found no actionable findings and cleared the authority-proof request.

title: feat: capture explicit repository disk snapshots
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explicit repository file access, publication and export must use the original attached disk—not an older Gateway mirror. Publication retries must preserve selected bytes and include requests queued after a lost receipt-binding reply.

Prerequisite #189106 landed as `7faf32da36cdb6f6021e662f92cbd9c1de783255`; GitHub automatically retargeted this existing PR to main. No replacement PR or early retarget.

## User Impact

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Mirrored sessions and ordinary turns retain their behavior. This implements explicit current-disk I/O and snapshot preparation, not full retained-disk activation. No schema, public protocol, product configuration, cloud allocation or deployment is added.

- File reads, hash-checked editor writes, downloads and attachment originals use attached-node bytes. Editor settlement never accepts the old mirror.
- Publication captures under existing session exclusion and native quiescence. Selected/queued request refs and publication companions install atomically. Fresh capture, accepted-checkpoint reuse and retained retry share one ref owner. Lost replies never cause recapture of later disk edits or advancement of SQLite acceptance for artifact-only publication.
- Explicit Gateway export preserves private history/files and rechecks source before binding. Partial staged indexes or unavailable history fail closed, preserving the original disk.
- Paused preparation and final durable Move/teardown remain later work. Missing/replaced disks never trigger stale reconstruction or automatic replacement.

## Solution and Scope

Existing repository/checkpoint, placement, workspace-operation, transport and receipt owners retain their responsibilities. No parallel manager, queue, cache or state store. Authority is checked at the final effect; cleanup custody survives revocation.

Against captured main `c2a39e4c5a8166d1f5ea6703d1dfaa7d7c45de79`: **34 files, +2,106/-129**. Production remains **19 files, +527/-123 (net +404)**; the latest correction changes no production code. Tests/helpers: nine files +1,550/-6; docs +20; four allocation records +8; inventory +1. The 65-line checkpoint-ref leaf was extracted after a real 700-line owner-budget failure, without an exception. The review repair contributed production +97/-33 (net +64) and one boundary regression, now allocated exactly 92 lines after required braces. The existing 50-line accepted-reuse allocation and shared scalar remain unchanged.

## Current Candidate and CI Repair

**Head `6e669f1d0a24b07f65e7c3e42924c239efadf888`, tree `34760b3be1416d4a2ab7e4df1323062d2b941646`.** This is a signed descendant of reviewed implementation `fcd45d9ba30e8fd1f878e3d29fbc2cc4a0d36b3a`; its only delta is required braces around the unchanged revocation assertion and the corresponding two-line test-allocation adjustment (**two files, +4/-2**).

[CI 41272536469, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41272536469) on `fcd45` completed **FAILURE: 67 successful, 25 skipped, two failed jobs**. The [lint leaf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41272536469/job/124748705268) reported `eslint(curly)` at `repository-workspace-snapshot.test.ts:152`; the other failure was downstream `openclaw/ci-gate`. A bounded job-tail read recovered the diagnostic missing from the earlier cached log. This was PR-authored, not inherited or flaky.

The same maintained CI-mode lint owner and `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` reproduced the exact error **red**, then passed **green with zero warnings/errors** after adding braces. The condition and thrown error are identical; no assertion was weakened. Canonical format/whitespace and exact ratchet **6,368,190 ≤ 6,386,775** passed. The CI-failure planner found no Vitest failures to rerun. The 78-case runtime proof and complete source review below are reused only for unchanged behavior, not claimed as a fresh runtime execution. The pending auto-merge request was retired through native recovery before changing the head. **Current-head CI remains required; the failed run is retained, not rerun or waived.**

## Implementation Qualification

Native signed baseline `92aad389fbb6a3c2344848a80efaa7ecb3ccd820` has original hosted `0dd64a1064ea2eb0df0ff776517934abcc816e75` and actual main `c2a39e4c…` as parents. All new task commits verify signed and retain Galin credit; the hosted head remains an ancestor. Earlier unpublished preparation imported an unsigned prerequisite marker and was correctly refused before push. Its source/receipts remain preserved. The replacement preparation excludes that side ancestry without changing signature protection, using an unsigned override, rewriting hosted history or re-signing somebody else's commit.

- **78 tests passed in three complete files:** checkpoint 28, native capture 8, repository publication 42. Vitest **113.29s**, maintained wrapper **115.52s**; compiler verification and cleanup completed. Real environment service, private node transport, loopback WebSocket, native workspace, HTTP transfer and actual Git-input authority are exercised.
- **P2 red/green:** independent review found retained capture ignored aliases for requests queued after receipt binding failed. Real transport reproduced a missing alias (false versus true), not setup failure: 43.52s Vitest / 45.88s wrapper. Repair retains source and companion identities under the existing immutable-ref transaction. The regression denies revoked final-input publication, then proves allowed retry/later-request reuse of original bytes despite disk edits, without new node effects or SQLite acceptance. Initial repair: 36 cases/two files passed in 73.96s wrapper; final 78-case run covers the extracted owner and publication consumer.
- Production and Gateway test types passed, including 13,923 SDK declarations. Default three-production-file lint passed in 3.88s; canonical formatting and whitespace passed. That local lint scope omitted the newly changed test; the resulting hosted error is explicitly repaired above. An earlier incorrect formatter write/check combination was rejected, then corrected through the same maintained owner.
- Independent canonical **autoreview P0–P3** covered the full **34-path** implementation against current baseline plus six intact owner contexts: one completed **190,372-byte** pass, **scoped-clean, zero actionable findings**, final source verified. The earlier full review's P2 was repaired, not relabeled. The latest two-file brace-only correction was directly inspected; no additional model-review execution is claimed for it.
- Before the P2 repair, independent replay reproduced the qualified 32-path child patch exactly on actual main (stable patch `bc88dded7db43a74033a95d0b34201355ba81b61`). Native conflict resolutions preserve landed recovery and exact canonical generated blobs. Source equivalence is distinct from execution.

## Historical Evidence and Nonpasses

- Unpublished `33fd93f3…`: 56 cases/four files passed in 335.20s, static gates and complete 32-path P0–P3 review clean. `5eaea8e7…`: seven native capture cases passed in 73.38s with typing/ratchet/whitespace. Historical source-scoped evidence only.
- Published `0dd64a10…`: 79 refreshed I/O/context/startup cases passed; [CI 41198174787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41198174787) was green for that head. [Hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189263#issuecomment-6542320236) reported no findings/before-merge items; advisory only. Its 18 real capture/cleanup cases passed in 154.73s with static checks and independent review. Separate 431-line allocation accompanies the original 971-line allocation. Negative admission/final-input controls refuse effects while preserving cleanup; allowed control retains selected/alias refs and companions.
- Original `101f2bbf…`: 80 owner cases/four files passed (144.93s Vitest / 147.18s wrapper), plus 11 cleanup/recovery and 12 quiescence cases. Editor mirrored-acceptance and retry without remembered turn context were reproduced red, then repaired. Types, lint, format/line budgets/docs links/whitespace and final independent review passed.
- [CI 41190140140](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41190140140) failed in two leaves plus aggregate: two prepared-context expectations and one held-process rollback timing case, reproduced on child and prerequisite `06079b6e…`. Execution: 2 failed/27 passed; startup subsets: 1 failed/3 passed/8 unselected. No weakening, skipped failures, rerun or passing replay labeled a repair. Later upstream fixes and prior-head green remain separate evidence.

## Limits

Synthetic local production-path fixtures—not real cloud retention, live-model disk turns, authenticated remote GitHub publication or paused wake. Prerequisite `4484` installed-v38 stable-upgrade proof is complete in #189106: synthetic legacy rows in the genuine release, preserved NULL/mirrored semantics, cold serving identity/readiness and cleanup. It closes that prerequisite's old installed-upgrade gap only, not full disk-feature or later-package acceptance. Release, deployment and controller adoption holds remain.

title: fix(ui): keep Logs wheel scrolling from stopping short
body:
Related: #188945, #189016

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Logs wheel scrolling stopping before the newest entry when Auto-follow is off and wrapped rows finish measuring during the scroll.

## User Impact

Readers can wheel to the newest retained log entry while keeping Auto-follow disabled. Idle anchoring and enabled Auto-follow continue to compensate for row resizing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The virtualizer's implicit end anchor can write the scroll position even when its row-size adjustment predicate rejects compensation. The existing reader-scroll policy now suppresses both compensation paths during active travel and restores idle anchoring afterward.

## Evidence

Native Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24.22.1, Playwright 1.64.1, headless WebKit 27.2 / revision 2370; unchanged browser test and assertions, no retries or tolerance changes.

| Comparison | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original file alone | 3/20 desktop WebKit failures at :112 | 20/20 invocations, 60/60 cases pass |
| Historical failing CI order on base/candidate source | 20/20 Logs runs, 60/60 cases pass | 20/20 Logs runs, 60/60 cases pass |
| Focused run under three measured CPU burners | 1/20 desktop WebKit failure at :112 | 20/20 invocations, 60/60 cases pass |

The historical replay uses the original job's 137 file/project specifications with the canonical CI configuration and verifies exact dispatch order from worker-ID receipts. No checked-in runner changes. One baseline shard had an unrelated `chat-transcript-disclosure-anchor.e2e.test.ts:400` failure. One candidate run was recovered after a session interruption: all 137 module outcomes and Logs cases passed, with dispatch/source/cleanup verified, but its wrapper exit is unknown; the other 19 candidate shard exits were zero.

The added view regression fails on base (an active reader moves 94 px during row growth), passes with the fix, and checks idle compensation resumes. Related Logs tests: 29/29 pass. Production UI and UI-page test types, scoped lint (zero errors; four warnings), formatter parity, controller guard, and test-line ratchet pass without baseline changes.

Local and native WebKit bundle hashes and row metrics match. Retained traces show local scroll-event delivery during wheel travel coalesced to 48–56 ms, with compensation interrupting travel 323 px from the bottom; the native traced pass first compensates at the bottom. This supports timing/layout sensitivity, but the unique host-level cause of the rate gap remains unresolved; instrumentation passes are excluded.

Review: local autoreview (Codex), P0–P3, scoped-clean with no findings on `b513040e660678693cee8d6131f35b206f0df833..f546940f6451ff3fa7d0aa2fd5783314c42694b9`. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; hosted review will follow the repository review route.

title: fix(auto-reply): stop queued turns replaying completed replies
body:
Supersedes #127967, thanks @HermanZeng.

Related: #126813

## What Problem This Solves

Queued messages can prompt an agent to answer an earlier question again after its message-tool reply has already been delivered.

## User Impact

The next queued request receives the confirmed completion context while retaining its own question, including requests to repeat or discuss the prior answer. Queue ordering and delivery ownership are preserved. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The successful execution hands its completion fact directly to the next queued input in the same physical session and delivery route. That input already owns context through preparation retries and consumption, so no separate handoff registry or lifecycle protocol is needed.

Production delta is +32 lines: the new handoff needs a producer and route checks. Duplicate route-key assembly was removed from the queue owner and shared with its existing grouping logic; overflow idempotency bytes stay unchanged. Further deletions would remove unrelated behavior. Regression tests add 139 lines, with a separate exact allocation and no shared-ceiling increase.

## Evidence

- On main `14e3eeccf84af998d84827ea43a8f3184b1e439f`, the new queue regression reached A → B → C once each but failed because B lacked predecessor-completion context. With the fix it passed, checking fresh B/C prompts, one completion directive each, and no automatic redelivery (2.1s test, 47.7s wrapper including cold preparation).
- Queue scope and collect suites: 99 tests passed across two files (64.3s wrapper). The added route cases keep context off other channels, targets, accounts, threads, reply anchors, room events, and later queued inputs.
- The complete touched runner suite (198 tests) and prompt-prefix stability suite (14 tests) also passed (132.5s wrapper; runner tests 68.5s including existing fixtures).
- Targeted typecheck, production/test lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Broad proof belongs to PR CI.
- Autoreview: Codex P0–P2, candidate against `14e3eeccf84a`, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The committed code matches that reviewed candidate; the allocation was checked separately.
- This is queue/execution-boundary proof using synthetic embedded-run delivery results. It is not live Telegram or real-model behavior proof, and does not claim the model can never choose to repeat itself.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

title: fix(gateway): reject oversized requests without disconnecting
body:
Supersedes #123122, thanks @sunlit-deng.

## What Problem This Solves

Oversized SDK requests reach the Gateway WebSocket receiver and disconnect the client with a generic `gateway closed (1009)` error instead of rejecting the individual request.

## User Impact

SDK and Control UI callers receive a payload-limit error with the actual serialized UTF-8 size and limit, and can send a smaller request on the same connection. Existing browser draft/attachment recovery is preserved. No settings or server limits change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing browser admission check and typed error into the shared pending-request owner. Apply the advertised hello policy immediately before sending, and reuse the existing 64 KiB pre-auth constant before hello. Remove browser-only payload state and validation. Keep the shared constant in a dependency-free leaf included in the extracted maintainer-wrapper inventory.

Production delta: +31/-25, net +6 lines, versus +69 in the contributor review. The small remaining growth supplies shared pre-auth/reset state and the byte counts in the error. Packaging inventory: +1 line. Tests: +59 lines, allocated for two distinct transport/handshake regressions.

## Evidence

- Both added regressions fail against unchanged main `8b1efb47c13011a10765f264cf46b97e72c12e78`: the real WebSocket SDK test gets `gateway closed (1009): `; the shared handshake test sends the oversized connect without local rejection. Both pass with this fix.
- The real WebSocket test advertises/enforces 8,192 bytes, rejects a multibyte oversized request locally, then completes `health` on the same socket with no close and no rejected request received.
- 295 focused tests across ten files pass: SDK handshake/request/held-request/pending lifecycle, browser Gateway/socket boundaries (including exact UTF-8 limits), chat send, and session startup. Commands complete in under 12 seconds each; [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41187700847) passed (1,414 seconds elapsed).

title: fix(feishu): show preview covers on outgoing videos
body:
Supersedes #98458, thanks @areslp.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes outgoing Feishu videos appearing with an empty preview.

## User Impact

Videos display a preview frame when cover preparation succeeds. If ffmpeg is unavailable or cover extraction/upload fails, the video arrives as a file attachment. No new dependency or configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [Feishu media contract](https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/im-v1/message-content-description/create_json?lang=zh-CN) documents `image_key` as optional and explicitly says omitting it leaves no cover. Main sent only `file_key`.

This replacement uses the existing ffmpeg runtime, bounded to five seconds and 1280×720, and shares the existing image/file upload validation. Cover upload has a five-second deadline and honors the smaller of the account limit and Feishu's 10 MiB image limit. Direct and thread delivery continue through the shared sender with current send authority.

The production delta is +75 lines for bounded extraction and fallback, with the existing upload closure reused instead of adding a second uploader. Regression tests add 81 lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/feishu-video-covers.txt` to protect cover forwarding, file fallback, timeout, and authority after extraction.

## Evidence

- Base `8b1efb47c130`: six expected regression failures (missing cover keys in direct/thread messages and missing file fallback); 21 existing tests passed.
- Replacement: 29 media tests and 29 real-transport send-authority tests passed. Media file: 10.09 seconds wall time, test bodies under one second; both focused shards: 39.11 seconds. The [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41187177230) passed; its changed-test job took 283 seconds including setup (individual file timing is not separately published).
- Scoped production/test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview on the complete local candidate against `8b1efb47c130`, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Unchanged helper implementations were outside its supplied diff; those owners were inspected separately.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff` only; it was never checked out or executed. This is a fresh implementation from main. Human commit-author credit is preserved for luopei and areslp.
- The attached sanitized screenshot is historical live proof supplied by @areslp: the upper video lacks a cover and the lower video displays an extracted frame. It was inspected and also shown in the task chat. No fresh live Feishu send was performed for this replacement; the current wiring is covered by regressions.

title: revert(doctor): restore damaged-state repair admission
body:
Related: #189025, #189039, #189050.

## What Problem This Solves

Reverts #189025 (`4872133405c`) because mandatory pre-repair capture prevents Doctor from repairing supported damaged state, a production defect exposed in large-14, and caused schema-preflight failures in large-19 on [main full CI 41172573619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619).

## User Impact

Doctor can reach its existing damaged-state repair owners again. Standalone original-state capture failures become advisory again; repair-specific backups and integrity checks still apply. Healthy repeated runs also avoid an empty cold-navigation maintenance lease that changed state bytes and prevented capture reuse.

The stalled-inventory cancellation from #189025 is rolled back and needs a fresh forward fix. This revert also rolls back its relaxed foreign-key original-image support; it does not implement mandatory preservation of malformed originals.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary schema admission rejects the supported legacy Workshop index before mandatory capture can finish, blocking the repair that owns that damage. A complete original-preserving forward fix needs independently verified private normalization; a partial capture exemption would not safely restore that contract. This change therefore applies the exact inverse of #189025.

Prerequisite `b11052f9534` avoids leasing an explicitly empty cold-navigation target list. It overlaps Peter's #189039 and open #189050 and is included only as the revert's prerequisite: the revert alone leaves healthy capture-repeat behavior broken. Both were open at the initial fresh-main/PR check; #189039 merged while this PR was being prepared. Those changes address later archive budgeting and projection performance, not the refusing capture boundary, and main still lacks the empty-target return.

## Evidence

- Original failing jobs: [large-14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619/job/124453674872) and [large-19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619/job/124453674979). After disposable installation setup, the real Doctor entry point reproduces the malformed-schema refusal before repair; unchanged required tests pass with this candidate.
- **242 tests passed across 17 files**: 19 required regression cases, 189 affected sibling cases, and 34 direct inventory/rehearsal consumer cases. Covers real Doctor repair, capture reuse, schema refusal, retained data, settlement, backup integrity, and inventory boundaries.
- Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, format, diff checks, and docs link audit passed.

body:
Supersedes #133376, thanks @ericcaiwx-star.

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode agents can read an installed skill's instructions but cannot read the companion references those instructions require.

## User Impact

Eligible local Gateway skills can expose their bundled text references through `skills_read({ name, relativePath })` or `skills.read(name, relativePath)`. Existing skill-read grants now cover files in that skill directory. Sandbox, remote workspace, node-hosted, and required-workspace placements remain instruction-only. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing installed-skill reader and worker bridge with one optional relative path. Current main's one-argument reader still ignores companion requests despite instructing agents to resolve relative resources beside SKILL.md. This is an independently implemented, credited replacement; the contributor's source was read with GitHub CLI and never checked out or executed.

title: fix(agents): fail stalled provider authentication at the run deadline
body:
Supersedes #93952, thanks @amittell.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent runs that hang indefinitely when provider credential lookup or a runtime token exchange never returns.

## User Impact

Authentication stops at the existing run deadline or cancellation with an error naming the provider and auth step and suggesting a retry. Run deadline and cancellation errors cannot fall through to AWS sentinel handling or further auth attempts. Provider-originated abort errors retain their existing recovery before run expiry. No new settings or credential storage are introduced.

Exchange hooks receive an optional cancellation signal and should pass it to their transport. JavaScript cannot forcibly stop a plugin that ignores cancellation; its late result is still rejected before credential installation. Claimed durable OAuth refreshes retain their existing settlement owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth controller shares one startup budget across lookup and exchange, then consumes the existing execution owner's published deadline, respecting paused or unlimited execution when an auth step starts. An already-running exchange keeps the deadline captured at entry; later deadline extensions do not rearm its timeout. Request-time OAuth lookup and exchange use the same bound and request cancellation. Final teardown cancels auth; temporary cleanup for forwarded harness candidates keeps later API-key candidates usable.

The simplification pass removed the duplicate unavailable-reason adapter and a redundant missing-state check. Production growth is +126 net lines: the shared deadline/cancellation helper, execution-deadline projection and wiring, request-time propagation, and abort/error boundaries are required to close the complete flow. Existing parameter types moved to the existing type module to keep the controller within its file limit. No test-routing registry changed. The separate 159-line allocation covers only this change's regression growth.

## Evidence

- Baseline `e1cd21501dd59366fefc3ff8263d97eeacdc799e`: focused negative control failed 4 of 5 selected cases. Hung lookup, hung exchange and AWS exchange remained pending at 100 ms; cancellation incorrectly installed credentials. Slow success passed.
- Replacement: all 88 focused tests passed across `auth-controller.test.ts`, `auth-controller.binding.test.ts`, `auth-controller.request-auth.test.ts`, and `provider-runtime-auth.test.ts` (70.48 s including compiled-worker preparation). New coverage includes slow success, one shared budget, request-time lookup/exchange deadlines, request-specific cancellation, late-result rejection, and forwarded harness candidate transitions, and provider-originated abort recovery. Existing durable OAuth settlement and account-authority tests pass.
- The initial CI run identified four test cleanup callbacks returning Vitest utilities instead of `void`; the correction uses block bodies. Both affected files pass again: 52 tests in 19.81 s. The correction commit also has a clean P0–P2 autoreview; production source was unchanged by that cleanup correction. The final auth-signal simplification and added provider-abort regression were then validated by the complete 88-test run and a fresh full-candidate P0–P2 security review. Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad build/typecheck/test proof is delegated to this PR's CI; no broad suite ran on the production host.
- Security-focused autoreview of the complete local candidate against the baseline above, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`. Fixed its findings about reset budgets, request-time lookup/cancellation, and temporary harness transitions. No provider or review configuration changed.
- Contributor source was read only with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. The contributor's Gateway traces support the original diagnosis, but no new Gateway or external-provider proof is claimed for this replacement. The Team Gateway was not modified or restarted.

Contributor credit: Alex Mittell <mittell@me.com>, with `Co-authored-by: Alex Mittell <mittell@me.com>` on the replacement commit.

title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command and URL configuration writes
body:
Supersedes #122348, thanks @ooiuuii.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can silently run a local MCP command when the same server definition also specifies a remote URL.

## User Impact

Explicit config validation and new or edited MCP writes reject mixed definitions with the server path and both field names. Existing definitions retain their runtime behavior with a warning. Doctor explains the two explicit repairs while retaining transport and authentication choices. Updates and incremental MCP repairs can preserve other unchanged legacy entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP normalizer owns the shared diagnostic, consumed by strict validation and warning-only reads. Writers compare unchanged legacy definitions against their captured source snapshot before runtime path expansion, including equivalent existing alias normalization. The repaired candidate is fully validated separately; an unrelated invalid legacy entry does not discard the per-server baseline. Doctor keeps its existing migrations and leaves the transport choice to the operator: automatic removal of HTTP/auth fields could enable local commands that node-host or native Codex previously refused. No settings were added.

Doctor and compatibility comparisons now use one retired-key normalizer, removing duplicate migration transforms, separate traversal wrappers, and an iterator. Alias repair on the mixed server itself preserves disabled semantics, timeout units, and canonical precedence. Production delta is +13 lines versus +93 in the original proposal; the remaining growth implements validation and compatible writes. Tests add 240 lines with a matching allocation for the distinct config, update, incremental-repair, and real MCP process boundaries.

## Evidence

- Main baseline `d13bd0f6067d878a4ced96272e20dc1e13c3cebf`: five final regression cases fail because both CLI scopes accept ambiguity and runtime/Doctor warnings are absent. A real baseline probe also confirms embedded stdio registration while the URL remains configured. The incremental-repair regression additionally failed on the initial candidate and passes after propagating the original snapshot baseline.
- Final focused proof: 48/48 pass across config CLI/I/O, MCP mutations, async validation, existing Doctor migrations, and persisted MCP integration. Wrapper wall time: 41.14 seconds including native worker preparation. The two hosted P1 findings reproduced as four failing cases before the source-baseline correction: tilde path expansion blocked update/MCP writes, and unrelated legacy disabled flags blocked Doctor in both roots. All now pass. Same-entry disabled/timeout aliases also failed in both scopes before sharing the migration normalizer and now have regression coverage. An additional strict core-only snapshot regression failed before its two-line orchestration correction and now passes without plugin metadata. Focused type checking and type-aware lint pass. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41179206195) and the required aggregate gate passed; final checks report 67 passed, 56 intentionally skipped, zero failed.
- The persisted proof covers both roots, backup and idempotent alias normalization, retained URL/auth/OAuth/TLS options, then an explicit stdio replacement followed by a real child process and published tool. All four requester-marked cases (both roots, auth present or missing) reject before process I/O. The real update-channel writer and incremental MCP mutation facade are exercised, including rejection of new/edited mixed definitions.
- Isolated upgrade proof: actual npm `v2026.10.9` created config and SQLite state and started successfully, then exact reviewed candidate `0a5895d852ea00abda666bd47b630b13b4cc1001` passed strict rejection, Doctor preservation/warnings, actual update-channel persistence and backup, sibling and same-entry alias repair, and repeat-Doctor byte identity. ## What Problem This Solves

Repository recovery needs to remember which exact retained disk owns accepted work, rather than treating an older Gateway mirror as the latest workspace after a restart.

Prerequisite #189019 is merged as `ff3ab23502010d1437c4afa5d7657a6d5e23111a`. GitHub subsequently retargeted this PR to `main`; the history-preserving integration retains the original 66-file authority/recovery child scope.

## User Impact

No disk-mode selector is enabled. Mirrored sessions keep their existing behavior. This is an inactive implementation prerequisite, not delivery of retained-disk workspaces.

Shared-state schema v38 adds nullable repository and pending-result authority fields after v37. Existing pending results remain mirrored, optional repository storage stays lazy, and older binaries refuse the upgraded schema. Rollback uses the existing exact predecessor backup.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing repository owner binds one immutable environment/resource receipt. The existing pending-result owner records that authority when accepting custody; retries never infer it from a replacement environment.

Fixes dead air when an automatic Voice Call response fails, times out, or produces no usable output.

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic profiles flatten first-party fs-safe frames to package labels, hiding the write and staging functions needed to investigate recurring Gateway stalls.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared CPU/heap/stall frame sanitizer, retaining the existing bounded symbol validation and package classification. No sampling, event-loop-health exclusion, or write behavior changes.

The requested call-site attribution is deferred under the authorized fallback: fs-safe 0.27.0 exposes `Root.write/create` and `stageFileInDirectory`, but `runPinnedWriteNative` and `NativeStagedFile` are internal. Root/parent admission awaits occur before `#prepare` calls synchronous `binding.createStagedFile`; an application wrapper would return its promise before this segment. OpenClaw has no `stageFileInDirectory` callers. Correct attribution needs a package-owned synchronous-segment hook carrying a fixed application owner label, then an application adapter to `runWithMainThreadTask`; it cannot be supplied by wrapping the existing asynchronous API alone.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on base: expected `runPinnedWriteNative`, received `[dep:@openclaw/fs-safe]`; passes with the fix. The same table covers private methods, invalid first-party symbols, third-party redaction, scoped/pnpm layouts, and hidden paths.

title: fix: managed updates refuse a valid runtime after Homebrew Node changes
body:
Fixes #189048
Related #188829

## What Problem This Solves

Managed updates can refuse a compatible Gateway after a Homebrew runtime path changes: the early engine check prevents an existing runtime fallback and omits the inspected Gateway install root from its diagnostic.

## User Impact

A compatible managed service Node takes priority over an incompatible PATH Node. An owned writable service can switch to a compatible existing updater or safely discovered runtime when the update will refresh its definition. Protected definitions and `--no-restart` retain their pins. Refusals identify the service/updater runtimes, PATH executable, target engines, and Gateway root.

Engines and later capability/identity checks remain enforced. This repair belongs to the installed updater. A refusing 2026.10.7 driver needs the documented [manual package-manager hop](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating/update-methods#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) to a release containing it, or a compatible service runtime selected by its deployment owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing service observation into early preflight and retain its selected runtime through staging and activation. Execution and preview both use the inherited runtime-recovery environment snapshot, falling back to the explicit native definition environment when unavailable.

pr-simplify removed custom PATH probing in favor of the existing guarded discovery owner. Early admission cannot provision a runtime; diagnostics never execute an additional PATH binary merely for guidance. The production delta is +52 lines; the separate +230 net test-line allocation covers selection, negative controls, guarded execution, preview, and activation. No shared baseline change.

## Evidence

- RED on pinned main `4d76d1d82f705391c461268a5d6b8190b889066b`: incompatible service 26.8.2 incorrectly refuses valid updater 24.22.1; both-old refusal incorrectly reports an unresolved Gateway root. - Review corrections were RED on `726c98337e6`: two real relative-PATH executable sentinels ran, and dry-run incorrectly refused an available compatible third runtime. Final guarded discovery passes all 68 existing owner tests; the final entry-point/preview pair passes all 25 tests in 60.65 s. The both-old control still refuses before staging or service stop.
- The complete CLI-update TypeScript leaf, targeted canonical oxlint (0 warnings/errors), formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview r5 is scoped-clean for the complete final candidate; no subsequent source changes. Final head: `8917aaaaf78fecf00caab2d476fd1dc4b6bc30a5`. title: fix(gateway): reject session invitations to invalid human identities
body:
Supersedes #134006, thanks @linhongyu510.
Closes #133956

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful but ineffective session invitations when historical human creators are channel handles or no longer identify a current Gateway profile.

## User Impact

Owners can invite current profiles, including people without sessions, while invalid human candidates fail with `unknown identity` without a membership write. Existing orphan rows remain visible and removable. Existing owner access, agent/system candidates, and role-based access rules are preserved. No settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing current-profile directory and authenticated caller as the human candidate sources in the shared picker/admission builder. Stop deriving human admission from historical session creators, whose projection has already discarded provenance. This covers durable and memory-only incognito creators without adding source filters at three indexing paths.

| Member candidate | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current profile, including a sessionless profile | Admit | Admit |
| Authenticated caller / owner | Admit | Admit; ownership authorization unchanged |
| Agent or system creator in the selected projection | Admit | Admit |
| Historical human creator with no current profile: channel, unknown, or orphan profile provenance | Admit | Reject |
| Arbitrary unknown ID absent from all candidate sources | Reject | Reject |
| Persisted orphan member, with no valid candidate source | List/remove; no admission solely from membership | Same; listing is cleanup evidence, never admission authority |

Security review: current-main reproduction demonstrates invalid membership admission and persistence, not an authentication or visibility bypass. Viewer membership still matches a verified profile ID and remains subject to role/visibility policy. Historical human provenance now cannot manufacture a candidate; current profile display facts remain authoritative. Human IDs matching a real current profile remain valid through that directory. Production delta is **-1 line** by removing the redundant historical-human candidate path; no unrelated cleanup.

## Evidence

- Base: `5388ada4c289a9298833ae1019652da8244e2d68` (current main at investigation).
- Red before: the handler/storage regression failed on unchanged main; all six historical human candidates (channel/unknown/profile provenance, each durable/incognito) were listed and successfully persisted. The arbitrary unknown-ID negative control was already rejected.
- Green after: 48 tests across seven focused files (sharing handlers, identity builder, profile display, sharing worker mutations, creator namespaces, and picker invalidation). The final touched suite passed 13/13 in 19.52s wall time (16.67s Vitest duration); CI `checks-node-changed` succeeded in 285 job-seconds (setup and other selected files included; no separate per-file CI timing). [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41170570883) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Targeted TypeScript, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- The regression also checks sessionless profile, owner, agent/system additions and removals, actual member mutation access, and list/remove cleanup without re-admission of a historical orphan.
- Local Codex autoreview, P0–P3 security-focused coverage of the complete local diff and owning source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Final local snapshot includes all three intended files; review completed after the fixture and allocation changes.
- Simplification: one candidate builder owns the decision; the raw creator projection is unchanged, and no provenance-recovery helper, index policy, new settings, or state is introduced.
- Test-line allocation is limited to this regression and the corrected valid-profile fixture; it protects admission, persistence, supported identities and historical cleanup in the existing handler suite.

title: fix: cancel usage pricing preparation when the Gateway stops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway shutdown can hang on usage backfill while catalog pricing preparation is pending.

## User Impact

Stopping the usage sidecar now cancels its pricing wait and releases its refresh lock. Committed cost-cache rows remain intact; unfinished refresh work is rebuilt on the next startup. No configuration, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidecar already aborts its work scope, but `prepareUsageCostPricing` awaited catalog preparation without observing that signal. The worker runtime holds its refresh lock across this await. Race this optional preparation against the existing scope signal, retaining the existing joins for native workers and admitted cache writes. Shared catalog preparation may finish independently; the cancelled refresh cannot continue to scan or write.

The incident journal identifies the usage sidecar as the only pending named owner at the 82-second shutdown deadline, but cannot identify its inner await. This regression proves a remaining cancellation hole after #187877; it does not establish that every production SIGKILL has this cause. Earlier stops with no pending close steps also recorded service-child cleanup failures, which need separate investigation.

title: fix(doctor): abort stalled recovery inventories and restore service
body:
Related #187900 #178359

## What Problem This Solves

Standalone `doctor --fix` can leave its managed Gateway stopped while waiting forever for a plugin's pre-repair backup inventory.

## User Impact

A stalled read-only inventory now observes the existing ten-minute capture deadline. If the original-state capture fails, standalone Doctor refuses repair and restores the service it stopped, including suspended Windows task autostart, with backup and retry guidance. Fast preparation and the update driver's existing optional-capture policy are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture timer previously only aborted a signal: plugin inventory did not observe it, and fresh shared-state snapshot preparation did not receive it. Capture failures also returned warnings that allowed standalone repair to proceed. This change propagates cancellation through fresh and reused inventories, keeps the deadline alive while waiting, and refuses unbacked standalone repair. Only the contractually read-only inventory callback is raced; admitted native capture work still settles before service restoration.

Mandatory capture also needs to preserve the orphan rows Doctor is supposed to repair. Under existing exclusive custody of a closed, checkpointed SQLite source, ordinary original capture now uses the existing private raw-copy producer and retains foreign-key findings with a warning. Physical quick checks still refuse corruption; explicit full verification, generic rollback, and durable journal/WAL acquisition retain strict checks. These original images carry no clean generation receipt or automatic restoration authority.

The reported Windows native stack remains unknown. Source also corrects the report's bracket: task suspension happens during stop preparation; `beginMutation()` only disables early recovery. The disabled task therefore does not independently prove that `prepareRepair()` had started. This PR fixes a deterministic never-settling inventory path, without claiming to fix synchronous or unkillable kernel I/O stalls.

## Evidence

- RED on the original owners: inventory cancellation never settles; managed preparation hangs on timeout and permits repair after capture failure. The fast control passes.
- GREEN: focused regression proves timeout/failure refuse preparation, restore task autostart, restart the fake managed service, and verify health; fast preparation remains successful. Late inventory results cannot admit later resources.
- Landlock + Bubblewrap host-contained production `prepareRepair()` proof: a 33,607,680-byte synthetic agent database and all 13 declared plugin payloads were captured, sealed, and verified in 9.665 s of test time (49.90 s wrapper including cold test compilation). No live Gateway, service units, containers, or operator state were used.
- 135 unique focused tests pass across the changed owners and affected siblings. The corrected backup owner passes 37/37 (86.18 s wrapper); all 15 schema-flow consumer cases pass and verify that original capture retains the damaged rows; reuse passes 9/9 (93.29 s wrapper), including native cancellation settlement. Targeted noEmit types, formatting, and diff checks pass. Targeted lint passed before the final malformed-callback guard and archive correction; exact-head CI supplies final broad lint/build proof. No full local product build or published-driver upgrade was run; the earlier lint wrapper automatically prepared SDK declarations.
- First-head CI run 41167390016 exposed four schema-flow failures caused by this PR's mandatory capture. The correction identifies the installation in those standalone fixtures and preserves relational evidence before repair; physical corruption still fails capture. The next head exposed only a fixture `prefer-array-find` lint error; its one-line correction passes the four affected schema cases (71.76 s wrapper) and an independent Codex P0–P2 delta review. Final-head CI results are recorded below.
- Fresh independent shared autoreview, Codex P0–P2, complete staged candidate against `c993c8f2a51a`: scoped-clean, zero findings (final source verification complete). The index-only orphan-repair finding from the preceding review was addressed by staging the correction with the refusal. The subsequent fixture-only lint correction also passed independent Codex P0–P2 review. Platform-specific native stalls were not reproduced by review.
- Simplification: existing cancellation, snapshot, and recovery owners; no new manager, schema, or public configuration. Production growth +64 lines; net regression growth +216 lines, exactly allocated for inventory cancellation/late results, managed-service failure/fast controls, and original-image integrity. The growth in the backup owner is needed to preserve damaged original data while refusing unsafe repair.

title: feat(workers): bind cleanup to recorded cloud resources
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Cloud worker recovery and cleanup need a durable binding to the original provider resource, rather than relying only on a reusable lease handle after a lost reply or restart.

Original work and design by @galiniliev; extracted and reimplemented at the contributor's request.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9e5ce302-c947-42c1-9be1-a5254aa17cf2)

## User Impact

New Crabbox Azure Sandbox workers record exact resource identity before setup/enrollment. Restart recovery refuses replacement identities, unavailable observations preserve ownership, and Stop remains pending until exact-resource deletion is confirmed.

**This is a prerequisite, not retained-disk activation.** Gateway checkpoints, existing idle suspension, and workspace authority remain unchanged. It enables neither retained allocation nor pause/resume nor disk-authoritative workspaces. Legacy environments without receipts keep their fixed-lease cleanup contract and are not silently rebound. Dependent lifecycle implementation is separately published in #189346, above authority #189106.

Shared-state schema **36 → 37** preserves old rows with a null receipt and fences older binaries. Rollback requires settling new environments and pending cleanup, then restoring the matching pre-upgrade backup with its binary; a package-only downgrade is unsafe. PostgreSQL migration and generated predecessor descriptors are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional generic provider receipt contract feeds the existing environment writer, provisioning, inspection, and teardown owners. Crabbox alone interprets Azure-specific identity and CLI flags. Receipt custody commits before subsequent setup effects; retries retain the original allocation and immutable identity. No separate manager, timer, queue, or state file is introduced. SSH bootstrap and Crabbox teardown phases are extracted without changing ownership to keep modules bounded. The **781-line** regression allocation is task-specific; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Initial provider/recovery proof: **56 tests across 5 files**; real-worker store/migration proof: **10 tests**, repeated after main integration. Existing store/projection coverage also passed 25 cases.
- CI repairs fixed receipt-column omissions, PostgreSQL physical column ordering, enrollment/teardown owner handling, predecessor schema composition, optional-fragment foreign keys in historical fixtures, and confirmed teardown settlement during Gateway drain.
- Repair proof included **110 placement/provisioning consumer tests across 6 files**, **13 tooling tests**, **24 lifecycle tests**, and **29 migration/descriptor/provider tests**.
- Later qualified **37 real PostgreSQL integration tests across 2 files** on CI's pinned pgvector image with its extensions and lock setting. This supersedes the earlier skipped PostgreSQL execution. The task container was stopped and reconciled absent.
- **37 migration/credential/cleanup consumer tests across 6 files**, **2 strengthened drain tests**, and **18 affected receipt/image-intent/drain/migration tests across 4 files** passed. Ten unchanged Doctor tests also passed locally; that replay alone was not claimed as a repair of the earlier merge-only failure.
- Targeted production/test typing, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generation, native schema parity, regression-budget/line-cap checks, and pre-commit passed. Initial committed SDK comparison acknowledgment: **4a99ee35**.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 autoreview covered the original change and subsequent repairs, with source verification and no remaining actionable findings. Generated catalog review was partition-limited; regeneration, complete schema-owner context, and migration tests provide cross-catalog evidence.
- A local fixture CLI exercised the actual stop boundary: baseline deleted a simulated replacement; the fixed implementation refused the replacement and preserved it.

## Current conflict repair and CI

Published head: **f4255b1d506b4bbe135f05c93ede950632172d06**; tested tree: **17b921cb2e20123acfc0fb2a6e430d0fdd728923**. The publisher's attributed marker commit preserves that complete tested tree.

History-preserving main integration at **ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff** resolved the sole conflict by regenerating the canonical SQLite catalog. Shared-state remains37; authority38 and retained lifecycle39 are excluded. Hosted readback confirms the conflict is cleared, with this PR still open and unmerged.

On the merged source:
- Canonical schema generation/verification and Kysely freshness passed; generator and catalog-equivalence suites passed.
- Receipt store/migration/provider boundary: **15 tests across three files passed**. Crabbox receipt/stop siblings: **14 tests across two files passed**.
- **56 update tests across four files passed**, including the previously failing Node-prefix, incompatible-service-runtime, writable-launcher, and target-schema cases. Main already contains owner fixture repair **20ab8ecd0dacb1e** (#189226); this PR does not independently weaken those assertions. The old candidate-admission suite was reorganized upstream and was not separately selected in this focused replay.
- Script typing and whitespace checks passed. Simplification retained the existing design; no new production mechanism was needed for the merge.
- Fresh three-pass P0–P3 autoreview against ef60dd054 completed. One reported Azure stop-recovery finding was rejected after source verification: receipts are produced/parsed only for azure-sandbox, and provisioning/destruction reject a differing provider before stop, so the azure-only legacy recovery branch cannot receive a valid receipt. Generated-catalog review remains partition-limited, covered by canonical regeneration and equivalence tests.

Current-head [CI run 41208499615](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41208499615), attempt1, completed **failed: 152 passed, 2 failed, 19 skipped**. All update-runtime shards, types/lint, all PostgreSQL shards, and iOS evidence passed. One memory-core assertion failed; the second failure is the aggregate gate. The executed synthetic merge was f37eefb03c0a51b459e1c59acda6799458005a91 (base88b56eea, headf4255b1d). Complete attached-check inventory at finalization: **186 success, 44 skipped, 3 failure, 1 neutral; none pending**. The third attached failure is the separate protected aggregate [publisher 41210377330](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210377330), not another product-test failure.

The remaining failure is manager-publication-admission.test.ts:349, expecting a parent-process PRAGMA integrity_check observation after an unclean reopen. Its test and observer helper are unchanged from main; the admission owner blob is identical at pinned ef60dd054, CI base88b56eea, and this head. Upstream84bfd8a4 (#189247) moved required scans into the integrity worker and changed lease-less unclean reopening to bounded admission. This is a source-attributed inherited assertion mismatch, not an observed exact-base replay. A focused local attempt timed out during runtime compilation before a test verdict; no assertion or safety guard was weakened. Failed CI is retained. The finalizer fetched the actual executed merge object, reproduced its tree from ordered base/head parents, and verified all ten determining sources are identical at the actual CI baseline, tested merge and PR head.
