## Exact installed-upgrade qualification

Native [run 41243053820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41243053820) passed the installed receipt cell in **282.359s**, command/wrapper exit 0 and settled. Actual installed **and serving** identities changed from published stable `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` to exact candidate `f4255b1d506b4bbe135f05c93ede950632172d06`; the assertion checks build IDs, not the equal version label. Candidate package SHA256: `4ac4bad3141cfa0b2c8aed2953d2f667a1e9297b928c479ef9c560913f067971`, from Package Acceptance 41236419893. Durable update `53387e26-d48b-40c9-8063-8b4321ba26b6` succeeded and finished.

- Existing SQLite/session invariants and a valid synthetic legacy failed/no-lease environment row survived update, stop and repeated maintenance, including Unicode/NUL data. The new receipt column is nullable TEXT/default NULL; no legacy identity was fabricated.
- A synthetic installed provider exercised the **real core receipt callback and writer** through public `environments.create`: identical replay succeeded, changed identity produced the specific `resource receipt is immutable` refusal, and the receipt persisted before an intentional provisioning error.
- Public destroy received the exact recorded receipt. A real service stop/start with PID replacement, public status and store reads preserved it; same-key terminal replay made no second provision. Observed: one provision, one exact destruction. No live cloud resource was allocated.
- Public scoped-backup recovery migrated an agent fixture 39→26 while preserving two outbox rows and an unrelated later write. This is **agent-scoped recovery**, not shared receipt-table rollback or retained-disk restore; shared-state migration/rollback coverage remains the separately recorded owner tests.
- Final service stop succeeded; Docker inventories had no added containers/volumes; independent native lease status was completed/no host. The finalizer verified all 13 supplied evidence-file hashes and reconstructed the exact executed driver from hash-verified stock tooling plus its bounded fixture patch. No product/candidate files or runtime safeguards were patched. Earlier setup/fixture failures remain non-passes.

## Remaining qualification gaps

No live provider allocation, authenticated controller readiness, or real-model disk-mode Gateway flow is claimed. The earlier isolated wire-E2E runner refused preparation because separation from managed Gateway artifacts could not be verified; no guard was bypassed. Crabbox 0.80.0 capability/help/source inspection is protocol evidence, not cold-boot reconnect or release-readiness proof. Exact f425 installed receipt qualification above does not automatically qualify later S5–S9 behavior, retained-disk activation, or controller release/adoption.

title: fix(cron): bound runs before runner startup and retain cancellation
body:
Related: #143624, #123419. Adjacent watchdog work: #184460 and #160804.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation can remain running indefinitely when its runner never reports startup, and disabling it can fail to cancel after run tracking is retired.

## User Impact

Finite automation deadlines now cover admission, setup, execution, and delivery. Disabling an active occurrence still cancels its exact runner after registry retirement, allowing another forced run after settlement. Busy-session waits now consume the configured job budget; unlimited jobs remain unlimited. Existing live-work and receipt fences remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferred watchdog previously armed only its setup timer, which lane waiting clears; the wall-clock timer started only at `noteRunnerStarted`. Start that timer at entry instead. Bind marker cancellation directly to its captured handle rather than looking it up in a registry that teardown can clear. This removes the superseded lookup helper and introduces no new state or options.

A reported shared-session automation remained running past its 1700-second deadline after a Code Mode bridge error, with no active agent run or terminal cron record. The journal confirms that sequence, but does not establish where its agent promise stopped. The bridge catch already settles its failed reply; this repair targets the independently reproduced cron timeout and cancellation gaps rather than changing recoverable tool-error semantics.

## Evidence

- Base: `298546d88934bf05bc7e208d13bf6ce2c538e3f2`. Real cron timer/runner owners with held external runners: both no-start cases fail on base because no `TimeoutError` is raised; durable-disable-after-retirement fails because its controller remains un-aborted. Both pass after the fix, with terminal `timed_out` history, cleared `runningAtMs`, and successful forced re-admission after settlement.
- 43 tests pass, each run separately with `timeout 150`, an explicit `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

  - `session-run.test.ts`: 14 tests, 8.27 s.

- Touched-file core type-aware lint (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The initial lint invocation using `tsconfig.core.json` failed during unrelated plugin declaration preparation: installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` declarations lack `DirectoryMode` and reject string `dirMode`. The supported core-lint configuration avoids that package-boundary preparation. Full typecheck and broad proof are delegated to PR CI under the host IO emergency; no dependencies, operator state, or Gateway were changed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against the base, with active-marker owner context: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the existing hosted ClawSweeper request was queued, so no duplicate request was posted.

title: fix(workers): recover cloud sessions after their node process exits
body:
Related: #188796 ## What Problem This Solves An attached cloud session can wait for a reconnect that cannot happen after its enrolled node process exits, even though the dedicated worker and workspace still exist. Retained-worker wake can reach the same dead end before ordinary runtime recovery runs. ## User Impact Recover the same enrolled node on eligible dedicated Linux Crabbox workers without allocating a replacement, reinstalling the runtime, pairing again, rerunning repository setup or replaying interrupted input. Preserve the resource binding, identity, configuration and workspace. Unsupported providers, desktop workers and records without saved runtime identity retain reconnect-only behavior; older runtime packages without the private consumer need an update or manual recovery. Adopt released [Crabbox v0.81.0](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.81.0) through the canonical managed-distribution owner. It contains the landed native command-lifetime repair in [Crabbox #3001](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3001). Existing configured distributions are not overwritten. No new public timeout/configuration, schema, retention policy, paid allocation or live deployment. ## Why This Change Was Made - Add an optional provider recovery operation under the existing runtime-refresh owner. Current requester/attachment/owner authority, an active dedicated inspection and the exact persisted resource receipt must qualify launch. - Retained wake already holds the environment operation lock. It calls the same internal resumer before waiting for reconnect, without reacquiring that lock or creating a second lifecycle owner. Current main's retention, prepared-intent, lease-inspection and bootstrap owners remain intact. - Compose two ordinary existing Crabbox invocations: read-only saved identity/runtime inspection, fresh host authority assertion, then separately admitted launch. Launch repeats package/PID checks; the canonical runner verifies the saved device, configuration and paired credential. - Private launcher IPC prevents an uncommitted detached child from entering the node runtime after its owner disappears. Publish the PID receipt atomically before commitment and wait for actual child exit on precommit cancellation. Retain an uncertain committed process/receipt for a subsequent probe rather than blindly replaying it. - Use one measured private 120-second work budget across both phases, still bounded by caller admission. Forward the existing cleanup-grace option with 20 seconds for this operation so the controller can finish its existing 15-second cleanup and full 5-second native TERM grace. No new public Crabbox command protocol, identity reader or core manager. ## Evidence ### Source and focused regression coverage Qualified local commit 4a9976e91405f709f96c085ecb933efa8658ba15, tree ac40b5077f476fa38e29d8f561ac5252144dfc9e, integrated with pinned main b2ceef2b5a5fbd8c88ff8497b8a986c692204141 because the published branch conflicted. All 16 production modules match the source-bound released-runtime proof. - Exercised all 11 affected/helper test files across their six owning shards (261 cases in the initial cohort). Preserved failures rather than treating them as flakes: an obsolete offline-cache version, an invalid dormant inspection fixture, an incorrect seeded-credential assumption and unread stderr in the launcher disconnect fixture. - Final complete retained-lifecycle and managed-binary suites: **10 + 33 passed**. Both launcher commit/disconnect cases pass with normal stderr draining and unchanged timeout/assertions. Unmodified passing cases were reused; exact published-head CI is separate evidence. - **Owning-boundary RED control:** both new retained service regressions fail with the exact pre-fix retained owner from pinned main: no restart before reconnect wait, and a replacement resource is not rejected. The qualified owner was restored byte-for-byte; both cases pass with the fix. This is an exact owning-module control within the integration, not a claim that the entire base checkout was tested. - Targeted TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line gates pass. Allocation is exactly **828** net regression lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. - Fresh independent production and final regression reviews found no actionable P0–P3 issues. Committed-range autoreview is **scoped-clean**, with no findings. Its static-review limits do not replace executed runtime proof or CI. ### Actual released controller/native runtime Canonical installation and resolution selected the released distribution with normal adjacent-pack discovery, not a private artifact override: | Input | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | Linux amd64 release archive | 1d25267b161c1ac6c12c15cd7c4cb96a49a8c1622d365fb932f3ef3bd3123d33 | | Controller | 20d0cb5b592f339a2928139909f1f95990f28f7a03558ee9f570bf9171f3876c | | Adjacent native manifest | f0a5abfc81ccbf1e8f9e8efd61a271dfb97c56110f271c225efeeb7a54985d16 | | Linux amd64 native runtime | 2fa8b9ac1250bdbbe6f291c2084bd1ae0f46a34337ba962de9c7474060f88c7b | An isolated Gateway, genuinely paired node and real OpenSSH ran inside task-owned rootless Debian. The full current generated enrollment/trust command ran real certificate registration before node launch, without modifying host trust. | Case | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Same-device reconnect | 74.1 seconds; existing device/runtime/workspace retained | | Retry | 70.2 seconds; reused the same committed PID and device | | Cancel held read-only identity inspection | Child exited; original dead-PID receipt unchanged; five exact retirements before return | | Revoke host authority during held inspection | Fresh host assertion rejects launch; no new connection; five exact retirements before return | | Cancel actual detached child before commit | Child exited; original receipt preserved; no later node effect; ten exact retirements before return | Recovery and retry each confirmed ten native completion/retirement records before provider return. Production 20-second cleanup and full 5-second native grace were not shortened. A delayed/unobservable remote wrapper remains explicitly uncertain: local exit or absent remote state is never remote quiescence and does not authorize automatic replay. ### Proof limits and retained failures - Two original cancellation harness runs exited 1 because the old oracle counted the canonical enrollment's initial connection. Their raw reports remain failed; an independent corrected oracle verifies no new connection, actual child exit, unchanged receipt and exact retirement. They are not relabeled as original-script exit-zero runs. - QA used the canonical npm-verification branch, not fresh bootstrap-archive installation. The released controller and adjacent native inputs were hashed and real native dispatch/receipts observed; an independent remote executable rehash was not captured before normal cleanup. - The earlier one-shot authority failure and v0.80 retirement defect remain historical evidence. The existing-API split addresses the reported held-probe case; a new public commit protocol was not necessary. Earlier maintenance CI was never proof that the one-shot implementation was safe to ship. - This is local Linux/static-SSH and service-boundary proof, not a new paid cloud allocation or a replay of separate R5/installed acceptance runs. No live Gateway/profile deployment or new Crabbox release occurred. All 15 owned proof containers and three task images were removed after verifying they were stopped; no proof Gateway/node/sshd remains. A temporary compiler-input scan conflict from the proof image filesystem was resolved by owned-resource cleanup, not a guard/ignore change. Original failure logs and source/artifact receipts are retained. Contributor credit: @galiniliev authored the S4 source commit `9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27` that informed this bounded extraction, reimplemented against current upstream owners at his request. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d50d6742-c669-438e-9779-276e1117ca73) - [Existing-command split review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8769e9c5-906b-4f16-988d-626eac19a170) - [CI synthetic-merge compatibility repair](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4489e496-7aa8-43f3-a3fa-d3a5939bee9a) - [Final canonical-owner maintenance review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b1e047e9-2553-47d0-adb4-788ba261b590) - [Final cancellation and settlement review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9fc975e2-8c3b-426a-a370-b55eaccbc29d)
Earlier verification sessions - [Exact-base Stop recovery attribution](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fafc6631-200a-4324-9b09-b753b63b4048) - [Real transport cancellation investigation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f1c1f0fb-88a9-4f27-9a1d-8f1e187e824b) - [CI synchronization follow-up](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/390ea07d-039d-4083-9d51-32d016ee34c7) - [Local Crabbox controller preparation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/92b15a87-7505-4ee6-9fb5-625340e35cf8) - [Final bounded independent review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2136e4a4-fa16-4804-8ee2-ac906264351f)

Signed commit [`2e60dcd3350f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e60dcd3350f1bc214ee15704744d65882bbbf68) has that exact tree. Modern Doctor delegation also passes **12/12**. title: fix: worktree sessions load their own bootstrap instructions
body:
Supersedes #129413, thanks @krell11

Fixes #129411

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worktree sessions receiving bootstrap instructions from the shared agent checkout instead of their recorded workspace.

## User Impact

Recorded worktree sessions use their own bootstrap files, including `AGENTS.md` and `SOUL.md`, while skill discovery stays anchored to the configured agent workspace. Runs restricted by `workspaceOnly` use their execution workspace. A cwd override alone does not change bootstrap identity.

Missing files have **no fallback to the shared checkout or a packaged template**. A worktree without `AGENTS.md` behaves like running the harness directly in that directory: no project instructions. OpenClaw retains its normal missing-file diagnostics. Rejected symlink paths and workspace escapes are logged and treated as missing; guarded reads remain inside the selected root. Other read failures retain their unreadable diagnostics.

**Native Codex boundary:** native project-document discovery remains Codex's documented loader operating on its cwd and permissions, including native symlink behavior. A native session whose cwd is the worktree already loads that worktree's documents. This PR changes neither native configuration nor the native loader and adds no in-memory defaults.

**Needs deploy:** affects Team worktree sessions directly; deploy after landing. No live Gateway changes were made during development.

## Why This Change Was Made

One selector in `workspace-run.ts` chooses the bootstrap root for embedded and CLI preparation. Bootstrap loading retains its existing session filters, budgets, and guarded filesystem reads. Skills resolve their configured anchor independently, so changing bootstrap cannot move the agent skill tier when a reusable snapshot is absent.

Production delta is **+19 lines**: the selector and its callers establish the recorded boundary, the skills change preserves independent ownership, and the loader preserves its diagnostic while marking typed symlink/escape rejections missing. The orchestrator adds zero lines. Shared workspace input types and duplicate config guards were consolidated in the same owner; there is no registry lookup, new state, or native configuration path. The separate test-line allocation covers 100 net lines of regression/support coverage.

## Evidence

- All five bootstrap/CLI regressions fail on main before the fix, as does the snapshot-less configured-skills regression. All six pass with the fix.
- Consumer run: **258 passed**, including bootstrap privacy/remote/memory consumers, workspace reads/cache, CLI preparation, embedded runtime, configured skills, native workspace snapshots, and prompt-prefix stability. Three existing library-read assertions fail identically with all six changed production modules restored from main: they expect `/regular file/i`, while the maintained filesystem reader reports `symlink path component not allowed`. This is retained as an investigated baseline failure, not counted as a passing test.
- Targeted lint, targeted typecheck of changed tests and their production import graph, formatting, `git diff --check`, and both production/full-tree unused-file scans pass. No full live-model proof was run.
- Final changed-file runs pass: CLI preparation **112 tests / 87.83s wall**, bootstrap preparation **19 tests / 10.63s**, and skills preparation **6 tests / 7.30s**. Wall times include compiler/startup overhead. The existing CLI suite exercises auth, MCP, and session recovery; the new case reuses that boundary fixture. The broader consumer run took 200.46s. Hosted CI remains the broad proof gate; CI timing is available in the linked checks after publication.
- The first PR CI head (`9a30e14`) exposed three assertions caused by overly broad missing-file classification (hard links, permission failures, and two-link atomic publication). The correction recognizes only typed symlink/escape failures. The affected workspace/read/bootstrap suites pass **89 tests**, and atomic publication passes **7 tests**; targeted lint and typecheck pass again.
- Final exact-head [CI run 41160224530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160224530) completed successfully for `28bfbb481e9d236622381d2808a1295dd3adda35` (10m19s). The exact-head watcher reached GREEN with zero pending checks; dependency and security-sensitive review gates also passed. Landed through `scripts/pr` as `80dead1a1837f1d9155c164cc76d17f5f1fc47a5`.
- Shared autoreview was rerun with a **300-second wall timeout** and produced no report (exit 124). No provider/route configuration changed. The authorized fallback fresh-context P0–P2 security/correctness review of the final diff against `3e1dbed3b0de4f1138e229a0564674c56f4c923e` found **no material findings**. It inspected the selector, all three consumers, guarded reads, skills ownership, and regressions; it was source-only and did not independently rerun tests or claim live/native proof. A follow-up fresh-context review of the CI correction also found no material findings. This is not a clean autoreview machine result.

The contributor's code was read through PR metadata/diff only and was never checked out or run. Human credit: krell11 <11bobin.kiryusha@gmail.com>; every replacement commit preserves that Co-authored-by trailer and excludes the agent trailer.

title: fix(visitor-access): reject oversized Cloudflare responses
body:
Supersedes #132491, thanks @RileyJJY.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive Gateway memory use when Cloudflare returns an unexpectedly large Visitor Access policy response.

## User Impact

Responses above 16 MiB are rejected and their streams canceled before the full body is buffered. Normal responses continue to work. The same bound applies to discovery and mutation confirmations, including best-effort provider cleanup; an oversized confirmation requires policy inspection before retrying. Existing durable cleanup retries remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Plugin SDK provider JSON reader instead of implementing another size limiter. Removing the mutable read result and its surrounding try/catch offsets the SDK import: production code is **−2 lines** (+3/−5). The README documents the limit.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `9f14244a6067e9ca0e22d1a2b8c5150e9cb7c693`: the new production-client regression failed because a valid streamed 32 MiB JSON response was accepted (25 passed, 1 failed; exit 1). With the fix, a 1 MiB response succeeds and a 32 MiB response is rejected and canceled before completion.
- Focused Cloudflare and visitor-service suites: **83 passed**, 1.12 s Vitest / 4.14 s command wall time. Complete `test:extension visitor-access --maxWorkers=1`: **116 passed**, 55.44 s Vitest / 62.44 s wall time, including plugin lifecycle, restart, and cleanup coverage. Commands ran in containers capped at 4 CPUs / 8 GiB.
- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41157993681) **passed**: 460 s workflow wall time; the `checks-node-changed` job took 280 s including setup and all selected tests. No CI failure exception was used.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The +27 test-line allocation covers the new bounded-stream regression and its positive control; no existing tests were restored or duplicated.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate against the main SHA above: **scoped-clean**, P0–P2, no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected the supplied SDK reader source; it did not independently execute tests or live integrations.

No live Cloudflare API call or built Gateway process proof is claimed; the regression exercises the production policy client with external response-stream fixtures.

title: fix(normalization): prevent native-value fingerprint collisions
body:
Fixes #133231

Supersedes #133232, thanks @Avi974.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes identical plugin/cache fingerprints for distinct Date, RegExp, Set and Map values passed to the shared stable serializer.

## User Impact

Existing plain JSON values retain byte-for-byte serialization and all existing hashes, including current undefined handling. Native values now have deterministic, distinct type-tagged encodings. Set and Map insertion order does not affect identity; numeric and string Map keys stay distinct.

Compatibility decision: an unsupported native-valued input recorded before upgrade can fail closed when retried against an effect-bearing durable fingerprint. This explicit conflict/rejection is accepted: it prevents duplicate effects and silent acceptance of distinct values. No shipped producer of these native values was found at those durable boundaries. Supported JSON inputs remain unchanged. No legacy-hash fallback, guard weakening, schema migration, or new configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retaining old collapsed-hash acceptance would keep the collision, and treating an idempotency conflict as a cache miss could repeat effects. The P2 is resolved by this explicit contract decision. title: fix(update): seal recovery captures on large state directories
body:
Fixes #188897

## What Problem This Solves

Large state directories can leave every pre-update recovery capture incomplete because the inventory exceeds a child process's stdout limit.

## User Impact

Recovery captures can now seal with large inventories. Failed optional captures explicitly warn `NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT` while the update continues; the warning remains in returned JSON and update history.

The fix must be installed in the updater performing the capture. A newer candidate cannot repair an older updater process already running. Older candidate workers retain their existing stdout contract and limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Metadata inventories now run in serial batches budgeted by escaped UTF-8 JSON bytes, with room for result fields, one aggregate deadline, and the same caller cancellation signal. Order, duplicates, missing files, and SQLite sidecar sizes are preserved; failure returns no partial inventory or subsequent child after cancellation. The per-child 1 MiB stdout cap stays unchanged.

The sibling audit also found unbounded database-discovery, backup-receipt, schema/generation, and candidate snapshot results. Both launchers now share an opt-in private result-file transport, read after successful process settlement and bounded like the existing recovery manifest. Legacy stdout interoperability and uncertain-cleanup retention remain intact. Payload capture already runs in process; progress backpressure handling needed no change.

Other open proposals for this issue: #188907 and #188912. This PR implements the requested fixed-cap batching design and covers the sibling result transports and warning behavior.

## Evidence

- **RED → GREEN:** main `ae01f1c113826d3ff41463e74da6c115e5b581ff` rejects 12,000 copies of an existing 160-character path with `output-limit`; the fixed owner returns all 12,000. Original-owner controls also reject the ASCII, UTF-8, and quote/backslash cases.

title: fix(workers): reject new turns on unusable provider leases
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fresh worker or remote-exec turn can claim input using a still-attached local record after its provider lease has become unusable, before background reconciliation observes the loss.

## User Impact

New turns qualify the exact attached lease before taking a claim. Unavailable provider observations leave ownership intact and reject admission for retry; dormant paired devices retain their existing reconnect behavior. Confirmed loss uses existing cleanup and never starts the new input. This adds a bounded provider observation to fresh lease-backed admission; it adds no configuration, schema, or public provider API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider lifecycle shares one loss-settlement implementation between maintenance and turn admission. The service serializes inspection with the environment owner and retains accepted cleanup after caller cancellation. Admission rechecks the same lease at claim commit and after waiting for an earlier claim. Existing recorded-loss and runtime-refresh recovery remain with their current owners. This inspection does not allocate a replacement or replay input.

title: feat: link Discord accounts from personal profiles
body:
## What Problem This Solves

People need to connect their own Discord account to their signed-in OpenClaw profile without asking an administrator to attest the link, and retain their existing session permissions when requesting work from Discord.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Profile gains Discord account linking, verified linked-ID status, and disconnect directly below Linked emails and above GitHub account. Linked members keep their actual allowed operator scopes in channel runs; linking does not grant administrator or command-owner privileges.

Deployment requires the selected Discord application's existing OAuth client configuration and the Gateway callback URL registered with Discord. Live Discord OAuth deployment qualification has not been performed; this PR does not change live configuration or credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flow reuses the personal-profile authorization boundary, provider-browser callback owner, and canonical channel-identity store. Discord proves the immutable user ID with the `identify` scope; short-lived one-use state and an initiating-browser cookie bind the callback. The initiating profile, connection, scopes, plugin and account configuration are checked again before storing the link. Tokens are not persisted. Conflicting links are rejected, and administrative attestation endpoints remain administrator-only.

Channel run authority now derives independently from verified profile permissions rather than command-owner status, while retaining the existing access-grant, revocation and queued-recovery checks.

title: fix(usage): return stale session costs when refresh stays busy
body:
Supersedes #132396, thanks @SebTardif.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session-cost requests that remain pending while another direct usage refresh holds the refresh owner. Main removed busy polling in #183029, but its replacement completion wait still has no report deadline.

## User Impact

Direct session-cost reports wait up to the existing ten-second refresh budget, then return safe last-known totals marked stale. `/usage cost` labels the Session total `(stale)`. Refresh continues under its existing owner; a session without a usable cached total remains unavailable. No settings, schema changes, or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing cache report deadline and projection owner. Remove the separate direct refresh, pricing-fingerprint and projection pipeline: production net **-13 lines**. Preserve selected-session ownership, cancellation and fresh results when refresh completes in time.

## Evidence

- Main owner files at `92e1a1bb115f2ea646e0b57b21d7c5cfa6649ca7`: the regression holds a real SQLite refresh lock, advances ten seconds of fake time, and fails because the direct report remains pending. The fix returns the previously committed 10 tokens / $1 with `staleSince` and `refreshing`, while owner work remains pending. No real ten-second sleep.
- 74 focused pricing, archive, incognito, worker-I/O and refresh tests passed (108.02 s runner / 111.57 s wall); the final organization reran all 24 refresh tests successfully (56.24 s runner / 59.30 s wall, including a cold worker compile). New regression body 2.48 s on the final run. Exact-head hosted [CI run 41154105086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154105086) passed in 557 s workflow wall time, including runner setup; the combined CI/security gate also passed.
- Targeted production/test typecheck and type-aware lint passed in a rootless container capped at four CPUs / 8 GB; formatting, the test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview of the final change and complete helper context: P0–P2 **scoped-clean**. `pr-simplify` complete.

title: improve: avoid minute-long worktree refusal test waits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The worktree refusal test waits about a minute for a synthetic replacement lease after the registry write has already been refused.

## User Impact

Focused worktree validation finishes about a minute sooner. Product behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fixture replacement lease live until the real worker operation reports `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`, then release only that fixture lease so normal failure settlement can reacquire custody. Production lease TTLs, authority checks, native admission, receipts, and joined cleanup stay intact.

## Evidence

Three successful serial before and three after runs per runtime, with the same private frozen dependencies, Linux host, temp/cache paths, Node 26.12.1, and the checksum-pinned CI Bun fork. All eleven cases passed in every timed run.

Median seconds (before → after):

| Runtime | Wall | Vitest | Case sum | Checkout-lease row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bun | 77.630 → 18.820 | 72.290 → 12.690 | 69.910 → 10.263 | 60.562 → 0.959 |
| Node | 85.630 → 27.780 | 79.950 → 23.070 | 74.369 → 20.416 | 60.908 → 1.303 |

The initial trace put the real insert rejection 3 ms after publication resumed, followed by another 59.799 s before service rejection. A separate counted trace retained two successful mutation-lease acquisitions and one insert attempt while removing **239 blocked acquisitions**; final settlement completed 195 ms after the native refusal.

Removing the real lease-expiry query's owner predicate makes the final test fail on **both Bun and Node** with “Publication was not refused.” The production mutation was restored byte-for-byte before final validation.

- Target plus `pending-slots.worker.test.ts` and `registry-publication.test.ts`: **13 tests passed per runtime**, including after mutation restoration.
- Focused target typecheck, type-aware lint, format, diff check, and line/max-lines/test-line/timeout/mock/assertion ratchets passed.
- Author simplification pass retained the real rejection signal and fixture cleanup; no test behavior was deleted. All four refusal rows, registry/checkout/lock assertions, acknowledgement/lost-reply rows, captured reads, and native cleanup remain.
- Complete-source isolated Codex autoreview: **P0–P2 `scoped-clean`**, no findings, one pass with the intact target, owners, and helpers. The reviewed test source against `1237490f19768dc2656c600f6bbbca46c948b42f` is byte-for-byte unchanged in `bcb219bdb740b6d435a4f4624359cda56202c203`. Parent review approved the test implementation and required restoring the unchanged cap; this head satisfies that correction and passes the native budget and line-cap ratchets. The reviewer performed static review; runtime/mutation evidence came from the focused executions above.

Parent source review and native landing are complete. No broad local suite or SDK build was run.

<details>
<summary>All twelve timed runs and exact budget accounting</summary>

Command for each runtime (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` or `node`):

```sh
timeout 900 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/registry-read.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

title: improve: show chat execution permissions beside the icon
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The web chat composer hides the current execution permission level behind an icon, so users must open the picker to see it.

## User Impact

Users can read the current permission mode beside the existing icon on wider web composers. The label follows the composer chip standard used by the model and effort pickers: the same padding, icon-to-label gap, 13 px type, weight, line height, letter spacing and vertical center. Narrow phone, touch-target and split-pane composers keep the compact icon-only control, with no partially clipped text. Permission enforcement and switching behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the picker's existing localized label, including resolved inherited defaults, rather than introducing another permission-state owner. Full Access keeps its accent color. No new strings, configuration, dependencies, or migrations.

Alignment follow-up (requested in review):

- The permission trigger is a `<button>`, so it took the browser's `letter-spacing: normal` while the `<summary>`-based model/effort chips inherit the app tracking. The shared `.chat-controls__inline-select-trigger` rule now inherits letter spacing for every chip.
- The lead-only `padding-inline: 6px` override (sized for the old icon-only control) is removed, so the labelled chip uses the family `--chat-composer-chip-padding-inline`.
- At viewports ≤ 640 px a fixed `width: 44px` touch target clipped the label to "D…" whenever the composer itself was still wider than 560 px. That rule is now a `min-width: 44px` floor using the family padding, so the whole label shows there and the 560 px container rule alone decides icon-only.
- Full Access colors the trigger itself instead of separate icon and label selectors. Net CSS for the whole PR is +24 raw bytes / +0 gzip versus base (`pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passes locally and in CI), fixing the asset-budget finding from the previous review.

## Evidence

- Rebased on current `main` (`3a9ffb1d9184437fd59201c3868074c8217358ec`); the only conflict was test-only and keeps upstream's Chromium/WebKit expansion.
- Browser measurement, default and Full Access: at 1280 and 900 px the permission, model and effort chips all report padding 8/8 px, gap 4 px, height 30 px, `13px 400 17.55px`, letter spacing −0.14 px and identical icon/label centers; at a 600 px window all three use the compact 4/4 px padding and 44 px targets with the label whole; at a 560 px window the label is absent.
- The composer layout E2E now checks those chip metrics and that the label is either whole or absent at 320, 393, 560, 600, 900, 1100 and 1280 px. Its Chromium case **fails with the previous PR CSS** (permission padding 0/0 vs 4/4 at 600 px) and **passes now**; `pnpm test`-runner wall time for that file is about 52 s including the UI build, with the Chromium case at 15.3 s.
- Production-bundle E2E for `chat-permission-refresh` and `chat-composer-picker-layout`: **6/7 passed**. The WebKit variant times out waiting for `sessions.messages.subscribe` before any permission assertion; the same failure reproduces with the task files restored to current `main`, so WebKit coverage is not claimed as passing.
- Picker unit tests: **6/6 passed** (`pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-permission-picker.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`).
- `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, stylelint (repo config), oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(update): dev updates hang on disconnected local main
body:
Supersedes #188857 (thanks @fuller-stack-dev)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update --channel dev` can hang replaying stale local `main` when a shallow clone hides its shared history with the update target.

## User Impact

Dev updates validate upstream without replaying disconnected history. Commits outside the validated candidate remain reachable at `refs/openclaw/update-preserved/main-<sha>`, with inspection and removal commands in the warning. If preservation fails, activation uses a detached HEAD and leaves `main` unchanged.

The installed updater must contain this fix; candidate code cannot repair an older updater's already-running preflight. Preserved refs remain until the operator removes them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing preflight owner checks the relation before replay and limits optional local checkout/rebase to ten minutes per step, or a shorter caller timeout. Timeout gets one clean retry of the current candidate; ordinary conflicts retain the existing walk-back order. Interruption and unverified cleanup stop the attempt. Git state inspection distinguishes an active rebase from a timeout before rebase state exists.

This reduced takeover omits the 1000-commit cutoff, expanded retry queue, preview changes and return-field plumbing. It uses the existing preflight and native Git-step owners, with no new public options, config, protocol or schema.

## Evidence

- The trusted real-Git shallow `blob:none` regression was RED on `e765de67512f14a644f726372b0bb2b46e614a6c`: it resurrected a retired file and activated a different commit. It is GREEN with this fix and verifies the preserved original ref.
- All 14 replay scenarios pass: connected work, merge-only content, default/shorter/early timeout, failed active abort, conflict, replay/preservation interruption, detached fallback and rollback. The standalone file took 15.37s wall time. Real Git deadline tests shorten execution to one second; they verify the requested ten-minute or shorter budget.
- The initial consumer selection passed 214 tests plus both immutable-worker tests. After the review repair, all 81 affected tests passed; unchanged consumer evidence is retained. Services typecheck, typed lint, format, test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed. The separate 273-line regression allocation covers these native Git/process contracts without changing the shared baseline.

title: fix(whatsapp): answer recent messages missed during gateway downtime
body:
Supersedes #132260, thanks @0xNagato.
Related: #20952

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp messages received during Gateway downtime being marked read and silently left unanswered when the linked account starts again.

## User Impact

Established linked accounts can answer recent offline messages after startup or reconnect, with a maximum age of 20 minutes at intake. Normal DM, group allowlist, and mention rules continue to apply. Newly linked accounts keep their short history guard; older offline messages remain outside the reply window. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use [Baileys' already-loaded initial-sync state](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/blob/7e7b0757e3f9f3c7789fb1cfd2f241d5002a199a/src/Socket/chats.ts#L1324), captured before asynchronous socket attachment, to choose the existing bounded age cap. A single rolling freshness rule replaces the separate reconnect window and handles startup, reconnect, and delayed offline appends. Durable account/chat/message-ID admission continues to prevent replayed replies across restarts, and the watchdog keeps its existing lifecycle policy.

Production LOC: **net -8** by removing the three-field reconnect window and its duplicate lifetime bookkeeping. Test fixtures/regressions: net +30; the test-line allocation grants the exact 27 LF increase counted by the ratchet. The added proof covers reply/restart deduplication and policy boundaries while replacing obsolete reconnect-window assertions.

## Evidence

- Main baseline `38fd51c52ab11ce75810ac7917bef4fc2b11010c`: the append boundary suite had **2 failed / 9 passed** with only the new regression and fixture overlaid. Five-minute-old offline messages never reached reply dispatch.
- The strengthened first-link test reproduced an incorrect historical reply when sync completed during asynchronous attachment; capturing the state before that await fixes it. Negative assertions now wait for the real inbound drain.
- Focused validation: **71 tests passed across 5 files** (connection/logging, append intake, delivery/dedupe, access policy, and group activation), using Node 24.22.1 in rootless Podman limited to 4 CPUs / 8 GB. The final run took 371.01s including a cold runtime/declaration build; the changed connection file took 66.57s (1% test execution) and the three inbox files took 18.44s together. The initial warm standalone append run took 10.36s. CI timing will be available on this PR.
- The normalization fixture consumers passed **15/15 tests** (25.07s). Targeted production and touched-test type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The media suite also passed **11/11** (9.14s), for **97 passing focused tests** in total.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, against the baseline above) found one INDEX-only startup-snapshot omission in an older staged state. The reviewed socket-session fix is included in the final staged change; the reviewer found no additional defects in the combined source.
- CI repair: `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` exposed a PR-caused omission in the media socket fixture. Its 11 cases reproduced the missing `authState` setup failure locally; adding Baileys' initial counter to that fixture made all 11 pass. Production code is unchanged. A separate autoreview of this repair delta was **scoped-clean at P0–P2**; media test types, type-aware lint, formatting, and the adjusted exact LF allocation passed.
- Contributor code was inspected using `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out, installed, built, or executed. This is a maintainer reimplementation from main, credited to Femi Odunaiya.
- Proof uses synthetic WhatsApp transport events, real intake/durable deduplication, access policy, and reply-send paths. A live paired-device test was not run, and the production Gateway was not changed.

title: fix(whatsapp): send pairing approval confirmations
body:
Supersedes #128857, thanks @SuperMarioYL.

Related: #56619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: newly approved WhatsApp senders receive no confirmation when an operator requests an approval notification from the CLI or Control UI.

## User Impact

`pairing approve whatsapp <code> --notify` and the Control UI's notification option send the standard approval text through the approved account. Notification remains opt-in and follows successful approval; pairing codes and request metadata are not included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared pairing notifier now uses the existing outbound sender when a pairing channel has no custom notification callback. CLI delivery uses the running Gateway; Gateway approval uses its active transport directly. Existing Telegram, Signal, and Discord callbacks retain their behavior. Suppressed delivery is reported as a notification failure without undoing approval.

The original callback-only proposal would run WhatsApp's process-local sender in the CLI, where no active listener exists. This replacement implements the useful behavior at the shared owner instead.

## Evidence

- On main's pairing implementation, the outbound regression failed in both CLI/Gateway routing cases (zero sends), and the Gateway suite failed to advertise or invoke WhatsApp notification. The paired owner files are unchanged between the tested main base `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1` and current main `080723ad2a0`.
- After the fix: pairing Gateway, CLI, shared adapter, and outbound suites pass. Coverage includes the selected account, standard text only, no notification for a missing request or uncertain approval, and preserved approval after notification failure.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, local changes against `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1`) found one P2: suppressed delivery could be reported as sent. Fixed it and added a real outbound-hook regression, red before that correction and green afterward. A fresh review of the final snapshot is scoped-clean through P2.
- Production and affected test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. Full [CI run 41151099877](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41151099877) and the aggregate CI gate passed on `d55de9f1f7573bfa5ff9170eba8544ce0a4fef3b`.
- Local suite wall times: Gateway 36.37s, CLI 4.35s, shared adapters 1.29s, final outbound 43.90s (26 tests). Cold worker compilation accounts for the longer runs; outbound test execution itself was under 5 seconds.
- Proof uses isolated state and captured Gateway/transport I/O; actual WhatsApp network delivery was not exercised. Contributor code was read through GitHub and was never checked out or run.

Production LOC is +11: the shared fallback and suppression outcome require new behavior. The change removes the Gateway's duplicate unsupported-notification branch and the notifier's redundant payload reconstruction; no unrelated deletions were added to reach a quota. Tests are +83 lines, with a matching allocation for routing, privacy, rejected approval, and suppression regressions. No new configuration, schema, or migration is required.

title: fix(memory): preserve concurrent sandbox flush notes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost memory notes when concurrent memory flushes append to the same sandbox workspace file.

Supersedes #131604, thanks @michielhdoteth.

Related: #117741

## User Impact

Concurrent flushes within one Gateway process retain every appended note. Cross-process writers remain outside this guarantee; the sandbox backend has no atomic append primitive. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sandbox append read and rewrote the entire file without joining the existing write/edit mutation queue. The fix serializes that operation using the bridge's physical file identity, preserving path safety and the authority check immediately before writing.

Consolidating duplicated source-execution scopes and eliminating the intermediate write-content variable keeps production LOC at **-1**. The real bridge regression adds 30 test lines, with an exact 30-line allocation because existing tests did not exercise concurrent memory flushes.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `38fd51c52ab11ce75810ac7917bef4fc2b11010c`:** four separate memory-flush tools all reported success, but the real sandbox bridge persisted only `seed` and `note-D`, losing the other three notes. The affected main source remained unchanged at publication.
- **Green after:** all 8 tests in `fs-bridge.backend.e2e.test.ts` pass, including the same concurrent-append reproduction. This runs the production bridge with a local shell/Python backend and real files, without Docker or a model. New case: 434 ms; full cold file wall time: 42.43 s (most time was compilation). The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41149547274) passed (8 min 19 s overall).
- **Consumer checks:** 245 passing tests across 12 core consumer files, plus 75 passing tests and one existing skip across gateway files, Codex filesystem streaming/composition, and OpenShell backend consumers: **328 passing tests across 18 files overall**. Additional checks ran in rootless containers capped at four CPUs and 8 GiB.
- Core and affected `agents-tools` test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The typecheck's existing state-logging root-budget advisory is unrelated.
- **Autoreview:** Codex engine, P0–P2, `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings on the production/test local snapshot against the main SHA above (diff SHA-256 `a69aa006a290400e7d167303caf0214b3272df2af772e6e40c46a47949a85a11`). Review could not execute tests in its sandbox; the tests above ran separately. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; one hosted review was requested and is in progress.
- The contributor head was read with GitHub view/diff and was never checked out, installed, or executed. This implementation and regression were written on a branch based on main. Contributor credit is preserved in the commit trailer.
- Live model-driven compaction was not exercised; the regression proves the actual memory-flush writer and sandbox bridge boundary directly. The Team Gateway was not modified or restarted.

title: fix: show effective next runs for one-shot automations
body:
Closes #188858

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Automations editor presents the original one-shot occurrence as its only execution after the same task has been rearmed for a later run.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish the configured time from the effective next execution, without accidentally replacing the authored time by saving an unrelated edit. Running and paused tasks no longer promise a pending execution from a stale deadline. No scheduler, retry, permission, or data-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The configured occurrence and runtime deadline are different facts. The existing schedule summary now shows both for an unchanged saved one-shot; editing a new time still previews the draft. List, detail header, and editor share the existing job-status presentation owner for running, paused, and next-run state. Timestamp differences are not guessed to mean a continuation rather than a retry.

## Evidence

- Production-bundle Chromium reproduction **failed on base** `4a393be419f30ecfd65972fe3ea1416c6f707316`: a fictional 12:00 configured occurrence with a 12:10 runtime deadline rendered only “Runs once at … 12:00 PM.”
- The same browser flow **passes with the fix**, including an unrelated-name save that omits both `patch.schedule` and `patch.state`, then reopening the editor (1.48s test time; 19.95s harness wall time). Browser timezone UTC, en-US, 1280×900, light theme; synthetic Gateway RPC data, not a live model-backed scheduling test.
- Focused UI/form consumers: **56 tests passed across 5 files** (6.62s command wall time). Regression covers mutable runtime refresh, running, paused-with-stale-deadline, no-next-run, and a new unsaved timestamp; existing tests preserve recurring forms and unchanged exact timestamp precision.
- UI production typecheck, all UI test typecheck shards, targeted oxlint, formatting, controller guard, i18n verification, test-line/line-cap/max-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Production Control UI build passed.
- Independent local autoreview: Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium/Ultrafast, P0–P2, final local candidate against the base above: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. title: fix(discord): avoid false failure notices for queued thread answers
body:
Supersedes #183192, thanks @hannnnn-l.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false Discord failure notices after a queued message is successfully answered in a thread created from that message.

## User Impact

Queued thread answers fulfill the original request without an extra failure notice in the parent channel. Genuinely unanswered turns still notify. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transfer the source-message route from dispatch into the existing queued delivery-correlation lifecycle before queued execution. The queued run owns its own registration through settlement, including when it starts before dispatch returns. Thread creation alone and replies to unrelated threads do not count as answers.

This avoids adding route reference counts or a second lifecycle helper. Removed the optional thread-adoption forwarder and redundant primitive aliases in the same owner. Production delta: +35/-31, net +4 lines required for the ownership transfer; regression tests: +39 lines, with an exact test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- Current main verified at `8873aeb433fd931c87e2bd5ba45f38b67215ae27`. Both new early/late queued-execution cases fail there at source-reply recognition (`expected false to be true`); the existing 20 cases pass.

The first [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41361126156) caught TS2454 in the new test cleanup variable; it now initializes explicitly. The 22 focused cases and touched-file checks pass after that correction. [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41361715626) and all 42 PR checks passed, including the full test-type graph and required gate. title: fix(active-memory): German recall questions skip deep recall
body:
Supersedes #182612, thanks @jochen.
Related: #151766

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory skips deep recall when German users ask about previous conversations in the default escalate mode.

## User Impact

German recall questions such as “Erinnerst du dich an das Rezept?” and “Was habe ich dir gesagt?” now start deep recall when deterministic retrieval has no strong hit. Future reminders and ordinary statements stay quiet; completed discussions about future plans can still trigger recall.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds German to the existing localized intent, future, and retrospective pattern table alongside French, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. It follows the existing Unicode boundary and bounded-context pattern style and accepts ß/ss spellings.

The production change is +9 lines. The owner has no equivalent dead or duplicate code that can safely offset the new language entry. The 25-line test allocation covers the missing recall constructions and false-positive controls, including past-morning wording, future passive requests, second-person past-tense endings, and spelled-out duration reminders.

## Evidence

- Current main `7c0ac6d1c3629db2fd5c6254590d4b223dc6aef5` has the same escalation implementation as the implementation base `ba6dbdfd482380fb4c525f401ac907d24671405a`. Both requested German phrases return `no-recall-intent`, which the plugin caller uses to skip deep recall.
- Against main’s implementation, the named escalation test failed all ten initial German recall cases (106 passed). After the fix and review regressions: **121 passed**, Vitest duration **0.97 seconds**. The positive cases exercise the production escalation decision in `escalate` mode.
- Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Full typechecking and broad integration proof are delegated to PR CI.
- Shared **autoreview**, Codex, P0–P2, complete change against `ba6dbdfd482380fb4c525f401ac907d24671405a`: all findings addressed. title: fix(sessions): stop expanding archive reads from exhausting memory
body:
Supersedes #182366, thanks @xydt-tanshanshan.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes archive reads exhausting memory when compressed session transcripts expand far beyond their stored size.

## User Impact

Archive reads now stop at the stored byte count plus 1 MiB and report an actionable error without changing the source archive. History fallback surfaces that refusal instead of returning missing history.

Compressed artifacts exceeding this expansion budget, including otherwise valid files, must be exported as uncompressed JSONL to read them through this file-reader path. Publication verification uses the original plaintext byte count it already knows, preserving compression and existing disk-budget retention. There is no schema, configuration, or archive-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared archive reader passed no output limit to the existing zstd codec. Its native chunk loop now enforces the limit before concatenating decoded output. The writer supplies its authoritative original UTF-8 byte count for bounded publication verification and reuse checks; ordinary archive reads do not trust a frame's declared size.

The simplification pass retains the existing codec, synchronous API, encoder, and streamed writer. The final change adds 24 net production lines for the limit, clear errors, propagation, and bounded writer verification. No unrelated deletion offsets were added.

## Evidence

- On main source `34de4be3eff02b3e6b002d10dd7ec9c8b9f42928`, an 82-byte crafted frame expands to 2 MiB: both shared-reader rejection cases fail, and the real history facade returns a page instead of rejecting. The reader remains byte-identical on inspected main `324dfc78`.
- All 74 tests pass across the six named archive-compression, archive-publication, archive-worker, history-reader, usage-worker, and history-eviction files. They cover refusal, unchanged bytes, near-budget compressed content, compressed publication/readback/reuse, large archive preservation, visible history errors, usage cancellation, and disk-budget retention.
- CI found a retention regression in the first head's encoding fallback. The exact failing retention scenario passes with main's reader/writer source (2 selected cases) and with the final fix; the final encoder and streamed writer are unchanged from main. The full six-file replay passes in 97.74 s, including compiler-cache preparation. Earlier isolated owner and history-reader runs took 0.675 s and 13.48 s. Exact-head [CI run 41355778736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41355778736) passed in 24 min 11 s wall time. The separate 64-line test allocation funds the regression contracts.
- Touched-file formatting and typed lint pass; `git diff --check` passes. PR CI supplies broad proof; no broad local suites, packaging, containers, browser tests, deployment, or live-state changes were run.
- Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete final working-tree candidate against `34de4be3eff02b3e6b002d10dd7ec9c8b9f42928` at P0–P2. It found no additional defects in that candidate. Its sole finding was explicitly INDEX-only, identifying the previous encoding fallback; staging the reviewed working tree removes it. The earlier writer/readback finding is resolved by the authoritative source-byte bound. This is a findings report with those resolutions, not a claim of a machine `scoped-clean` verdict.

title: fix: unblock Doctor upgrades from beta v16 agent databases

## User Impact

Doctor preserves the original database, validates session identities, and restores missing canonical invalidation triggers inside its existing schema transaction. Invalid rows and unrelated schema drift still refuse with preservation/support guidance. Complete-trigger v16 databases retain their existing flow. No schema-version or public-config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Beta.6 [shipped v16 without the validity projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/4d6bdbdbf33fe3ece3c53853fab9931882ff3f3c/src/state). The repair uses the existing schema facts, typed Kysely stream, parser, trigger definitions, transaction, and SQLite backup owners. Independent config-only repairs remain a follow-up: changing fail-stop ordering needs dependency classification and consistent config/agent-discovery snapshots.

## Evidence

- RED locally on `8f3da9e8e46e`: exact beta.6 SQL produces the three reported missing-trigger errors through Doctor media-persistence.
- GREEN on final `c6421baf59b3a` tree: 42 named media-persistence/historical tests, including beta repair, original backup, invalid identity, unknown column/table/index, missing table, unexpected uniqueness, drifted trigger, rollback and repeat-run controls. Vitest wall 77.70s including worker compilation. Agent DB owner suite: 60 passed, 3 existing skips (unchanged-contract proof reused).
- [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41351544566): published beta.6 package owner created v16 with app_version 2026.7.2-beta.6 and zero validity triggers. Final source candidate built successfully; real `doctor --fix --non-interactive` completed twice. Assertion-safety and database-dialect ratchets pass; touched-file lint has zero errors and one 704-line owner-dispatch advisory. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. title: fix: bound transcript lists when meetings are inaccessible

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one `transcripts` list call can walk the entire archive when most or all meetings are inaccessible to the caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `TRANSCRIPTS_LIST_MAX` at the tool's pagination owner and return `nextOffset` after every consumed row, including denied rows. This removes the unbounded automatic page walk and its repeated hard-coded page size. The necessary continuation argument, result, and instructions account for the net +10 production lines; no new budget constant or state owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- On current main `1cbfa2c57741c0a69037077bd9bf0730bd220a93`, both new real-store regressions fail: fully denied and partially accessible pages each perform 201 authorization checks instead of stopping at 200. With the fix, each stops at 200 and the next call finds the authorized older meeting.

title: fix(daemon): diagnose split Node installations with effective repair advice
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing diagnostics when a Gateway's Node binary survives removal of the different Node version that holds its OpenClaw package, leaving the next startup to fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

## User Impact

Startup, status, and Doctor explain the split and give repair advice consistent with the existing runtime/pin policy. Hidden `.fnm` roots, symlinked packages, dangling entrypoints, and unreadable version directories are covered. Windows fnm advice selects `installation/node.exe`. The new diagnostic preserves eligibility for existing unattended unsupported-Node repairs.

For an intact installation, explicitly select its Node with `gateway install --runtime-path <path> --force` after stopping the service. If the package is gone, reinstall OpenClaw under a supported Node and run `gateway install --force` from that installation. Operator-owned systemd drop-ins remain under operator control.

## Why This Change Was Made

One audit/advice owner compares physical installation identities and keeps inspection errors diagnostic. The existing installer retains ownership of runtime selection and pins. No config or database schema changes. Advice assumes the version manager’s normal Node binary layout; manually aliased Node binaries inside version directories can produce imprecise advice.

Related: #190512. Original implementation by @DonnieFi; this credited takeover completes the symlink, Windows command, CI assertion, unattended-repair classification, and portable permission-test fixes found during re-review.

## Evidence

- Full untrusted contributor diff reviewed before execution. Contributor execution, installs, builds, and tests are confined to sanitized no-role Crabbox Linux leases.
- Final head `c60caf8dfaf34b64c4096e624541d5aca974981b`: 84 follow-up tests pass across the authority, prefix, and service-audit files (53.56 seconds), with scoped formatting and matching-config lint. The strengthened real-audit/noninteractive-prompter case is red on `fe5033` and green with the one-line classifier fix; operator drop-in and custody regressions remain green. The final 51 Doctor/preview consumer tests also pass (11.21 seconds), for 135 affected tests total. The exact committed follow-up patch matches the tested and packaged remote tree (SHA-256 `69c0146a1b8166162a410f17df95eacfbfbda7c9149cf3f1e2a6d722cbfd7a74`). Unchanged startup inputs retain the earlier five-file proof.
- The four added regression cases are red on contributor head `7fdc14992e` for their intended assertions and green with the repairs. Doctor's two symlink cases use real filesystem links.
- Real nvm/systemd proof with Node A=24.22.1 and B=24.16.0: main has no specific finding and restart fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after B is removed. The contributor head emits startup/Doctor/status diagnostics. The advertised explicit B selection yields an active healthy B/B service; after removal, reinstalling under A plus the advertised install command yields an active healthy A/A service. No service-manager stubs.
- Full-candidate Codex autoreview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean; subsequent fixture, simplification, and runtime-classifier deltas received independent reviews. title: fix(config): redact inline environment credentials in config reads
body:

## What Problem This Solves

Config reads expose inline `env.vars` credentials when their names do not match a secret-name heuristic.

## User Impact

CLI `config get` and Gateway `config.get` snapshots redact inline environment values regardless of their names. title: improve(agents): preserve outcomes across handoffs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Handoffs can over-prescribe a method or treat partial delivery as the end of a task, requiring the user to repeatedly restart already-authorized work. Existing completion guidance also omitted materially greater effort as a reason to consult the owner.

## User Impact

Agents receive a shared default for outcome-focused handoffs and reasonable recovery, while respecting real authority, evidence, budget, pause, and cancellation boundaries. New authority or materially greater time, compute, cost, or scope calls for an owner decision. No permissions, retry engine, scheduling, provisioning, or configuration changes.

**Draft:** live baseline/candidate behavioral evaluation and remaining build/typecheck gates are not complete. This is prompt guidance, not a guarantee of model compliance.

## Why This Change Was Made

One concise five-bullet section covers copy/paste handoffs, receiver recovery, and completion reconciliation. The default runtime and native Codex, Copilot, and Agents API harnesses consume the same section; raw/no-prompt calls retain their existing behavior. Mandatory continuation and verified completion remain requirements. Escalation for new authority, an unavailable external decision, or materially greater effort keeps the unfinished objective open; it is not task completion. This is standing prompt guidance, not detection of the word "handoff".

The simplification pass retained existing owners and machinery: net production growth is 22 lines, largely prompt text and three native call sites. Regression growth is 30 lines, including two parameterized cases and assertions in existing prompt/native tests; the allocation records those distinct delivery boundaries. The largest new file is a 136-line opt-in QA scenario using the existing runner, not new runtime infrastructure. It captures sender composition, clean completion, recovery, pause, and effort-escalation cases; artifact assertions and human semantic adjudication are explicitly separate.

## Evidence

- Target-output authoring probe: each guidance condition drafted three actual copy/paste briefs from mixed preparation notes, a confirmed later local-owner authorization, a narrowly scoped one-review-request limit, a consumed one-paid-attempt budget, and incomplete remote inventory. Both preserved real boundaries without exporting the preparer's one-debugging-attempt/no-app-host suggestion as owner policy, confusing preparation status with a permanent veto, or returning platform proof to an incapable Linux author. The paid-attempt control stayed binding. No material handoff-authoring failure or comparative improvement was observed in this pair; this remains a small task-level-guidance comparison under the same hosting instructions.
- Harder supplemental engineering probe: the seeded offline application passed its shipped smoke test but failed 21 of 23 withheld acceptance cases. Each Sol high/Fast-requested arm had to repair revision/refund selection, exact multi-currency money, timezone/DST filtering, CSV parity, file/module CLI behavior, and output preservation, then build a headless adapter and source-bound proof package. Both the old-guidance and proposed-guidance solutions passed all 23 frozen acceptance cases and independent package checks. Neither received acceptance feedback or repair coaching before submission; later continuations only transferred unchanged ZIP bytes. Initial sandbox-provisioning failures occurred before agent execution and were excluded, then the existing sessions resumed serially in separate directories. **Again no comparative improvement was observed.** This tests a synthetic application under task-level guidance, not the changed installed OpenClaw system prompts.
- Supplemental execution probe: two fresh `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` contexts, high effort and Fast requested, received old versus proposed guidance as task text and completed the same synthetic local proof assignment with real tools. After discovering and discarding an initial shared-directory pair, the rerun used verified separate directories and capture identities. Both restored missing input, repaired setup/harness issues, reconciled a committed capture after an error without redispatch, and delivered independently checked seven-member ZIPs with unchanged candidate/protected-file identities. Both succeeded without follow-up coaching; **no comparative improvement was observed**. The shared hosting system prompt was not swapped, so this is supplemental guidance-influence evidence, not the installed baseline/candidate evaluation.
- Follow-through correction (`38d9ba96aca0ce035aca533df493ba091fc728bb`): restored firm continuation language in delegation and completion guidance. Three assertions in one existing prompt test fail on the preceding PR head and pass on this correction (36.83s wrapper wall time including compilation). Formatting, whitespace, and unchanged generated snapshots pass. Fresh incremental Auto Review against `fd4efe79bb0598b539f1d59daa5ecb38cb92be24` found no P0 issues. Earlier full-candidate results below retain their original scope.
- Telegram-as-base and Discord-as-generated-diff snapshot storage predates this PR; the snapshot generator and channel behavior were not changed.
- Shared full/minimal prompt regression: two expected failures before the guidance, green after. Native Codex full/minimal regression likewise failed before native integration.
- Focused embedded/native/QA catalog run: 176 existing and new cases passed in 88.28s wrapper wall time, including cold compilation. After the final wording reduction, the seven affected assertions passed (60.63s including compilation); unrelated cases were intentionally skipped in that final check. CI seconds are pending.
- Shared prompt/cache and agent-tool prefix-stability companion tests passed. No tool schema or cache lifecycle changes.
- Targeted lint/type-aware checking: 12 touched TypeScript files passed; SDK boundary declarations regenerated. Formatting, SDK export registration, prompt snapshot drift, and whitespace checks passed.

title: fix(gateway): keep verified PR states on passive sidebar rows
body:
## Problem

Sidebar rows watch their PRs passively: they read task publication receipts only and never call GitHub. Those receipts have no PR metadata. After a socket reconnect, a page reload, or reopening the mobile drawer, the client snapshot is cleared. The row then falls back to the generic PR icon, so merged, closed and draft states disappear until someone opens that chat again. On iOS this happens nearly every time the app returns to the foreground.

## Solution

The Gateway already caches GitHub metadata it has verified (`readSessionPullRequestMetadata`, keyed by credential scope, host, repo and number). This change reuses that cache. It adds no new storage and no new lookups:

- **Passive reads peek the cache.** `withCachedPullRequestStates` attaches the last verified state chip (owner, repo, number, branch, title, URL, state) to each receipt. It never starts a read. Diff stats and CI rollups are not included, so sidebar pushes stay small and can't show stale CI. The credential scope is resolved once per host per load, not once per PR.
- **Full reads refresh a stale passive sibling.** A full (foreground) read can verify a task PR state that the watched receipt-only cell for the same session still lacks. When that happens, the passive cell reloads, which reads the receipts cache plus the peek. That happens at most once per verified state, so a cache miss can't turn into a reload every poll. Without this, a long-lived passive cell, such as another browser's open sidebar, would keep serving its old snapshot to reconnecting clients.
- **The client keeps richer details.** When a passive state chip arrives with the same state as a retained full record, the client keeps the full record (CI and diff stats). It only replaces the record when the state changed.
- `removeMembership` moved into `control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts`, next to `addControlUiSessionPrMembership`, to stay under the subscriptions line cap.

Authority does not change. Passive viewers only get state chips that a full viewer of the same receipt audience already gets, fetched with the same shared credential scope. The personal-credential passive path is unchanged.

## Accepted edge case

The cache is held in memory and bounded. After a Gateway restart or eviction, a passive row shows the generic icon until any full view verifies that PR again. Keeping terminal states across restarts would need a durable state column on publication receipts, which is a schema change and is not part of this PR.

## Evidence

- New regression in `control-ui-session-task-prs.test.ts`: an active viewer verifies a merged task PR. An existing passive audience and a reconnecting passive reader both receive `merged`, and no extra GitHub request is made. It fails on the base, passes with the fix, and fails again with only the sibling refresh disabled.
- Unit coverage: passive pushes carry only state-chip fields; a stale passive cell reloads once per verified state even when its cache misses; the client store keeps richer retained details while the state agrees and takes the chip when the state changes.
- Real Gateway + browser e2e (`task-pull-requests.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`): after hydration, a fresh page with the parent row passive shows `data-pull-request-state` and makes no new GitHub requests. It is red on the base (`null`) and green with the fix. `sidebar-pull-requests` e2e also passes.
- Gateway PR suites plus the UI store and indicator tests: 194 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, including typecheck, lint, format and the line cap. The dead-export scan was skipped because of an unrelated existing failure in `src/plugins/worker-retention.ts`.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch range): scoped-clean.
- `control-ui-session-prs-branch.test.ts` has 3 failures that also fail on the unmodified base in this environment.

title: fix: preserve MEMORY.md when Doctor merges fail
body:
Related: #187291 by @syxscott.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can truncate or tear `MEMORY.md` when a legacy root-memory merge write fails. The existing repair archives only `memory.md`, leaving the original canonical memory without a recovery copy.

## User Impact

Failed writes preserve the live canonical memory, and each merge keeps `MEMORY.md.pre-merge` beside the legacy archive. Earlier backups remain intact and a second Doctor run after a completed merge leaves the file unchanged. Workspace directory aliases and existing file/directory permissions remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

This takes over #187291 with Syxscott's atomic publication fix and one small correction: allocate a unique repair directory with `mkdtemp`, because timestamp-only recursive mkdir can reuse a directory and overwrite its backups. Publication uses the existing atomic writer with the actual directory mode, preserved file mode, synced temporary file/parent, and its permission-error copy fallback disabled. Doctor documentation includes the backup location and recovery step.

Syxscott is retained as the source commit author and co-author; Peter Steinberger receives the requested co-author credit. No new abstraction or compatibility path is introduced. Production source grows by 23 lines and tests by 129 lines; the separate test-line allocation covers publication failures, aliases/modes, and the backup collision/idempotency regression.

## Evidence
