title: feat(ui): preview background session starts on their route
body:
## Problem

A Cmd+K background start shows its session row in the sidebar as soon as the Gateway commits it. Opening that row before the Gateway answers `sessions.create` showed an empty chat with only an elapsed timer, often for 20 seconds or more while a worktree or worker was prepared. If the start failed, the session route never showed the failure or any way to retry it.

## Solution

Background starts now get the same optimistic preview the foreground New Session handoff already uses:

- **Key chosen up front:** the client picks the session key before sending, in the same format the Gateway generates and the foreground instant handoff already sends. The session route is known immediately.
- **Preview:** while the start is in flight, that route renders the existing pending-session view. It shows your message, a "Starting…" indicator with the elapsed time below it, and "New session" as the title, or the session's real title once its row exists.
- **Failure:** the same view shows the error and **Try again**. Try again resubmits the same prompt under the same session key, so an open route follows the retry. The Cmd+K notice from the previous PR offers the same retry.
- **Success:** the preview hands the route to the real conversation only after the accepted first turn is retained for display, so there is no empty frame between the preview and the transcript.

**Ownership:**
- `chatSubmissions` (the app-owned display store) gains a keyed set of background previews beside its single foreground handoff slot, plus `creationFor(sessionKey)`. The chat route loaders and the pending view look a preview up by session.
- The new `BackgroundCreatePreview` (`background-create-preview.ts`) is owned by each submission flow: it chooses and keeps the key, and admits, fails or retires the preview. The flow change is four call sites.
- Connection bootstrap no longer gives transcript priority to a session route that is still a preview, matching foreground previews.

The Gateway already accepts an explicit key on `sessions.create`, as the foreground handoff uses. Placement (device or required worker) starts keep their own startup preview and are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `chat-page-pending-create.test.ts`: a background preview on its route shows the prompt, "Starting…" with the elapsed time, and the "New session" title; a failure shows the error and an enabled **Try again** that calls the retry; admission mounts the real pane on the same route.
- `draft-submission-background.test.ts`: the chosen key reaches `sessions.create`; a refused create keeps the preview with its failure; Try again sends the same key and clears the error on the same route object; on success, the accepted turn is already retained when the route admits.
- `chat-submissions.test.ts`: previews are kept per session and only for their owner; a stale handle cannot update or clear a replaced preview; `creating` and `creationFor` are correct.
- New E2E `command-palette-background-preview.e2e.test.ts` (Playwright, mock Gateway): start from Cmd+K with the create deferred, open the session route in-app, see the prompt, "Starting…" with seconds and "New session"; reject, see the error, click Try again (same key), resolve, and see the real conversation on the same URL with the prompt.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, commit mode, P0–P1, with the instant handoff, initial-turn handoff, Gateway `sessions.create` and chat page state as source context) found no actionable findings (`scoped-clean`).
- Unit, at low parallelism on the head rebased onto main: `chat-submissions`, `bootstrap-location`, chat route and pending-create tests, all of `pages/new-session` and `command-palette*` — 1075/1075 pass.
- E2E: every `command-palette-*` and `new-session-page*` file — 57 files, 267/267 pass. This covers the foreground instant handoff and placement startups that share this code.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`/`verify`, `git diff --check`: pass.
- Gap: not run against a live, isolated Gateway with a slow real create; the E2E holds `sessions.create` open (deferred) to simulate it.

Follows #190451 (concurrent Cmd+K starts) and #190417 (optimistic Cmd+K start).

title: fix(ui): own chat bubble ignores the accent color when the viewer's profile is unknown

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the viewer's own (right-side) chat bubble shows an identity color instead of the accent when the Control UI doesn't know the viewer's profile. Examples are Tailscale or trusted-proxy sign-in without a profile, or a connection without self-profile access. Two gateways with the same appearance settings then paint your own messages differently.

## User Impact

User impact: your own bubble always uses the accent, either the theme accent or the accent you picked in Appearance, on every access path. Other participants' bubbles on the left keep their identity colors, and placement is unchanged from `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185821 made own messages use the accent, but it decided "own" only by matching the sender's profile to the viewer's profile id. Placement uses a different rule: a user turn goes on the left only when the viewer's profile is known and the sender is someone else. Everything else is on the right and is the viewer's.

When the viewer's profile isn't known, turns that carry a sender stamp stayed on the right but got that sender's identity hue. Identity tint now follows the same peer decision as placement. title: feat(ui): start Cmd+K sessions concurrently
body:
## Problem

After #190417, Cmd+K closed as soon as a background start was sent. It still kept that start's draft as its only draft, so reopening Cmd+K showed the pending prompt locked on "Starting…". You could not write and start a second prompt until the Gateway answered the first, which can take 20 seconds or more while a worktree or worker is prepared.

## Solution

Each Cmd+K start now owns its own new-session draft once it passes local admission. The palette immediately gets a fresh, empty draft for the next prompt.

- **New owner:** `PaletteReleasedStarts` (`palette-session-starts.ts`) holds released starts until they settle. It observes each draft's own transition out of `submitting`, so reconnect resumptions and retries are tracked without polling.
- **Success:** the existing "<session>: Running" notice with **Open session**. Acceptance no longer closes a palette that now holds a newer prompt.
- **Failure:** the notice reads "Session didn't start: <error>" with **Try again**, which resubmits the same prompt, attachments and settings. Failed starts keep their prompt in memory, capped at the eight newest.
- **Owner changes:** a start never reports to, or retries for, a different account or Gateway. Each released start records its presentation scope and settles silently under another one.
- **Rejected first turn:** the created session already keeps the rejected prompt with its own retry, so the palette's duplicate recovery is removed: `retainRejectedPrompt`, the `initial-turn-rejected` gate, `onRejectedPrompt` and the palette "Open session" recovery button. The notice's **Open session** still opens the session.
- The "Edit prompt" reopen path from #190417 is replaced by **Try again**, because the palette no longer holds the failed prompt.

## Accepted limits

- Opening a start's session before the Gateway answers still shows an empty chat; the next PR shows the prompt there.
- Clicking a notice action (such as **Try again**) leaves keyboard focus on the page body, because the notice removes its own button. This is how all notice actions behave today.

## Evidence

- New `palette-session-starts.test.ts`: one notice per failure, Try again resubmits once, at most eight failures are kept, accepted and aborted starts settle silently, and a replaced owner gets no notice and no retry.
- `palette-session-draft.test.tsx`: starts a second prompt while the first is pending, retries the failed first start with the same prompt, and a double Try again sends only once. The account-change case now asserts no notice; it caught a real cross-owner notice during development, which the scope check fixes.
- Unit: `ui/src/pages/new-session/`, `ui/src/components/command-palette*`, `chat-submissions`, `chat-page-pending-create` — 948/948 pass.
- E2E, Playwright against the mock Gateway, all `command-palette-*` and `new-session-page*` files: 264/266 on the first run. The two failures were the notice-focus assertion described above. The updated create and images files then pass. A new case starts a second prompt while the first is deferred, rejects the first, and retries it.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint on changed files, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: pass.

Production change: about +110/−90 lines, with a new 110-line owner module, net of the removed launcher-rejection path.

title: fix: clear no-op migration warnings for disabled plugins
body:
Fixes #190411

## What Problem This Solves

A disabled plugin with retained settings can leave a data/settings migration warning permanently pending even when none of its source data exists.

## User Impact

Doctor clears a confirmed no-op without enabling the plugin or registering its runtime or tools. Retained settings, including `config.enabled: false`, survive. Detected source data, failed inspection, missing contracts, and settings that still need repair keep the obligation pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Doctor contract checks both migration phases without repair authority. The migration-preparation owner now requests that inspection for inactive pending owners with retained config, validates the settings without their exclusion, and settles through the existing ledger/config/lifecycle owners with a warning. Existing dormant deferral and re-arming for owners without protected config remain unchanged.

Main already prevents the original empty-config runtime registration through #178165 (`36b28bb0f51d9006bae3baafa47959b3332e3c8a`). No published version tag contains it as of November 1, 2026; v2026.10.9 and v2026.10.10-beta.5 both lack it. This PR does not publish a release or promise a backport.

## Evidence

- **RED on main:** [tests-only CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41319377412/job/124886590516), head `4f35e574cfef661fc81721e58fd625f48b1d93a0`: absent-source Doctor case failed with the exact unavailable-owner pending obligation; 26 sibling/control tests passed. Source-present controls cover both phases, preserve source bytes, and forbid disabled-owner migration/runtime execution. A separate TS2532 fixture error was corrected before this implementation push; it is not the behavioral RED.
- **Existing startup fix confirmed:** the same CI job passed the production startup/loader test with the entire plugin config withheld. A restart-health test also covers successful readiness with a non-activated migration-held plugin diagnostic.
- **GREEN on exact head `a6d7a130a320dfec0870173039038ad563cc4789`:** [Doctor lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41320504219/job/124890065341) passes all four inactive-owner scenarios (no source, source in either phase, detector failure); 60 tests pass across its 6 files. [Restart-health lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41320504219/job/124890065556) passes both activated cases; 188 tests pass across its 2 files. Full exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41320504219) completed successfully, including all PostgreSQL conformance lanes, typechecks, lint, and the aggregate gate. The first implementation run found a test-only empty-field expectation mismatch; the corrected assertion follows the existing public snapshot contract.
- Focused lint of touched TS files (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Local worker compilation was stopped under the production-host restriction; a queued Crabbox request was canceled, so no remote command result is claimed for that lease. CI supplies the worker-build and broad proof; no full historical binary upgrade was run.
- Baseline CI file durations: Doctor deferral 146.13 s, startup 9.64 s. The four new Doctor cases took about 16.4 s combined. The Doctor boundary is necessary to exercise real config retention, SQLite obligations, both migration phases, and runtime admission together; helper-only tests miss this activation-policy failure.
- **Review:** shared autoreview, Codex, P0–P2, complete committed range `e69dca056a9b..a6d7a130a320`, scoped-clean with no findings. Health projection owner context was included after the test expectation correction. Local ClawSweeper CLI is unavailable; [one hosted fallback review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190441#issuecomment-6559945179). It is advisory and does not replace the completed independent autoreview or CI.
- **Simplification:** reused the existing read-only inspector and settlement owners; no config/schema/public SDK additions. Production delta: +56 lines. Net test growth: 101 lines, covered by a separate allocation for these regressions.

Co-authored-by: steipete <58493+steipete@users.noreply.github.com>

<details>
<summary>Hosted review disposition</summary>

Hosted review disposition for the reviewed head `a6d7a130a320dfec0870173039038ad563cc4789`:

- The review reports **zero code findings**. There is no identified schema, storage-layout, or retained-data compatibility defect in this patch. It invokes existing read-only detectors and settles through the existing ledger owner; the regression uses real Doctor preflight/config/SQLite ownership and proves that retained settings and present source bytes survive. Full exact-head CI, including all PostgreSQL conformance, is now green.

title: fix(imap): retry temporary DKIM verification failures
body:
Supersedes #150980, thanks @coaiMax.
Related: #150558.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes legitimate IMAP mail being permanently skipped when DKIM key lookup has a temporary DNS failure but DMARC reports fail.

## User Impact

Temporary verification failures enter the existing bounded retry path. Mail stays rejected until a later verification meets the configured authentication floor; permanent authentication failures and unsigned mail still reject by default. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify exact nested DKIM `temperror` results at the existing sender gate. Keep authentication strength, admission thresholds, sender allowlists, trusted-header opt-ins, unsigned-body rejection, and the three-attempt retry budget unchanged. Consolidating the mapper's duplicate unverified-result returns reduces production code by one line.

Contributor credit: every replacement commit carries `Co-authored-by: lijing <li.jing25@xydigit.com>`, the human author of both original commits. Contributor code was read through GitHub and was not checked out or run.

## Evidence

- **Red on main:** [CI run 41319323750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41319323750/job/124886444266), test-only head `882323bdca2cea43795432c0fbe19baa2a322b28` on main `e69dca056a9b089020cc530df4be4c8accc2ee0b`: both real DNS recovery cases fail because the watcher records `gate=dmarc-fail` instead of `gate=authentication-temperror retry=true`; 53 tests pass, including all permanent-rejection controls. File wall time: 44.02 s, with approximately 3 s in tests and 88% in transformation.
- **Green after:** [CI run 41319864098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41319864098/job/124888064245), repaired head `af9eb73a82271ae39fdd23bc591fc1ead3230bfd`: both DNS recovery cases and all permanent-rejection controls pass. The extension job passed 79 tests across three files in 42.74 s (93% transformation; ETIMEOUT recovery 118 ms, ESERVFAIL recovery 80 ms). The full CI run completed successfully, including lint, type checks, baseline ratchets, and security-fast.
- The regression uses loopback IMAP, real RSA signing and real mailauth verification, and DNS ETIMEOUT/ESERVFAIL fixtures. It asserts no dispatch or cursor advance on temporary failure, then reauthentication and exactly one dispatch after DKIM and DMARC pass. Negative controls assert rejection without retry for DKIM fail, permerror, none, and neutral. This proves the watcher-to-dispatch boundary; a live mailbox/model session was not run.
- Local autoreview of the complete replacement against `e69dca056a9b089020cc530df4be4c8accc2ee0b`: **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**. Included the sender gate, watcher, fixture helpers, configuration, mailauth version, authentication ladder, and operator documentation. The reviewer confirmed that only exact DKIM temperror gains retryability and no authentication floor is bypassed.
- Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Focused local tests could not reach the tests because the compiled-worker prerequisite needs unrelated plugin dependencies; a smaller probe reached the same prerequisite and was stopped. Local type-aware lint was stopped at its broader prerequisite. Testbox was queued and stopped; CI supplies execution and broad checks. No full local suite, packaging, container, or browser proof was run.

title: fix(ui): prevent comment lifecycle browser test response timeouts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent 30-second response timeouts in the UI comment lifecycle browser test, observed on unrelated CI heads ([main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41284747343), [composer styling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41305234131)).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This repairs the test's coordination of history reconciliation and attachment reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

History reconciliation can cancel the initial attachment reader. The test incorrectly treats its replacement as a later ticket-renewal read and holds it behind a gate that cannot open until the initial response completes.

Hold attachment metadata until the triggered history refresh and native pane render complete, then acknowledge that the body request has started before checking the pending-read UI. Preserve the existing content, height, cache, renewal and remount assertions.

## Evidence

| Mode | Unchanged base target failures | Final target failures |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Complete test file, alone | 1/20 | 0/20 |
| Original 137-file CI shard order, 4 workers | 0/1 | 0/20 |
| Complete test file, four CPU burners on four CPUs | 1/5 | 0/20 |

One of the 20 full-shard replays also failed the unchanged `browser-auth-recovery.e2e.test.ts:240` while waiting for a sign-in popup. All six comment lifecycle cases passed in that replay. The complete shard totals were 11,559 passed / 1 failed; the auth failure is retained and was not rerun. The suites use isolated fork workers and fresh browser contexts. title: fix(update): recover unpublished activations after lease database loss
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reboot can remove the temporary lease database while an npm activation is still `prepared`, causing its recovery helper to refuse repair and even status despite nothing being published.

Fixes part of #167557. Credit to [Subseaking’s analysis](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/167557#issuecomment-6559108569), which identified the unpublished state and exact previous installation/launcher identities.

## User Impact

Recovery can retire this unused preparation automatically, preserve its evidence by rename, and let updates proceed. Status reports the retained operation without recreating the missing lease database. This is a partial fix; published-operation first-hop recovery and the issue’s other reported symptoms remain outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Original and separately staged helpers now use the existing fresh-owner settlement path for a missing lease only when phase is `prepared`, intent is null, publications are empty, and the live package, launcher directory and launcher identities match `previous`. It logs a warning and archives the journal, control directory, candidate and that operation’s remaining npm stage. Unrelated stages remain with their owners. Existing publication, rollback, ownership and remount protections stay in place.

Ordinary update/repair on the base already settled untouched preparations; this adds the missing helper path, warning, launcher verification and stage preservation. Status no longer requires lease authority or repairs permissions.

The lease DB stays in its existing temporary location. Moving it safely needs compatible coordination with older updaters and multiple profiles; a copy would create competing lease owners, while the store rejects file symlinks and hard links. The follow-up and first-hop limitation are documented.

## Evidence

- RED on the main base: missing-lease status and original-helper repair refused; separate-helper repair required a remount; automatic settlement lacked the requested warning (4 failing regression cases, 7 controls passing).
- GREEN: 39 focused tests across lease recovery, real separate-helper process invocation, update admission and repair/triage. The final archive-owner extraction was rechecked with all 11 lease-recovery cases. A proof-only follow-up then passed all 14 cases, adding a real competing executor and SQLite ownership reassignment before journal closure and evidence archival (10.56s wrapper).
- Ordinary package repair (35 tests) and remount recovery (37 tests) passed, including rollback, changed launchers, ownership conflicts and archive failures.
- Targeted oxlint with type checking, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation is PR CI; no local containers, broad suites, packaging or live Gateway changes.
- Local final four-file run: 138.31s including compiler preparation. Observed test time: lease recovery 3.40s, helper commands 14.74s, CLI admission 61.23s, repair/triage 1.92s. The long CLI cases are existing process-custody/admission tests. CI completed at 2026-11-01T15:36:26Z; summed job execution time was 9572 seconds, including broad conformance lanes. Per-file CI timing was not separately collected.
- Simplification: reused settlement/executor/archive owners and removed lease authority from descriptive status. Production growth is necessary for narrow qualification, warning, read-only inspection and evidence preservation. The 254-line test allocation protects these distinct boundaries and refusal controls.

Independent Codex autoreview completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 for the production repair and final proof-only follow-up. A follow-up P2 test gap (earlier identity refusal instead of actual ownership admission) was corrected and independently re-reviewed clean. Exact-head CI [41319946851](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41319946851) completed successfully for `48f5a3152e7b031ff9df6d59a71063d336d2137c`; the native watcher returned GREEN (superseded cancellations excluded). No release is included.

The hosted review found no introduced correctness defect and requested stronger authority proof. The added regressions reassign the real `managed_update_handoffs.owner` row immediately before the production journal transition/archive, then require the actual executor-ownership refusal. Before close, control bytes stay unchanged; before archive, the closed receipt and candidate stay in place and no archive is created. A separately acquired executor owning the recreated store refuses helper repair on the historical identity and refuses settlement on actual current executor ownership. These use production owners, without new hooks or authority code.

Compatibility scope: this PR changes no journal schema, descriptor fields, lease schema or protocol; it consumes the existing external-helper version-1 journal and preserves its descriptor and file identities. A fault-injected released-installation upgrade with user settings/data was not run: Crabbox queued and was stopped, per host policy. Focused persisted-state/helper proof and PR CI supply the available evidence; old sealed helpers are explicitly unchanged.

title: feat(ui): release Cmd+K launcher as soon as a background start is sent
body:
## Problem

Starting a background session from Cmd+K kept the palette open with a locked "Starting…" prompt until the Gateway accepted `sessions.create`. On a busy Gateway, where the worktree or required worker is prepared before the first turn, that can take 20 seconds or more. The session row was already in the sidebar, but the palette kept blocking the user.

## Solution

The Cmd+K start is now optimistic. All changes are in `PaletteSessionDraft`, which already owns the palette's submission:

- **Close on send.** Local checks inside `DraftSubmissionFlow.submit` run synchronously. If the draft is still submitting after `submit()` is called, the start has passed those checks, so the palette closes right away. Closing keeps the request alive (the "A closed launcher still owns its submitted transaction" contract), and the user returns to their foreground chat with their draft and caret unchanged.
- **Success:** unchanged. The existing "<session>: Running" notice with **Open session** still appears.
- **Rejected first turn:** unchanged. The session notice and in-palette recovery still apply.
- **Create failure or unknown outcome:** a new notice shows "Session didn't start: <error>" with an **Edit prompt** action. That action reopens Cmd+K with the prompt, attachments, mentions and inline error kept, ready to retry. Previously this error only appeared inside the open palette.
- **Dismiss while pending.** Escape, the toggle and the modal's cancel action now close the palette even while a start is pending. Reopening shows the pending start as read-only, and a second Mod+Enter cannot start a second session.

Nothing changes in the Gateway, the protocol or `DraftSubmissionFlow`.

## Accepted limits

- While one start is in flight, Cmd+K shows that pending start, so a second prompt has to wait until it settles. Running several starts at once would need a separate `NewSessionDraft` for each submission. That should be its own change.
- Opening the session from the sidebar before the Gateway dispatches the first turn still shows an empty chat until the turn arrives. Showing the prompt there needs a run identity agreed between the client and the Gateway. Follow-up.
- If the palette was reopened from the failure notice, closing it again cannot return focus to the notice button, because the notice is gone.

## Evidence

- New regression `releases the launcher once create is sent and reopens a failed prompt from its notice` (`palette-session-draft.test.tsx`): **fails on `main`** (palette stays open) and passes with this change.
- Updated the palette unit and E2E suites for the new behavior (closed after send, reopen to see the pending or rejected state, retry from the failure notice):
  - Unit: `palette-session-draft`, `command-palette*`, `draft-submission-background`, `palette-session-menus` — 130/130 pass.
  - E2E: `ui/src/e2e/command-palette-create.e2e.test.ts` (Playwright, real Control UI build against the mock Gateway, with a deferred create) — 8/8 pass. It covers local and device starts, the rejected first turn, and failed create with retry.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, oxlint on changed files (0 errors; 1 existing warning in untouched code), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: all pass.
- Review: local ClawSweeper is not installed on this host, so this uses the maintainer fallback route. Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, base `7c26e8c` → head tree `aaa76c0` (same tree as `c863e44`), P0–P1, with `draft-submission-flow.ts` and `session-notice-owner.ts` as source context) found no actionable findings (`scoped-clean`). One hosted ClawSweeper review was also requested.
- Gap: not yet tested against a live, isolated Gateway with a slow real create. The E2E holds `sessions.create` open (deferred) to simulate a slow create.

Production delta: +38/−7 across `palette-session-draft.ts`, `command-palette-state.ts`, `command-palette-view.tsx` and English copy.

## Problem

One-shot (`at`) automations in the session Details → Automations list rendered through the generic cron presenter as `At 11/1/2026, 11:00 AM`: an "At" prefix plus a full numeric date with year. In the narrow Details row the long string truncated the automation name and the time itself, so the row read as a confusing timestamp rather than "when does this run". `nonCronSessionAutomationSchedule` (the session-automation row owner, shared by the desktop Details panel, mobile Details sheet and mobile automation list) now formats `at` schedules itself in the viewer's local time zone:

title: improve(ui): shorten catalog dashboard browser replay
body:
Related: #189670

## What Problem This Solves

The default catalog dashboard browser replay spends at least 72.5 seconds in fixed host-time waits even when `OPENCLAW_CATALOG_DASHBOARD_MS=0`.

## User Impact

Faster browser replay with the same 24 triggers, exact catalog request counts, reconnect assertion, and capability-refresh assertion. No product behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compact mode pauses the Playwright clock after boot and advances it while actions finish. Every row joins expected catalog reads, delivered mock replies, UI readiness, and idle callbacks, then crosses another four seconds of browser time and joins work again before recording counts. Zero-read rows cross the same window. This covers the 2.5-second metadata debounce, 750 ms chat idle deadline / 50 ms fallback, and 500 ms shell idle delay.

The observer wraps the actual socket returned by the routed mock constructor. A held catalog reply must appear in its pending-ID set before release; that control failed with the inactive observer and passed with the correction. Config timestamps and synthetic capability expiry use browser time. Positive-duration elapsed-time pacing and its timeout formula are retained.

Net test lines: **+133**; production lines: **0**. The remaining growth implements wire/idle observation, paused-clock action driving, and the held-reply control required to make settlement meaningful. The final cleanup shares the clock-poll loop and uses one response listener per socket, reducing the prior +137-line candidate without dropping assertions. No shared helper, production hook, config option, or budget allocation is added.

## Evidence

The following measurements preceded that final mechanical cleanup. Same focused runner and isolated Chromium environment; host load varied, so every trial is shown. Baseline was at `b2bfad1071b0`; the final candidate is based on `87ba257f66d0`, with identical target/catalog/settlement owners before the test edit.

| Trial | Before case (s) | After case (s) | Before Vitest total (s) | After Vitest total (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 88.546 | 4.445 | 106.86 | 19.12 |
| 2 | 95.083 | 4.525 | 128.38 | 19.21 |
| 3 | >120, timeout | 4.569 | 174.87 | 19.18 |
| Median | **95.083** | **4.525** | **128.38** | **19.18** |

The third baseline is right-censored above 120 seconds; its ordering still determines the three-trial median. Measured case-median reduction: **90.558 s (95.2%)**. Vitest-total reduction: **109.20 s (85.1%)**. After-command walls: 20.739 / 20.622 / 20.667 s (median 20.667 s).

Baseline trial 3 stopped after `revisit-main-b`. One bounded original-file rerun reproduced the 120-second timeout at the same stage (reporter case 127.621 s, Vitest total 145.27 s). Diagnostics showed a connected Gateway and ready UI, without recorded browser errors. Passing compact replays do not establish the cause or repair of that inherited navigation/deadline failure.

Final-commit browser proof ran on **Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6bqkarv0ezmej27g2sytzje`**, [run 41315520238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41315520238). The remote command verified head `b65e96ab3007035937c282524d8c5b96b66d79df` and test blob `401049ebb380447129aac454eb6d86a277941b48` before running:

| Final-commit check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean replay | **PASS**, 24 rows, 6.135 s case |
| Extra immediate catalog read | **Killed**: `commands-only` 1 vs 0; `catalog-change` 2 vs 1 |
| Extra read delayed 1500 ms | **Killed** by the same exact-count assertion |

For both delayed-read rows, browser timestamps showed initial settlement at +100 ms and the read firing at +1500 ms: **1.4 seconds after settlement**, inside the old three-second window. Both mutations and their logging probes were restored, and the remote command checked a clean diff for the two temporarily edited files.

The aggregate Crabbox command exited **0**; the owned lease stopped after success. The backing Actions Testbox step may show cancellation when Blacksmith stops the delegated session. An initial Testbox attempt stopped before testing because its synced checkout lacked dependencies; the retry used the documented frozen-lockfile bootstrap entirely on the remote VM.

Additional validation:

- Touched-file format, focused lint, typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed after cleanup. Typecheck uses a scratch config extending the canonical UI E2E graph with this test as its sole include root.
- Retained metadata owner suite: **13 passed** in earlier focused proof; no shared helpers changed.
- Positive-duration mode with `OPENCLAW_CATALOG_DASHBOARD_MS=90000` passed all 24 rows in earlier proof (137.683 s case). An exploratory tiny positive duration hit the unchanged 120-second budget under load; no timeout was increased.
- Isolated Codex autoreview of committed head `b65e96ab3007` against base `87ba257f66d0`: **scoped-clean through P3**, no actionable findings. Review inspected source only; no project code or browser tests executed.
- Rechecked #164863's actual file list and an exact target-file search before editing; no target/helper overlap.

Final browser execution occurred only on Testbox after the production-host redirect. At publisher closeout PR CI was still running, with no failing checks reported. It serves each bundle through `gateway.controlUi.root` (configured roots opt out of the build-identity check), swapping staged copies by rename between samples so base and head share one Gateway.

Per page it sends one real wheel event to the top and records wheel→first-message-change and wheel→idle wall time, ScriptDuration/TaskDuration/Layout/RecalcStyle deltas, long tasks, heap, rendered rows, and every `chat.history` read (latency, bytes, message count). title: improve(ui): older chat history pages no longer rebuild every loaded row
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading an older history page in a long chat gets slower the more history is already loaded, because each page rebuilt the transcript items for every loaded message.

## User Impact

Scrolling back through a long, idle conversation now builds transcript items for about one page's worth of messages each time, however deep the history goes. What renders does not change: rows, grouping and keys match a full rebuild. While a run is live (streaming, queued input, tools in flight, compaction, subagent wait), the transcript still takes the full build.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the only structural change is an older prefix (the retained messages are the same objects) and the session is idle, `buildCachedChatItems` rebuilds just the new page with the first retained turns as its seam. It then keeps the retained rows only if:

- the seam turn renders the same with and without the page, and matches the retained rows;
- the page cannot change anything transcript-wide: display order, row keys (source-key collisions), the first owner of a canvas or inline view, index-keyed compaction/reset dividers, model-selection state, participant count, or prompts that reply-to-current answers resolve against.

Any other case takes the full build. The build records those facts (`chat-thread-facts.ts`); `chat-thread-prepend.ts` makes the reuse decision; `chat-thread.ts` stays the cache owner and stabilizes only the rebuilt head. The reuse decision is only needed once an older page lands, so it stays out of the chat boot graph: `chat-thread.ts` imports it on the first change that grows the front of loaded history, and that prepend takes the full build (today's behavior) while it loads.

Accepted limits: live runs always fall back. A page that shares one of the facts above with retained history (for example, a reused message id or a redelivered canvas) also falls back, so that page costs what it does today.

## Evidence

**Work count** (messages passed to `buildChatItems` for each 1,000-message older page): base = every loaded message (4,000 → 30,000); head = 1,032 at every depth.

**Timing.** Measured in a vitest/jsdom bench (not committed): a 30,000-message synthetic session, 1,000-message pages, 5 interleaved base/head pairs on a shared host (load 4–10). Values are ms, median / p95.

| older pages | build base | build head | chain base / head | index base / head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2–5 | 40.6 / 57.2 | 18.1 / 26.3 | 5.9 / 6.4 | 7.8 / 7.8 |
| 11–15 | 121.6 / 150.8 | 17.0 / 23.5 | 19.3 / 22.0 | 29.2 / 31.5 |
| 21–25 | 272.2 / 315.0 | 18.1 / 28.6 | 42.6 / 41.7 | 66.4 / 64.5 |
| 26–30 | 336.6 / 401.6 | 20.3 / 35.0 | 59.1 / 52.2 | 84.5 / 79.9 |

**Equivalence.** New tests in `chat-thread-incremental.test.ts`:
- At every seam split of 150-message sessions, the spliced items deep-equal the full builder's. Sessions cover tools, `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield` handoffs with acknowledgments, inter-session results, canvas, compaction, reasoning, internal-system turns, steers, transcript display positions, model selections, failure streaks, heartbeats, search open, hidden tool calls, archived and single-person sessions.
- One-collision variants: a reused message id, a repeated run prompt, a late reply-to-current for an older run, a redelivered canvas, a model switch, a second participant, and unkeyed dividers.
- Successive older pages, so facts carry across splices.
- Each variant asserts a minimum number of seams that reused rows, so fallbacks cannot make a pass trivial. Disabling any single check fails a variant, except the explicit participant-count check, which the seam comparison also enforces.

**RED on `origin/main`, GREEN on head:** the work-count test (3,000 messages built vs. < 1,100) and the per-variant reuse minimums.

**Chat boot bundle** (`pnpm ui:build && pnpm ui:check-performance`). title: fix(ui): earlier chat pages still slow down as loaded history grows
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in long chat sessions, each "load earlier messages" page still costs more main-thread time than the last, because committing the page re-read every message already loaded instead of only the new page.

## User Impact

User impact: scrolling back through very long sessions keeps a flat pane-side cost per older page; the history merge, session projection, and snapshot cache no longer scale with how much history is already on screen. No behavior or visible change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #190249 the older-page commit still did three O(all loaded) passes per page:

- **Overlap detection** (`prependUniqueNativeMessages`) computed the source identity of every loaded row. An older page ends where the loaded transcript begins, so overlap can only lead it; the scan now stops at the first loaded source the page lacks.
- **Projection publication** rebuilt the session projection over the whole transcript (`createSessionProjection` reads every row's identity) and then restored provenance through an occurrence map. A new `prependChatSessionProjectionMessages` in `history-merge.ts` (the projection owner) classifies only the page and keeps every loaded entry as-is. Entry classification only carries state forward, so older rows cannot change the loaded entries after them; this is exactly what the old full rebuild produced, because every loaded row was restored from its existing entry. A changed projection scope still falls back to the full republish.
- **Snapshot cache bound** (`boundChatSessionSnapshot`) weighed every message before trimming from the oldest end. It now weighs from the newest row and stops once the rows alone exceed the 12 MiB budget, then resumes the unchanged trim loop at the next sequence-group boundary. The retained window, its pagination, and `weight === JSON.stringify(snapshot).length` are unchanged.

Accepted edge cases (named, not coded around):
- Pairing-QR retention is skipped for the prepend: loaded entries keep their own QR blocks and transcript rows never carry them (pairing media is live-only).
- An unserializable message older than the retained cache window is now trimmed unread instead of evicting the whole snapshot. Gateway history is JSON, so this needs a locally constructed non-JSON row.
- If a loaded transcript were ever out of source order at its oldest edge, an overlapping duplicate past the first non-matching row would no longer be removed (visible, recoverable by reload). Pages come from transcript cursors, so the overlap is always the leading run.

Unchanged and intentionally out of scope: the pending-user adoption scan (one property pass over entries, no identity reads), the O(N) pointer copies of the immutable message/entry arrays, and render-side transcript building (`chat-thread*.ts`, `components/chat-transcript-*`), which another lane owns.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: per older page, pane-side message reads and commit time stay flat as loaded history grows (base grows linearly).

**Work count and time per 1,000-message older page** through the real pane entry point (`ChatPaneHistory.loadOlderMessages` → prepend → projection → `commitCurrentChatHistorySnapshot`), jsdom/Node, 40,000-message synthetic session (user / assistant with tool call / tool result rows, ~130–600 characters of text each), 5 measured pages per depth after 2 warmups, two interleaved base → candidate runs (B A B A) on a loaded shared host (load avg 10–30). "Metadata reads" counts every `__openclaw` read (identity, source identity, sequence, serialization).

| Loaded before page | Base metadata reads/page | Candidate | Base median ms (max), runs 1 / 2 | Candidate median ms (max), runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~4–9k | 41,006 → 69,007 | 9,002–9,006 | 5.9 (5.9) / 7.5 (20.6) | 3.2 (3.3) / 2.8 (2.9) |
| ~14–19k | 111,007 → 139,010 | 9,002–9,006 | 10.2 (12.5) / 11.4 (14.3) | 3.4 (3.5) / 3.9 (17.0) |
| ~26–31k | 207,867 → 243,870 | 8,004–8,008 | 23.2 (33.0) / 18.8 (40.1) | 2.4 (2.5) / 2.1 (2.3) |

Candidate reads are ~8–9 per *page* row and independent of depth; base adds ~7 reads per *loaded* row per page. The 17.0 ms candidate max is a single loaded-host outlier; the other four measured samples in that cell were 3.4–5.9 ms.

**Regression tests (red on `origin/main`, green here):**
- `chat-pane-history.test.ts` "prepends an older page without rereading the loaded transcript": loaded rows read during one older-page load — base 1,000 of 1,000, candidate 1.
- `history-message-identity.test.ts` "bounds prepend serialization": loaded rows inspected — base 1,000, candidate `overlap + 1` (1 and 51).
- `session-message-cache.test.ts` "measures the trimmed envelope once and never weighs the older rows it drops": rows weighed — base 4,000, candidate retained + 1 (3,018); weight still equals `JSON.stringify(snapshot).length`.

**Checks run:**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat ui/src/lib/chat`: 637 files, 7,646 tests passed.
- Same paths under `vitest.ui-isolated.config.ts` (includes `chat-pane-history.test.ts`, `chat-pane.test.ts`): 32 files, 490 tests passed.
- Browser E2E (`vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`, production build, Chromium): `chat-history-prepend-anchor.e2e.test.ts`, `chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts`: 2 files, 20 tests passed (prepend anchoring across shared/manual/touch/momentum variants, coalesced activity at 390/1440 px, empty/failed/retry earlier-history loads).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`: pass. oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK.
- Local autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

**Gaps:** the workload above is an uncommitted scratch vitest bench (pane from `chat-pane-history.test-support.ts`, scripted `chat.history` pages, counting getter on `__openclaw`), kept out of the tree to hold test-line growth to the three regression assertions. I also did not rerun the lead's real-Gateway + production-bundle CPU profile at 30,000 messages; the counts above come from the real pane entry point with a synthetic Gateway in jsdom. The remaining per-page browser cost there is render-side transcript building, which this PR does not touch.

title: chore: investigate sandbox checkpoint lease loss
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Investigation of sandbox preparation lasting about 22 minutes before losing its reconciliation lease. **Closed without a verified fix. The proposed five-second reuse probe budget is withdrawn.**

## User Impact

No shipped behavior change. The proposal did not demonstrate a repair of renewal during authoritative synchronization and could pause runtimes sooner on large workspaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead review corrected the initial attribution: reuse probing precedes runtime quiescence, which precedes authoritative canonical checkpoint synchronization. Both synchronization sites add to one `synchronizeCanonical` timing key. The recorded quiescence phase therefore contradicts attributing the entire failed operation to a lease-aborted reuse probe. The aggregate timing cannot split the duration between sites.

## Evidence

Against original base `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094`, temporary isolated production-path probes held canonical scan I/O and post-commit checkpoint acknowledgement beyond the initial custody lease lifetime. Both observed further committed renewals and completed reconciliation with the expected file contents. A controlled-clock test also confirmed repeated phase durations accumulate under one key. Three tests passed across two focused shards in 12.08 seconds.

These passing controls do not establish what blocked the production renewal. The state writer serializes individual native commands, while manifest reads/computation use separate workers and a retained callback alone does not occupy the writer. A busy native writer, delayed renewal reply, or event-loop stall remains unproven. No deterministic red-on-base renewal defect was established, so there is no justified production fix to land.

title: improve(database): avoid repeated PostgreSQL search snippet work
body:
Supersedes #188951, thanks @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL version 2 text searches spend database CPU computing the same headline twice for each snippet.

## User Impact

Search returns the same results and punctuation-preserving snippets with one headline evaluation per SQL result row. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PostgreSQL snippet owner now reuses normalized text and its headline through scalar subqueries. Two `OFFSET 0` fences prevent PostgreSQL from expanding those expressions at each reference. Existing candidate limits and ranking stay in their owners.

Production delta is +3/-3 (net 0): the duplicated headline expression disappears. The existing migration test gains 21 lines to pin the returned snippet and inspect the real PostgreSQL plan; its separate allocation covers exactly that regression growth. Simplification reuses the existing fixture without another helper or test setup.

## Evidence

- Acceptance: preserve the result ID and exact snippet bytes, with one headline and one punctuation-normalization expression in the PostgreSQL plan.
- Base `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094` plus the regression: expected result and snippet pass; the headline-count assertion fails (four plan occurrences across the Limit/scan outputs; the expression itself contains two evaluations).
- Replacement: 15/15 tests pass across PostgreSQL text migration, engine search conformance, and session-search product flow. This includes ranking, filtering, bounds, literal/prefix matching, and a late punctuation-joined match. Test runtime: 18.90 seconds total; runner including fixture compilation: 53.56 seconds. The changed migration test takes 172 ms.
- Real PostgreSQL in a task-owned rootless Podman container capped at 4 CPUs and 8 GiB. No production database or Gateway state was used. The contributor head was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed.
- Scoped formatting, lint, typecheck (the two changed TypeScript files and their dependencies), and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation runs in PR CI.
- Independent autoreview (P0–P2) completed `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41305632844) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Full shard job times were 1,230 / 1,283 / 1,326 seconds, including setup and the broader suite; these are not the incremental cost of this regression.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190309#issuecomment-6557864724) found no actionable correctness or security defects on the same head.

This establishes reduced expression evaluation, not an end-to-end latency claim. The PostgreSQL product harness exercises search through the tool and Gateway handler; no live model/Gateway deployment was run on the production host.

title: fix(xai): keep Talk connected after an interrupted answer is replaced
body:
Supersedes #184210, thanks @Marvinthebored

Closes #184207

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes xAI Talk disconnecting when speech interrupts an answer and xAI starts its replacement without sending the interrupted answer's terminal event.

## User Impact

Talk continues with the replacement answer, discarding late output from the interrupted answer. Genuine provider errors and invalid overlapping responses remain errors. No configuration changes or migrations are needed. Accepted edge case: a downstream completion observer that throws remains a logged application fault and may require restarting the call; this fix does not add arbitrary-observer recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI adapter already recognizes the new speech and identified successor, but it replaces its own response ID while Talk still owns the predecessor. Settle that interrupted response as cancelled before publishing its successor, using the existing speech/response state and completion callback.

Production delta: +13/-9 lines (net +4). Removed duplicate response-ID assembly and a redundant guard; the remaining growth supplies cancellation dispatch and its callback-close check without adding state or relaxing shared relay ownership.

## Evidence

- A real loopback WebSocket drives the publicly registered xAI plugin through Talk's production session harness and relay ownership. The regression fails on main `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094` with `Realtime provider output has no live response owner.` and passes with the fix.
- Covers distinct cancelled/completed turns, preserved user transcription, discarded stale audio/text/tools, ordinary overlap rejection, provider-error propagation, and fatal malformed-audio closure. The 163-line regression has a dedicated test-line allocation because existing plugin-only tests do not compose relay ownership.
- 54 focused xAI lifecycle tests passed. Targeted type checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation runs in PR CI.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the final local diff against the main commit above: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The review included the bridge, protocol, relay ownership, session harness/runtime, and existing xAI lifecycle tests.

Proof limits: synthetic provider events over a real local WebSocket; no paid xAI call, physical microphone, or full Gateway boot. Contributor source was read as a diff and was never checked out or executed. Final regression: 409 ms test time, 46.25 s wall time including a cold compiled-worker build (the earlier warm run took 8.76 s). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41305603606) passed in 445 seconds; the changed-test job took 274 seconds including its other selected tests and setup. Both required CI-gate checks passed.

title: docs(ui): design a bounded held window for deep chat history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading earlier messages in the Control UI gets slower with every page, and memory keeps growing, because the chat pane holds every row the reader has loaded and re-walks all of them on each older page. The 12 MiB cap applies only to the cached snapshot, not to the live pane.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. This draft proposes how to keep per-page cost and memory flat at any depth. It needs the product decisions listed below before any code ships.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task asked for the smallest safe first stage. I didn't find one that avoids product decisions, so this draft has only the design (`docs/reference/control-ui-held-history-window-design.md`). The design covers:

- **Ownership:** `state.chatMessages` stays the only held array and is still published only through `history-merge.ts`. `ChatHistoryPagination`, which already owns the older edge, gains one optional fact: `gap: { afterSource, beforeSource, newerCursor? }`. `ChatPaneHistory` makes the eviction decision through one pure function. `buildChatItems` emits a single `history-gap` boundary item.
- **Window shape:** a deep block, at most one gap, and the live tail block. The alternative was a detached tail (evict the newest rows). I rejected it because `insertSessionProjectionEntry` places a live persisted row after the newest held row, so with the tail evicted, live rows would land straight after the deep rows. Delta reads, send/steer pending rows, input placement, stream rows, end-follow, **Scroll to latest**, `reconcileHistoryTail`, the snapshot cache and the `chat-history-state` read model all assume the held rows reach the live tail. Keeping the tail block preserves that assumption, so none of those writers change.
- **Eviction policy:** runs only after an older-page prepend, once held rows exceed `K_max` (proposed 5,000 rows or 12 MiB weight); it trims to `K_target` (proposed 4,000). It removes only rows between the deep block (prepended page through viewport plus a two-page margin) and the tail block (latest page plus pending, queued or live-run rows). Cuts fall only where a sequence group ends and a user row starts the next turn, so tool calls/results, reasoning and handoffs are never split. Evicted rows are below the viewport, so the anchor doesn't move. Eviction is paused while search is open, during reply navigation and in catalog sessions.
- **Reloading newer rows:** a gap sentinel mirrors the older one, with the same intent, settle and failure gates, plus an explicit **Load newer messages** action. Requests use `chat.history { cursor: newerCursor }`, or a `messageId` probe when no cursor is held, like today's `needsBoundary`. The gap closes when a page reaches `beforeSource` or returns no `newerCursor`. `windowReset` falls back to `reloadChatHistoryWindow`.
- **Live events and Scroll to latest:** both keep working as they do now. Reaching the tail may drop the deep block and the gap.
- **Cache:** with a gap present, only the tail block is cached (with `needsBoundary`), so the persisted schema doesn't change.
- **Reply navigation:** a target inside the gap fills the gap instead of paging older.
- **Stages:** (1) the gap fact, eviction, the gap row, downward fill without top trimming, and tail-only cache commits; (2) sentinel-driven fill plus top trimming, with `TranscriptPrependAnchor` handling leading removals; (3) reply navigation into the gap and shrinking on **Scroll to latest**.

### Decisions needed

1. **Loaded rows can leave the client.** In-app search filters held rows only, and so do browser find and reply previews. Options: pause eviction while search is open (proposed for stage 1), show a "matches in unloaded history are hidden" hint, or add server-side transcript search.
2. **Gap affordance:** a visible **Load newer messages** divider in the middle of the transcript (a visual change), or invisible auto-fill only.
3. **Bound:** `K_max`/`K_target` (proposed 5,000/4,000 rows, capped by the existing 12 MiB weight).
4. **Sequencing with the incremental-render lanes:** ship the bound after that work or alongside it.

## Evidence

- **Work count per older page (code reading):** at least six full passes over held rows: prepend identity, session projection publish (including `createSessionProjection` / `readSessionMessageIdentity` per row), projection compare/copy, snapshot commit, `buildChatItems` (about nine internal passes) and the transcript chain/index/rows projection.
- **Isolated stage timings:** medians of 3 runs, one 1,000-row older page prepended onto `held` rows, measured with a scratch vitest that was not committed. Host load average was about 17, so treat these as relative.

  | held | prepend | projection | buildChatItems | chain+index |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1,000 | 0.3 ms | 0.3 ms | 8.7 ms | 9.5 ms |
  | 4,000 | 0.8 ms | 0.6 ms | 21.1 ms | 28.6 ms |
  | 8,000 | 1.2 ms | 0.9 ms | 37.9 ms | 49.5 ms |
  | 12,000 | 1.8 ms | 1.3 ms | 59.1 ms | 52.8 ms |
  | 16,000 | 2.7 ms | 1.5 ms | 81.5 ms | 75.6 ms |

  That is linear growth at about 10 µs per held row for these two stages. A 4,000-row bound would hold them at about 50 ms per page instead of 157 ms at 16,000 rows.
- **Lead's end-to-end measurement** (isolated Gateway, production bundle, 30,000 messages): Gateway `chat.history` is flat at 35–75 ms per page. Browser script time per page is about 150 ms at pages 1–5 and about 305 ms at pages 21–25 (4x CPU throttle: about 650 ms vs about 1,350 ms).
- **Gateway prerequisite exists:** both-direction anchored paging is already supported and tested. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=1 src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-page-cursor.test.ts` passed 21/21, including reversing an older page with its `newerCursor`.
- **Checks:** oxfmt check on the doc passed, `git diff --check` is clean, and local autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`) found nothing actionable.
- **Gaps:** no implementation and no RED/GREEN tests yet, by design. Total memory at 30,000 held messages wasn't measured. The timings above come from a loaded shared host.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(update-repair): preserve repair budgets across wall-clock changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repair aborts and inflated timeouts when the host wall clock changes during update repair or embedded triage.

## User Impact

Repairs retain the operator-granted elapsed-time budget across forward and backward clock corrections, and reported attempt durations remain nonnegative.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completes #190064 (381abce5), which fixed the embedded runtime, by using the existing shared monotonic clock for the repair loop, inference selection, and delegated worker. Existing budget defaults, cancellation, authority checks, IPC durations, and absolute timestamps are preserved.

title: fix(ui): keep older chat history still while reading it
body:
## Problem

On mobile (reported from iOS Safari), messages jump around while you scroll up through older chat history after it loads. Three things cause it, and each one moves the messages on screen when a row above the viewport changes size:

1. **Rows skipped by `content-visibility: auto` (≤768 px).** Offscreen overscan rows keep their virtual estimate (120 px) until they reach the viewport. Then they render at full size and push the messages being read down, by up to about 1,300 px in the repro.
2. **Corrections land one frame late.** Since #188470, virtual-core applies row measurements on the next animation frame, so it isn't committing the range inside native resize delivery. Rows lay out in normal flow, though, so each estimate→real correction above the reader is painted once as a jump before it snaps back.
3. **iOS defers every correction for the whole gesture.** iOS WebKit cancels touch and momentum scrolling on a `scrollTop` write, so virtual-core holds every correction until scrolling settles. The transcript stays displaced for the whole fling, then snaps.

## Solution

- `TranscriptReaderAnchor` (new, owned by the virtualizer host) watches mounted rows. When a row above the viewport changes size, it corrects during that same resize delivery, before paint, using native geometry only. It never commits the range, so the #188470 contract still holds:
  - Outside iOS gestures, it writes `scrollTop`. Like virtual-core's own path, the write is recorded as maintenance and the native range grows first.
  - During iOS touch or momentum, it shifts the row column instead: a negative margin, mirrored in `scrollMargin` so virtual and DOM offsets still agree. The shift folds into `scrollTop` when virtual-core reports that scrolling has settled. It skips elastic overscroll.
  - When virtual-core lands the measured size, the anchor's predicate reconciles it (no double correction). It also takes over iOS-held corrections that virtual-core would otherwise defer. Restoration, scroll commands, and the prepend and disclosure anchors still own placement while they are active.
  - Hidden panes (collapsed side panel, `clientHeight` 0) report zero-height rows; those deliveries are ignored so a restored panel keeps its reading position.
- The compensation predicate now covers rows above the reader in both scroll directions. Virtual-core's default skipped re-measured rows while scrolling backward, which is exactly when reading older history.
- Mobile rows no longer use `content-visibility: auto`. The virtualizer already limits how many rows are mounted, so overscan rows now lay out (and get measured) while still offscreen.
- The history sentinel's IntersectionObserver now observes anew when it fires during a maintenance correction. It used to drop that notification, and since an unchanged intersection is never reported again, auto-loading at the top could get stuck.
- Row-key commits moved into `chat-transcript-header.ts` (with the existing header-margin helper) to stay under the host's line budget.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/e2e/chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts`: 30 recent + 160 older variable-height messages. It reads up to the top to load the older page, then reads upward through it for 240 frames, sampling the **painted** frame and following the first visible message.
  - Base (`bf73e1aa`): fails on all three — Chromium 390 px with iPhone UA: 36 shifted frames, worst 1,255 px; WebKit 390 px: 29 shifted frames, worst 1,246 px; Chromium 1280 px: 38 shifted frames, worst 809 px.
  - This branch: 0 shifted frames on all three.
- Existing e2e: `chat-history-prepend-anchor` (all variants, including touch and momentum), `session-dashboard-active-panel` (caught the hidden-pane case in CI; fixed and green), `session-progress-scroll`, `chat-widget-autosize`, `chat-composer-accessory-focus`, `warm-boot`, `post-deploy-session-entry`, `chat-saved-attempt-navigation`, `claude-sessions`, `chat-flow.messaging`: all green.
- Unit and browser: all `chat-transcript-*` tests, chat history, thread, page and session-progress suites — 988 tests green after merging current `main`.
- Real Gateway (temporary harness, not committed): isolated Gateway, a 400-message session, the real `chat.startup` plus `chat.history` paging at 390 px with an iPhone UA, reading upward through about 90 messages (1,109 frames): 0 shifted frames on this branch, so no regression. In that harness the base build also showed 0, because the rows had real sizes cached before they mounted, so this run is no-regression evidence, not a reproduction.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt, madge import cycles, assertion-safety ratchet, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.
- `main` was merged in to pick up the fix for an inherited `check-lint-core-2` failure (`src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts`, untouched here).

## Test change

`chat-transcript-end-follow.browser.test.ts` ("holds the canceled viewport…") used to grow the earlier row in the same task as `cancelScroll()`. Now that is a real resize above the reader, and it gets compensated. The fixture now grows the row while the smooth journey is still in flight, which is the skipped-measurement case the test is about. The assertions are unchanged.

## Accepted edges

- iOS: if you reach the very top in the same gesture that accumulated a column shift, the first rows stay clipped above the edge until the gesture settles (one fold, invisible to the reader).
- A row that grows above the reader and unmounts before its measurement lands has its correction retired instead of reverted.

## Not verified

- No physical iPhone. iOS behavior was exercised through virtual-core's UA-based iOS path in Chromium and Playwright WebKit.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ci): clear main deadcode and release-admission reds
body:

title: fix(ui): shorten completed work duration label
body:
## Problem

The collapsed completed-work heading in Control UI chat spells out durations in full, e.g. **Worked for 4 minutes, 9 seconds**. On phones it takes up a lot of the line, and it's harder to scan than the other compact metadata around it. Vyctor asked for a shorter label.

## Solution

`WorkGroupSummary` now formats its duration with the existing `formatDurationCompact` helper instead of `formatDurationLong`. That changes the label to **Worked for 4m 9s**, which was also the format before #164430. The locale-aware narrow units still come from `Intl.NumberFormat`, and the **Worked** fallback with no duration is unchanged.

Scope is limited to the "Worked for …" disclosure. The separate turn recap row (**Done in …**) still uses the long format; it can follow in a separate change if wanted.

## Before / after

Synthetic session, 390px-wide viewport, run duration 249 s:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Worked for 4 minutes, 9 seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b696b92f-ac66-4711-bf01-ef770fd814f0) | ![After: Worked for 4m 9s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59171029-d123-48bf-9a95-e49356247404) |

## Evidence

- Unit/browser tests: `chat-activity-disclosure`, `chat-transcript-duration`, `chat-transcript-render`, `chat-pane-session-events`, `browser-tab-card`. 5 files, 129 tests passed.
- Control UI e2e: `chat-cold-load-anchor`, `chat-run-lifecycle`. 2 files, 17 tests passed.
- Screenshots came from a throwaway mocked-Gateway e2e. The before image was taken with the label formatter temporarily restored to `main`.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md` examples updated to the compact format.
- `git diff --check` clean.

title: fix(memory): explain skipped trigger recall
body:
Closes #164382
Supersedes #184306, thanks @wyf027

## What Problem This Solves

Trigger recall silently skips unavailable or disallowed memory tools, private-destination checks, and chat filters, leaving operators without a reason for missing recall.

## User Impact

Operators now see the first failed trigger condition in debug logs, or also at info level when `config.logging: true`. Recall eligibility and tool authority are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing plugin-owned skip diagnostic and document the reasons. The fix adds no configuration or subsystem and removes a redundant context alias. Production delta: +16 lines; removing further unrelated code would not simplify this repair.

## Evidence

- Seven registered-hook regression cases fail on main `52fb7e066e6c69081b8ccdb5ba65d9f8ad39272d` specifically because the reason is missing (59.43s including cold compilation).
- Fixed owner and trigger-recall sibling suites: **133 passed**, 50.30s wall time. The hook file took 18.85s; trigger-recall took 28.96s including compilation. Diagnostic cases took 92–109ms each and cover native/legacy missing or denied tools, groups, allowed-chat filters, and explicit chat denials. Logging-disabled cases also assert that info logging stays off.
- Focused typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. The 36-line regression allocation extends existing hook fixtures and denial cases without a new fixture or product seam.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) reviewed the complete local candidate against the main commit above, with the diagnostic owner, session policy, and provider test context supplied: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute tests; focused results above were collected separately.

title: chore(test): avoid five-second CLI admission lock probe
body:
Related: #156703

## What Problem This Solves

The CLI fallback contention regression test spends five seconds proving that a SQLite write lock is held before exercising the actual fallback flow. This maintainer-directed test-health lane targets the 5.616s case in [CI run 41293098118](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41293098118).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The target case is about five seconds faster, with its real SQLite contention and cold session-reader regression coverage retained. Production code, SQLite busy timeouts, and mocks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the synchronous writable `loadSessionEntry()` precondition with a test-local raw connection to the same shared-state database. Set its `busy_timeout` to zero and assert that `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` fails with `database is locked`. A scoped `using` closes the probe before `runLocal()`.

The awaited agent-database close remains before lock acquisition. The raw probe neither opens an agent database nor reads session metadata. The existing CLI callback still requires the holder transaction to be live when execution is reached, then releases it for settlement. The final assertions still require a successful reply, the existing native session ID and binding, exactly one CLI call, no result error, and no embedded-agent fallback. No incidental coverage was removed.

## Evidence

Three serial full-file runs before and after, on the same Linux host with the repository's default pinned Bun runtime and unchanged runner settings. All six runs passed all 18 tests. Acceptance: remove roughly five seconds from the case median, every after case faster than every before case, and kill the original writable-open mutation.

```sh
timeout 600 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-admission.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile=<report.json>
```

| Phase / run | Command wall | Vitest duration | File test time | Target case |

| before 1 | 70.24s | 34.74s | 12.055s | 5.591s |
| before 2 | 23.02s | 17.96s | 11.631s | 5.602s |
| before 3 | 22.73s | 17.96s | 11.715s | 5.532s |
| after 1 | 16.88s | 12.18s | 6.647s | 0.545s |
| after 2 | 21.71s | 11.94s | 6.551s | 0.546s |
| after 3 | 17.07s | 12.48s | 6.789s | 0.547s |
| **before median** | **23.02s** | **17.96s** | **11.715s** | **5.591s** |
| **after median** | **17.07s** | **12.18s** | **6.647s** | **0.546s** |

Command wall includes wrapper preparation and cleanup. File test time is the Vitest JSON suite end/start interval; Vitest duration is the reporter's duration. Before run 1 also prepared worker artifacts (31.69s); all raw measurements are retained in this table, while medians reduce that cold-build outlier's effect.

Median gains: target case **5.045s / 90.2%**, file test time **5.068s / 43.3%**, Vitest duration **5.78s / 32.2%**, command wall **5.95s / 25.8%**. Supporting GNU-time medians: user/system CPU 23.76/5.50s → 23.24/4.39s; peak RSS 1838.0 → 1857.2 MiB (+1.0%, no memory improvement claimed).

**Cold fixture and mutation:** temporary diagnostic assertions using the existing `isOpenClawAgentDatabaseOpen()` confirmed no cached writable agent handle immediately after the awaited close or after the raw lock probe. The control case passed. Then the read-only metadata branch in `withAdmittedCliCandidate()` was temporarily replaced with `loadSessionEntry({ ...target, readConsistency: "latest" })`, restoring the pre-#156703 synchronous writable open. The same case failed in **6.795s** at its retained success/payload assertion: expected `kind: "success"`, received `kind: "final"`. The cold-handle assertions and real-lock precondition passed before this failure. Both the mutation and diagnostics were reverted; no production diff remains.

Validation:

Command: `timeout 600 pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-*.test.ts src/agents/session-placement-admission.test.ts src/agents/session-placement-admission.caller-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`. The five lines preserve a real, non-mocked lock precondition and close its raw connection before the product flow; no new helper or production seam is needed. The test-line scalar is unchanged because this is growth; the ratchet passes at exactly 6,373,300 lines against the existing 6,390,531-line effective ceiling (17,231 lines of slack). title: fix(ui): loading earlier chat messages gets slower with every page in long sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scrolling up to load earlier messages in the Control UI gets slower with every page in long chats, until each page takes several seconds.

## User Impact

User impact: loading earlier messages stays fast deep into long sessions. In a 30,000-message chat on a crowded Gateway with 4× CPU throttling, the wait for pages 21–25 drops from about 3.3–3.4 s to about 1.6 s, and the longest blocking task from about 2.5 s to about 1 s. Loaded history (count, order, deduplication), the saved cache contents and the rest of the history flow are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each older page rebuilds work across the whole loaded transcript. Two parts of that rebuild got much heavier and grew with depth:

- **Row footprints (regressed in #183595).** Rebuilding the transcript row index re-serialized and hashed every loaded message to compute its saved row height key. Loaded history messages are immutable, so each message's fingerprint is now computed once and reused (WeakMap keyed by the message object). The key changes format, so saved row heights miss once after upgrade, then refill.
- **Snapshot trimming.** Once the cached chat passes its 12 MiB limit, committing a page dropped older rows one group at a time and re-serialized the snapshot envelope (including row display facts, #186512) on every step. That envelope is identical for every trim before the newest 80-row display window, so it is now measured once. Trims inside that window still measure their own envelope, and the stored weight still equals `JSON.stringify(snapshot).length`.

Not changed: the remaining rebuild of display items over the whole transcript on each page (it existed before the regression). That is the next step: append pages without rebuilding, and bound how much history is held. Not changed on purpose: when a tail refresh (for example a run finishing) lands while an older page is in flight, the page is dropped and the boundary shows "Couldn't load earlier messages" with Retry; the next scroll loads normally. That is the existing designed outcome.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, production bundles.** A private benchmark harness (not committed) drives Playwright Chromium against an isolated real Gateway process: real WebSocket, SQLite and `chat.history` paging, with production UI builds of this head and its base `9172615`. Each arm uses its own worktree and build. Workload: 30,000 messages with realistic content (markdown, code blocks, tables, links, 20–220-line tool results; user → tool call → tool result → reply). Crowded profile: 200 workspace skills, 40 other sessions and live `chat.inject` traffic every 400 ms. Each run makes 25 scroll-up pages (25,080 messages loaded). Runs were interleaved base/cand/cand/base on a shared host with load average 7–20.

| Profile (medians) | base `9172615` (2 runs) | this PR (2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: wait for pages 1–5 | 942 / 967 ms | 913 / 839 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: wait for pages 21–25 | 3431 / 3273 ms | 1570 / 1617 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: script time per page, pages 21–25 | 3247 / 3036 ms | 1322 / 1370 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: longest task, pages 21–25 | 2578 / 2530 ms | 926 / 1011 ms |
| Unthrottled: wait for pages 21–25 | 756 / 747 ms | 405 / 409 ms |
| Unthrottled: script time per page, pages 21–25 | 650 / 653 ms | 304 / 309 ms |

- **Correctness in every run:** all 25,080 loaded messages present, unique and in source order. A separate 8,000-message crowded run loaded all 8,000 messages in order on both arms. Page sizes and page counts are identical between arms.
- **Snapshot commit (unit-level micro benchmark, 12,000 messages, 256 KB envelope):** 606 ms per commit → 2.2 ms. The retained cache contents are identical to base for all 39 measured commits.
- **Regression tests:** RED on base, GREEN here.
  - Index rebuild after an older prepend hashes less than one loaded message's worth of text, with unchanged revisions. Base hashed 118,213 characters.
  - Trimming 4,000 rows measures the envelope at most twice. Base measured it 984 times.
- **Tests and checks:**
  - All UI tests under `ui/src/pages/chat` and `ui/src/lib/chat` pass: 637 files.
  - The changed test files take 2.8 s and 2.2 s wall time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`).
  - Existing history browser suites pass against this build: real-Gateway `chat-loading-performance`, plus `chat-history-loading`, `chat-history-prepend-anchor`, `chat-cold-load-anchor`, `chat-flow.history-recovery` and `warm-boot`.
  - `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and the test-line ratchet pass.
- **Review:** local autoreview (Codex, P0–P3, branch vs `origin/main`) is scoped-clean with no findings.

**Gaps:**
- The live team Gateway was not tested. All Gateway runs used isolated real Gateway processes with synthetic transcripts.
- No mobile device or WebKit runs were done; CPU throttling stands in for a slow device.
- Three harness runs (on both arms) ended with a Gateway child-process cleanup timeout after measurements were complete. This is a host load issue in teardown, not in the measured flow.
- The benchmark harness is not committed.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski
