title: test(ui): preload lazy plugin detail views before timed waits
body:
## Problem

`ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.generations.test.ts` > *accepts a changed schema with the same version while retaining drafts during unrelated revisions* failed in `checks-ui (3/3)` on #190204 ([run 41294337020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41294337020/job/124812189889)) with `expected null not to be null`. The error came from the first `waitForSolid`.

The plugins page lazy-loads `settings-view.tsx` and `catalog-detail.tsx` (`plugins-page-view.tsx`). `waitForSolid` wraps `vi.waitFor`, whose default budget is 1s. This is the first test in the file, so its wait includes the cold import and transform of the settings view. On a loaded 2-CPU runner that import alone can take longer than the budget.

## Solution

Import both lazy detail modules once in a `beforeAll` before any test runs. The lazy components then resolve from the module cache, so the 1s render waits only measure rendering. No product code, timeouts, retries or assertions change.

## Evidence

Each column is 6 concurrent runs of the file pinned to one CPU (`taskset -c 0`):

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result | 6/6 fail (same test, same assertion) | 6/6 pass (15/15 tests) |

- An unloaded run of the file: 15/15 pass.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` are clean.

title: fix(infra): release completed SQLite readers and prevent cursor restarts
body:
Supersedes #184076, thanks @ava-perry.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WAL growth when a completed SQLite reader is stepped again on affected Node bindings; returning an old iterator can also rewind a newer reader using the same statement.

## User Impact

Completed readers release their snapshots, checkpoints can finish, and later iterator calls cannot restart queries or disturb successor readers. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SQLite observer now returns native iterators on exhaustion and remembers completion after either exhaustion or explicit return. Repeated calls receive a terminal result. Remove the superseded iterator capability experiment and its private worker-admission fields together; retain the loaded-library safety and identity query using one `get()`.

Simplification pass: production **−48 lines**, tests **+18 net lines** against `a11289439ae9`. The removed probe/transport pays for the terminal-state handling. The separate 18-line regression allocation covers real WAL checkpoint progress and preservation of a successor cursor after stale calls, after subtracting obsolete probe fixtures.

## Evidence

- Base `a11289439ae9940e6487c82ef439af80da180571`, Node 24.18.0 / SQLite 3.53.1: new real temp-directory database regressions fail. After exhaustion and another `next()`, PASSIVE checkpoints only **3 of 4 frames**; after explicit return, a stale return rewinds the successor and yields row 1 twice.
- Fixed branch on Node 24.18.0: observer + native runtime suites **79 tests passed**, 5.00s total wrapper wall time. WAL fully checkpoints and TRUNCATE returns `{busy: 0, log: 0}`; the successor yields the remaining rows exactly once.
- Node 26.12.1: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/sqlite-native-observer.test.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts src/state/openclaw-schema-metadata.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **148 passed**, 44.12s wall time including the initial worker build. Test execution remains under five seconds per file. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41298266266) passed, including all three PostgreSQL shards and `openclaw/ci-gate`; elapsed **1460 seconds** including setup and all jobs.
- Focused TypeScript compilation of the six changed TS files plus canonical ambient declarations, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. No references to the retired probe or iterator flags remain in `src`.
- Shared autoreview, local candidate against `a11289439ae9`, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**. It reviewed the supplied complete diff and native Node source; unchanged repository context was unavailable and it did not rerun tests. Subsequent changes only remove an unused type import and record the test allocation.
- Contributor source was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. This is an independently implemented, credited replacement. Production Team services were not modified.

- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190242#issuecomment-6556912819), exact head `1dd1097bd13e`: complete, no actionable findings. It records the same full-Gateway proof limitation.

title: feat(ui): show GitHub avatars in the publication account picker
body:
## Problem

The mobile **Publish as** row and account picker showed initials ("R", "V") instead of the accounts' GitHub avatars. `sessions.github.options` only returned `login` and `accountId`, and the picker deliberately rendered initials rather than build remote image URLs in the browser.

## Solution

- `sessions.github.options` now returns an optional, display-only `avatarUrls: { shared?, personal? }`. The Gateway builds each URL from the verified account ID and **that account's GitHub host**:
  - github.com → `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/<id>?v=4`
  - GitHub Enterprise (`gateway.github.host`) → `https://<host>/avatars/u/<id>`
  - Personal publication accounts are always github.com.
- The host travels with the options identity (`prepareGitHubPublicationOptionsIdentity` / `configuredAppGitHubOptionsIdentity`). On an Enterprise Gateway, a client-built `avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/<id>` URL would show an unrelated github.com user's avatar.
- `src/shared/github-account-avatar.ts` is now the single URL builder. The profile page's existing GitHub identity projection uses it too, with no behavior change.
- `GitHubPublicationAvatar` renders the image with `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` and falls back to initials when no URL is offered or the image fails to load. The selected-publisher row only uses an image when the recorded publisher matches the offered account ID.
- Selections and publication requests never carry avatar URLs.

## Impact

- Cost: one extra small object in an existing response. No extra GitHub API calls, because the URL derives from the already-verified account ID. Each avatar is one browser image request, cached by the browser.
- Privacy/CSP: same as the profile page's existing GitHub avatar (`img-src https:` is already allowed). The security-model docs note publication account choices and the Enterprise host.
- Protocol: additive optional field; older clients ignore it.

## Screenshots

Built Control UI bundle, mocked Gateway, 393×852, account menu open.

| Before (initials) | After (GitHub avatars) | Fallback (avatar request fails) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: initials in the Publish as row and account menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9803b2d-ef51-4fea-bf16-cbfe76d79a00) | ![After: avatars in the Publish as row and both account menu rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7a646af-48b9-411f-a3b6-58f89ccc9dee) | ![Fallback: avatar 404 falls back to initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b4ac794-e3df-4bed-bc70-4cbd1e0e8428) |

## Evidence

- New regression tests:
  - `src/gateway/github-personal-publication.test.ts`: options return host-aware URLs (Enterprise shared host + github.com personal).
  - `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-github-publication-mobile.test.ts`: renders the supplied image with no-referrer, then falls back to initials on `error`.
- Updated consumer tests for the new identity host and response field: `src/agents/github-tool-identity.test.ts` (caught by the first CI run) and `sessions-github-read.test-support.ts`.
- Passing locally: `github-tool-identity`, `github-publication-availability.worker`, `sessions-github{,-read,-read.target,-readiness}`, `session-utils-store-lookup`, `github-personal-publication`, `github-publication-legacy-options`, `users-list`, and the mobile publication UI test.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxfmt, oxlint, and `check:control-ui-controllers` are clean.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex), branch mode against `bf73e1aa822` at P1. Result: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Visual: the Playwright screenshots above, all inspected; the after run asserts that all three images loaded.
- Not run: a live Gateway with real GitHub credentials, or a GitHub Enterprise host end to end.

title: fix(ui): stop iOS Safari panning the page under the composer while typing
body:
## Problem

In mobile Safari, with the keyboard open in chat, dragging up on the composer or on a thread that's already at its end scrolls the whole page. The view jitters and a blank area shows up under the composer (reported with a screen recording from an iPhone).

**Root cause:** iOS Safari draws the keyboard over the page instead of shrinking the layout viewport, so the area under the keyboard still belongs to the document. When no scroller inside the app takes a vertical drag, Safari pans the *visual* viewport into that area. `connectShellViewport` responds to each `visualViewport` scroll by moving `--shell-viewport-height` (`height + offsetTop`). That update lands one frame after the pan, so the shell keeps chasing the viewport (the jitter) while the unused layout area below it shows through (the blank area). `overflow: clip` / `overscroll-behavior: none` on `html, body` don't help because this is a visual-viewport pan, not a document scroll.

## Solution

The shell viewport owner (`ui/src/app/shell-viewport.ts`) already knows when the keyboard is open. Only during that time it adds one capturing, non-passive `touchmove` guard that cancels a single-finger vertical drag when no scrollable element on the touch's composed path can move in that direction. The guard decides once per gesture, as WebKit locks the gesture to one scroller. It ignores:

- drags an in-app scroller can take (the thread, an overflowing composer textarea, popovers)
- horizontal drags (the nav-drawer swipe) and multi-touch (pinch)
- drags that start after a 300 ms press-and-hold (text selection, caret loupe)
- downward drags while the visual viewport is offset (`offsetTop > 0`). Safari often scrolls the header away to reveal the focused composer; dragging down moves back toward it and only shrinks the shell, so it stays native and the header remains reachable

The guard is removed as soon as the keyboard closes or the owner disconnects, so touch handling stays unchanged the rest of the time.

Accepted edge case: a press-and-hold followed by a drag over bare chrome can still pan. This is rare, visible and recoverable, and is the cost of keeping native selection.

## Evidence

- New unit regression `cancels keyboard-open drags that would pan Safari's visual viewport` in `shell-viewport.test.ts`: **fails on `main`**, passes with the fix. It also covers the offset-viewport case: downward drag stays native, upward drag is cancelled. All 12 tests in the file pass.
- Real Control UI DOM check (temporary Playwright probe, not committed): mocked Gateway, 40-message chat at 390×844 with `isMobile`/`hasTouch`. Focused the composer, shrank `visualViewport` to simulate the keyboard, then sent CDP touch drags:
  - on `main`: `touchmove` was never `defaultPrevented` for any drag
  - with the fix: drags on the composer and up past the thread end are cancelled; drags down and up inside the thread are not, and `.chat-thread` scrolled 4877→4849→4999; after the keyboard closes, nothing is cancelled
- Local autoreview (Codex engine, branch mode, base `bf73e1aa822`, head `006c3c5f3c9` = same tree as `00887c1a06e`, max priority P2): `scoped-clean`, no findings; "patch is correct (0.82)". The reviewer also noted that native iOS selection, navigation and pinch behavior can't be verified with synthetic tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` all clean.

**Gap:** Chromium doesn't pan the visual viewport the way iOS WebKit does, so the jitter itself isn't reproduced here. I tried an iOS Simulator run on a macOS Crabbox, but the machine was still provisioning after ~30 minutes, so I stopped it. A check on a real iPhone in Safari is still needed.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(windows): preserve process identity probes across clock changes
body:
Supersedes #184162, thanks @SunnyShu0925.

Human credit in [replacement commit d31ec002facd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d31ec002facd84d7de5eb6c169bc63fae0a67932): `Co-authored-by: SunnyShu <0668000539@local>`. The native squash policy removed this local-domain address from the landed commit; the original human attribution is retained here and in the replacement commit.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows process identity probes can expire early or run beyond their timeout when the system clock changes during Gateway lifecycle checks.

## User Impact

Windows operators retain the requested process-verification time budget across clock corrections. No configuration, identity format, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `performance.now()` convention for the shared native/PowerShell/WMIC deadline and round remaining subprocess budgets up to integer milliseconds. This is a maintainer-owned reimplementation; the contributor branch was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed.

Production LOC: +3/-3 (net 0). Regression tests: +23, with a dedicated 23-line allocation protecting both clock-jump directions and fractional subprocess timeouts. Simplification retained only the three owner expressions and one parameterized regression.

## Evidence

- Base: `29526f13194aa8b214a40879b477215f16effad4`. Both new cases fail before the fix: a backward jump grants WMIC 21,000 ms within a 1,000 ms request; a forward jump returns no identity before probing.
- After the fix: 139 tests pass across seven focused owner/consumer files; one Windows-only native case is skipped on Linux. The changed file alone completed in 0.664 seconds (1.87 seconds runner wall time); all focused shards completed in 45.08 seconds. [Exact-head broad CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41297453197) passed in 468 seconds.
- Targeted typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI.

Review snapshot matches head `d31ec002facd84d7de5eb6c169bc63fae0a67932`. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190236) also reports no findings. No findings remain.
- This Linux proof exercises the production identity owner with controlled clocks and fixed external-I/O fixtures; it does not claim a live Windows Gateway stop or upgrade test. Contributor code was not run anywhere.

title: fix(ui): dock the New Session draft on the mobile keyboard
body:
## Problem

On `/new` on a phone, opening the keyboard kept the page's centered composition. Once iOS Safari pans the layout to the caret, the shell stays at full height, so an empty, scrollable band sits between the composer and the keyboard.

## Solution

- `shell-viewport.ts`, the single visual-viewport owner, now sets `data-shell-keyboard` on the root while it detects a soft keyboard (same detection that already zeroes `--shell-safe-area-bottom`), and removes it on dismissal and disconnect.
- On phone widths, `new-session.css` anchors the welcome and draft to the bottom while that attribute is present, with the same 10px bottom gap as the mobile chat composer (`[data-mobile-composer]`). The resting (keyboard-closed) layout stays centered.

## Evidence

- `new-session-page.keyboard.e2e.test.ts` now also covers the Safari pan-to-caret case (`offsetTop = 874 − 380`) and asserts the composer sits exactly 10px above the keyboard, the gap measured on the mobile chat page in the same harness. **Red on base** (31px gap) and on the first revision (6px), green with the fix.
- `shell-viewport.test.ts` asserts the attribute follows keyboard open, pan, dismissal, and disconnect. **Red on base** (2 cases), green with the fix (11/11).
- Neighbouring mobile e2e suites pass: keyboard, mobile-new-conversation, responsive-welcome, mobile-shell-geometry.
- `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, oxfmt check, `git diff --check` clean. `pnpm ui:build && pnpm ui:check-performance` passed: total CSS is 308069 B gzip against the 309366 B ceiling.

Before/after screenshots (402×874, keyboard leaves 470px visible after Safari pans) are in the comments, including a chat-vs-`/new` comparison of the bottom gap.

title: improve(ui): round the phone owner page and fade long names
body:
## Problem

On phones, opening the sidebar's Owners title (and the People presence title, which shares the same picker) slides in a choice page that covered the drawer as a flat, square-cornered block. Long owner names, and unlabeled owners that fall back to a raw profile id, wrapped onto two or three lines.

## Solution

Scoped to `.sidebar-session-owner-filter.picker-select--sheet` in `sidebar-rail.css`, so the session-filter bottom sheet's own pages and the desktop dropdown are unchanged:

- **Card.** The page floats as a card inset by `--space-2`, using the shared menu surface tokens: `--overlay-modal-radius`, `--menu-surface`, `--menu-shadow`, `--menu-backdrop`, and a hairline border. It has `--space-3` padding on the top and sides.
- **Fits short rosters.** The card is as tall as its rows. Long rosters stop at the drawer's bottom inset, and the list scrolls inside the card.
- **Trigger ring.** The trigger's open-state accent ring is hidden so it doesn't show through the card's translucent top edge.
- **Names on one line.** Option labels never wrap and never get an ellipsis. The label box fills the row, and its trailing 48px fade out softly in two steps (full opacity, then 45%, then transparent), with an RTL mirror. Names that end before the fade zone are untouched.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/e2e/session-owner-filter-mobile-sheet.e2e.test.ts` (390×844). It fails on `main` with `expected 0 to be greater than 0` on the page radius and passes with this change. It checks:
  - the page has a nonzero radius and a shadow
  - a short roster is less than half the viewport tall
  - every row is one line with `text-overflow: clip` and a gradient mask
  - only the long name and the raw profile id overflow
- Related e2e checks pass (21/21): `session-owner-filter-keyboard` (including its 30-owner compact containment case), `session-owner-filter-empty-section`, `mobile-sidebar-session-menu`, `people-activity-filters`, and the new test.
- `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check`.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance` passed on the first revision. Total CSS raw was 1,595,204 B against a 1,599,319 B ceiling. The follow-up adds about 500 B raw, so it should still fit; I haven't rerun the check after it.
- I inspected before/after mock captures at 390px and shared them in the requesting conversation.

title: improve(ui): tighten the mobile header project line
body:
## Problem

On the mobile Control UI chat header, the project name under the session title sat too far below it. The two lines read as separate items instead of a title with a subtitle.

The extra space came from padding in both line boxes. The title button had a 22px minimum height around a 20px line. The project chip used a 12px font in an 18px line. In a mocked-Gateway run at 390px, the title and project line centers were 20px apart.

## Change

- `.mobile-header__title`: `min-height` goes from 22px to 20px. This matches the 20px session-title placeholder, so the row doesn't move when a pending title arrives.
- Mobile `.chat-pane__workspace-chip`: line height goes from 18px to 14px, and `min-height` from 18px to 14px.

The title and project block is now 34px tall instead of 40px. The header still centers it against the 40px controls, so header height (54px) and control sizes are unchanged. The line centers are now 17px apart. Descenders in the project name are not clipped, as the screenshots below show.

## Evidence

Mocked-Gateway Control UI E2E at 390×844, DPR 3, built from this branch.

![Mobile header before/after, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a93f5bc8-09f4-44da-a372-6d172e464085)

title: fix: invalid Rewind requests interrupt retained sandbox sessions
body:
Related: #190181

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an invalid Rewind or branch-switch selection can retire a usable managed sandbox, and a real workspace conflict hides its recovery instruction behind an ineffective retry message.

## User Impact

Invalid selections leave the retained runtime and workspace edits untouched. Workspace conflicts explicitly ask users to resolve the conflict before retrying, without exposing internal paths or error text. No schema, configuration, permission, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker, native, and memory adapters preflight through the planner's shared semantic selection before workspace retirement. The final transaction still validates the selection and ownership; preflight is not a reservation. It creates no transcript plan, UUID, or editor payload. A fixed typed workspace-conflict error carries only safe recovery guidance through the handler.

The handoff proof now follows an actual handler-generated persisted receipt through owner resolution and the workspace writer, including refusal at the adoption COMMIT boundary and replay after reopening SQLite. Existing pending-reset and next-cut recovery remain covered.

## Evidence

- Red on base `a3751eaf96`: a missing-message Rewind issued runtime removal before rejection; a genuine canonical/private conflict returned the generic retry instead of the resolution instruction.
- **116 tests passed across 9 files**: 10 managed-workspace cut cases, 4 persisted-handoff/replay cases, 87 handler/storage/memory/native siblings, and 15 direct planner/accounting consumer cases. SQLite, Git, handlers, receipts, and owner decisions are real; container-engine I/O is fixture-backed. The landing owner independently reran the 14 critical cases at the published byte-identical tree; all passed.
- Focused TypeScript check, typed lint on all 9 touched source/test files, formatting, whitespace checks, and the staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh independent **autoreview, P0–P2**, against `a3751eaf96` and the complete candidate: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed the diff and complete owning-source context; it did not independently execute tests. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190219#issuecomment-6556627011) also completed at `10fe706` with no findings or before-merge blockers.
- [Exact-head broad CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41295420435) and security gates passed at `10fe706`; the native watcher reported GREEN. Changed test-file wall times: **89 s** for runtime/rejection coverage and **41 s** for persisted handoff coverage, including compiler startup. CI test-time sums: **14.457 s** for the 10 runtime/rejection cases and **15.524 s** for the 4 persisted-handoff cases. These integration tests traverse real Git and both SQLite owners; selector mocks cannot prove runtime preservation or adoption rollback.
- `pr-simplify`: shared the managed-workspace fixture and consolidated foreign-receipt cases around one persisted cut instead of repeating full setup/adoption. Net production growth is **90 lines**; **382 net regression-test lines** are allocated specifically for these production-boundary regressions, with the shared scalar unchanged.

**Known proof limitation:** live-model proof remains unavailable because the existing source-attribution CLI preflight forbids operator agent messages from agent exec. The marker was not removed, and no alternate injection route, live Gateway/session mutation, or deployment was used.

Requested and co-authored by @shakkernerd.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @shakkernerd](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/93f063b6-25ec-40dc-913b-49817f7188f2)
- [Original implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/08100518-99bc-4d77-a461-a39c9b3fb8f9)

title: fix(update): avoid false migration refusals on older upgrades
body:
Related: #188978

## What Problem This Solves

An update driven by released 2026.9.36 can fail in the installed candidate Doctor with `SQLite migration source changed after update capture`, then leave the older updater unable to finish reporting.

## User Impact

Doctor setup preserves the older updater's physical SQLite capture, so a recovery-journal lookup cannot itself cause a false migration refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial plugin-cohort discovery now uses the existing artifact-preserving reader before Doctor admits the capture. The fresh native journal read and live ownership checks at configuration publication remain in place. This uses the existing snapshot owner and its inspection-copy cost.

## Evidence

- Real published 2026.9.36 → pinned main `ba1f8c05821a`: candidate canary Doctor passed; installed Doctor failed on capture attribution. The base updater then reached its unchanged 1,500-second command timeout without final JSON. Configured-plugin and legacy-state flows independently reproduced the same Doctor failure.
- New owning-boundary regression is RED on pinned production because discovery changes the captured physical SQLite generation before the callback; the identical test is GREEN with this change.
- All 36 cohort/attribution tests pass, including real-write, same-content-commit and replaced-file refusal controls. Scoped production/test types, type-aware lint, default formatter parity, docs listing and diff checks pass.
- Full canonical package from `61e79b266b8d` passed inventory and import-integrity checks with 391 declarations. All three fresh published 2026.9.36 upgrades to this exact package PASS: base, configured plugins, and legacy operator state. Each recorded update success, exact build replacement, state survival and Gateway probes/status. The legacy flow also passed cron ownership, agent turn, plugin/UI, no-op update and backup/rollback checks.
- Fresh independent shared Codex autoreview of the final local diff against `ba1f8c05821a`, P0–P2: complete/scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewed file bytes match commit `61e79b266b8d`.
- The exact +19 test-line allocation covers this raw SQLite capture regression; the shared ceiling is unchanged.

- Exact-head CI [run 41290862424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41290862424), attempt 1, is successful on `61e79b266b8d`: 58 successful checks, 65 planned skips and one neutral result, with no pending or failed checks; the enforced aggregate also passed.

Canonical repair for the authorized update-reliability campaign: this PR. Hosted review found no introduced defects and identified the equivalent human-owned #190176. This bot-authored PR carries the campaign's full three-flow extended-stable replay, independent review and fully green exact-head CI. The production repair is equivalent; the requested steipete co-author credit is preserved, and the sibling's branch remains untouched.

title: fix: keep managed tool downloads from blocking guest turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes guest sandbox turns becoming stuck behind workspace recovery after a managed tool download, such as Crabbox, exceeds the 64 MiB result limit.

## User Impact

Re-downloadable managed tools stay with their runtime, so downloading them no longer prevents source edits from synchronizing or subsequent turns from starting. The size limit still applies to user files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sandbox exec defaults `HOME` to its container workspace; the default state directory is `$HOME/.openclaw`, so the managed installer writes tools into that workspace. Add only the checkout-root `.openclaw/tools` subtree to the existing derived-path policy, as with #188089, and regenerate its two embedded programs. Neighboring paths, nested project fixtures, and staged inputs remain covered by the existing preservation assertions.

## Evidence

- No duplicate found in open PR/issue searches for the reported error, Crabbox workspace synchronization, or managed tool caches.
- Base `091884c4c7895512ad700f27b96a5065207c2b25`: the extended `workspace-generated-paths.test.ts` fails two cases because `.openclaw/tools/cache.bin` and its ancestry leak into capture. A direct call through `parseChangedWorkspaceResult` reproduces the exact oversized error for `.openclaw/tools/crabbox/0.80.0/linux-amd64/crabbox`.
- Fixed: `timeout 600 pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-generated-paths.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23 passed; 37.10 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation (generated-path tests total under 1 second). [Exact-head CI run 41290717042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41290717042) passed.
- Fixed production reconciliation accepts a source edit alongside that oversized tool and still rejects oversized user files under `.openclaw/tools-notes`, `fixtures/.openclaw/tools`, and `.openclaw/project`.
- Targeted typecheck using the repository test configuration, targeted type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, `runtime:scripts:check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Simplification: one existing exclusion owner; production/generated delta +4 lines, test delta −1 line. No new helper, test file, or size-gate exception.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete working-tree candidate (published unchanged as `fb5d9188c3884cfb1b9da04011804d1534761896`) against the base above: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the repository fallback is covered by the already queued hosted ClawSweeper review; no duplicate request was posted.
- Validation covers real filesystem capture, remote manifest scripts, rsync, and the production comparison function. No live Gateway/model, Docker, or full local suites were run on the production host.

title: fix(sessions): avoid recurring Doctor warnings after native status
body:

Supersedes #184079, thanks @wangjx-xydt.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recurring Doctor legacy-delivery warnings when native `/status` is the first reply after `/new`.

## User Impact

Native status commands preserve canonical delivery without reintroducing a retired session field. Existing affected rows remain repairable through Doctor; no migration or configuration changes are needed.

The fast session initializer still copied the provider into the retired top-level `channel` field. title: fix(ios): hide archived chats from the active sidebar
body:

Fixes selected archived chats remaining in the iOS active sidebar, including pinned chats and a selected-row placeholder recreated after the active roster refreshes.

The existing iOS session-list owner filters archived rows alongside snoozed rows and suppresses missing selected-row placeholders after a complete active roster arrives. title: docs(config): warn before serializing Windows env snapshots
body:

Contributors can miss that Windows environment snapshots cannot cross worker serialization boundaries.

title: fix(slack): retain the thread subject on follow-up turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Slack channel and group thread follow-ups losing the original subject when the root is no longer in the session transcript or recent history.

## User Impact

The agent receives permitted thread-root text on later room-thread turns. Top-level messages stay top-level, and existing thread IDs and labels remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack withheld the existing thread-starter field after session initialization. Its reply preparation owner now supplies it on room follow-ups; shared reply admission already renders it as current conversation context. Existing sender filtering and DM behavior remain in effect.

Supersedes #172976, thanks @joetam.

Production LOC delta: 0 (+2/-2). The repair adds no new helper or state. Regression tests extend the existing preparation fixture by 12 lines, with a matching test-line allocation for warm-thread subject retention and top-level isolation.

## Evidence

- On main `cc8e68e3716fdc440a91707fab8c95a860785b71`, the warm-thread regression fails because `ThreadStarterBody` is absent while both thread IDs are correct; the top-level negative control passes.
- With the fix, all 121 tests across five focused Slack files pass (16.68 seconds wall time). This includes preparation, root filtering, DM handling, threading, and reply delivery.
- The existing shared reply-admission test confirms starter-only context reaches the warm-turn model context without entering the transcript (1 passed, 27.36 seconds wall time).
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41290292051) passed in 440 seconds (7 minutes 20 seconds).
- Local autoreview of the complete change against that main revision: `scoped-clean`, P0–P2. Its review covered the changed Slack owner and shared reply admission; unchanged root-fetch/filter internals were inspected separately against main.

title: fix(cli): load PowerShell completion with apostrophes
body:
Supersedes #173223, thanks @KhanCold.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PowerShell completion failing to load when a command name contains an apostrophe or an option choice contains a typographic apostrophe.

## User Impact

Completion scripts load and preserve literal choices and quoted command paths, including aliases. Users with an existing cache should regenerate it with `openclaw completion --shell powershell --write-state`. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing PowerShell quoting helper for generated literals and apply the same delimiter escaping to inserted choice arguments. Current main already handles ASCII apostrophes in choice arrays; command paths and typographic quote delimiters remain broken. Descriptions are not emitted by this generator.

The replacement was implemented from trusted main; contributor source was read through GitHub and never checked out or executed. Both human commit-author identities from the original PR are credited in the commit.

## Evidence

- Base `cc8e68e3716fdc440a91707fab8c95a860785b71`: the new regression cases fail (10 failed, 29 passed, 7 existing Fish skips); native PowerShell 7.6.9 rejects the script with “Missing statement block in switch statement clause.”
- Fixed focused completion suite: 39 passed, 7 existing Fish skips, 2.36 seconds wall time. Checks generated escaped literals and native completion for all five recognized single-quote delimiters, separated/equals values, canonical paths and aliases. Native proof ran on Linux PowerShell; Windows PowerShell was not run locally.
- Targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed. The focused production/test typecheck passed; exact-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41290186045) on `b735b2b16ee3bf0dbacb1cc3de722e9c6ff0a80e`.
- Local autoreview of the complete change against the base above: P0–P3, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Production and tests match reviewed snapshot; the test-line allocation was mechanically corrected from 35 to the formatted 38 lines afterward.

title: fix(ui): drop empty sidebar disclosure column
body:
## Problem

#189969 removed the hover condition from the disclosure-slot reserve added in #189906. Since then, every desktop sidebar row that has Archive but no child sessions keeps an empty column (about 30px) on its right edge. Only rows with the `> N` child toggle use that column. On every other row, titles truncate early and PR badges and hover actions sit one slot in from the edge.

## Solution

Remove the `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` block that shifts `.sidebar-recent-session__aside` and pads childless rows by `--sidebar-child-session-toggle-width`. Rows with a child toggle keep their existing rule (actions sit just left of the toggle). Childless rows go back to aligning their title, badges and actions with the row edge. That is the same edge the toggle uses.

## Accepted edge case

#189906 kept Archive away from where a disclosure toggle used to be. If a row's last child is removed while the pointer is resting on its toggle, Archive moves under the pointer. That fix relied on the column this PR removes. We are dropping the guarantee because the case is rare, visible (Archive shows on hover first) and recoverable (sessions can be unarchived). Keeping it costs every row an empty column. Its browser regression is replaced by the alignment regression below.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI E2E, desktop 1280×900, nav width 320, hovered childless row under a parent with `> 1`:

| Before (main) | After |

| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/099a8f61-c50a-4ba8-bb13-cde9bde50f09) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3950d9cb-6c66-4a65-83fb-64f466992dfa) |

title: feat(chat): choose how follow-ups interrupt active work
body:
Related: #57208 (prior interrupt/priority-control context; this PR does not implement pause/resume or drop queued siblings).

**Nov 3 update — prepared locally, not yet published:** two feature repairs and additional authority proof are ready, but the managed publisher refused the base integration because this request lacks full operator write authority for the upstream workflow-file changes. A maintainer with that authority must publish the saved candidate. The branch still points to `fcedbe2a1b07b1557154d53af0b8ea73bb40f6c5`; do not treat the locally prepared evidence below as proof that this remote head is repaired.

## What Problem This Solves

Users need a clear choice between waiting, steering at the next boundary, and interrupting current work for a follow-up, across chat surfaces rather than only in the Control UI.

## User Impact

User impact: choose a personal Queue, Steer, or Interrupt & send default, or promote an already accepted queued message without copying and resending it.

Interrupt requests cancellation immediately but waits for the incumbent writer to settle before the selected input runs. Other queued messages remain queued in order. Explicit per-message/session choices take precedence over the authenticated submitting profile's default, which takes precedence over channel/global defaults. Offline TUI controls remain session-local rather than inventing an authenticated personal profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a per-item **Interrupt & send** action and explain the three follow-up modes in the Control UI.
- Route interruption through shared `chat.interrupt` and existing queue/admission owners, promoting the original accepted input rather than cancel-and-resend. Keep input identity, scope/incarnation and current-authority checks, sibling ordering, and writer settlement intact.
- Expose common `/followupmode queue|steer|interrupt|default` and `/interrupt list|<id>` controls through the existing shared command catalog/forwarding paths, including the TUI and native/text-channel command surfaces. Active-run-safe controls do not themselves trigger the personal interrupt default.

This is the interrupt-options feature only; it does not claim to fix the separate lingering-steer or acknowledgment-copy bugs.

Contributor credit: @TheAngryPit. The source commit preserves the verified co-author trailer.

## Evidence

### Locally prepared repair candidate (not on the branch yet)

- Pinned base: `d40aa7c6f2ba70e0c59e244d09a325d25e1457b0`. Conflicts were confined to the append-only method table and generated predicates; upstream methods were retained and validators regenerated from canonical schemas.

- Reproduced another defect red through an actual Gateway: changing the personal default during delayed preparation reclassified an already accepted Queue input as Interrupt. The local repair preserves its accepted RPC timing choice; future inputs still use the new preference.
- Six real isolated-Gateway scenarios passed: RPC and shared-command interruption, a caller lacking session-write access, requester membership revoked across the handler’s actual awaited read, revoked queued-source authority, and the delayed-default regression. Observed provider cancellation/execution effects directly; a revoked source also failed at later execution and a fresh authorized input worked. These use a synthetic HTTP model, not a live provider or native Codex.
- 153 affected queue/command/TUI tests and 105 method-scope/prefix-stability consumer tests passed. Core, root-product-test and TUI-test typechecks passed; targeted lint/format and generated-validator/registry checks passed. Normal commit hooks passed; the hook skipped protocol regeneration for the partial commit index, so that check was run separately on the full candidate.

**Remaining proof:** latest-stable upgrade qualification has NOT run. The normal consumer installation of `openclaw@2026.10.9` was refused by the environment’s seven-day package-age policy. No exception, substitute baseline, schema change, or migration was introduced. This is neither proof of incompatibility nor successful upgrade proof. An operator-approved exception for that exact baseline, or its normal admission, is needed.

<details>
<summary>Investigated proof limitations</summary>

An overbroad post-revocation FIFO assertion also observed unrelated retained owner inputs ending with generic errors after the sharing revision changed. The final security cases isolate their distinct contracts: no cancellation/promotion from denied authority, no provider execution from the revoked source, and a fresh authorized request still works. Survival of other retained inputs across sharing-policy mutations is not qualified or claimed fixed. The prior unforced command-ordering failure led to the deterministic late-default regression and its repair; a passing replay alone was not used as the fix.

Hosted re-review has not been requested on the old head. Publish this candidate and current proof first, then request re-review.

title: fix: keep unrelated system Gateways from blocking Doctor migrations
body:
Fixes #190177. Supersedes #190180 with credit to @Satoshi-Kusumoto for the report and investigation.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can mistake another account's system Gateway for the caller's own state and refuse migration; the same incorrect facts can disrupt Gateway workers.

## User Impact

Caller-owned state can migrate when the older system Gateway is proven to use a different database. Shared or unverified state remains protected across accounts. Unreadable files, failed account/path inspection, manager or PAM selectors, and private filesystem mappings retain the restriction. Relative selectors also retain it rather than resolving against the CLI's working directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the service account's default home through NSS and carry incomplete inspection into the existing migration guard. Compare canonical paths and existing database identities, including symlinks and hard links. The systemd reader collects the extra environment and namespace facts under its existing bounded inspection contract; migrations and worker policy retain their current owners.

Unlike the proposed ownership heuristic in #190180, directory ownership never establishes separate state. This repair must be in the candidate CLI; it does not modify the installed updater, service lifecycle, database schema, or live Gateway.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `42d5039f0aa8`: a foreign service with a different account home falsely refuses migration. The shared-home and explicit-shared-state controls correctly refuse. The same run exposed unsafe allowance after unreadable environment/path inspection: 4 failed, 6 passed.
- Nineteen native-reader-to-migration cases pass. They cover separate/shared roots, explicit selectors, symlink and hard-link aliases, unreadable required/optional environment files, failed NSS/path inspection, manager/PAM sources, private binds, root mappings, and denied namespace inspection. Six new safety controls also failed before the review corrections.
- Final affected CLI/daemon suites: 171 tests passed in six files. The unchanged Doctor schema boundary and worker-owner suites also passed (37 tests); the Doctor suite exercised real isolated migration, backup, and refusal paths.
- Targeted production/test typecheck, seven-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- New test cost: about 0.1 seconds of test execution; the final six-file run took 43.21 seconds, predominantly shared compiler preparation. Exact-head [CI run 41292762491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41292762491) passed all 42 planned jobs on `5d6fc87645d411a299dc47ea0f3de84608aba01c` (attempt 1; 427 seconds wall time). Per-file CI time was not collected.
- Test-audit/pr-simplify: one boundary regression table, 270 justified test lines recorded in a separate allocation. Production grows by 191 net lines to collect affirmative identity facts and retain uncertainty; no ownership walker, account-match callback, or competing migration policy.
- Independent shared autoreview (Codex, local snapshot against `42d5039f0aa8`, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The first review found manager environment and private-mount gaps, corrected before the final review and covered by RED/GREEN controls. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the current head is already queued for hosted ClawSweeper review, so no duplicate request was posted.

Only isolated, timeout-wrapped local tests were run on the Team host. No production Gateway, operator state, or protected checkout was touched. A live multi-account upgrade/Gateway run was deliberately not performed under that host constraint. The reporter's live EnvironmentFile contents remain unverified; the reproduction uses synthetic, independently specified service facts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the run's surviving finalized replies when finalizing again, using ChatLog's existing tracking and pruning. Production LOC delta: **0** (one expression replaced). title: fix(media): play M4V attachments through codec-aware playback
body:
Supersedes #172163, thanks @fhgffy.
Closes #172162.

## What Problem This Solves

M4V video attachments skip codec-aware playback, leaving nonportable codecs without a playable inline rendition.

## User Impact

Portable H.264 M4V attachments pass through unchanged; supported nonportable M4V attachments can receive the existing bounded H.264 MP4 playback rendition. Original downloads remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize `video/x-m4v` in the existing MP4 codec-inspection and `mov` demuxer policy. Production LOC stays at **net 0** by removing the redundant `video/matroska` policy entry: canonical MIME normalization already maps it to `video/x-matroska`, whose entry remains and is exercised by the resolver tests.

History check: M4V was omitted in the original [playback-transcode feature, #115987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4229e96e0ec3394ab9d154d09992d825c64d8685). The later [container metadata fix, #116928](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b186d81c46d4cd7074589cf1a9fde5a9a4c0e52f) preserved M4V typing and explicitly deferred video-specific work. No removed M4V playback mapping was found.

## Evidence

- Base: `3db01a06ea008ec476e65cbf982d2d44cc148b27`. Two M4V resolver regressions fail on unchanged main: H.264 lacks native classification; nonportable M4V returns fallback instead of preparing. The 28 sibling cases pass.
- After repair: **150 focused tests pass** across playback resolution, staging, and MIME detection. Wrapper wall time **38.50 s**; MIME Vitest **0.267 s**, playback/staging Vitest **35.38 s**, including first-generation compiled-worker preparation. The [exact-head PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41288042350) completed successfully: 38 successful jobs, 5,317 aggregate job wall seconds (includes setup and broad checks; not per-test billed time).
- Real unmocked FFmpeg fixtures through the production detector and playback resolvers: both 500 ms, 16×16 M4V files previously returned fallback. A 1,681-byte H.264 source now returns native/passthrough; a 964-byte MPEG-4 Part 2 source goes preparing → transcoded, with ffprobe confirming H.264/yuv420p, 500 ms, 16×16. Both originals remain byte-identical.
- Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, one-page MDX validation, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. Tests grow by **8 lines**, with an exact scoped allocation for the native/conversion regressions and retained Matroska alias behavior; the shared baseline is unchanged. Author simplification and test-audit passes are complete.
- Canonical Codex autoreview (`gpt-6.1-sol`, medium, P0–P3) completed **scoped-clean**, with no findings, on the complete local candidate against the pinned base. Local ClawSweeper CLI is unavailable.

No live Gateway, browser/player, native-device playback, or external channel was exercised. Real resolver/FFmpeg proof covers the changed policy boundary; broad PR CI passed before merge.

title: fix: managed sandbox turns fail after Rewind
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: resending or retrying a message fails before the model starts after Stop → Rewind in a managed local sandbox. Branch switching has the same ownership gap.

## User Impact

Users can change local conversation history and continue with the same private checkout and saved edits. Foreign session incarnations remain rejected. This change does not deploy or rewrite any affected live session.

## Why This Change Was Made

History cuts must still rotate transcript identity to fence stale writers. The workspace owner now settles source edits and retires old runtime writers first, then records a private, bounded handoff receipt atomically with the cut. Fresh successor authority can finish that exact transfer after interruption without recreating the checkout or discarding its baseline/recovery state. A subsequent cut or reset consumes an earlier pending handoff before replacing its receipt.

Existing SQLite, reconciliation-lease, checkpoint, and runtime-retirement owners are reused; there is no new table or manager. Necessary growth is +247 net production lines and +233 regression lines.

## Evidence

- Red on base 33e8f6c: production Rewind/branch-switch handler + real SQLite and managed/private Git checkouts fails at the strict incarnation guard.
- Fixed candidate: 7 regression scenarios cover preserved edits and ignored guest files, edited resend/Retry, stale/foreign owners, conflict and commit revocation, disk reopen, interrupted receipt cleanup, consecutive cuts, and reset before adoption. Together with reset/memory/compound-worker siblings: 41 tests passed across 4 files.
- New regression file: 127.97s cold wall time, mostly shared worker compilation; CI timing pending. Real storage/filesystem coverage is necessary because a predicate mock would pass while the original flow stays broken. A 233-line allocation records this regression growth.
- Core typecheck, targeted gateway-methods test typecheck, targeted lint (15 files), formatting, line-cap/max-lines/test-line ratchets, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, complete 17-file local candidate against 33e8f6c, later committed unchanged as 6a80521: no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper source was unavailable; hosted review remains the selected fallback.
- Complete runtime build on 6a80521 passed (75.8s, including bootstrap import guard and postbuild stamps). The subsequent isolated agent CLI preflight was refused by the source-attribution guard.

Full isolated Gateway/model-turn proof is not claimed: this agent-exec context cannot inject operator agent messages without losing attribution. No live Gateway was restarted and no affected session was modified. title: fix(macos): recover companion Gateway after an in-place app update
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #190149: the macOS app can quit with “Client credentials unavailable” after an in-place update when a remote primary also hosts an app-managed local companion Gateway.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `GatewayAutostartPolicy` for stale-service eligibility and retain the companion's `--allow-unconfigured` installation flag. No new lifecycle owner or configuration is introduced.

The legacy managed-Node exclusion is deliberate: `ManagedNodeGatewayMigration` separately owns version updates and same-version Node-to-Bun migration. This early bundled-service replacement must not bypass that migration policy or the user's runtime choice. Legacy Node startup recovery is unchanged by this fix.

title: fix(browser): connect configured extension relays at HTTP startup

title: fix(mcp): preserve requester identity for CLI tool policies
body:
Supersedes #171791, thanks @alkor2000.
Closes #170576.

## What Problem This Solves

Owner-aware tool policies reject legitimate CLI-backed MCP calls because the original requester's identity is lost before policy evaluation.

## User Impact

Policy plugins receive the host-verified sender, channel, account, role, and ownership facts for CLI-backed tool calls. Unknown or absent identity remains unproven. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing harness requester projection, captured CLI grant, and tool-hook context. Inline the grant builder's two redundant session-key and elevated-default forwarding helpers; production code decreases by 6 lines overall.

Security note: requester identity comes only from the host-prepared run. MCP headers and tool arguments cannot assert sender, agent, or ownership. Attach grants and generic bearer callers acquire no requester identity. Requester-origin provenance and the live grant checks after awaited policy execution remain intact.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41284797823) passes, with 501 seconds workflow elapsed. The changed-node CI job takes 308 seconds across its selected contracts (not a per-file timing). The [combined CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41285360806) also passes.

- On main `4475bed8cf500c9be80257b2f142c1136bd9dfbd`, the six real HTTP requester-policy controls produce 3 intended failures (owner denied; guest and unknown-ownership metadata absent) and 3 passing denial controls. Baseline wrapper: 49.15 seconds.
- After the fix, all 97 tests in the MCP HTTP, grant-store, and CLI grant-builder suites pass (66.58 seconds wrapper). The six requester cases take 44 ms combined and cover forged headers and tool arguments, missing identity, unknown ownership, attach grants, and a generic owner bearer. Final grant-builder replay: 15 pass in 6.37 seconds wrapper.
- The CLI preparation/grant-transfer case passes (83.89 seconds wrapper; 111 unrelated cases filtered). The existing worker compiler dominates cold-run wall time; the HTTP owner boundary requires a real listener, capture, admission, and hook dispatch. Tool policy and tool effects are synthetic; no separately launched Gateway, vendor CLI/API, live channel, or deployment proof is claimed.
- Focused production/test import-closure typecheck, six-file typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Test growth is 101 lines, allocated in a dedicated record for the six HTTP security controls and existing preparation expectation; the shared baseline is unchanged. Broad proof and CI timings come from this replacement PR's CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview: `scoped-clean`, complete local candidate against main `4475bed8cf500c9be80257b2f142c1136bd9dfbd`, P0–P2, including unchanged requester projection, HTTP authentication/dispatch/cache, and policy bridge context; no findings. The reviewed snapshot matches the submitted source.

title: fix(database): Team Reports fails to port to PostgreSQL after a successful dry run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database port failing before it can record a recovery manifest when a profile contains Team Reports data, even though dry-run succeeds.

## User Impact

Operators can port populated Team Reports to PostgreSQL, resume interrupted publication, and return it to SQLite without renaming existing PostgreSQL schemas or losing retained rows. No schema, configuration, permission, or durability policy changes; SQL quoting and custody checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Team Reports already generates a quoted namespace containing `team-reports`. Anchor and recovery validation now share the restricted native-name contract, including that hyphen, while still rejecting quotes, statement separators, dots, and NUL. Catalog comparison normalizes the quoted namespace qualifier PostgreSQL emits in index definitions so the real schema and temporary reference compare equally. Existing namespaces are not renamed.

## Evidence

- **Real built CLI, isolated PostgreSQL 17.9, Node 26.12.1, synthetic populated Team Reports:** base dry-run exit 0; actual port exit 1 in capture-originals, no durable manifest, original file SHA-256 unchanged. Complete fix: forward dry-run and port exit 0; reverse dry-run and port exit 0. Retained `started_at_ms=9007199254740993` verified in PostgreSQL and returned SQLite as exact int64. Other SQLite families remain out of scope.
- **Regression red/green:** original anchor validation fails both new original/intended cases (17 existing passed, 2 new failed); repaired validation passes all 19. Removing only catalog qualifier repair makes the new real PostgreSQL Team Reports command regression fail; restoring it passes interrupted publication → resume (same anchor namespace) → SQLite return with int64 row preserved.
- **Qualified full sibling suite:** `pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with task-local conformance preload: **7 passed**, including state, workboard, agent, Team Reports, scoped backup, resume and rollback. Wall 149.4s (tests 78%); the complete command/custody and native workers require this integration boundary. Isolated new case: 17.0s test time. Recovery unit suite: **19 passed**, wall 38.5s including compiled-worker preparation. Hosted PostgreSQL shard wall times: 1209.94s, 906.41s, and 975.32s.
- Existing PostgreSQL privilege/ownership/RLS/catalog refusal suite: **1 passed** (1.8s test, 36.8s wall including compiled-worker preparation); no guards relaxed.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, targeted seven-file lint, infra test TypeScript project, formatter check and `git diff --check` pass. Native test bootstrap on Node 26 stalled; supported Node 24 test route passed, while real CLI proof used Node 26.12.1.
- An initial full sibling run lacked the documented `public.unaccent` extension and failed agent preparation, then surfaced OWNER_UNAVAILABLE. Installing that extension only in the isolated task cluster yielded the complete 7/7 result; no product guard was changed. One subsequent setup refusal followed expiry of the task PostgreSQL process; recovered within its same isolated data directory.
- Auto Review (OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol), local complete delta against native main base `546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d`, P0–P2 full-candidate scope (including CI consumer repairs): **scoped-clean**, no findings. This is not a claim of hosted review completion.
- **CI consumer repairs:** two malformed-anchor fixtures now use a genuinely invalid dot-containing identifier rather than a now-supported hyphen. Reproduced 2 failed / 67 passed, then **69 passed** in 25.7s wall; rejection, source-byte and cleanup assertions unchanged. Added the new namespace module to the native wrapper source inventory: source closure red 1 failed / 3 passed → **4 passed** (28.3s wall), plus eager runtime inventory **1 passed** (8.8s wall). No additional production changes; original real-product proof remains applicable.
- **Exact-head CI:** `1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694`: complete paginated check inventory reached 132/132 terminal with no failed checks; all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs passed. The required [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41285226589) is **success**, observed 2026-11-01 07:33 UTC. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun used.
- **Hosted review:** initial automatic review produced no verdict because input-safety put it on hold. No detected material is reproduced here; maintainer qualification/recovery is still required before a fresh hosted request. [Mitchell’s diagnostic comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190124#issuecomment-6636616441) identifies TruffleHog 3.99.4, the Postgres detector, and an unknown/unverifiable result against the reserved `example.invalid` host in the pre-existing synthetic fixture at `src/infra/database-engine/port-command.integration.test-support.ts:22`; no fixture value is reproduced. Canonical-source comparison confirms line 22 is byte-identical on base `546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d`, this head, and current `main` (line SHA-256 `eed91e5292521194254903f9d57a8ec12e5c47a5bf3c60a3f601c283fd42dc8f`). Base blob `f72e99227a2bdf706afd213b30827482b0807c16`, head blob `f9c2e0b623ca778981e92deb72d518a2f7f7ef9e`; the only PR hunk changes the cleanup regex at line 89 and brings the base blob into scan scope. Editing the fixture in this PR would not remove that base input. This human diagnosis is **not** maintainer fixture qualification. Current main still has the original blob; qualification in ClawSweeper policy or a landed main-branch repair has **not been verified**. The hold remains; no fresh review was requested.
- Simplify: one shared namespace contract replaces two drifting regex owners; owned catalog facts normalize in place instead of another projected copy. Production +17/-9 lines; 61 regression lines allocated separately because they protect recovery directions, unsafe-name refusal, and the real port/resume/reverse boundary. No live Team data, channels, provider calls, or migration were used. Full all-five-family rehearsal remains with its independent integration owner.


<details>
<summary>Retained CLI receipts, executed hosted regression, and namespace ownership audit (metadata-only follow-up)</summary>

### Actual retained CLI transcript and source binding

The original synthetic-profile receipts still exist and were read again; this is a short redacted extraction of their actual fields, not a new run. Paths, connection strings, credentials, configuration and database contents are omitted. PostgreSQL 17.9; actual CLI process Node 26.12.1:


```text
$ openclaw database port --family team-reports --to postgres --json --dry-run
BASE: exit 0; phase=preflight; originalUnchanged=true; manifestExists=false
$ openclaw database port --family team-reports --to postgres --json
BASE: exit 1; "Database port capture originals"; originalUnchanged=true; manifestExists=false
PROOF CANDIDATE: exit 0; phase=complete; engine=postgres; active manifest archived
$ openclaw database port --family team-reports --to sqlite --json --dry-run
PROOF CANDIDATE: exit 0; phase=preflight; engine=postgres
$ openclaw database port --family team-reports --to sqlite --json
PROOF CANDIDATE: exit 0; phase=complete; engine=sqlite; active manifest archived
```

The baseline source was the native refreshed main base `546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d`, not an unpublished integration tree. The managed guest Git HEAD remained `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`; the retained build stamp therefore reports that guest commit and `builtAt=2026-11-01T06:22:54.839Z`. The CLI proof exercised a **working-tree build**, before publication—not a clean build of `1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694`. Retained build/proof receipts and the implementation history bind the tested production patch SHA-256 `170f5d0082103aa3df64dbecd6d03c7afa95470d5f665939e668cef1a470f483`. A fresh read-only comparison against the four immutable public production blobs at the published head found byte equality for `physical-store.ts`, `port.worker.ts`, `postgres-namespace.ts` and `database-port-recovery.ts`. The later publication changed only test fixtures and the native wrapper inventory. Thus production proof is reused by byte identity; no runtime build of the later commit is claimed.

### The gated new regression really executed in hosted PostgreSQL CI

The suite is gated by `describe.skipIf(!fixtures.connection)`. This exact native [PostgreSQL conformance (3/3) job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41283634885/job/124780735056), run `41283634885` at head `1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694`, contains the following actual pass line (terminal color codes removed only):

```text
2026-11-01T07:22:03.8401020Z  ✓  infra  src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts > family-scoped database port > resumes and reverses Team Reports without renaming its quoted namespace 35514ms
```

The same log records the PostgreSQL-agent/SQLite-state backup sibling passing at 07:21:28 (30757ms), interrupted scoped publication/resume at 07:22:46 (18778ms), and rollback at 07:22:56 (10065ms). These are executed pass records, not skipped-case or aggregate-only coverage. The admitted log reader is tail-bounded, but all quoted lines are present in its returned native log.

### Uppercase recovery identifiers are intentional anchor compatibility

Yes: sharing this validator intentionally lets recovery represent identifiers the anchor owner already accepted. The [pre-change anchor contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d/src/infra/database-engine/physical-store.ts#L22-L29) allowed `[a-zA-Z_]` followed by `[a-zA-Z0-9_]*`. The former recovery-only lowercase regex was narrower than that existing anchor contract. The [src/infra/database-engine/postgres-namespace.ts:1-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/postgres-namespace.ts#L1-L3) shared contract retains that uppercase support and additionally admits the native Team Reports hyphen; [src/infra/database-port-recovery.ts:16-23](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-port-recovery.ts#L16-L23) applies it to both original and intended locations. PostgreSQL identifiers remain quoted, preserving case rather than relying on unquoted case folding. This does not change the lowercase-only **new-schema prefix configuration** ([src/config/zod-schema.database.ts:44-52](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/config/zod-schema.database.ts#L44-L52)) or rename stored namespaces.

Port-provider, orchestration, publication-context and backup facade/worker references pass recorded namespace facts to these SQL owners; they do not build another namespace SQL expression. Diagnostic messages, manifest/config identity fields, descriptor call arguments and catalog JSON/hash namespace replacement were classified separately as **non-SQL**, not counted as quoting evidence. No unquoted namespace identifier was found in the stated SQL scope.

### Why in-place catalog normalization has exclusive local ownership

[src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:403-414](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L403-L414) issues a new native Client query for that invocation, reads its JSON catalog, validates it, then `.filter(...)` creates a **new local facts array**. No cache, shared projection or retained other consumer receives the array or its elements. Before normalization, `some` and the filtered structural comparison inspect it; the separate invalid-index/constraint query does not receive `facts`. [src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts:65-100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts#L65-L100) validates/serializes for equality without retaining inputs. Only after those checks does [src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:452-463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L452-L463) replace each local fact's value and return the array to its caller.

Dependency ownership was also inspected, not inferred from the `filter` alone: installed `pg@8.23.1` client.js:687 creates a new Query for the string query; query.js:28 constructs a new Result; result.js:15 initializes `rows = []`. The installed pg-types text parser registers `JSON.parse` for JSON/JSONB (textParsers.js:202–203). `withPostgresConnection` constructs this ordinary Client without a custom row/parser cache. Thus the parsed catalog fact objects are fresh for this call too, not just a fresh array over cached shared objects. Normalization mutates that private result only; it does not weaken definition comparison or SQL quoting.

</details>

title: fix(browser): preserve aliased tabs and retained dashboards during eviction
body:
Supersedes #171427, thanks @trukhinyuri.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recently used browser tabs and retained dashboards being closed at the managed eight-page cap when their durable records use a profile alias.

## User Impact

Aliased tabs keep their recorded activity, and active or stopping dashboards remain protected. Released dashboards have relinquished retention and no longer displace session pages through stale activity timestamps. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing eviction reader now recognizes durable profile aliases and omits dashboard activity. The shared retention guard also honors aliases, protecting dashboards both during candidate selection and immediately before close dispatch.

Production LOC is unchanged (+15/-15): replacing the redundant timestamp comparison branch with a maximum keeps the repair in the existing owners. The cap, eviction order, and asynchronous best-effort cleanup remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current main `7e8ba3d34d1090633c197b688af2fbab25fbbf2c`: four new owner-boundary regressions failed with the wrong `/json/close` target (aliased activity, released-dashboard activity, and active/stopping aliased dashboards). The unrelated-profile control passed.
- After repair: 29/29 tab-selection tests and 52/52 dashboard ownership tests pass through production profile operations. These use synthetic CDP/store I/O; no live Gateway or Chromium proof is claimed. Eviction suite: 6.59s wall initially green; combined final two-file check: 22.42s wall. The final browser CI bundle passed in 198 seconds.
- Browser package typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. CI caught optional-field narrowing errors in the new Vitest table; these are repaired and a focused compiler project for the affected test now passes. The 29 runtime tests pass again (34.13s wall including compiler setup). Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41282128063) passed on `ab630a6819e2c1f97e1f5a1de8712a90241ddc54`, including the test-type lane (53 seconds) and required aggregate gate.
- Final local autoreview with complete eviction, retention, and tracking owner context: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the hosted review found no actionable findings on the production-identical first head.
- The five table cases add 58 test lines; the matching per-change allocation funds these distinct regressions and the unrelated-profile negative control without changing the shared baseline.
- Contributor code was read using `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` only and was never checked out or executed. Reimplemented from main with Yuri Trukhin credited in the commit.

title: feat(android): start new chats from Overview

## What Problem This Solves

Android Overview lets users resume a conversation but has no direct action for starting another one.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Overview now calls the same ordinary-new command as the sidebar, without new state, and reuses the existing translated Android label. title: fix(voice-call): guide ongoing errands into call briefs
body:
Supersedes #171089, thanks @aounakram.
Closes #171087

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent placing an outbound errand can put its purpose only in the spoken opening because the voice-call tool does not explain the ongoing task handoff.

## User Impact

The initiating model is told to put the ongoing task in `brief.task` and keep `message` as the verbatim opening. This clarifies an existing capability; no API, defaults, or permissions change. Improved model selection or live-call outcomes are not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-call brief introduced in #165716 already reaches both realtime speech and agent consultation. Its instructions explicitly govern the conversation after the opening. The remaining discovery gap is the tool's "Intro message" description. Replace that description with a single instruction and align the existing documentation sentence.

Production LOC delta: 0. No extra machinery or deletion is needed. The registered-tool regression adds 15 test lines, with an exact 15-line allocation to protect this model-facing instruction; docs add one line.

Human credit: `Co-authored-by: Aoun Akram <aounakram@me.com>` from the original PR commit author. Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or run; this is an independent reimplementation on current main.

## Evidence

- Red on main `546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d`: the new registered-tool schema regression failed because the description was "Intro message" instead of guidance to put the ongoing task in `brief.task` (23 ms).
- Green: `env -u OPENCLAW_CLI pnpm test extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/call-brief.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 75 tests passed, including the new regression (2 ms). Total Vitest 47.62 s / shard wall 49.78 s, mostly first-use transform. The first unfiltered run inherited `OPENCLAW_CLI=1` from the host and skipped service startup; it was stopped, then rerun with that variable unset only for the test process.
- Stable prompt contract: `env -u OPENCLAW_CLI pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed; shard wall 29.73 s.
- Targeted schema typecheck (`run-tsgo --ignoreConfig --noEmit --skipLibCheck --target esnext --module nodenext`), changed-file lint (`run-oxlint --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json`), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Tests/checks were bounded with `timeout` and `nice` on the task-owned checkout; broad proof is PR CI.
- Canonical autoreview, Codex, P0–P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings across the complete local functional diff and supplied plugin registration/brief context. The allocation was subsequently narrowed to the exact 15 added lines and normalized to the required integer format. The local ClawSweeper CLI is unavailable on this lane; one [hosted review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190110#issuecomment-6554301336) under the maintainer fallback route and was still running at merge (advisory).
- This is production-registration boundary proof of exposed instructions. No live telephone call or running-Gateway/model-selection evaluation was performed. Existing realtime/consult tests support the established handoff; they do not prove model compliance.
- Test-line budget passed (`pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main`): 6,368,964 lines under the 6,387,904 ceiling. The staged inventory variant hit its 30 s deadline; the equivalent committed working-tree check passed.
- Broad proof: [CI run 41279561002](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41279561002) passed on exact head `bc1a6c49727ea4ec91bd554c650ce9863e1dc6c8`; all 33 executed jobs succeeded. Elapsed CI wall time was 466 s (7 min 46 s); incremental regression CI seconds are not separately available in the grouped jobs. Merged as `7898daa82ca0135ff97d23eb649ab5f523cbdd8b`.

title: fix(ui): suggest usage filters beyond the first six catalog entries
body:
Supersedes #171051, thanks @ooiuuii.

Closes #171050

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Usage autocomplete omits matching models, providers, agents, channels, and tools beyond the first six catalog entries.

## User Impact

Typing a filter can discover any matching catalog value, with at most six suggestions shown. Spelling, ordering, and quoted multiword values are preserved. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing suggestion owner now matches before applying the display cap. This deliberately accepts full-catalog matching requested in #171051 while retaining the six-result limit.

Production: +1 line for the post-match cap; the redundant empty-value predicate was removed in the same expression. Tests: −17 lines by replacing the capped test-helper fixture with the actual matcher contract. No unrelated production deletion was warranted.

## Evidence

- Baseline: `546523f8cfc7bf809d653241658e74ebba86af6d` (current main at investigation). The committed regression failed with `[]` instead of the later agent matches. After the fix, query + view tests passed: 24 tests, 3.21s wrapper wall time. The regression covers all five categorical keys, quoted input, spelling, missing matches, and the six-result cap.
- Focused Chromium proof through the actual `/usage` source route and real `buildUsageOverview` producer, with synthetic mock Gateway transport: before, `model:seventh` offers no suggestion; after, `model:seventh-model` appears, clicking and pressing Enter sends `sessions.usage` with the selected query and displays only its matching session. RED 9.03s; GREEN 5.25s wrapper wall time. This was a temporary proof harness, not a live Gateway/provider or bundled-build claim.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped type-aware oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41279405330) passed, including all three UI shards and the selected browser E2E shard.
