title: fix(gateway): honor TLS when probing configured SSH endpoints
body:
Supersedes #171105, thanks @zhangguiping-xydt.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a healthy configured TLS Gateway reporting a failed SSH probe because the diagnostic sends plaintext WebSocket traffic through its tunnel.

## User Impact

Configured TLS Gateways can be probed over their matching SSH route, retaining the endpoint's certificate identity and URL path. No configuration migration or new option is required.

Security note: SSH forwarding does not bypass TLS verification. A saved fingerprint remains enforced before the WebSocket upgrade; without a pin, normal CA and hostname verification remain enabled. Other SSH targets, remote ports, and configured direct transports do not inherit the endpoint's TLS settings. SSH host-key policy is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe retains the configured endpoint only when the existing route resolver identifies the selected SSH target and remote port. The existing Gateway client owns forwarding-address substitution and TLS validation. The diagnostic reports the canonical TLS endpoint; its tunnel metadata still records the allocated local port.

Production delta is **+28/-22, net +6**. Removed duplicate origin-scoping branches, redundant default-port handling, nested local-certificate selection, and duplicated result assembly in the same command owner. The remaining growth binds the configured TLS endpoint to its SSH route; no parallel TLS implementation was added. The explicit async result type is retained because closure writes otherwise cause incorrect null-only inference.

## Evidence

- Red on main `e0ed68c7b845b240221e289c1160b5dddced5945`: the seven-case regression has four TLS failures and three passing route exclusions. Matching-pin probes report `socket hang up`; wrong-pin and CA cases never reach TLS verification.
- Green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/gateway-status.tls.test.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **37 passed**, 36.83 s wall time, including 259 ms for the seven transport cases. Wrong fingerprints report a mismatch and untrusted certificates reject without a WebSocket connection. Tunnels close after each diagnostic.
- Targeted tsgo, type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. [Broad PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41278561812) passed on `7634599046adf1313070ff6f072915c3df1d19c7` (452 s wall; the four changed-test jobs used 570 s combined). Per-test CI timing is unavailable.
- Local autoreview: P0–P2, base `e0ed68c7b845b240221e289c1160b5dddced5945`, complete local candidate and unchanged transport/route owners supplied; **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The original async return annotation was subsequently restored to satisfy the targeted linter; runtime behavior is identical.
- The **200-line** regression allocation covers the public command, real TLS/WebSocket traffic through a real TCP forwarder, trust rejection, route exclusions, and cleanup. OpenSSH process startup is substituted; SSH authentication and a full Gateway/model boot were not exercised. Contributor code was read through GitHub only and was never checked out or executed.

Human contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: zhang-guiping <zhang.guiping@xydigit.com>`.

title: fix(ui): stop chat retries when scroll anchoring makes no progress

title: fix(backup): let large Git backups finish content work
body:
Supersedes #170450, thanks @wangmiao0668000666.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Git backups failing to commit, restore, or verify when hashing or materializing large artifacts takes longer than the generic two-minute Git deadline.

## User Impact

Local content work gets a deadline sized from the data: one second per MiB, with a two-minute floor and a 24-hour cap. Small backups keep the existing deadline. A wedged command still has a finite limit; no configuration or backup format changes are required. Remote push deadlines are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main still gives `update-index` and streamed blob reads the fixed 120-second deadline. Size staging from the refreshed owned files, treating pruned files as zero bytes, and size restore/verification from Git's committed blob sizes. The existing backup owner applies both budgets; unrelated files never enter the size inventory.

The contributor identified the staging failure. This replacement derives the deadline from actual data instead of giving every backup a fixed 24 hours. Artifact validation and size preparation now share one traversal. Production growth is +15 lines; the remaining size accounting and bounded policy are necessary, and no equivalent dead code was found to remove safely. Two parameterized regression tests add 114 lines, with a dedicated test-line allocation for the previously uncovered timeout and bound contracts.

## Evidence

- On main `8662c66b9050fb9328ad291fa2d198cca449df99`, both owner regressions failed at the intended content boundary: staging raised `GitCommandTimeoutError` with the 120-second budget; restore failed its slow-blob fixture.
- With the fix, all six size/bound cases passed through real SQLite and Git owners. Fixed external size and latency fixtures model small, 256 MiB, and 100 GiB artifacts without allocating gigabytes or sleeping. The tests also preserve unrelated files, prune retired artifacts, and restore with the working copy removed. Budget tests: 7.97 s wall, about 6.3 s test time.
- Existing ownership and cleanup suites: 14 passed. Backup suite: 21 passed, one Windows-only skip, and one inherited Git-author-environment failure; its focused rerun with inherited author/committer variables removed passed. The fallback-identity implementation is unchanged from main.
- Focused typecheck (changed source/tests plus repository ambient types), targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. [Full PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41274662028) and the [final security/gate publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41276106286) passed for `1f8d7858268f7b1d0c77cdf9f745dfce447e7d4a`. Real multi-gigabyte throughput and remote pushes were not tested locally.
- Shared autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, base `8662c66b9050fb9328ad291fa2d198cca449df99` through the final local candidate: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed source matches committed head `1f8d7858268f7b1d0c77cdf9f745dfce447e7d4a`. Hosted ClawSweeper also found no actionable defects; the disclosed proof limitation is owner-boundary coverage rather than a shipped-CLI slow-I/O trace.
- Contributor code was read using `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or run. This is an independent implementation with the human commit author credited.

title: fix: SQLite snapshots fail in EFS-encrypted Windows caches
body:
Supersedes #169159, thanks @JasonBuildAI.

Related: #169157.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite snapshot reads and Doctor migration detection failing when Windows EFS-encrypted cache directories reject same-directory renames with `EXDEV`.

## User Impact

Affected Windows users can inspect SQLite state without relocating their cache or disabling encryption. Other rename errors still fail visibly; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copy directly into the existing partial snapshot instead of promoting an intermediate `first` file. At final publication, fall back only on `EXDEV` to the existing guarded, exclusive file-copy primitive, flush the destination, and remove the staged file. The family stays private until preparation returns, so publication does not require an atomic rename. Existing cleanup owns failed copies.

Production delta: +21/−8, net +13. Removed the intermediate file, its redundant rename, and its cleanup branch. The remaining growth is the required durable fallback; no new module, wrapper registration, or policy owner. Legacy `first` artifacts remain recognized for abandoned-snapshot cleanup after upgrades. Test delta: +44, with a dedicated allocation for the three preparation paths and the distinct non-EXDEV failure control.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `9af7ded4487eb38dce6401b46d89b2e4f491d2f9`.

- Green: primary snapshot suite, 30 passed (10.56 seconds wrapper wall time, 8.84 seconds Vitest duration). Copy and cleanup suites also pass (39 existing tests plus the four regressions before their move to the primary suite; 36.86 seconds wrapper wall time including compilation).

Hosted ClawSweeper review of the same head also found no actionable defects; its native Windows evidence gap matches the limitation below.

title: fix(litellm): allow single-image Gemini edits
body:
Supersedes #169129, thanks @LiuwqGit. Thanks also @obviyus for the edit-only scope and earlier boundary evidence.
Related: #169120.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes single-image Gemini edits through LiteLLM failing with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError` because OpenClaw always sends `n=1`.

## User Impact

Default and explicit count=1 image edits omit `n`; callers requesting multiple outputs retain their count and normal backend errors. Generation behavior is unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing LiteLLM multipart edit builder now sends `n` only for counts greater than one. LiteLLM's [Gemini edit adapter](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/60fc121ce8ab995cb2997e0bbd0a980ee93c627d/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/image_edit/vertex_gemini_transformation.py#L51) supports `size` but excludes `n`; its [parameter validator](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/60fc121ce8ab995cb2997e0bbd0a980ee93c627d/litellm/images/utils.py#L37) rejects unsupported supplied parameters. There is no global parameter dropping or model-name special case.

Production delta: **+4/-4, net 0**. The existing multipart explanation is consolidated into one comment covering the upload and Gemini constraints. There is no new helper or state owner. Test growth is **11 lines**, with a scoped allocation for the distinct default/explicit edit-count regressions and unchanged generation-count control; existing upload assertions and scaffolding are reused.

## Evidence

- Main `042ad2da5f2e5a83ab03a748fd9ac607bc7fd491` unconditionally sends multipart `n`. Landed #190058 (`a460b0c1ead257e25296b586b3ad6d46bf47ab81`) changes OpenAI geometry, and #189830 (`c43e20b17d563b059a620c2d25ff3713897537b2`) changes returned image reporting; neither repairs LiteLLM edit counts.
- Before production edits, the expanded provider suite failed **3 cases**, with **18 passing**: omitted count with one/two references and explicit count=1 all received `"1"` where the expected multipart field was absent. Explicit count=2 and generation controls already passed. Command wall time: 41.70 s, dominated by first-run worker compilation.

This covers the production provider's request assembly, reference uploads, URL output handling, credentials, and deadlines. The successful CI shard reports 0.095 s of provider case time and 1.176 s of URL-suite case time; those are summed test-case times, not standalone command wall times.

Supplied unchanged context includes the shared image-provider owner and LiteLLM URL suite. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; its hosted review was automatically queued for this head. AutoReview supplies the completed independent review.

No paid Gemini API call, real LiteLLM proxy run, live Gateway operation, or Team deployment was performed. Earlier contributor fixture evidence is not presented as a live Gemini result. title: fix(tooling): handle Windows paths in repository checks

title: fix(update): preserve repair budgets across clock changes
body:
Supersedes #185384, with thanks to @SunnyShu0925.

## What Problem This Solves

Installation-repair agent turns can receive a 1 ms timeout or an inflated timeout when the system clock changes during preparation.

## User Impact

Repair turns keep their configured elapsed-time budget across forward and backward wall-clock corrections. The invoking repair runtime must contain the fix; an older updater does not gain it from a candidate it has not started.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `monotonicDeadlineAfter` and `remainingMonotonicMs` helpers for the process-local per-turn deadline. The existing fixed abort timer, expiry clamp, authority checks, and cleanup retain their current behavior.

- Regression through `runUpdateRepairTurn` with isolated state and a mocked embedded transport: after 250 ms of preparation, a 10,000 ms budget must pass 9,750 ms even when wall time jumps ±60,000 ms. Operators see a warning for each node's distinct withheld command set, while identical reconnect outcomes remain available at debug. Command admission and pairing behavior are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared node-connect reconciler owns this warning for WebSocket and watch HTTP nodes. Reuse `rememberBoundedKey` and the existing close/restart lifecycle set instead of introducing a separate cache implementation. Keys include the node identity and sorted unique withheld commands, so another node or a previously unseen policy outcome still warns.

The bounded history retains 1,024 distinct node/set keys per Gateway run. Returning to a previously warned set stays at debug; eviction can produce another warning. Gateway close and in-process restart clear the history.

Production delta is +11 lines; test delta is +57 lines. The necessary growth is the shared dedupe/lifecycle wiring and warning key; no safe dead code in this owner was identified to offset it. A separate 57-line test allocation covers reconnect, changed-policy/node, and lifecycle regressions without changing the shared baseline. The simplify pass retained one warning owner and no custom cache machinery.

## Evidence

- On current main `52e113b095d9414278358ef643a7947104e49b57`, the regression fails at warning counts: identical reconnects each warn (3 failing regression cases, 9 existing tests pass; 2.47 seconds wall).

- Focused oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, mock-export and test-line guards: pass. Initial PR CI passed the typecheck, lint, and test jobs, then exposed two test-guard defects, corrected here by preserving logger exports and using an integer-only allocation. Final [CI run 41268886286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268886286) passed all selected jobs on `ec3f9d5bf7bdd68fec9490083db4c33b2fc3cb71` (8m 28s elapsed).

title: fix: worker transfers trust unverified peers with whitespace TLS pins
body:
Supersedes #168533, thanks @avelev99.
Related: #167094.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker workspace transfers accepting an untrusted HTTPS peer when the gateway certificate fingerprint contains only whitespace.

## User Impact

Blank fingerprints now use standard CA verification; explicit correct pins still accept self-signed peers, and wrong pins reject them before sending credentials or workspace bytes. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize with the existing shared fingerprint helper before choosing TLS pin mode. Move malformed-pin rejection to request creation and remove duplicate normalization from the socket verifier. Production delta: -2 lines; regression tests: +19 lines, with an exact separate test-line allocation for download/upload TLS admission coverage.

Security review: the previous raw-string truthiness check disabled CA validation for whitespace while the verifier skipped trimmed blanks. Only a normalized SHA-256 pin now disables CA validation, and that pin is verified before HTTP transmission. HTTP behavior, pooled-socket pin verification, and proxy routing are preserved. Upstream CLI/WebSocket and worker-endpoint validators also reject malformed pins; this is hardening of the shared transfer owner, not a claim of a demonstrated CLI interception.

## Evidence

- Baseline `d1b6e3010097ca5130bd630beba99ed9d7fc5e75`: focused regression run failed exactly the whitespace download and upload cases because both transfers completed against a self-signed HTTPS peer; the other eight admission cases passed.
- Fixed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/node-worker-transfer-client.test.ts src/node-host/node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 67 passed, 1 platform skip; 35.56 seconds wall time including a cold worker compilation, about 1 second executing tests. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41267168966) passed in 505 seconds wall time; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` is green.
- The real `runNodeWorkerWorkspaceTransfer` download/upload paths reject undefined, empty, whitespace, wrong, and malformed pins with zero decrypted HTTP bytes and zero HTTP requests received by the rejected peer. Existing correct-pin tests complete downloads and uploads, including pooled and replacement sockets and managed proxies. The shared self-signed certificate is expired, so CA-mode assertions accept either self-signed or expiration rejection.
- Targeted typecheck of the changed source/test import closure, targeted Oxlint, formatting, test-line allocation check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview, Codex, P0–P2, against the above main base: scoped clean, no actionable findings. The subsequent change only renamed a shadowed test callback parameter for lint.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. This replacement was independently implemented on main. All fixtures and credentials are synthetic; no production Gateway or live state was changed. No full Gateway/model session or latest-stable upgrade was run for this transport-only change.

title: fix(voice): Discord controls and phone consults fail with PostgreSQL agent stores
body:
Related: #189036

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm) requested and guided this repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/91bf5c8e-90b2-4f50-a7b4-fd877499b08b)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord voice active-run controls and realtime phone-call agent consultations fail when agent storage uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

The two bundled voice surfaces can use PostgreSQL-backed agent stores while retaining model-selection locks, current speaker/call authority, and the existing synchronous SDK contracts. No configuration, schema, migration, or permission-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both consumers still reached synchronous session-entry reads on the Gateway thread, which PostgreSQL intentionally refuses.

- Expose the existing worker-backed model-lock check as an additive async SDK helper, reuse its existing candidate selection/predicate, and await it in voice-call before fast-context lookup and before returning its result. Recheck the live call after each wait.
- Allow asynchronous caller-policy preparation in the existing run controller and migrate Discord to it. Preparation repeats for each injection admission; a separate live caller assertion remains at enqueue and cancellation effects, including the legacy key-selected path.
- Preserve the synchronous helper/callback and released dependency-adapter contracts; no synchronous fallback is selected after a worker failure.

This is distinct from @ceckert's #189036: that PR owns the four Gateway Talk surfaces and explicitly excludes these bundled SDK consumers. This PR leaves those Gateway callers untouched and does not import that branch. Both touch the shared run controller; whichever lands second must reconcile that common owner without duplicating its implementation or dropping either set of live guards.

The private async lock check is consolidated rather than adding another lock owner. Production changes are +58/-22 lines; no new manager, cache, or storage owner is introduced. The 242 net test lines cover the distinct consumer lifetime, worker-failure, model-lock, fingerprint and final-cancellation boundaries and are recorded in their own test-line allocation.

## Evidence

### Actual product and storage boundary

Built the clean baseline `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0` and the candidate with the canonical `pnpm build`, on Node 24.20.0. All six changed production blobs remain unchanged since the candidate product proof; later adjustments only prepare runtime config in the cancellation-test fixture and migrate the root Discord integration assertion.

The disposable Gateway used real PostgreSQL 17.11 agent storage (`database.engine: sqlite`, `database.families.agent.engine: postgres`). A signed synthetic Twilio webhook issued the one-use stream URL; a carrier WebSocket sent documented start/media frames through the real voice-call server and bundled OpenAI Realtime bridge. Local Realtime WebSocket and model SSE protocol fixtures supplied synthetic transcript/tool output and a deterministic model response. The actual OpenClaw agent turn, session controller, storage, public history RPC and shutdown ran normally. No paid provider traffic or live Team state was used.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean baseline, PostgreSQL | Final tool result contains `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`; zero agent-model requests. |
| Candidate, PostgreSQL | One agent-model request; final tool result contains `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER`; authenticated `chat.history` returns that assistant answer. |
| Independent PostgreSQL read after clean Gateway shutdown | `assistant_rows=1`, `marker_answers=1`. |
| Candidate, SQLite control | Same signed-carrier flow returns `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER` with one model request; clean shutdown. |

A separate source-bound probe runs the real registered voice-call consult handler and the actual Discord voice consumer/public controller against real PostgreSQL session reads. Both baseline consumers refuse at their synchronous session reader; both migrated consumers pass on PostgreSQL and SQLite. The Discord backend is a synthetic guarded run attached through the real controller, not a real Discord transport. A separate Gateway-role probe confirms the deprecated synchronous PostgreSQL read still throws the original main-thread guard.

Limits: the carrier is a simulator, and Realtime/model responses are protocol fixtures. This does not claim real Twilio/Discord server operation, microphone capture, speech recognition/synthesis quality, or commercial model inference.

### Regressions and checks

- With the original six production files temporarily restored, the three new run-control regressions fail for the intended behavior: allowed async-policy steering does not reach the backend, and cancellation proceeds instead of honoring the revoked caller. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; the complete stop/control suite passes 12 tests.
- New consumer cases deny use after speaker revocation, session/call replacement or closure, worker failure, and a model lock applied during fast-context preparation. Existing synchronous callback/dependency-adapter cases remain covered. The synchronous model-lock helper and dependency-adapter type are byte-identical to the baseline.
- Shared Talk/control suites: 52 tests passed. Discord voice runtime e2e: 27 tests passed in both configured runs. Prompt-prefix stability: 14 tests passed. Voice-call runtime: 26 tests passed. The exact six-file Discord shard replay printed 169 tests passed.
- Core/extension production types, owning core/extension test-type graphs, targeted typed lint, formatting, SDK export/declaration generation, mock-export, line-cap and test-line checks pass. Full canonical build passed with bounded native thread pools after an initial local process-limit failure.
- Exact-head CI caught one missed root Discord integration assertion of the old callback shape. Reproduced locally (2 failures), migrated its expected async callback/live guard, and reran the complete file: 8 passed, exit 0 (13.19 s including preparation). A repository-wide callback search found no other unmigrated Discord expectations; legacy Gateway/synchronous SDK tests remain unchanged.
- Native Auto Review: complete local candidate against `9c22cf86`, through P2, **scoped-clean**, no findings. It reviewed code/context, not execution.

One larger run observed `realtime-turns.test.ts > treats a bare wake name as an activation for the next realtime transcript` fail before agent dispatch. An unchanged-code exact-shard replay printed all 169 Discord and 26 voice-call tests passed, but exec finalization failed during a transient stopped-container incident. No fix or clean terminal exit is claimed for that replay, and baseline attribution of the original wake-name failure remains unconfirmed. The separate control/prefix run subsequently completed with exit 0 after the sandbox recovered.

New-case files reuse existing suites rather than adding a cold suite/job: individual new cases take 1–2 ms in the consumer output; the voice-call file completed in 7.52 s wall, and the control/prefix command in 62.55 s including compilation/preparation. Exact-head CI for `d783c53ce3d87fdf4fb69130909dd9b7f3fae5da` passed [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41267798066/job/124735928893): no failed or timed-out jobs, all selected prerequisites succeeded, and `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false`. The formerly failing root integration shard is green.

- @etzelm

Fixes native diagram bundles identifying Pele as 1.6.0 even though they ship 1.9.0.

## User Impact

Accurate third-party version attribution in Android and Apple renderer resources. No rendering, dependency, permission, or license-term changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Correct the canonical notice used by both native packaging paths and guard its Pele/DOMPurify headings against the package pins. No new production machinery: one notice line changes, with an 11-line regression allocation.

- Real renderer build and Apple resource preparation reproduced the stale heading before the fix.
- Version-parity regression failed on the old notice; final focused suite passes 3/3, independently rerun by the parent with the repository-owned runner.
- Native asset and Apple cache suites: 9/9 passed. Real renderer build and Apple preparation/cache-hit checks passed; shared and Apple resources match byte-for-byte.
- Installed Pele MIT + Lucide ISC text matches redistributed notices; license text is unchanged.
- Focused lint, strict single-file typecheck, format, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh isolated Codex P0–P3 autoreview: scoped-clean.
- No Android device/SDK or Apple execution toolchain was available. This is packaging proof, not current-head native visual/runtime acceptance. No leases or native CI dispatches/reruns.

title: fix(sessions): cold PostgreSQL conversations fail after idle readers close
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cold transcript writes and restoration-dependent operations failing on PostgreSQL after the Gateway's cached native reader retires.

## User Impact

Cold conversations no longer depend on a boot-admitted main-thread database connection. SQLite, native maintenance, source checks, writer ordering, cancellation and commit settlement retain their existing contracts. No configuration, schema, durability, retention or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the agent database's existing worker execution generation for cold restoration. Preserve the ordinary committed display notification as well as the separate facts-only receipt publication; reopening historical archives must still refresh readers.

The author simplification pass kept one owner and no new connection, fallback, cache or API. Production is net −1 line. The new real-engine regression and adjusted native-publication fixture add exactly 142 test lines, with matching scoped allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

Qualified locally on **Node 26.12.1 and real PostgreSQL 17.11** with SQLite controls; all state, services and model traffic were disposable and local.

- **Base red, fixed green:** a Gateway-role main process with no host compatibility reader restores a real cold archive, preserves the original rows and rewrite generation, publishes one ordinary display notification, then appends and reads subsequent messages. The base throws “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker”.
- **Built Gateway RPC:** the warm baseline initially succeeds because startup retains a reader. A fixture explicitly invokes that production reader owner's idle cleanup—not a shortened production timeout or a natural 30-minute wait. After observing native readers **1→0**, base chat.inject refuses with the same guard and makes zero provider requests. The final build succeeds, retains original history, completes a real agent turn through a deterministic loopback HTTP model, survives a new-process restart, and completes a later turn: **two actual model HTTP requests**. No Team data or paid provider was used. An initial fixture signal collided with the Gateway restart signal; the corrected non-restart stimulus was rerun on both base and final source.
- **86 focused tests passed across six files**, covering both engines, publication, cancellation, stale source/owner checks, missing/corrupt archives, reopen and parent-fork consumers. Final command wall time: **119.6 seconds**, including compilation/wrappers. The two-case conformance file runs in about 5–6 seconds of test time; hosted CI time is not yet available.
- Production and affected infra/session test typechecks, scoped lint/format, whitespace, exact test-line allocation and database worker ratchet passed. The inventory remains **168→168 T1** calls; this is not a whole-Gateway SQL or performance claim.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review, complete local candidate against 9c22cf86, P0–P2: scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed the supplied diff/source context, not an independent test execution.

**CI follow-up:** [Initial exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266454178/job/124730545714) caught an obsolete incomplete-mock exemption for the fixture removed here. The same failure reproduced locally. Removing precisely that one exemption makes the mock-factory ratchet pass; no exemption was added or broadened. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of this one-line follow-up is scoped-clean. Runtime/test source and the built-product proof are unchanged; the updated head requires its own CI.

### Inspectable shipped-runtime capture

Re-ran the same local shipped-Gateway flow with actual whitelisted RPC, reader-owner and received HTTP-request observations recorded below. This is **metadata/evidence only**: the full tracked index equals published head `e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` (`git diff --cached --exit-code e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` exited 0), and `git diff --exit-code` exited 0.

The maintained `createOpenClawTestInstance` starts `dist/index.js`; that working-tree runtime was built with `pnpm build:runtime`. The native publisher preserves the guest Git HEAD, so the retained build stamp correctly says base `9c22cf86`, `inputsClean:false`, **not** the published commit. The production inputs equal the published tree; the subsequent commit only removes the stale mock exemption. The complete regular-file dist manifest was identical before/after this run. Hashes below identify captured bytes, not independent attestation.


The fixture invokes the actual reader owner's `closeIfIdle()` using a task-only SIGURG preload, rather than waiting 30 minutes or changing production policy. title: docs: correct pairing and transcript storage guidance
body:
Supersedes #167983, thanks @akshitkhokhani.

## What Problem This Solves

The setup and security guides point operators at legacy pairing JSON files and omit authoritative cold transcript archives from backup and retention advice.

## User Impact

Operators can locate current pairing approvals and preserve cold history when copying databases. Documentation only; no runtime or security-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the shared database as the pairing authority, identify SQLite as the default while linking the optional database engines, and direct transcript retention to supported session maintenance. Preserve the existing permissions, full-disk encryption recommendations, and raw-transcript/redaction guidance.

## Evidence

- Source audit on main `ebf13610e1b8`: the three summaries still named legacy pairing files; the cold-archive warning was absent. The corrected summaries now match the channel/account-scoped reader and writer in `src/pairing/pairing-store-sqlite.ts`, database path and engine owners, Doctor migration, and canonical pairing documentation.
- Verified cold archive location, explicit missing/corrupt-file failures, and backup embedding against `session-cold-storage-codec.ts`, `paths.ts`, `session-cold-storage-backup.worker.ts`, and the canonical session-maintenance guide.
- Docs checks: formatting, Markdown and template lint, MDX, i18n glossary, internal links (16,213 checked; zero broken), config examples, changelog validation, and `git diff --check`. Initial table alignment failures were corrected and the affected checks rerun successfully.

title: fix(agents): detached tool runs lose their final reply
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Detached tool runs can finish their work but lose the recovered final reply; a cancelled finalizer can also append that reply to its borrowed transcript after admission closes.

Supersedes #167892, thanks @ethanhawkes-gif.

## User Impact

Detached runs return their recovered answer through the original transcript, and revoked runs cannot persist a late answer. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing harness admission for tool-free finalization, retain its native registration fingerprint, and carry the live run assertion into the borrowed manager's write admission. Current main already retains child writer context (#140399) and serializes session turns (#175837); these remaining finalizer boundaries still needed repair.

Production LOC is net zero (+43/-43): one finalizer parameter object replaces duplicate identity assembly, and redundant projection aliases are removed. The 210-line regression allocation covers the real runner/native-registration/tool/transcript composition that scripted backend tests miss.

## Evidence

- Unchanged two-case regression: **2 fail** on pinned main `7db5a3f79d186d617ae96fa48f64ebb2f8d49b91`, **2 pass** with this change. The affected production files also match newer main.
- Real `runEmbeddedAgent`, built-in harness, file write, native registration, private-session replacement, borrowed transcript and persistence. Only provider responses are scripted; no paid provider or production Gateway was used.
- Negative control: restoring harness admission without the manager assertion recovers the answer but persists it after real run admission is closed; the revocation case fails.
- Regression test time: under 2 seconds for both cases; cold wrapper wall time 38.3 seconds including compiler preparation. Broad CI passes: [run 41265778749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265778749).
- Seven affected harness, finalization, parent/child ownership, and prompt-prefix test files: **203 tests pass**.
- Reproduce with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.borrowed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck (`core-test-agents-other`), changed-file lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.
- Codex autoreview: final local candidate against `7db5a3f79d18`, P0–P2, **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. No reviewer configuration was changed.
- Contributor code was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed on this host.

Hosted ClawSweeper review of `d4bacc15eb75`: [no findings or before-merge work](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189984#issuecomment-6552454420).

title: fix(cron): let Doctor recover migrated Codex automations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #189908.

Migrated `heartbeat-main` automations on an explicitly selected Codex runtime remained unbound after repeated `openclaw doctor --fix` runs, then failed the inference-account safety check.

## User Impact

Doctor can record the host-managed OpenAI account that the Codex run would use, together with its runtime, while preserving inherited models and fallbacks. The refusal leads with explicit account adoption and limits its Doctor hint to eligible host-managed accounts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The blanket runtime skip conflated Codex selection with native account ownership. Doctor now passes Codex facts to the existing auth planner for every probe and records a stored account only when the current plan selects one. Native/implicit authentication stays unbound; locked-session, account authorization, revocation, backup, and transaction safeguards remain in place.

Related: #189939. Thanks to @Satoshi-Kusumoto for the diagnosis and recovery-message guidance, reimplemented here with commit-author credit. This working repair supersedes that PR's blanket statement that Doctor never handles explicitly selected Codex runtimes.

## Evidence

- The committed owner regression is red against main `079889d5a09102246b34b363ff340591729d5a80`: repairing twice followed by scheduled auth throws the issue's original `Automation has no recorded inference account ... or with openclaw doctor --fix` refusal. Restoring the fix makes all three runtime-source cases pass (model, provider, session override).
- Focused validation: **40 tests passed** across Doctor account migration, real-runner account continuity/refusal, inference-binding execution, and prompt-prefix stability. Total 195.54s; the Doctor file took 58.45s including its existing full-Doctor tests. The three new owner cases took 3.832s / 2.108s / 2.679s.
- Full process regression: the exact persisted migrated `heartbeat-main` shape, explicit Codex runtime, Doctor CLI twice, separate isolated Gateway, and a completed forced cron run. The real Codex adapter sent the expected synthetic OAuth account before `turn/start`, and assistant history contained the result. **Passed: 72.07s total / 61.962s test time.** Uses the existing synthetic app-server fixture; no live provider or published-stable binary installation is claimed. A complete runtime build passed; test-only fixture iterations reused those identical production artifacts through the supported prebuilt-dist contract.
- Targeted lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, reviewed the final substantive local candidate against `079889d5a091`; scoped-clean, no findings. A subsequent callback-variable rename fixed lint without changing behavior.
- [Exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265245806) for `0aa6dd6cfa52d0c2972b01df9ac4b5491b33c47c`, including production/test type checks, lint, architecture and boundary guards, docs, prompt snapshots, changed tests, and the test-line ratchet. The dedicated allocation funds **282 net regression-test lines**. The task-owned Crabbox allocation queued and was stopped; the local full test-line scan exceeded its 90s bound, so broad proof comes from this completed CI run.

The production delta is +24/-3 lines. The test growth covers repair/runtime selection, native-login non-adoption, and the Doctor-to-Gateway process boundary; no new runtime owner or API was introduced.

<details>
<summary>Additional exploratory evidence</summary>

An extra in-process variant that performed unbound auth before Doctor hit `Auth profile changed before authorization enrollment`. No authorization code was relaxed. The committed regression follows the reported repair-twice-then-run sequence and passes, as does the separate Doctor/Gateway process proof. The deeper cause of that additional warm-process CAS sequence was not established and is outside this fix.
</details>

title: fix(clickclack): discussion rooms fail with PostgreSQL agents
body:
Related: #188643, #175199

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a ClickClack discussion room from Panels → Discussion fails when the Gateway's agent database family uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Discussion rooms can be created and reopened with PostgreSQL-backed agents. SQLite behavior, session resets during channel creation, current-account checks, and binding commit authority are preserved. No configuration, schema, retention, or public SDK change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opening path still performed a synchronous session read at its effect boundaries. PostgreSQL correctly refuses that read on the Gateway thread. This uses the plugin's existing prepared-session authority helper for each effect and final binding commit, releasing each preparation in a finally block. It deliberately reacquires current session authority after HTTP instead of freezing one incarnation for the entire open. Existing FIFO, quarantine/recovery, and binding CAS owners remain unchanged.

This is separate from #188643, which fixed NUL-containing revocation keys when shared state uses PostgreSQL.

## Evidence

**Baseline:** built source `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, isolated PostgreSQL 17.11, synthetic state/token, and a loopback ClickClack HTTP fixture. Actual CLI/Gateway `sessions.create` succeeded; `session.discussion.open` returned `UNAVAILABLE: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker…` before any remote channel POST. The committed real-storage regression also fails on unchanged production source at `service-open.ts:274 → assertEngineStoreExecutionAllowed`.

Initial published head: `25e6c72731ff6134258e171a8cc59c64dc7539ce`. Its Git tree `b51a601c9703edd63bea0891dcf7c493cb8ffd11` exactly matches the reviewed, built implementation commit below; the managed publisher added its commit attribution/receipt without changing source bytes. Both commits have the exact @etzelm coauthor trailer.

**Built product at the reviewed implementation commit:** `f54f44abfa07d4a474aa27639b0109a6bcd72107`. Both official build stamps report that head and clean inputs. The executing runtime was the repository's pinned Bun fork, version 1.4.4. No Gateway handler, session reader, authority owner, or database boundary was mocked.

| Actual built Gateway case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL agents: create → discussion open → independent discussion info | Open; exactly one remote channel; persisted binding matches the PostgreSQL session row |
| PostgreSQL agents: public `sessions.reset` while the channel-create HTTP response is held | Open; lifecycle revision changes, session ID is preserved by the public reset contract, and the persisted binding remains current |
| SQLite parity through the same CLI/Gateway flow | Open; exactly one remote channel; independently read persisted binding matches the current session |

All three product cases passed and completed fixture cleanup. The three Gateway PIDs and PostgreSQL PID file were verified absent afterward. Independent SQL checks compared the binding with `session_nodes.current_session_id`; results were not inferred only from an RPC acknowledgment. The PostgreSQL product cases took 26.0s and 26.8s of test time; SQLite took 24.2s. These are behavior receipts, not performance claims.

**Focused validation:**

- New service regression uses real SQLite/PostgreSQL session and plugin-state owners; only external HTTP transport is replaced. It covers ordinary opening, a changed session ID during HTTP, and archive/removal/credential/destination changes before creation. It is red on the base and green on the repair.
- SQLite service, persistence, CAS/refusal/recovery, shutdown, and new authority tests: **69 passed in 3 files**, 75.21s wall time including preparation.
- Supported PostgreSQL conformance runner: **2 passed in 2 files**, including the new agent-storage regression and existing PostgreSQL shared-state revocation case, 36.98s wall time. The new regression itself took 1.8s. PostgreSQL catalog/trigger preflight passed.
- Conformance-planner tests: **6 passed**. Targeted production and test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and the test-line budget passed. The dedicated **234-line allocation** covers the final 233-line real-storage regression and one line of phase-based reset-fixture growth; the shared ceiling is unchanged. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review**, full six-file candidate against `9c22cf86…`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The author simplification pass retained the existing authority owner and only the lifetime handling needed for these effects.

**CI follow-up:** the first hosted run exposed an ordinal-based reset fixture in `service.test.ts` (`session read 2`), reproduced locally as 38 passed / 1 failed. The new authority preparation intentionally adds a read and refuses a stale selected incarnation. The fixture now triggers its existing initial-read and after-create-read reset scenarios by service phase instead of read count; its binding and presentation assertions are unchanged. All **108 tests in the four affected service files** pass (63.2s command wall time), including both reset cases. Production code is unchanged from the built product proof. Follow-up targeted typecheck/lint/format, the exact 197-line test budget, author simplification, and fresh independent Auto Review of the two-file follow-up passed. No failed assertion or authority guard was relaxed. Fixture-follow-up source tree was `6aaf0b18460ad9e5d47a8eba831c3287703b6ae8` (local reviewed `cb3ccc3bcd08afeb621046ae3fa6882e1141304c`; managed published `ea0008ae395997ed69823495f54190e7d47febc0`). That prior review exposed the authority-recovery issue repaired below; latest-head CI and re-review remain separate gates.

### Authority-recovery finding repaired

ClawSweeper correctly found that an authority refusal was entering transport reconciliation. The follow-up separates preparation/adoption bookkeeping from attempted HTTP, permits ambiguous-outcome recovery only after a dispatched mutation, and re-prepares live authority before every recovery/name-conflict relist. No catch identifies errors by message, and no guard is relaxed.

The real-storage regression now counts channel GETs as well as creates. It was red on the reviewed head (4 GETs observed versus 3 expected), then green on SQLite and PostgreSQL. It proves successful ambiguous-create recovery still relists and adopts, while archive/removal/credential/destination refusal produces no follow-up GET; retirement during a failed POST produces neither relist nor binding. PostgreSQL conformance: 2/2 passed, new regression 1.945s; SQLite strengthened regression 1.759s. The exact grant is now **234 lines** (233-line real-storage regression plus one phase-fixture line), with the shared ceiling unchanged.

At clean local commit `46586bfbd0b227746dbf9545b5433f261278827c`, official built Gateway/PostgreSQL product proof was rerun: allowed open/reset-during-HTTP/info passed; public `sessions.patch {archived:true}` during the held create response refused attachment and an independent persisted-state query found no binding. Sanitized channel traces through the real HTTP client:

```text
allowed/reset: GET /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> POST /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> open/info; binding matches current PG session
archive during POST response: GET /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> POST /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> UNAVAILABLE inactive; binding absent; no follow-up channel request
```

Archive product test: 23.5s, runner exit 0; allowed reset: 26.4s, runner exit 0. An earlier archive attempt passed assertions but had a worker graceful-shutdown error; the verbose diagnostic run above completed cleanly, which does not establish a fix to that harness event. A separate attempted product credential-reload fixture was **not accepted as proof**: waiting for config.patch application while holding the plugin HTTP response caused a reload drain timeout; observing persistence alone was not equivalent to applied authority. Credential/destination retirement is therefore proven by the real-client/real-storage service boundary, not claimed as completed built-Gateway reload proof. No live account or provider was used.

Both final build stamps report local commit `46586bf…` with clean inputs. Managed published head is `a0fd38358dc454a223dc872e17177e6f26ba3719`; local source tree is `ed73f23dce42000afce2233d6accb8b203ae5959`. All owned Gateways and PostgreSQL were stopped.

**Known local failure, not hidden:** `test/scripts/extension-test-plan.test.ts` has three filesystem-inventory failures: owner-boundary balancing, candidate-checkout inventory, and Workboard directory/glob selection. All three reproduce after restoring both changed routing inputs to their base bytes. The ClickClack repair and test do not participate in those discovery cases. No assertions, guards, or baselines were weakened; hosted CI remains separate evidence.

**Limits:** the ClickClack network endpoint is synthetic, not a live external account. No model inference, paid provider calls, live Team data/service operations, actual migration, or deployment was performed. This changes storage/control behavior, not visual rendering.

fix(browser): recover after the Chrome relay owner disconnects
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes browser control staying broken after the authenticated Chrome relay owner websocket drops, until the Gateway restarts.

Supersedes #168189, thanks @jimmarkunas.

## User Impact

The next browser call can reconnect to the configured Chrome relay without restarting the Gateway. Recovery authenticates the same profile and port; it does not select another browser or replay the interrupted action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lazy lifecycle already checks owner liveness, but retiring a dead borrowed client requests a cleanup acknowledgement over its closed socket and retains that rejection. Let the connection owner discard a closed client, then reuse the existing authenticated acquisition path once on the next call. Native cleanup and attachment fencing remain daemon-owned, and live-socket shutdown still waits for acknowledgement. There are no background reconnect loops or new settings.

Production delta: **−2 lines**. Removed redundant retirement-acknowledgement state, since retirement already invalidates the client, and updated the obsolete lifecycle comment. The takeover deliberately leaves attachment scheduling and handshake deadlines outside this repair.

## Evidence

- Regression on main's browser code (`b7d77957a83a`; affected inputs identical at `101a6afdecdc`): **1 failed, 2 passed**. A real authenticated websocket is dropped after browser control enumerates a fixture tab; the next readiness call fails with `Relay owner connection unavailable` while closing the old owner.
- With the fix: **26 passed across 5 focused files**, 37.83 seconds wall time including compiler preparation. The changed owner integration file takes about 112 ms of test time. Recovery successfully enumerates the tab again and makes exactly two authentications to the configured profile and port.
- Negative controls pass: listener proofs for another profile, port, owner, or key are rejected. Existing native-detach acknowledgement, peer-loss cleanup, retirement, and lifecycle tests also pass.
- File-scoped Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The local package-boundary typecheck could not resolve absent generated Plugin SDK declarations; PR CI subsequently passed production and test type checks.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local change against `b7d77957a83a`, with relay server/bridge/native cleanup context: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The test allocation was subsequently reduced to its exact 29-line growth.
- Simplification pass retained one owner and removed duplicate retirement bookkeeping. Test delta: **+29 lines**, allocated in `relay-owner-reconnect.txt` because the prior tests covered graceful retirement but not unacknowledged socket loss. Hosted [CI run 41262881240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262881240) is green on `4d19ac7c7417` (493 seconds wall time; the broader changed-node test job took 337 seconds). Security review also passed.

Proof uses production browser-control, Playwright, authentication, relay, and lifecycle code with a synthetic extension; no live Chrome, agent/model, or production Gateway was exercised. The contributor's code was read with GitHub view/diff only and was never checked out or executed. Human contributor credit is preserved in the commit trailer.

title: fix(config): preserve rollback snapshots when pre-update writes are interrupted
body:
Supersedes #185021. Related: #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an interrupted update snapshot write can destroy the previous `.pre-update` config rollback point and leave partial bytes visible to readers.

## User Impact

User impact: the previous config copy remains intact until its replacement is complete, and a failed snapshot attempt can retry. Malformed older copies remain refused by post-update recovery. This requires the updater taking the snapshot to contain the fix; it does not establish power-loss durability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry kaguranananana's reviewed atomic-publication fix and updated isolation proof from c677d8552b4. The existing snapshot owner now creates a private exclusive temporary file beside the destination and renames it after writing. Failed writes or renames clean up and release the retry marker. No new snapshot format or recovery owner is needed: package rollback uses captured activation preimages, and the post-core reader already refuses malformed explicit snapshots instead of consuming them or falling through to a potentially stale `.bak`.

## Evidence

- Green post-core consumer suite: 8 tests, including a malformed `.pre-update` alongside a valid `.bak`, with no channels restored and no config replacement. File wall time 43.19s including import/transform; test time about 22s. Existing command lifecycle coverage is reused.

Separate processes are necessary to prove selection after importing under another home without touching operator state. All 26 focused tests plus three managed package/profile consumer tests pass; format and `git diff --check` pass.
- [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262460016) passed completely (attempt 1, 1,404 seconds), including selected typechecking, lint, tests, PostgreSQL conformance, and CI/security/dependency gates. The bounded local lint attempt timed out during boundary preparation; a queued Crabbox allocation was stopped before its payload. No broad suite ran on the production host.
- Autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium, P0–P2, complete local candidate against 079889d5a091; `scoped-clean`, no findings. Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed the same head with no code findings; its requested upgrade compatibility proof is now complete below.
- Simplification: one snapshot owner, no new durable state or rollback validator. Source delta +18, tests +56; the separate 56-line test allocation covers the interruption/retry regression, isolation migration, and torn-input recovery case.

Proof: filesystem fault injection and real post-core command composition establish interruption and refusal behavior; the installed-package upgrade establishes existing-state compatibility. The [single-scenario stable-upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262665301) passed on its first attempt: published stable 2026.10.9 to exact candidate d6889e4660ab through the updater, with existing-state survival assertions, Doctor checks, isolated Gateway startup, health/readiness probes, and status checks. title: fix(auth): inline API-key failures break on PostgreSQL agent stores
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway using PostgreSQL agent storage cannot record an authentication failure for a config-backed API key and instead reports “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker.”

## User Impact

User impact: inline API-key failure bookkeeping completes on PostgreSQL without a spurious database-thread error. The caller keeps its normal provider sign-in error, and SQLite keeps its existing behavior. No schema, configuration, public API, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The operation already captures the agent database execution before asynchronous preparation. Pass that execution to the existing worker store instead of acquiring a second, native database handle on the Gateway thread. Write ordering, live-owner checks, transaction/publication handling, and cleanup remain with their existing owners.

The simplification removes nine net production lines (mostly wrapper removal; the larger displayed diff is indentation). The regression reuses the existing Gateway-thread subprocess harness and production retry controller. Its 138 new test/support lines have a separate test-line allocation; the shared budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on base `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693`, the PostgreSQL 17.6 Gateway-role probe exits 1 at `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseRuntime` with the main-thread guard error. The same probe succeeds on SQLite.
- **After:** the PostgreSQL probe succeeds and both caller-visible and persisted failure counters equal 1. Unrelated main-thread PostgreSQL SQL still refuses before and after the operation.
- **Focused conformance:** 15/15 tests pass: the new PostgreSQL/SQLite subprocess regression (2 tests, 3.92 s file duration) plus the existing inline-auth worker suite (13 tests, 10.90 s). The complete focused invocation, including preparation, took 50.62 s. CI timings are not yet available.
- **Static checks:** core typecheck, state/logging test typecheck, lint and formatting on all four TypeScript files, staged whitespace check, and test-line ratchet pass.
- **Independent review:** bound Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, local candidate against the exact base above, P0–P2 coverage: `scoped-clean` with no findings. The reviewer inspected source and supplied results; it did not independently rerun tests.

### Full built-Gateway before/after proof

Ran on 2026-11-01 at 01:28 UTC with real PostgreSQL 17.6 and isolated state. Both source snapshots were built through the supported `sourcePerformance` build profile: baseline `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693` and this exact PR head `1c4c86387d86ed90417d22776034807461026cca`. The PR source tree was verified as `3c41427fbe1ce1c3318095f9dd3f0a7939c9356f`.

Each case launched its own **actual built Gateway process**, connected an authenticated normal test client, then executed `sessions.create → chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history`. A loopback OpenAI-compatible provider fixture received the real configured API-key request and returned HTTP 401 with `authentication_error / invalid_api_key`. Gateway execution, model routing, the retry controller, transcript persistence, and database writes were real—not mocked or called directly by the fixture.

| Built revision | Agent engine | Provider requests | Persisted inline errorCount | Forbidden native-open diagnostic | Public terminal/history |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| baseline `975e68c` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 0 | Present | Normal sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| baseline `975e68c` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |

Every request's Authorization header matched the synthetic config-backed key. The terminal status is intentionally `error` because the provider returns 401; the public error remains “Couldn't sign in to the AI service.” This fix repairs the missing durable bookkeeping and spurious internal database error, **not** the provider's authentication failure. Counters were read from the actual agent store after each Gateway stopped; no expected counter was seeded.

The live WebSocket hello reported the expected build identity in each case:

- Baseline: `2026.10.9-975e68cf820a-2026-11-01T01-07-49.804Z`
- PR: `2026.10.9-1c4c86387d86-2026-11-01T01-09-15.610Z`

The repository E2E runner completed all four arms successfully: one fixture test, **32.36 s** of test time, **80.25 s** file duration / **91.44 s** complete successful invocation including compiled-process preparation. Temporary fixture SHA-256: `f76e215c18c96949a8943597c5b9fd373a9c6abcce31e08e7bb18e4b22859151`; inspected result JSON SHA-256: `6474feafe5a94de5af25491bffe45b555818e2b2dd0b349b1db4d7cb66c6128e`. title: fix(codex): recover unused native threads without dropping history
body:
Supersedes #167873, thanks @davelutztx.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex conversations repeatedly failing with `thread not loaded` after an unused native thread disappears while its managed client and conversation binding remain.

## User Impact

The next turn can create a fresh native thread and continue. Bindings with recorded conversation history remain intact when native state is missing, including after a client restart. Loaded threads without an owned inference route still fail closed. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the inference ownership check onto the existing lifecycle status read, where exact missing-thread errors already reach recovery and its logged warning. Warm reuse without its inference route takes that same cold path before writes. The existing `historyCoveredThrough` marker prevents recovery from replacing a conversation with acknowledged history.

This removes the duplicate preflight `thread/read`: production +18/-22, net **−4 lines**. Regression tests/support grow by 66 lines; a separate 63-line allocation covers the counted test growth. No new state, dependency, or public contract.

- Reproduced on main `edd9cd176a24`: the managed unused-thread regression rejects with the exact `thread/read` error; the recorded-history-after-restart regression incorrectly starts a replacement. Both pass with this repair. Same-client history and loaded-unowned controls remain protected.

Model responses use synthetic loopback HTTP. The managed-route regression uses the real client wire against synthetic app-server responses; no live Gateway or external model call is claimed.

title: fix(voice-call): ignore echoed caller transcripts during playback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes phantom caller turns when realtime transcription returns the assistant's own words during carrier playback.

Supersedes #159145, thanks @mnowrot. Related: #159140.

## User Impact

Unconfirmed playback echo no longer enters caller history or independently starts a host-forced agent consultation. Callers can still interrupt through the existing local speech threshold or provider barge-in.

This filters host caller turns. Realtime providers still receive every inbound audio frame and own their VAD, transcripts and responses; provider-side echo interruptions and transcripts arriving after the tail remain outside this fix. Quiet overlapping speech without a barge-in indication can be ignored during the window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing audio controller admits caller partials/finals only after detected caller speech, a provider interruption, or expiration of carrier playback plus a 400 ms tail. Carrier timing accumulates successfully sent audio even after the local pacing queue drains. An admitted partial remains eligible through its final, and finalization consumes that admission.

The original blanket masking of local barge-in is not retained because it also prevents genuine caller interruption. No config, provider implementation or SDK contract changes. The Deepgram UtteranceEnd fix in #191498 is untouched.

Production delta: +34/-1, net +33 lines for the carrier deadline and turn-admission state in existing owners. The simplify pass found no dead or duplicate owner path that could safely offset this necessary growth. The separate 43-line regression allocation covers the broken behavior and both interruption owners without new test scaffolding.

## Evidence

- Current-main negative control: base `77fadc09500839734b3a148646e54358dfc6df3d`, real handler and carrier WebSocket, quiet injected media followed by STT returning `Hello, how can I help you today?`. Expected no caller turn; main instead emitted that exact `call.speech` transcript. One regression failed for the intended reason.
- After the fix: 53/53 focused handler/pacer/audio-controller tests passed; the expanded handler/lifecycle/call-control run passed 75/75. The final two-case regression covers playback, the 400 ms tail, post-tail caller speech, local/provider barge-in and renewed playback. Runs used [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41546147614), lease `tbx_01m6f9nvc3hc0jsbxfdmh3dpjd`.
- Focused test wrapper wall time: 26.43 s for the first three named files, 21.01 s for the expanded three-file run (17.79 s Vitest duration, including transforms/setup). [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41547848762) succeeded with no failed jobs. The two added regression cases took 22 ms (local barge-in) and 18 ms (provider barge-in) in CI.
- Touched-file lint: all four TypeScript files passed. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local autoreview through the shared helper, Codex, P0–P3: `scoped-clean`, no findings against the logical patch based on `77fadc095008`. Subsequent edits only applied formatter output and adjusted the regression-line allocation to match.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. This is a credited reimplementation. No PSTN/live-provider proof is claimed. Focused tests, their dependency install and artifact builds ran remotely. Native landing used only scripts/pr’s managed, lockfile-keyed dependency cache locally, under the authorized exception; the production Gateway was untouched.

title: fix(plugins): recover reply publication after failed replacement
body:
Closes #189579

## What Problem This Solves

A failed serial plugin replacement can retire model/reply publication and fail to restore it, leaving conversations unavailable until a manual Gateway restart. New inbound messages can also exhaust their recovery attempts while a recovery restart waits for admitted work.

## User Impact

Config writes and explicit `plugins.reload` now request the existing work-draining recovery restart when their actual model/reply rollback fails. The plugin operation still reports failure and `committed:false`. Failed model owners use their existing backoff while restart resources remain live, preserving queued replies’ recovery budget. Cancellation or failed emission resumes ordinary recovery.

Ordinary plugin failures whose reply publication survives keep their existing behavior. Already dead-lettered messages require the documented manual resubmission. This fix is not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin lifecycle owner records actual rollback-publication failure in the existing typed error. The Gateway consumes that fact under current reload ownership and reuses its recovery coordinator, including fresh lifecycle-lease preparation after the failed operation unwinds. The model owner reads existing live restart timers, polls and admission leases. No new queue, schema, configuration, retention policy or mirrored recovery state.

The earlier low-level reply fixture now uses canonical dispatcher settlement, so its retained delivery callbacks release their actual session admissions before subsequent restart tests. No controller reset, drain bypass or timeout increase is used.

## Evidence

- **Original-boundary RED:** baseline `0827b5340d339` on pinned `bf35e054`, [CI 41551456186/job 125640857413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551456186/job/125640857413). Both entry points reach stop/rollback-publication failure with `committed:false`, then fail at the absent restart assertion. The retained-ingress contract independently demonstrates an extra rebuild consuming recovery budget. Setup failures are excluded from causal proof.
- **Exact final-head GREEN:** `e12c43568ecbfa9425013f0113e22e33f90a2eb7`, [CI 41561580871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41561580871), including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and lint/types/docs gates. Applicable security/dependency statuses are consumed again at native merge admission.
- [Real config-write and explicit reload contracts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41561580871/job/125673868725) pass in 685 ms and 753 ms, preserving the failed operation and requiring preparation after its lifecycle lease unwinds. Corrected successful-reload and activation-failure reply siblings pass in 1209 ms and 655 ms.
- [Retained ingress, cancellation and ordinary failure accounting](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41561580871/job/125673868587) pass in 551 ms; [failed scheduled custom-emission lifetime](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41561580871/job/125673868527) passes in 3 ms.
- Fresh **full** independent autoreview against pinned `bf35e054`: both passes complete, no actionable P0–P2 findings; final source verification passed. The exact allocation of 259 test lines covers 160 primary/sibling, 81 ingress and 18 restart-lifetime lines.
- CodeQL’s aggregate annotation is **NEUTRAL**, reporting 17 main-branch configurations not found for this PR; this is retained as a coverage limitation, not represented as a successful scan. Expected skipped lanes remain skipped.
- Tests exercise actual registry/instances, config actor, SQLite lifecycle lease, model publication, restart coordinator and retained queue. Immediate remote capacity for a separate managed/live Gateway proof was unavailable; both task-owned leases were cancelled/settled without payload execution. No live Telegram/provider, operating-system restart or published-release upgrade proof is claimed. No product tests, compiled-worker staging or broad checks ran on the production Team host.

Reported and investigated with @AS76 and @brandonulrich.

title: fix(ios): discard stale wake commands after chat or Gateway changes
body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Buffered Voice Wake recognition can outlive a chat, agent, or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Destination changes discard pending commands and buffered results from the old capture; fresh listening resumes through existing admission gates. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing, which remains separate in #165515.

Gateway session resets and push-to-talk socket invalidation now also tear down and restart Voice Wake recognition, rather than only canceling the pending command. Restart remains subject to the existing listening and admission gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing VoiceWakeManager owns recognition retirement: destination invalidation tears down the old pipeline/generation and cancels its command; internal start/teardown use cancellation-only bookkeeping to avoid recursive invalidation. Phone-focus and selected-agent changes invalidate before assignment independently of Talk's session-key shortcut. Watch-started Talk can already hold the next phone destination or next agent's main key, so that shortcut alone cannot retire the old capture. Current main's focus persistence, selected-agent cleanup, configured-route authority, and restoration ordering are preserved. No new routing owner, generations, configuration, automatic resend, or basic focused-routing callback changes.

## Current validation

title: fix: skip discarded plugin setup captures during startup
body:
Supersedes #154885, thanks @unknowbug.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway startup captures a large installed plugin dependency tree just to run an auto-enable probe whose result is discarded for an already-enabled plugin.

## User Impact

Already-enabled non-channel plugins avoid unnecessary setup capture. Probes still run when channel enablement, a restrictive allowlist, or preference ordering can change selection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generation capture copies and hashes declared dependency packages to retain immutable source and resources. The auto-enable owner now filters satisfied selections before requesting that work, and readiness stays on metadata. Capture containment, symlink, hardlink, receipt, and native-admission checks remain with their existing owners.

The shared filter serves both asynchronous preparation and candidate detection. Removed the redundant xAI-specific collector and repeated configured-entry checks. Production delta: +3 lines; the remaining growth connects the filter to both callers.

## Evidence

- Main `054516fb8e11f06358bab0ab2b90d5313c4ac6fb`: the synthetic real-capture regression fails with **17 dependency files captured, expected 0**.

- **72 tests passed** across the five named auto-enable files on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41537703095). The new regression covers the production setup/auto-enable composition without mocking capture; its 90 lines have an exact test-line allocation.

title: fix: show guest avatars and resolve owner filter names
body:
## What this fixes

Guests can see initials or raw profile UUIDs where OpenClaw already knows a person’s name and photo. This change uses one presentation rule across person surfaces: saved name, verified GitHub login, then a shortened `Person …` label. Editable names remain raw and nullable, and authentication emails stay private.

The authenticated avatar route owns photo selection: upload, existing shared-owner host photo, verified GitHub, then Gravatar. Session readers may fetch the exact ID of any known profile, including `gateway-owner`; this grants no directory enumeration, emails, roles, or private account metadata. Remote URLs come from the verified identity owner, with redirect, size, and time limits. Device authority is revalidated before image disclosure.

The repair removes upload-only projection flags and duplicate caller-side photo policy. It reuses the resident profile, worker-read, and HTTP authority owners. No schema or configuration migration is needed.

## Validation

- Integrated main’s email-privacy changes and repaired stale owner-menu, presence, and resident-profile expectations.

title: fix(deepgram): answer calls when noise prevents endpointing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers hear no response when background noise prevents Deepgram endpointing from completing their confirmed speech.

Supersedes #158226, thanks @Weiming-Hu. Credit also preserves @weiming, the other human commit-author identity in the original PR.

## User Impact

Deepgram can complete confirmed caller speech on its provider-detected word gap while the call remains open. A long pause can split a thought into separate turns. This fallback requires interim results and endpointing at most 5000 ms; other configurations retain their existing behavior. No new settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main only completes open turns on `speech_final` or `from_finalize`; its fallback timer is close-only. Enable `utterance_end_ms` using the existing endpointing value (minimum 1000 ms), flush confirmed text on valid `UtteranceEnd`, and ignore the provider's stale `-1` sentinel. Provisional text is never promoted to a completed transcript.

This deliberately revisits the endpointing-only choice in 73b0312e525126200e1ac83c632166112eed16f7 to address the reported noisy-call stall. Deepgram documents the [word-gap behavior and limits](https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/utterance-end). The original PR's new idle-flush option, watchdogs, and retry machinery are omitted.

Production delta: +9 lines net (+14/-5). Removed the single-use `clearFinalizeFallback` wrapper and kept its cancellation in the turn owner. Test delta: +14 lines; the separate allocation covers the stalled-turn, stale-event, and duplicate-terminal regressions.

## Evidence

- Fake Deepgram stream through the real WebSocket session: red against main `054516fb8e11f06358bab0ab2b90d5313c4ac6fb` (confirmed text plus `UtteranceEnd` produced `[]` instead of `["a"]`); green after the fix, **15/15** tests. Existing close, reconnect, bounds, and provisional-gap cases also pass.
- [Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41537201489): named file `extensions/deepgram/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts`; red wrapper wall 48.52 s, green 39.32 s (Vitest 36.77 s, mostly cold worker compilation). [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538807625) passed on the replacement head in 15m32s wall time across the planned jobs; an individual-file CI timing was not exposed in the retrieved logs.
- Touched-file type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors, exit 0. Touched-file oxfmt check: exit 0. `git diff --check`: pass.
- Autoreview of the complete local candidate against the pinned main above, with full Deepgram owner/test and Voice Call consumer context: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191498#issuecomment-6590379983) also found no actionable findings and recorded the same live-call proof limitation.
- Contributor code was read with `gh` only and was never checked out or executed. No live Deepgram/carrier call was run; this proves the event-stream boundary, not acoustic behavior or an absent provider event. PR CI supplies broad proof; no broad checks ran on the Team host.

Supersedes #149589, thanks @triciah73.
Related: #163315

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ollama memory embeddings fail when the configured local hostname resolves to loopback or a container host-gateway address, while chat to the same host works.

## User Impact

The provider-owned endpoint receives the existing chat private-network policy; separate remote embedding endpoints retain their existing SSRF checks.
