title: fix(sessions): find CJK text inside transcript words
body:
Related: #140736

Supersedes #143127, thanks @holny

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session transcript searches returning no results for interior Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text, such as `会议` in an unspaced sentence.

## User Impact

After a word search misses, CJK terms can find literal substrings with excerpts around the match. Other terms retain native word, punctuation, symbol, and prefix semantics. The retry scans selected transcript text; narrow the session selection for large histories. Queries that already return hits keep their existing behavior, so broader partial recall remains tracked by #140736.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `unicode61` index treats an unspaced CJK run as one token. A native SQLite probe also found zero `trigram` MATCH hits for the reported two-character query. A query-side retry handles short terms while retaining persisted indexes and avoiding a startup rebuild or schema migration.

Both retrieval attempts execute inline in the existing worker kernel and share filters, active-branch exclusion, ordering, limits, and hydration. Substring-only scans filter mapped sessions before reading text. Residual terms use native word parsers: SQLite probes one bounded query row in a private in-memory FTS5 index built by the existing schema owner, and PostgreSQL uses its native simple parser. This preserves meaningful indexed Unicode symbols without restoring handwritten separator ranges.

Production growth is +102 lines, including the native parser probe needed to preserve the recent punctuation contract. There was no safe pre-existing dead/duplicate owner code to offset this; retrieval retains one query. The 36 regression-test lines extend existing fixtures across both engines.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`: all 5 new CJK cases failed with empty hits; all 15 existing cases passed.
- Residual-punctuation regression red on `dfa2276f7ddefbcb4ac4dca3900bf25893c7306b`: `会议 -` returned no hits, with the other 19 owner cases passing.
- SQLite owner proof on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **20/20 passed**, wrapper **66.59s**, Vitest **64.25s**. Includes punctuation-only remainders and an indexed 🦞 positive/negative control.
- Real PostgreSQL product flow on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-test-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/session-search-product.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **4/4 passed**, wrapper **68.93s**, Vitest **66.16s**. Adds CJK punctuation, mixed-word, and missing-word checks. Existing real-worker fixtures and backend setup account for the file wall times.
- These focused commands ran on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox, lease `tbx_01m6f5bxrp176pqjkh0wzcgb5j` ([lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41535859930)); both exited 0 before lease shutdown. Touched-file oxfmt and type-aware oxlint passed with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; `git diff --check` passed.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6f6xv0f6g16cwx241yt89mv` ([workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539705281)): SQLite **20/20 passed**, wrapper **76.96s**, Vitest **74.48s**; touched-file format/type-aware lint passed. The ClawSweeper punctuation finding is addressed by native token probing and the regressions above. title: fix(xai): stop OAuth refreshes from retaining a stale expiry
body:
Supersedes #144082, thanks @jensonhirst.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated xAI OAuth refreshes when a successful token response has no usable access-token lifetime and inherits the previous token’s expiry.

## User Impact

Valid refreshed tokens remain reusable until their new refresh window. A response without a usable lifetime now fails sign-in or refresh and requires signing in again. During proactive refresh this can end the old token’s remaining temporary availability earlier; accepting that recovery avoids publishing a false expiry and repeatedly spending rotating refresh grants.

## Why This Change Was Made

Require the shared login/refresh parser to derive an expiry from `expires_in` or the access token’s JWT `exp`, then publish it unconditionally. Keep the existing identity, endpoint, retry, and refresh-settlement policies. xAI already uses the shared safe duration converter; the shared OAuth runtime does not supply a replacement HTTP refresh client.

The five added production lines enforce the missing-lifetime check; both optional-expiry publication branches disappear. The 44-line test allocation covers rejection at login/refresh and fake-clock reuse through the existing usability contract.

## Evidence

- Red on main `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`: the five new lifetime rejection cases fail because invalid responses are accepted (43 controls pass).
- Green on this branch: 52 tests pass across `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts`, `xai-oauth-refresh-bytes.test.ts`, and `xai-oauth-entry.test.ts` (16.34 s Vitest / 19.85 s wrapper). Fake clocks cover one refresh, reuse, the five-minute proactive refresh boundary, and actual expiry, with both duration and JWT lifetimes.
- Focused tests run on Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox, lease `tbx_01m6f1bkkdv4scs68ezhrbs2ab`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41525298288). No contributor code was checked out or run.
- Touched-file lint passes for both changed TypeScript files; formatter check passes for those same files. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P3, no actionable findings. The helper refused the public `credential-state.ts` filename as context; its exact margin semantics were inspected separately in source and exercised by the focused tests. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; [hosted ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191464#issuecomment-6588770585) with no findings or pre-merge blockers. Its reviewed-head end-to-end proof limitation is stated below.
- Source audit: the OAuth manager validates refreshed credentials with zero margin before SQLite settlement, while ordinary reuse uses five minutes. A still-future inherited expiry therefore previously persisted and immediately refreshed again. No credential schema or storage owner changes.
- No live xAI account or full Gateway run was used; HTTP responses are synthetic fixtures. This proves the plugin lifetime boundary and shared eligibility contract, not live-provider response frequency.

title: fix(discord): keep browser private-network access out of CDN downloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord attachment and sticker downloads accepting private or link-local CDN destinations when the Gateway enables private-network browser access.

Supersedes #144259, thanks @SebTardif.

## User Impact

Discord CDN downloads ignore browser `allowPrivateNetwork` and `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`. Existing installations relying on these broad flags for private-address CDN answers must use an explicit trusted hostname in `browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames`. Normal public CDN hosts, RFC2544 proxies, and explicitly enabled IPv6 fake-IP proxies remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select supported fields in the existing Discord policy owner instead of spreading arbitrary browser permissions. Keep hostname and origin exceptions, configured denials, and the narrow IPv6 proxy option. The fixed Discord RFC2544 default makes its old Boolean merge redundant; production code decreases by 6 lines. Slack and Telegram build independent media policies and do not share this browser-policy merge.

## Evidence

- Crabbox/Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41522872804. Corrected regression fails for both browser flags with main policy blob `39430d5ac880d95492d9456c85c63c332b599bea` from `d316aecc43b9820300ba49b55ab2106abfd32eb6`; that policy blob was also verified unchanged on current main.

The regression runs real `resolveMediaList` → `saveRemoteMedia` → DNS/SSRF checks and media storage, with synthetic DNS and HTTP response fixtures. Public attachments and stickers save exact response bytes; RFC1918, loopback, IPv4 metadata and IPv6 link-local answers reach no HTTP fetch. RFC2544 and opt-in IPv6 ULA downloads succeed.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) found one test-harness issue: directly passing a Vitest fetch spy selected the guard's DNS-free mock branch. A plain async wrapper now exercises real DNS policy checks; red/green was repeated with that correction. Final autoreview of the full local delta against `d316aecc43b9820300ba49b55ab2106abfd32eb6` is scoped-clean through P2, with no remaining actionable findings.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Oxfmt passes for all four touched source/test/docs files; `git diff --check` passes. All compilation and Bun staging required by these wrappers ran remotely.
- The 72-line test allocation covers the new destination-authority regression, including both media types, both broad flags, private/link-local DNS and preserved narrow proxy behavior. No shared test ceiling change.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff` only; it was never checked out or run. No live Discord account, HTTPS CDN network or Gateway/model E2E was exercised. Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41530199811) completed successfully in 765 seconds of workflow wall time, including queue time; all required checks passed before merge. The first CI run identified missing required attachment fields and an overloaded DNS mock type; both fixtures were corrected without casts, and the corrected named file passes all 4 tests (78.51 seconds Vitest wall time), touched-file lint/format, and a fresh P0–P2 autoreview of the correction against `fe11e0bc405a7938ab868a1be433421d577f00ae`.

Restoring the replacement policy passed (53.42 seconds Vitest wall time):


Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41527822982. The redirect began at an allowed CDN address and targeted another allowed CDN hostname resolving privately. title: fix(doctor): explain workspace imports blocked by earlier refusals

Use the workspace receipt's existing `originatingRefusal` at the warning owner. Canonical read-only diagnosis still runs, legacy files stay untouched, and later runs still inspect current workspace state. No receipt, schema, persistence, migration order, exit status, or updater protocol changes.

The simplification pass retained 11 added production lines to carry the existing context through the existing adapter and choose the correct advice; there was no dead or duplicate owner code to remove safely. title: fix(codex): inherited workspace edits stay stale across turns
body:
Supersedes #161722, thanks @Oldrich333.
Related: #161707

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long-lived Codex sessions keep stale inherited workspace AGENTS.md instructions after the file is edited.

## User Impact

Nonempty edits reach the next turn, including native thread resume, without resetting the conversation. This intentionally replaces the documented frozen inherited-snapshot behavior. Empty or missing files and failed workspace preparation retain the last snapshot delivered to the bound thread; transient threads do not replace that fallback.

Prefer the workspace instructions already prepared for the current turn and update the saved fallback after the existing acknowledged policy handoff. The guarded workspace reader already caches unchanged local content by file identity, size, mtime, and ctime, so this adds no cache or filesystem reads. title: fix(macos): prevent first-launch Gateway failures after upgrades
body:
Related: #188683 — this is a separate updater repair; no endpoint changes are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app can fail its first launch after an upgrade by starting an old Gateway after credential preparation has migrated state beyond that Gateway's supported schema.

## User Impact

App-managed profiles can complete the upgraded first launch without Retry, relaunch, manual Doctor, or data reset. Explicit pins, installation ownership, service custody, and schema/integrity refusals remain intact. No new schema, configuration option, dependency, or committed version bump.

The native `doctor --client-credentials` operation now also completes pending local runtime-intent migration; it still does not start/stop services or force a runtime choice. Generic Gateway/node credential callers retain their existing ready fast path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Credential readiness and daemon runtime-pin readiness are independent. The narrow credential Doctor skipped the pin handoff, leaving `migrationPending` after schema advancement. Swift correctly preserves the old seed while that handoff is pending.

The native CLI now waits for the existing daemon migration owner after credential maintenance releases custody, retaining the captured engine selection. This also runs when credentials are already ready after a partial attempt. The existing owner preserves pin bytes/timestamps and refuses conflicts while retaining both stores. Swift activation, seeding policy, and pin formats are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Regression:** two actual credential-cutover cases fail before the repair because intent stays pending, then pass with it. They cover no legacy pin and preservation of a stored pin. An additional already-ready credential/pin-conflict case verifies refusal. These fixtures migrate schema 24 → 39; the real-app proof below starts at 20.
- **Focused tests on refreshed base:** 83 pass: credential suite 23/23, daemon migration suites 17/17 and 5/5, CLI registration 38/38. Wrapper wall time 103.98s; CI seconds unavailable. Seven PostgreSQL-only cases were skipped in the prior-base run, not certified here. New regression cases add about 2.7s test time and a justified 117-line allocation.
- **Static checks on refreshed base:** targeted command/test typecheck, lint, format, whitespace, documentation MDX and test-line budget pass. Broader original docs checks remain prior-base evidence; glossary coverage was skipped for lack of a local merge base.
- **Review:** fresh Auto Review through P2 found no actionable defects against refreshed base `f6efce5707dcdf140bb277b2d3fc7115b912600f`, including integration with its updated async pin-migration owners. The unchanged Swift credential wrapper was supplied context and inspected separately. Review is not native execution.
- **Real first launch:** the requester supplied an isolated macOS release-to-candidate run. This Linux session verified its 39 checksum records, exact patch/manifest identity, process lineage, continuous exec coverage, readiness, and retained-profile facts. Native execution was supplied, not performed by this session.

### Local macOS proof after conflict repair (2026-11-02)

- Head `db14fbef10e5ee80e0bd098fe6e44f65dee2216e` merges main `f68e832179c1`; the sole conflict was `docs/install/updating.md`, resolved by retaining both independent additions. The PR's feature delta is unchanged; no new runtime behavior or tests were added.
- Regression control: with only `startup-client-credentials.ts` restored to main's implementation, all three new cases fail for the intended reasons: both cutovers leave `migrationPending`, and already-ready credentials fail to reject conflicting runtime intent. Restoring the fix makes all three pass.
- Local macOS arm64 focused proof: **83/83 pass** across `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` (23), `register.maintenance.test.ts` (38), `runtime-pin-migration.test.ts` (5), and `state-migrations.daemon-runtime-pins.test.ts` (17). Run via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <these four files> --maxWorkers=1`; wrapper wall time **107.23s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Targeted command/test typecheck, four-file type-aware lint, seven-file formatting, three-page MDX validation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Limits: production-owner integration and CLI registration proof, not a new packaged native-app/Sparkle upgrade run or live PostgreSQL qualification. Prior native proof below remains tied to its original candidate. This mechanical conflict repair does not claim a new independent code review or current-head CI completion.

### Native result — original proof candidate

The base was refreshed only to resolve a documentation conflict. Repair production/test bytes and feature-added/removed lines are unchanged. The macOS run remains evidence for its explicitly pinned pre-refresh candidate, not native execution of the refreshed head.

State migrates **20 → 39** and the source-bound pin receipt completes **before runtime selection**. App PID 12143 starts Gateway PID 12229 with matching candidate Bun, CLI, and SQLite-library identities. Authenticated readiness succeeds and the same approved node reconnects. Config/endpoint, auth/keypair fingerprints, and main pairing identity/grants persist; shared state, client credentials, and daemon control stores all report integrity OK.

**Limits:** one arm64 ad-hoc local replacement with guest-only version 2026.10.10, not signed Sparkle delivery or a full native matrix. The exec trace is continuous through readiness/node connection, with three later gaps during RPC verification. Node-surface metadata refreshes/reapproves automatically, so pairing bytes are not wholly unchanged. Bonjour dependency and transient CPU-degradation warnings remain disclosed; readiness succeeds. No provider turn, live explicit-pin matrix, or pause/quit matrix is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable trace, source binding, and fixture</summary>

Source: base `325d62a031f15f4a271e5f47ae9ad13a79fb7c1b` plus the eight-file patch SHA-256 `f6e03907214f9d94ed4561bbf3bff8ed61b2aa95d9ff4b72aea08ea91fcc69a1`. The official v2026.10.9 release is `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, archive SHA-256 `b13bef633fc60a30bcc903aceaba71ad2a4185fdd6fdb6e0c278d770454577a1`, with verified release signature. ```text

Exactly one app exec and one Gateway-start exec appear. Every Bun/Node exec in the index has corresponding detail. The one old-runtime exec invokes its CLI with `--version`, not `gateway run`. Candidate Bun/CLI/SQLite hashes match the package; live mappings independently identify candidate Bun and SQLite. title: fix: environment-selected dev profiles target the wrong Gateway port
body:
Supersedes #165372, thanks @itachi47.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: CLI/TUI clients and the macOS app select port 38556 instead of the dev Gateway's port 19001 when started with `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=dev` and no explicit port.

## User Impact

Environment-selected dev profiles connect to the same default endpoint as `--dev` and `--profile dev`. Explicit environment/config ports and macOS stored port overrides retain their existing precedence.

An existing dev service explicitly pinned to 38556 keeps that port. Its clients must keep a matching explicit port (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=38556`), or the service must be reinstalled on 19001. This repair accepts that manual recovery for old pinned services; service definitions are not rewritten automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lightweight profile utility now owns named-profile port defaults, including the reserved dev port. CLI bootstrap and config resolution share it without importing config-path initialization into early bootstrap. The Swift default mirrors it.

The simplification pass removed the config resolver's inline profile hash, the CLI's duplicate hard-coded dev port, and a redundant environment trim. Production grows by 12 lines for the shared function/imports and Swift dev case; regression tests grow by 9 lines. A dedicated allocation of four test lines covers the four new TypeScript table cases; Swift cases reuse the existing precedence test.

## Evidence

- Current-main baseline: `c83eef98ef50bb727014881f8723b8a4d0f26233`; the broken owners were also rechecked unchanged on main `7a96bac8ed5ec3d7f03bdfcc8fb0034fa8b1ac28`. In Crabbox, `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed exactly the two dev-default cases: `expected 38556 to be 19001`; the other 44 cases passed. File duration: 77.71s, dominated by worker compilation.
- With this fix, `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts src/cli/profile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 70 cases. Config file: 37.98s (97% transform); CLI profile file: 0.673s; total test runner time: 41.88s. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41512798878), lease `tbx_01m6ewp8vex916t6mcfk75gzy5`.
- Touched TypeScript format and type-aware lint checks passed (zero warnings/errors). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41514476305) passed in 1,104s, including all selected Node and UI test shards, lint, and types. [macOS Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41514476336/job/125514818651) passed: app and tests compiled with `--build-tests` (685s build step; 1,062s job). Standard PR CI deliberately skips Swift test execution; Swift runtime test execution remains a gap.

title: fix(agents): reject FIFO native-hook credentials without blocking
body:
Supersedes #172271, thanks @Leon-SK668.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native hook relay hangs when its credential path is a writerless FIFO, even with `--timeout 1000`.

## User Impact

Invalid special-file credentials promptly return the existing deny response. Regular credentials retain the 16 KiB limit and verified HTTPS transport. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `readRegularFile` from `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`, which supplies nonblocking/no-follow opening, regular-file and descriptor checks, bounded reads and cleanup. This removes the duplicate credential-read implementation: production **+8/-19, net -11**. The sibling #191347 already uses this package's regular-file guard; its recovery reader retains its distinct synchronous, ENOENT-only absence contract. No second helper is introduced.

## Evidence

- **RED on main `c83eef98`**: real `mkfifo`, no writer, actual relay CLI with a one-second timeout; bounded child hits `ETIMEDOUT` after ten seconds. HTTPS control passes. Main's credential-reader blob was rechecked unchanged after main advanced.
- **GREEN on Testbox**: same CLI regression returns the existing deny response in **794 ms** and preserves the FIFO. Both remote-client files plus the CLI and CLI import-boundary files pass: **24 tests, four named files**, wrapper **52.09 s** including uncached preparation; remote-client group **2.16 s**. Valid TLS/capability delivery, redirect/response bounds, oversized credentials, cancellation and socket-close settlement remain covered. [Testbox provision run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41512859439).
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41514008339) **passed**, 31 successful jobs on exact head `4d3b9811`; elapsed **17m39s**. Merged as `2dd3ffec0063c60ef3815637a2e85c6757a42fd5`.
- Touched-file typed lint: zero warnings/errors; oxfmt/Bun format parity and `git diff --check` pass. Source validation and worker compilation ran on Testbox. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Local **Codex autoreview, P0–P2, scoped-clean**, complete final local candidate against `c83eef98`, including the allocation record; no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the maintainer review route uses autoreview and the hosted ClawSweeper review already queued for this head; no duplicate request was sent. `pr-simplify` keeps one read owner and removes the duplicate low-level read/cleanup sequence.
- Exactly **47 net test lines** are allocated for the bounded real-CLI FIFO regression and retained byte-limit proof; shared scalar unchanged.

Contributor source was read through `gh` only, never checked out or executed. Proof uses synthetic credentials and the real source CLI; native macOS/Windows and an actual model turn were not run. The FIFO regression skips Windows.

title: fix(cli): reject reserved keys in provider and MCP assignments
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`__proto__` assignments silently disappear when saving provider environment or MCP environment/header settings.

Supersedes #172325, thanks @wangmiao0668000666.

## User Impact

title: fix(k8s): restore temporary workspaces on non-sticky volumes
body:
Related: #156985

Supersedes #157046, thanks @myagizmaktav.
Supersedes #164067, thanks @cellrishi-code.

## What Problem This Solves

Kubernetes deployments can reject session-observer temporary workspaces because the mounted `/tmp` volume is writable without sticky protection.

## User Impact

Applying the updated manifest supplies a safe `/tmp` for temporary workspaces while retaining the non-root Gateway and filesystem safety checks. Custom temp volumes must be writable by the init container; arbitrary-UID platforms must adapt the init and Gateway identities together.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fsGroup` adds group permissions and setgid, not the sticky bit. Reuse the existing UID-1000 init container to create and chmod its own child directory, then mount that child at `/tmp` with `subPath`. Preparation errors stop initialization with a diagnostic. This incorporates both proposals without adding another init container or image.

Main's private-state temp fallback (#187737) still rejects a group-writable, non-sticky state-volume ancestor, so it does not replace a safe temp mount. No filesystem checks are relaxed.

## Evidence

- On Blacksmith Testbox (`tbx_01m6ehr69awk6s4bnch9azx2k8`, [allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41482686669)), ran `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` against trusted main plus the new regression: **1 failed, 6 passed**, with `insecure-permissions` naming the mode-2777 ancestor and missing sticky bit. With the manifest repair, the same files passed: **7 tests**, 1.32 s Vitest duration / 2.82 s runner wall time. The manifest file took 35 ms, including 26 ms for the regression.
- The regression executes the manifest's init shell against fixture paths, models the `subPath` boundary, and uses real fs-safe workspace creation, writing, reading, and cleanup. No Kubernetes cluster or model/provider call was run. Neither contributor's branch was checked out or executed.
- Independent local Codex autoreview of the complete change against `21e7ad20d3e5f56ddaefdb44b59a2716d5ea05da`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings; subsequent edits narrow a YAML value for lint and apply mechanical formatting. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; one [hosted review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191294#issuecomment-6582837591) under the maintainer workflow. It completed on the final head with no findings.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint passed with zero diagnostics. Oxfmt passed all three touched source/doc files; markdownlint passed with zero issues (the repository config also includes the docs collection). `git diff --check` passed. After the YAML type narrowing, both named suites passed again: 7 tests, 1.50 s Vitest / 3.47 s runner wall, manifest file 25 ms and regression 19 ms. All Node dependencies, SDK declaration preparation, and Bun staging ran remotely. PR CI supplies broad checks.

The simplification pass retained one existing init owner and one filesystem regression. Runtime TypeScript: +0/-0; manifest: +6/-0; tests: +65/-2 (net +63); docs: +6/-0; test-budget allocation: +2/-0. The six manifest lines are necessary preparation and mount wiring; no dead or duplicate main-branch code in this area can be removed to offset them. The separate 63-line test allocation covers this regression without changing the shared baseline.

Fixes Ollama setup failing to reuse an existing protected connection when its saved endpoint, credential or custom request settings are needed.

## User Impact

Users can prepare the existing Ollama connection without replacing its saved credential references or changing their current default model. Choosing a different endpoint does not send the previous connection's key or headers to it.

Saved URL reuse and credential identity are one boundary: using the right URL with the wrong auth owner is still a broken or unsafe connection. Setup now resolves only the selected connection's private HTTP inputs and carries the existing guarded transport through discovery, inspection, optional pulls and cloud-status checks. Saved configuration keeps its authored references.

Transport precedence, network/TLS/proxy policy and secret materialization still use existing public SDK owners. title: fix(cli): recover Windows Control UI publication from temporary file locks
body:
Supersedes #156445, thanks @YangManBOBO.

Related: #156443

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent Windows plugin Control UI build failures when antivirus or an indexer temporarily denies publishing a staged generation.

## User Impact

Windows plugin builds recover from temporary rename denials. Existing immutable generations still require matching bytes; permanent failures retain the original filesystem error and staging is cleaned up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main treats `EPERM` as an existing-generation collision even when the destination does not exist. Keep publication in its current owner and use the existing async retry scheduler for six attempts, waiting 100/200/400/800/1600 ms. Retry only `EPERM`, `EBUSY`, or `EACCES` on Windows while the destination is absent; true collisions incur no retry delay.

The existing UI-script rename helper is synchronous and the package-update helper is bound to update authority and path-identity checks, so neither fits this async build publisher. No new rename helper or structural refactor is introduced. Production growth is +16 lines; there is no dead or duplicate code in this owner to safely offset it.

## Evidence

[Red-before CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41474967757/job/125379112130) at `450d0059fa06d`: the unchanged main publisher fails 7 cases, with 25 passing, in `src/cli/plugins-control-ui-build.test.ts` (12.91 seconds). Transient `EPERM` reaches a nonexistent-destination read; the other Windows denials are never retried. The same tests cover exhausted retries, other errors/platforms, cleanup, and collision validation.

[Green-after CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41476601885/job/125385273400) at `1c290f39a2261`: the byte-identical test file passes all 32 cases in 8.71 seconds. Plugin UI reproducibility and scaffold compilation also pass. [The full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41476601885), including lint, type checks, UI checks, and baseline ratchets, passed on this exact head.

Autoreview completed on the full change and supporting source at P0–P2 with no actionable findings. The simplification pass retained the existing owner and validation path. The exact +43 regression-test lines are allocated separately to protect the distinct Windows recovery/error and immutable-collision contracts; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

Two Testbox attempts stopped during setup before tests ran, so PR CI supplies red/green and broad proof. No tests, broad checks, containers, or builds ran on the production Team host. Native tooling used only its managed dependency cache. Windows behavior is covered with injected platform and filesystem errors; a real Windows antivirus hold was not run. The contributor's code was read through `gh` and was never checked out or executed.

Contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: YangManBOBO <pan.xiaobo@xydigit.com>`.

title: fix(worktrees): keep pack maintenance converging beside fetch
body:
## Problem

Part of the **worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02**. On the team Gateway, the Control UI "Updating repository…" phase (`preparing_worktree_base`, default-branch base refresh in `src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts`) took p50 5.2 s, p90 48 s, p99 261 s and max 302 s over 176 starts. GitHub `ls-remote` takes about 0.95 s. Meanwhile the shared `blob:none` project clone has built up 1,216 packs (1,211 promisor, about 430 GB), no multi-pack-index, and stale temporary pack files.

Live evidence from read-only log and pack-directory inspection (no writes to the live clone):

- **Fetches wait behind maintenance.** The slowest `git/ref-mutation` holds on 2026-11-02 were 807 s (10:57), 429 s (05:34), 298 s (03:32), 168 s (04:30) and 124 s (09:46). Each one ended next to a managed-worktree cleanup pass. A fetch queued behind the 10:57 hold waited `queueWaitMs=229670`. That matches the slowest sample's `baseRefresh=234126`, which happened even though the fetch itself has a 60 s timeout.
- **One lost lease stops pack maintenance until restart.** `worktree Git maintenance suspended (packs) … OpenClawStateLeaseError: project checkout lease … was lost (lease loss: expired; expiredByMs=1 …)` was logged at 2026-11-01 08:14, 2026-11-01 12:59 and 2026-11-02 05:34. Each time, pack consolidation and temporary-pack cleanup stopped for that repository until the Gateway restarted.
- **Some temporary files are never reclaimed.** The pack directory still holds 14 `tmp_idx_*` and 6 `tmp_rev_*` files, some from September (~172 MB of indexes). These are left by interrupted `index-pack` runs. Cleanup only matches `tmp_pack_*`, and `gc.auto=0`, so Git's own prune never runs. The ~1.9 GB of recent ~375 MB `tmp_pack_*` files are interrupted consolidation outputs. The existing 24 h cleanup reclaims those, but only while pack maintenance is not suspended.

## Root cause

All on `main` @ `63c25f72`, in `src/agents/worktrees/git-maintenance.ts`:

1. **L219–236:** `maintainWorktreePacks` runs the whole pack pass inside `enqueueGitRefMutation`: temp cleanup, `verify-pack` of up to 128 MiB of indexes, and the `pack-objects --stdin-packs | index-pack` rewrite, with up to 30 min budgets since #189606. Every `fetch` and `update-ref` on the shared clone, including base-ref refresh, waits for the whole pass. The queue was originally needed for repository-wide MIDX writes and expiry, which #182204 removed. Today the rewrite copies every object of the selected packs regardless of refs, so only retiring the inputs touches files a fetch may be reading.
2. **L560 → L570:** the catch exempts only `ProjectCheckoutBusyError`. A lease lost mid-pass (heartbeat expiry, an `OpenClawStateLeaseError`) reaches `failed.set(repoRoot, state.stage)`. Pack maintenance is then marked failed for the process lifetime, as if the repository were corrupt.
3. **L246:** `/^tmp_pack_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/` never matches `tmp_idx_*` or `tmp_rev_*`.

## Solution

- Only retiring the replaced inputs joins the ref-mutation queue. Verification and rewriting run alongside fetch. The content-slot → ref-queue order is unchanged, and retirement still never overlaps an OpenClaw fetch (on Windows, an open pack cannot be unlinked).
- Any `OpenClawStateLeaseError` (busy or lost checkout ownership) now records a deferred pass instead of suspending. `withOpenClawStateLease` rethrows the loss as that error even when the loss killed the running Git child. A lost pass keeps its hourly slot, so it retries on the next hourly pass. Busy projects keep their existing behavior. Real Git failures still suspend as before.
- Temporary-file cleanup matches every `tmp_<kind>_` file, as Git's prune does. The existing Linux file-lease helper, 24 h age rule and identity checks are unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md` updated for queue scope, lease-loss deferral and temporary-file kinds.

No new config, state or dependencies. Production delta: +46/−37 in one file.

## Impact

- Base-ref refresh no longer waits for pack verification or rewriting. On the live samples, waits drop from minutes to the milliseconds `fs.rm` retirement takes.
- A stalled lease heartbeat costs one batch instead of all pack maintenance until restart.
- Old `tmp_idx_` and `tmp_rev_` files are reclaimed.

### Convergence rate (synthetic repo)

This was a scratch measurement and is not committed. It used the real `createWorktreeGitMaintenance` on a synthetic repo with 40 distinct full-history packs, each one all history up to a different commit, like the live duplicates. Pack metadata was stubbed to the live shape (240 MB pack, 20 MB index). One maintenance pass ran per simulated hour:

| pass | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 40→35 | 35→30 | 30→25 | 25→20 | 20→15 | 15→10 | 10→5 | 5→1 | 1→1 |
| this PR, lease lost during pass-2 verification | 40→35 | deferred | 35→30 | 30→25 | 25→20 | 20→15 | 15→10 | 10→5 | 5→1 |
| `main`, same lease loss | 40→35 | suspended | suspended | … | … | … | … | … | suspended (all 15 passes, stuck at 35) |

The rate is −5 packs per pass (a 6-pack batch under the 128 MiB index budget becomes 1 pack). For the live clone's ~1,206 full-history packs, that projects to roughly 240 uninterrupted hourly passes (~10 days), before counting new packs arriving.

## Evidence

- **Red on `main`** (the three tests below with the base `git-maintenance.ts`): all three fail for the defect.
  - lease loss: `outcome: "failed"` with `project checkout lease … was lost (lease loss: expired …)`.
  - ref queue: a ref mutation issued during the rewrite times out after 5 s, and the pass ends `stage: "suspended"`.
  - temp cleanup: `tmp_idx_abandoned` survives.
- **Green:**
  - `pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.gc-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21/21.
  - Same file plus consumers `service.gc-lifecycle.test.ts` and `service.removal-budget.test.ts`: 59/59.
  - New tests take 80–224 ms each. File wall time is 191–282 s on this IO-starved host (transform 59–72%). CI seconds pending.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint on touched files, `run-format`, `format:docs:check` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` (under the ceiling, no allocation needed) all pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, branch mode, P2, with the cleanup helper, project-checkout, lease-error and git-exec sources as context): scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.87)".

## Accepted edge cases

- If a real Git failure and a lease loss happen in the same pass, the pass is deferred rather than suspended. The next hourly pass sees the Git failure again and suspends.
- An interrupted consolidation still leaves its ~375 MB `tmp_pack_*` output until the 24 h cleanup reclaims it.
- One batch per pass (hourly) is unchanged. Longer passes would hold the project checkout lease that session creation waits 30 s for, and add IO on an already IO-starved host.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Pack producer.** The live duplicates are full-history commit and tree packs (~720k–980k objects each). In a `blob:none` clone, a lazy promisor fetch of a missing commit uses no-haves negotiation, so it downloads all history again. A synthetic repro turned a 600-object base pack into a new 610-object pack after one `git cat-file -e <new commit>`. Fixing whichever callers trigger lazy commit fetches matters more for long-term convergence than consolidation throughput.
- **Lease heartbeat.** It is still unexplained why the heartbeat misses its 30 s window (`heartbeatAgeMs=30001`) under host IO pressure.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:2c02ef0f-93ed-4073-8394-ee46433fcdb6 -->

## Concurrent registration validation

Independent validation with the benchmark added in #192275 used 1,501 packs, 700,000 shared objects, 62,000 tracked files (~1.14 GB), and six concurrent deferred managed-worktree registrations while real verification was delayed five seconds. Five interleaved A/B pairs plus two A/A controls and a separate allocation pair passed without retries or discarded arms.

Registration median/p95 fell from **17,847.6/19,408.4 ms to 189.2/313.8 ms**; every candidate registration completed during the verification pause. Owner CPU median was **4.848→4.451 s**, process-tree CPU **26.63→24.93 s**, peak-process RSS **730,016→734,288 KiB**, and sampled allocation **99,247,320→99,641,072 B**. A/A owner CPU varied +3.17% and wall time +0.27%. Each arm consolidated 1,501→476 packs and passed retained-object, branch/tree, and full fsck checks. APFS/macOS synthetic owner proof; deployed Linux/btrfs behavior remains unmeasured.

Fresh complete-range Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Focused maintenance/lifecycle/removal suites: **58 passed, one platform skip**, 147.27 s wrapper wall time. #192275 separately bounds any remaining registration queue wait to 30 seconds with a notice and retryable error; resource-limited maintenance placement remains unchanged.

title: fix: hide operator Home from guests and start new sessions by default
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted guests could see the rolling operator Home conversation even when its composer denied participation. Implicit startup also opened Home instead of New Session.

## User Impact

Operator Home rows and transcript reads are withheld from session-only restricted guests. General-read and full-session operators retain explicit Home access. Implicit startup uses New Session while valid explicit links, unsent drafts and non-Home/native restoration remain supported. No new configuration option or permission grant is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session-sharing policy owns Home admission. Discovery, exact readers, HTTP/media, mentions and remote-ingress adapters forward current main-key/scope facts; sharing-cache identity includes the main key. Full-read mention requesters and connect-less internal callers remain supported without exempting restricted session-only grants.

The UI checks Home authority before cached transcript hydration, including literal aliases. Bootstrap owns native restoration before routing. Not-found recovery preserves non-Home conversations while excluding cached Home using canonical identity bound to the navigation-selected owner, including ownerless global keys.

The latest update completes individually audited conversation-fixture entry/navigation cutover through the existing URL helper while preserving intentional New/default, query/hash/history and denial controls. CSP interception and navigation use the same exact session URL. API, service-worker and phone setup repairs preserve their security/recovery assertions.

Denied Home and New Session reuse the existing Welcome status renderer and app-owned handle, preserving pending/failure/retry presentation without a second owner, polling, redirects, permission or locale changes. This minimal integration changes three production files, +14 net LF. Identical menu-locator reuse removes the affected fixture's max-lines violation without an exception.

## Evidence

Latest published head: `88d20b5fb91ba0840495ddda6a1e7104199a73b6`. The direct-5f49 update is 215 paths, 264,481 bytes, SHA-256 `7179c96bdcc202399b2d2794e9b031aa77360700d2a530450ef942479b04dd50`. - Original route-owner regression: **21 passed /42.91s Vitest**. Earlier scoped UI proof: **525 tests /20 files**; final cached-Home recovery: **83 tests /4 files, 3.70s**. Earlier failing regressions remain retained.
- Maintained source-browser proof (mock Gateway, not a production bundle): six conversation/default/global-owner/recovery cases passed in **24.26s Vitest**; URL-helper red/green and old-versus-corrected CSP interception were exercised (**5.95s**).
- Public Welcome fixture using the maintained source-server hook: **8/8 passed, 26.19s Vitest /34.20s wall**, retaining original three-pending, failure/retry, ready/deep-link and New unsent-draft/no-send/no-Home-RPC controls. Original pending failure is retained. Affected sidebar menu: **1 passed /8.80s wall**, ten unrelated cases not selected.
- Integration lint **21.39s**, UI types **1.67s**, E2E types **2.92s** passed. Baseline 1001-line violation was reproduced and repaired at 999 through identical locator reuse; scoped lint **6.14s** passed without suppression.
- Actual isolated source Gateway with normal plugin loading, synthetic Visitor grant and signed-device HTTP/WS: **65 passing assertions, two failing overbroad oracles, exit1 /69.07s**. Home readers/subscription, media/icons, events and mentions passed with ordinary/full-read/full-operator controls. [Original ten privacy/default-entry screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191140#issuecomment-6582235930) cover desktop/mobile disclosure before, New/default entry and denied Home after, plus explicit full-read controls. title: fix(ui): stabilize Details docking checks under load
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent WebKit CI failures when the Details browser test switches a docked inspector to a popover under CPU load.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. The existing browser test waits for the native popover transition to complete before checking its open state, role, and geometry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resizing reaches the popover through ResizeObserver and Solid's scheduled updates. The test previously sampled native state against the default poll deadline. It now subscribes to the [native `toggle` completion event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#queue-a-popover-toggle-event-task) before changing the width and retains the same assertions. Timeout values, retry policy, production code, and test baselines are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original line-309 signature on unchanged `d934b070ce30`: 1/20 file runs with tests and two CPU burners sharing two CPUs. Alone: 0/20 failures. The original failure capture shows the expected popover layout by screenshot time.

title: improve(worktrees): skip the default-branch fetch when origin has not moved
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default-branch worktree creation unnecessarily fetches when origin still advertises the commit already tracked locally. The redundant fetch also enters the repository's Git ref mutation queue.

## User Impact

Worktree creation skips that fetch for an unchanged default tip. Changed or unavailable advertisements retain fetching and the existing warning/fallback behavior. Hydration, local fast-forward rules, cancellation, and the 30-second preparation reuse window remain owned by the existing preparation flow. To bypass the reuse window, fetch and choose an explicit base ref. No new configuration or cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the commit already returned by `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and compare it with the local remote-tracking ref. This avoids an additional network request. The takeover rebases the original work onto main including `75694cca` and repairs the affected service fixture: creating the new commit directly in the bare remote keeps the local clone stale, so the test still exercises a real fetch and its timeout.

Related: #191130 (refresh deadline; separate change), #194712 (hydration output; separate change).

## Evidence

Rebased onto `7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d`, which includes `75694cca`. The original implementation and verified contributor credit are retained.

The original two CI failures reproduce: the service fixture's push updates its own `origin/main`, so fetching correctly disappears and the expected 60-second fetch timeout is absent. Creating the commit directly in the bare remote fixes the fixture while retaining the timeout assertion. The unchanged-tip regression fails on the exact main parent because it performs an extra fetch. Real-Git coverage also checks default-branch switches, force-pushed rewinds, explicit refresh during the reuse window, and cancellation recovery.

Focused validation: 168 passed, 2 existing skips across `base-ref`, `service`, `service-branches`, `git-fetch`, and `git` suites. The repaired two consumer cases pass in 5.24 seconds; the three owner/Git files pass in 100.04 seconds (including transform time). `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed. An isolated built Gateway's actual `worktrees.create` RPC produced the expected checkout SHA with one advertisement and zero fetches for a matching tip, and one advertisement plus one fetch for an independently advanced tip. No external services or production data were used.

Codex autoreview against the pinned base, including staged repairs and the benchmark, was scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings. The original and rebased production module bytes are identical.

### Measurement

Acceptance was fixed in this PR before measured runs: use the real default-base owner, five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and five A/A pairs with fresh clone paths/processes; require identical selected commits, unchanged-tip fetch count 1 → 0, improved phase wall time/CPU/allocation, and investigate regressions above 20%.

Synthetic local-origin partial clone: 62,000 logical files, 1,142,784,000 target bytes, 600,000 unrelated historical blobs and 1,239 packs. Darwin/APFS, warm/unspecified filesystem cache; no agent/session database populated because this phase reads Git state rather than sessions or transcripts. This measures local owner work, not btrfs, network latency, mutation-queue contention, or complete send latency. Five-sample p95 is the maximum, not a production tail estimate.

| Metric | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseRefresh, ms | 211.93 / 345.15 | 136.02 / 153.03 |
| Main-thread CPU, ms | 17.798 / 19.338 | 12.464 / 13.222 |
| Native Git CPU, ms | 80 / 100 | 30 / 40 |
| Native Git peak RSS, MB | 30.097 / 30.163 | 24.609 / 27.361 |
| Main-isolate allocation, MB | 17.032 / 23.747 | 19.221 / 21.507 |
| Git commands / fetches | 7 / 1 | 6 / 0 |

Every paired wall-time and JS-CPU sample improved. A/A wall medians were 197.97 / 196.00 ms (−1.0%), supporting the 35.8% AB latency improvement. **Allocation improvement was not demonstrated:** its median increased 12.9%, its mean decreased 1.75%, and same-source A/A allocation had substantial spread (median −6.5%, p95 +14.8%). Do not treat the allocation acceptance criterion as passed or claim allocation neutrality. The counts, wall time, and CPU support retaining the optimization.

Reproduce using `scripts/perf/worktree-base-refresh-measure.ts --seed <fixture/seed> --base-file <saved-main-base-ref.ts> --output <new-directory>` through `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. title: fix(worktrees): bound default-branch fetch by one refresh deadline
body:
## Problem

"Updating repository…" (gateway phase `preparing_worktree_base`) can hold session startup for minutes. The default-branch refresh is supposed to be bounded by `ls-remote` (30s) plus `fetch` (60s). On the team gateway (worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02), the slowest start took 270.7s with `baseRefresh=234126ms`, and its fetch **succeeded** without a warning. A borrower sharing that attempt waited `baseWait=120557ms`.

## Root cause

The gateway's diagnostics for that start show that the time was spent waiting in a queue, not in Git or on the network:

```
10:57:40.637 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=0       queuedOperationMs=807300   (another writer on the same clone)
10:57:44.425 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=229670  queuedOperationMs=3787     (the default-branch fetch)
```

`fetchRemoteDefault` runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<default>:refs/remotes/origin/<default>` with `{ ...options, timeoutMs: 60_000 }` (`src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts:473` on `main`). A fetch is a ref mutation, so `withGitRefAdmission` (`src/agents/worktrees/git.ts:198`) first enqueues it on the per-clone `enqueueGitRefMutation` queue (`git.ts:238`). The 60s timeout starts only after the queue admits the fetch and its process starts. While queued, the fetch is bounded only by the caller's signal, and that signal has no deadline here.

As a result, any long ref writer on the same clone (`worktree add`, hydration, pack maintenance, a fast-forward) stretches the "60s" fetch to the length of its own run. In the slow start above, the fetch queued for 229.7s and ran for 3.8s, which adds up to the 234s `baseRefresh`. On Nov 2, the same log also shows other holders running for 123–807s and queued waiters waiting 47–230s.

## Solution

Give the default-branch refresh one deadline. `fetchRemoteDefault` arms a 90s deadline (the existing 30s + 60s budgets) before `ls-remote`, combines it with the caller's signal, and passes the result to the fetch:

- If the deadline expires while the fetch is still queued, the ref queue drops the fetch before it starts.
- If the deadline expires while the fetch is running, the process is stopped like a timeout.

Both cases take the existing fetch-failure path: keep the cached `refs/remotes/origin/<default>`, report `fetchSucceeded: false`, and add a warning that names the 90s budget and the wait for other Git ref updates. This adds no fallback mode, option, or queue policy.

The caller's own signal still owns cancellation and attempt retirement. The deadline applies only to the fetch call, so an expired refresh is not treated as a cancelled owner.

## Impact

- A held ref queue now adds at most ~90s of refresh to a default-branch start, instead of the holder's full duration (230s observed, up to 807s possible). The start then proceeds on the cached default with a visible warning.
- Borrowers sharing the attempt get the same bounded result.
- As before, the fallback does not mark the base fresh, so the next start retries the fetch.

## Evidence

Regression test in `base-ref.test.ts`: "uses the cached default when the fetch outwaits the refresh deadline in the ref queue". It uses a real Git repo and remote, a real ref-queue holder on the same clone, and the real `resolveWorktreeBase`. Only the 90s timer is replaced by a test-controlled signal.

- Base (`63c25f72`): **red**. The test times out after Vitest's 120000ms because the fetch stays queued behind the holder.
- Fix: **green**. The whole `base-ref.test.ts` file passes (51 passed).

Wall-clock repro (a scratch test that is not committed; real timers, real Git, real ref queue, with another writer holding the clone's ref queue for 150s):

| | wall time of `resolveWorktreeBase` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | 151,482 ms | waited for the holder; `fetchSucceeded: true` |
| Fix | 91,698 ms | cached default, `fetchSucceeded: false`, deadline warning |

Other checks: `git-fetch.test.ts` and `git.test.ts` pass (43 passed). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.

Review: local autoreview (Codex engine, branch mode, base `63c25f72` → head `4c0ad6c7`, max priority P2) was scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The reviewer noted limited surrounding context and that it did not run the tests.

## Accepted edge cases

- The local reads before and after the network refresh (`git remote`, `config`, `symbolic-ref`, the cached `rev-parse`) keep their standard 120s budgets. They do not queue, and they are needed to produce the cached fallback. They are slow only when the host itself is IO-starved.
- The `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` update after a successful fetch is also a ref mutation, so it can still queue. It runs only when the remote default branch changes.
- `baseHydration` (`estimateWorktreeGitBytes`) is not covered, because the checkout needs those objects. Its 120s and 240s tails on this host come from local Git reads reaching their 120s budget on a clone with 1,216 packs and no multi-pack-index, and those starts failed. That belongs to clone maintenance, not to this deadline.
- The 807s ref-queue holder on Nov 2 was not identified from the logs. This change bounds its effect on startup but does not shorten the holder.
- I did not measure a remote that hangs. In this sandbox, a synthetic hanging `upload-pack` made `ls-remote` end with a cleanup-uncertain error at its 30s timeout on base. That is a separate path from the queue wait.

title: improve: compare large media and audio buffers directly
body:
Related: #191063, #190634, #190167, #190168

## What Problem This Solves

Media upload and queued-audio tests spend seconds walking multi-MiB Buffers through Vitest's deep matcher.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same retained cases preserve exact byte, length, order, and metadata checks while summed retained-file case-time medians fall from **10.699s to 0.619s**, saving **10.079s (94.2%)** in this measured batch.

The sum of retained command-wall medians is **63.604s → 64.851s**. These runs show reduced case time; they do not show an aggregate command-wall speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native `Buffer.equals` assertions inside each plugin test. X uses its existing Node assertion; xAI uses labeled Vitest boolean assertions. The earlier shared-helper imports were rejected by the enforced plugin test boundary and are removed without adding an exception. Keep the media chunk indices/sizes and request metadata assertions. For xAI, assert exactly two queued chunks and compare each position against its corresponding original input. Production code, fixture sizes, cases, timers, and cleanup are unchanged.

The update-helper conversion is dropped because its measured whole-file case-time saving is below the approximately 0.3s retention threshold. Both that helper and the consumer held by #156200 are byte-identical to the base. Its measured trial remains in the evidence table for transparency.

The final change adds **2 test lines** for explicit queued-array cardinality/position checks. The exact +2 allocation records this limited growth; the shared scalar baseline is unchanged. The allocation itself adds two non-test lines, so the complete diff is net +4 lines. Optional 256 KiB targets are omitted.

## Evidence

Three baseline and three candidate runs per file executed serially on **one Blacksmith Testbox** `tbx_01m6e84j0a1p828v613858gkw0`, routine/8-class profile, reporting 2 usable CPUs and approximately 8 GiB RAM: [workflow 41455773748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455773748). Both sides used frozen-lockfile dependencies. Baseline is pinned `origin/main` `f4619fdf2adef4884293111fd4c42dafa3cbd76f`; the measured helper-based candidate is `8d3eebc3fdb850755e23b09f478eedb7de429ba0`. The boundary repair calls the same native byte-equality operation directly; paired timings were not repeated after that repair. Separate detached worktrees preserve each source revision. Runtime preparation is excluded from measurements.

All 18 uninstrumented timing executions passed, and case inventories matched across all six runs of each file. **Case time is the sum of native JSON reporter per-case durations**, not native module duration. Wall time measures the entire named-file command, including imports, worker preparation, and cleanup. These are same-box observations, not a predicted CI critical-path reduction.

| File / consumer | Median case-time sum, baseline → candidate | Saved | Median command wall, baseline → candidate | Decision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `extensions/x/src/api.media.test.ts` | 7.404s → 0.442s | 6.962s | 10.563s → 5.013s | retain |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.test.ts` | 74.601s → 97.437s | -22.836s | 134.306s → 192.727s | drop |
| `extensions/xai/lazy-capability-providers.test.ts` | 3.294s → 0.177s | 3.117s | 53.041s → 59.837s | retain |

Both retained conversions exceed the approximately 0.3s retention threshold. The migrated-update totals varied substantially across runs, so no claim is made that its slower whole-file observation is caused by the byte helper; the requested retention rule is applied to the measured medians.

<details>
<summary>All timing samples, seconds</summary>

| File / consumer | Version | Case-time sums 1 / 2 / 3 | Command walls 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/x/src/api.media.test.ts` | baseline | 7.598 / 7.404 / 7.387 | 12.396 / 10.394 / 10.563 |
| `extensions/x/src/api.media.test.ts` | candidate | 0.438 / 0.442 / 0.515 | 5.747 / 3.900 / 5.013 |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.test.ts` | baseline | 95.751 / 74.601 / 66.532 | 169.164 / 134.306 / 115.904 |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.test.ts` | candidate | 89.813 / 97.437 / 115.132 | 157.210 / 192.727 / 206.803 |
| `extensions/xai/lazy-capability-providers.test.ts` | baseline | 3.630 / 3.119 / 3.294 | 72.560 / 50.490 / 53.041 |
| `extensions/xai/lazy-capability-providers.test.ts` | candidate | 0.229 / 0.177 / 0.170 | 62.446 / 53.842 / 59.837 |

Each measured command used the repository runner and exactly one named file:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=json --outputFile=<sample.json>
```

The update file is an unchanged consumer of the trial helper conversion, which is reverted in this PR. Initial detached-worktree preparation failed before tests because UI dependency links and built subprocess dependencies were missing. Checkout-owned frozen installs and canonical `prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --with-ai-package` preparation resolved those setup failures. One update trial exceeded the initial 180s outer process envelope; subsequent trials used 300s, with the tests' own deadlines unchanged. Only completed, passing samples enter the table. The completed X samples were retained with their original input digests.

</details>

Temporary probes at each existing comparison exercised real produced Buffers. Each probe corrupts the first, middle, and last byte, truncates one byte, or appends one byte, then invokes the original baseline matcher or candidate helper. Every altered operand must throw **AssertionError**. Restored operands must pass again and match their original SHA-256 digest. Original assertions remain in place after the probes; xAI's baseline array matcher is exercised separately for each changed element.

Each cell is **baseline / candidate**:

| Converted comparison | First | Middle | Last | Truncate 1 | Append 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| X assembled media (4 MiB + 7 B) | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject |
| Update observed progress (dropped experiment) | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject |
| Update drained stderr (dropped experiment) | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject |
| xAI first copied chunk (1 MiB) | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject |
| xAI second copied chunk (1 MiB) | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject | reject / reject |

**All 50 rejection controls passed**, with matching failure types on both versions: 30 cover the retained comparisons and 20 cover the dropped update experiment. Every restored operand digest matched. All six temporarily instrumented source files were restored and their SHA-256 digests verified; final remote digests also match the frozen baseline/trial inputs. Retained source digests match the measured helper-based candidate, and the dropped helper matches the base. The final direct assertions preserve the same `Buffer.equals` inputs and expected values; the mutation matrix was not repeated after the boundary repair. No probe is committed.

- Scoped lint, format, and typecheck of the three trial roots, including both retained files and their imports, passed on Testbox. The typecheck extends the canonical core-test shard with the required ambient declarations.
- `git diff --check` passed. The simplify pass retains only native byte comparisons, explicit ordered-chunk checks, and the exact test-line allocation.
- The measured helper candidate had a P0–P2 scoped-clean isolated Codex review against base `73f784f92ec7b8c5bc8c5a88c5a798757a65f776`. A fresh isolated Codex review of the full repaired local candidate against that base identified no working-tree correctness defects; its INDEX-only finding was resolved by staging and committing all repaired files. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Exact repaired-head CI passed before merge.
- Original benchmarks, tests, builds, installs, and scoped validation ran on Testbox. During landing, the native PR wrapper materialized its frozen tooling dependencies after IO avg60 passed the required gate, under `ionice -c3 nice`; only touched-file formatting and Git checks ran locally. No local test suite, lint/typecheck sweep, container, browser, staging, or packaging ran. PR CI supplies broad validation.
- The benchmark Testbox was stopped after proof. Landing-time focused proof request `tbx_01m6echrjb7v2qc2vs6v1qwvt9` queued and was stopped before execution, so it supplies no candidate proof. The native state is completed and cleanup settled after its associated workflow was cancelled. It supplies no test proof.
- Incoming-head CI [41465374009](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41465374009) ran X media (17 passing cases) and xAI lazy capability providers (4 passing cases); `check-additional-boundaries` and `checks-node-changed-boundary` rejected the two helper imports. The repair removes those imports. Fresh exact-head CI [41468126042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41468126042) completed successfully for `5764871375f06a30ad87dabe71e435c8686f072e`: X media 17/17 and xAI 4/4 passed in job [125355267346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41468126042/job/125355267346); both previously failing boundary jobs, lint, typecheck, the test-line ratchet, security, and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. The PR was cleanly mergeable with all required statuses green before landing.

title: improve: hand off portal previews in private chats
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents without a Control UI side panel are directed to the Portals page even when the user explicitly requests a private app-preview link in chat.

Requested by @vincentkoc in the [original discussion](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2115408545948852444).

## User Impact

Agents are explicitly guided to return the existing portal's authenticated launch URL for a requested private handoff to the authorized recipient, while retaining the Control UI panel path for in-UI previews. They must not automatically post bearer links to group/public chats or present loopback-only routes as phone-accessible links.

This is an agent-guidance change, not a new transport, automatic message sender, permission grant, or network setup. The agent still needs existing portal tool access and the deployment still needs reachable private ingress. No authentication, tool policy, Gateway configuration, or tunnel behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small, static guidance source now supplies the system-prompt presentation advice, both portal tool descriptions, and open/list results. It distinguishes authenticated url from token-free publicUrl and keeps private sharing, link withdrawal, and reachability limitations consistent. Existing portal URL generation and proxying remain the single networking owner.

The focused regression extends existing prompt and portal-tool tests; no additional Gateway boot or test harness is introduced. The separate 13-line test allocation covers the exact net regression growth without changing the shared baseline.

## Evidence

- The new generated-prompt contract failed both screen/no-screen cases before the production change and passes afterward.
- Focused tests: **89 passed** across UI presentation, portal tool routing/results, full system-prompt assembly, and tool-prefix stability. The selected wrapper completed in 835.39 seconds including cold worker preparation. Modified-file timings: UI presentation 2.40 seconds; portal tool 33.98 seconds, dominated by transform/import work (test execution 28 milliseconds). CI seconds are not available yet.
- Targeted agents-tools and agents-root TypeScript projects passed; type-aware lint passed for all six changed TypeScript files; formatting and git diff checks passed.
- Documentation link audit: 16,232 internal links checked, zero broken.
- The repository-wide staged test-line ratchet did not complete within a 300-second execution budget. The staged diff has 13 net new test lines and its separate allocation is exactly 13; the CI ratchet remains pending.

An initial 300-second execution deadline interrupted cold worker/boundary preparation before the larger test and lint checks completed. After reconciling the stopped processes, the same scoped checks completed with sufficient build time; no test assertion was weakened.

**Remaining proof gap:** no live model-driven Telegram handoff or physical-phone/Safari run is claimed. Earlier local PoC checks exercised actual portal authentication, app assets/navigation/downloads/streaming, and link withdrawal, but the available deployment returned loopback-only exposure. These tests protect the model-facing guidance and existing tool contracts; they do not prove model compliance or remote phone reachability.

title: fix(plugins): distinguish CLI inspection from Gateway state
body:
Closes #155080

Supersedes #155761, thanks @Yun-0000.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `plugins inspect --runtime` can report a plugin as loaded even when the running Gateway never loaded it.

## User Impact

Runtime inspection names its local status `CLI status` and reports the running Gateway's state separately. JSON adds `inspectionScope: "cli"` and `gatewayRuntime` (or `null` when no Gateway runtime fact is available). Local hooks/tools remain available; snapshot output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `plugins.list` RPC already reads the Gateway's active plugin registry, so the CLI reuses it without adding an RPC. Gateway lookup/query failures produce a warning and unavailable Gateway state while preserving the local report.

The simplification pass removed the detail formatter's duplicate runtime flag. Production growth is +39 lines to query and label the two processes, preserve local diagnostics when the Gateway is unavailable, and retain the existing detailed inspection contract.

## Evidence

- [Crabbox/Blacksmith run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41446401174), lease `tbx_01m6e49xnw1v32jb6fn203sjb0`: `pnpm test src/cli/plugins-cli.inspect.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.cold-inspect.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

Final autoreview of the complete change against `d934b070ce304c378607dd8edacbc2774c9b5105`, including the RPC owner, schema, and fixtures: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no unresolved findings.
- [CI at `3cd392e5f2f2d8097ec8370023059ffa741029a1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41450742951/job/125295941178) passed both affected files, including unavailable-Gateway fallback: 5 cold cases (14.67s shard wall) and 15 inspect cases (5.41s). title: fix(anthropic): read deeply nested Claude session history
body:
Related: #153719

Supersedes #155453, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

Fixes: opening Claude session history fails with a stack overflow when a saved message contains deeply nested tool results or metadata.

## User Impact

Users can read the affected history and load earlier messages. When native content cannot serialize safely, the reader keeps readable text and message metadata, marks the item as truncated, and leaves the source transcript untouched.

The regressions use 50,000 nested object/array pairs and check text order, metadata, serialization, older-page cursors, and unchanged native files. title: improve(ui): move Draft beside Incognito on desktop
body:

On desktop and tablet, the new-session **Draft** toggle sat in the composer footer and only appeared while you hovered it. On narrow phones it already sat at the top next to **Incognito**.

title: improve: speed up plugin artifact byte assertions
body:
Related: #189965, #190072, #190167, #190168, #190634

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin artifact tests spend seconds walking multi-MiB Buffers through Vitest's deep matcher.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same native artifact capture tests run faster while retaining exact byte and length checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep `expectBytes(filename, bytes)` and its synchronous `fs.readFileSync`, then delegate comparison to the existing `expectBytesEqual` snapshot helper (`Buffer.equals`), with the filename as label. All 2 MiB fixtures, real captures, scope/inode/receipt assertions, and missing-file failures remain intact. No production changes or new test cases.

One test-support file changes: +3/−2, **net +1 test line**, solely from importing the existing comparison owner. The worker test held by #188890 is untouched. Fresh actual file-list checks of 37 candidate PRs found consumer overlap with #181491/#188890, but no overlap with this helper; those consumer files remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Three baseline and three candidate samples per file ran serially on the same Linux Blacksmith 16-vCPU Testbox `tbx_01m6dzd0n5qceaxnx6sxdtg3c7`, with frozen-lockfile bootstrap: [run 41435027915](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41435027915). Every timing execution passed. All source input digests matched the frozen baseline; candidate helper bytes match this branch.

The first timing column is the **sum of the reported per-case durations**, not native module/file duration. The final column is measured whole-command wall time, including imports, worker preparation and cleanup. Worker preparation varied substantially, so these are same-box observations, not a predicted CI critical-path saving.

| Consumer | Median case-time sum, baseline → candidate | Saved case time | Median command wall, baseline → candidate |
