title: fix(ui): preserve New Session test failure diagnostics
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing failure diagnostics when New Session browser tests close their contexts during teardown.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. Developers get the existing diagnostic report and screenshot before the test page is destroyed. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

**This does not explain or fix the original CI renderer crash. Its cause remains unresolved.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated page opener maintained a second context list and closed contexts directly, bypassing the suite's capture-and-cleanup lifecycle. It now delegates to the existing suite owner; the dedicated New Session factory enables that owner's tracked cleanup. No shared runner, timeout, guard, or diagnostic policy changes.

One native Vitest/Chromium regression verifies the private report is complete when the context closes, the original error and real screenshot survive, public diagnostics exclude private failure text, the next test has no leaked contexts, and the browser disconnects. Only external application-server startup is stubbed. The helper changes remove five net lines; the native regression adds 144 lines, with an exact 139-line net test allocation.

## Evidence

- **Base red → fixed green:** the context-close witness changes from `closedWithReport: [false]` to `[true]`. The fixed native regression passed in 12.347 seconds (57.50 seconds Vitest wall time). Hooks, Chromium, capture, and teardown are real.
- **Affected consumers:** 12 tests passed across responsive-welcome, keyboard, agent-identity, and config-startup, covering multiple contexts, mobile options, nested helper construction, and existing `withPage` cleanup.
- Both affected UI typecheck leaves, type-aware scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line ratchet passed on the reviewed source.
- On the standalone main-based candidate: exact patch/owner-input comparison and whitespace checks passed; the canonical test-line ratchet passed with 6,394,283 lines under a 6,404,433 ceiling.
- Fresh local autoreview covered P0–P3 on base `acc670a76cf53736398652c6314380472de9427a` → reviewed source `e11c9ae01625b3072f5043ee1156d99bbf4389e7`: complete, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings.

### Provenance and limits

Standalone head `b88d2f47121ffb2caadf63d4a8da353f53dae836` transplants only that diagnostic repair onto official main `fcf176cc1f600fea3dde30bfab8930b7751ffe7a`; it does not include the synthetic CI-merge or backup feature ancestry. The four-file patch is byte-identical to the reviewed repair. Git object comparisons across 2,027 selected owner, helper, configuration, and manifest paths confirm unchanged lifecycle/diagnostics/shutdown owners and regression/toolchain inputs. The three differences are outside the lifecycle regression (a visual benchmark probe, one mobile-test selector, and a sidebar locator).

Execution above remains bound to the reviewed source. Main has since changed application mobile chrome and overlays, so the 12 application-test results are **prior-source evidence, not current-head CI**. The lifecycle regression does not boot that application, and its owning inputs remain unchanged. Local proof used **Node 26**, while the failed CI run used **Node 24**. Original crash and setup evidence are retained. No duplicate full build, install, or CI rerun was used to manufacture an attribution.

### Exact-head real-application capture — November 3

A separate qualification on unchanged head `b88d2f47121ffb2caadf63d4a8da353f53dae836` removes the application-startup stub from the earlier proof. A private exact-source export, normal frozen dependency installation, and one maintained bundled UI build were used; no tracked source or PR changes were made.

- The real prebuilt application rendered `/new`, including its checkout control and composer. The maintained New Session page opener and suite owned the page/context; no `page.setContent`, manual diagnostic capture, or early context close was used.
- Exactly **one deliberately marker-bearing assertion failed and one subsequent lifecycle test passed**. Runner exit **1** is intentional—not a claim of two passing tests. No additional failed case, unhandled browser rejection, page error, or capture error occurred.
- Exactly one capture contained the public report, private report, and an **80,892-byte PNG**, all already present when the context closed. `rendererRead: "completed"`, `hostBeforeRead.pageClosed: false`, and `hostBeforeRead.browserConnected: true` were observed. The screenshot was privately inspected and shows the real New Session UI.
- The following test found zero retained contexts. The suite connection disconnected; Chromium exited normally with code 0; the recorded runner/worker PIDs and task-path processes were absent, and the preview port was closed.

Source admission verified 62,723 tracked blobs, 111,856 dependency entries, 3,700 bundle files, and six native-plugin files. That completed admission and its postchecks were reused unchanged; the final invocation checked 18 current lifecycle/config/launcher inputs plus the fixture, bundle identity, native assets, package versions, and browser. The bundle manifest SHA-256 is `8ed6b76610d74926e8497009cde14fa10fed2c2513603c46c9e63c441282e4bb`; screenshot SHA-256 is `fba3154426e9ed551c57f2a1e256d5e2e121fef18535785eb1dd837cc8c5ebd7`.

**Limits:** Node 26.12.1 and installed Chromium headless shell 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248); Gateway transport remained synthetic and service workers were blocked by the standard fixture. This qualifies diagnostic lifetime on the real application, not real Gateway/model behavior or the original renderer crash. The bundle retains its producer's E2E metadata; source identity is bound separately by the manifests. Earlier source-admission, metadata-layout, and CommonJS/ESM setup failures and a stopped pre-test filesystem read are preserved, not counted as product failures or successful runs. title: feat: schedule automatic updates in Settings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway operators cannot choose when automatic updates start.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Updates now offers hourly (the existing default), daily with a time, weekly with a day and time, and a custom cron expression. Times follow the Gateway host’s timezone, not the browser’s.

## Why This Change Was Made

One optional `update.auto.schedule` cron string stores the schedule; presets are UI projections. No timezone field, new package dependency, or storage migration is added. Existing cron calculation and the Gateway scheduler remain the owners.

Configured schedules gate campaign starts, including startup, restart, and interactive Dev refresh. Missed windows are skipped. Stable rollout delays, idle/countdown behavior, restart safety, manual updates, and the one-hour hold remain intact. Schedule changes hot-apply and cancel pending campaigns without interrupting an applying update.

Requested by and implemented for @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a6452bb-b935-4086-8f43-3e795f64d30e)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7bf59300-3432-4c32-b379-9b13390a8546)

## Evidence

- Built Control UI with a synthetic Gateway: all five Updates E2E scenarios passed (151.20 s total). The schedule scenario exercised hourly → daily 04:25 → Tuesday 04:25 → custom cron → hourly and asserted serialized `config.set` writes. Inspected before/after screenshots and weekly/custom states are embedded below.
- Daily campaign admission failed on base because it started at 10:00 despite a 10:30 schedule. The repaired daily, sub-hourly, skipped-window, hot-rearming, and interactive Git behavior passed. Both final extracted schedule regressions also passed (668.00 s including cold preparation; 7.143 s test execution).
- Initial implementation: scheduler/consumer tests 75 passed, 71.61 s wall; campaign/lifecycle/manual-refresh 41 passed; config 74 passed, 19.20 s; existing cron/DST 13 passed, 1.76 s; Updates view 42 passed, 3.12 s.
- Initial implementation: core/UI production typechecks, infra fixture typecheck, targeted lint, Solid controller guard, i18n verification, changed-document formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Initial canonical autoreview against `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.84. The review includes the extracted scheduler and test fixture. Lead independently reviewed campaign admission, hot reload, cron reuse, and UI serialization.
- [Published-driver upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439871998/job/125269758422) passed on attempt 1: published npm `2026.10.9` → exact candidate `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852` (`2026.10.9`), with no candidate relabeling. Readiness returned 200, running version and durable-session survival were verified, and package integrity/npm-12 installer acceptance passed. The cell took 435 seconds; the complete workflow took 2,154 seconds. This uses synthetic state and the maintained systemctl harness, not native-systemd qualification.

### CI repair validation

The [first PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439183580) identified PR-caused import-cycle/extracted-wrapper closure errors, two test static-analysis errors, and omitted config baseline artifacts. The follow-up repair moves the existing cron validator and timezone normalization unchanged into a shared leaf, includes that leaf and the already-pinned `croner` package in extracted wrappers, corrects the test typing/shadowing, and regenerates the baseline. No scheduler policy or visible UI changes were made.

On an isolated AWS Linux runner with 4 vCPUs, 15.3 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, and one test worker:

- Selected CI regressions: 35 tooling + 16 native provisioning tests passed, with 2 existing skips; 385.577 s wall. All originally failing test cases passed.
- Cron/config/CLI consumers: 99 tests passed across four files; 89.494 s wall.
- Runtime/tooling lint passed with zero warnings or errors (36.996/158.004 s). UI E2E test types passed (19.200 s); architecture check found zero cycles (42.303 s); config generation/check, test allocation, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- All 37 feature/repair source hashes matched before and after execution. Generated outputs were downloaded unchanged and matched the final worktree; 15 retained proof-artifact hashes were verified. The single temporary runner was released after 35m36s, without extending its lifetime.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of the repair delta against `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.93; final source verification passed.

The config baseline intentionally grows by exactly one core key (2,584 → 2,585) for the requested optional `update.auto.schedule` field. Channel/plugin counts and hashes are unchanged. The 250-line test allocation covers campaign admission/restart, hot policy changes, config rejection, routed UI persistence, and the two additional fixture/import lines needed for the repair; the shared scalar budget is unchanged. Per-test CI seconds are not yet extracted from broad CI artifacts.

### Final CI result and remaining proof gap

[CI run 41455922677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677) completed with **failure** on head `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372`; all 89 job records are terminal. The sole failed workload was [control-ui-performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125313331221); the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. The [final failure table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125323853067) classifies this as **new**: the matching main job passed, and selected scope was not compared. It is not relabeled as inherited-only.

Both performance builds succeeded. Chat boot gzip increased from **1,278,812 B to 1,278,972 B (+160 B)**, with 20 requests unchanged. Because the base already exceeds the 1,277,887 B fixed cap, only the existing **64 B** build-variance allowance applies: the candidate is **96 B over** its effective 1,278,876 B limit. Startup JS increased 9 B, New boot JS 17 B, and CSS growth was zero.

Logged payload growth is confined to the lazy Settings copy and Updates-page chunks at the log's rounded precision. The same schedule UI source previously produced a -4 B Chat gzip delta against an earlier main base. This suggests generated asset-hash/minifier sensitivity, but it does **not** establish hash-only byte equality or a passing budget. The performance job does not retain the paired distributions, and its helper deletes the temporary base build. A matched base/head build with retained JavaScript, compression sidecars, HTML, and source maps is still required for decisive attribution and any justified fix. No performance budget or variance allowance has been changed.

Validation scope: earlier cold-worker attempts timed out before executing the extracted fixture; the final extracted tests passed. The optional full changed-file gate reached its 600-second local budget after its first six checks passed. Focused repair validation is green, but full CI is not green for the reason above. The upgrade rehearsal remains evidence only for `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`; the repair changes runtime module inputs, and no upgrade rehearsal of `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372` is claimed. No live Gateway settings or services were changed.

### Password-free rejection fixture (November 4)

Commit `0eaabb3cc7606d7e381cf70b9919c737093fc16f`, published in head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`, replaces one synthetic negative-URL fixture in `src/config/config-misc.test.ts` with a transparent username-only URL containing no password. The existing expected-false schema assertion is unchanged. The original combined fixture short-circuited on username; this replacement preserves that rejection without claiming independent password-branch coverage. No encoding, runtime reconstruction, scanner policy, or production behavior changes were made.

- Focused config suite: **74 passed**, 42.97 s test time / 45.28 s wrapper wall, with one worker.
- Actual-schema sensitivity proof verified nonempty username and empty password, rejection by the real schema, acceptance of the clean origin, and that masking only the parsed username in an isolated process makes the unchanged expected-false assertion fail. The URL parser was restored and the production owner remained byte-identical.
- Targeted formatting, lint, config test types, and diff checks passed. Fresh canonical autoreview was P0–P2 scoped-clean with no findings, confidence 0.99, and final source verification passed.
- This delta is test-only; existing screenshots remain representative. It does not repair the prior performance failure or extend the old-head upgrade evidence above.

**Hosted review remains blocked before a verdict.** The [November 4 re-review request at 11:01:54 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628986837) targeted head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`. Its [correlated status changed to Failed at 11:05:46 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628989117); [run 41818159154, exact-review job 126534173101](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41818159154/job/126534173101) failed at the `agent_input_scan` stage (`reason_code: findings`, non-retryable), producing no review verdict. The retained manifest reports **two findings**. Only the **first** has been located: the unchanged base synthetic negative-URL fixture at `src/config/config-misc.test.ts:153`, in base revision `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`; its blob identity and path hash were independently matched against GitHub. The second finding has not been identified. This is a fresh refusal, separate from the [November 2 refusal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6580594500), and it does not establish that the new username-only literal passed scanning. Base content and removed patch text remain in the review range. No raw fixture values are reproduced here, no scanner policy was changed, and successful local autoreview is not represented as hosted approval.

title: improve(ui): hide self-only People in Session Details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session Details shows a People section even when the signed-in viewer is the only person associated with the session.

In a single-user OpenClaw setup, a People section that only lists the person already using it feels unnecessary and out of place. On a multi-user server, the same section provides useful ownership and collaboration context. The intention is to remove the self-only noise while keeping People when it tells the viewer about someone else.

## User Impact

The right-hand Details sidebar omits that redundant section. Another person's session and sessions with multiple people still show People. Unknown viewer identity or incomplete people metadata keeps the existing conservative display. No unrelated header, sharing, mobile, or layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing deduplicated owner/creator/participant union and compare its sole typed identity with the authenticated viewer. This adds no state or identity-resolution policy. The bundle repair deletes a redundant actor projection and compares the schema-qualified profile viewer by identity type and ID; other namespaces remain distinct.

title: fix(doctor): await inspection snapshots and native repair phases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can start a synchronous SQLite snapshot from lint, inspection, migration, or a later native repair guard. Large databases then block signal handling and leave expensive images behind. Chrislro’s stack sample in #178359 identified the parent blocked in node::SyncProcessRunner.

## User Impact

The candidate awaits snapshot preparation and repair observations, carries cancellation through worker cleanup, and checks free space when inspection needs a private image. Current admission reads are consumed in the synchronous frame that performs a service, configuration, credential, or database effect, with existing physical ownership and final native checks retained.

Core #190788 already supplies platform boot provenance, cancellation and capacity protection. This PR completes the coupled caller cutover and guards unexpected cold synchronous preparation. Private CURRENT images compare the complete captured family before admission. Unknown provenance still requires the conservative integrity gate. No schema, public configuration, protocol version, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

Assembled head8bd6391d72f4697da9f5378753f8ce6fa9e326b8 includes main714490716002d24b939817366f277872b6ea2825 and the late Reader/Process fixes. Main’s bounded restart recovery and FIFO readiness behavior is preserved; both conflict resolutions received independent source review and exact-file static checks.

Canonical autoreview through P2 passed the individual stages, the complete current-admission candidate (two passes at b7d4b161), and the NOCOW child-join correction. Whole assembled-range review and runtime qualification remain pending. The current source-derived selection contains809 named owner files, all84 standing state-migration files, three agent-admission files and six critical CLI/Doctor flows. Selection is not passing-test evidence.

Remaining work before landing: a valid legacy-v2 quarantine generation can still request a synchronous target fingerprint through an async native-opening path. That owner/caller path is being completed; deliberate public synchronous calls retain visible refusal. Current-head cancellation, capacity guards, repair/upgrade flows, named owners, strict export scans, final integration review and fully green exact-head CI are required before merge.

Prior guard-only CI exposed cold admission failures. Process0f diagnostics locate its first writable restart stall after the config-snapshot callback; they do not prove native restart entered. These failures remain recorded, without inferred repair claims.

Simplification removed the full-file/decoded-row admission cache, moved the unrelated ClawRouter diagnostic outside this PR, and replaced ten intermediate allocation records with one exact2458-LF allocation across130 changed test/support files. Each post-await native phase prepares and consumes fresh owner facts.

Refs #178359, #187900, #185879. Credit @chrislro for the determining stack sample: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639. Not yet released.

title: fix(ci): provision Node codegen prerequisites and retain Baseten routing

## What Problem This Solves

Node CI can select standalone codegen without provisioning its Bun child, and Baseten admission currently routes to tooling instead of the existing native-credential infra worker owner.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. CI receives the prerequisites and worker custody required by the tests it selects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split the remaining CI prerequisites from #190870 (c744c746 and 266c7b5d), applying only their manifest and Baseten registration hunks. Main still needs both: the two new regression cases fail on main fcf176cc1f600fea3dde30bfab8930b7751ffe7a, then pass with this change. Main already removed Baseten's private preload in #190958; that test is unchanged here.

The manifest preserves Node as the test runner while provisioning pinned Bun only for codegen selections, including whole tooling-config selections. Baseten joins the existing infra owner alongside Levanto. No new runner group or concurrency change.

- Reviewed recent hourly main failures: [41420906680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41420906680) and [41413401584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41413401584). Their failing tests are unrelated to these prerequisites; hourly Bun-mode CI already provisions Bun. The Node-mode omission and Baseten misrouting are demonstrated by the current-main planner regressions, not inferred from unrelated red jobs.

title: fix(ui): pin Pages and Users sidebar headers like Sessions
body:
## Problem

The Sessions sidebar header sits above the list scroller, but the Pages and Users headers were rendered inside it. So:

- the Pages/Users header scrolled away with its list, and the scroll fade masked it;
- with a non-overlay scrollbar, the scrollbar gutter took width from the header, so the collapse button sat further left on Pages than on Sessions;
- collapse-button placement relied on per-panel margin overrides (`.sidebar-session-toolbar …`, `.sidebar-online …`), while Pages had none.

## Solution

- Render the Pages and Users headers in the same slot as the Sessions toolbar, above `.sidebar-shell__body` (`app-sidebar-owner.tsx`). The lazy Pages/Users bodies now render only their lists.
- `app-sidebar-panel-headers.tsx` now owns one header shell (`SidebarPanelHeader`: drag region plus collapse toggle) and one filter button (`SidebarPanelFilter`). Sessions, Pages and Users all use them, so the headers can't drift apart again, and chat boot JS stays within the Control UI performance budget.
- Remove the auto-margin rules for the collapse toggle and their per-panel overrides. The title, or the filter button's existing `margin-left: auto`, now pushes the actions to the end of every header.

Builds on #191019 (shared `.sidebar-panel-header__title`).

## Evidence

- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-users-filter.e2e.test.ts`: at 1280×320, the Users, Pages (scrolled to the bottom) and Sessions headers and their collapse buttons have identical bounding boxes. On `main` the test fails because the Pages header scrolls to `y: -102`. With this fix it passes.
- `ui/src/e2e/native-desktop-titlebar.e2e.test.ts` (web/macOS/Tauri header alignment): passes.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-online.test.ts`, `app-sidebar-lazy-views.test.tsx`, `app-sidebar-rail.test.ts`, `app-sidebar-session-row-render.test.tsx`, `app-sidebar-pages-identity.test.ts`: pass. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base <main sha>` passes locally: chat boot JS gzip is 1277808 B, under the 1277887 B cap.

title: improve(ui): clarify chat permission picker copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat composer's permission picker used internal language ("Execution permissions", "session root", "Guarded", "Workspace", "operator.admin") that doesn't tell people what the agent can actually do in their chat.

## User Impact

User impact: the permission picker now says in plain words what the agent can read, edit, and run in this chat, with one name per mode. Config values and behavior are unchanged; **Ask me** and **Auto-review** are display renames of `guarded` and `workspace`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the copy Vyctor approved for the permission picker (sentence case, "chat" instead of "session", no internal jargon). Only English source copy changes; foreign locales pick it up through the normal locale refresh.

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger tooltip | Choose what available tools may do in this session. This does not change the tool profile. | Choose what the agent can read, edit, and run in this chat. |
| Menu heading / trigger aria prefix | Execution permissions | Permissions |
| Default row title | Default | Agent default |
| Default row description | The agent's configured permissions. | Uses this agent's settings. |
| `read-only` | Read Only · Agent tools can read within the session root, but cannot write or run commands. | Read only · Can read files in this chat's workspace. Can't edit files or run commands. |
| `guarded` | Guarded · A human reviews requests beyond the session root. | Ask me · Asks you before doing anything outside the workspace. |
| `workspace` | Workspace · An AI reviewer checks requests beyond the session root. | Auto-review · An AI reviewer approves actions outside the workspace. |
| `full` | Full Access · No reviewer; files and commands are unrestricted. | Full access · Edits files and runs commands anywhere, without review. |
| Full access locked | Full access requires operator.admin access. | Only admins can turn on Full access. |
| Update failed | Failed to update permissions: {error} | Couldn't change permissions: {error} |
| Saved, refresh failed | Permissions were saved, but refreshing the session failed: {error} | Permissions saved, but this chat didn't refresh. Reload to see the change. |

Notes:
- The **Default** badge on the agent's default mode row and the `Default ({mode})` format are unchanged. The default row's accessible name now matches its visible title: **Agent default (Ask me)** (new keys `agentDefault` / `agentDefaultWithMode`).
- The same mode labels appear on New Session's permission picker (same component), so it changes too.
- Aligned the one other UI string that named the mode: Agents → Tools help now says "Full access" instead of "Full Access".
- The refresh-failed message no longer includes the raw list-refresh error, per the approved copy; the call no longer passes it.
- Docs that quote the UI labels now use the new names (permission modes, tool policy, troubleshooting, sessions/sidebar, panels, dashboards). `docs/gateway/permission-modes.md` gains a "Control UI label" column mapping each config value to its new name.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI (control-ui-e2e harness, synthetic session, light theme), agent default mode `guarded`, before = current `main`:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menu | ![Permission menu before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7985228-6124-48b2-a374-08536262b7ff) | ![Permission menu after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/377de0ab-2cdc-4474-9fe8-8c594129a7e2) |

title: improve(ui): name the effort and speed controls consistently

## What Problem This Solves

The composer's effort and speed controls used several names for the same two settings ("Chat thinking level", "Thinking", "Effort"; "Fast mode", "Fast Mode", "Fast responses", "Speed"), and the tier/speed availability messages read like internal status ("Fast requested, currently served as default").

title: improve(ui): clarify composer action copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer's action copy (context ring, Compact, mic, send, Stop, and the Goal entry hint) used internal or wordy phrasing ("Open context usage details", "Replaces older context", "Tap to talk", "Hold to start dictation", "Write a message to send."), and the Stop button had two names ("Stop" visibly, "Stop generating" for screen readers).

## User Impact

User impact: the composer controls use short, plain chat language. The context ring tooltip now shows how full the context is at a glance, and Stop has a single name with its Esc shortcut in the tooltip.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context ring tooltip | Open context usage details | Context: {pct}% used |
| Compact button tooltip | Replaces older context with a summary. | Summarizes older messages to free up space. |
| Compact tooltip during a reply | Available when the current run finishes. | Available after this reply finishes. |
| Mic tooltip | Tap to talk · Hold to start dictation | Tap for voice chat · Hold to dictate |
| Mic menu toggle | Hold to start dictation | Hold to dictate |
| Settings › Appearance toggle | Hold microphone button to start dictation | Hold the mic button to dictate |
| Composer Stop button (accessible name / tooltip) | Stop generating / Stop | Stop / Stop (Esc) |
| Send button with an empty draft | Write a message to send. | Type a message first. |
| Goal entry hint | Enter your objective. | Describe what “done” looks like. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Approved copy pass for the composer actions area (one PR per composer area). Only English source strings and two small display tweaks change:

- The context ring tooltip uses a new `contextUsage.percentUsed` string with the same percent the ring's accessible summary already computes (including the `~` for approximate counts); the unused `contextUsage.open` string is removed. When only plan usage is shown (no context percent), the tooltip falls back to the existing accessible summary. The ring is a native disclosure, so assistive tech still announces that it expands.
- The composer Stop button's accessible name is now `Stop` and its tooltip uses the existing `Stop (Esc)` string (Esc already stops the reply). `Cancel reply` is untouched because it cancels a reply-to quote, not the agent's reply.

Known gaps: the subagent pane header/notice Stop buttons and the mobile header menu item still say "Stop generating"; they stop a child run from a different surface and were left for a separate decision. It can’t be turned on for a single chat. | | `menu.webSearchClearStaleEnable` | Web search is disabled in config. Click to clear this session’s enable override. | Web search is off in Gateway config. Click to remove this chat’s override. | | `menu.scopeSessionHint` | The server is saved globally disabled and enabled only for this session. | Saved for all chats, but on only in this one. | | `menu.scopeEverywhereHint` | The server is saved and enabled for every session. | Saved and on in every chat. | | `menu.depsMissing` | deps missing | Missing dependencies | | `menu.skillBlocked` | not available for this agent | Not available for this agent | Unchanged on purpose: the "Add attachment" trigger tooltip, the upload labels (Add attachment… / Photo / Media / File), the "Reset" action label, the "Plugins" section, and the MCP empty state. `depsMissing` and `skillBlocked` are standalone tooltips on skill rows, so they read correctly in sentence case. title: improve(ui): simplify model picker copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer model picker used long, technical wording ("session", "compacted", "centrally configures", "Chat only") that does not match the rest of the composer, which talks about chats.

## User Impact

User impact: model picker hints, the switch confirmation, the no-tools badge, and the admin-restricted note are shorter and use plain language. Behavior, settings, and config values are unchanged.

| Key (`chat.modelControls.*`) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selectionScopeSession` | Selecting a model changes only this session. | Applies to this chat only. |
| `selectionScopeAgent` | Selecting a model updates this agent's default. | Changes the default for this agent. |
| `selectionScopeGlobal` | Selecting a model updates the global default. | Changes the default for all agents. |
| `switchWarning` | This conversation is cached for {current}. Switching models means it reprocesses the whole conversation on your next message, which can spend more tokens. Longer conversations may also be compacted. | Switching re-sends the whole conversation to {new} with your next message, which uses more tokens. Long conversations may be summarized. |
| `chatOnly` | Chat only | No tools |
| `chatOnlyHelp` | This model can chat, but it cannot use tools. Choose another model for files, commands, web, or media tasks. | This model can't read files, run commands, or browse. Pick another model for that. |
| `restrictedModelsHelp` | Your administrator centrally configures the models available here. | Your admin chooses which models are available. |

Unchanged on purpose: route labels and details (Claude CLI · native, API · OpenClaw, completion routes), `claudeCliNotReady`, decision-model strings, and the effort/speed strings (separate PR).

Translations whose source text changed are dropped by hash and fall back to English until the post-merge locale refresh, so no locale shows a raw `{new}` or `{current}` placeholder.

The selection-scope strings are aria-only: they are appended to the model trigger's accessible name, for example `Chat model: Demo model A. Applies to this chat only.`. There is no visible surface to screenshot for them.

title: fix(workers): allow cloud dispatch to finish after node enrollment
body:
Related: #188796, #159178, #135838.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud-worker dispatch failing immediately after a new node connects when the provider rechecks its live provisioning authority.

## User Impact

Providers can continue setup after their own authenticated node enrollment without mistaking that progress for a replacement owner. Changed operations, epochs, enrolled nodes, setup bindings, resource receipts, caller authority, cancellation, and destroy intent remain fenced. No configuration, SDK, schema, retention, or durability migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provisioning previously reused teardown’s exact-node comparison against a snapshot captured before enrollment. The existing lifecycle owner now distinguishes the still-live provisioning operation from an already-fixed teardown identity and retains the first admitted node binding. Teardown’s exact predicate is unchanged.

The broader open authority work in #159178/#135838 already identifies this distinction. This narrow prerequisite does not import or supersede its V1 SDK rollout or remaining acceptance gates.

## Evidence

- The real enrollment regression fails on base `d9627ecb437b2a0fdaa2215137b291dbbc806137` with the installed failure: `Worker provider operation failed: Worker environment owner changed during teardown`. Both cases reach actual bootstrap token verification/consumption and immutable pairing publication before calling the public provider callback.
- Final candidate `9693b20c7d320d3a0448655914299b181cb1f34a`: **85 tests passed across six owner/sibling files**, including cancellation, replay, confirmed cleanup, generic provisioning, and project preparation. Vitest 74.54 seconds; wrapper 76.59 seconds, including cold compiled-worker preparation. The changed file’s preceding behavior-equivalent standalone run passed 13 cases in 11.78 seconds / 13.45 seconds wrapper; hosted per-file CI cost is not yet available.
- Core production and Gateway consumer-test types, four-file scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, test-line/line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety/database-worker ratchets passed. No baseline exception; test allocation records the 141-line real-boundary regression growth.

Unchanged credential-broker source was policy-blocked; complete callers established it is not needed for this provision-attempt assertion, distinct from unchanged completion admission.

- Published head `2787ffb77a8da26749bb9547880d4f7bdc061e93` preserves the exact qualified tree `cf979f696da04da7e6955b3c5012c96a1a989ad2`; the publisher added only an empty attribution commit atop the signed candidate. [Exact-head CI run 41420259186, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41420259186) **passed**, including the Actions CI gate and `security-fast`.

### Repaired installed acceptance and cleanup

[Package Acceptance 41422166087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41422166087), attempt 1, passed for the published head above. [Installed acceptance run 41430331976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41430331976), local attempt 7, returned controller/native/outer **exit 0 and PASS**. Its Actions workflow later shows cancelled because the retained Testbox was stopped after evidence collection; that is separate from the successful product proof.

- The exact repaired package was installed to an independent prefix. Installed CLI/SDK, managed Gateway process, serving build and pinned TLS matched; the image's preinstalled app was not the system under test.
- Four invalid capability profiles refused before provider allocation or agent turns. Authenticated first node enrollment then reached an active disk-authoritative worker placement.
- A real write-tool invocation produced **48 bytes** on the original worker resource (SHA-256 `00c83c1895290341ecfdd614ecf65f919529915b3f6038c827e019d087102056`). Durable transcript ACK reached **4** and terminal ACK **5**; claim, pending result and journal cleared. Repository/checkpoint and compute expiry stayed unchanged, demonstrating no published Gateway backup—not packet-level absence of transport.
- Public exact-source **Move** returned placement from generation **5 to 8**, exported workspace custody to Gateway and cleared disk authority. Original worker container and volume were absent afterward.
- Gateway and inference processes joined. Outer container, runtime volume and network were absent; remaining native container/volume inventories were empty. **125 evidence files / 444,361 bytes** were retained and rehashed after cleanup.
- Initial normal stop exited **5** at the GitHub-settlement deadline and retained its claim/key. Independent inspection then confirmed complete remote settlement; the same supported owner finalized with **exit 0**. Fresh inspection confirmed completed/not-ready/no-host, complete remote settlement and generated-key-directory absence. Cleanup is complete.

### Final-effect authority qualification

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191006#issuecomment-6574148884) reported **no discrete patch defect**, but requested installed success and replacement-node/caller-revocation evidence before provider I/O. Both named observations are now qualified for this narrow repair.

A test-only overlay on the exact published production source ran the real bootstrap verification, token consumption and immutable pairing publication, then called the public authority callback immediately before an actual local filesystem write. The current enrolled owner wrote/read successfully; controlled replacement-node and revoked-caller observations both rejected **before the write**, with forbidden files absent; restored current authority wrote/read successfully. The service reached ready, closed its retained guard and completed teardown. **One selected test passed; 12 were skipped**, not counted as passes. The original run completed in 589.70 seconds (Vitest 567.78 seconds, selected case 1,045 ms), under its original 600-second bound, without replay. Production and installed-fixture bytes stayed unchanged.

The installed synthetic provider composes config-owner and core `assertCurrent` checks. Its Docker dispatch checks immediately before process spawn with no intervening await, then checks again after awaited completion. This connects the qualified callback rejection to that provider's final dispatch boundary; no production defect was identified.

**Limits:** replacement is a controlled live-owner read observation, not an actually paired replacement device. Negative effect proof uses real local filesystem I/O in a substituted provider, not a negative Docker/cloud run or a guarantee for providers that ignore the callback. Installed success uses a synthetic local provider and deterministic HTTP inference (two requests), not live cloud providers or paid-model correctness. Neither proof qualifies pause/resume/restart/cold boot, release/adoption or deployment. The earlier installed `8085604` failure and its missing callback-tuple/archive-size evidence remain historical failures; no old native payload was replayed. Broader SDK rollout requirements remain with their owning work.

title: fix: request sound for Control UI Web Push on macOS
body:
Supersedes #163601, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.
Related: #163544.

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Web Push banners can arrive silently in Safari on macOS even when the user has enabled notification sounds.

## User Impact

Attention notifications request sound, subject to the user's browser and macOS settings. Same-tag approval replacements retain `renotify: false` to avoid another alert.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service worker already calls `showNotification` with a title and body, but omits `silent`. [Apple's WWDC23 Safari guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10120/?time=884) documents that macOS defaults notification sound off and requires explicit `silent: false` to request sound; user notification settings remain authoritative. [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerRegistration/showNotification#silent) documents the device-default behavior when omitted and the separate `renotify` option for replacements.

Set that standard option at the existing presentation boundary. Inline the one-use title binding without changing its fallback, keeping production LOC flat. Extend the existing approval replacement regression instead of adding duplicate setup; test LOC also stays flat.

## Evidence

- Current main's worker at `6cdd495d50338f3e456dffd88f03e849e33b4a96` still omits `silent`; its bytes match the tested baseline `b2bf8e641ba4c1854cf7fc85729421be2b01d0da`.
- Crabbox / Blacksmith Testbox: `pnpm --dir ui test src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Red before: 1 failed / 31 passed, specifically because the worker's `showNotification` options lack `silent: false`. Green after: 32 passed; file duration 0.844s, including existing navigation, avatar, and quiet replacement coverage. [Remote run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41413998489).
- Touched-file `oxfmt --check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig ui/tsconfig.json ui/public/sw.js ui/src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts` pass; `git diff --check` passes. [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41414730516) on `5694606ed52293cfd6713f9505248cca480ae417`; workflow elapsed time was 8m14s (whole run). The aggregate required gate also passed.
- Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `b2bf8e641ba4c1854cf7fc85729421be2b01d0da`: scoped clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings. Simplification reviewed; production delta 0, test delta 0.

Proof limit: the regression executes the production service worker's push handler and checks the options passed to the browser API. It does not prove audible playback on macOS, sound-disabled settings, or Chromium behavior. The Safari repair is based on Apple's documented platform contract. The contributor's branch was read with `gh` only and was never checked out or run.

title: fix(ui): avoid typing stalls in software-rendered chat panes
body:

Related: #162324

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes typing stalls in large Control UI chat panes when Chromium uses software compositing.

## User Impact

Large software-rendered panes avoid the expensive outer superellipse clip. The pane keeps its radius, dimensions, overflow clipping, and layout; its corners become ordinary rounded corners on all platforms, including hardware-rendered browsers. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main (`6deb24aa46547acdcee93fcf0aaa8d381383d1c2`) still applies `corner-shape: superellipse(1.5)` to `.chat.chat` while `.chat` clips overflow. The actual chat view renders this class around the conversation and composer. The contributor's reversible real-page trace identifies this outer clip as the source of repeated pane-sized software repaints, rather than input-handler work. Switch only that declaration to `round`.

The existing curvature test now covers the outer pane in both supported and unsupported browsers, alongside all its existing surface checks. Production LOC is unchanged; the two-line test allocation covers the added table entry and fixture. Simplification retained just the one-line production fix, with its explanation here.

## Evidence

The extended `ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts` fails against unchanged main specifically because `.chat` computes `superellipse(1.5)` instead of circular corners: 1 failed, 2 passed, 2.56 seconds. With the one-line CSS repair: 3 passed, 1.53 seconds. The scaled 17.5px radius and unsupported-browser 14px radius remain intact, and other surfaces retain their curvature.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

This is their software-renderer evidence on 2026.9.7, not a newly measured current-main or physical-GPU benchmark. The computed-style regression verifies current main and the replacement; it does not measure repaint latency. Hardware-specific visual timing was not newly measured; geometry and all existing curvature cases pass. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Contributor source was read only through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; its branch was never checked out or executed. This replacement was implemented on main.

title: fix(gateway): warn when restart intent cleanup fails
body:
Supersedes #160805, thanks @changeroa.
Related: #153483

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent restart-intent cleanup failures when the Gateway state database refuses the deletion.

## User Impact

Operators see a `restart` warning with the storage error explaining why an intent remains. Cleanup stays best-effort so a persistence failure does not interrupt startup or service recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same logger and error context as the existing restart-intent write failure. A stale row does not schedule a restart: signal handling consumes it with a transactional delete, then checks the target PID and 60-second lifetime. No repeat-restart path was demonstrated, so adding a startup refusal would introduce an availability risk.

The production delta is +2 lines; there is no safe dead or duplicate code to remove from this owner without expanding this conservative restart-path fix. The +32 test lines and matching allocation cover the missing diagnostic, retained intent, and successful cleanup after recovery. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Evidence

title: feat(beam): allow owned publication by restricted guests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted Visitors can work in their own sessions but cannot send Beam snapshots without being granted the much broader `operator.write` permission.

## User Impact

A verified, currently invited guest can publish a Beam and refresh only the retained row they initially published. Publication does not grant catalog read, delete, or continuation access. Staff behavior remains unchanged. Guest success receipts retain version-1 compatibility and additionally return optional `canView: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One plugin-owned upload operation now serves staff and guests inside the existing shared-state worker. It replaces the host observe/CAS retry loop; there is no new SQL schema/version, SDK surface, configuration, shared token, or broad operator grant.
- The immutable initial publisher profile is separate from mutable uploader attribution. Legacy live ownerless rows are not claimable, even when their uploader matches.
- Ownership and creation quotas are checked atomically: 20 unexpired rows per publisher for guest creation; no guest creation at the shared 500-row cap and no guest eviction. Owned refresh remains allowed at either cap; staff oldest-entry eviction remains unchanged.
- The original profile/Visitor authority is captured before awaits and retained through worker transaction and commit admission. Accepted-write settlement stays with the state owner: an authorized commit is not undone or replayed after later closure/revocation. A later HTTP response retains its own live-authority check.

Vincent K, verified as an active OpenClaw organization administrator, accepted this scoped ownership/permission/bounded-quota design in the maintainer task discussion on November 2, 2026. The complete initial patch and existing SDK admission/TTL contract were inspected during the task before initial draft publication; the PR was subsequently marked ready so exact-head CI could run. Both exact patches were inspected during the task. The separately reviewed six-file CI repair and subsequent proven type-only lint repair were accepted for publication. This is not a merge-green claim. Welcome/localization, Beam welcome guidance, and notification groups remain HELD and untouched.

No backfill is performed. Rollback to an older receiver restores staff-only uploads; an accepted replacement by that older receiver may strip the ownership field. After re-upgrade, the resulting ownerless row remains unavailable for guest refresh until deletion/expiry permits creation. Namespace, seven-day retention, timestamp/completion ordering, and staff retention are unchanged. These limits are documented in the Beam guide.

## Evidence

- Actual isolated Gateway HTTP with durable synthetic profiles, restricted roles, real VisitorAccessService, and the real state worker: original guest upload `403`; candidate `200` with `canView: false`. Unauthenticated, read-only, uninvited, foreign, legacy-ownerless, and forged-owner requests refused.
- Actual HTTP races: 21 concurrent same-publisher creations produced 20 successes and one quota refusal; competing same-ID publishers produced one success and one forbidden response; racing the last shared slot produced one success and one cap refusal. Guest refusal did not evict; owned refresh and staff oldest-entry eviction worked at capacity.
- Actual revoke/reinvite and expiry during awaited upload produced no successful acknowledgment and no persisted row under the original capture. A fresh invitation could publish. Aborted local transports surfaced as egress-proxy 502, so this is safety evidence, not qualification of a stable denial status.
- SDK operation suite: **17/17 passed**, including transaction/commit authority rollback, accepted settlement after closure, and lost-ack non-replay.
- Initial targeted Beam production and test-consumer typechecks passed together (29.3 seconds). Formatting and patch whitespace checks passed.
- Two independent initial P0–P2 reviews found no actionable findings. A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the six-file CI repair also found no actionable findings. Both exact patches were inspected during the task.

### CI-discovered consumer repair

Initial non-draft CI run [41399614386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41399614386) exposed three actual failures, not environmental verdicts: extension lint, the real HTTP identity consumer bypassing plugin operation-module capture, and the new guest store suite missing the real host-broker test project. The follow-up uses the operation-aware plugin loader, awaits resource cleanup, routes the guest suite through the existing database-worker project, fixes the reported lint diagnostics, and adds read-only HTTP denials with unchanged persisted transcript assertions.

- The original HTTP identity entry point reproduced red locally with the same Internal-error response as CI.
- The same repaired HTTP consumer plus guest-worker and HTTP-authority suites passed **7/7**, cold wall **78.4 seconds** (worker preparation 39.956 seconds). The consumer proves real HTTP profile isolation, read-only `403` without transcript replacement, close/reopen persistence, and staff/shared-token behavior.
- Completed CI run [41408391127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41408391127), on head `a3ffdd5623215e841fb016d10f2c4a7dccbf1958`, passed all Node test and production/test typecheck jobs. It retained one PR-caused extension lint error: the fixture's generic entries method lacked the SDK return contract. The method now explicitly returns SDK-owned `PluginStateEntry<T>[]`, matching `PluginStateOperationTransaction.entries`, with no executable behavior change or new casts/suppressions.
- In an independently qualified native PR checkout, the unchanged prior head reproduced that exact lint error. Applying the exact accepted two-file patch made `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/beam/src/beam-store.test-support.ts && git diff --check` pass, exit 0: `[plugin-sdk boundary dts] fresh; skipping` and `No problems in 1 file [3.61s]`. That temporary proof patch was then reversed, leaving the native checkout clean. This is scoped lint proof, not a full local build verdict.
- The same completed CI run also failed the global extension-test boundary because `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` imports a Baseten runtime file. The parent investigation compared the actual CI merge checkout with its ordered main parent and found both that Baseten file and the boundary guard unchanged; this is separately attributed inherited evidence, not a reason to ignore PR-caused lint.
- Net regression growth is now **142 lines**, with an exact named allocation. Source updates address observed defects; no check was dispatched/rerun or branch re-pushed merely to obtain green.

### Completed prior-head CI and recovery guidance

- CI run [41410742762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41410742762) completed **SUCCESS** for head `d6e65048363771b8fbe4d7eb5b44cba5a04ade42`. The fresh ClawSweeper review of that head judged overall correctness correct, proof sufficient, and security findings **None**. Its only finding was P3 recovery guidance for an ownership refusal.
- That P3 is addressed by explaining the existing options in the `403` response: publish a new source session with a new Beam ID, or ask a Gateway operator whether the retained snapshot can be removed. The guest HTTP regression checks the foreign-publisher refusal and the new Beam ID guidance. It failed red with the old copy in **37ms**, then passed with the new copy in **24ms**. Canonical formatting, the two-file lint check (**3.93s**), and patch whitespace checks passed in the qualified checkout.
- The subsequent three-file patch changes only that human-facing refusal text, its regression, and the allocation. Authority, status, storage, quotas, ordering, and TTL are unchanged. Earlier HTTP and released-state compatibility evidence covers those unchanged boundaries through D6; it is not a claim that every production byte is identical on the subsequent head.
- New-head CI run [41414124249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41414124249) is pending for `3415e3af6c0453098a54d8e6f27ba276e9cbf5a1`, not yet green.

### Investigated local oversized-request timeout

The original declared-oversized request socket-close case timed out at **120 seconds**; that failure evidence is retained, not replaced by a passing retry. The qualified checkout reproduced it in the complete, identically ordered 15-test Beam receiver file with the accepted three-file candidate: **14 passed, 1 failed, 130.43s wall**. The observed environment had Node 26 `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, HTTP/HTTPS proxies present, and neither `NO_PROXY` nor `no_proxy` included loopback.

The controlled comparison changed **only the test invocation environment**: preserve every existing bypass value and append `127.0.0.1,localhost` to both `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy`. With **identical source and full test order**, all **15/15 passed**, **10.46s warm wrapper wall**, **8.75s Vitest**, and the oversized body-close case took **8ms**. This includes ordinary staff HTTP and the complete Beam receiver flows. It qualifies the fixture's loopback transport; there is no product body-close fix, global proxy disabling, timeout increase, skipped/weakened assertion, or claim that repetition fixed the original failure. CI per-file execution cost is unavailable.

### Historical sanitized real HTTP and persisted-state excerpt

This is the retained prior capture from the isolated synthetic Gateway/Visitor/worker harness after the test-only repair, before the subsequent human-facing ownership-refusal text change. The old refusal text below is historical, not the current full response. No real conversations, provider credentials, external Cloudflare login, private addresses, or live Gateway configuration were used. Each STATE line is a fresh real keyed-store lookup at that checkpoint. The revoked-request lookup is **before** the fresh invitation publishes that ID.

~~~text
HTTP unauthenticated 401
HTTP reader 403
HTTP uninvited 403
HTTP guest-A 200 {"canView":false,"ok":true,"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
STATE guest-accepted {"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","publisher":"guest-A","uploader":"guest-A","completed":false,"fixtureTextPreserved":true}
HTTP guest-B 403 {"ok":false,"error":"Beam is not owned by this publisher"}
STATE after-foreign-denial {"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","publisher":"guest-A","uploader":"guest-A","completed":false,"fixtureTextPreserved":true}
HTTP guest-A 502 [local transport after revoked authority]
STATE captured-revoked-request-not-persisted null
HTTP guest-A 200 [fresh invitation, new authority]
HTTP guest-A 502 [local transport after expired authority]
STATE expired-request-not-persisted null
PASS catalog method authority gates, staff read/copy, revocation+reinvite and expiry while upload awaited
PASS real Gateway HTTP trusted-proxy auth + durable profiles + current Visitor policy + worker upload
~~~

Actor names are synthetic labels; successful receipt URLs and repetitive fields were omitted. The 502 observations establish neither a stable denial status nor successful delivery; the independent persisted-state lookups establish no unauthorized write.

### Remaining gates — explicitly not green

- **Newest exact-head CI remains required.** Prior-head D6 CI passed; current `3415e3a` CI is pending as recorded above. The scoped lint commands passed in the qualified checkout. The source checkout's old artifact lock remains preserved; other local checks stopped by that fence are not retroactively qualified. Earlier default Bun-backed lint had timed out without a diagnostic verdict.
- Full `pnpm build` was stopped after reaching tsdown-packages; full local build evidence is incomplete.
- **Released-state component compatibility passed; full Gateway update remains unqualified.** Published stable `2026.10.9 (8b18b55)` actually produced retained disk state. Candidate `67fe909` (production bytes unchanged by the test-only repairs through `d6e6504`; the subsequent patch changes only human-facing ownership-refusal text) consumed that same disk through the real async plugin loader, host broker/worker, and HTTP handler after canonical Doctor maintenance migrated schema **20→39** with full and scoped backups. Synthetic transport authority was used; no publisher was seeded. Staff catalog/transcript read, guest `POST /api/v1/beam/sessions` **403** even matching the legacy uploader, fresh unchanged row JSON+metadata, preserved settings, and independent-process cold read passed; the original backup inventory stayed intact. This does not qualify full Doctor health or live Visitor authentication.
  - In the owned isolated environment, the command prefix was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`. Case `extensions/beam/src/released-state.doctor.test.ts` passed **1/1, exit 0**. Case `extensions/beam/src/released-state.compat.test.ts` passed **1/1, exit 0** separately with `BEAM_PROOF_STAGE=candidate-postmigration` and `BEAM_PROOF_STAGE=postmigration-cold-read`.
  - Actual sanitized stdout from the migration case:

    ~~~text
    CANONICAL_DOCTOR_RECEIPT {"previousSchema":20,"newSchema":39,"backups":2,"rowUnchanged":true,"settingsSemanticsPreserved":true,"configBytesChanged":false}
    ~~~
- Personal external Cloudflare login and full RPC/UI continuation remain unqualified. Guest expired-row recreation/quota expiry remains a named boundary: the host fake clock tests authority expiry, not transactional worker TTL. No unsupported clock seam, new timers or fixtures were added.
- Local proof used synthetic data only. A clean CI install remains necessary for broad qualification; the local dependency copy differs only in unrelated tokenjuice/optional metadata, and no dependency files changed.

The PR is ready for CI, **not claimed merge-green on the newest head**. No deployment or live credential/configuration change was performed. The parent maintainer owns native workflow and landing; this child does not merge.

title: fix(ui): make workspace repositories easier to find
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Saved repositories are difficult to distinguish and find in the workspace picker, particularly when several repositories share a short name and for session-only connections.

## User Impact

Users can search organization/repository identities of projects they can already discover. Lists with six or more saved/recent entries expose search automatically; the header stays available while the inventory scrolls. Selection shows repository identity in the workspace chip.

This is read-safe display metadata only: no additional discovery, private-content, cloning, remote-search, publication or other permissions. Origin URLs, credentials, checkout paths and observed placement stay outside session-only responses.

## Implementation

The Gateway projects optional `repositoryIdentity` from the raw stored origin through the canonical configured-host Git URL parser. The UI consumes that authoritative projection instead of parsing unavailable origins. Unsupported origins retain display names. UI and Gateway ship together; no older-Gateway fallback is added.

Automatic search returns after passive empty dismissal, respecting explicit collapse. Only the picker opts into row typing to an already-visible search; shared selects retain list typeahead. The existing composer autotype exemption prevents capture stealing row typing. Existing layout CSS keeps search outside the scrolling inventory; superseded sticky CSS is removed without a budget increase. The identity regression uses the canonical RPC invocation helper, not an incomplete cast.

## Reviewed Source and Verification

Reviewed head: `d96b69052ac265fc2a1a980a81a68eab30ecf1ce`. The full initial source and exact six-file follow-up received source inspection and fresh independent bounded review, with no actionable findings.

- [Exact-head CI 41424200536](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41424200536) completed **successfully**, including UI, browser, type/lint/security and performance gates. No rerun or unchanged push was used to obtain green.
- Three-file UI order: **14/14**, 3.25s Vitest / 4.42s wrapper. The composer-capture regression failed before repair and passed afterward.
- Existing shared-select browser suite: **26/26**, retaining its large-catalog keyboard-position assertion.
- Real UI source with mocked Gateway I/O: **Chromium 4/4** (22.86s), **WebKit 4/4** (26.46s), guest/maintainer at 1280/390px. Covers automatic search, dismissal/reopen, explicit collapse, row typing/focus, fixed search, filtering, retained query/clear and selection.
- Updated identity case: **1/1**, 11ms assertion / 59.95s cold wrapper. UI production and Gateway-method test types, canonical scoped lint, styles, i18n, controller guard, formatting, LF ratchet and whitespace checks passed. An existing native-listener reactivity warning was not suppressed.
- Exact allocation: **128 net LF**, without raising shared ceilings. Protocol/validator/native outputs were generated through their owners, not hand-edited.
- Prior-head CI genuinely ran project-list tests: **30 Node + 30 Bun**, including read-safe identity, write-only checkout details and origin redaction; focused identity also passed both. This is handler proof for unchanged Gateway production inputs, not a new router-admission/revocation claim.
- Full `pnpm build` at this head passed in **5m07s** (build owner 5m02.8s).
- Canonical `ui:check-performance:base 7ce05f41e0a69f01503788eb1dbc2b1476e638fa` passed in **56.638s**: CSS raw/gzip zero growth, chat-boot gzip +462B and New Session +410B below fixed ceilings, startup -4B and request counts unchanged. That owner controls build identity/release flags; its outputs differ from the standard build.
- **Standard absolute-budget probe did not pass:** CSS gzip 309591 > 309366, CSS raw 1601636 > 1599319, chat-boot gzip 1278560 > 1277887. Absolute compliance is not claimed; the canonical relative gate and actual CI passed. No cap/baseline increase, timeout increase, skip or assertion weakening was used.

## Investigated Historical Failures

[CI 41399977882](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41399977882) failed on prior `74177299`. The follow-up repairs source-attributed shared-select typeahead, invalid invocation fixture and incremental CSS growth; current-head CI/build/relative performance evidence is separate from the failures below.

Two old E2E causes remain **unresolved**: moved-authority URL waiting in `chat-snapshot-route.e2e.test.ts` and one WebKit390 upward-reading residual of 1,238px. Neither is labeled infrastructure, proven pre-existing or fixed. The pane's `--visible` class is valid; main's later canonical-path/active-pane fixture alignment is not established as this timeout's repair.

Bundled probes preserved per-file case order: candidate **13/13** (52.40s), diagnostic candidate **13/13** (50.69s), exact original base `afbe0a8` **13/13** (62.99s). These establish **non-reproduction, not fixes**. Local Node26/single-worker differs from CI Node24/four workers. Retained CI artifacts lack failing-frame geometry to distinguish painted displacement from offscreen overscan selection or sampling/correction ordering. Temporary diagnostics were restored; no speculative chat repair was added.

The earlier catalog-header run (13 passed / 1 failed) is also unexplained. Original-order/cold passing probes do not establish its cause or repair. Earlier 19-test results are prior-revision only. Compilation/bootstrap timeouts were setup evidence, not product assertions or green tests. These investigations remain recorded despite the later successful current-head CI.

## Visual Evidence

[Inspected synthetic before/after images and interaction limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190911#issuecomment-6570666640).
