title: fix(auth): ignore invalid credential symlink targets
body:
Supersedes #151739, thanks @Alix-007.

## What Problem This Solves

External JSON credential discovery aborts when a credential symlink points beneath a regular file.

## User Impact

Invalid legacy credential targets are skipped so discovery can continue, and readable credentials keep their existing selection behavior. Other path-resolution errors still propagate. No operator action or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add ENOTDIR to the shared optional JSON reader’s existing absent classification alongside ENOENT and ELOOP. JSON reading/parsing and credential precedence remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main production code: [baseline CI, changed tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41392280456/job/125106480898), head `3dcb6ef`. Both the filesystem-reader regression and actual Gemini credential discovery fail with ENOTDIR. EACCES, EISDIR and EPERM controls pass; existing malformed-JSON and directory-read tests also pass. Current main’s reader blob was verified identical to the baseline.
- All final-head [PR CI checks passed at `c1af21e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41393168474). [Credential discovery: 18/18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41393168474/job/125109254514); [JSON reader: 14/14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41393168474/job/125109254557). The discovery regression also verifies that replacing the invalid target with a valid credential symlink selects the expected credential.
- Autoreview, full range `88177be..c1af21e`, P0–P3, with complete producer, caller and test source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The initial error assertion was strengthened to check the propagated code; error object identity is outside the caller contract.
- Final CI cost: credential file 1.03s test-run duration / 2.52s wrapper wall; JSON file 0.939s / 2.41s. Baseline costs were 1.09s / 2.07s and 0.949s / 2.46s, respectively.
- Simplification: one shared absent check, no caller catches or new policy owner. Production +1/−1 (net 0); 43 added test lines cover the kernel error, retained errors and discovery/selection boundary, with a scoped 43-line allocation.
- No tests, containers, or repo-wide checks ran on the production Team host. The native wrapper prepared its managed dependency cache after IO gate admission. Crabbox setup did not reach tests; the owned Testbox was stopped. Broad proof is PR CI. Contributor source was read with gh only and was never checked out or executed.

title: fix: await Doctor shared-state repair preparation
body:
Doctor could still synchronously prepare shared-state snapshots and credential-generation observations while opening or repairing state. This change retains the existing maintenance owner through awaited preparation, then applies the same synchronous native mutation phases with current authority checks.

Credential custody and initial source/companion observations are prepared before shared writes; postimages are awaited after native commit. Corrupt-index and orphan-delivery preservation finishes before the repair transaction; deletion still verifies current rows against the preserved payload. Direct callers of the preserving-backup owner now await it outside their write transactions. Released synchronous SDK repair and native startup contracts remain available through the same kernels.

Validation:
- Prior prepared head `8bcbab54`: the public schema-preparation regression failed on main with four synchronous snapshot children, then passed on the repair. AZ ran 56 named files / 922 tests under explicit Node timeouts; scoped formatting/lint passed and six-pass canonical autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This is prior-head supporting evidence.
- Merged current main `68e6772d` cleanly into the existing branch as `51f973de992b9ca80f11b1f010e2d0533406e01a`. No conflicts or manual source edits; the authored PR diff remains exactly 69 files, 3,511 additions and 1,300 deletions.
- The separate compiler-policy prerequisite is merged in #191447 as `f5861171a2961d2105c2565affd506de19d16c55` and is included in this head. Its exact-head CI and real-child regression passed.
- Fresh integration benchmark proof: [job 125556848070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526574447/job/125556848070) passed all 7 tests in `bench-sqlite-reliability.test.ts`, including the previously failing snapshot-reliability case (55.424 seconds).
- The completed [PostgreSQL open-path lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526574447/job/125556845766) passed both new cases: unchanged warm/cold anchor discovery (6.751 seconds) and cancellation cleanup of an unpublished writer (10.737 seconds). All three PostgreSQL lanes passed.
- The [Doctor process job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526574447/job/125556848705) passed both previous deadline cases on this head: cron repair/readiness 39.383 seconds overall; historical-agent ordering 74.841 seconds overall. Existing child deadlines are unchanged. No rerun was used, and these passes do not attribute the old-head timeout.
- [Fresh exact-head CI 41526574447](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526574447) passed on `51f973de`, attempt 1: 122 jobs (96 successful, 26 skipped), all 202 check runs complete without failure, and all aggregate/security statuses successful. Fresh canonical complete-range autoreview on `68e6772d..51f973de` completed **scoped-clean** in all eight passes, with no actionable P0–P2 findings and final immutable-source verification passing. No CI rerun or timeout change was made.

Previous head `8bcbab54` failed [CI 41510282601](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41510282601) in the nested SQLite reliability worker and two Doctor process deadlines. The compiler-policy defect was fixed separately above. All three PostgreSQL jobs on that old head passed, including new shared-state opening/cancellation cases. The historical-agent order deadline matches main; the cron 30-second child deadline did not have matching inspected main CI evidence, although the exact case passed on both head and main in AZ's isolated Testbox. Neither deadline failure recurred on the current head; no rerun was needed.

Latest-stable installation and native macOS/Windows qualification remain unrun. This is **not yet released**.

Related: #178359, #187900. Supersedes the remaining repair scope of #191054 after landing.

title: fix: cancel Doctor cron and daemon snapshot preparation
body:
Doctor Cron inventory blocked task cancellation during a nested SQLite snapshot copy. Daemon runtime-pin migration also prepared its local target inside the shared-source transaction.

Await the copy under the command/task signal and join child and temporary-output cleanup. Prepare the daemon target before the source transaction and retain both native owners through generation observations. Native writes remain synchronous; target copies commit before source retirement, and completion receipts follow source commit. Exact values, timestamps, conflict refusal and retry behavior remain intact.

Validation:

- Main reaches the held Cron copy but times out on cancellation at 20 seconds. The fix passes in 3.46 seconds, proving child/snapshot cleanup and unchanged source bytes.
- The public daemon capture regression fails on main with four synchronous reader calls and passes with zero. Interrupted retirement and SIGKILL recovery pass.
- Sixteen named owner/consumer files pass 270 tests with one platform ACL skip, including the affected existing state-migration files. Scoped format/lint/diff checks pass on seven TypeScript files. Canonical independent P0–P2 autoreview is clean across the complete eight-file patch.

Test allocation: 126 net lines; scalar unchanged. No configuration or schema version change. Native macOS/Windows large-family and latest-stable installation qualification remain unrun. Fully green exact-head PR CI is required before landing.

Related: #178359, #187900, #185879. The preceding three split stages are landed. **Not yet released.**

Thanks to [chrislro's reported stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639).

title: fix: await native credential migration observations
body:
Doctor's native credential imports and identity repair synchronously inspect database generations around native writes. These reads can block signal handling even though the caller is asynchronous.

Await those observations outside transactions while retaining the existing native custody. One generator supplies the native transaction/admission policy to the synchronous SDK driver and the awaited Doctor adapter. Device auth and identity import/repair consume that adapter. Main's companion/PostgreSQL migration contract is preserved; unused later-stage preparation and inherited CI/process/backup changes are removed. The wrapper inventory includes the seven direct dependencies introduced by the awaited reader import.

Validation: the stable Doctor token-import entry point fails on main with three synchronous generation-reader calls and passes with this change, preserving token and source bytes. Four named credential owner files pass (61 tests, four PostgreSQL-only skips locally), including public capture/Doctor/rollback, cancellation and authority loss. Six existing affected state-migration files pass (95 tests across two shards,55.16s). Scoped format/lint/diff checks pass on all12 changed TypeScript files. Exact-head PR CI is required before landing. Explicit Node replay of the same ten named files also passes (156 tests, four PostgreSQL-only skips,226.02s). The existing wrapper source-closure tests pass4/4, and its focused eager inventory contract passes1/1. Canonical independent P0–P2 autoreview is clean across all production/test changes and the seven required wrapper source-inventory records. Test allocation151LF; no scalar change.

Native macOS large-family/latest-stable installation qualification is not claimed by local focused tests; broad and PostgreSQL execution belongs to exact-head PR CI on this production Team host. No Gateway or live state operation is part of this PR.

Related: #178359, #187900, #185879. Preceding split stages #190870 and #190872 are landed. **Not yet released.**

Thanks to [chrislro's reported stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639).

title: fix: await Doctor process and restart lease inspection
body:
Related: #178359, #187900.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor and service inspection can block cancellation while synchronously preparing Gateway process and restart lease observations. Awaited maintenance inspection also needs to follow a legitimately replaced state file rather than a retained admission's old inode.

## User Impact

Process and restart observations await the existing read owner and cleanup. Offline maintenance can inspect the current physical state file after restoration or a database port. Native process signals, service actions and restart-intent writes still require current caller authority and captured process identity. This is the second split stage of the Doctor repair. Not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the canonical awaited snapshot/read transport for Promise-only lease inspection. Descriptive reads use the existing independent warm-source path when the retained writer's physical identity still matches, preserving native-transaction refusal and original-source fallback for replaced paths. Maintenance snapshot admission captures the current physical file under acquired custody while retaining caller admission, cancellation and custody checks after awaits.

Await direct service callers, preserve synchronous native-supervisor callbacks, and share the stale-process cleanup policy between async and native drivers. Restart-intent writes inspect their admitted transaction. Preserve main's live-Gateway copy exclusion.

The 37-file diff contains process/restart inspection, direct callers/tests and allocation records. Inherited backup implementation, auxiliary snapshot, schema, CI prerequisite and temporary diagnostic changes are removed. Previous stage #190870 is landed; #190873–#190875 remain separate. No stack branch was merged into another.

## Evidence

- Current lease and warm-source suites: 50 passed, one skipped, 55.72 seconds under a 180-second timeout. New real Gateway-lock regression reproduces the PG restore identity error on parent32cbe6, then passes with the fix; a retained live original is replaced by dead-owner state and maintenance preserves the replacement bytes.
- All 16 affected state-migrations files passed 370 tests on this head in 276.78 seconds under a 420-second timeout. The original seven include shared-auth/caller-mode/retained-agent and runtime-pin migration, including SIGKILL recovery; nine direct owner consumers cover audit logs, APNs, device identity, exec approvals, lock, MCP OAuth, meeting transcripts, node host and Web Push.
- Full canonical independent Codex P0–P2 review was scoped-clean for the complete process patch. Fresh review of the physical-identity delta and complete determining owners is also scoped-clean. Test allocation is 193 net LF (175 plus 18 for the real regression), shared scalar unchanged. Scoped format/oxlint and diff check pass.
- Prior unchanged process/PID/restart and daemon/CLI consumer evidence is retained; broad current-head proof belongs to CI.

Parent32cbe6 CI41472933181 proved both real Bun restart cases (972ms/625ms), all three serialized lifecycle cases and the complete 166-test CLI group. Its sole product failure was PG backup restore at lease admission: a new physical file was compared with the retained old inode. Recent main41465453264/job125345759351 passed that exact restore case, so no flake exception or failed-job rerun is used. This candidate fixes the lease owner and its regression; restore implementation is unchanged. New exact-head CI must be fully green before landing.

Local full update integration was stopped when canonical preflight unexpectedly started a prohibited runtime build; no local pass claimed. That consumer stays in PR CI under production-host restrictions. Native-platform/latest-stable upgrade qualification remains unrun. Immediate-slot Testbox requests queued and were stopped; no running production Gateway or operator state is used.

Current exact-head CI: [223e606ca3a7b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41478382024).

title: improve(test): reuse workflow successor fixtures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workflow successor tests rebuild the same signed Git fixture for 18 ordinary cases.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All 74 cases remain; the single-file Vitest median falls from **519.900s to 475.320s**, saving **44.580s (8.57%)** in three baseline and three candidate Testbox runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `reuseBaselineFixture` helper for the first describe, with separate ordinary and baseline variants. Each variant restores its entire private root at its original absolute path. Captured JavaScript state stays read-only and cases remain serial. This removes 17 repeated ordinary-fixture constructions without a new cache/helper or production change.

Every case, assertion, negative control, signed-commit check, hosted-ancestry check, and native workflow transition remains. All source from `expectExit` through the case bodies is byte-identical to baseline. The 55-case `proofFixture` group remains fresh because its captured review object is mutable.

The diff is one test file: +7/-3, **net +4 test lines**. Those four lines select the two existing restorers; no cases or assertions were added.

## Evidence

```sh

The probe passed and its additions were removed before mutation proof.

The same four mutations to the remote `scripts/pr` source copy ran on the original baseline test bytes and the exact timed candidate bytes. title: fix: await Doctor session and shared-auth inspection
body:
Related: #178359, #187900.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can block cancellation while preparing private session and shared-auth database inspection images.

## User Impact

These session and shared-auth readers await preparation and cleanup while preserving source files and current repair ownership. This is one stage of the Doctor cancellation repair; it does not claim to resolve every Doctor hang. Not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move private preparation to the existing async reader owners, await shared-auth migration detection and session recovery inventories at their callers, and retain synchronous native auth bootstrap. Recheck repair ownership after awaited reads before publishing credentials or retiring recovery artifacts.

Merged current main and removed the CI prerequisites already landed in #191050, along with unrelated backup/port, quarantine, generic snapshot and fixture changes. The remaining 37-file diff covers these readers and their direct consumers and tests. Later split stages remain #190872, #190873, #190874 and #190875.

## Evidence

- All six existing state-migrations files touching shared-auth passed: five unchanged files in the six-file run, plus 36/36 in the corrected shared-auth owner rerun (96.95 seconds including compiler preparation). The first combined run passed 147/148 tests; the sole failure was an assertion spanning the next stage’s gateway lease owner. title: fix: explain state lease renewal failures before expiry
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace operations can lose a state lease without showing whether renewal failed or remained pending.

## User Impact

Operators can identify a rejected renewal, an unsettled renewal, or no renewal since the last successful commit. Lease durations, retries, authority checks, and write settlement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing parent timer records renewal attempts, warns once for the first non-loss failure, and reports the accumulated count at close or expiry. Expiry warnings and the loss cause include the pending start time, the last failed attempt's error classification, or the age of the last successful commit. Logs contain scope/key and bounded error names/codes, including broker codes alongside native SQLite cause codes; error prose, stacks, and database paths are omitted.

The simplification pass consolidated repeated timer cleanup and kept the existing owner. Production grows by 44 net lines. The existing lifetime fixture gains 79 lines for five table cases, including the required mock-isolation explanation. These parent-timer outcomes previously had no coverage; one shared fixture and a separate 79-line allocation keep the regression growth contained without changing the shared scalar.

## Evidence

- **Red on base:** all five final cases fail against unchanged production source at `db41a6a3a2e44726c08e2ba64442c27f2fd45ae1`: rejected renewals make zero warning calls; pending/idle expiry reports only `state lease expired`. Complete log and test-only patch are retained in the reliability loop's R17 proof directory. Wall time: 32.77 seconds, 35.68 seconds through the wrapper.
- **Focused proof:** 28/28 tests pass in the lifetime and async timer files; 32.67 seconds, 34.81 seconds through the wrapper. Test bodies take under one second; worker preparation accounts for almost all wall time. Touched-file TypeScript, source/test lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Review:** independent Codex-backed autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean on the complete runtime candidate that became `af69caa177ad213ca452367d3d1fe083b6e1af65`. Final head `2ff247c121b31e06ee1202daa9a554133927a240` adds only the CI-required logger-isolation comment and its allocation. The actual owner scanner rejects that fixture without the comment and accepts it with the comment. No baseline or lint rule was weakened. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; its automatic hosted review already acknowledged the PR.
- **Broad proof:** [CI run 41391258427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41391258427), attached to final head `2ff247c121b31e06ee1202daa9a554133927a240`, passed. Its ratchets pass; the prior run's missing mock-isolation explanation was repaired.

No production Gateway/state was modified or fault-injected. A pending request identifies an unsettled actor operation, not the particular blocked actor phase.

title: fix(gateway): reject ambiguous capability-scoped request paths
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inconsistent Gateway routing when a capability-scoped URL's inner path begins with repeated slashes or backslashes: route checks can see `//example/__openclaw__/canvas/` while a handler reparsing `req.url` sees `/__openclaw__/canvas/`.

Supersedes #146923, thanks @arpe1618.

## User Impact

Malformed scoped requests now return HTTP 400 before capability route resolution or handler dispatch, for both HTTP and WebSocket upgrades. Valid scoped links still work; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject literal and percent-encoded leading separators in the existing shared normalizer before rewriting the request URL. Preserve the existing 401 response for unparseable unscoped targets. Replace redundant scoped-path state and an unreachable fallback while adding the guard, keeping production LOC unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41389176805) passed on `d56465b740e251a1f6c7a0025fd816299f601135`; 1,523 seconds elapsed CI wall time, including PostgreSQL conformance. All 61 PR checks passed, with no failures or pending checks.

- [Red baseline on Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41386845612): the two named files had 9 expected failures and 37 passes with unchanged main production code. A raw request with a live capability returned 200 with `routePath: "//example/__openclaw__/canvas/"` and `handlerPath: "/__openclaw__/canvas/"`, concretely demonstrating the disagreement. The affected production paths are identical between baseline `5396fbf92a3f91c6c994218cc51b983a1380db11` and fetched main `0405ef3527b9b5ec538e82a0b00fdfdf520fe8a9`.
- [Green focused proof on Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41387448666): `pnpm test src/gateway/plugin-node-capability.test.ts src/gateway/server.plugin-node-capability-auth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 46 passed, 37.13 seconds combined wall time. Raw HTTP and upgrade requests cover `//`, `%2F%2F`, backslashes, and encoded/mixed separators; the live-capability HTTP case verifies rejection before route resolution and a valid scoped link still returning 200.
- [Sibling legacy-listener proof on Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41388752279): `pnpm test src/gateway/server/plugin-legacy-listeners.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 12 passed, 34.55 seconds wall time. Confirms primary-listener 400 responses while preserving legacy-port acceptance and invalid-secret rejection. Cold worker transformation dominates both focused runs.
- Touched-file oxlint and oxfmt checks passed on the corresponding Testbox runs. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI; no suite, worker compilation, or dependency install ran on the production Team host.
- Final local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, baseline `5396fbf92a3f91c6c994218cc51b983a1380db11` through the final working-tree candidate committed as `d56465b740e251a1f6c7a0025fd816299f601135`): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Full normalizer, HTTP, upgrade, security-path, and integration-test context supplied. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; hosted ClawSweeper identified one stale legacy-listener expectation, addressed in `d56465b740e251a1f6c7a0025fd816299f601135` and covered by the clean final autoreview.
- Simplification: production +0 net lines; tests +62. The separate test-line allocation covers the public normalizer contract and raw HTTP/upgrade boundary regressions, reusing the existing server harness.

title: fix(sessions): replay creation requests across Gateway restarts
body:
## Problem

Process-local `sessions.create` idempotency loses the original binding when the Gateway restarts. Retrying can create another session and repeat preparation or its initial turn.

## Change

Atomically persist the existing optional idempotency key's namespaced fingerprint and original key/session ID/lifecycle revision with the session row. The existing passive history reader resolves receipts before label/resource preparation. Current requester, sharing, scopes and lifecycle authority still gate replay; stored authorization only restricts replay and never restores authority. Deleted/reset incarnations are refused, including same-ID resets. Renaming the original does not break replay when another session takes its former label.

The five-minute retry window remains. Replay does not allocate a worker, prepare a workspace or resend the initial message. Restart replay returns `creationReplayed: true` and `runStarted: false`: no new turn started, not a claim about completion of the original work. Inspect the original session for recovery. title: fix: reuse admitted worker transcript and cron stores
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker turns failing at the PostgreSQL thread boundary and Cron session runs reading scratch from a different partition than the scheduler that admitted them.

## User Impact

Worker launch and scheduled session execution retain their admitted transcript and Cron sources. There are no schema migrations, configuration changes, permission changes, or required operator actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the transcript source already held by the history worker instead of reopening the native database on the Gateway thread. Thread the admitting Cron service’s selected store path into session execution; direct callers still resolve their configured store, and explicitly prepared scratch retains precedence. Existing source-custody checks, revocation, and release behavior remain in place. This removes seven net production lines rather than adding another owner.

Integration adapted from Galin Iliev’s requested fixes; commits credit @galiniliev. This PR is independent of the database portability and scheduled-widget changes.

title: fix: use current client capabilities for scheduled widgets
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled turns offering an inline widget when only a remembered client—not the current turn—supports inline rendering.

## User Impact

Authorized scheduled turns without a current inline-capable client use pinned board widgets instead. Ordinary conversations retain their recorded-capability tool catalog, and current inline-capable clients still receive inline widgets. There are no configuration, schema, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Determine scheduled admission before selecting widget capabilities and use only the current client’s capabilities for scheduled turns. Keep the existing recorded-capability fallback for ordinary turns and the existing pinned-authoring policy/session checks. The change moves the existing scheduled predicate rather than adding another capability owner; production code shrinks by one line.

title: feat: support attended-session permission defaults

## Problem

Attended users cannot choose a per-agent creation permission default without repeating it on every request. A New Session picker must also show that creation default accurately, rather than label configured Full Access as Read Only.

## Change

Add opt-in `agents.entries.<agentId>.newSessionPermissionMode` using the existing creation and caller-classification owners. Explicit request modes win. It applies only to fresh, directly attended, profiled operator sessions—not existing sessions, forks, catalog sessions, autonomous runs, or delegated callers. `full` still requires current `operator.admin`.

Expose the attended creation default separately in agent metadata and New Session. Existing-session Default remains based on its existing tool-policy contract. Selection is extracted from the oversized creation service; the independent final-write permission guard remains. Replacing a pending default before persistence produces a structured retryable refusal, not an uncaught exception. No schema migration or existing-session permission rewrite.

title: fix(runtime): validate retained imports after composition pruning
body:
## What Problem This Solves
Installed-runtime finalization reparses the composition's JavaScript import graph after lifecycle pruning, even though the composition already owns those edges.

## User Impact
Installed runtime builds reuse the qualified import graph while still rejecting missing dependencies of retained modules after pruning. Removed importers no longer demand their removed dependencies. Standalone package checking keeps its original scan behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made
The existing composer records its graph in the hash-bound archive inventory. Its staged checker consumes that graph against the actual remaining files, and the finalizer uses the same checker. No new graph owner, runtime manager, package identity, or schema version. The maintained checker is staged with the maintained finalizer so their argument contract agrees.

## Evidence

**Direct CLI proof on `c359124b3f84ae13feb5fede70dc2a6f057ec0a5`:** launched `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/compose-installed-runtime.mts` with a minimal offline package and dependency inventory, then executed the checker copied into the composition's `.runtime-bootstrap`. No Vitest assertions or mocked checker were used. The fixture supplies the production `acorn` dependency; it is not a full OpenClaw installation. Actual sanitized output:

```text
composition: graph=[dist/entry.js -> dist/leaf.mjs], inventoryBound=true
intact retained dependency: exit 0
retained importer missing target: exit 1
  OpenClaw package dist import closure failed:
  dist/entry.js imports missing dist/leaf.mjs
removed importer no longer requires target: exit 0
missing bound graph: exit 1 (ENOENT)
```

The driver exited 0 after checking every exit above and removed its disposable package tree. Earlier driver attempts identified fixture setup omissions (wrong staged path and missing fixture parser dependency); neither was a product failure.
- Base reproduction:32/33 passed with the new graph regression failing as expected; retained parent proof.

Independent P0-P2 autoreview scoped-clean; unchanged graph and helper owners personally inspected. pr-simplify retained the existing composition/checker ownership.

One bounded direct reproduction confirmed its synchronous whole-repository shallow clone blocks in git pack-objects filesystem I/O, without executing candidate code;90s timeout exit124. Full suite is not claimed green. No fixture exemption, skip, timeout increase, or unrelated repair committed.

title: improve(tests): reuse channel import guardrail scans
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel import guardrails repeatedly parse the same core and extension sources, slowing focused contract checks. This optimization was requested for the test-health lane.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All **13 existing cases and their assertions** remain. The setup-inclusive single-file median falls from **46.563s to 34.537s**, saving **12.026s (25.83%)**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collect plain module references once per source set while each native parser batch is live, then reuse those references across the existing policy cases. The private-path check keeps unfiltered references; the other policies keep their existing JS/TS-extension and import-meta filtering. Import-equals rejection and diagnostic/comment/example controls remain effective.

The change is confined to one test file. The module-scoped cache holds filenames and plain reference data. Native snapshots retain their existing lifecycle. Simplification review retained this small cache so every policy keeps its separate case and failure reporting: **+41/-26, net +15 test lines**, with zero added cases and zero production lines changed.

## Evidence

Three baseline and three candidate runs used the same Blacksmith 16-vCPU Testbox **`tbx_01m6d58e5fhwmcgbbrxpvfaecw`**, associated with [run **41383994987**](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41383994987). Timing, work-count probes, and paired mutations reused that lease, with frozen-lockfile bootstrap on the VM. Source base: `ac6af4df297273b4d72f1d85971b5006c8b39530`.

Command, repeated three times per version:

```sh
corepack pnpm test src/channels/plugins/contracts/channel-import-guardrails.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

All six benchmark runs passed all 13 cases. The primary metric covers the complete single-file invocation, including setup and worker preparation.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Single-file command elapsed, setup included | 46.563s | 34.537s | **12.026s (25.83%)** |
| Vitest-reported invocation duration | 44.670s | 32.640s | 12.030s |

| Samples, seconds | Baseline 1 / 2 / 3 | Candidate 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command elapsed | 48.376 / 46.554 / 46.563 | 34.537 / 34.638 / 34.466 |
| Vitest duration | 46.450 / 44.670 / 44.670 | 32.640 / 32.720 / 32.560 |

Separate instrumented probes, excluded from timing samples, counted native source batches:

| Source set | Files | Baseline batches | Candidate batches |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Core | 13,632 | 3 × 426 = 1,278 | 426 |
| Extensions | 5,833 | 2 × 183 = 366 | 183 |
| **Total** | **19,465 distinct** | **1,644** | **609** |

This removes **1,035 batches (62.96%)**. The two tiny parser controls remain.

The mutation gate ran the complete 13-case file for every matrix cell. Mutants were injected into task-owned copies of real core/extension sources. **Killed** means the named existing policy assertion failed; passing controls require all 13 cases to pass.

| Source mutation / control | Baseline | Candidate |

| Core private import-equals | Killed: private-path check | Killed: same check |

| Extension cross-plugin facade, type import | Killed: cross-plugin facades | Killed: same check |
| Extension private seam, type import | Killed: extension public seams | Killed: same check |
| Diagnostic path, comment and string examples | 13 passed | 13 passed |
| Extensionless reference and import-meta asset filtering | 13 passed | 13 passed |

**All seven gating mutants were killed on both versions; both controls passed on both. No baseline kill became a candidate survivor.** All restored source hashes matched, and the source copies passed `git diff --exit-code` after restoration.

An initial runtime import to a nonexistent module failed worker preparation on both versions with zero tests executed. That setup-only probe is excluded from the gate above. The corrected type-import probes reach the existing source-guard assertions; the collector already includes import types.

Native children could not inherit work held only on a parent's retained repository disk. Review also exposed successful file-only fallback after private-history failures and source reassignment reaching child checkpoint publication.

## User Impact

Children receive independent checkpoints with current private Git history and working files. The parent retains its disk, active turn and staging index; the child starts from HEAD plus working files, not a shared disk or copied index. title: feat(database): recover retained workspace owners without waking workers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partial recovery can leave a retained repository disk without its native environment or placement owner. Restoring an old full state database would revive stale execution authority and unrelated state.

## User Impact

The offline dependency recovery command can restore or repair the selected original retained owner using sealed source and expected-destination images. It preserves exact disk custody but leaves runtime admission closed, revokes worker credentials, and clears turn claims. No provider, node, setup script, pairing, grant, or role is executed or restored. Explicit wake still uses current authorization, node pairing, provider receipt, and runtime admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190833 has merged; this PR now targets `main`. Current candidate: `f9fe6dd249a4d3b932cf98f2ba36a3c3eed893ec`. Earlier stacked qualification is retained below. Current schema39 native resource receipts, retention, environment/placement writers, and workspace disk binding remain the owners. Both images use current native codecs; source unfinished-work facts are read independently of destination checks. Current configuration fields must match the acquisition; machine/OS/execution selection remains historical metadata. All three owner records restore in one existing offline transaction after immutable skill/checkpoint artifacts. The request refuses drift and does not automatically retry against changed expected records.

No schema migration, donor v37 parser, Enterprise profile repair, Azure special case, or parallel recovery state is added. The retained kernel and command integration are separate reviewable commits in one dependent PR.

## Evidence

- Native kernel regressions: 2/2 passed, 4.476s test bodies /76.93s wrapper; existing workspace and retention siblings: 4/4 passed. Reopen, dormant launch refusal, conflict refusal, source unfinished work, credential removal, pruning safety and rollback covered.
- Offline retained command integration initially passed 1.655s/43.75s with synthetic acquisition; fresh review found production acquisition-field mismatch. Fixed current profile projection and expanded test to real-shaped executionMode/machineClass/os plus genuinely changed settings refusal. Final production-shaped rerun passed: 1.663s test body /43.18s wrapper. title: fix(workboard): clarify status when releasing claims
body:
Supersedes #155650, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

Related: #155367

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers can mistake `workboard_release` without `status` for finishing or pausing work even though the card keeps its current status.

## User Impact

The tool description and status-field help now explain that omitting `status` only clears the claim and preserves the current status, including `running`. Callers can pass a status such as `todo`, `ready`, or `review` when pausing or handing off work. Runtime defaults remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue explicitly accepts clarifying this contract. Workboard already permits running cards without claims, release preserves status, and reclaim separately defaults running cards to ready. Inferring a new destination on release would change those semantics. The tool and documentation now describe the existing distinction.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounds active-transcript projection inserts at the owning SQL boundary so an oversized supplied chunk does not exceed SQLite’s bind parameter limit.

## User Impact

This is maintenance hardening of the existing internal SQL owner. Large projection input stays inside the caller’s existing transaction; rollback and sibling rows are preserved. Current native reconciliation already sends 512-row chunks, finalization catches up at most 512 tail rows, and current database ports rebuild only FTS, not active projection rows. No current end-to-end native port failure is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing 512-row transcript insert limit instead of building one statement for every active row. No new option, API, schema, transaction owner, or competing implementation. This patch is independently reviewable and not a dependency of the database-port correctness change. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s batching fix. The 71-line regression allocation covers the real SQLite limit, row coordinates, rollback, and sibling isolation.

title: fix: accept signed filesystem identities in recovery receipts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database-port recovery and local client credential receipt loading when Node exposes a native device or inode identifier as a signed decimal string.

## User Impact

Operators can resume ports and use their existing client credentials on these filesystems. Exact file/root binding remains required: changed identities still refuse admission. No schema version, credential restoration, permission, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writers already serialize Node’s bigint identities verbatim. Both readers now accept the same signed decimal representation without normalization or precision loss. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s portability work.

The two existing parsing owners remain; no helper, state, or compatibility path is added. Production delta +6/-4 lines; regression delta +68 lines, allocated for identity round trips and replacement rejection.

## Evidence

### Existing focused qualification

- Baseline: signed receipt round trips fail (2 cases); signed recovery manifest publication fails (2 cases).
- Fixed: 30 tests passed across receipt and recovery suites; wrapper wall time 3.51s, test time approximately 0.23s. Core and infra test typechecks, focused lint/format and whitespace checks passed.
- That original qualification used checkout `41653af9e09596f1190724be941cd46d128d6d15`. Both production owners and both test files are blob-identical to this PR; other changes in that checkout are not attributed to this PR.
- Independent local review and the earlier hosted review found no actionable product findings. The latest hosted Gold assessment preceded the inspectable terminal traces and credential-command proof now included below; it found no product defects.

### Real public CLI and kernel-mounted signed-root proof

On November 4, exact baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914` and exact PR head `b612f55ebf698a6cc87eec12526fc50ae798d539` were exercised through the documented built public launcher, `node openclaw.mjs database port`, using separately bound source/dependency/build artifacts.

A private, unprivileged kernel FUSE mount projects the high bit of the actual backing-root inode. Unmodified Node bigint stat and the real command observe the negative value; there is no mocked stat, product source patch, preload, handwritten manifest, or injected SQLite data. This is an intentionally controlled affected-filesystem fixture, not a claim about naturally occurring Azure/NFS hardware. PostgreSQL 17 uses a disposable local, resource-bounded fixture with synthetic data; the canonical state row is created by the product owner.

The maintained libfuse low-level passthrough inode/refcount owner is retained. Independent source review found no consequential adaptation defects. Native qualification passed nine descriptor operations after unlink, directory/root identity, fsync, immediate staging-directory removal before descriptor close, and normal unmount. Binary SHA-256: `c24df350f980603777275d29bf51258b2f52a8e9420318f8b223fdfa0a86cb3c`.

| Case | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Baseline port on negative root | Refused signed-manifest publication after real capture completed; canonical row present, no active manifest, unchanged config and empty destination. |
| Fixed port interrupted during staging | Qualified external PostgreSQL DDL fault reached the real worker; owner-written preparing manifest retained the exact signed root, hashed artifacts and canonical snapshot; no destination/reference namespace remained. |
| Baseline resume of that unchanged manifest | Refused before staging; manifest, source, config and artifacts stayed byte-identical, destination remained empty. |
| Fixed resume of that same owner-written manifest | Completed real SQLite-to-PostgreSQL conversion, archived the manifest with the same operation/root identity, matched the canonical source row to PostgreSQL, and published the matching live anchor and family-engine config. |
| Independent fixed interruption for root-change case | Produced a genuine signed-root recovery manifest with the same fault/custody checks. |
| Fixed resume after actual root replacement | Refused at the same absolute path after actual root inode changed; device stayed unchanged. Every child inode/byte and protected manifest/source/config/artifact stayed unchanged; destination remained unchanged. The injected SQL fault was removed before refusal. |

Five cases passed in the 37.142-second run; it stopped before the final CLI call because the harness incorrectly assumed remount changes both device and inode. A fresh C-only run (17.178 seconds) repeated only its required interruption and completed the final refusal case. The product compares the complete root-identity tuple; the corrected oracle requires the same path and actual changed inode and records device identity instead of assuming allocation behavior. No earlier blocked run was relabeled.

Functional evidence SHA-256:
- Five-case run and independent cleanup: `cdf20816a824bdc47ffc46c32a56efd8cfdfe30f4117422680c7260a54f33a53` (184 evidence hashes; 95 recorded host PIDs absent).
- C-only completion and independent cleanup: `4a4a9fe988353f421b9e0a952339af72200a23432c1c41ceab12e1231ea0e93f` (134 evidence hashes; 56 recorded host PIDs absent).

Both containers were absent by name and ID, all task mounts and listeners were absent, and native command settlement was normal. A closed TCP TIME_WAIT entry was distinguished from a listener. Original 160/170/1500-second limits and the sole process-settlement owner stayed unchanged.

The public staging error deliberately preserves the worker's anchored `stage:` prefix; the test now parses the actual JSON envelope and saves contemporaneous server fault evidence before classifying it. A phase label alone never substitutes for manifest, row, artifact, namespace or custody checks.

### Limits and investigated earlier attempts

The command-level proof covers port-root signed inode behavior, inode-only root replacement, and the real local credential-loading command on a signed shared-file identity, including invalid-private-key and byte-identical changed-file refusal. Credential migration production, Gateway authentication and negative native device values are not claimed by these commands; signed-device behavior retains focused owner-boundary coverage.

Earlier attempts remain retained: a source-runner timeout with unknown cause, optional full-syscall captures that reached their trace cap, high-level FUSE staging hidden-file/ESTALE fixture failures, and the interrupted public-phase/device-allocation oracle runs. The current proof uses the qualified low-level fixture and documented built launcher; passing runs do not establish the cause of the old source-runner timeout. No CI retry, baseline increase, or product assertion was waived.

### Inspectable retained terminal evidence

These are complete selected command stdout/stderr records, not regenerated outcomes. Only the two task run directories and two wrapper directories are replaced by the literal aliases `$RUN1`, `$RUN2`, `$PHASE_PREP`, and `$ROOT_PREP`. Numeric identities, operation IDs, errors, timings and exit codes are unchanged. title: improve(backup): omit Codex diagnostics from restart checkpoints
body:
## Current-head CI repair — 2026-11-05

Head `e1829e4211e124ff7f8d6dc606344ec8edd3077e` preserves the cache/backup/renderer work below and repairs a stream-follow coalescing defect discovered while investigating the Activity CI assertion. This section supersedes earlier current-head status summaries; historical failures remain evidence, not passing results.

- **Original CI:** [run 41975853878](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41975853878) finished with 56 successful and 24 skipped jobs; Activity UI E2E3/7 and the aggregate gate failed. The original landscape assertion observed a 208px bottom gap. The final classifier labels it new (matching main job passed, scope not compared); it is not reclassified as inherited or a renderer crash.
- **Owner defect:** another content update can replace a pending animation frame after a delayed native scroll changes the live bottom-distance flag. The replacement then loses the already-admitted follow. Keep that decision alongside the existing frame ID across coalescing; preserve enabled/identity checks, native scrollback behavior and disposal. No new listener, timer, threshold, dependency, layout or public option.
- **Proof:** extending the existing helper case with one coalesced update fails on the original source (expected one scroll, got zero), then passes with the repair. Helper plus Update-view consumers: **12/12 pass**, 3.069s wrapper. Strengthened real Chromium Activity suite: **4/4 pass** across phone, tablet, landscape and desktop, 19.791s wrapper. A separate 4x CPU-throttled diagnostic also passes all four cases, 25.299s wrapper, including initial following before the test manually scrolls. Browsers exit normally.
- **Limits:** the first native diagnostic trace observed initial following stall before any user scroll; the old test's manual initial scroll masked it. A subsequent strengthened pre-fix browser attempt passed, so no deterministic browser red/green or exact reproduction of the CI interleaving is claimed. The deterministic owner regression and caller tests prove the repaired coalescing contract; fresh CI must establish the former shard result. The original historical renderer-crash cause remains unknown.
- **Cost/gates:** one net production line and two lines added to existing tests; no new cases or fixture framework. Exact two-line allocation, shared scalar unchanged. Official test-line gate passes **6,479,702 / 6,479,702**. Targeted supported typecheck, lint, formatting and whitespace pass. ## What Problem This Solves

Local-companion restart checkpoints unnecessarily capture Codex’s changing diagnostic SQLite log database and its companions.

## User Impact

Local-companion capture omits only the activated Codex plugin’s managed agent-home `logs_2.sqlite` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`. Full backups and unrelated same-name files remain unchanged. Codex state, credentials, session rollouts, and other databases remain preserved. Omitted diagnostic history is not recovered; Codex recreates the log store.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep vendor policy in Codex manifest `backupResources` and add an optional generic `local-companion` profile selector to the existing planner. No global filename exclusion, extra policy owner, schema/version change, or template-exclusion option is introduced. Native backup safety and source-preservation behavior remain intact.

The native contract was inspected in [Codex 8f73cde](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4): `codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs:29,59-65,146-148,297-310` separates logs from durable databases and recreates missing stores with WAL; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/logs.rs:3-57` records bounded diagnostic/feedback history. OpenClaw’s managed-home owner is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:7-42`. Custom external Codex/sqlite homes are intentionally not inferred.

title: fix(database): keep migration archive capture responsive
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes migration captures losing their renewable Gateway suspension when large filesystem archive preparation blocks the capture process.

## User Impact

Externally quiesced SQLite migration capture keeps renewing the existing suspension while archive creation and verification run. Cancellation joins the child before returning. Existing source-artifact preservation, PostgreSQL refusal, exact snapshots, restore behavior, and schema39 remain unchanged. No live Gateway changes or schema migration are required; the capturing binary must contain this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture now delegates blocking archive work to the existing update inspection subprocess owner with a 30-minute deadline, instead of introducing another process lifecycle. The child explicitly calls `verifyBackupArchive` before its bounded verified receipt; the archive creation helper does not consume `verify: true`. The parent keeps its existing revalidation and manifest-publication checks.

Simplification removed in-process archive execution and its ineffective verify flag. The launcher, wiring, and worker share the existing inspection lifecycle. The dedicated 133-line test allocation protects renewal, child settlement, archive validity, and caller-relative workspace contents without changing the shared baseline scalar.

title: fix(channels): preserve ingress retries after lost claim ownership
body:
Supersedes #158083, thanks @YangManBOBO.
Closes #158082.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recovering abandoned inbound-message claims consumes delivery retries and overwrites the last real failure timestamp, which can cause premature dead-lettering on a later genuine failure.

## User Impact

User impact: messages interrupted by a lost worker retain their delivery retry budget and failure history. Genuine dispatch failures still reach the existing retry limit. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stale-owner recovery returns the existing row to pending without recording a delivery failure. Keep that distinction in the current worker kernel while preserving its existing claim fencing. The ordinary failure path continues to record attempts.

The simplification removes the two recovery-only retry-field assignments and their unnecessary expression callback: production net **-1 line**. The existing drain lifecycle regression gains a stale-owner case with **+3 test lines**, covered by a matching test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e`:** the production drain/SQLite-worker regression failed because recovery changed attempts from 1 to 2 and lastAttemptAt from 100 to 101, without another delivery failure.
- **Green after:** 80 tests across `ingress-drain.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.claim-ownership.test.ts`, and `ingress-retry-policy.test.ts`; named-file command with `--maxWorkers=1` completed in 39.46 seconds including worker preparation (changed drain file: 23 cases, 5.931 seconds of reported case time; changed-channel CI job: 106 seconds including setup). The regression repeats lost-owner recovery three times, verifies preserved retry facts and successful redispatch, then verifies a genuine failure dead-letters at the configured limit. Existing cancellation and claim-fencing coverage also passes.
- Focused proof ran on Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox ([remote environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41378106033)); PR CI supplies broad proof. No live transport or production Gateway was exercised or changed. Contributor code was read with gh and was never executed; this is an independent reimplementation on current main.
- Local `autoreview`, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, reviewed the complete candidate at `09da8acdd4c201716ac6e7152bdd1d2d6e77af91` against the pinned main above: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the maintainer fallback uses autoreview and one hosted review request when ready.

title: fix: await Doctor snapshots and recover same-boot database leases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can block JavaScript signal handling while preparing private SQLite images for large agent databases. [chrislro’s macOS stack sample](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639) identified `spawnSync` waiting on the snapshot child with an 8.4 GB agent database. Missing macOS/Windows lease provenance also forces repeated full integrity gates after interrupted runs. Related: #178359, #187900, #185879.

## User Impact

Await lint snapshot admission, auth/lease inspection, recovery inventory and converted repair-planning reads through the existing owners. Cancellation reaches the owned snapshot child and joins cleanup. Reports share a read-owned image; writable plugin images remain exclusive. Required copies check database, WAL and rollback-journal sizes against available cache space and report insufficient capacity clearly. Unknown capacity remains best effort.

New macOS/Windows leases reuse the existing platform boot identity reader. Same-boot dead owners can use the existing cheaper recovery gate; legacy, unavailable or mismatched provenance still requires full verification. Existing leases are not backfilled. The candidate Doctor/worker must contain the fix; an older installed updater cannot gain it from the candidate alone. **Not yet released.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Artifact-preserving inspection still needs private images because native read-only SQLite can change WAL/SHM coordination files and some checks need writable private state. Capacity reservation is conservative even where copy-on-write could succeed. Existing admission, quarantine and transaction owners retain their decisions. Released synchronous SDK APIs and native final-effect checks retain their contracts. No new configuration or schema version.

This is the core stage of the complete caller cutover. Remaining session/shared-auth readers, process inspection, native credentials, Cron/daemon reads and repair preservation are in #190870, #190872, #190873, #190874 and #190875. Those stages remain pending.
