title: feat(slack): fork channel threads into independent conversations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack thread conversations need an independent continuation with inherited context, without replacing the source session.

## User Impact

Send @OpenClaw /fork [title] as an ordinary message inside an existing public/private channel thread. A new top-level root in the same channel becomes the fork thread. Title is optional. Native custom slash commands, DMs, top-level/synthetic threads and Enterprise Grid org installations are refused. Existing mention/access rules still govern follow-ups; routing grants no permission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse authenticated message/thread facts, ordinary-session SQLite bindings, normal routing and provider links. Literal root/recap text disables mentions and unfurls. Current command/account/installation authority reaches creation, binding and recap. Known resources survive later failures; ambiguous root creation is not repeated.

The reviewed cleanup and requested private-DNS upload fixture repair from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190953 are incorporated. Composed baseline ea64a1bff51dfbfd2df6fc1a3ca17073dcddd4c2 exactly matches tested H tree a0e6439460155035e268a38d4d66bb6c326d00d9. Chunking and error enrichment stay at their existing owners; redundant/no-op wrappers are removed. No store, schema, configuration, dependency or permission-policy change.

Current head64a69f26b0ec8c7d7c84dd2c83f64fe6915051a1 also repairs an evidenced Darwin process-census selector defect found while investigating the blocked wrapper check. Darwin ps -g is mode-dependent; -A plus explicit PGID filtering retains positive zombie-only proof. Failed, empty/missing, malformed and target-live snapshots still refuse completion; Linux session/thread selection is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Slack feature, cleanup and upload repair — baseline ea64

- Composed tree:101/101 cases across eight files,559.98s wall—core10,fork14,upload20,blocks24,bot-thread6,errors7,direct-authority9,reconcile11. Real core-policy proof plus source tracing carries current authority through Slack transport effects.
- Canonical production/changed-test types, scoped lint/format/whitespace and exact parent/core mock/test-line/line-cap ratchets passed with local inputs. Tests cover genuine versus synthetic threads, wrong actor/thread, membership, account/installation changes, ambiguity, binding reopen, link failure and literal serialization.
- Upload fixture causal controls reproduce ambient-proxy failure and fail again when only isolation is removed. Repaired upload20 plus69 siblings pass, including explicit trusted-proxy success. Production SSRF, credentials, retries and dependencies are unchanged. Fixture adds24 lines; cleanup removes18, so fixture credit is6.
- Whole-feature, cleanup and fixture independent P0-P2 reviews pass. H CI41601127682 and composed-main CI41602967212 succeeded at their exact heads. These do not substitute for the new head's gates.

### Darwin census repair — current head

- Selector negative control on original source:21 pass,2 fail. Final process/census campaign:104 pass,38.11s wall. Target-live, other-group, missing and malformed snapshots retain conservative outcomes.
- The selected wrapper case passes on Linux,7.62s. Types2.34s, scoped lint/format, test-line and line-cap guards passed. Fresh independent review plus required local P0-P2 autoreview are clean; final hashes verified after transfer to this exact parent.
- Original Darwin workflow41602967049/job125805845023 failed the current-recovery/older-binding wrapper case. Its artifact does not establish PS compatibility mode or a complete causal link to this selector defect. The selector contract is repaired; Linux passes are not native-Darwin proof or a claim that the recorded failure is definitively fixed. New native Darwin CI is required.
- Native admission previously aborted before dispatch; no accepted merge intent was replaced or bypassed. No process-custody, retained-workflow or security guard is weakened.

## Limits

No new live Slack/Gateway restart qualification was run. QA supports receipt-backed SUT-root registration, but credential readiness alone is not that proof. Original failed sibling/CI attempts remain historical, not relabeled green. Local walls are not CI seconds. New-head CI/security/native admission remain required; no operator Gateway deployment is included.

title: feat(discord): fork threads into independent sibling conversations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread conversations need independently routed siblings with inherited context.

## User Impact

/fork [title] creates a same-parent sibling for existing public text threads, private text threads and forum posts. The title is optional. Private forks add only requester and bot, disable member invitations and disclose that source members are not copied; members with Manage Threads may still have access. Media/announcement threads, DMs and top-level channels are refused. Command authorization and native permissions remain required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared core prerequisite is landed. The plugin qualifies source/parent/history access, reuses available required forum tags, creates one sibling, verifies private requester membership and binds the returned destination to the ordinary copied session. Current command/account authority reaches creation, binding and recap. Literal recaps suppress native mentions/embeds. Known created resources survive partial failure; uncertain creates are not automatically retried.

The additional permission-owner refactor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190949 is incorporated before this main landing. Current head d4c91a7b9d894900c29d45abda588e82952570a7 has exactly the tested tree of 719d171aa43f821419c274ce91e749d5b3be9f9a, based on landed core b515cc7f9f1f6af4f401be45c7464f9f3300e8d1. Qualification-local facts reduce public reads17 to6 and private reads18 to7, while preparation and pre-create independently refresh. No cross-phase/global cache or second permission owner.

Existing native permission/client/binding/outbound owners serve the flow. No new thread manager, store, schema, configuration, dependency or updater change.

## Evidence

- Current integrated provider proof: 116/116 cases, 363.34s wall—fork30, permission authorization13, basic send54 and DM authorization19. Five real core command-policy cases additionally passed178.62s.
- Independent history/private-membership/bot-permission/API-error refusals cover preparation and pre-create. Owner/admin/ManageThreads behavior, forum tags, native sibling validation, returned privacy, single-attempt recovery and retained binding cases remain.
- Public/private count regressions failed on the original parent with17/18GETs before passing with6/7;12 public qualification reads precede POST, excluding the separate post-create lookup.
- Source tracing carries B's actual current-policy producer through Discord scheduling/dispatch, native creation, binding and core recap. This combines real core producer proof with Discord transport-owner tests using mocked HTTP, not a live-platform claim.
- Canonical production/changed-test types, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, dependency pins and exact feature-parent/landed-core mock/test-line/line-cap guards passed with local inputs. Existing418 feature and42 permission-regression credits remain scoped; no scalar or guard waiver.
- Original whole-feature and complete-context permission-refactor P0-P2 reviews are reused for byte-identical patches. I exact-head full CI41601355347 succeeded before incorporation. The composed main-targeted head has its own exact-head CI/security/native admission.
- Original feature evidence remains historical: missing-entry red, adapter/outbound48, fork/binding lifecycle42, package verifier22 and build. Unqualified startup screening is not a performance claim; original runs are not relabeled current-head CI.
- No new live Discord slash/private/forum run was performed. The QA runner still lacks receipt-backed SUT-sibling recorder/cleanup handoff; no ownership guard was bypassed. Optional native qualification gaps are disclosed separately from meaningful boundary proof and enforced landing gates.
- Local wall time is not hosted CI seconds. No operator Gateway deployment is included.

title: feat: fork threaded conversations with Telegram support
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Threaded channel conversations need a real context fork, not a fresh thread with an empty session or a subagent. Landing review identified stale nonowner command admission and loss of literal recap protection after a formatting rejection; both are repaired.

## User Impact

`/fork [title]` in a Telegram forum topic creates a sibling topic bound to an independent copy of the selected conversation context. The original retains its session. The sibling receives the last three available visible text excerpts; busy sources copy only the last completed prefix. The title is optional. Manage Topics and existing bindings are required; DMs and unthreaded chats are refused.

Prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190763 is landed. Discord, Slack and Control UI typed-command parity remain separate dependent PRs. Existing Control UI menu forks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared command owns authorization, ordinary-session copying, source selection, history projection and recap delivery. A lazy optional channel capability owns native sibling placement and current account/access authority. This copies conversation context, not a Git checkout or external side effects.

The ancestry/header-cut and command-transcript owners commit a copied-session checkpoint before native effects and record the final outcome before acknowledgement delivery. Recap mirrors are display-only. Known resources survive later failures; uncertain native effects are not blindly retried. Command artifacts do not advance the last-completed model boundary, so repeated active forks exclude unfinished model input.

The existing authorization producer now retains a current-policy assertion for admission and awaited effect boundaries. Telegram code-only fallback pages retain native pre entities after HTML/rich rejection. Ordinary prose fallback and per-attempt transport authority remain unchanged. No second authorization/copy engine, store, schema, configuration option, dependency, updater migration or permission bypass is introduced.

## Evidence

### Qualified main integration: 70dd219b4f6abe2692ec37510af0c0dd56dd3750

Rebased onto pinned main d6c8ad3ff2fe2bd5c540f0a8dd7002a437f08c7c after A landed. All three range-diff mappings are identical: feature, runtime repair and SDK fixture correction. The checkout remained clean with checkout-local dependencies/declarations and the declared Node/pnpm/TypeScript/Vitest toolchain.

- **173/173 tests across eight files, 187.96s wall**: core fork 10; real retained authorization five; serialized literal fallback four; native SDK contract two; registered outbound/send/recovery HTTP and native-command delivery siblings 152.
- Canonical core-test-plugin-sdk and core-test-messaging types passed (12.48s); Telegram package-boundary production types (0.49s) and all Telegram test roots (1.45s) passed.
- Initial Telegram types exposed stale local SDK declarations for an existing current-source export. Canonical regeneration emitted 13,981 files (54.58s); both graphs then passed. No source/package change or guard bypass was used.
- Pinned-main mock, test-line and line-cap guards passed; line-cap covered 29 changed source files. Three affected MDX files and whitespace checks passed. Hosted CI seconds remain separate from local wall time.

### Landing repairs and SDK contract

- Real command-policy tests cover admitted nonowners and revocation before admission, native creation, binding and recap. Four actual HTTP cases cover HTML/rich rejection, revoked fallback authority and ordinary prose. Literal entities use UTF-16 offsets/lengths.
- The published native SDK result fixture now includes optional assertAuthorizedCurrent. All three strict type-equality assertions, both strict runtime comparisons, Reflect.ownKeys equality, deprecation-once and model-resolver privacy proof remain. Both resolver exports exercise refusal, admitted-nonowner and current-policy revocation.
- The SDK fixture reproduced the exact two TS2741 errors/propagated TS2554 and runtime mismatch before correction. Fixed canonical SDK types, two runtime cases and 53 siblings passed. Repair test credit is 336 lines, including 25 SDK contract lines; no shared scalar or ignore changed.
- Original repair sibling run had 258 passes and one rich-pre newline expectation failure. The expectation was corrected to the renderer contract; final regressions passed. That original run is not relabeled green.
- Independent P0–P2 repair-delta review completed scoped-clean with 31 intact context files. Its prior whole-feature INDEX-only findings are addressed by the repair, not relabeled clean. Rebase preserved all reviewed production patches exactly.

### Original feature baseline: bb6c4c29b07fd30a35c0145aa74a7988a858b272

- Original shared dispatcher/copy/bind/durability/active-prefix 10, Telegram adapter three, registered HTTP 34, prefix nine and transcript-owner 46 passed. Original per-file --maxWorkers=1 walls: 47.59s / 35.86s / 23.37s / 1.83s / 18.45s.
- Original builds passed (5m15s; committed replay 4m7.7s), with advisory UI asset-budget warnings. Original committed Telegram cold-import snapshot qualified. SDK comparison introduced no entrypoint or breaking removal; prepareFork is optional/additive.
- Real Telegram Test Server, compiled baseline and mock model: five action/reply pairs, exactly three recap excerpts, distinct sibling, isolated restart and independent source/fork context. No-title run created “Forked conversation.” Owned forum/process/credential cleanup completed. This is event/transport proof, not a client screenshot or new refusal-path live proof.

## Stack

A is landed; B targets main. C / D / E and the separate F–I follow-ups retain incremental review and exact-head gates. Current-head CI/native admission remain required; no operator Gateway deployment is included.

title: fix: restore prepared registry reuse for plugin subagent completions
body:
Refs #157935

Supersedes #157936, thanks @amoghasgekar.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-started subagent completions bypass a matching prepared plugin registry when registration drops the run's execution directory scope.

## User Impact

User impact: completion cleanup reuses the matching prepared registry, preserving the admitted agent directory and inherited or managed workspace. This removes an unnecessary plugin-loading path that is a likely cause of the stall reported in #157935. The regression proves registry reuse; end-to-end outage latency remains unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main's cleanup reuse path from #183996 requires `agentDir`, but plugin-run registration supplies neither directory. Carry the admitting runtime's `agentDir` and `workspaceDir` into registration and use the existing session workspace resolver for inherited workspaces and managed cwd values. The original contributor patch supplied only `workspaceDir`, which would still miss the current fast path.

The existing publication owner continues to decide whether a registry matches; historical or unpublished scopes retain its existing asynchronous fallback. No new cache, option, schema, or migration is added.

## Evidence

The new registration-to-completion regression uses the real registration record producer, prepared publication lookup, and context-engine completion consumer, with a spy on the fallback plugin loader. Registration persistence and plugin evaluation are isolated; this is owner-boundary proof rather than a live Gateway latency measurement.

On Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox ([lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41373754629)), the identical named test file fails on main `cd2f589dfe4c` and passes with this fix:

| Workspace scope | Main fallback loads | Fixed fallback loads | Fixed completion callbacks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Admitted runtime | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Inherited workspace | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Managed cwd | 1 | 0 | 1 |

Command: `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-subagent-cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. All three baseline failures reach the zero-fallback assertion with `agentDir: undefined`. All three fixed callbacks receive their expected directories. Test time is 474 ms total after the fix; wrapper time is 28.12 s including worker preparation (baseline: 34.74 s). Exact-head [CI run 41374429976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41374429976) passed on `f64c0fef8dccb59d87385dafc0715ca375225c01`; both required gate publications succeeded before native landing.

Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Focused caller proof on the same Testbox passed 29 tests across `agent-run-subagent.test.ts`, `subagent-control.publication.test.ts`, and the plugin cases in `agent.test.ts` (81.53 s wrapper time; unrelated cases were explicitly filtered). PR CI supplies broad proof.

Codex autoreview of the complete candidate against `cd2f589dfe4c`, through P2, is scoped-clean. Its earlier test-only review found that config fallback could masquerade as a session override; the fixture now gives config a different workspace from the admitted publication.

Pr-simplify retained only the directory handoff, existing workspace resolver, and regression. Production grows by 17 lines; no safe dead or duplicate code was found to offset them. The 115-line test allocation covers the new three-scope regression and required caller fixtures; the shared baseline is unchanged. Contributor code was read with gh and never checked out or executed.

title: improve(test): speed up personal section editor E2E
body:
Related: #190724

## What Problem This Solves

Personal section editor E2E tests spend time waiting for incidental menu, drawer, and dialog animations while checking settled behavior.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same eight cases run faster: summed file medians fall from **34.479s to 23.936s**, saving **10.543s (30.6%)** per complete batch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `reducedMotion: "reduce"` at the seven mock-file and four real-Gateway-file context option sites, following #190724. Existing production CSS already removes incidental motion for this preference, including modal show/hide durations and the global transition override.

Both files assert final membership, persistence, scope, isolation, native interactions, or settled geometry. Every case, assertion, request count, native click, focus/keyboard path, and clock boundary is preserved. Shared helpers, suite defaults, production CSS, and deadlines are unchanged. AST comparison confirmed that the eleven context properties are the only semantic changes.

The test-only diff is +639/-605, **net +34 lines**. Most displayed changes are formatter indentation and wrapping around existing `withPage` callbacks. The simplification pass retained only the requested context properties and required formatting.

## Evidence

Three baseline and three candidate runs used the same Blacksmith Testbox **`tbx_01m6cy76nx20b44vvws4jmzdv8`**, with remote frozen-lockfile bootstrap: [run 41373074378](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41373074378). The requested runner tier was Blacksmith 16-class; the allocated VM reported four online CPUs and approximately 15.4 GiB RAM. Each benchmark run passed all eight cases. The canonical UI E2E command prepared the private QA runtime and exercised the real file's isolated Gateway/trusted-proxy fixture.

These are native Vitest file-summary durations including file hooks. Summed medians describe complete-batch runner work, not CI critical-path time.

| File under `ui/src/e2e/` | Baseline median | Candidate median | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `personal-session-groups.e2e.test.ts` | 22.740s | 14.492s | 8.248s |
| `guest-personal-groups.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` | 11.739s | 9.444s | 2.295s |
| **Sum of file medians** | **34.479s** | **23.936s** | **10.543s** |

<details>
<summary>Individual samples and benchmark command</summary>

| File | Baseline samples 1 / 2 / 3 | Candidate samples 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mock | 22.353 / 22.740 / 22.776s | 14.515 / 14.492 / 14.479s |
| Real Gateway | 19.644 / 11.739 / 11.403s | 9.444 / 9.458 / 9.285s |

All samples, including the first cold real-Gateway observation, are retained. Every candidate sample was faster than every baseline sample for its file.

```sh
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/personal-session-groups.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/guest-personal-groups.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The test command ran three times per version on the same box.

</details>

A separate untimed browser probe confirmed `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches === true` in all eleven acquired contexts. All eight cases passed, including the existing `animation.finished` waits; none hung. The probe was removed afterward and is absent from the timed candidate and committed patch.

The mutation gate ran on the same box and Actions run. A temporary product-code mutation in `personal-session-group-actions.ts` replaced the submitted section name `This week` with the previous name `Focus`, independently of motion. Baseline controls used original test bytes; candidate controls used the exact timed and committed test bytes.

| Existing coverage | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mock personal-layout case: renamed section retains its member | Killed: expected renamed section row count 1, received 0 | Killed: same assertion |
| Real-Gateway case: renamed section persists after reload | Killed: expected `Later, This week`, received `Later, Focus` | Killed: same assertion |

Both files killed an assertion-targeted mutant on both variants. No baseline kill became a candidate survival. All product mutations and probes were reverted, and restoration digests matched the original product bytes and timed candidate bytes. The final diff contains only the two intended test files.

- Touched-file format, lint, and scoped typecheck passed remotely.
- Isolated Codex autoreview of the final candidate: **P0–P2, scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Runtime proof was collected separately.
- All browser executions, runtime preparation, dependency installation, and static checks ran on Testbox. No local browser/container, dependency install, broad suite, or broad lint/typecheck ran on the production Team host. PR CI supplies broad validation.
- The proof Testbox was stopped after both proof commands completed with exit 0. Stopping the lease leaves its allocation workflow marked cancelled.

title: fix(infra): avoid macOS Tailscale lookup on Linux and Windows
body:
Supersedes #154139, thanks @xydt-juyaohui.

## What Problem This Solves

Tailscale discovery launches an unnecessary `locate Tailscale.app` subprocess on Linux and Windows when no usable CLI is found.

## User Impact

Linux and Windows skip this unsuccessful application lookup. macOS discovery, binary validation, and missing-binary reporting keep their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the macOS-only fallback in `findTailscaleBinary`, with an injected platform for cross-platform coverage. Reuse the existing invalid-CLI regression instead of adding another suite. Production grows by three lines for the guard; there is no duplicate platform check or dead branch to remove safely in this owner. Tests grow by nine lines, covered by a dedicated test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- Verified on current main `cd2f589dfe4c98651f5ce435838736b58aa77ddd`: the unconditional fallback accepts only macOS app paths.
- Red before: the production discovery tests fail for Linux and Windows because `locate` runs once instead of zero; the macOS case passes.
- Green after: all 34 tests in `src/infra/tailscale.claim.test.ts` pass, including zero locate calls on Linux/Windows and one on macOS. Standalone Vitest with the repository infra config took 1.38s wall time (about 0.14s test time); The CI changed-node test job passed in 274 seconds including setup; per-file CI timing was not separately inspected.
- Touched-file lint (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. The normal runner started broad worker preparation and was stopped; standalone Vitest preserves source imports without that build. [PR CI run 41372497374](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41372497374) passed on `f665824bd63c34ab2162cac33ef2312062068997`; the combined CI/security gate also passed.
- Autoreview: Codex, P0–P2, local snapshot against `cd2f589dfe4c98651f5ce435838736b58aa77ddd`, scoped-clean with no findings. Review covered the complete diff; unchanged source context was unavailable to that reviewer, and it did not execute tests.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or run. This replacement independently implements the fix and preserves the human commit author's credit.

Hosted ClawSweeper disposition: its P3 suggestion to remove the platform parameter was declined because explicit platform injection was part of the requested design. The default remains `process.platform`; the review reported the patch correct and identified no correctness defect.

title: fix(meetings): keep browser audio alive through clock changes
body:
Supersedes #155848, thanks @ly85206559.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes browser meeting audio stopping early or lingering after the system clock changes in Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom.

## User Impact

Active input keeps working through clock corrections, and idle capture still releases its audio resources after the existing ten-second timeout. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared generated browser capture script now measures heartbeat age with the page's monotonic `performance.now()` clock at initialization, renewal, and expiry. The process-local helper cannot be imported into the injected page. Production LOC is unchanged (3 added, 3 removed); no additional owner or compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

- On current main `cd2f589dfe4c98651f5ce435838736b58aa77ddd`, the new `setSystemTime` regression fails in both directions: +60 seconds closes capture early; -60 seconds fails to expire it. The test also checks renewal, PCM delivery, playback restoration, and cleanup.
- After the fix, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/meeting-bot/browser-audio-capture-source.test.ts src/meeting-bot/realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 19 tests (0.907 seconds Vitest, 2.11 seconds shard wall time). Broad [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41372468829) passed on the exact reviewed head, including UI end-to-end; the whole CI workflow took 500 seconds.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) reviewed the complete local candidate against the main commit above and returned `scoped-clean`, with no findings. The subsequent commit contains the reviewed source unchanged. Hosted ClawSweeper also found no actionable defects and confirmed the disclosed Chromium proof gap.
- Simplification retained the existing capture owner and added only two clock-direction cases to its fixture: +19 test lines, with an exact 19-line allocation for this regression.
- The generated production script ran with synthetic media in the existing VM fixture. Real browser/vendor meeting validation was not run on the production Team host. Contributor code was read via GitHub only; it was never checked out or executed.

title: fix(channels): preserve ordinary thread session bindings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary thread-bound conversations were recorded as ACP sessions and could enter the wrong reconciliation lifecycle after restart. Landing review also exposed opaque plugin-owned targets being sent through ACP agent selection, including metadata-omitting refreshes.

## User Impact

Ordinary session bindings remain ordinary through creation, persistence, reload and cleanup in Discord, Matrix and Telegram. Canonical ACP keys, supported main/global ACP aliases and explicit subagents retain their behavior. Plugin-owned opaque targets work with explicit multiple agents and no default agent. This is prerequisite A of the threaded `/fork` stack; it does not expose `/fork` itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing public session/subagent contract in each plugin’s private record. The worker-backed ACP metadata reader classifies supported aliases; unreadable stores refuse classification before native creation. Legacy ACP-coerced ordinary rebinding preserves same-target metadata without bulk rewriting historical explicit tags.

The landing repair uses canonical plugin-ownership metadata, not target-key prefixes, arbitrary agent selection or broad exception swallowing. Discord creation/hydration/reply identity tolerate an absent agent owner. Matrix preserves plugin metadata through creation, projection, persistence and hydration.

For partial refreshes, only the same target and same public-kind family inherit ownership facts. Child placement, replacement targets and kind changes do not inherit them. Native/action hints remain incoming-only; Matrix introText is not replayed from stored metadata. Currentness callbacks and effect-boundary checks remain intact.

No database schema, configuration, dependency, retention or intentional permission-policy changes. The updater is unchanged and no migration step is added. The separate F refactor consolidates classification; this PR repairs lifecycle behavior in the existing owners.

## Evidence

### Current landing repairs: deff77c2df96014cd4e4d523b08ef70f7e73ec55

- Real interactive producer → approval → actual adapters, with alpha/beta agents and no default: opaque-target failures reproduced before repair. Tests retain real ACP-reader delegation and cover refresh, persisted reload, detach, incomplete ownership and replacement/kind isolation.
- Initial opaque-target repair campaign: six adapter/sibling files, 117 passed (944.90s). Final standalone creation/reload suites: Discord 22 (40.97s), Matrix 27 (136.00s), Telegram 35 (61.90s).
- Partial-refresh regression reproduced AgentSelectionRequiredError in all three adapters. Final original ordered five-file database shard: 103 passed (77.20s). Unchanged reply-delivery sibling: 14 passed in the preceding campaign. A test-owned kind-change row was explicitly unbound to repair the original ordered cleanup failure; no assertion was weakened.
- Tests use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` with task-specific compiler caches. Added repair test lines are explicitly allocated: 167 opaque-target lines and 148 partial-refresh lines. CI seconds are reported by the attached run, not inferred locally.
- Focused production/test types, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace and the extension-test core-import guard passed. Fresh P0–P2 independent reviews of both repair deltas completed scoped-clean with zero findings; the final refresh review received 34 complete context files.
- Committed final CLI-startup build completed successfully. Discord, Telegram and Matrix cold-import snapshots all qualified with no gaps; process/temporary-home cleanup was verified. Earlier dirty/stale-declaration screenings remain unqualified and are not reused as this result.
- No new live-channel or live-Gateway run is claimed for these repairs. Current-head CI and native admission remain required before merge.

### Original feature baseline: 26fa359d7ca57211e1c9fe6cfed9d88bb82befbe

- Ordinary-target regressions failed on all three original producers (acp instead of session).
- Original per-file `--maxWorkers=1` proof: Discord 21 passed, 45.11s; Telegram 31, 16.94s; Matrix 26, 11.14s. Discord authority/state/subagent siblings: 23 passed.
- Original focused types/lint/format and diff checks passed. Original `pnpm build`: exit 0, 8m17.6s, with advisory UI asset-budget warnings. Subsequent landing findings are repaired and reviewed above.

## Stack

A → B (shared command/core recording/Telegram) → C (Discord) / D (Slack) / E (Control UI), with separately published F–I refactor follow-ups. Retarget dependents after prerequisites land, preserving incremental review and exact-head qualification. Landing is authorized; operator Gateway deployment is outside this request.

title: fix: honor explicit npm and npx commands on Windows
body:
Supersedes #185425, thanks @AmelioMansour.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows command execution ignoring an explicitly selected npm/npx executable or wrapper and running bundled npm instead.

## User Impact

Trusted callers can select their npm/npx executable or wrapper without silently switching installations. Bare aliases keep their existing Windows defaults. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restrict the bundled-npm shortcut to bare aliases at the resolver owner. Explicit selections retain the existing executable checks and trusted batch wrapper, with `shell: false`; command trust and authorization stay with existing callers.

title: fix(exec): preserve no-timeout results from macOS app nodes
body:
Supersedes #185434, thanks @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: commands on macOS app nodes lose their result after 20 seconds when `exec` requests `timeoutSeconds: 0`.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands can return their output after 20 seconds. Gateway invocation bounds, cancellation, configured policy, finite timeout caps, and explicit socket deadlines remain in effect. Delivery requires a macOS app build with the updated bundled node runtime; no Team Gateway deploy is needed for the fix itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway normalizes zero to `timeoutMs: null`, which Swift already executes without a process timer. The socket client must distinguish an omitted timeout (`undefined`, retaining its 20-second default) from explicit zero or null. This repairs that decision at the existing owner without changing Swift or execution policy.

The existing socket tests now cover null alongside zero and verify that an explicit finite socket deadline still overrides null. Production LOC delta: 0; test LOC delta: 0. No new machinery or test harness was needed.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41365038582) and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` pass for `a908e6808cdc25fdc3e3c42f4791952831c1f1ae`, including changed-test lanes, type/lint checks, baseline ratchets, and security checks.

- Main checked at `71becfa19f32a86eb3e62bccf713f5be7107884f`: traced exec timeout resolution → Gateway zero-to-null normalization → node-host forwarding → socket response deadline → Swift nil timeout handling.
- Red before: the null case in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts` fails on main because a response timer is installed (1 failed, 15 passed; wrapper 2.59 s).
- Green after: `pnpm test src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed, wrapper 1.76 s. The real Unix socket receives output after a simulated day; explicit 50 ms override, finite command budgets, omitted default, and cancellation retain coverage. CI timing is reported by the PR checks.
- Touched-file lint, format check, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, final local snapshot against the main SHA above): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It reviewed the changed files plus the Gateway, node-host, exec timeout, and Swift callers; it did not execute tests.
- Baseline failure retained: the additional `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` run fails in the malformed matching response case with `read ECONNRESET` at its peer cleanup assertion. The same failure reproduces with the unmodified main socket owner (1 failed, 7 passed). Its finite 5,000 ms command and explicit 1,000 ms response budget are unchanged by this patch; other sibling cases pass. Socket reset behavior remains an investigated baseline uncertainty, not a passing check.
- Local node-host test preparation began compiling the broader worker bundle and was stopped to respect production-host limits. PR CI owns node-host and broad proof. This Linux host has no macOS toolchain; no native app execution or Swift build is claimed. The TypeScript transport regression does not prove native process cancellation.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` only and was never checked out, installed, built, or run. This replacement was implemented independently on main and credits Mitchell Etzel in the commit.

title: fix(ui): require explicit toast severity
body:
## Problem
Failure producers frequently omitted toast severity. A denied clipboard operation reached the real toast renderer without its error class and looked like a successful copy.

## Solution
- Require `ToastOptions.severity`: explicit `success`, `error`, or `undefined` for neutral/unadorned notices.
- Classify all 156 production producers, including eight conditional clipboard outcomes, and update synthetic callers and consumer expectations in the same cutover.
- Keep the existing renderer, tokens, layout, stacking, actions, and message copy unchanged. Pending publication, intentional discard, operator-stopped work, and bounded partial imports are not mislabeled as completed successes or failures.

## Impact
Preferences, chat/dashboard actions, session management, clipboard feedback, browser/portal actions, templates, uploads/downloads, and background-session notices share the enforced contract. Future callers cannot silently omit an outcome.

Related open PRs: #192013, #192014, #192015. This is based on main, not their branches. It overlaps #192013 at the options contract and #192015 in producer files. Explicit `undefined` preserves #192013’s no-icon convention; no new neutral variant is introduced. The component/stack redesign and alert-role changes remain with #192013/#192014. #192015’s copy changes are deliberately not duplicated.

## Evidence
- Baseline clipboard E2E fails at the renderer boundary: expected the error class after the actual session-menu copy action, received false. Only external clipboard I/O is denied; the production menu, toast owner, and renderer remain mounted.
- Final-head E2E passes for success/error at 1440×900 and 390×844, in Claw light, Claw dark, and CRT dark. Fresh captures rebuilt all six comparisons byte-for-byte identically to the originals. All six were personally inspected for clipping, alignment, spacing, and theme consistency.
- 87 affected consumer test files / 1,579 tests pass. This includes all 12 toast browser tests, rich feedback at 1280/390/320px, oversized errors, and native-modal/anchored/bottom placement. The changed-file selection also passes: 26 files / 604 tests (overlapping coverage).
- UI typecheck, 121-file formatting, focused lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Lint retains eight warnings on unchanged Solid/reactivity statements, with no errors. A resource-stalled first test attempt was rerun in full and passed.
- AST check: every production call specifies severity. Normalizing away severity leaves identical ASTs in all 92 migrated production consumers; the remaining production change is the owner’s required type field.

title: fix(agents): stop retaining completed tool calls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained completed tool calls when a tool leaves an async resource or captured async scope alive after execution.

## User Impact

Completed tool-call context can be collected while background resources continue. This removes a confirmed retention edge in the Team heap regression window; it does not establish that this edge explains the entire observed production heap plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill-usage recorder added in #191661 closes over a callback that captures the executing call's context. Closing it only changed a boolean. Clear that callback on close instead, preserving active skill attribution and refusal of late attribution.

The existing plugin skill-usage integration test now drains queued diagnostics before tracker cleanup, retains an async snapshot, and checks that the completed call context is collected and late recording still returns false. Fixture reuse keeps regression-test growth at **0 lines**; production growth is **+1 line**. No configuration, schema, durable retention, or public API change.

## Evidence

A focused offline Node probe runs the real `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` path with `--expose-gc`: 16 completed calls, each with a synthetic 512 KiB call-context payload and an independently retained timer. After event-loop turns and forced GC:

| Source | Payloads retained | Retained heap delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base | 16/16 | +8,695,488 bytes |
| Fix | 0/16 | +240,344 bytes |

The narrower production-recorder probe changes from 16/16 retained (+8,449,152 bytes) to 0/16 (+57,992 bytes). A separate 16-iteration GC-diagnostic subscription probe stays below 60 KiB growth. These synthetic measurements prove the ownership defect; they do not measure production savings.

Focused two-file lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Codex-backed autoreview pass (no actionable P0–P2 findings). The final-head integration regression [passes on Bun in 421 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736512183/job/126267851700), including persistence, collection, and late-call refusal. The [final-head CI run completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736512183), with 38 jobs passed and 30 plan skips; `build-artifacts` is skipped by the scope plan. Testbox queued and the task-owned request was stopped; no local broad-test fallback. No production Gateway RPC, profile, signal, state change, or deployment was performed.

title: fix(ui): follow the Activity page scroll owner on phones
body:
## Problem
Activity changes scroll owners at its phone/short-landscape breakpoint, but live auto-follow still reads and writes the inner stream. On base `91d08c31`, the phone regression leaves a 395px bottom gap; explicit resume also misses the end. Related: #190393, #190409.

## Solution
- Select the outer content on phone/short-landscape layouts and the stream on desktop.
- After DOM insertion, own one capture listener on the containing page for the mounted Live view. Filter events to the active scroll owner; no reactive listener-rebinding effect is needed.
- Make shared auto-follow read its configured container instead of the event listener's currentTarget, so captured and element-bound callers agree on one owner.
- Cover follow, wheel-scroll pause, and resume at 390×844, 768×1024, 932×430, and 1440×844; reuse the existing shared-helper test for captured-scroll delivery.

## Impact
No CSS, theme-token, markup, or public API changes. Update-run retains its own inner scroll containers and is covered by its existing tests. Logs/transcripts are unchanged. Production delta against the merge base: +28/−5 lines; test delta: +121/−3 (net +118).

## Evidence
- Base browser reproduction: expected bottom gap <2px, observed 395px. Existing matched captures show 395px → 0px following and 3664px → 0px after resume.
- Final bundled Chromium regression: **4 passed**, 29.84s wall time, with synthetic Gateway events and fixed fixture time. Final source hashes were recorded with the run.
- Shared captured-scroll regression: **red before the helper fix** (expected scrollTop 0, got 1000), green afterward. Activity, shared auto-follow, and update-run unit suites: **47 passed**, 6.16s wall time.
- Final UI typecheck, targeted oxlint, format check, controller guard, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- CI on `6a1b82b6f2b7979bf6d2f30e2643229231de79f6` has settled; UI e2e and i18n passed. Production types and all six test-type jobs fail in untouched MCP modules. Their compiler diagnostics match #192368, #192383, and #192389; the package-boundary declaration errors match those PRs as well.
- The test-lines ratchet reports 47 inherited over-budget lines, also observed on #192368, #192383, and #192389. This PR adds 118 test lines and an exactly matching 118-line allocation. Local reproduction reports the same 355-line excess on both the original base (zero test delta) and this branch; the allocation does not absorb existing debt.
- The shared startup-JS budget check reports 90,688 B against 90,687 B. The same budget check fails on unrelated #192377 (90,696 B) and #192373 (90,701 B). The aggregate CI gate reflects these failed jobs.
- Prior light/dark visual scenarios: **4 passed**. No rendered change was made in this CI repair, so the six existing comparisons are retained rather than recaptured.

## Visual proof
Six labeled **BEFORE | AFTER** phone comparisons are attached below: light/dark × following/paused/resumed. The captions include the measured distance from the actual scroll owner to the bottom. Also inspected matching 1440px light/dark captures for all five checkpoints; desktop layout and behavior stay consistent. Fixture data is fictional.

## Accepted edge cases / follow-ups
- Verified in Chromium browser fixtures, not on physical phones or against a live Gateway. No color/markup changes, so custom-theme, loading/error, and translated-copy layouts are unaffected by this scroll-owner-only change.
- The responsive query intentionally matches the existing page-scrolling CSS, including short landscape phones; keep them in sync if that layout breakpoint changes.

title: feat(auth): allow operator access without credential enrollment
body:
Supersedes #179959, closed after replacement verification.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot currently grant ordinary assistant access without also granting personal credential enrollment.

## User Impact

Additive `operator.read.no-credential-enrollment` and `operator.write.no-credential-enrollment` grants preserve ordinary capabilities and existing saved-account use while withholding new provider and personal GitHub enrollment. Existing read/write/admin grants retain their behavior. This is an API/UI guardrail, not host-execution containment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the shared ordinary-capability predicate while keeping issuance, retained grants, and role ceilings strictly attenuated. Enrollment uses one method classifier and live authority checks. The cutover includes Gateway callers, plugins, web/native clients, and the current shared personal-identity owner; saved-account selection/unlink and GitHub status/cancel/disconnect remain available.

Phone Back and Escape did not agree on a settings subpage's parent. Plugin configuration exposed both problems: the shell's Escape path discarded the location, and the plugin page's capture handler bypassed the shell entirely, jumping straight to the installed list.

Related: #191206, #191222.

## Solution
- Rename the existing location-aware Back target to `settingsParentTarget` and use it for both phone Back and shell Escape.
- Let plugin settings Escape bubble to the shell instead of maintaining a second navigation implementation. Keep modal, menu, IME, skill-preview, and focused-field handling intact.
- Preserve plugin configuration → detail → list ordering and `from=plugins` origin navigation. Keep the intentional top-level behavior: Escape exits Settings; phone Back is absent there.

## Impact
All settings child routes use the same parent decision, including agent/model setup and appearance subpages. Plugin discovery keeps its own dismissal behavior. No CSS, colors, layout, configuration, or public contract changes.

Built on main; open #191395 also touches `app-shell-view-state.ts`. This change only renames its parent-target import/call and does not modify that PR or its branch.

## Evidence
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740388557) has settled. UI unit tests, all seven UI E2E shards, lint, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passed.
- `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, and `check-test-types-core-1` through `-5` fail on existing MCP catalog type errors in `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` and `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts`. Their diagnostics are also present in unrelated #192379 and #192380; none involve this PR's files. [Production type log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740388557/job/126281963579).
- `control-ui-performance` fails while measuring the base checkout: startup JS gzip is 90,700 B against a 90,687 B limit. Unrelated #192377 has the same base-checkout budget failure (90,696 B against 90,687 B). [This PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740388557/job/126280862140), [#192377](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41739536216/job/126278042337). The aggregate CI gate remains red because of these type and base-performance failures; no budget or baseline was changed.
- Original behavior proof: base `91d08c31d14cd85be17e5ecb4d8a0ec075ef53bb` failed the new Escape regression at 390px and 1440px while Back passed. The original repaired production-browser matrix passed 24/24 cases.
- [Typecheck failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41728599587/job/126242290897): the redundant new shell fixture used invalid `context: null`. The repair removes that duplicate fixture while retaining owner and full-shell coverage.
- [UI unit failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41728599587/job/126240816225): an old test still expected the plugin page to dismiss settings itself. The repair retains discovery-owned dismissal and exercises settings dismissal through the shell.
- [Test-line failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41728599587/job/126240815826): CI reported +70 test lines. Consolidation removes 72 net lines. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` now passes with **net delta -2**, following its documented non-growth rule despite inherited overage. No baseline/allocation files changed.
- Local validation: **41/41 unit cases** passed; the final parent-matrix simplification was rechecked separately. **14/14 production-browser cases** passed across settings-subpage-back and plugins-settings-keyboard, including phone Back, phone Escape, desktop Escape, and filter restoration. UI-app, UI-pages, and UI-E2E typecheck graphs passed. Targeted lint: zero warnings/errors. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- The earlier [UI E2E 2/7 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41728599587/job/126240816244), where native paste received `ABCD-1234` rather than the copied note, was not root-caused. That shard passes on the current head; this does not establish a flake classification or prove a clipboard fix.
- Loaded-settings browser coverage does not prove dismissal while settings transport is pending.

## Visual proof
Re-inspected all six existing synthetic-fixture comparisons at 390×900 and 1440×900 in light and dark modes. Fresh GETs returned six PNGs byte-identical to the inspected originals. This repair changes only tests, so no recapture was needed. Each parent comparison has Back above Escape; before is left, after is right. List comparisons confirm that the Workboard filter survives returning through the parent levels. No color changes require a custom-theme comparison. Loading/error/empty layouts were not changed.

title: fix: preserve Chromium sandboxing in diff rendering and QA browsing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Chromium sandboxing being disabled by default when the Diffs renderer or QA Lab opens a browser through Playwright.

## User Impact

Diff PNG/PDF rendering and QA browser sessions request Chromium sandboxing. Diffs preserves the existing explicit `browser.noSandbox: true` opt-out for trusted environments that cannot support it. Such environments now need that opt-out instead of silently running unsandboxed.

Browser binaries must still be kept up to date independently: this does not update Chromium, change the main Browser plugin, or claim to remediate particular Chromium CVEs. Diffs and QA Lab are source-tree plugins excluded from the root npm package.

## Why This Change Was Made

Playwright disables Chromium sandboxing unless launch callers explicitly enable it. Both launch owners now do so. Diffs shares browsers only when the resolved executable and effective sandbox policy match, so an earlier opted-out render cannot supply an unsandboxed browser to a default-policy request. Existing active renders retain their own browser and idle cleanup.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, real production diff rendering produced PNG and PDF with `--no-sandbox`.
- Regression assertions fail on the baseline: Diffs 3 failed / 14 passed; QA lifecycle 3 failed / 11 passed. Added coverage also checks policy changes and independent browser reuse/cleanup. The 36-line allocation covers this regression growth.
- After the fix, explicit Diffs opt-out still produces real PNG and PDF. Default rendering fails closed with Chromium's `No usable sandbox` error on this host, which cannot support Chromium sandboxing. Successful sandboxed rendering remains unverified here.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fixed-head regression runs and type-aware lint could not complete: local compiler/artifact preparation stalled before returning results. This is a **draft** pending exact-head CI and a sandbox-capable runtime check; no passing fixed-head suite or typecheck is claimed.
- Independent review identified shared-browser policy reuse. The keyed-cache repair was re-reviewed with no remaining code blocker; the reviewer explicitly retained the validation gaps above.

## Worked on by

- @fuller-stack-dev

title: fix(ui): localize cron metadata and usage summaries
body:
## Problem
Several automation and usage summaries bypass the English catalog or construct sentences from translated fragments, preventing localization and grammatical reordering.

## Solution and impact
- Route cron state/payload labels and action feedback through whole templates in the existing lazy cron catalog. `cron.job` remains separate from the concurrently changed `cronSchedule` namespace.
- Use whole templates for run token totals and usage role/tool counts, without lowercasing translated role labels.
- Preserve user/plugin values, protocol statuses, delivery details, and the existing English `Tokens` capitalization. Message counts use the active UI locale.
- Register cron copy at the agent Automations consumer. No startup-English, translation-memory, locale-metadata, configuration, or protocol changes.

- Four changed regression suites with one worker: 14 passed, 141.77 seconds wall time on the loaded local host. CI per-suite timing was not yet available.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. One existing Solid reactivity warning is in an unchanged run-row callback.
- Fixed CI's heterogeneous token-table type error using the owning `CronRunLogEntry` usage type and string-only interpolation parameters. The exact `core-test-ui-pages` graph passed locally in 22.9 seconds.
- Added the policy-supported, dedicated 177-line test allocation for the four independent routing boundaries. The shared scalar is unchanged; this allocation covers only this PR's regression growth.
- Fixed the hosted review's `Tokens` capitalization finding. The existing run-history consumer test was reproduced red on `1.2M tokens`; after restoring `1.2M Tokens`, the run-history and token-i18n suites pass (7 tests). This was the sole failed test in the previous `checks-ui (1/3)` run.
- Local autoreview completed at P0 with no findings; the broader local attempt timed out. Both concrete hosted-review findings (English capitalization and test allocation) are addressed.
- After integrating main `041a0941490d6a22ab182df5dbb90848f53a66b1` for its landed CI repairs, the five focused regression/consumer suites pass: 19 tests. Catalog verification, UI typecheck, and diff checks also pass.

## Current upstream blockers
Before the integration, all 28 failed UI tests on head `14c9ef59fc5db3d2662bc2712a986e368559db62` reproduced on untouched main `3bbf77af66fb0459e297cc6fa873aebed2e5568d`. Integrated the landed upstream toast-test repairs from #192431 rather than changing unrelated tests in this PR.

After integration, the same ten affected suites now have 301 passing tests and 13 failures. All 13 remaining failed-test names also reproduce in an isolated, untouched checkout of main [041a0941490d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/041a0941490d6a22ab182df5dbb90848f53a66b1), across sidebar interactions, model-provider priority, dialog preparation, and attachment feedback. These remain upstream blockers outside the localization lane.

The test-line ratchet also remains blocked by inherited main debt. Untouched main `041a0941490d` reports 6,446,904 lines against a 6,446,759 ceiling: 145 lines over, delta zero. This PR reports 6,447,081 lines against a 6,446,936 ceiling: the same 145-line debt, plus exactly 177 added lines and a matching 177-line allocation. No shared baseline increase or allocation for unrelated debt was made.

## Maintainer-directed exception
`control-ui-performance` is intentionally left red for maintainer handling. title: fix(qa): prevent cron fallback rescue and verify owner model transcript
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191570 — found during its real behavior proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two stale assumptions in the cron owner-conversation repair QA scenario: a fallback can rescue its deliberately failed runs, and chat history intentionally omits the scheduler's repair request.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. The QA scenario can exercise the intended owner-repair path and verify both the repair request and reply without requiring internal scheduler inputs to appear in the user-facing chat feed. No production changes, configuration migration, or user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Disable model fallbacks in both `agents.defaults` and `agents.entries.qa`, matching `provider-http-503-visible-failure.yaml`.
- Replace the `chat.history` check with the existing `readQaSessionTranscriptEvents(env, ownerSessionKey)` helper and assert against the owner's model-transcript events.

The scenario introduced in #161007 predates #173416, which intentionally hides `internal_system` / `cron_failure_repair` inputs from chat history, the chat feed, and pending inputs while retaining them in the model transcript. The source contract is confirmed in `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.history.ts` and `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.automation-repair.test.ts`. Increasing chat-history limits cannot fix this check. The helper is already exposed by the QA flow runtime; no new helper or product behavior is needed.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

The following four runs were performed and reported by @holgergruenhagen on a Mac with current main `57405d6f170`, using `mock-openai` and:

~~~sh
pnpm openclaw qa suite --scenario cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation
~~~

1. **Main unchanged — fails for fallback rescue:** `expected failed run 1`; the run has `status: ok` because the configured fallback rescues the scripted failure. This independently matches the initial sandbox reproduction, which recorded `fallbackUsed: true`.
2. **Main + fallback-only PR — fails at the stale history check:** the owner session repairs the job and fixes the step file, then the scenario reports `the repair turn is not in the owner session transcript`.
3. **Same candidate, unbounded and expanded chat-history reads — same failure:** neither omitting `limit`/`maxChars` nor using `limit: 1000`, `maxChars: 500000` reveals the request. Owner history contains five messages, including `Fixed the sync step file. QA-CRON-REPAIR-FIXED`, but no repair request; no other session's history contains it. The Gateway log identifies the repair prompt under `agent:qa:qa-channel:group:group:qa-cron-failure-repair`. This is the intended display projection, not truncation or wrong-session routing.
4. **Main + both changes — passes all 3/3 steps in 93.5 s:** `repairRequests=2`; the step file is fixed; the reply is `Fixed the sync step file. QA-CRON-REPAIR-FIXED`; the unowned control job still sends its failure alert.

Independent sandbox replay on checkout `99652357adba0bbfcdaa18277b7d26ea9d3dffce` plus the exact two-part scenario patch also passed:

~~~sh
pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation \
  --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/cron-repair-transcript-retry
~~~

~~~text
exit code: 0
scenarios: total=1 passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0
steps: 3/3 passed
repairRequests=2
stepFile="Sync step fixed by the owner conversation.\n"
reply="Fixed the sync step file. QA-CRON-REPAIR-FIXED"
control: unowned job failed twice and sent its failure alert
~~~

An earlier sandbox attempt timed out waiting for the initial owner reply, before reaching the changed assertion. The fresh isolated-Gateway replay above completed successfully; the earlier timeout is not counted as passing.

Static checks: `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt --check`. Simplification/inspection: one YAML file only, retaining the existing fallback configuration pattern and the existing transcript helper; no production change.

## Worked on by

- @holgergruenhagen

<!-- openclaw-publication:ae51b845-ff5f-479c-83a7-29222d0d466d -->

## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3e244ef9-af8e-4e16-96a6-5d826da7bbb3)

title: fix(usage): avoid transcript scans when archive preparation fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage refresh scans uncheckpointed SQLite history before discovering that an archived transcript cannot be expanded. Discovery commits no new rollups after that failure, so later background triggers can repeat the scan.

## User Impact

Refresh prepares file-backed archives before collecting SQLite transcript statistics. A failing archive keeps its visible error and avoids unrelated transcript scans. The archive still needs operator repair before discovery can succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reorder preparation in the existing collection owner. The worker already sorts stale files independently and retains complete inventory for pruning. No cache, cadence, schema, retention, or decompression-limit changes. Related: #180195; this does not add per-session failure isolation.

Production: +7/-5, net +2. Tests: +9/-11, net -2. The existing real-worker I/O case asserts archive rejection and zero statistics reads, then restores its fixture. Two marker fixtures now reuse their already prepared canonical scopes; every assertion is preserved. No test allocation or shared baseline change.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: an oversized archive must reject real-worker refresh before any uncheckpointed SQLite transcript statistics are read.

- [Red on test-only head `efe6baedacf1c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41718321921/job/126205824642): the assertion receives one unbounded `transcript-stats` read instead of zero. Remaining baseline jobs were cancelled after capturing that failure.
- [Green on candidate `629d4f6e71bc8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41718321349/job/126205329255): all 12 usage I/O tests pass; the owning shard passes 564 tests. This covers archive cancellation, incremental append/rewrite, selectors, historical filtering, pruning, quarter backfill, and metadata failures. The changed case takes 5.259 s; the file's 12 reported test durations sum to 50.802 s in this shared CI shard, which uses real database workers and lifecycle cleanup.
- [Required build passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41718321349/job/126205283596); all five core lint stripes, production types, and both core test-type stripes passed on that candidate.
- [Final-head worker I/O proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41725448014/job/126229994770) passes all 12 usage I/O tests on Bun, including the changed case (1.619 s), on `b6b972cc707b0e270cabfbfa85c24a060e5d0495`. Final-head build, selected type/lint checks, test-line ratchet, and the CI gate also pass.
- Supporting synthetic DB check through the actual collection source: 17 archive failures cause 17 statistics scans on base and zero with the fix. That check excludes Gateway lifecycle and worker transport; the real-worker CI above supplies that boundary proof.
- Codex-backed autoreview at P0–P2 is scoped clean for the final candidate snapshot, now committed as `b6b972cc707b0e270cabfbfa85c24a060e5d0495`, against `99652357adba0bbfcdaa18277b7d26ea9d3dffce`. Whitespace check passes. Local heavy checks were prohibited on the production host; build and worker proof ran in hosted CI.

The broad manual campaign is not green: both heads show the same locale fallback-baseline drift and the same two unused exports outside this patch. The candidate also has a checkout timeout and other test failures, including a startup-maintenance assertion that passed on baseline; those additional failures remain unclassified. Normal PR CI on `629d4f6e71bc8` passed its runtime/build/lint/type jobs and failed only the test-line ratchet: inherited debt of 355 lines rejects any net test growth. title: fix(ui): stop counting queued subagents as running
body:
## Problem

On mobile Control UI, the chat working line said **"20 subagents running"** while the composer's Subagents chip said **"8 working"** for the same session. The working line (and the session header's "Subagents · N running") counted every unfinished child, including children with `status: "queued"` that are still waiting for a concurrency slot. Details already counts queued children separately from Working ones.

## Solution

`chat-subagent-wait.ts` owns both counts. `countRunningSubagents` (header) and the `running` value from `projectSubagentStatus` (working line) now leave out queued children, using the same rule as Details' Working count. The handoff wait still includes queued children, because the parent is still waiting on them.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `chat-subagent-wait.test.ts`: 2 running children plus 1 queued child. Without the fix it fails (`expected 3 to be 2`); with the fix it passes, for both the working line and the header count.
- `pnpm test` on `chat-subagent-wait`, `chat-pane-child-roster`, `chat-pane-header` and `chat-working-indicator`: 73/73 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files: clean.
- A one-off Control UI e2e at a 390×844 mobile viewport with a mock Gateway (3 running children, 2 queued; not committed). Before the fix the line read **"5 subagents running"** next to **"3 working"**. After the fix it reads **"3 subagents running"** next to **"3 working"**. Screenshots are in a PR comment.

## Test cost

The dedicated 19-line allocation accounts for this PR’s existing regression coverage without changing production code, tests, or the shared baseline. The scoped staged guard still reports 355 excess lines, exactly the same debt as its comparison base after accounting for the 19-line test and allocation deltas. title: fix(update): keep exec SecretRefs cold during private rehearsal
body:
Closes #192066
Reported-by: [mtblackman16](https://github.com/mtblackman16) in #192066.

## What Problem This Solves

Update rehearsal can reject a healthy installation when an exec SecretRef needs credentials that intentionally remain outside disposable scratch state. The private candidate now leaves that capability cold and records an availability warning while validation continues.

## User Impact

An unavailable exec-provider prerequisite during private rehearsal produces a recorded warning rather than a failed update check. The existing snapshot receipt carries that warning into the update run report. Authored SecretRefs remain references; normal Gateway activation still checks credentials against the serving installation. Structural reference errors and explicitly required data/auth owner policies retain their checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rehearsal must not execute real secret providers or touch real credentials. Resolving against the real state root would cross that boundary even if intended to be read-only, because arbitrary exec-provider code can read or write there. The shared resolver therefore defers exec dispatch under the complete private-rehearsal contract, and the existing owner-isolation path leaves optional and legacy capability inputs cold. No credential files or resolved values are copied into rehearsal state, and no config option, schema, SDK contract, or protocol is added.

## Evidence

- Final candidate `3f317d88cc4a58df7e972c4758fa39cdf2a0262b` rebases patch-identically onto main `a12e3ae8d85d1f86263054bcd44687b082c710ba`, including budget repair `53a21b7062791c72bf6b2db2adbbb78d7ffae387`. All three commits match the remotely tested patch; secrets, rehearsal/startup/test files and dependency manifests are unchanged. Fresh final autoreview: scoped-clean P0–P2, confidence 0.81.
- **Red on base:** test-only `7e1582e89eb3704c99fb4a39e0cb87e40224bdce` changes only the two regression files and their allocation relative to 9b0. The cold-owner case fails with `SECRET_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`; the real Gateway startup fails because required secrets are unavailable. Malformed-ref control passes. This is actual test execution after an independent frozen install; earlier detached-worktree dependency setup failures are excluded.
- **Green on 60ac:** resolver 2/2, actual Gateway canary 1/1, rehearsal resources 26/26, and `pnpm build:runtime` passed on one granted Crabbox/Testbox lease, [run41726628941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41726628941). The lease was stopped after commands joined, so the enclosing lease workflow concludes cancelled; its successful command results are execution proof, not green PR CI.
- **Production rehearsal:** `validateUpdateCandidateCanary` completed in 17.968 seconds through snapshot, child Doctor, lint/config/plugin/recovery checks, child Gateway startupz/readyz and cleanup. title: fix(ui): keep commentary's tool call inside its activity group
body:
## Problem

In chat, commentary followed by a tool group could leave its own tool call in a standalone row. `coalesceToolActivityMessages` merged the commentary into that call's invocation row; `chat-thread-grouping` then classified it as an assistant group to keep the text visible. Later calls formed a separate activity group.

## Solution

- Split prose/media and identified tool calls into separate rows in source order. Mixed `text, call, text, call` messages keep their order, including calls without merged results.
- Prepared activity belongs only to invocation rows, not their split prose. Raw calls still count correctly when the source has no prepared activity.
- When tools are hidden, remove call-only rows but retain handoffs, permission requests, and accompanying content on anonymous calls that cannot be split into identified rows.

User text accompanying `tool_result` blocks now also gets its own row rather than appearing inside the tool group. Reasoning stays in order beside calls rather than inside a nested raw-details log.

## Screenshots

Captured from a Control UI e2e scenario (`installMockGateway`, synthetic history: commentary + call, a second call, a reply).

| Before (main) | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: standalone tool row beside commentary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87a8028f-77d8-4cc9-a22c-577acf4f2dab) | ![After: one activity group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b52d934-b05f-4f4c-8774-aa9e9d64c065) |
| Commentary, then standalone `Recheck ratchet` and `Ratchet numbers` rows | Commentary, then one `2 commands` activity group |

## Evidence

- The original split regression failed on main and passed with the fix. The committed coalescer test now covers text and thinking interleaved with calls, and verifies prepared activity appears only once. The hidden-tools regression verifies commentary survives an anonymous call.
- Final independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) found two defects on `b4031469`: duplicated prepared activity on prose, and lost commentary beside hidden anonymous calls. Both were reproduced with failing tests and fixed. Follow-up autoreview of the repair relative to `b4031469` found no actionable P0–P2 defects; only whitespace changed afterward. The repair is committed in `4993df67`.

title: fix(ui): pause queued messages after Stop
body:
## Problem

Pressing **Stop** while messages wait in the composer queue previously sent the next queued message as soon as the aborted run ended. The `aborted` terminal event drained the queue just like `final`.

## Solution

Stop parks the rows waiting when it was pressed.

- `handleAbortChat` records never-attempted queued rows before the abort request, because the terminal event can beat its response. This covers Stop, Esc, typed `stop` and `/stop`.
- `chat-queue-pause.ts` keys those rows by Gateway owner and conversation scope, shared across panes. `drainStoredChatOutbox` skips parked rows unless the user explicitly retries, steers or saves an edit.
- Messages submitted after Stop are not parked, including a correction typed before the abort settles.
- A row above the queue reads **Queue paused · You stopped the run**. **Clear** discards parked rows; **Resume** releases them in order. The notice disappears once the parked rows are gone.
- The notice uses the queue rows' icon column and text inset. Both actions now use **neutral muted text and icons**, a neutral text hover state and a soft hover surface—no accent/red foreground or filled pill. The secondary reason truncates first on narrow widths.

Normal completion, errors and Gateway-side aborts keep draining as before.

## Accepted edge cases

- The pause is in memory per tab; reloads and other tabs do not preserve it.
- If the abort request fails, the rows remain parked behind a visible Resume.
- Gateway-held follow-ups retain the Gateway's existing Stop policy; this parks browser-held rows only.

## Latest color correction — validation blocked

At Vyctor's request, `7cbbc8353bbc3f93662b20be3206da1761e682b7` adds `.chat-queue__resume` to Clear's neutral default and hover selectors. No layout or behavior changes.

Source inspection confirms both selectors use the same neutral theme tokens. Fresh light/dark screenshots and local checks could not finish: the execution service repeatedly stalled and reported child-cleanup hard-deadline failures. Both the full E2E runner and a focused component-browser route were attempted. title: fix(desktop): extract Windows updates with zip 9.2.2
body:
Related: #192032. Credited maintainer replacement of Sebastien Tardif’s patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows desktop update extraction still locks ZIP 4.6.1, which falls inside the published CVE-2026-115909 and CVE-2026-115905 ranges.

## User Impact

Windows ZIP installer archives use ZIP 9.2.2 while preserving the existing behavior that leaves the desktop app open when installer launch fails. Linux and macOS retain their tar paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pinned Tauri updater requires ZIP 4. The available crates.io [updater 2.14.1 performs Windows cleanup before installer launch](https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/blob/updater-v2.14.1/plugins/updater/src/updater.rs#L1017), reversing the shipped recovery fix. Preserve the exact pinned fork source in a documented local copy, expand its workspace settings, and raise only its Windows ZIP requirement. Remove the vendor copy when a released updater includes both ZIP >=9.0.5 and the existing launch-recovery behavior.

All 17 copied files other than Cargo.toml match steipete/plugins-workspace 63e8185eb184cf0af6b665f631e2314c7b14d9c6 by Git blob identity. Signature verification still precedes installation; cleanup still follows successful ShellExecuteW. Download signatures reduce exposure to malicious archives but do not make the affected dependency desirable.

## Evidence

- Current head d24acc5c1d6261d8086856cbba473f62bf429216: [native Windows power/runtime/installer/desktop boundary tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41714019527/job/126189451234) passed; [macOS companion tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41714019527/job/126189450618) passed; [Linux companion build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41714019527/job/126189450081) passed. The Windows job also builds the installer without publishing; landing requires every exact-head check to complete successfully. The successor corrects co-author trailer grouping and has identical product bytes to the independently reviewed candidate.
- Original contributor head 7bb6a29a634b645d6c3ec2b6b018a4fcf36d99da: 39 successful and 53 skipped checks, including the native Windows desktop test/build and Linux/macOS companion builds. This is prior-head evidence; this replacement requires its own exact-head green CI.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the complete replacement delta against fd3538294f7ad410557683629941439bd156420c: scoped-clean P0–P2, confidence 0.88. No repository code was executed during review.
- git diff --check passed. No contributor code, package staging, broad tests, or containers ran on the production Team host.
- Runtime gap: native Windows ZIP extraction/installer launch proof remains unrun. A task-owned AWS Crabbox native Windows lease was granted but its OpenSSH bootstrap never became ready during the bounded attempt; no product payload ran. The replacement’s exact-head native Windows CI test/build is the selected proof route; a separate installer-launch exercise is not claimed.
- No UI-driven latest-stable upgrade, release-signature download, or real installer upgrade is claimed.

Simplification: this replaces the remote pinned updater source with a byte-identical local source owner so the incompatible ZIP dependency major can change without reverting shipped launch recovery. The 20-file delta is +3,391/-27 lines; most growth is the unchanged dependency source. No test-only production hooks, config options, state formats, or changelog entries were introduced.
