title: improve(ui): clarify settings access and save feedback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings failures were terse, the shared access denial exposed an internal permission scope, and terminology varied across navigation, forms, profile access, secrets, and Labs. Trigger-word errors also needed clearer summaries while preserving existing display redaction.

## User Impact

Clearer failure summaries and next steps, neutral admin requirements, sentence-case labels, and consistent plugin/device terminology. Unsaved drafts, retries, reconnect behavior, permission checks, config keys, and routes are unchanged. Trigger-word tests now guard the existing sensitive-value redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep copy in the existing English catalogs and retain the existing UserFacingError/display-redactor path. Tests exercise that path with a synthetic credential rather than introducing a second redactor.

The shared config capability does not identify whether the browser or the member lacks access, so it now says “You need admin access to change settings.” It does not guess a reconnect or team-admin remedy. The internal `nodeHost` section remains the same service, labeled “Device service.”

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Save failed | Couldn’t save settings. Try again. |
| Settings not applied | Couldn’t apply settings. Review your changes. |
| Configuration changes require operator.admin access. | You need admin access to change settings. |
| No items yet. Click “Add” to create one. | No items yet. |
| No settings match “{query}” | No settings match your search. |
| Plugin management and extensions | Manage plugins and their settings. |
| Node Host | Device service |
| Host Desktop / Cloud Worker Desktop | This computer’s desktop / Cloud device desktop |
| Administrator access is required to manage secrets. | You need admin access to manage secrets. |
| Could not save trigger words: {error} | Couldn’t save trigger words. Try again. + existing redacted detail |

## Evidence

- 184 focused unit tests passed across settings save/status/sidebar, config writes/search, Talk, Profile/reconnect, and Labs.
- 31 mocked browser tests passed: 10 guarded-config save/reconnect tests and 21 agent/config/secrets consumer tests.
- Matched light-theme save-failure captures passed with the original and updated summary; the crop waits for a fully visible card.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` completed with no generated changes; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed.
- Touched-file oxfmt and oxlint passed (0 warnings/errors); `git diff --check` passed.
- Startup delays and worker-start failures were resolved through the supported Node entrypoint; they were setup failures, not product results.

Before (origin/main save-failure copy, mocked Gateway, light theme):

![Before: terse settings save failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0698d7b8-997c-4382-b5ee-4eb29cdba582)

After (same mocked failure and retained draft):

![After: actionable settings save failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7f2e948-09d9-4708-948e-1a7706623a40)

### Boundaries and follow-up

Existing secondary details remain in place: the settings save indicator, config-form rejection reasons, secrets partial failures, and trigger-word errors. Trigger-word details remain redacted; no competing details component was introduced. Deep technical/raw-schema text and unrelated channel/provider/plugin copy are not part of this pass.

The local real-Gateway profile E2E could not start: the preparation guard could not verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts. No managed artifacts were rebuilt. The updated assertion is included; this lane still needs the approved isolated runner or CI.

CI and landing are left to the parent maintainer workflow.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:c7fa6cd9-86ca-4f79-ac67-a08eb6efd9e3 -->

Landing integration retains the Labs warning that experiments can change, break, or disappear and applies the infrastructure subtitle separately. It preserves the newer actionable settings-load errors and Device service casing. All 59 focused Labs/Profile cases passed, with i18n baseline/verification, scoped lint, formatting, and whitespace checks. Existing broader settings and browser proof is reused. A 26-line allocation covers the actual test growth; the inherited 183-line overage is unchanged. The final merge with current main is clean.

title: improve(ui): clarify connection and sign-in recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves
Connection recovery mixes “Offline,” technical authentication labels, and inconsistent Gateway/sign-in wording. Switching Gateways also warns about “that host” without naming the destination.

## User Impact
Recovery uses “Disconnected,” clearer next steps, and consistent sign-in language. The switch warning names the destination. Forgetting a browser still clears its saved sign-in for one Gateway, signs this tab out, and preserves other Gateways, preferences, and device identity. No permissions, authentication policy, storage behavior, or retry timing changes.

## Why This Change Was Made
Applies Vyctor Brzezowski’s approved Control UI glossary to the L2 connection area. English stays in its existing startup/lazy catalogs; technical token/password labels and diagnostic details remain available. The only presentation wiring change passes the destination host into the translated switch warning.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Offline | Disconnected |
| Showing stale data. | Showing last known data. |
| Connection to the Gateway was interrupted. Reconnecting automatically. (WebSocket {code}) | Disconnected. Reconnecting automatically. (WebSocket {code}) |
| Connection to the Gateway was interrupted. Check your connection and try again. (WebSocket {code}) | Disconnected. Check your connection and reconnect. (WebSocket {code}) |
| Could not verify access. | Couldn’t verify access. |
| This link asks the browser to connect somewhere else. | This link connects to a different Gateway. |
| Anything you enter after switching goes to that host. | Anything you enter after switching goes to {host}. |
| The link also carries a token for it. | This link includes a token for that Gateway. |
| Your saved credential for {host} stays here and is not sent. | Your saved sign-in for {host} stays here and isn’t sent. |
| Saved sign-in for this gateway | Saved sign-in for this Gateway |
| Activity refresh failed. Retrying… | Couldn’t refresh activity. Retrying… |
| Connect to see Gateway activity. | Reconnect to see activity. |
| no auth / token auth / password auth / proxy auth | No sign-in / Token / Password / Proxy sign-in |
| This Gateway expects its token/password. | Enter the Gateway token/password. |
| Reconnect this browser to the current Gateway to troubleshoot a stuck connection. | Reconnect to the current Gateway to try again. |
| Pairing QR expired | Pairing code expired |
| Run /pair qr again to generate a fresh setup code. | Run /pair qr again to get a new setup code. |
| Gateway endpoint, credentials, and handshake status. | Gateway connection and browser sign-in. |
| Ask your server administrator to review your access. | Ask an admin to review your access. |

Also shortens the forget-browser explanation, uses contractions for unapplied changes, and gives session-list recovery errors “Couldn’t…” summaries while retaining raw details.

## Evidence
- Mocked Control UI, synthetic data, light theme; inspected and cropped before/after captures below. No live Gateway data or secrets.
- Gateway status and Connection settings E2E: 3 files / 7 tests passed, including desktop/mobile retry, automatic recovery, and applying a replacement Gateway.
- Browser-auth recovery/loading, connection bootstrap, Gateway observers, refresh status, Logs, Profile, and Usage unit coverage passed; changed English assertions updated.
- Connection page: 26 tests passed with one fork worker; Gateway status pure contract and URL confirmation isolated test passed. The dialog regression checks destination interpolation and the current Gateway’s sign-in warning.
- English baseline regenerated (no baseline-file delta); i18n verify passed. Touched-file oxfmt, oxlint, and diff checks run. Oxlint reports one existing style-prop warning on the unchanged wrapper.
- Independent review caught that forgetting a browser removes browser-wide saved device authorization, not only tab-local sign-in. The final confirmation explicitly distinguishes “this browser’s saved sign-in” from signing “this tab out.”
- Docs audited; Connection settings instructions updated. The /pair qr command is retained.

### Before
![Before: connection settings and saved browser sign-in](.openclaw/tmp/copy-l2/before-cropped.png)

### After
![After: clearer connection settings and saved browser sign-in](.openclaw/tmp/copy-l2/after-cropped.png)

### Gaps and unchanged scope
The dashboards stale-banner E2E file was updated for the shared copy but its standalone harness could not start: Vite reported `TypeError: code.charCodeAt is not a function` on both default and fork-worker attempts. No product assertion ran in those attempts. An intermediate connection-page run also hit worker startup/late-modal timing failures; the final fork-worker run passed all 26 cases.

The shared F1 “Show details” contract is absent on this base. Per the task’s fallback, raw details remain: WebSocket codes in connection.interrupted/interruptedRetrying, redacted GatewayStatus lastError tooltips and existing Connection details, and {error} in connection.sessionMoveRefreshFailed, sessionMoveUncertain, and sessionOperationCompletedPreviousConnectionWithRefreshError. The last three now have clearer summaries. No competing details component or new status state was introduced. Existing CLI setup-code help remains unchanged.

No native app/plugin copy, foreign locales, translation memory, CI watching, or landing is included.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:317b716d-2274-4b2a-983a-91892ef128aa -->

Landing repair updates only the failed copy assertions still present in the integrated tree. All 66 affected unit cases, three sidebar recovery cases, and the diagnostics browser case passed. The already-correct session-controls test is unchanged, and the unrelated toast geometry failure remains with its owner. Formatting and whitespace checks passed; the original connection and sign-in proof is reused. The merge with current main is clean. A six-line allocation covers the actual integrated test growth.

title: improve(ui): clarify channel setup and DM access copy

Channel setup and DM access messages use internal terminology, unclear permission guidance, and ambiguous wording after a successful approval.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the approved Control UI glossary within the channel hub, setup/settings, WhatsApp status, and DM access queue. Keep pairing-review permission distinct from admin access and command ownership. title: improve: render chat composer mentions inline
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected people should behave as whole inline mention chips, not an avatar followed by an independently editable name or a painted overlay. Earlier revisions also lost recipient identity during some editing/history operations.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show one atomic avatar-and-name chip using the sent-reference styling. The caret cannot enter its letters; selection and deletion respect the whole chip. The extra “Will notify” strip is removed. Raw messages and clipboard text remain canonical `@Name` text with selected recipient spans. No new dependency or configuration change.

Straight and curly possessives attach directly after selecting a person. Read-only/disabled composers reject rich paste and composition mutations. Undo/redo preserves recipient identity for repeated names and across the first native-to-editor handoff, including same-text selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lazy CodeMirror editor owns layout, selection, history, clipboard, and composition. The hidden textarea is only the established raw-value/controller port; it is not a visible overlay. Current-main integration preserves the moved dictation owner and lazy reply preview, and routes remaining focus/selection callers through the shared editor bridge.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen, with @vyctorbrzezowski’s atomic-editing and manual-testing requirements. The possessive issue was reported by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion and initial implementation with @Patrick-Erichsen and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/31236f32-4426-45a7-be8f-b1aed8f96632)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e42589fc-b3f8-4478-8032-adc37344a926)

## Author response to the acceptance report

Current head: `a7bb4e2d44ef41de71f8451f761ab7dcbe214973`. The report below was run on `4ae188c3` and is unchanged. Two commits follow it: `005d8712` fixes the report's three findings, and `a7bb4e2d` applies an independent review. Neither has been retested in the macOS app, in Safari or on a phone.

### The report's three findings

| Finding | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Backspace also navigates back (macOS app) | The editor forwards each key to the hidden textarea as a copied event. Copying the whole event also copied WebKit's legacy `keyIdentifier`, and WebKit runs default actions for an untrusted keydown that carries it: Backspace goes back in history, Tab moves focus. | Forwarded keys are built from named fields only. |
| 2. Safari drag moves part of the selection | WebKit delivers a fast first `mousemove` before `dragstart`. CodeMirror treats a move of 10 px or more as a new selection, so the drag started with a smaller selection. | The editor remembers the selection that was grabbed and restores it at `dragstart`. A press that ends without a drag forgets it. |
| 3. Long names clip at 320/390 px | Chips were `white-space: nowrap`. | A chip is one inline box. It moves to the next line whole, and a name wider than the composer wraps inside it. |

Long name in a narrow composer, before and after:

![Before: long mention name clipped at the composer edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5edf0b50-02d9-4329-aa3c-489397527a31)

![After: long mention name wraps inside its chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d481a99-32c8-4822-a3df-31574e28a837)

### Independent review

An isolated read-only reviewer agent read `cda0b61a..005d8712`, focused on the code changed since the earlier full review and on iOS and WKWebView risks. It ran nothing. Outcome: no P0, two P1 and eight P2. This was not a local ClawSweeper or autoreview run; a hosted ClawSweeper review is still due when the PR leaves draft.

Fixed in `a7bb4e2d`, each with a test that fails on `005d8712`:

- **Backspace dead key.** Backspace beside a separator the chip needs put the caret back where it was, so every further press did nothing. It now steps over the separator.
- **Unreadable selection.** Selected text in the rich editor used CodeMirror's light default, which is light on light in the dark theme. It now uses the app selection color, focused and blurred.
- **Mobile resting capsule.** After sending a message with a mention, the retained empty editor kept its full height in the one-line capsule. It now rests like the textarea.
- **Undo after send.** A native snapshot from before the owner cleared a sent draft could seed undo history when the next mention was inserted without typing. A snapshot is now used only when the selection replaced it. Accepted edge: a sent draft ending in a plain `@word` still passes.
- **Stale grabbed selection.** A tap inside a selection could leave a selection for a later touch drag to restore.
- **Dragged move reported as typing.** A move now reports `insertFromDrop`.
- **Scrollbar.** `scrollbar-width: thin` made Chromium ignore the app's 8 px scrollbar that the overflow padding assumes. With real scrollbars the old head measured a 10 px bar against 8 px of padding; the new head measures 8 against 8. This one has no automated test, because headless Chromium hides scrollbars.

Selection in the dark theme, before and after:

![Before: selected text is light on a light highlight](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4df4a82-7956-42fb-b964-8dfc47d4330a)

![After: selected text on the app selection color](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c6a4acc-038e-4783-aa6f-8eeadf61d144)

Rejected, with reasons:

- **"Programmatic focus into the editor never sets mobile editing" (P1).** The editor's content element carries `contenteditable="true"`, which the existing check already matches. Confirmed in a browser.
- **"A paste replayed after the editor chunk loads can land in the next draft" (P2).** This needs a first-ever recipient paste, a slow chunk load and a send in between. The result is visible and recoverable, and a guard would add always-loaded code.

Named by the review as worth checking on a device, not confirmed as bugs:

- IME composition next to a chip on iOS keyboards.
- Whether the software keyboard stays up when the first mention mounts the editor on iPhone.
- Caret position in the macOS app, where each selection change also writes to the hidden textarea.

### Proof on this head

- 124/124 unit cases and 145/145 Chromium browser cases passed, with UI types, lint, CSS lint, format and the test-line ratchet.
- **WebKit 27.2 (Playwright's Linux build, not Safari or the macOS app)**, using the shipped editor module: Tab from the editor lands on the next stop (two stops away on `4ae188c3`), and the reported drag moves the whole selection (`A@Alice Morgan  right-side-endBC ` on `4ae188c3`). Finding 1 was not reproduced as back navigation, only through this shared Tab mechanism.
- The repository's WebKit browser-test lane could not connect on this host, so the browser suites ran in Chromium only.

### Asset size

- Against the branch base `cda0b61a`, `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passes: Chat boot JS +693 B, New boot JS +819 B, total CSS +40 B gzip and +50 B raw.
- **Against main `5cef30a3` it fails** (local trial merge, not pushed):
  - Chat boot JS measures 1,303,841 B against a 1,303,711 B limit, 130 B over. This PR adds 882 B there.
  - New boot JS on main alone measures 806,388 B against its 805,886 B cap, so only 64 B of growth is allowed. This PR adds 623 B.
- No thresholds were raised. This needs an owner budget decision or a reduction before the PR can pass that check. Local sizes can differ from CI by a few hundred bytes.

### Other points from the report

- **Twelve-ID synthetic clipboard.** Intended. The composer cannot hold more than 10 recipients, so it never writes such a clipboard. Foreign metadata that claims more than 10 is rejected as a whole and pastes as plain text. Pasting into a draft that would exceed 10 keeps the existing recipients and binds only up to the limit, which is the 10+2 case that passed. The original handoff wording for item 6 was wrong.
- **Attachment focus (item 15).** Also on main, as the report says. Not changed here.

<!-- maintainer-acceptance-2026-11-12:start -->
## Inline composer mentions — full test report

**Two editing regressions and one visual regression were confirmed against main. I would not consider the tested head ready to merge.** No fixes were made during testing. These results apply to the exact revision below, not automatically to later changes.

### Scope and environment

- Candidate: `4ae188c349e1ba45e9ef7a9e5bfcdabd482e52eb`, branch `roboclaw/composer-inline-mentions-20261103`.
- Matched main: `fb83d658cf3b6257a43b322c1e701ba757a0d546`.
- **Real isolated Gateways**, authentication, sends, durable history and authenticated recipient Inbox reads. **Only the model was a local response stub.** Provider/model behavior was not validated.
- 24 synthetic profiles covered a crowded picker, duplicate display names, a long name, non-Latin names, photos/initials and a failed-photo fallback. Recipient IDs, not just display labels, were checked.
- Chrome **157.0.8103.39 headless** on macOS **27.0.1**, plus Chrome **157.0.8103.79** with real OS keyboard/mouse in a disposable macOS **26.6.2** VM.
- Firefox **160.0**: headed native-OS lanes plus separate headless WebDriver lanes. Safari **26.6.2**: actual Safari, native-OS and separate WebDriver observations.
- Actual macOS app **2026.11.3, build 2611000390**, built at candidate, on macOS 26.6.2. Native A/B held the executable constant while UI/Gateway switched between main and candidate. SHA-256: `a1d2188e763cd2bdb3ed1708dd5e90b89173ac7396a05e0f3c446f199bb1ac89`. No `apps/macos` source difference exists between the compared revisions.
- The app's shared-password **Owner** fixture cannot send bound human mentions without a signed-in human. Main has the same policy. Native delivery items 1/2/21 remain unqualified; this does not excuse unrun editing/layout tests.

### Coverage

**92 rows: 23 handoff items × 4 surfaces**, each with Chat and New Session results. These are coverage cells, not test-execution counts.

**PASS:** applicable subcases supported. **FAIL:** contrary result observed; notes identify pre-existing behavior. **NT / partial:** whole item remains not tested, but some subcases passed. **NT:** not qualified as a whole, including blocked setup. **N/A:** explicitly inapplicable. Partial coverage never becomes a whole-item pass.

Across 184 cells: **67 PASS, 7 FAIL, 110 not tested**, including **6 N/A**. Seven failing cells represent the three new findings and the pre-existing Chrome attachment-focus behavior in both contexts, not seven new defects.

New Session has no conversation prediction/history or pre-creation split-pane surface. No dedicated focus-composer shortcut was identified in the inspected catalog. Mention/slash/skill menus use composer-wide anchors; emoji uses the caret. These applicability/design facts are not failures.

The undo acceptance sequence was: type `hi @al`, select Alex, undo back to `hi @al`, then redo the same recipient chip; separately cut/undo a chip and verify that undo after sending does not resurrect the sent draft. Boundary checks used `'s`, `’s` and an immediately following letter. Clipboard checks distinguish copied chip metadata from plain external `@Name` text. For IME, only observed marked composition and its committed result counted.

### Chrome

| # | Handoff item | Chat | New Session | Evidence boundary / remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pick and send | PASS | PASS | Correct recipients, durable sends and authenticated Inbox receipts. |
| 2 | Same-name recipients | PASS | PASS | Both Alex IDs survive edits; each receives the same message. |
| 3 | Undo/redo, cut, post-send undo | PASS | PASS | Undo/redo, native cut/undo and empty post-send undo verified. |
| 4 | Clipboard round trips | PASS | PASS | Same composer, another Chat, New/second tab and TextEdit verified; plain return does not notify. |
| 5 | First paste after reload | PASS | PASS | Empty reload followed by first OS paste restores IDs. |
| 6 | More than ten mentions | NT / partial | NT / partial | Normal 10+2 paste retains 12 names / 10 bindings. Literal 12-ID clipboard remains separate; see diagnostic below. |
| 7 | Text and file drag-and-drop | NT / partial | PASS | Chat: cross-split and Finder pass; internal Chat OS drag not repeated. New: internal drag and Finder pass; pre-creation split not applicable. |
| 8 | IME composition | PASS | PASS | Real Japanese marked composition before/after chip and in restored draft passes. |
| 9 | Unavailable editor / recovery | NT / partial | PASS | Chat: picker/recovery pass, blocked OS paste missing. New: unbound paste, negative Inbox receipt and explicit-reload recovery pass. |
| 10 | Atomic chip editing | PASS | PASS | Arrows, Backspace and whole-chip selection verified. |
| 11 | Possessive / letter boundaries | PASS | PASS | Straight/curly possessives attach; a following letter gets a space. |
| 12 | Send keys, prediction, history | PASS | PASS | Send preferences and unindented newline pass; Chat prediction/history pass. Those two are not applicable to New. |
| 13 | Menus with a chip | PASS | PASS | Keyboard operations preserve IDs. Mention/slash/skill anchor to composer; emoji anchors to caret. |
| 14 | OS text services | NT | NT | Spellcheck/autocorrect, text replacement, OS emoji picker and dictation not fully exercised with chips. |
| 15 | Focus and tab order | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL also on main: attachment removal focuses BODY; attachment-menu Escape focuses trigger. Click/type-to-focus and common tab order verified. |
| 16 | Growth and scrolling | PASS | PASS | 80-line draft grows/scrolls; text x stays within 1 px; horizontal scroll stays zero. |

### Finding 1 — Backspace also navigates backward in the macOS app

**Severity: major. Surface: actual macOS app; Chat and New Session.** Versions and exact candidate/main heads are above. This is a navigation/editing regression, **not demonstrated permanent text loss**.

1. Visit a Chat, then open New Session so Back has a previous destination.
2. Type `ab @Ali`, choose **Alice Morgan** through the real picker, then append `cd`. Complete draft: `ab @Alice Morgan cd`.
3. Focus the native accessible text area and put the caret immediately after the mention (exported AX caret `[16,16]`).
4. Press native **Backspace** without modifiers. A control also used a CGEvent with empty modifier flags.
5. Repeat in Chat with New Session as its preceding history entry. Use **Forward** to inspect the retained draft.

**Expected:** remove the whole mention and remain editing on the same screen.

**Actual:** the chip is removed **and the app navigates to the previous page**. Deleting an ordinary character with the rich mention editor active also reproduced navigation.

**Frequency/control:** candidate **2/2 New Session, 2/2 Chat**. Main stayed in the current screen in both controls. Executable, shared-password setup and enabled prediction were held constant. Main's older text representation deletes a character rather than a chip; the matched invariant is **no navigation**, not identical token deletion.

```text

After Forward: ab  cd
New case AX label: "What should this session work on?" → "Chat composer".
Chat case: inverse navigation.
```

Forward recovered the edited draft. No send occurred. AX observations/screenshots support this result; **no equivalent DOM dump or JavaScript console capture exists for this exact sequence**. Cause was not isolated or fixed.

### Important boundaries and excluded conclusions

**Normal overflow versus a synthetic 12-ID clipboard.** Copying ten real mentions and pasting into two existing mentions retained twelve names with ten bindings. This is not one clipboard containing twelve distinct bindings pasted into an empty editor. The UI does not itself produce a twelve-binding clipboard. A separate synthetic OS-clipboard producer supplied twelve valid IDs: text survived but **all bindings were rejected**; its ten-ID control was accepted. Keep this literal-handoff discrepancy separate from normal UI copy/paste. It is not established as a new regression, and the synthetic diagnostic was not repeated in every surface/context.

**Unavailable editor: picker selection and paste are different.** The fault target was `composer-editor-mentions-*.js`, including identity/gzip/Brotli representations. Cache hits do not qualify as induced load failures.

- Chrome New qualified the source clipboard, empty prestate, blocked load, plain paste with no binding, normal send with no `humanMentions`/matching Inbox, and same-payload recovery after unblocking/reload. Chrome Chat lacks its own blocked-native-paste subcase.
- Safari New case **83** showed visually plain paste during genuine 404 and a chip after exact restoration plus same-tab reload. **No metadata read or send receipt proves absence of a recipient for that paste**; item 9 remains partial.
- Safari case **84** chose a person through the picker while the asset was missing. Its send retained **Alice[17,30]** and generated **one authenticated Alice Inbox receipt**. A plain-looking fallback does not imply missing recipient metadata. This positive picker receipt cannot substitute for a negative paste receipt.
- Firefox hard reload retained cached rich editor during server 404, and later recovery paste was unqualified. The native app likewise retained its rich chip and a pairing dialog interfered with focus. **Neither has a qualified fallback/recovery transition or a product-failure verdict.**
- Initial fault setup still served gzip from memory and was aborted; only verified 404 windows counted. Exact hashes and HTTP 200 were restored afterward. These recovery claims require **explicit reload**, not automatic recovery.

**Other controls and invalidated attempts:**

- Initial headless partial-drag and unsuccessful mouse-transfer observations were not treated as native OS regressions. Safari's later matched OS gesture is the separate confirmed finding above.
- An early paste copied the address-bar URL rather than the intended selection and was excluded. The later empty-prestate/clipboard-controlled result is counted.
- Initial queue probes had empty draft/unsettled handoff. Only final hold→queue→release→recipient receipt counts.
- Early skill probes expected a hyphenated raw slug. Canonical normalization produces `mention_fixture_skill`; corrected keyboard selection passed.
- Immediate-reload suffix loss did not reproduce in three controlled blocked-chunk trials. Initial main-only-selector mistakes and a session-switch probe that stayed in the same logical session were excluded.
- Attachment removal focusing BODY and attachment-menu Escape focusing its trigger also occur on main. They are reported in coverage, not attributed to this PR.
- Bound mentions prevent Incognito sending on main too; this restriction is not new.
- IME required real marked composition, not merely a Japanese input source producing Latin letters. Safari's independent textarea failed qualification. A later invalid Firefox attempt does not erase earlier genuine composition evidence.
- Delaying a real local `sessions.create` request showed **Starting** and a new composer, not a remotely pending placement lock. No UI property was altered to fabricate this state. The real `users.setRole` read-only result applies only to the Chrome run that executed it.
- Large-paste checks prove preservation and continued input with error/geometry observations where stated. They are not comparative latency benchmarks or a blanket performance guarantee.

title: improve(ui): mark Incognito with a dashed composer instead of a banner
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Incognito chats have a two-line limits banner under the header and a labeled pill before the title, but no desktop composer marker. Replace that intrusive chrome with quieter, persistent visual cues.

## Solution

- Remove `ChatPaneIncognitoNotice`, its header/pending/mobile plumbing, and superseded CSS.
- Move the desktop header indicator into the trailing actions as an icon-only button. Its accessible name and clickable retention tooltip remain; the existing mobile indicator remains.
- Use one shared dashed-composer rule in all themes, including focus and dictation. Owners pass the same Incognito decision used by the header, including canonical-key fallback and pending creation.
- Add a neutral top shade: theme ink at 7% in light mode, black at 32% in dark mode, fading below the header to transparent by 240px. Match the transcript-edge blend to avoid a visible band.
- Scope shading to the **visible cached pane**, not the whole cache/cell. Hidden Incognito sessions must not tint regular replacements.
- Remove the obsolete sole-child header fragment left after deleting the banner, keeping the compiled boot path smaller.

No session-retention or permission behavior changes. The creation page's lifetime/limits copy stays; `/new` itself is unchanged.

## Final landing evidence

Final source: `0a7d1dab4a3188088212dd06121c3446fc3feb2f`, published as `95718932a317e34a0d432b8bec391f5e8077e78f`. The exact CI comparison base `1139abee8063e7f6447a0329cdac394090b47cc3` was integrated to reproduce the chat-boot growth failure; no conflict-driven or speculative refresh.

- Header plus style-browser regressions: **38/38 passing**, 8.55s wall time on the integrated base. Both retained-pane theme cases fail against pre-repair CSS and pass with visible-pane ownership; isolated style run 1.18s.
- Real Control UI with mocked Gateway: `new-session-page.instant-thread.e2e.test.ts`, **15/15 passing**, 36.90s wall time on the integrated base. Covers pending admission, confirmed chat, rollback and navigation, including the dashed composer before creation completes.
- Bundle comparison against `1139abee`: chat boot JS gzip **1,282,215 → 1,282,153 B (-62 B)**; CSS raw **1,665,936 → 1,665,930 B (-6 B)**; CSS gzip **322,908 → 322,921 B (+13 B)**. All budget gates pass under the existing 64-byte build-variance allowance; no budget was raised.
- Test-line allocation **59**: 10 net composition-regression lines plus the 49-line retained-pane style fixture. The shared scalar stays unchanged. Gate passes against the integrated base.
- UI typecheck, earlier applicable UI-test typechecks, CSS stylelint, formatting, commit-hook line-cap checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent source review found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper was killed by its memory bound. The documented autoreview fallback completed on the final `1139abee..0a7d1dab` range, P0–P2 scope: **no actionable findings**. The reviewer did not independently execute tests or verify images; the lead did. One hosted re-review was requested on the earlier repair and remains advisory.

Inspected light/dark desktop and phone screenshots are delivered in chat and embedded in the [final visual proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192240#issuecomment-6621111856), alongside the [original before/after comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192240#issuecomment-6614745824). These captures remain applicable: the final wrapper deletion preserves the same single header DOM element and changes no presentation rule.

## Simplification and accepted edges

The repair removes the multi-stop gradient machinery and obsolete header fragment, reuses the existing transcript blend, and keeps one visible-pane shading owner. It retains the requested look within both bundle budgets.

Inactive split-view cells hide their header actions, including the icon; their dashed composer remains. The shade covers chat panes, including pending creation, not `/new`. Screenshots use synthetic fixtures, not live user data.

title: fix(ui): People and session hovercards switch to other rows while moving to them
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the sidebar People list and the session list, moving the mouse diagonally from a row toward its hovercard crosses other rows, and each crossed row immediately replaces the card. Today you have to steer straight across your own row to reach the card. Session links share the session hovercard and had the same problem.

## User Impact

User impact: you can move straight toward a person's or a session's card, even across other rows, and the card stays. Moving straight down the list still switches cards right away, and stopping on a row switches to that row.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared portaled hovercard owner now has a safe-triangle hover-intent check, the same corridor Zag uses for the submenus we already ship (Zag's `isPointInPolygon` ray casting over the card's near edge). When a mouse leaves the trigger while its card is open:

- The corridor runs from the pointer's last point inside the trigger to the card's near edge, and includes the card. While the pointer stays inside it, the card stays open.
- Any trigger crossed on the way waits. It takes over only when the pointer rests on it for 150 ms or leaves the corridor while still over it.
- If the pointer leaves the corridor anywhere else, the card closes normally.

Gotchas from Floating UI `safePolygon`, Amazon's menu-aim, and our own testing:

- **Sparse samples:** fast moves can land the exit event well past the row edge and off the line toward the card. So the corridor apex is the last point *inside* the trigger, clamped to the trigger, not the exit point.
- **Boundary jitter:** the apex backs off 4 px from its edge so that jitter on the edge stays inside.
- **Adjacent triggers:** this is the case where Floating UI added `requireIntent`. We switch on rest instead of on cursor speed, so careful, slow movement toward the card still counts as intent.
- **No pointer-events blocking:** we don't block pointer events (Floating UI's `blockPointerEvents` side effects). Crossed rows still show hover styles; only the card handoff waits.
- **Touch and window exits:** touch input and leaving the window keep the existing 220 ms timed close. Only mouse and pen exits that the owner can observe use the corridor.

Two consumers use the corridor:

- **People rows** (first commit).
- **Session rows and session links**. The session hovercard provider passes pointer exits to `schedulePointerExit(event)`, and a target hovered while the pointer is still heading to the open card goes through `deferPointerSwitch`. Rows and links share one provider, so both get the behavior.

Other hovercard consumers keep the old `schedulePointerExit()` behavior.

## Evidence

People:

- New Control UI e2e `sidebar-users-filter.e2e.test.ts` › "keeps a person card while the pointer crosses other people toward it", driven by real Playwright mouse moves on a paused virtual clock. It covers three paths:
  1. A diagonal path to the card's lower half across Bob and Jacqueline keeps Ada's card.
  2. A straight sweep from Ada to Bob switches within the normal 80 ms.
  3. Resting on Bob inside the corridor hands the card to Bob after the rest delay.
- **Red on base** `331c1aed9a2`: the same test fails at the crossing assertion (`expected +0 to be 1`: the card closed or switched). **Green with the fix.** The other three tests in that file also pass.
- `ui/src/components/portaled-hovercard.test.ts`, `app-sidebar.people.test.ts`, `app-sidebar-online.test.ts`, `portaled-hovercard-focus.test.tsx`: 122 passed.

Sessions:

- New Control UI e2e `session-progress-hovercard.e2e.test.ts` › "keeps the session card while the pointer crosses other rows toward it", with real Playwright mouse moves on a paused virtual clock: a diagonal path to the card's lower edge crosses two rows, and the card still shows "First aim row" 600 ms later.
- **Red without the session commit** (the corridor owner plus the old session consumer): `expected +0 to be 1`, because the card closed. **Green with it.** The rest of that file passes, including the existing open/sweep/close timing test.
- `session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts` and `session-hovercard.test.ts` (46 passed) and the session hovercard browser tests (2 passed).

Both:

- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxfmt `--check`, oxlint, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex, `--max-priority P1`): scoped-clean for the People branch against `origin/main` and for the session commit against the People commit. Its stated limitation: it reviewed diffs only and did not execute the code.
- The session proof ran on the same tree as the session commit (cherry-picked unchanged onto the People commits).

Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/hovercard-hover-intent-corridor.txt` allocates the 102 net test lines added by the two e2e regressions above. Each one is the red/green proof for its fix, and neither duplicates an existing test.

Control UI performance: CI on `8d918a2` measured chat boot JS at 1,295,263 B gzip, against a base of 1,294,259 B and a limit of 1,294,652 B: 611 B over. Two behavior-preserving trims follow, measured with local `ui:check-performance --report-only` builds:

- The corridor builds its polygon from the card rect and inlines Zag's ray-casting check, so the boot chunk no longer carries the unused `@zag-js/rect-utils` rect helpers: −315 B.
- Person references and SKILL.md hovercards had identical document-level Escape handlers; the portaled hovercard owner now provides it as `handleEscape`. A duplicate touch check in session hovercard registration is dropped, because `sessionProgressHoverTargetFromEvent` already rejects touch: −314 B.

Local chat boot JS: 1,282,499 → 1,281,870 B (−629 B). Local absolute numbers differ from CI's, so CI on this head is the budget check. After these trims: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxfmt, oxlint clean; 202 unit tests (person reference, SKILL.md hovercard, session titling/target/hovercard, People sidebar, portaled hovercard and focus), the 7 placement browser tests, and both e2e files (12 tests, including both regressions) pass.

Gaps: WebKit was not run locally. The host was heavily loaded, so the e2e tests use a paused clock instead of wall-clock timing.

title: feat(ui): auto-load older sidebar sessions on scroll
body:
## Problem

To see older sessions in the sidebar you have to click **Load more sessions** at the bottom of the list. Reaching the end of the list should load the next page by itself, but only where the new rows show up at that end.

## Solution

- `RosterLoadMore` watches the existing button with the shared `createIntersectionObserver` helper. When the button comes into view, it calls the same owner action as a click (`loadMoreSidebarSessions`).
- It loads one page each time the button comes into view. If the new rows land off-screen, or a load fails, the button stays where it is, so nothing fires again until the user scrolls away and back. That prevents request loops without any retry or backoff state. The owner's existing `sessionsLoading` guard still drops overlapping loads.
- The observer callback only loads when the host's `effectiveSessionsGrouping() === "none"` and `effectiveSessionSortMode() !== "people"`. These owner methods are now part of `SidebarSessionListHost`, so no new prop is threaded through the list.
  - **Auto-loads:** flat list ("none"), sorted by created or updated time. Older rows mostly land at the end of the single ungrouped section, and the existing visible-limit bump shows them.
  - **Stays manual:** custom groups (`category`, which also adds the smart group/coding zones), `person`, `project`, and the People sort. In these views the new rows go into earlier sections or between existing rows, not at the bottom.
- The button stays as the manual fallback, the loading indicator and the keyboard/screen reader path.

Accepted edge cases:

- If the flat list is short enough that the button is already on screen when the sidebar opens, one page loads straight away. Nothing more loads after that.
- In flat view, a page can still land above the fold. Created order sorts by creation time while the server pages by update time, and session catalog sections sit below the native list. In those cases, auto-load still loads at most one page each time the button comes into view, the same as a click.
- If you switch to the flat view while the button is already on screen, nothing loads until it scrolls out of view and back.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-load-more.e2e.test.ts` cases with a 40-row first page and a 600px-tall viewport:
  - `none`: scrolling the button into view requests the sidebar's `offset: 40` page with no click, and the button goes away. **Fails on base** (the request never happens), **passes with the fix**.
  - `category`: scrolling the button into view sends no paged sidebar request. Clicking it still loads.
  - Request matches are scoped to `source: "sidebar"`, because the chat pane follows the mocked cursor too.
  - The existing hidden-only page tests still pass (4/4).
- `app-sidebar.session-feedback.test.ts` now installs its pending page before switching to the flat view, because the visible button may start that page itself. 10/10 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean. The only lint warning (`solid(reactivity)` in `renderSessionList`) was already on base.
- Test-line growth (+73) is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/sidebar-auto-load-more.txt`.
- A fresh independent review returned "ready". Its one actionable item (the gate comment overstated the guarantee) is fixed.

## CI status

All checks pass except these two budget gates. `main` is already over the limit for both:

- **`control-ui-performance`:** `main`'s chat boot JS is 1281327 B, over the 1281063 B cap. The gate therefore allows at most 64 B of growth, and this PR adds +184 B. Reading the gate from the host instead of a new prop brought it down from +239 B.
- **`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test-lines):** `main` is over its test-line ceiling, so any positive net delta fails, even when it is allocated.

No visual change. The button looks the same; only what triggers it changed.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ui): cap the Subagents summary at two statuses
body:
## Problem

The Details → Subagents summary shows every status at once (Working, Waiting on subagents, Queued, Done, Stopped). The counts wrap onto several rows and Done ends up mid-row, so the summary stops working as an at-a-glance signal.

## Solution

The summary now shows at most two statuses. `projectDetailsSubagents` decides which ones; the component and CSS only lay them out.

- **Anything working** (waiting parents count as working): Working beside the avatars, then **Queued** on the right if anything is queued, otherwise **Done**.
- **Nothing working but some queued:** Queued, then Done.
- **Only finished:** Done beside the avatars.
- **Failed and stopped runs count as Done.** Agents usually retry or spawn a replacement around them, so Stopped never gets a status of its own. The per-row list still shows each child's real outcome.

The second status is always pushed to the right. The first status uses the primary text color.

The per-row list and the collapsed "N subagents running" header are unchanged.

title: fix(ui): send selection comments as message text, not files
body:
## Problem

"Add to chat" selection comments were staged and uploaded as `selection-comment.txt` attachments. Queued rows showed `selection-comment.txt, selection-comment.txt`, the transcript stored a file per comment, the model received the selection as an attachment, and the action was gated on uploads being enabled.

## Solution

A staged selection comment now becomes part of the user message at send time: each comment is rendered as a Markdown quote of the selected passage followed by the comment, in order, ahead of the user's own text. No file is delivered.

- `chat-send-submit.ts`: selection annotations contribute message text through `annotationMessageContext` (shared with browser annotations) and are excluded from `deliveredAttachments`. The uploads check only applies to real files.
- `chat-selection-attachment.ts`: adds `formatChatSelectionQuote`. The staged text payload stays only for local draft persistence and is never sent.
- `chat-view-frame.ts`: "Add to chat" no longer requires uploads to be enabled.
- Goals now refuse selection annotations the same way they already refuse browser annotations, so a comment cannot be dropped silently. The shared copy reads "annotations" instead of "browser annotations".

Commands keep the existing behavior: annotations stay staged until the next real model prompt.

Older transcripts that already contain `selection-comment.txt` still render through the existing sent-comment path (covered by the rewritten lifecycle e2e test).

## Screenshots

Mocked Control UI, 1100×760, dark theme. Each case adds a comment from the assistant's passage, then sends "Also summarize the risks." while a run is active.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queued | ![before queued](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d7d9c65-0fe4-4756-b6f8-25019393a2d0) | ![after queued](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0fa005a-60a9-4127-b23f-d01f958fb3ce) |

Before: the comment is a separate file-backed `1 comment` chip. After: the passage is quoted inside the user's own message, followed by the comment and the typed text.

## Evidence

- `chat-send-submit.annotations.test.ts`: the selection case fails on base (message lacked the quote and still sent a `text/plain` file) and passes with this fix.
- UI unit tests (chat-view, comment controller and preview, session rail, goals, send annotations): 225 passed.
- Control UI e2e (`chat-selection-to-main`, `chat-comment-lifecycle`, `chat-comment-draft-recovery`, `chat-comment-pane-retirement`, `settle`): 24 passed. They assert `chat.send` carries the quoted comment in `message` with no attachments, including ordering with the draft, multi-line selections, and comments kept across `/clear`.

title: fix(ci): keep native update fixtures on the selected Node runtime
body:
## Problem

The native systemd stage of [scheduled CI run 41674175748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41674175748/job/126063141279) failed with `Fixture runtime differs from controller`: the controller used Node `v24.22.1`, while the unprivileged fixture user resolved system Node `v22.23.4`.

CI installs its selected Node below a private runner temporary directory. Adding that directory to a fixture user's `PATH` does not make its ancestors traversable, so command lookup falls through to the system runtime.

## Change

Copy the controller's Node executable into the existing world-traversable fixture runtime directory, and put that directory on the fixture user's `PATH`.

title: fix(ui): keep collapsed Details sections collapsed for the session
body:
## Problem

If you collapsed **Processes** (or another section) in Session Details, it could open again later while a process was running. Session Details kept collapse choices in component state tied to each mount. Coming back to a session after its chat pane was dropped (each pane keeps only 3 recent sessions) remounted Details, which reset every section to its default and opened Processes again.

## Solution

`chat-details-session.tsx` now keeps disclosure choices in a module-level map, keyed by the session identity it already uses (session key + agent + session id). The map holds entries only for the current page load and is bounded with the existing `session-cache.ts` LRU helpers (20 sessions).

- A new session (including `/new`, which changes the session id) still starts with sections expanded.
- Once you collapse a section, it stays collapsed for that session after remounts, until the page reloads.
- Nothing is persisted: no settings, schema or browser storage changes.

Accepted edge case: if you visit more than 20 sessions, the oldest choices fall out of the cache and those sessions go back to the defaults.

## Evidence

- New Control UI e2e test in `ui/src/e2e/session-details-background-work.e2e.test.ts`. It collapses Processes, lets the processes leave and come back, then visits 4 other sessions so the pane is dropped. It checks that the old Details element was disconnected (a real remount), then returns and expects Processes to still be collapsed.
  - **Fails without the fix** (`aria-expanded` is `"true"` after the remount); **passes with the fix**. All 3 tests in the file pass.
- Without the fix, collapse already survived processes leaving and coming back, closing and reopening Details, and a Gateway restart. The only failing path was the pane remount.
- `chat-details-session.test.ts`, `chat-details-arrival.test.tsx` and `chat-details-output-intent.test.tsx`: 31/31 pass.
- `run-tsgo -p ui/tsconfig.json`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared QR view now resolves camera authorization before constructing VisionKit’s scanner and refreshes authorization when the app becomes active. This also covers Settings and ESP QR scanning. Onboarding no longer writes a transient opening message to its persistent status line; queued QR results, actual errors, and reconnect suppression keep their existing lifecycle.

- [Chris’s device report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192118#issuecomment-6613230664): iPhone 16, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2, based on `595322e4dc38c5f886ada0efb2365e680295afd7` with identified local fixture and selector changes. The fixture blob is `ef75abe3752922495ce0cdaa7abe79f51ca161d9`, matching the supplied patch. Personal signing/bundle settings and generated personal Info.plist changes are excluded. - Independent full-patch review and the local equivalence check found the two fixture extractions behavior-preserving: identical ordered messages, payloads, IDs and timestamps; reversing the extractions restores the entire original file byte-for-byte. Both correctly retain the existing `now` value.

title: improve(test): speed up config save browser tests
body:
Related: #191958 (clock and owner-proof precedent)

## What Problem This Solves

Config-save browser tests spend real time waiting through secret-field idle windows and saved-revision polling.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same 14 cases pass faster: summed file medians fall from **54.607s to 46.819s**, saving **7.788s (14.26%)** on the measured Testbox.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install the existing Playwright page clock before navigation. Advance every original 1.5s/1.2s secret idle window in full, retaining the zero-write assertions, then resume normal time for neighbor autosave. Advance time between Apply-status reads so the real config polling owner, mock WebSocket responses, and promise settlement still determine the result.

Typed, cleared, template/include, Cancel, exact Save payloads, RPC acknowledgments, Saved-before-Apply, external-edit/reload values, and all geometry assertions remain. No production change, direct refresh, fabricated state, timeout change, or injection seam.

The resize comparison now waits for the shell's actual CSS transition to finish before taking its reference box. The earlier candidate exposed the existing same-frame stabilization poll accepting a still-moving layout; its failed geometry run is excluded from the final timing samples. The coordinate-stability poll and both exact box assertions remain.

The simplification pass kept this within the two existing test fixtures. Test delta **+16/-4, net +12 lines**; the requested `config/test-lines-allocations/ui-config-clock.txt` records the 12-line justification. Including that two-line record, the complete delta is **net +14 lines**. Production delta: zero.

## Evidence

Three baseline and three final candidate runs used the **same Blacksmith 16-class Testbox** `tbx_01m6h3yv7sfjwg54xn4r0bnef4`, with frozen-lockfile installation: [Testbox run 41674898066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41674898066). All six measured runs passed all 14 cases. The file numbers below are native Vitest file durations, including hooks, rather than command wall time or a CI critical-path claim. Baseline source: `868609a3f6cb9d736d89b577b57ebedb899d5d4f`. Candidate commit: `33800a46f58b063383e016526341c328b61775b0`.

| File under `ui/src/e2e/` | Baseline median | Candidate median | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `config-secret-field-save.e2e.test.ts` | 10.429s | 7.324s | 3.105s |
| `config-safe-write.e2e.test.ts` | 44.178s | 39.495s | 4.683s |

<details>
<summary>Three samples and relevant case medians</summary>

| File | Baseline samples (s) | Candidate samples (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config-secret-field-save.e2e.test.ts` | 11.536 / 10.429 / 10.106 | 7.324 / 7.302 / 8.618 |
| `config-safe-write.e2e.test.ts` | 44.178 / 45.918 / 40.470 | 39.957 / 39.495 / 37.034 |

| Case | Baseline median | Candidate median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| reports autosave without moving the page and preserves untouched 64-bit identifiers through reload | 6.774s | 2.952s |
| preserves a refreshed external edit after reverting a retained Raw draft | 6.027s | 3.569s |
| holds a secret field while the field beside it keeps autosaving | 3.416s | 2.249s |
| replaces a stored secret on Save, and leaves it alone on Cancel | 2.193s | 1.423s |
| keeps a stored secret read-only when the file holds a template or an include | 3.818s | 2.237s |

Command, repeated three times per version:

```sh
corepack pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/config-secret-field-save.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/config-safe-write.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json=<sample-report>
```

</details>

All paired mutation controls ran on the same Testbox. Mutations changed production behavior temporarily and were restored between executions. **Killed** means the existing test failed; **survived** means the selected existing tests passed.

| File | Product mutation | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Secret field | Send the held secret through `config.patch` after 750ms, inside the claimed idle window | Killed: zero-write assertion | Killed: same assertion |
| Secret field | Disable `config.apply` submission | Survived: 4 passed | Survived: 4 passed |
| Secret field | Replace the field Save patch with `{}` | Killed: exact patch assertion | Killed: same assertion |
| Safe write | Send held secrets early | Survived: 10 passed | Survived: 10 passed |
| Safe write | Disable `config.apply` submission | Killed: Apply RPC wait | Killed: same wait |
| Safe write | Replace submitted config bytes with `{}` | Killed: identifier and exact payload assertions | Killed: same assertions |
| Safe write | Drop refresh adoption while a draft is dirty | Killed: `original-api` instead of `external-api` | Killed: same assertion |
| Safe write | Disable the applied-revision polling owner | Killed: both targeted Apply-status waits | Killed: same waits |

The two cross-file survivors also survive on unchanged baseline tests. The other file owns the missing behavior and kills the same mutant in both versions:

- Early secret writes are owned by **“holds a secret field while the field beside it keeps autosaving”** in `config-secret-field-save.e2e.test.ts`: `expect(await gateway.getRequests("config.patch")).toHaveLength(0)` fails with one early request. The cleared-secret case also fails its zero-write assertion. Safe-write has no secret field.
- Apply submission is owned by **“edits schema and raw config with guarded set, patch, reload, and apply requests”** in `config-safe-write.e2e.test.ts`: it awaits `gateway.waitForRequest("config.apply")` and asserts `expect(applyParams.raw).toBe(rawDraft)`. title: improve(ui): clarify goals, questions, and recovery copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Goals, question recovery, and provider review use inconsistent names for sessions and replies. Some storage failures are hard-coded English, and failure messages do not consistently explain what to do next.

## User Impact

- Uses **session**, **reply**, and **device** consistently in this scoped flow.
- Keeps storage and send failures actionable without losing draft/recovery guarantees.
- Resolves both persistence messages through i18n when shown, rather than caching English strings.
- No changes to delivery, replay, goal state, provider approval, protocol keys, or foreign locales.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Conversation changed. Cancel and select Goal again. | Session changed. Cancel and select Goal again. |
| Save without starting a run. | Save without starting a reply. |
| Interrupt this turn, update the objective, then resume the goal. | Interrupt this reply, replace the objective, and resume the goal. |
| Chat paused as a precaution | Session paused as a precaution |
| Could not send your answer. Your draft is preserved. | Couldn’t send your answer. Your draft is still here. Try again. |
| Received · waiting for worker setup | Received · setting up device |
| Could not store the previous draft in browser storage. It remains available in this tab. | Couldn’t save the previous draft. Keep this tab open or copy it before reloading. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to goals, async questions, outbox recovery, and provider review. Existing translation keys are preserved. The two exported English constants become translation functions, with all callers migrated together. Documentation and assertions quoting changed copy are updated.

Four test lines are allocated solely for formatter wrapping of actionable strings; no new scenarios or duplicated fixtures were added. Self-simplification retained the existing state and UI owners.

title: fix(ui): keep the latest message out of the session hovercard
body:
## Problem

The session hovercard's task area is meant for progress reports. When a session had no progress card, it fell back to the session's latest message preview, so a user turn (for example "Land") appeared in that box as if it were task progress.

## Solution

Remove the latest-message fallback. The task area now renders only the progress card (commentary/plan/heads-up). With no progress card, the hovercard shows title, attribution, context, and pull requests only.

- `HovercardExcerpt` and `writeHovercardExcerpt` (the three-line clamp search) and the `.session-hovercard__excerpt` styles

- `ui/src/e2e/session-hovercard-excerpt.e2e.test.ts`, which only covered the excerpt clamp

Sidebar row subtitles still use `lastMessagePreview`. This change does not affect them.

title: fix(ui): stop truncating peer names on mobile footers
body:
## Problem

On phones, a shared-thread peer message footer truncated names that easily fit the screen (reported: "Vyctor Brzezows…" at ~375–390px wide).

Cause: on mobile the peer group grid capped its content track at the message width (`--chat-message-column-max`, 82%/88%). The footer lived in that same capped track, and its reserved touch controls (reply, rewind, copy, react, time — kept in the layout while hidden so revealing them never moves the row) took most of the remaining width. The name was left with ~96px while the rest of the row stayed empty.

## Fix

In the mobile layout, peer groups put the width cap on `.chat-group-messages` instead of the grid track. Bubbles keep exactly the same width (the avatar column and gap are 0 on mobile, so 82%/88% of the area is the same as before). The footer now gets the full row, so names that fit are shown in full. Resting and revealed geometry stay the same, so nothing moves when the controls appear.

Accepted edge case: very long names on very narrow screens (e.g. "Alexandria Montgomery-Winter" at 320px) still ellipsize, which is intended.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the real Control UI against the mock gateway: peer "Vyctor Brzezowski" at 375px with reactions enabled. Before, `scrollWidth 99 > clientWidth 98` and the name read "Vyctor Brzezow…". After, it renders in full in both the resting and revealed states.
- Regression assertion added to `chat-attributed-identity.e2e.test.ts`: at rest, a fitting peer name is not truncated at 390/430px. It fails on base (35px hidden) and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e` on `chat-attributed-identity`, `chat-flow.reactions`, `chat-reply-attribution`, `people-activity-card`: all passing (including the existing stable-footer and tap-target assertions at 320/390/430).
- `ui` browser tests `chat-responsive` and `chat-content-column` (mobile message widths): 70/70 passing.
- oxfmt check and `git diff --check` are clean.

Before/after screenshots (375px, resting and revealed) are shared in the originating chat.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: improve(ui): clarify session devices and stop actions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session placement and stop controls use “worker”, “runner”, and “turn” where people need to know which device is involved and what stopping it preserves.

## User Impact

- Session setup, recovery, and runtime-update notices use device and reply terminology.
- Active cloud placements say **Stop cloud device…**. Paired devices and unknown placement targets no longer inherit cloud-only stop language.
- The cloud dialog explains that the device is released while the conversation and accepted changes stay. The paired-device dialog says that other sessions keep running.
- Desktop, browser, terminal, pairing, portal, and process errors identify the failed action and a next step. Uncertain terminal delivery still tells you to check before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the bounded D3 pass of the approved Control UI glossary. Stop copy uses the existing placement owner: active placement without a paired-device runner identifies a cloud device; nonactive or unknown placements stay neutral. This does not change stop/reclaim, synchronization, retry, or permission behavior.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Choose worker… | Choose device… |
| Runner failed | Couldn’t continue this session |
| Device offline | Device disconnected |
| Stop cloud worker… | Stop cloud device… |
| Stop worker? | Stop this cloud device? / Stop this session on the device? |
| device-service · device-profile | Cloud device · device-profile |
| Wait for the active turn to finish… | Wait for the current reply to finish… |
| Installing worker runtime | Preparing this device… |
| Could not load desktops | Couldn’t load desktops. Try again. |
| Terminal delivery could not be confirmed… | Couldn’t confirm command delivery. Reconnect to check the terminal before trying again. |

The paired stop description is a complete interpolated sentence, rather than concatenated English around the device name. Menus consume the stop owner’s recorded copy decision. Confirmation copy has one catalog owner. Documentation quoting changed controls is updated. No foreign locales, translation memory, protocol keys, native apps, or plugin-owned copy were changed.

## Evidence

- **408 original touched unit tests passed** across 17 files. CI exposed additional direct consumers; their repaired assertions passed **157 tests** across eight more files. The final stop-owner simplification also passed **82 focused tests**.
- **51 original browser scenarios passed**, including 18 dependent boot-module boundary scenarios. The final owner simplification passed six focused menu/device-stop scenarios; the last assertion repair passed three browser screenshot/download/upload scenarios.

- Touched-file oxlint passed except the existing Sessions test file’s max-lines violation: **1,068 counted lines on both base and head**. The initial CI fixture literal-widening error is fixed and all UI test-type shards pass.

Before:

title: improve(ui): show errors with a next step and collapsed details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI errors can mix a recovery message with a raw diagnostic. This makes a small save failure noisy and gives people inconsistent ways to inspect its cause.

## User Impact

Migrated errors show a next step first, with diagnostics behind collapsed “Show details.” Existing redaction, retry, dismissal, links, and toast placement are preserved. A new error resets an open disclosure; unrelated updates do not.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing config-error, toast, lazy-panel, and chat owners rather than adding a competing error pipeline. Dashboard-default saves and Labs settings are representative callers, not a UI-wide copy rewrite. No new state store or dependency.

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard default save | “Could not save the dashboard default: {error}” | “Couldn’t save the dashboard default. Try again.” + collapsed details |
| Labs setting save | “Could not update feature” + diagnostic | “Couldn’t save this setting. Try again.” + collapsed details |
| Lazy panel | “Panel failed to load” / “Something went wrong while loading this panel.” | “Couldn’t load this panel.” / “Try again.” |
| Error disclosure | “Details” | “Show details” |
| Chat startup | “Couldn’t start this conversation. Open Settings → Logs for details.” | “Couldn’t start this session. Try again.” |

**Deliberately preserved:** existing caller-owned chat recovery text (for example, “Session is busy; wait for the current run to finish.”), specialized reply/stop errors, and stale-file recovery instructions. Those producers do not yet separate summary from diagnostics; replacing their instructions with a generic retry would regress recovery. Later copy PRs can migrate those producers explicitly.

## Evidence

- Shared toast/panel regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix: collapsed state, expansion, and redaction. Desktop/mobile chat regressions cover replacement lifecycle and preserve caller recovery instructions.
- Initial focused suite: **210 tests passed across 11 files**. After CI/review repairs: **69 focused tests passed**, then **29 chat tests passed** with the recovery regression; the exact chat test-type partition and UI typecheck passed. Touched-file oxfmt/oxlint, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks passed (only pre-existing sidebar lint warnings in the broader run).
- Final attachment-read lifecycle production-bundle E2E: **17 tests passed**, including failed rewind retaining its draft. Both screenshot scenarios passed in an isolated source export with mocked Gateway failures.
- Final local boot comparison against `e5bd90ed866fb7656ece78250a46e8d0a343cfe0` passed: chat boot JS **1,280,907 → 1,280,694 B gzip (-213 B)**; **20 → 20 requests**. Total CSS **320,638 → 320,638 B gzip (+0 B)**. No budget/baseline increase.
- The **69-line test allocation** matches net added test lines. The local ratchet reports inherited ceiling debt; this change does not increase that debt or raise the shared baseline.
- Local ClawSweeper reviews and an independent review completed. Both substantive findings were fixed: reset disclosure on replacement, and preserve caller-owned recovery guidance. CI also caught a test-only DOM typing issue, now fixed and checked in the exact type partition. No hosted re-review loop was requested.
- Final repaired source: `150873b4f033ad95ced58f880bd2cb12b9718a50`; current publication: `85a96b28bf0976f6402a870d7c52c9e1a32fd5d1`. Current-head CI remains the landing gate; earlier-head results are not treated as current-head proof.

### Visual evidence

Inspected synthetic diagnostics, light theme, identical 1280×900 viewports; crops preserve the captured geometry. Toast/panel visuals are unchanged by the later chat recovery fix.

title: fix(ui): tighten mobile chat message action spacing
body:
## Problem

On mobile (touch / ≤768px), the chat message footer icons (reply, copy, add reaction) sat far apart and unevenly. Each button got `margin-inline: 10px` so its 44px-wide `::before` touch target would not overlap a neighbor. That pushed icons 24px apart (48px center to center). The reaction trigger didn't get the margin, so the last gap was smaller (38px).

## Solution

- Mobile action rows drop the flex gap. Every action, including `.chat-reaction-action`, owns `margin-inline: 4px`, so all icons sit on one even 32px center-to-center rhythm.
- The transparent `::before` hit area fills the button's own margins (32px wide). It still grows up 44px over the group's own message, never into the turn gap. Hit areas never overlap a neighbor and never overflow the row's box, so session-activity rows keep zero horizontal overflow.
- The 44px-wide `--chat-touch-target` token is removed (this rule was its only consumer). Desktop is unchanged.
- The attributed-identity e2e tap-area contract now expects width ≥ 32 (was 44). Height stays ≥ 44, and all four corners must still hit the button. This follows the explicit product direction not to space icons out for 44px-wide targets.

## Screenshots

Mock Control UI, `--fixture reactions`, 390×844 touch, dark. The real DOM is captured with nothing injected.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: reply, copy and reaction icons spaced 48px then 38px apart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67845398-53db-4918-ad43-6b800fc78c18) | ![After: reply, copy and reaction icons evenly spaced 32px apart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76795444-6a57-4d84-b26d-4a1ed4e38c1c) |

## Evidence

- New `chat-message-footer-actions.browser.test.ts`: reply→copy visual gap ≤ 8px at 390×844 and 1366×900. It fails on base (`expected 24 to be less than or equal to 8`) and passes with the fix.
- Measured icon x positions (reply / copy / reaction) in the reactions fixture. Before: 134.5 / 182.5 / 220.5 (48/38 steps). After: 128.5 / 160.5 / 192.5 (32/32 steps). Every footer item shares one vertical center (cy 257.3).
- `ui-e2e`: `chat-attributed-identity`, `chat-mobile-bubble-margin`, `chat-message-actions`, `chat-flow.reactions` and `chat-transcript-focus` pass locally.
- `chat-responsive.browser` and `chat-message-footer-actions.browser` pass. stylelint and oxfmt are clean.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against main: chat boot JS -94 B, chat boot CSS -18 B. It passes, and the CI `control-ui-performance` job is green.
- Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/mobile-chat-action-spacing.txt` allocates the 47 lines of the new browser regression test. This is the only coverage of the mobile action spacing, and it fails on the base. `check-test-lines-ratchet` passes locally against main (slack 30).
- Earlier e2e failures (`chat-skill-library`, `activity-session-feed.capture`) were pre-existing on main. Main has since fixed them (`331c1aed`, #192168), and this branch includes those fixes.

title: fix(agents): let channels create sessions with spawn authority
body:
## Problem

Since #164304, explicit requests to start a session are routed to `sessions_create`. Its separate admitted-operator/session-write gate rejects channel turns without an operator grant, including callers for whom `sessions_spawn(visible: true)` already works. Production Discord requests returned "sessions_create requires current session write authority…" instead of creating a session.

## Solution

Remove the separate gate and route `sessions_create` through the existing visible-spawn owner with an independent mode. Creation shares the same caller attribution, admission, sharing restrictions, sandbox/tool-policy inheritance, and permission mode. Independence changes supervision, not authority: no completion owner or child-run registration, no yield expectation, and the opening brief is delivered verbatim.

The existing Gateway restrictions remain authoritative. In particular, a linked member who is only a viewer of the shared source session cannot use either creation path; removing the operator-only gate does not bypass that sharing restriction.

## Review fixes

- Preserve committed creation receipts and opening-input custody when the source turn stops. The requesting tool is fenced at commit; after acceptance, the destination owns its run and receipt. Cancellation before commit remains rejected.
- Migrate lifecycle fixtures to real stored parents and prepared model catalogs, keeping persistence, acceptance, retirement, revocation, guest-isolation, and target-replacement assertions.
- Preserve leading indentation and trailing newlines in independent opening messages; reject invalid destination values such as `group: null`.
- Correct account-selection documentation: this path uses spawn inheritance rather than the person's saved new-chat default.
- Update retired gate assertions and generated prompt fixtures; preserve the existing supervised dispatch call shape.

[Detailed disposition of ClawSweeper's reviewed-head findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192037#issuecomment-6624906350). The review covered `6185104`; repairs are in `1606a46`, `852efe9`, `ca89fff`, and `e40eb6a`.

## Intentional behavior changes

- `permissionMode` is no longer a `sessions_create` input; it inherits the creating turn's mode.
- Independent sessions record spawn lineage and count toward the spawn-depth limit, without reporting completion to their creator.
- Retry semantics match visible spawn: no idempotency key, so retrying the same tool call can create another session.
- Out-of-workspace `cwd` selection follows spawn's `status: "forbidden"` result instead of the old thrown-error shape.

## Validation

- The channel-creation regression test fails on base with `{ gated: true }` and passes with the fix.
- After integration with main at `76ff9d1`: 55 tests passed across `server.agent-input-authority.test.ts`, its retirement suite, `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.session-scopes.test.ts`, and `sessions-create-tool.test.ts`. These exercise actual creation/input persistence and include pre-commit cancellation, accepted-input custody, revocation, target replacement, required guest isolation, read-only inheritance, and no added operator authority.
- At `852efe9`: 108 tests passed across session-owner tool exposure, visible-spawn/delivery-backlog consumers, and model-runtime choice. Lint and prompt-snapshot check passed. The regenerated snapshot changes in that commit are formatting-only.
- At `e40eb6a`: all 47 channel-operator-authority tests passed, including explicit Slack-admin, Discord-admin, and Discord-member cases. Permitted linked administrators get agent-created sessions owned by their linked human profile; a shared-session viewer is refused by both visible and independent creation without a persistent session effect, and unlinking invalidates retained creation authority. Lint, formatting, and the actual owning `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugin-sdk.json` typecheck pass. The earlier infra typecheck did not cover this file; CI identified that gap and the test matrix was corrected. No extra `delegatedBy` field is asserted for these channel fixtures.
- The production and agent-tools test typechecks passed on the lifecycle repair. Opening-message whitespace is covered by an exact-message Gateway test.
- Live Discord QA on the earlier fix head used leased QA bots and a temporary local Gateway. An unlinked driver with no operator grant mentioned the SUT; the agent called `sessions_create`, received a successful result with a new session key, the session appeared in `sessions.list`, and the SUT replied in Discord. Assertions checked tool results and Gateway state, not model prose. This remains prior-head live evidence; the driver was channel-allowlisted and was not a forbidden-viewer test. The QA lease was verified available and released after restart recovery.

### Final-head checks and re-review

At `e40eb6a1aed0292948bb3c9a861c72583c5e82df`, GitHub reports 73 successful checks/statuses, no failures, and no pending checks. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts are successful ([CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793824920/job/126463267145), [gate run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41796999338)).

[ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192037#issuecomment-6609150974) completed for that exact head at 2026-11-04T08:02:06Z: the four prior findings are addressed, no new actionable defect was found, and both "Before merge" and "Findings" are "None". This is review evidence, not a substitute for maintainer judgment.

Proof limits remain explicit: the live base run was interrupted by a Gateway restart and not repeated; the base refusal is demonstrated by the regression test and recorded production failures. The live Discord run predates the final repairs; the final-head CI and lifecycle tests cover those repairs. No Gateway deployment or restart is part of this PR.
