title: improve(ui): ask before destructive actions with clear buttons
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several Control UI confirmations asked with a plain "Confirm" title or a statement title ("Delete", "Unsaved changes", "Delete cloud worker profile") and packed the question into the body, and the skill library and personal instructions still used the browser's native `window.confirm` (which answers silently in webviews without a dialog bridge).

## User Impact

Every confirmation in the Control UI now opens the shared in-app dialog: the title asks the question, the body states the consequence, and the buttons are the action verb plus Cancel (Cancel first, primary last).

title: fix(ui): omit reply excerpts for adjacent messages

## Why This Change Was Made

title: feat(plugins): force reloads without stranding active conversations
body:
Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/85b7d33e-fd16-4ea2-85ee-46951f9ab0e2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7f95fa70-c4ab-4275-9766-c09eae3e53c1)

## What Problem This Solves

Waiting for a plugin reload from an agent turn can deadlock on that same turn's retained runtime, requiring fragile detached-exec and manual wake-up choreography.

## User Impact

Developers can use `openclaw plugins reload <id> --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json` to interrupt supported blocking native runs, reload safely, and automatically continue their conversations. The Gateway owns the durable operation independently of the calling exec or socket; `--operation-id` lets a later CLI invocation observe the same operation without submitting another reload.

Existing reload behavior without `--force` is unchanged. Forced continuation is limited to supported native conversations with durable input custody; other runtime owners follow the documented refusal or safe-drain behavior. Force never permits unloading code underneath live plugin work.

## Why This Change Was Made

A persisted operation and continuation journal bridges interruption, normal cleanup, reload publication or recovery, and fresh session admission. Queue ownership survives restart, aliases/shared physical stores, and stale concurrent journal writers. Continuations retain prior tool results, respect current destination authority and explicit Stop, and do not replay completed external actions. The operation has a bounded ten-minute drain; disconnecting a forced-reload observer does not cancel an accepted operation.

## Evidence

- Isolated native exec and code-mode-to-exec flows both loaded edited plugin version 2 and automatically continued the same conversation. Each completed external append occurred once, with three model requests.
- Initial regression suite: 155 passing tests across 13 files. Targeted recovery, physical-store custody, stale-writer and late-transfer regressions were observed red before their fixes and green afterward; latest owning consumer run: 34 passing tests across five files.
- Lifecycle-mapping extraction: 32 passing plan tests; staged line-cap checks passed.
- Core and affected test types, targeted production/test lint, formatting, validator generation and runtime build passed. Documentation validation checked 1,404 files with zero issues; glossary check passed.

Known validation limits: one broader readiness test observed this host's egress-proxy HTTP 502 instead of connection refusal; a direct-loopback diagnostic passed, and the original test was restored without relaxing assertions. title: fix(doctor): release worker readers before NOCOW repair
body:
Closes #191957

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `doctor --fix` refuses btrfs NOCOW repair when its memory health probes leave agent database readers open in a worker thread.

## User Impact

Doctor releases its own selected worker readers before rewriting the stores. Unknown native handles still block repair and preserve the original files. The running candidate Doctor must contain this fix; existing updater NOCOW opt-in and recovery behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory status manager closes before NOCOW repair, but the shared retrieval worker retains its reader. Doctor now uses the existing process-wide reader cleanup operation under maintenance custody before native file checks and exchange. No schema, configuration, protocol, timeout, or release changes.

Thanks @synapse-homeroot for identifying the retained memory-search worker in the release reproduction.

## Evidence

- RED on pinned main `a0cb9b130ff5711671849521ddbd2bc673e8f4c2`: the real maintenance/NOCOW entry point reports exactly two native `fuser` self-holder refusals after real memory status managers close; the stores without those probes rewrite. Test about 3.4s; wrapper 60.83s including cold native-worker compilation. This RED witness predates the loader-only correction described below.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex autoreview covers P0–P2 and is scoped-clean.

title: fix(gateway): guests cannot see who is online in the Users sidebar
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests can use the Users sidebar but cannot see who is online or idle: hello presence, live presence events and `system-presence` required broad `operator.read`, while guests have only session scopes. Their own `presence.activity` reports were also rejected.

## User Impact

Guests receive online/idle presence and references to watched sessions they can already access. Operator readers retain the full presence view. Email, `onlineSince`, device/network details and connection identifiers are never included in the guest projection. `presence.query` remains operator-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPresenceRecipientProjection` allowlists person fields for session-only readers: profile identity/name/avatar, `ts`, `lastActivityAt`, a disconnect marker, and permitted watched-session keys. Rows without resolved profiles carry no person. Detail level is included in view and audience cache keys.

`system-presence` and `presence.activity` declare `operator.sessions.read` directly in the Gateway's method descriptors. The presence event guard accepts session readers while retaining recipient-specific projection. No role configuration change is needed.

The final correction removes the earlier additions to the UI-imported shared method set. There is now no diff in `ui/` or `src/shared/` against the PR's base; presence permission declarations stay Gateway-owned. Earlier attribution of the bundle-size failure solely to main was insufficient because that shared set ships in the UI.

Accepted tradeoff, approved by code owner Json: retain one wire row per connection so source/delta keys stay aligned. The UI still groups people into one displayed row; guests can infer connection counts. A per-person wire protocol would need separate key handling, not simply collapsing this array.

The integration with #191978 preserves its demoted-guest denial of `users.list`, `presence.query` and other people's Activity timelines. Online presence is the separately approved exception; demoted session readers receive only the person-level view.

## Evidence

- Real-Gateway regression covers guest hello, `system-presence`, live presence events, private-field omission, watched-session filtering, denied `presence.query`, and accepted self activity. Original guest RPC assertion is red on base and green with the fix.
- Final Gateway-only declaration correction: **82 tests passed** across presence audience, own-session method scopes, shared session scopes, and presence activity. Gateway-server test typecheck, targeted lint, format and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(gateway): serve agent avatars to session-scoped readers
body:
## Problem

Guests see the agent's emoji in Control UI instead of its avatar image.

Guest roles typically hold only session scopes (e.g. `operator.sessions.write`). `agent.identity.get` is session-readable, so guests receive the agent's `/avatar/<agentId>` URL — but the avatar HTTP route authorized as `assistant.media.get`, which requires `operator.read`. The image request returned `403` and the UI fell back to the emoji.

## Solution

Authorize the `/avatar/<agentId>` route as `agent.identity.get`. The bytes are the image behind the URL that method already hands to the same caller, so they now share its session-read authority. Assistant media file reads are unchanged and still require `operator.read`.

Scope note: per-agent visibility matches `agent.identity.get` today (neither checks the role's agent allowlist per `agentId`); this PR keeps that parity rather than adding a new restriction.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts`: the existing "avatar metadata without operator.read" test now runs as `gates avatar metadata on scopes %j`. A trusted-proxy request with no scopes still gets `403`; one with only `operator.sessions.write` gets `200`. The guest case is red on base and green with the fix. title: feat(ui): move conversation versions into the session menu
body:
## Problem

The chat header shows a standalone **Versions** (history) icon next to the session ⋯ menu. It is a rarely used action, but it takes a permanent header slot.

## Solution

Move Versions into the session ⋯ menu as a **Versions ▸** submenu, next to **View**.

- The submenu lists the same version rows (headline, message count, age, current-version check). Selecting a row calls the same `onBranchSelect` path.
- The "About versions" help popover is replaced by the same help text shown as a muted note at the top of the submenu. This matches the mobile Versions page.
- The submenu is capped at 360px tall, so long histories scroll inside it instead of running down the whole window.
- The Versions item is disabled while switching versions is blocked (archived session, agent busy, or the version list is still loading). The block reason shows as its title.
- Compact menus open Versions as a page (Back + rows), the same way they open View.
- Mobile is unchanged: versions stay in Details.
- Removed the `ChatPaneVersionsMenu` component, its custom element, its CSS (trigger, heading, info and help rules), and the header's two-icon width reservation (`--chat-pane-menu-count`). The header now reserves one icon slot because only the ⋯ trigger is left.

title: fix(google): stop citation requests when a search is cancelled
body:
Supersedes #155494, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cancelling a Gemini web search still allows citation redirect requests to run, including later batches.

## User Impact

Cancelling a Google search cancels active citation requests, prevents further citation requests, and preserves the caller's cancellation reason without caching a late result. Ordinary redirect failures still keep the original citation URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the search's existing AbortSignal to the citation resolver, which owns cancellation checks and guarded HEAD requests. The optional parameter preserves existing one-argument callers. This replacement covers cancellation; the original proposal's citation-admission optimization remains a separate follow-up.

Removed redundant header branching and the single-use header-cache-key binding in the same Google owner, preserving case-insensitive Headers.set precedence. Citation enrichment updates the provider's newly created objects directly, removing duplicate arrays and copies. Production delta: zero lines; tests: +63 lines.

## Evidence

- On main `66e2433288b23cb4c4fef5889f2fbcfcc19f9601`, both cancellation regressions fail: cancellation after the response still starts a HEAD request, and cancellation during the first batch starts all 25 redirects instead of stopping at ten.

The Google file took 55.46 seconds including 46.28 seconds preparing compiled workers; the redirect file took 3.82 seconds. Both named files completed in 64.64 seconds. Tests exercise the provider factory and real citation/guard owners with a controlled fetch boundary; no live Google inference was run.
- Independent autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete local candidate against the same main commit: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. The hosted review of the earlier head raised a scope-only P3 about header cleanup; the final cleanup preserves Headers.set semantics and is retained as same-owner duplicate removal within the net-zero production budget.
- The custom-endpoint regression verifies that provider attribution replaces case-colliding operator headers. It was red on the initial cleanup and green after correction.
- Touched-file lint for the Google runtime/test and citation resolver passes with zero warnings/errors; formatting passes for all four changed source/test/docs files. `git diff --check` passes.

title: fix(control-ui): edit failed messages before resending
body:
Co-authored with @jacobtomlinson, who reported the failed-image recovery problem.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ca95be7d-a3c5-4c24-b9f9-96a9837c99f2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6069afbd-66cf-483e-b289-9f5dad989353)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a rejected image-heavy message cannot be corrected from the failure notice, and continuing leaves its original images in active model context.

## User Impact

Users can choose **Edit message** on the latest failed turn, confirm the existing rewind, remove attachments in the composer, and resend. Image-only messages work too. An existing unsent draft is left untouched; editing is disabled until that draft is sent or cleared. **Try again** keeps its existing continuation behavior so completed tool actions are not replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `sessions.rewind` owner rather than add a provider-specific image cap or another history-editing path. Rewind removes the rejected tail from active context and clears its resume bindings while retaining the original as an inactive branch. Current-failure, canonical latest-user, imported-entry, and draft guards are checked again at the point of effect. Older failures cannot rewind newer user input. Rewinding does not undo external actions.

Cached failure facts, details, and Try again remain eager. Only the optional new editor, its admission selector, and its copy load on demand. They consume live scope, reader, rewind, and confirmation operations from their existing owners; the shared RewindButton retains its original behavior. The new copy has one dedicated cold namespace, leaving shared recovery copy intact.

## Evidence

- Production Control UI browser regression: **3 passed** — text-plus-five-images and image-only recovery, draft protection, canonical rewind ID/order, exact retained-four payload hashes, reconnect/history reload, and unchanged continuation semantics. The test holds the optional edit-module request and verifies failure facts and Try again are already visible before releasing it. Cached-failure unit assertions remain synchronous.
- Owning Gateway/session integration: **27 passed**, including rejected images excluded from fresh `openModelContextAsync → buildSessionContext → convertToLlm` output after rewind and four-image resend. The original branch remains durable. Covers inline images and persisted media references; unchanged backend proof reused.
- Recovery/shared-control tests: **93 passed**; transcript invalidation: **22 passed**; catalog-source suite: **30 passed**; verifier suite: **6 passed**. Original state regressions fail on unchanged main; catalog composition preserves both shared and cold copy.
- UI/scripts typechecks, focused lint, formatting, docs formatting/MDX, and `git diff --check`: passed. Exact merged-source `lint:ui:i18n` also passed unchanged.
- Exact failing CI inputs reproduced: merge `1da6b8021bd64d2380e3430cad40fb0bd82f6b13`, base `5ead822527e350cecdf30cbe0f04b1f418fdb349`. The old candidate reproduces **1,280,771 B** chat-boot gzip, over the unchanged **1,280,674 B** limit. The qualified runtime candidate measures **1,280,434 B** — **337 B smaller**, with **240 B headroom**. Startup is **90,546 B**; request counts stay **3 startup / 20 chat**. No performance limits, checker logic, or recorded boot-module lists changed. Prior head `5886d63` subsequently passed hosted performance and i18n checks.
- Test-cost policy: duplicated failed-input fixtures were consolidated and existing cases extended rather than adding a matrix. `config/test-lines-allocations/failed-image-message-recovery.txt` allocates **504 lines**, exactly the measured positive regression delta. Both working-tree and staged ratchets pass on the exact merge/base, with **24 lines slack**. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. This funds the required browser, canonical-context, and current-owner/draft regressions.
- Local single-worker costs: state/controller file **1.23 s**, catalog-source file **9.94 s**, browser file **22.73 s**; original focused image-context integration **13.59 s**. CI seconds for the final head remain pending its run.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the cold-owner boundary and allocation completed through P2 with full owner/caller context and final source verification: **no actionable findings**. Reviews were static; test executions above were run separately.
- Final type-only architecture correction replaces the page-host dependency with exact read-only fields using canonical leaf value types. **Madge: 0 cycles; runtime import guard: 0 cycles.** UI typecheck, focused lint, and **33 owner tests** were rerun successfully. Type-erased module JavaScript is byte-identical, so unchanged runtime/bundle/media proof is reused rather than claimed as new-head CI. A separate fresh independent P2 review found no actionable findings.
- [Hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191871#issuecomment-6603688507) reported no findings on prior head `bc3da5acc7f3`; no duplicate review request was posted.

**Proof boundary:** browser Gateway I/O and courtyard images are synthetic; the backend integration reconstructs real agent/model context. A live GLM/provider request is not claimed; isolated provider credentials were not imported.

## What Problem This Solves

When Incognito or Draft is turned on from the desktop new-session page, the toggle shows a bold red label, which is louder than the session header controls it now sits beside.

## User Impact

User impact: a turned-on Incognito or Draft toggle on the desktop new-session page now reads as a normal selected header control (regular-weight label in the header's active text color on the selected surface) instead of bold red text.

title: improve(memory-wiki): skip reparsing unchanged pages
body:
Supersedes #166339, thanks @corvid-reads.

## What Problem This Solves

Memory Wiki compiles repeatedly parse unchanged vault pages, making large vault compilation unnecessarily expensive.

## User Impact

Repeated compiles in the same process reuse unchanged page scans. Edited, renamed, and deleted pages still update the generated indexes and compiled snapshots. Files continue to be read and hashed for source-generation correctness; separate CLI processes remain cold. No config, schema, or stored-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compiler already computes a SHA-256 digest for every page. Reuse scan summaries and projections by vault, relative path, and that digest, including between compile passes. Retain only current pages, at most four vaults, and at most 16 MiB of serialized summaries per vault. Serialization detaches source substrings and protects retained results from caller mutation; no Markdown source or parsed trees are retained.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: exercise the production compile entry point twice with two unchanged synthetic pages and rendering disabled; the second compile must make zero scanner calls. Check same-size edits with restored mtime, renames, deletions, compiler rewrites, and interleaved vaults. Count work only; no host timing benchmark.

- Base `7d69eb973bc43faa15babe2d82e419c7a672ccb8`: scanner calls **2 → 2**, regression fails because the second compile should parse zero unchanged pages.
- Replacement: scanner calls **2 → 0**; all **19 tests in three named files** pass: `compile.scan-cache.test.ts`, `compile.test.ts`, and `compile.related-index.test.ts`.
- Command: `pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.scan-cache.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.related-index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Executed on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41620158752). Final focused command: 42.61 s including worker startup; the two regression cases took 74 ms and 99 ms. On final head `fd0ce558bac3c9e8c063526bca33fd8bc6641070`, [the CI regression job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41623796107/job/125877286440) also passes with counts **2 → 0**; the two cases take 137 ms and 173 ms. Its shared job takes 514 s including setup and other tests, not the isolated cost of this file.
- Production delta: **+29 lines**. Existing scan/projection logic moves into one helper; the additional code owns reuse, content validation, deletion pruning, and bounded retention. No unrelated deletions were made to satisfy a LOC quota. The separate 83-line test allocation covers the work-count and invalidation regression.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed. The replacement is independently implemented from current main.

Local autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, reviewed the complete change with full compiler/cache-owner context and the final type-narrowing correction: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. A source-string retention finding was fixed before final review. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Touched-file type-aware lint passed on Testbox with zero warnings and zero errors; its required extension-declaration preparation also passed. PR CI supplies broad validation.

Proof covers the production compiler owner. Shipped CLI/Gateway wall-clock performance was not measured.

Final head `fd0ce558bac3c9e8c063526bca33fd8bc6641070`: [required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41623796107) and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass, including both repaired type checks. No inherited-failure exception is used.

title: fix(android): keep wake listening active in the background
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android wake-word listening pauses when the app leaves the screen and repeatedly restarts the speech recognizer while idle.

Supersedes #154873, thanks @jayala.

## User Impact

With wake words enabled, listening can continue in the background under the existing microphone permission and node foreground notification. Android 13+ recognizers supporting caller-supplied audio keep a continuous session across unrelated speech, avoiding repeated recognition-service start tones. Older or unsupported recognizers retain plain-session fallback and can still play platform tones.

Existing saved wake-word enablement also enables background listening. The setting now explains this behavior. Disabling wake words or retiring the service microphone grant closes capture and prevents pending retries from restarting it. Cold background service starts wait for visible microphone eligibility. No new permissions or settings are added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing foreground service owns the microphone grant; Voice Wake consumes it alongside Activity visibility. Wake reuses Talk's recorder and pipe cleanup instead of adding another capture implementation. Terminal errors release capture, and devices rejecting supplied audio fall back to plain sessions. Spoken replies from the original PR are outside this fix.

## Evidence

- Main red: [Android Testbox 41621123137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41621123137), main `7d69eb973bc43` plus the two named regressions. Both fail: no microphone service type and no `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` segmented session. Gradle completed in 3m58s. The workflow is canceled during lease cleanup; this is a test-result claim, not a green workflow claim.
- Fix green: [focused Android Testbox 41622280432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41622280432) passed `VoiceWakeManagerTest`, `VoiceWakeRuntimeTest`, the background/service lifecycle cases, and `TalkModeManagerTest.rawPttCloseWaitsForInFlightDeviceCleanup` (2m11s). The checkout was pinned to `a7cc0a17d1a9` plus verified SHA-256 hashes of the exact UI/test delta committed in `d69082308b4b`. Assertions exercise the real Android adapter, verify supplied-audio descriptor closure and recognizer destruction, and reject a pending retry/late callback after disabling or retiring background authority. Cold sticky startup receives valid wake words without creating a recognizer. The native string inventory was regenerated in that remote checkout.

No physical-device, acoustic, or stable-upgrade campaign was run or claimed; this task uses Android CI as proof. No authorization bypass was demonstrated by the hosted review, and no saved-state schema is changed.

title: fix(ui): restore subagent colors in desktop Details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The desktop Details panel stopped showing subagent identity colors. The Subagents summary renders as overlapping gray robot glyphs instead of tinted, per-subagent avatars, in both the docked and floating panel.

Root cause: #189537 ("tighten the desktop Details panel") added a desktop-only override that set every `.chat-details-subagents__avatar` to `background: transparent; color: var(--muted)`. It also put the stacked summary avatars on the 16px row-icon slot with a 15px glyph, so with the stack's `-6px` overlap the bots crowd into each other. That PR's own comment says collapsed People "matches the native Subagents avatar" at 20px, so the stack was meant to keep its native size.

## Solution

In `ui/src/styles/chat/details-desktop.css`:

- Remove the muting override, so avatars use the hue tint and ink from `chat-details-subagents.css` again.
- Limit the row-icon slot sizing to row avatars (`:where(.chat-details-subagents__row) > .chat-details-subagents__avatar`). Stacked summary avatars go back to their native 20px chip with a 14px glyph. `:where()` keeps the shared `:is()` rules at the same specificity for every other icon in the list.

Expanded rows stay on #189537's shared icon and text axes and now show their colored icon.

Mobile Details is not changed. #189549 muted the mobile sheet avatars on purpose to make the rows quieter.

The stacked chips keep their existing 1px ring in the panel's surface color (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--details-subagent-surface)`), which separates the overlapping chips. This PR does not change that ring. It matches the panel when the row is idle and stands out as a light outline only when the row is hovered, the same as before #189537.

## Impact

Visual only, desktop Details (docked at 1728 and floating at 1100). No behavior or data changes. The CSS gets slightly smaller.

## Evidence

- Regression assertion in `ui/src/e2e/session-details-background-work.e2e.test.ts`: at the docked (1728) and floating (1100) desktop widths, the four stacked avatars must have four distinct background tints.

title: fix: allow catalog continuation after native terminal exit
body:
Supersedes #145930, thanks @ericcaiwx-star.

Related: #145637

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an existing native conversation remaining unavailable for Web continuation after its terminal exits because the retained catalog pane still has the provider's earlier `canContinue: false` result.

## User Impact

Users can continue once the provider allows it, without reloading the page. Provider denial still blocks continuation. Loaded transcript pages and the older-history cursor remain intact; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog reader now handles the existing Gateway `terminal.exit` event and reuses its scoped metadata lookup for blocked conversations. A metadata-only read preserves the retained transcript. An unfinished transcript keeps its existing full-read/resume path.

Fixes plugin-triggered deferred agent turns being rejected as unavailable after the triggering request completes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes candidate Doctor failing the exec-approvals migration with “database is locked” after an update-admission read during an upgrade from 2026.10.10.

## User Impact

The candidate can import exec approval policy and local socket credentials while preserving verified rollback attribution. The candidate must contain this repair; it is not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's update-admission reader retained an idle native WAL connection after the first shared-state open. The next captured migration could not acquire exclusive custody while that connection remained open. Captured SQLite maintenance now uses the existing current private-snapshot reader, including its existing copy cost for large stores. Native exclusion and live admission checks remain enforced; PostgreSQL keeps its existing path. No retries or timeouts are added.

title: fix(cron): scheduled turns time out while compacting history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled conversation turns repeatedly timing out before runner startup when their existing history requires preflight compaction. A real summary request was already executing, but cron still treated the turn as stalled setup and aborted it after 60 seconds. Repeated occurrences could reach the existing auto-disable threshold without compacting the history.

## User Impact

Scheduled work can complete required preflight maintenance under its existing per-run deadline instead of being prematurely cancelled as setup. The configured deadline, normal stalled-setup protection, cancellation, and later fallback behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing source-admission owner before required memory checkpoint/compaction work: await the scheduled start gate, recheck live admission, claim occurrence custody before effects, and report runner/context-engine progress to cron. This also prevents pre-execution policy replay after maintenance may have performed model or tool work. No new scheduler, timer, configuration option, or permission is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real shared-session admission and preflight compaction, with only external provider I/O synthetic: red on `97e996675b41f0c2d18d7cd51a5cfc32982c1306` with the exact setup-timeout error while a summary request was active. ## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The accepted chat-dispatch handoff retained the parent’s finite plugin execution scope. Reuse the existing prepared-runtime scope exit so the child establishes its own runtime custody while preserving the admitting Gateway. The asynchronous prep overlap is intentional; the ownership leak is at the accepted-work handoff, so no second preparation owner or blocking-ACK workaround is added.

## Evidence

- Real chat.send/plugin-lifetime regression: the baseline fails with `Plugin invocation scope is closed`; the candidate passes while retaining ACK, terminal-publication, cleanup-warning, admission-release, and single-user-transcript assertions. title: fix(plugins): refuse new source captures on low-space volumes
body:
Supersedes #161840, thanks @BorClaw.

Related: #161839.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin load retries keep copying source after the destination volume is nearly full.

## User Impact

New source captures and installed snapshot staging refuse below 512 MiB with an error asking the operator to free space and retry. Existing state-to-temporary-volume fallback remains available, and setup preparation contains the source failure so startup can continue. A plugin that needs a refused capture remains unavailable until space is freed. Unreadable disk statistics retain best-effort loading.

The floor is a preflight check, not a reservation for a copy's full size; an in-flight copy can still consume the remaining space.

## Why This Change Was Made

#191501 (`779f51d2`) avoids discarded setup captures, but actual source loads, workers, recovery copies, and installed snapshots still allocate payloads without a space check. Reuse the existing nearest-ancestor disk-space reader at allocation and snapshot staging, and the existing source-acquisition failure classification for setup recovery.

The simplified implementation adds 15 production lines, sharing the guard across source, worker, and native allocations. The touched owner paths retain necessary Windows path handling and custody cleanup; there was no safe equivalent dead code to remove. title: fix(web-search): honor sandbox provider trust during search
body:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sandboxed agents executing a configured third-party web-search provider that the existing sandbox trust policy excludes.

## User Impact

Sandboxed search permits only bundled or verified official providers, matching web fetch. Existing sandboxed configurations selecting third-party providers must enable or select an eligible provider to restore search; the execution error states that recovery step. Nonsandboxed search keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the session sandbox flag through both search resolver routes into the existing shared manifest trust filter. The sandbox-only availability hint does not load rejected provider code or mislabel unavailable eligible providers as trust failures.

Existing provider settings remain selected; no config migration or rewrite is involved.

Tests shrink by two lines: the regression uses the existing provider suite, and redundant callback reinitializations already covered by `vi.clearAllMocks()` are removed. title: fix(buzz): keep room history rate limits from stopping replies

Give each room its own recovery tail and retry only NIP-01 `rate-limited:` query closures. Waiting releases both replay capacity and query permits. Recovery reuses the existing replay guard; other failures retain their current fatal handling.

title: fix: preserve command output with long temporary paths
body:
Related: #190843, #190845.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes buffered commands failing with EINVAL when a long temporary directory makes their Unix-socket path exceed the platform limit. This also prevented private repository history from reaching native child sessions, despite file reconciliation succeeding.

## User Impact

Commands can complete under long temporary roots, and repository operations can preserve private Git history instead of falling back to files-only recovery. Missing or unwritable temporary directories still fail normally. No configuration, authentication, execution-permission or cancellation behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native-resource broker already uses a portable socket-path budget and a private short fallback. Buffered command output now shares that decision. It checks the actual created path, removes an oversized rendezvous directory, and preserves private permissions, current launch authority and cleanup.

The two regressions use real sockets and subprocesses, covering absolute and UTF-8-byte-overlong paths, output, cleanup, refusal and ordinary temporary-directory errors. The exact 122-line test allocation covers these distinct owner-boundary contracts.

## Evidence

- **44 process/broker cases + 5 native-resource cases passed**, including output transfer, cancellation and cleanup.
- **3 real broker/Git diagnostic cases passed:** private history exported/imported/adopted under long and short paths; revoked authority refused import and preserved the base.
- [Real-Gateway qualification run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41571285323): **2/2 tests passed**, including complete mirrored and retained native-child flows, four authenticated nodes, private ancestry/current bytes and parent authority/filesystem preservation. Model and provisioning transports were deterministic fixtures; this is not live frontier inference or commercial volume provisioning.

On observed main c86fbe68e5a1ae494e49ac6ad41aef9585210ab6, format, whitespace and the test-line ratchet passed. Static review did not execute tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the documented autoreview fallback was used. The original e704 hosted review identified the inventory omission addressed below. The completed [fresh hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191659#issuecomment-6595387495) on `61b12733e4b6c7bfa83c2e756d88c9e54ca1c680` rates overall/proof Platinum and patch Diamond, with zero actionable findings. The collector-only proposal was separately qualified against that retained log and empty/incomplete/conflicting-output controls; it is not part of this production PR.

Proof reuse is component-specific: prior-tree execution is not current-candidate CI or whole merge-tree equivalence. Linux Node24.22.1/Node26.12.1 were exercised; no Darwin/Windows runtime claim. Current-head CI and overall Platinum-or-higher hosted review remain landing gates.

title: fix(acp): prevent task replay after dispatch hook failures

title: fix(exec): sessions remain running after the root command exits
body:
Supersedes #147335, thanks @Decent9967.

Related: #147304.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec sessions stay running after their shell exits when a background descendant keeps stdout or stderr open.

## User Impact

Ordinary non-PTY host exec on Linux and macOS completes after root exit and a bounded 250 ms output drain. Later descendant output is discarded; keep work in the shell's foreground when its eventual output is needed. Descendant cleanup, cancellation, and memory ownership remain independent of the terminal result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor already separates the terminal result from descendant extinction. One completion helper uses the adapters' retained root-exit events and the existing output fence for both direct children and service relays. The transport keeps draining under its existing cleanup owner. Completion does not signal the background child. Sandbox/external transports, internal processes, PTYs, Windows, and execution approval checks retain their existing behavior.

Removed the single-use `setForcedReason` wrapper. Production grows by 31 lines for the bounded completion wait; regression coverage grows by 97 lines, with a matching test-line allocation. Keeping the timer in a small helper preserves the supervisor's existing file-size limit.

## Evidence

- Red on main `928818442b99b6daf992e2f0472f54d535c3a271`: both direct and service-relay reproductions of `sh -c "sleep 30 & echo done"` remained pending after two seconds. title: fix(android): load cursor history without losing reading position
body:
Related: #191596

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android cannot browse earlier chat pages and can pull readers to a new remote prompt while they are reading history.

## User Impact

User impact: readers can load older messages, catch up with cursor deltas, and keep their reading position while live responses arrive. Confirmed reasoning-level changes now survive subsequent delta reconciliation, so later sends do not revert to the old history window's level.

Cursor resets and reconnects reopen the normal tail; pages outside that tail must be loaded again. Existing full-message expansion survives unchanged history updates, but its Compose-local fetched content can require **View all** again after Activity recreation. No Gateway contract, cache retention, schema, dependencies, or outbox retry policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat controller now owns cursor-backed history windows, validates complete delta envelopes before advancing their cursor, and uses the same canonical upsert for live message events and catch-up. Directional pages do not supply branch/run/outbox evidence. Snapshot-only Gateways keep their existing reads.

The reader distinguishes remote content from explicit local send intent, saves a stable row key and offset, and leaves **Jump to latest** in its existing header location. **Beginning of conversation** requires explicit `hasMore: false` coverage on a normal snapshot, or exhaustion of a successful advertised directional older-page read. Directional pages omit `hasMore`; missing cursors on bounded/legacy snapshots or cached views still do not prove completeness. Config changes force a normal history read because deltas omit default-model metadata.

## Evidence

### Source identity and bounded repairs

- Current published head: `f703f9c03ba15664cecf477222fe159a4f37a2d6` on `openclaw/fast-crab`, updated on this same draft PR through native `github_publish` (publication receipt `8dd002c3-74a9-4ffc-accb-dea7bce2cc3d`). Original attachment base: `65dfe23a008b733fbdaf0dc79762149345f75d06`; managed guest source base/HEAD: `913f025cd15ba79d4002ad4e6db1fe2739ba8f8f`. - Repair input: the [exact-head local verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191597#issuecomment-6593866579) and [downloadable evidence/provenance correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191597#issuecomment-6593999941). The evidence archive's 19 files were checked against its SHA-256/size manifest. That earlier archive's 3,789-test reference belongs to the initial revision; its `2ef1d3d` result is 172 targeted tests. The separate exact-head `cdc305f8add6` full-suite evidence is recorded below.
- Reset events now retire advertised cursor windows without skipping the existing session-settings publication path. Queued permission writes still observe the replacement physical session identity; snapshot-only metadata refreshes do not gain extra history reads.
- Display IDs remain distinct from canonical transcript entry IDs. Canonical reconciliation preserves display identity across cursor updates without admitting a display ID to a reaction write.
- Reader fixtures preserve the intended ownership contract: remote history does not force-follow; an explicit **Jump to latest** moves the reader; local send admission starts following; final-answer fixture rows and navigation through the reader owner exercise stable-position restoration. Existing session/permission and reader-position assertions were retained, with a negative remote-follow assertion added.
- Latest P2 repair: `parseHistory` uses the current top-level `thinkingLevel`, then the current `sessionInfo.thinkingLevel`, and no longer inherits that setting from `previousHistory`. If both are absent, the existing settings owner retains its confirmed value. Existing generation/pending-mutation guards and snapshot precedence are unchanged.

title: fix(voice-call): keep opening greetings audible during caller interruptions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: early caller speech or noise clears the opening greeting before callers hear it.

Supersedes #159144, thanks @mnowrot. Related: #159139.

## User Impact

The opening greeting plays through, and callers can interrupt subsequent replies normally. Overlapping caller audio and transcripts are discarded during the opening. Input before the first greeting audio remains live; no pre-audio mute, new option, or migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing audio controller protects the opening until its response ends and the existing carrier playback clock drains. It excludes the answering-machine hold acknowledgement, and releases on explicit clear or continuity reset. Provider-side cancellation already caused by input sent before playback starts remains outside this host playback fix. Carrier timing uses the existing send-time estimate rather than adding an acknowledgement waiter.

This builds on #191537's echo admission and leaves #191498's Deepgram UtteranceEnd behavior intact. Production delta is +29 lines net; the redundant audible-output forwarding callback was removed. The remaining state distinguishes the opening from later turns and keeps response completion from exposing its queued tail. The separate 60-line regression allocation covers both interruption owners, a generation gap, the queued tail, complete carrier audio, and resumed later-turn interruption without another test harness.

## Evidence

title: fix(cron): honor explicit failure alert destinations before repair
body:
Closes #169401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing first failure alert when a conversation-owned automation explicitly routes failures to an alerts destination: owner-conversation repair currently replaces that alert, potentially delaying a daily monitor’s notification until the next day.

## User Impact

An explicit per-job failure destination now receives the alert when due instead of having it replaced by a repair turn. Inherited destinations stay repair-first. No new configuration key or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor the operator’s explicit notification choice. Job-level channel, recipient, or account selectors in `failureAlert` or `delivery.failureDestination` bypass repair; policy-only and mode-only overrides do not. Existing opt-outs, thresholds, cooldowns, transient retry holds, incident deduplication, repair settlement, and terminal-notification behavior remain in place.

This implements the destination-specific exception proposed in #169401 following maintainer acceptance of that product direction. The cron notification owner keeps the decision; no new state or parallel delivery path is introduced. The delivery guide documents the exception.

## Evidence

- Red first on base `2be13a6bdc761deaf59efceccb343852bbaee3c1`: both new explicit-destination cases failed because a repair was requested instead of an alert.
- `pnpm test src/cron/service.failure-repair.test.ts src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **52 passed** (46.42 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation). - Targeted cron test typecheck and lint passed; formatting, delivery-doc MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Proof was run on November 1; the candidate is unchanged.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, GPT-6.1 Sol), complete local candidate against the base above, P0-P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable in this sandbox. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191570#issuecomment-6592875774) completed for this head: no findings and no before-merge actions. It noted a live-delivery proof gap. The AWS QA proofs (mock and real GPT 6.1 Sol inference) and contributor live comparison below add complementary evidence; successful real-chat announce delivery and account-only selection remain unproven.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41555568784) completed successfully for `1f547521e4f71bb535f3075da3051d2b99180ef7`; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. No CI repair was needed.
- Production delta: +11 lines net; regression tests: +86 lines net with a separate matching test-budget allocation. Tests reuse the production CronService and existing external-I/O fixtures.
- **Real-model behavior proof on direct AWS Crabbox (GPT 6.1 Sol)** (lease `cbx_de8dfffc032f`, eu-west-1; stopped after use): isolated QA Gateway + qa-channel with `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode live-frontier --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (fallbacks disabled; `OPENAI_API_KEY` forwarded as a secret, not printed; isolated `HOME`, no forwarded OpenClaw env), same lease for before/after. All turns use real GPT 6.1 Sol: the owner conversation, both cron jobs (no model override), and the repair turns. Each job's real model run fails for a real reason: a long report task with `payload.timeoutSeconds: 4`, which produces `cron: job execution timed out (last phase: model-call-started)`. A cron timeout is not held for transient retry, so alert/repair selection applies. The scenario (not committed) is `cron-explicit-failure-destination-sol-proof`: an owned job with `delivery.failureDestination` set to a separate alerts group, plus an owned control job with an inherited route.
  - Before (only `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts` reverted to `2be13a6`), [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f320d64984bb784e13a5c2007b7cae6e): **fails as reported**. After two real timeouts, `alerts=[]`, and the owner conversation got a real repair turn instead: "Both runs hit the automation’s 4-second timeout while requesting a 3,000-word report. May I increase its `payload.timeoutSeconds` to 300…?"
  - After (`1f547521`, verified source), [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_17beb2c27b8d7d3a6c8d1213cba4d7a7): **pass**. After two real timeouts, the alerts group received `Automation "qa-cron-sol-explicit-…" failed 2 times / Cause: timeout`, with no owner-conversation repair for that job. The inherited-route control job still got the owner repair turn ("Both runs hit the automation’s 4-second timeout… May I increase its timeout to 300 seconds…?") and no alert.
- **Mock-model proof on direct AWS Crabbox** (lease `cbx_0d7f4d42e2b3`; stopped after use): the same Gateway shape with `--provider-mode mock-openai` and scripted turn failures. Before, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_23056f2bcf7ae62ddda0fbd4ef6a8881): `alerts=[] repairRequests=2`. After, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_30fc6af8162f4f24f24bb4f74a334ec4): the alert was delivered with `repairRequests=0`, and the inherited control stayed repair-first.

For the same reason, the existing `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` scenario fails on base and head alike (its first run succeeds through `gpt-5.6-luna-alt`). This is pre-existing and unrelated to this change; it is a separate follow-up.

title: fix: iOS reconnects keep replaying rejected push registrations
body:
## Current maintainer review — delivery proof still missing

[Detailed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191565#pullrequestreview-5813972422). The existing rejection-persistence regression fails on main and passes on the private current-main integration. The iOS/Watch build, 24 native tests, 310 selected backend tests, core typecheck, scoped lint and generated PostgreSQL verification passed.

**Still Draft.** These tests do not prove restored alerts or background wake. The laboratory build is ad-hoc `localSandbox`; an authorized official signed physical-device run and hosted renewal-identity qualification are still required. The persistent recovery/retention contract and released-version upgrade/rollback also remain unqualified. No fabricated recovery screenshots, source fixes or merge were performed.

Tested author head `fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5`, private integration `5e97c3c229d6039fcf3ce77291f7cdf0b52be2f9`, frozen main `4d67ec34f59707df2d777912e9de9abd8d44aa32`. Later main `243e1c65` has no relevant input changes.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and historical evidence</summary>

## Takeover coordination — publication unblocked 2026-11-06

The reviewed source is now published in this same PR at [fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5). Its public GitHub tree exactly matches reviewed/tested tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. The final PR diff contains only the32 intended product files. Generated Bun caches caught during publication verification were removed in a follow-up commit; history was preserved. The publication gate was cleared under the authorized request; no global permissions were changed.

@ekinnee — thank you for the [579aa20d product candidate](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/commit/579aa20dc9d9d2167c875de325d2c49435cfea79) and [source-bound handoff/checklist at6296e75f](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/tree/6296e75fdf53bbba143c699a020cbc307a458456/handoff/pr191565). The APNs-specific cleanup was incorporated; unrelated demo/macOS baseline cleanup already superseded by upstream and evidence-only handoff files were not imported.

**Testing help requested:** if your Mac setup remains available, can you rerun the same selected Swift suites and simulator build on fc1fa6bc? Your earlier28-test/native-build result remains bound to579aa20d, not this refreshed source. Separately, can you run the signed-device checklist on your approved iPhone/test Gateway once a signing maintainer supplies an authorized official-relay-capable build tied to the final SHA? Personal Team signing alone is not that proof. Please confirm whether you can install the authorized build through its supported distribution channel. We need actual notification receipt and background-wake observations across rejected-cache recovery, reconnect/relaunch and bounded repeat attempts, without reinstalling/re-pairing as recovery. Share sanitized results only—no signing keys, tokens, grants or private device identifiers.

**Still draft:** maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, official signing, current-source native/visual/device qualification and final-head CI remain pending. Restored notification delivery is not claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Official iOS apps can reconnect successfully while continuing to reuse relay enrollment that APNs rejected with `410 Unregistered`, leaving alerts and background wakes unavailable.

## User Impact

This proposes bounded, registration-scoped recovery and an in-app retry path without reinstalling or re-pairing. Permission, successful publication, and delivery health remain separate: renewed/published registration is explicitly **delivery unverified**.

**Draft — not ready to merge.** Maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, native Swift build/test/lint checks, before/after UI screenshots, and signed official-device receipt testing remain outstanding. This PR does **not** establish that notification delivery is restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway preserves typed relay rejection on the existing registration owner. Republishing the same enrollment cannot erase the rejection merely by advancing its timestamp. Test pushes, wakes, and approval sends share the rejection-recording path; a stale result cannot poison a replacement enrollment.
- iOS consumes the existing authenticated `node.event` result, requests a current APNs token, and forces fresh relay enrollment for one automatic recovery cycle per unchanged token/scope. The existing publication flow serializes overlapping callbacks; failures stop automatic renewal and expose **Retry notification setup** in Diagnostics.
- Scoped Keychain enrollment caches retain rejected enrollment and consumed budgets across relaunches and Gateway switches. A matching shipped singleton is moved only after its scoped copy is saved. A new handle alone does not reset the budget; explicit manual retry or a changed token can authorize another attempt.
- Direct APNs behavior and unrelated registrations, pairings, Gateway credentials, and App Attest keys are preserved. No new RPC, configuration option, dependency, or version bump. Missing-registration #146791 is not folded into this fix.

## Evidence

**Current published source:** HEAD fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5, base2dc6deb7dd2fae392c03da64da175cc842ccdd70, tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. Current-tree verification passed326 unique tests across8 selected files /4 wrapper shards (53 infra +78 Gateway +195 schema/catalog tests,106.70s), production core and affected test typechecks, focused type-aware lint on12 files, pinned SwiftFormat0.63.1 on11 files, and scoped whitespace. Fresh independent review completed three chunks with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The32-file patch independently reproduced the exact tree; the published GitHub tree and required human credit were verified. This is not current-source native build/device or broad-CI proof. Earlier dated results below remain historical/prior-head evidence.


**Revision qualification (2026-11-03):** `pnpm test src/infra/push-apns.store.test.ts src/infra/push-apns.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.apns-registration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **52 tests across 3 files**, 66.82s wrapper wall time. The rejection regression now uses real HTTP instead of mocked fetch. The registration regression no longer mocks the event handler or pairing owner. This proves those local boundaries, not the hosted relay, WebSocket authentication handshake, iOS consent/route revocation before actual enrollment/publication, or device receipt. Fresh independent review of the complete candidate completed three chunks with no P0–P2 findings.

The primary regression failed before the production change for the intended reason: after a fixed relay `410 Unregistered` response, store reconstruction and unchanged enrollment republication had no retained `relayRejection`. The seven existing store tests passed on that baseline.

| Local check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Current push transport/store suites | 50 passed; real loopback HTTP rejection, reopen/unchanged republication, zero-I/O suppression, delayed old rejection vs replacement, successful HTTP control, revoked send authority, peer/direct controls |
| Current node.event registration integration | 2 parameterized tests / 6 route scenarios passed through actual handler, paired-device binding, NodeRegistry and worker admission; replacement/invalidation preserve prior and peer registrations at transaction and commit |
| Final store + read-kernel suites | 12 passed, including rejection/reopen/republication, fresh admission of an older-state copy, replacement protection and unaffected peer/direct registrations; 45.31s command wall / 5.02s Vitest |
| Earlier Gateway event/registration/push sibling suites | 79 passed; final modified event suite rerun: 54 passed, 64.02s command wall / 58.14s Vitest (mostly compiler/import setup) |
| Production and targeted infra/Gateway test typechecks | Prior production checks passed; current infra and Gateway-methods test typecheck shards passed |
| Scoped production/test lint; touched TS/JSON/Markdown formatting; whitespace | Passed |
| Kysely/PostgreSQL generation and SQLite catalog checks | Passed; generated outputs verified |
| Staged test-line budget | Passed; owned allocation accurately updated to 289 net TS regression/fixture lines |
| Pinned iOS formatting | SwiftFormat 0.63.1 built from exact tag; six files mechanically corrected; `pnpm format:swift ios` passed, 0/504 files require formatting |

Native Swift regressions are added for cached rejection, reconstruction, same-token renewal, repeated attempts/manual retry, **A → B → A enrollment counts**, changed-token renewal, direct transport, and matching-only legacy-cache migration. They have **not been executed** here: Linux has no Xcode/iOS SDK. The pinned SwiftFormat gate now passes; that is not a native build, SwiftLint, Swift test, or delivery result. No real device received a test push.

<details>
<summary>Review, persistence contract, and remaining qualification</summary>

**Review:** Local Auto Review, P0–P2, completed all four batches against base `bf35e054b0062c64e5577b165a3ae629adc3d2d0` and final candidate tree `cca63b6b6d1a2c7d6ceeb703fbaaaf83c455483c` with no remaining findings. Earlier findings about scope eviction resetting/bypassing recovery were addressed with per-scope enrollment persistence and an enrollment-count regression. This is static review, not human maintainer acceptance or native/device proof. The simplification pass retained one registration owner and removed redundant enrollment-flight bookkeeping; the complete token/publication cycle is serialized at its existing caller.

**Proposed persistent contract:** One nullable `relay_rejection_reason TEXT` column on `apns_registrations`, through existing same-version additive admission; null means no recorded rejection, not verified health. The affected SQL operation is an additive column change, with no row backfill or new index. SQLite STRICT admission may inspect existing rows; production-scale upgrade timing has not been measured. The existing database migration/backup owner is unchanged; no new backup mechanism is introduced. A compatible pre-change shared-state backup and matching runtime are required for rollback qualification. The test uses a closed, isolated older-state copy, not a released-binary upgrade.

Keychain cache/retry state is scoped by installation, Gateway identity, relay origin, environment, profile, proof policy and topic; records persist across scope switches and replace only that scope's enrollment. Matching legacy singleton migration leaves other bindings untouched and removes the singleton only after a scoped save. App Attest state is not reset. This persistence/retention/rollback contract still needs maintainer acceptance before merge.

**Before ready/merge:**
- Run the native build, focused Swift tests and pinned SwiftLint check; inspect and attach sanitized before/after Diagnostics screenshots in chat and this PR.
- Reproduce on the affected signed official device and compare token reacquisition alone, fresh enrollment with unchanged token, and the combined path. Re-establish the rejected baseline between experiments; verify actual alert receipt and background wake, not just APNs 200/publication/a different handle. Do not target unrelated devices.
- Qualify the hosted relay's enrollment identity semantics. If fresh enrollment returns an identical handle/grant, this candidate conservatively retains Gateway rejection; actual renewal semantics and the smallest successful recovery remain unproven.
- Complete latest-stable upgrade/rollback and supported-backend qualification. An integrity-verified 2026.10.10 released-store baseline and WAL-safe SQLite backup were created, but the isolated current-source harness did not complete credential-migration custody; that setup failure is **not** a product migration verdict or passing upgrade evidence. Live PostgreSQL migration and production-fleet upgrade cost were not tested.
- Obtain maintainer contract/security review and applicable CI. CI seconds are not available yet; no hosted review or merge was requested.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

title: fix(google): restore tool calls with Python keyword parameters
body:
Supersedes #143178, thanks @HighervGround.

Related: #143176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gemini tool calling when a declared parameter is a Python keyword such as `from`, `class`, or `lambda`.

## User Impact

Google and Vertex tools retain their original parameter names at execution. Existing suffix names and nested user data remain intact. This replacement includes only the Google parameter repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared Google converter chooses unused underscore aliases for declared top-level keyword parameters, restores returned arguments, and reapplies the aliases during signed history replay. GenerateContent, Vertex, Interactions, and explicit prompt caches use the same mapping. Cached requests retain canonical schemas for decoding while omitting cached declarations from the outgoing request.

The duplicate prompt-cache declaration builder is removed. Necessary production growth implements collision-safe schema-based mapping across the existing transports; there is no new cache, setting, persistence format, or dependency.

## Evidence

- Current-main source check: `65a125adc598deff3ded853f155acfa616d39c0c` passes tool properties and returned arguments unchanged. The contributor's captured Vertex bisection reports `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` with `automations.in`, and a valid call after renaming that property. [Google's function-calling documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling) describes JSON Schema parameters but does not document a Python-keyword restriction. No live Gemini API calls were made.
- Red before: on the unchanged main implementation, `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts` had exactly the two new failures (outgoing schema and inbound restoration), with 32 existing tests passing. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551852373).
- Green after: 211 tests pass across the four changed behavioral suites (SDK/Interactions, prompt cache, managed Google/Vertex); the 14 prompt-prefix cases and the 28 message-conversion/lifecycle/request-config cases also pass. Touched-file type-aware lint (0 warnings/errors), format, and `git diff --check` pass. [Crabbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552191472). Final named-test invocation took 45.49 s plus setup; the managed transport file took 10.84 s wall time, with the cache suite dominated by existing compiled-worker setup. Exact-head [CI run 41555285820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41555285820) passed: 45 successful jobs, 28 skipped, 11 min 51 s wall time and 7,810 summed job-seconds.
- CI repair proof: [the first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41553763628) found an extension test importing a core helper and a declaration-only assertion helper accepting the SDK’s broader tool-list type. Both test-only defects are fixed; production code is unchanged. The boundary guard, managed Google/Vertex transport, and SDK regression file now pass all 167 cases in 57.71 s, with touched-file lint/format green. [Crabbox repair proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554614333).
- Review: Local autoreview of the complete implementation diff against `65a125adc598deff3ded853f155acfa616d39c0c`, P0–P2, returned `scoped-clean`; no findings. A supplemental P0–P2 review of the CI fixture repairs against `6fe9bc666896375a6ae42fa5e2f925acbaae10f9` also returned `scoped-clean`. Simplification retained one schema/argument mapping owner and removed the duplicate cached declaration projection.
- LOC: production +116/−19 (net +97), tests/support +342/−11 (net +331). The dedicated test-line allocation covers only these regressions: schema projection, execution, signed replay, managed/Vertex transport, Interactions argument deltas, and cached declarations.
- The contributor branch was read through `gh` and was never checked out or run. Validation ran on our reimplementation in Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox. Broad proof is PR CI.

title: fix(memory): recover indexing after embedding request timeouts
body:
Supersedes #144488, thanks @Finn763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes memory indexing repeatedly sending the same oversized request after the embedding watchdog expires, leaving the indexing pass incomplete on a slow provider.

## User Impact

Indexing retries smaller requests after a watchdog timeout. A single input that still times out fails visibly. Query deadlines and provider-owned timeout defaults stay unchanged; no configuration or reindex is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing batch policy now splits a watchdog timeout immediately instead of spending three attempts on the same payload. Existing network retries, cancellation, malformed-response handling, ordering, and cache publication keep their owners.

Main already includes #167891 (603f60a38cfe658f3b9f1aee509595f39dc4540e), which removed the independent HTTP timeout and bounded deep probes. Sync cleanup also releases the pending promise and preserves dirty work after failure. The remaining defect is batch convergence, not a permanently latched sync. We are declining a new timeout setting: automatic recovery fits the existing provider-owned timeout contract without another public control.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 41552993820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552993820) passed on 3ad47b920f306e84a8f2d7055836b6a66fae25d7, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. No inherited-failure exception was needed.
- Hosted ClawSweeper review of that same head found no actionable findings or before-merge requirements; it notes the disclosed live CLI/transport proof gap.

- On main 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, the new manager regression fails for both text and structured batches with `MEMORY_EMBEDDING_OPERATION_FAILED`; the 24 existing manager cases pass.
- Blacksmith Testbox [41551644742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551644742): both affected suites pass, 85 tests. The real manager watchdog aborts requests of sizes 3 and 2, then returns all three vectors in order through singleton requests, with no unchanged-payload retry or provider degradation. Existing policy tests retain network retries and single-input stopping behavior.
- After a typed abort-error fixture correction: 26/26 manager cases pass again, touched-file type-aware lint reports zero warnings/errors, formatting passes, and `git diff --check` is clean. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate against 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, P0–P2: scoped-clean. The subsequent typed fixture rejection was inspected manually; production is unchanged.
- The focused two-file run takes 30.62 seconds including worker preparation; the final manager-only rerun takes 38.49 seconds. Test bodies take under one second. New watchdog cases use fake timers. The successful `checks-node-changed` CI job takes 298 seconds including shared setup.

Proof uses a synthetic provider through the production manager watchdog and split policy. Real single-core llama.cpp hardware and a live agent turn were not exercised. Contributor code was read with gh only and was never checked out or executed.

Simplification: one existing policy owner, no new state, helper, setting, or SDK surface. Production +5/−1 (net +4); no dead or duplicate production code in this narrow owner could be safely removed. Tests grow 30 lines for the missing watchdog recovery boundary, covered by a separate allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

title: fix(sandbox): remove containers when backend preparation fails
body:
Supersedes #143755, thanks @aishwary-dongre.
Related: #143685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a newly created Docker or Podman sandbox stays running when backend preparation fails after its container has started.

## User Impact

User impact: failed provisioning removes its newly allocated container and registry entry while preserving the original error. Reused containers and the existing revoked-access retention policy are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep backend mount inspection, filesystem bridge loading, and persistent-generation preparation inside the existing container lifecycle lock and cleanup boundary. This reuses immutable-ID cleanup and consolidates the duplicated allocation result; it adds no rollback tracker or attempt-wide custody protocol.

This is a bounded provisioning repair. Failures after a completed backend is returned to agent-attempt preparation remain follow-up work under #143685. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

Production delta: +37 lines, including the typed internal preparation callback; most of the backend diff is indentation. Duplicate allocation-result construction was removed. Tests grow by 22 lines, covered by the dedicated regression allocation record.

## Evidence

- Reviewed current main at `9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d`, existing cleanup from #150713, and the recent Podman timeout fix #188770. The remaining leak was the backend inspection after the lifecycle returned.
- On Blacksmith Testbox, the new fake-runtime regression is red on main: create=1, start=1, remove=0 after backend inspection fails. With this fix, the same regression removes the fresh allocation, preserves a reused runtime, and propagates the exact original error object.
- 73 focused tests pass across `docker.access-lifetime.test.ts`, `docker.partial-create-cleanup.test.ts`, `docker-backend.test.ts`, and `dependency-template.test.ts`. The four-file run took 68.86s command wall time; one stale mock-call expectation was corrected, and its 33-test backend file passes in 41.47s command wall time. Wall time was dominated by transforms. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551266696).
- The two affected Gateway checkpoint cases and both cleanup regression cases pass on a fresh Testbox lease (51.40s command wall across two named files). title: fix(update): select PostgreSQL in migrated finalizer
body:
Closes #191542

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: migrated update finalization starts a fresh process without the parent’s PostgreSQL selection. Its first ledger adoption opens the SQLite engine anchor as a state database, reports a missing schema role, and never publishes the final result.

## User Impact

Normal fresh-process finalization now enters the existing updater database scope before executor, ledger, and terminal-result access. It reads the configured engine and environment-backed connection through the canonical owner, preserving PostgreSQL history and the local anchor.

The capability check stays configuration-free. The Windows native Job is retained before any pool worker starts. Doctor, post-core, and plugin-cohort modes retain their existing recovery and configuration owners; cleanup remains the existing best-effort owner with database drains before pool closure. No schema, configuration, credentials-in-wire, protocol, or timeout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Engine selection is process-local and cannot cross the spawned finalizer boundary. Reusing `withUpdateDatabaseEngine` repairs the producer rather than inferring an engine from the anchor or repairing the anchor as SQLite. The extra pool call is retained only for sibling modes; normal finalization uses the canonical scoped preparation.

## Evidence

- **Actual causal RED:** baseline `f381764cf5964d7885ed459f41a9cf8041dfd244` on pinned `bf35e054`, [PostgreSQL conformance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41553655060/job/125648227953). The executed fresh child reports “schema role missing; expected global” for its PostgreSQL anchor, then the regression fails because no parsed child result was returned (13.2 seconds). The infrastructure group had 274 passing cases; both other conformance shards passed. Earlier skipped ordinary-node tests and static assertion-narrowing failures are not product proof.
- The regression retains the actual parent selection, delegated executor, fresh finalizer, PostgreSQL pool and ledger. Only the absent native-service observation is isolated and guarded to owned state. Production child mode excludes test preloads and worker environment-data fallback. It requires the parsed child result, terminal PostgreSQL row, and anchor-only local file, so parent fallback cannot pass.
- The supplied core result intentionally fails to bound the same adoption/publication boundary without unrelated Doctor/package work. This does not claim a complete successful Git update, actual schema migration, or managed Gateway restart.
- Fresh complete independent autoreview against pinned `bf35e054` (Codex, P0–P2): scoped-clean. Focused canonical oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Production TypeScript net +12 lines; most diff is lexical scope indentation. Exact allocation181 covers175 PostgreSQL process-test lines, one native-service fixture line and five existing wire/cleanup fixture-isolation lines. No test-only production seam or timeout increase.
- **Actual fixed-head GREEN:** `6dd924b6f93b415ae58e87a75fd7180430005f55` passed the [executed PostgreSQL finalizer regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41557001142/job/125658928774) in 17.561 seconds. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the required exact-head checks succeeded, with planned skips retained. The protected `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/dependency-review`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` statuses also succeeded. CodeQL's aggregate is neutral because 18 other analysis configurations are absent; this is a coverage warning, not proof that all CodeQL configurations analyzed the change. No local product tests were run on the production host. This proves selected-storage finalization and result publication for the intentional failed-core case; it does not claim serving health or a full successful Git upgrade.

Reported by @etzelm. The earlier CLI-role repair #187160 establishes a different bootstrap fact; this change supplies the missing engine selection.

title: docs(macos): explain Gateway Local Network recovery
