title: fix: allow verified upstream workflows in guest publications
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A guest can refresh a feature branch from upstream and still have publication rejected because inherited GitHub workflow changes are mistaken for guest-authored changes once the histories diverge.

## User Impact

Guests can publish ordinary work after inheriting verified upstream workflows without needing full operator write permission. Guest-authored workflow edits remain blocked, including edits whose final contents happen to match upstream. Ambiguous, incomplete, or overly large histories fail closed with a visible next step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the repository-only blanket divergence refusal with a pinned, complete source-side ancestry proof. Each proof is bounded to 1,000 commits and 32 additional ancestry boundaries.
- Compare the previous publication and the accepted source against their own ancestors. This preserves legitimate upstream merges without laundering source-owned edits.
- Keep exact workflow path, mode, blob, and absence comparisons in one shared owner for local and repository-only publication. Preserve current-authority checks before external effects.
- No new configuration, dependency, schema, or broader guest permission.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original failure through the repository publication coordinator before the fix.
- Both workflow regression suites: **62 cases have passing evidence** (60 passed in the combined run; the two I/O-timeout cases passed on targeted retry with unchanged timeout limits). Coverage includes first/existing publication, source merges, crisscross ambiguity, pagination beyond 100 commits, malformed pages, bounded work, and authority revocation.
- Guest refresh-to-publish recovery integration: **1 test passed**.
- Core and affected test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The 216-line test-budget allocation passes the local budget gate.
- Fresh independent source review: no actionable findings. Local autoreview at P0–P2 on an equivalent pinned candidate snapshot (`1db1416…` to `75f7b7d…`, tree `ee26ff5…`): no findings. The CLI review lacked unchanged-repository context; the independent review covered affected owners and callers.
- Required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks passed on `65997aa5d57f9b6a24c28587f02dd842a465ae6e`.

### Independent live GitHub boundary proof

Using the production publication coordinator, isolated synthetic requester/session fixtures, and real GitHub transport against an owned private test repository at the same production head:

- **Allow:** divergent source inheriting upstream workflows published a real PR. Independent PR/ref/content readback verified the published head, preserved upstream workflow, and ordinary code change.
- **Reject:** a guest-owned workflow edit whose final contents matched upstream was rejected with **zero attempted publication mutations**.
- **Revoke:** authority was revoked after the real source-side ancestry comparison completed. The requester was confirmed unauthorized; publication failed with `identity_changed`, with **zero publication mutations**, including zero after revocation.

The private harness is excluded from this PR. Earlier harness setup/transport/assertion failures were corrected; they are not counted as passing product tests. The positive publication was retained and read back rather than repeated to fix stale harness assertions. These are live GitHub-boundary results, not a full Gateway/model end-to-end replay or deployment. The committed regression suites use real Git objects with mocked GitHub transport.

## Worked on by

- @fuller-stack-dev

Successful cold template preparations end with `reason=ready`, hiding why the previous generation could not be reused.

title: fix(whatsapp): retry DMs while LID identity is unavailable
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp DMs are silently lost when their LID-to-phone mapping becomes available after intake.

Supersedes #158140, thanks @YangManBOBO.

Part of #119475

## User Impact

DMs from `@lid` and `@hosted.lid` remain eligible for delivery while their phone mapping is temporarily unavailable. The mapped phone still goes through the existing sender authorization policy. Group handling is unchanged.

Permanently unresolved messages use the existing shared retry policy: exponential backoff capped at three minutes, dead-lettering after both the eight-attempt floor and 24-hour minimum age. A pending message can hold its conversation lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Throwing for an unresolved direct LID lets the existing durable ingress owner retry instead of completing a non-message. Completed-message receipt preparation catches normalization failures per message so a lost mapping cannot abort later messages in the same batch. Deduplication uses the existing transport-key completion tombstone.

Open overlap #106998 (`c281acb789bec20665a9d9bd395e22be00606372`) changes group classification and quoted-message identity metadata. Its resolver retains the unresolved-mapping `null` contract. It neither covers nor conflicts with this retry behavior; this fix works independently.

title: improve(k8s): limit remount permission changes and document storage adoption
body:
Related: #192959

## What Problem This Solves

Kubernetes can widen private storage permissions during an fsGroup remount, and the template needs to distinguish prevention from recovery of existing data.

## User Impact

The template requests `OnRootMismatch` to avoid repeated kubelet permission walks when the volume root already matches. The full restart issue in #192959 remains unresolved: this does not repair already widened paths, establish private ownership, or govern CSI drivers that delegate fsGroup handling through `VOLUME_MOUNT_GROUP`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document the persistent capture sibling, safe use of explicitly provisioned `subPath` children, and storage-owner adoption of existing data. Switching the supplied root-state PVC to an empty child can hide its state; existing home-volume children require verified ownership, source-entry protection, and trusted target ancestry. Credential and capture admission checks remain unchanged. No automatic migration, chmod implementation, operator commands, or new security authority is introduced.

## Evidence

- Existing named file `test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts`: **4 passed**, 175 ms, through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with a narrow one-file config, Node, one worker, and a private fixture root. Retained log: `.local/da-k8s-pvc-restart/qualification/k8s-manifests-private-tmp.log`. This covers manifest wiring and sticky temporary storage, not kubelet/PVC behavior.
- Targeted repository oxfmt check: both changed files passed. Log: `.local/da-k8s-pvc-restart/qualification/format-check-final.log`.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Only `docs/install/kubernetes.md` and `scripts/k8s/manifests/deployment.yaml` changed, with 69 additions. Product build is not applicable to these documentation/YAML changes; no build, staging, or packaging was run.
- Independent official autoreview (Codex, local candidate against `863cd7ed4151688667338f534ef348aeeb7bdf4b`, P0–P3): **scoped-clean**, no findings for the complete two-file patch. The helper omitted unchanged sensitive credential implementation context; the independent reviewer inspected those guards separately. Patch SHA-256: `877c147abd64461b3377d3361e74a78a3c6e9a3ee9f6cb82e56e703dc502ff97`; both candidate raw SHA-256 hashes verified unchanged before commit. Retained review: `tmp/reports/dh-k8s-safe-review.md`; official status: `tmp/reports/dh-k8s-safe-autoreview-2-status.json` (local evidence, not public artifact URLs).

**UNRUN:** actual initial boot and PVC remount on Kubernetes/OpenShift, existing-PVC adoption, and recovery on the proposed layout. The fixture tests are not equivalent to a real PVC lifecycle. The full issue needs a qualified deployment layout, initializer, and live proof. The unrun proposed regression remains outside source and is not part of this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a nested child session leaves it hidden behind collapsed sidebar ancestors, including after following a **Waiting on** link.

Unrelated branches and sections remain unchanged, including those with running work. Ordinary same-route refreshes respect subsequent manual collapses and Show more choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection owns navigation-scoped reveal bookkeeping for both rows and sections; the section organizer remains the only writer of section settings. A selected-only recursive search unwinds the ancestor path, pagination retains its root, and stable route identity handles partial or late lineage. The new navigation state is language-private. Existing run-only subagent folding stays unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Reviewed source:** `1c12515bb627444df363abebd40163eb8b1b9cfd`; published head `a2352ed8ec5ecf5759a23c15777f8287d81eb1e8` has its identical tree. **154 focused tests and all 11 Chromium scenarios pass**, including 20 projection and 22 lineage/snapshot cases. The browser flow exercises three levels, a collapsed owning section, off-cap children, direct URL reload, actual history navigation from an explicitly collapsed path, and an unrelated running branch. The initial browser regression fails on baseline `b6d6079da6edcbc35f7d86d9abf475429a1e7a69` after navigation, not during setup. Local wall time on the busy host: 66.14 s for the four unit files and 141.78 s for the browser file.
- **Exact CI-base repair:** integrated `0fd7cc749198916d05c2d607ed59c7eb1bbffb64` because the previous CI merge-ref used that newer boot graph. Removed duplicate section-reveal lifecycle state. They cover distinct lineage, pagination, grouped disclosure, manual-collapse, URL and history failures. The shared scalar is untouched; the exact-base ratchet reports 30 lines slack.
- **Performance:** final qualification is the exact-head `control-ui-performance` result in [this PR's checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192974/checks), under unchanged byte ceilings and variance allowances. The local comparison for the language-private candidate stalled in full-source Git archive for over nine minutes, before a build or measurement. That failed setup is not product proof; PR CI uses its pinned Node runtime. No performance-budget exception was added.
- **Inherited UI failure:** the offline-catalog case in `chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx` fails identically on exact CI base `0fd7cc749198916d05c2d607ed59c7eb1bbffb64` and the merged candidate (expected Offline, received Disconnected; 14 other tests pass). Its test and production files are unchanged by this patch.
- **Independent review:** after local ClawSweeper's endpoint Git reads became unavailable, the documented isolated Codex autoreview fallback completed a full P0–P3 review of `0fd7cc749198916d05c2d607ed59c7eb1bbffb64..1c12515bb627444df363abebd40163eb8b1b9cfd`, with intact owning/caller/test source context, one full pass and **no actionable findings**. The earlier proposed transient-section-storage requirement is declined: opening the owning section intentionally uses its existing persisted disclosure operation, like a manual toggle. Unrelated sections and subsequent same-route manual collapse are preserved and tested; the requested repair does not require automatic recollapse or a second transient settings overlay. Hosted ClawSweeper review is tracked separately in the discussion and is advisory under the repository workflow.

### Before and after

Actual product UI after following **Waiting on** into the same synthetic three-level hierarchy. Before: the selected conversation opens but its owning group and ancestors stay collapsed. After: the selected path is visible and the unrelated Website section stays collapsed. Later ownership and representation repairs preserve this behavior through the current browser regression. Both images were inspected and verified inline on the actual PR.

The existing sidebar tree and registry ancestry already fold activity recursively. The missing path was the resident row owner’s stored-child aggregate: an immediate child contribution did not include that child’s own derived descendant activity.

Reuse that owner and its canonical child links, child-inclusion/promotion policy, and invalidation lifecycle. Propagate descendant expiry and volatility into the existing contribution cache, with a path-local cycle guard. No new persistent state, parallel graph, client polling, or run-control semantics. A paused chain without active leaf work stays inactive.

title: feat(sessions): discover own sessions and post without starting turns
body:
## Current status

Current head: 490871ac852aa9794a7c7944fe6b20b0027140fd. Open for maintainer review; **not a merge-readiness claim**. No merge or deployment is authorized. This is the existing replacement for #192811, related to #178739 as a partial first stage, not a closure. The continuing session below retains publication ownership.

## Latest schema line-cap correction

The exact-dce9 hosted review first reported no findings (revision 8), then its automatically started revision 9 identified a separate PR-caused line-cap violation. The newer finding supersedes that earlier clean verdict. Locally reproduced: packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts grew from 700 to 701 counted lines against cap 700.

The value and type re-exports from sessions-post.js are now one standard combined declaration. Exported names, types, runtime behavior, consent and access rules are unchanged. No cap, budget, baseline or coverage was reduced. The same line-cap checker changed from exit 1 to exit 0; canonical formatting, gateway validator check (all generated outputs unchanged), protocol-registry check and diff check passed.

This head differs from dce9 only in that source file (+1/-2 lines). Final validated tree: ddf6b5505fb45d25729e4f1f798647818945bc29. Earlier runtime tests remain bound to their stated consent candidate; this equivalent export consolidation is not represented as a new model run.

The hosted dce9 CI census at 22:18 UTC reconciled 178 checks: 106 success, 67 skipped, 1 neutral, 2 failed and 2 running. The failures were baseline-ratchets and its aggregate gate; iOS/macOS Periphery remained running. The hosted test-line diagnostic was 49 over on its merge result, distinct from the local accepted-base 51 deficit. Neither is waived. New-head CI/review and human maintainer disposition remain unverified.

## Current risk-weighted test reduction

At the requester's direction, this revision reduces low-value coverage rather than adding tests. Production code and behavior are byte-identical to 39988537. Only two test suites and their allocation record change.

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Own-post suite LF | 781 | 782 |
| Consent suite LF | 375 | 330 |
| Combined test LF | 1,156 | 1,112 (-44) |
| Gateway test cases | 24 | 23 |

Removed the dedicated self-note exemption integration case: the canonical communication owner already tests send/receive Never on the same endpoint without approval. Accepted gap: a future post-specific false rejection of a self-note is no longer independently exercised end to end; it is relatively unlikely, visible and recoverable, outside the core cross-session use case.

Removed the missing-target dispatch variant—not because it was impossible or already sanitized. Accepted gap: unknown-session error classification could regress. Real catalog denial envelopes, creator/outbound rejection, and durable append/incarnation protections remain covered.

Strengthened existing cases without adding tests: the creator-only negative now uses a shared Bob-created target in an all-visible, nonsandboxed context, where the operator otherwise has write access; it asserts the exact creator denial, runId and durable non-persistence. Tree-scoped foreign-read/list isolation remains. Config-withdrawal cases publish an immutable replacement and track the current object, leaving the captured original unchanged. Ordinary-send Never controls, real Ask decisions, after-await withdrawal, cross-human isolation, idempotency and non-steering coverage remain.

Validation: 23/23 focused tests passed in the helper and again in the parent publication worktree (94.51s runner / 97.39s command). Gateway-root typecheck covers both changed suites; targeted lint, format, scoped diff checks and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed with no findings. Test ownership proof is reused because filenames/registry are unchanged. Runtime/cache conditions differ from earlier runs, so no controlled speedup claim is made.

Reviewed patch SHA-256: 61373ee69f620320f6bcc49a4fa40abf5b21e8d7e8db849ee98e30429bcb3448. Final published tree including allocation bookkeeping: e9d63dae81ab90cb50cbd81c2fb69d645f6447e2.

Allocation credit was reduced by exactly 44 (387 to 343); total feature growth/credit is now 1,142, not 1,186. No unused credit was retained to hide main's deficit. The accepted-base ratchet still fails with 6,552,829 lines against 6,552,778 ceiling, the same inherited 51-line gap. This cleanup is not presented as a budget waiver or full CI pass. New-head hosted outcomes remain unverified.

## Problem and solution

People currently relay context manually between independent sessions they created. This PR adds creator-scoped discovery/read access and persistent, attributed text-only posts that do not start, steer, interrupt, or continue the recipient agent. Later normal turns can access the note.

The feature reuses existing access, communication-consent, and transcript owners. Explicit self/agent/A2A/outbound restrictions, foreign-principal isolation, session-incarnation checks, idempotency, and current requester/target authority remain enforced. No session-link registry or separate permission/state owner is introduced.

## Latest repair: communication consent

The prior hosted P1 was reproduced through registered tools and the real session/Gateway fixture: ordinary sends rejected source communication.send=never and recipient communication.receive=never while passive posts persisted. Passive posts now use the existing communication owner for Never/Ask, actual human approval, lineage and live-policy assertions through durable append, closing the lifetime afterward.

The requester explicitly chose **option 1**: preserve existing passive-post thread targeting while enforcing consent. An internal passive-delivery intent shares the exact consent/approval owner but not peer-turn thread-target restrictions. Ordinary sends retain tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets. The creator-only tree exception is preserved without manufacturing spawned ownership; canonical same-session/owned-task consent exemptions remain unchanged. No new public option, ACL, schema, live setting, or grant change was added by this repair.

Ask coverage uses the real QuestionManager and question.resolve with explicit Allow/Deny, not mocked automatic approval. Controls cover Never at both endpoints, pending/denied non-persistence, approved append, consent withdrawal before append, thread targeting versus ordinary-send opt-in, and canonical same-session exemption.

The previously fixed P2 remains: all passive-post denial branches use canonical sendFailure so catalog output validation receives schema-required runId instead of replacing intended refusals with output_contract errors. Caller, target, communication, visibility and outbound guards remain composed through persistence; source-transcript writer detachment is retained.

## Consent-repair validation (before test reduction)

- Parent integration: both Gateway suites **24/24 passed**, 109.02s runner / 112.01s command wall time.
- Helper final layout: **24 Gateway tests plus 10 canonical test-ownership tests**, exit 0, 126.682s. Original own-session-posts suite is unchanged; consent tests have a dedicated canonical database-worker file.
- Shared communication-owner, question-authorization and fixture consumers: **90 tests passed**, 155.837s.
- Never reproduction was red on the published source: two cases, exit 1, 52.585s.
- Final Gateway-root typecheck with --listFiles passed and explicitly included both production owners, the new test and shared fixture. Targeted lint, six-file format, scoped full-index diff, docs inventory and import-cycle checks passed. Post-split checks were completed; interrupted attempts are not counted as passing receipts.
- Fresh native independent P0–P2 review of the exact six-file diff with full ordinary-send/post, consent, approval, append and source-authority context: **scoped-clean, no findings**. Static review did not rerun tests.
- Reviewed patch SHA-256: 9adbd600d910f3608511569ef9fa1538ea596299ee12045d78d75e3ba05cc08b. Reviewed source tree before allocation: fdc71884a11f7de60df58ba9f5df66ae7d6384c8. Final candidate/published tree including allocation: 4696da35dc1d5e22322cf5dc417aeee9c0687d63.

The consent regression adds exactly 387 LF lines (375 new test + 12 net shared support), with a separate 387-line allocation. Total feature test/support growth and allocation are both 1,186. No shared baseline or inherited-debt credit was increased. On accepted base 650091daacdc10aa374e82a6327e8beffe136072 the ratchet still fails with 6,552,873 lines versus ceiling 6,552,822: the same inherited **51-line deficit** as before this repair. This remains an explicit maintainer/CI gate, not a waived or passing check. Current hosted CI seconds/results remain unverified.

## Earlier repairs and integration

- Current accepted base remains 650091. Its only prior conflict was the overflow-compaction fixture; the fuller upstream prompt/provider mock was retained and its 13 tests passed. No new base refresh was performed for this consent repair.
- Earlier CI fixes corrected the fixture Promise contract, canonical test ordering without changing isolation, session access/resolution import cycle, legacy advertised-method append order, and generated prompt snapshots. They have source-bound local and hosted receipts on their recorded earlier heads, not relabeled as new-head results.
- Engineering commits [444d35b5](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/commit/444d35b5479e01d95da0ffbaceb0005516343499), [b5456f34](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/commit/b5456f34603ee68b46a77f748f0852d91a6e818d), and [aa69e44a](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/commit/aa69e44a565f6aaf2911c547197c4a3b00ba8a7f) supplied foreign-owner and post-admission withdrawal regressions. Controls directly inspect durable non-persistence.

## Independent runtime evidence — keep source identities distinct

- [Restricted-principal trial at 273780c3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192948#issuecomment-6684006275): two separately authenticated synthetic restricted profiles created/posted to their own Drafts; cross-owner listing/posting was denied; direct transcripts held only allowed markers. The candidate Gateway/WebSocket harness ran on Mac loopback. The VM reached the temporary proxy but did not host that Gateway. Not real Team guest acceptance.
- [Real-model follow-up at 273780c3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192948#issuecomment-6685073824): idle post persisted before a model turn; a later Ollama turn retrieved the exact marker through sessions_history after the client timed out. Busy overlap returned posted, retry returned the same ID with replayed=true, SQLite held one marker, and the observed active turn completed without mentioning it. This supports model-accessible persistence, deduplication and observed non-interruption—not automatic prompt inclusion or an internal active-prompt snapshot. Unreliable smaller-model attempts are excluded.
- Engineering's monitor-1825 coordination report at exact 9cc4fcb4: isolated Node 24 production-handler fixture **2/2 passed, 40.59s**. title: fix: stop older Telegram photos replaying in Codex image requests
body:
Supersedes #144567, thanks @yelloduxx.
Related: #144556.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unrelated older Telegram photos accompany a new Codex photo request when conversation history is reconstructed.

## User Impact

A new photo turn keeps its entire current album; a text follow-up keeps the latest eligible photo album. Captions and saved attachment references remain available for explicit retrieval. A current photo with intentionally omitted pixels also prevents older photos from being substituted.

This intentionally limits automatic replay of image-only Telegram user turns. Mixed document/image turns retain their existing behavior, and images already in native thread history remain there.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection uses the media host's canonical image classification, including stickers and path-derived image types. A zero-budget host request recognizes current photo sources without hydrating attachment content. The existing projection keeps historical text and references while selecting complete photo turns.

Removed the redundant projection-options copy. Production grows by 41 lines for source classification and photo selection; the 116 added regression lines have an exact allocation record.

## Evidence

- Synthetic nonbrowser tests use real PNG bytes, the production media host and run-attempt path, and capture native `turn/start` input with a mocked Codex app-server. Five selection cases fail on trusted main `7aa96ecca2f815b45f0923e38f71f649edb02bbf`; two additional current-photo omission cases fail before the metadata-only repair.
- Final focused proof: 86 tests passed across six named files, including all 13 attachment-boundary cases. The boundary file completed in 16.40 seconds; all six test shards completed in 156.14 seconds on Testbox.
- Touched-file type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final local candidate against `7aa96ecca2f815b45f0923e38f71f649edb02bbf`: scoped-clean through P2, with full producer/admission/recorder context. The current-photo finding from the earlier review was reproduced and fixed.

Live Telegram and final provider HTTP requests remain unverified. Broad build/CI proof is pending; this replacement stays a draft for independent parent review and landing. The contributor's code was not checked out or executed.

title: fix: preserve child results when the parent continuation stalls
body:
## Problem

A parent agent accepts a completed child result, and then its follow-up turn stalls. The session watchdog fails that turn with `Reply operation stalled`. Before this change, the batch settled with no delivery at all. The child's work was done and saved, but the user never saw a result or any notice that one existed. Retrying the parent turn is not a safe fix, because it could repeat external operations that already ran.

## Change

When the watchdog fails an admitted parent continuation, the batch now owes a **delivery-only fallback** and never another agent turn.

- **Detection:** the typed watchdog cause is recognized through the real Gateway `UNAVAILABLE` error envelope. This applies only to requester settlement (`subagent_settle`). Ordinary announces, media completions and harness completions keep their existing failure handling.
- **Where the notice goes:**
  - Direct-message origins get the notice in that chat through the existing direct-delivery owner.
  - Threads, groups, channels and internal requesters get it appended to the requester's session transcript, so it shows in history and in the parent's next turn.
- **Privacy:** if any child in the batch is private (`completionTarget: "parent"`), including after `sessions_yield` and in mixed batches, the notice is generic and contains no child findings. Only all-public batches include the retained results. This keeps the contract from #156540: a yield may publish the parent's own answer, never its private child input.
- **Authority:** current requester ownership is checked right before the transcript append, and again inside it against the expected session and lifecycle revision. If ownership was revoked or replaced, nothing is written or sent.
- **Retries:** an external send is retried only when the existing `isRetryableDeliveryNotSentError` classifier proves nothing was sent (for example `ECONNREFUSED` on `connect`). An ambiguous or interrupted send is never resent.
- **Budget:** the stall fallback has its own bounded budget of 3 attempts. A stall on the parent's last attempt therefore still gets a notice. The marker is persisted before the first attempt, so a restart cannot start a second parent turn.

No new configuration, storage owner or coordinator. The only new persisted field is the optional `requesterStallFallback` marker on the batch. `fallbackResultText` and `fallbackCapturedAt` already existed.

**Accepted edge case:** a stall from a group, thread or channel origin is marked `external` before the attempt, even though the notice ends up in the transcript. If the process restarts during that single SQLite append, recovery treats it as an unconfirmed external attempt. It records the outcome as ambiguous instead of resending: the results stay retained, no notice appears, and nothing is duplicated.

## Real behavior proof

All cases ran against an isolated real Gateway (loopback, temporary state) with real agent turns. The parent stall came from the real session watchdog, and every requester reset was a real `sessions.reset` through the Gateway. A unique sentinel in each child result was scanned across every visible transcript record and outbound send.

Full redacted terminal output, commands and evidence: **[live proof on `bfde2eb8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192845#issuecomment-6708198274)** and **[upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192845#issuecomment-6708198445)**.

| Case (head `bfde2eb8` unless noted) | Boundary | Result | Final-effect evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Committed opt-in test `subagent-parent-stall.live.test.ts`, public batch (`f8b0a1eb`) | transcript, allowed | Pass | Child result visible once and not repeated after two more sweeps. The child and parent external operations each ran once. |
| Private child after `sessions_yield` | transcript, findings forbidden | Pass | Only the generic notice is visible. Sentinel `visibleHits:0`; its only hit is the hidden input record (`display:false`). No outbound send. |
| Mixed private and public children | transcript, findings forbidden | Pass | Generic notice only. Neither the private sentinel nor the public result is visible. |
| Requester reset just before the fallback write | transcript, revoked before effect | Pass | The append threw `Requester completion ownership changed before stall fallback.` Nothing was appended or sent. |
| Requester reset **during recovery**, after a persisted fallback retry and past its backoff window | transcript, revoked during recovery | Pass | No append to the old or new session, no send, sentinel absent. The retry was dropped without reaching the write again across two backoff windows. |
| DM origin, public batch, real `qa-channel` outbound adapter | outbound, allowed | Pass | `outboundSends=1 outboundWithResult=1`, `delivered:true, path:"direct"`. No transcript append. |
| DM origin, requester revoked before the send and across the retry window | outbound, revoked | Pass | Send refused with the ownership error. `outboundSends=0`, no append, sentinel absent from the old and new session. |
| Telegram group origin, private child (`f8b0a1eb`) | route selection | Pass | No direct route and nothing sent. The notice was appended to the requester transcript without findings. |
| **Base `c5b22153`**, private child after yield | transcript | **Fail (expected)** | The notice contained `Child result … PRIVATE_SENTINEL_<id>` in a visible assistant message. This is the leak this PR fixes. |

**Upgrade from latest stable** (`openclaw@latest` 2026.11.1 → `bfde2eb8`, same state directory):

- Stable wrote a completed batch and a pending yielded batch, the latter stopped mid-child. No stable row carries `requesterStallFallback`.
- `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 and migrated the agent DB v27→v41 and the state DB v22→v39, with backups.
- The Gateway restored both stable payload shapes with no subagent, announce or settle errors, and the stable transcripts read correctly.
- The pending batch settled normally with no fallback, because an absent field means no fallback is owed. A new spawn → yield → settle run then worked end to end.

**Limits of this proof**

- **Instrumentation:** the private, mixed, revoked and DM cases come from a temporary, uncommitted live test. It wraps the real transcript-append and direct-send functions, calling straight through and recording attempts. Pass/fail also uses the real chat history, full transcript reads and qa-bus send counts.
- **Recovery revocation:** the during-recovery case forces the first fallback write to fail in order to create a persisted retry. It is not a process crash between persisting and retrying.
- **Delivery record after revocation:** when the requester is revoked, the child's delivery record stays `pending / intentional_non_delivery` while the requester's wake state is cleared. No further attempts occur.
- **Telegram:** synthetic group key and target with no plugin loaded, so this covers route selection only.
- **Unit-only:** the stall-on-last-parent-attempt budget and the proven-no-send retry classification.
- **Upgrade:** run natively, because the Docker upgrade harness needs Docker, which this host lacks. `openclaw update` itself was not exercised. A succeeded-child batch waiting only on the parent wake could not be captured from stable, because stable sends that wake immediately.
- **Found during the upgrade proof, not caused by this PR:** a child result left `pending/retryable` while its parent was mid-turn at shutdown is retried after a stable → stable restart. Current `main` without this PR, and `2026.11.5-beta.1`, instead mark the parent `orphaned-run-interrupted` and leave the delivery pending. That needs a separate fix on `main`.

## Tests

Each regression was confirmed red on the previous head and green with the fix:

- `uses only a generic notice for private findings (mixed, yielded, attempts)` — private, mixed and yielded batches withhold findings, and a stall on the last parent attempt still gets the fallback.
- `retries stall recovery only after proven no-send` — `ECONNREFUSED`/`connect` is retried; `ECONNRESET`/`read` is never retried.
- `delivers a truthful visible notice (route, findings)` — transcript, DM and group routes; group origins append to the transcript.
- `does not append after an ambiguous external send`.
- `announce watchdog stall` row — ordinary announces keep `path: "direct"`, `disposition: "retryable"` and the error callback.
- Real-SQLite transcript test for visible persistence and idempotency.

**Validation**

- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed on `f8b0a1eb` and again on the merged head `bfde2eb8`.
- Targeted oxlint and format checks passed, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- 468 tests passed on `f8b0a1eb` across the announce directory, transcript fallback, delivery state, registry store and the requester-wake end-to-end suite (32 cases). The same 39 files pass again on `bfde2eb8`.
- Mock-export ratchet passed.
- Test-line ratchet: test growth is +606 lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/subagent-parent-stall-recovery.txt`. The hosted ratchet check passed on `f8b0a1eb`.

Size against the merge base: production +289/−21, tests +870/−264, docs +14/−4.

Reviewed locally by two independent passes; the last pass approved with no blocking findings. `bfde2eb8` merges current `main`, including the unrelated UI e2e fix #194504; this PR's code is unchanged since `f8b0a1eb`. No merge or deployment is part of this PR.

title: feat(android): sign in to Gateways protected by browser-session proxies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android native connections do not inherit a browser-session reverse-proxy login. The onboarding flow could also wait indefinitely for optional phone-node access after operator chat was already authorized.

**Published source:** [6cde97f4079e2a2ca0c806c9aa572ee207a99bc5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6cde97f4079e2a2ca0c806c9aa572ee207a99bc5). GitHub commit/tree readback confirms tree b993b3a3201c2167c0f06adeebffe649dccdee28 and all 42 feature source/test/documentation files. This includes the browser-lifecycle/consumer corrections and the exact non-test WebView shadow registration needed for complete JUnit discovery. Current-head CI and hosted/maintainer review remain separate gates; no merge or deployment.

## User Impact

- Enter one full Gateway URL: HTTPS defaults to 443, explicit ports win, and the existing local HTTP, IPv6, path and bare-host port18789 contracts remain intact.
- After verified native operator admission, browser authentication returns to the original native flow automatically. A legitimate device-pairing requirement can hand back to native approval; cookies, HTTP200 or a matching URL alone never confirm login.
- An operator-ready connection can continue to chat while optional phone-node access remains pending. Node capabilities still require their separate consent and Gateway approval; companion-only readiness is not operator login.
- Explicit replacement/signout retires only that Gateway's app browser authority, role grants and locally cached conversations. Other Gateways and the persistent device identity remain intact. Saved-session signout is reachable on the persistent Settings → Gateway card after automatic return.
- Renderer loss disposes only its owned browser and retires unadmitted work without revoking an already-admitted native session. Late callbacks cannot revive a retired attempt. Actual platform profile calls require MULTI_PROFILE support.
- Browser capture stays protected in ordinary debug and release builds. Recording requires an explicit debug-only build flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

One app-private WebView-profile owner supplies cookies for actual native HTTPS request URLs, with exact-origin/port and browser domain/path selection. Native admission, profile/attempt/cookie epochs, cancellation and target-bound runtime state own progress. Pending role grants and subsequent consumers cannot inherit a different browser principal's acceptance. Accepted-profile rotation/restart preserves its credential scope; explicit account replacement does not reuse it.

There is no LDAP client, JS credential bridge, TLS bypass, external-browser cookie copying or automatic device/node approval. Gateway shared-secret and trusted-proxy enforcement remain separate. Signout is local app-session retirement, not a promise of IdP-wide logout or LDAP-account revocation.

Related: #147061, #147307, #147305. Existing Cloudflare CustomTabs/service-header work is not recreated. Main's merged identity-disclosure fix #195997 and native fixture work #197407 are preserved in the integrated base.

Related: #178739

> **Draft handoff for external validation.** This is a partial first stage and does not close the full issue. Real-agent/model runtime acceptance is unfinished; this PR is not ready to merge.

Reuses the existing authorization, visibility and canonical transcript-writing owners instead of adding a parallel permission system. title: fix(ui): stop repeated lookups on pages with many session links

Related: #180093 (separate Gateway suspension presentation repair).

## Problem and behavior

The reviewed owner follow-up replaces one cross-map pruning call with pruning of the written map. Source-counted calls per cache write fall from two to one; unregister still prunes both. This is a readable owner-level reduction of redundant work, **not evidence that gzip improved**.

title: feat(models): customize provider names and artwork
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom model providers cannot choose a recognizable name and artwork independently of routing identity.

## User Impact

Optional `models.providers.<id>.name` and `icon` leave provider IDs, model references, credentials, routing and sessions unchanged. Omitted fields retain existing appearance. Fragment for an otherwise configured provider:

```json
{
  "name": "Workstation",
  "icon": { "source": "file", "path": "icons/workstation.png" }
}
```

Other sources: `{ "source": "url", "url": "https://example.com/icon.png" }` and `{ "source": "builtin", "name": "server" }`.

PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP inputs are limited to 2 MiB, 4096 pixels per side and 16 megapixels, then normalized to static PNGs at most 256 pixels per side. SVG is unsupported. Relative files resolve from the active config directory, with existing home expansion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Presentation is projected from current config after model visibility policy, not inserted into inference catalogs. Settings, pickers, account/model controls and usage views reuse the connection-scoped catalog and authenticated resource transport. Precedence: configured artwork/bundled icon → provider brand → effective-name initial.

The asset route reads only configuration-selected artwork, never request-supplied paths. HTTPS uses bounded SSRF-protected fetching with redirect/DNS checks. Source paths/URLs never cross the catalog wire. Current authorization, including paired-device credentials, is revalidated after loading and before delivery, including cache hits. Invalid/unavailable artwork falls back safely.

title: feat(skills): import personal skill bundles from URLs
body:
<!--
Required PR title: type: user-facing description.
Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled so maintainers can help update the branch.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Personal skill imports require manual downloads and uploads even when a skill and its companion files already have an HTTPS source.

## User Impact

Import an HTTPS `SKILL.md` or archive bundle through **Plugins → Skills → My skills → Import skill**. Recognized GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea/Forgejo folder-link shapes are normalized without a browser hostname allowlist. Companion files, nested relative paths, and binary files use the existing bundle representation. File, folder, ZIP, and ClawHub imports remain available.

Operators can permit private-network downloads with `skills.library.import.allowedOrigins`: exact HTTPS scheme/host/port entries, absent or empty by default. Grants apply to everyone already authorized to import. An explicitly approved loopback-literal origin retains the shared guard's exception; metadata/link-local destinations and unrelated private origins remain protected. This grants network access, not repository authentication: the Gateway still needs corporate DNS/VPN and TLS trust, and browser login cookies or publishing credentials are not forwarded.

Repository archives must fit the existing download/extraction limits before directory selection, so a small skill inside a large repository can fail. Use a smaller direct bundle URL and selected directory in that case. Unknown forge webpages need the explicit archive fallback; ambiguous refs can use the ref/directory overrides.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement is a source adapter into the existing guarded HTTP, safe extraction, canonical bundle, scanning, install-policy, and personal-save owners—not a separate installer. The same import RPC gains a closed URL source alternative. Remote files/archives retain truthful third-party, mutable, network source facts rather than being classified as user-authored local files. Current write authority and private-origin grants are checked across awaited work.

The GitHub-only repository importer, chooser, and superseded policy/test plumbing are retired. There is no Git clone/sparse-checkout system, browser host-list expansion, or fetched-script execution. Canonical validator regeneration causes large numbering changes, but independent normalization isolated the semantic change to the import-parameter predicate.

## Evidence

**The complete candidate authority case passed in real CI. The required stable-upgrade case is still blocked; overall CI is partial/failed—not merge-ready.**

The [exact-head run 42318674850](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42318674850) tested head `4d595fe1b42a39c095203072d3a775432ebe7260`, tree `f7f608e7747663469ee5e76ac611b100e23b908a`; expected, observed and build commits match. Sanitized artifact `13551964748` contains only `report.json`, `imported-skill.png` and `companion-detail.png`. Its ZIP SHA-256 was verified as `13cb6b7dc0a3f54923d4c920416a9aa373d9044cf855eb34414094ee86735e62`.

Actual report: `status: partial`, `authorityStatus: passed`, `upgradeStatus: failed`. All nine authority assertions passed:
- Owned HTTPS source and alternate-host reachability.
- Strict private-network default and read-only access reject before any source request.
- Browser → authenticated Gateway → HTTPS → real policy/extraction → SQLite publication, with correct personal ownership and exact nested/text/binary/executable companion bytes.
- Exact-origin and redirect boundaries issue no next request to an ungranted target.
- Real install-policy denial creates no publication.
- Live role revocation during a held redirect: one initial request, zero next requests, no publication.
- Live role revocation during held publication: committed role change causes the exact canonical post-HELLO connection retirement; settled staging/immutable artifact and library-entry counts remain unchanged. Reconnection through the same profile, requesting the original full scopes, receives a genuine correlated server rejection for a fresh import and makes zero outbound requests. A generic close is not counted as an RPC denial.
- Live origin-grant revocation: effective config version changes while the same authenticated connection stays alive; the held request cannot follow the redirect or publish. One initial request, zero next requests; `connectionStable: true`.

The independent enabled watchOS/direct-node TLS consumer also passed both tests on this head. The proof file ran both required cases: candidate authority passed; stable preparation failed. No skip or continue-on-error masks the failure.

**Remaining required proof:** latest-stable settings/skills/two-revision upgrade survival has not run. The November 7 CI attempt was blocked for exact root `openclaw@2026.11.1` under the checked-in seven-day npm cooldown. At the November 17 policy recheck, official npm `latest` was **`openclaw@2026.11.5`**, published **November 17 at 09:59:33.472 UTC**, so the required current-latest baseline is withheld until **November 24 at 09:59:33.472 UTC**. Its registry signature and SHA-512 integrity metadata were verified; no package installation or redundant CI rerun was started while that baseline remains ineligible. No age-policy exception, older-version substitution, direct-dist fallback or transitive cooldown change was applied. The same policy-respecting completion check is retained for November 24 after eligibility.

The isolated workflow uses pinned exact-head checkout, normal build, real Gateway/HTTPS/policy/SQLite owners and read-only repository permissions. No live Team policy, credentials, services or deployment changed. Both components remain required; the partial result does not turn the overall gate green. The branch also currently has conflicts with main.

The prior importer-owner and UI tests, focused type/lint/format checks and fresh independent source reviews remain supporting evidence, not substitutes for the failed real-runtime checks. The newly added diagnostic/privacy and report-completion contracts have been exercised. Scoped proof tests have their own allocation; the shared test scalar was not raised.

title: fix(ui): resolve declared favicons and remove failed icon gaps
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat links can retain an empty favicon-sized gap indefinitely. The proxy only tried `/favicon.ico`; for example, docs.openclaw.ai returns 404 there while declaring `/assets/openclaw.svg` in its page metadata.

## User Impact

- Discover declared PNG and SVG icons when the conventional favicon is unavailable.
- Remove the empty icon slot after a failed fetch, while preserving the existing reserved space during loading.
- Preserve favicon opt-in, authentication, HTTPS/SSRF protections, caching and concurrency limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing bounded link-preview metadata reader instead of adding another parser. The favicon proxy opts into SVG discovery; preview callers retain their existing raster-only behavior. Fallback requests share one five-second deadline and revalidate current request authority at the transport boundary.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the docs `/favicon.ico` 404 and confirmed the declared SVG returns 200.
- **129 targeted UI tests passed**, including actual browser decoding/layout coverage. The empty-slot regression fails on the original CSS.
- **99 Gateway icon/link-preview tests passed on the final source**, including declared PNG, declared SVG and revoked request authority. The declared-icon test fails against the original handler (404 instead of 200).

## What Problem This Solves

Single-line feedback toasts have more vertical padding than their content needs. The common “Session archived / Undo” toast is 52px tall, despite its action remaining a compact 28px control.

## User Impact

- Single-row center and anchored feedback uses 8px vertical padding instead of 12px. Archive/Undo is 44px tall; plain status feedback is 36px tall.
- Wrapped titles, actions that move onto another row, and explicit or automatically split descriptions retain 12px padding.
- Arrival notifications retain their existing roomier block proportions.
- Horizontal spacing, action targets, corners, surfaces, severity colors, shadows, positioning, stack behavior, and timers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested and design-reviewed by @vyctorbrzezowski, following the shared-toast anatomy, lanes, and copy treatment in #192013, #192014, and #192015 (and the earlier surface standardization in #189640).

The shared renderer derives actual single-row layout from its title and content—not character count or the absence of a description alone. A card-local ResizeObserver updates that presentation after width/font/text-scale changes and disconnects with the card. Measuring contents rather than the toast box avoids padding feedback and collapsed-stack height errors. No new public option or caller-by-caller compact variant.

- Regression is red on the base at the intended boundary: expected 44px, received 52px.

- Production UI builds completed as part of the real-flow browser proofs.

The exact UI controller guard, formatting, focused Oxlint, UI typecheck, and all 34 focused tests pass on the repaired source; fresh review found no actionable issues. ## What Problem This Solves

title: fix(gateway): align delegated creator proof with spawn attribution
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The delegated-creator Gateway product test still expects the selected human as the acting creator after #192037 deliberately moved `sessions_create` onto visible-spawn attribution. [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41799644616/job/126472460773) reports the exact human-versus-agent mismatch.

## User Impact

No production authorization or attribution changes. The test continues to prove that the initiating human retains creator effects, the selected noncreator is denied, and revocation prevents a held sharing write.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before, the exact persisted-actor expectation was the selected human/profile plus the causal human in `delegatedBy`. After, it requires the acting agent `{ type: "agent", id: "main" }` plus the same exact causal-human/profile/id in `delegatedBy`, matching #192037’s source and documentation.

Every creator publish/unpublish check, selected-user denial and no-effect snapshot, real sharing-admission hold, role revocation, rejected request, and final unchanged-state assertion remains intact. The production owner and tool arguments are unchanged. No timeout, skip, retry, suppression, or baseline change. title: chore(ci): diagnose disk reserve refusals in large41
body:
## Problem

[CI 41784433080 / large41](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41784433080/job/126423702015) at `bcae09093b5a06099cd3a3f0f3d5f4e4b499ad7f` failed 20 cases: 16 printed 3.3–3.4 GiB available against the unchanged 4 GiB reserve; four omitted the preparation Result. The retained logs do not identify disposable job-owned bytes. Two sibling jobs ended during runner shutdown without a bound external cause.

## Change

Add opt-in metadata on a serial, throwaway GitHub-hosted job: filesystem counters at capacity refusal and bounded footprint snapshots between child invocations and after normal disposal. Each snapshot cooperatively stops after 1 second or 250,000 entries, yields every 128 entries, and reports incomplete roots. It does not enumerate symlink targets, read contents, print paths/inode identities, or infer exclusive reflink ownership/reclaimable bytes.

Record first parent signal, native child exit tuple, and bounded error-kind/code/process-tree state while preserving cleanup, rethrow, exit and signal behavior. Expose failed preparation Results without serializing successful ownership bindings. Keep all assertions, authority/data contracts and the 4 GiB reserve.

A task-scoped workflow opened one probe on this draft branch only. It checked out original `bcae0909` and overlaid the exact diagnostic files from `60839b5c4593426ed85daf52061dd4aa5591f6d4`; the original encoded three-group large41 composition included all 63 gateway runtime/state files, startup-fixture lifetime, worktree preparation, dispatch and command/daemon groups. No shared CI driver or runner routing changed.

## Evidence

[Probe 41802517967 / job 126481483255](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41802517967/job/126481483255) is **terminal FAILURE** at diagnostic head `60839b5c4593426ed85daf52061dd4aa5591f6d4`:

- Original composition passed: three completed invocations, zero failed invocations. All 20 originally failing case names match passing cases in this log. This is a passing replay, not a proven repair.
- Focused footprint and existing lifecycle tests: 62 passed; 7.17 seconds wrapper wall time, 5.29 seconds Vitest duration. New footprint suite: two tests, 4 ms. Syntax, format and touched-script lint passed.
- Test lint failed on the new cleanup variable shadowing its `root` helper; Gateway-test lint was not reached. Follow-up `fb3d00e767ad61eadce9938f8e20dfa3f3e24d38` only renames two references. The exact failing rule was checked locally RED on the original text and GREEN on the correction with pinned oxlint; this limited check does not replace full repository lint. The failed probe is preserved, with no second reproduction or current-head CI-green claim.
- Independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2: scoped-clean on the complete diagnostic snapshot against `1ba543b6dd6ffe014139c02a4b62a7904c52a2a2`; the subsequent identifier-only lint correction is recorded above.
- Exact own test-line allocation: 83 LF, shared scalar unchanged. It covers footprint safety/budget contracts, termination metadata in existing lifecycle cases, and missing preparation detail.

The supported `ubuntu-24.04` label and four-CPU class matched, but physical conditions differed: original Intel Xeon 6975P-C versus probe AMD EPYC 7763; the probe sampled **75.635–76.612 GiB free**, far above the original shortage. The compiled-worker aggregate was 274.215 MiB and returned to an empty 4 KiB root after verified disposal. The scan completed worker/cache roots but exhausted its budget partway through dependencies; the pnpm store was unvisited, not zero-sized. The original runner's physical allocation/ownership inventory was never captured and is not recoverable from retained logs. No safe deletion target or causal leak fix is established.

Artifact [13309573121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41802517967/artifacts/13309573121) contains bounded metadata only; downloaded ZIP SHA-256 `cf3dccec5776ddf325f621910636b548face35daefaaa6483ac08f3c51903470` matches the Actions digest.

Limits: snapshots are non-atomic and cannot preempt an individual stalled syscall; different image/cache/Git-fetch state prevents byte-identical footprint claims. The probe used a stricter 60-minute outer cap versus the original whole-config policy's 120 minutes; test/hook/watchdog limits and resource ceilings stayed unchanged, and the cap was not reached.

**Diagnostic draft; no merge requested.** Stop after this one probe at the missing original ownership fact. No speculative cleanup, reserve waiver, expected-failure exception, rerun or new matrix. Original failures remain unresolved; separate beta acceptance retains its existing verdict. No BR/auth/beta/macOS owner branch, Gateway, live state, release or changelog change.

<details>
<summary>Earlier proposal and evidence, preserved with their original scope</summary>

Related: #187722

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Ready for review.** The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation on an iPhone. Returned kit v3 now verifies the Apple build, all 373 selected iOS tests, and all 21 selected shared-package tests for the repaired candidate matching `c22355b8f89a`. Actual normal-size UI screenshots and the requester’s lifecycle recording are now attached below. Remaining physical audio/lifecycle cases, large-text layout, and pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this recording. The confirmed conflict with `main` was resolved in `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`, integrating base `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. Current-head CI is green (38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures or pending checks at the November 6 check). The requester has also posted current-head targeted simulator red/green results and base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders, summarized below. Earlier Mac-kit results remain evidence for their explicitly identified candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Layout issue also observed without the mute button — November 6

**Requester comparison result:** the requester reproduced the intermittent issue with and without the mute button in **the same chats containing very long messages**, and reports **no apparent worsening with this PR**. This is the requester's comparative device observation; it was not independently executed in this session.

This supports treating the overlap as a pre-existing long-message layout problem, **not an observed mute-button regression or exacerbation**. It remains a separate investigation, not a blocker specific to this PR on the available evidence. The earlier blanket merge hold is withdrawn. No layout repair or root cause is claimed, and other review and validation requirements are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Original observation and related investigation</summary>

The supplied recording and four screenshots show lost reading position and newer user/assistant bubbles overlapping older assistant content. The overlap is visible even after the Talk card disappears. No message-role or persisted-transcript corruption has been established.

![Real iPhone screenshot: newer chat bubbles overlap an older assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b46564f-ae0c-403a-a419-ea7bc374dd7c)

This inspected crop removes model metadata and unrelated surrounding UI; originals are retained unchanged. Seven transcript layout/identity/rendering files are byte-identical to base `0499ce287bb8`. That source comparison alone did not prove baseline behavior; the requester’s subsequent device comparison is the additional evidence.

[PR #192232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192232) addresses related lazy-height instability causing blank transcripts. It remains an investigation lead, not a verified repair for this overlap. No code from it has been imported, no layout repair is claimed, and no broad device/provider test matrix is requested.

</details>

### Conflict-only integration — November 5

- Published head: `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`; verified ancestry includes main `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`.
- The sole manual conflict was the demo fixture helper extraction: main independently made the same extraction with different helper names. Kept main's names and verified the complete fixture file matches that main revision byte-for-byte. The fixture and shared initializer build repairs are now already upstream, reducing the PR-relative diff to 13 files.
- Native mute manager/regressions, WebRTC mute, relay mute, and Talk-strip UI are byte-identical to the earlier Apple-tested candidate. All 13 PR-relative files plus the two upstream build-repair files were verified against the published head.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,637 entries, no drift); base-relative staged whitespace check passed. Fresh full-candidate Auto Review against the integrated base: P0-only, scoped-clean, no findings. No Apple code was executed in this Linux session; these checks do not replace current-head Apple integration validation.
- [Latest completed ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6626345064) covers current head `417349df1cf4`: overall Gold, patch quality Diamond, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review, and no before-merge items listed. It notes remaining declared device-proof gaps separately; this rating is advisory. The targeted source-hunk red/green report and requester device evidence are retained below.
- Current-head CI is green as observed November 6: 38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures/pending checks. This includes iOS screenshot/evidence and Periphery build jobs; the dedicated iOS build matrix is skipped, so this is not a claim that every Apple test suite ran in CI. No merge has been submitted.

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch. Kit v2 subsequently exposed build blockers; kit v3 confirms the build repairs and automated regressions pass, as detailed below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.

- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Passed on the requester's Mac in kit v3:** all seven regression definitions, including their parameterized cases. Actual current UI screenshots from the requester's recording are now attached below. ### Additional requester evidence on integrated head — November 5–6

All reports below name head `417349df1cf4` and base `0499ce287bb8`.

- [Simulator red/green report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6667982238): on Xcode 27.2, the requester reports **red** after reverting only finalization, muted-recognition, and relay-silence source hunks while retaining the tests: 7 mute tests with 21 issues, and 10 relay tests with 3 issues. **Green** on unchanged PR head: 18 tests across `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests` and `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, plus 10 shared relay tests, all passing. Reported mute-suite time: 721 seconds. This is targeted regression sensitivity, **not a literal plain-base test run**. These are attributed results from the comment; raw xcresult/log bundles for this new run were not supplied to this session.
- [Base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669395455): publicly accessible immutable images were downloaded; normal and large-text active/muted examples and large-text connecting were inspected. They show real SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` output from a fixed 393-point test fixture at 3x, not full-app screenshots. Head adds the expected gray/orange crossed microphone and muted wording. At accessibility3 the muted text wraps mid-word (`Micropho / ne muted`); status/transcript text is also constrained. Treat the real chat's large-text layout as unverified, not accepted based on this fixture.
- [Requester's evidence mapping and remaining device checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669410988): simulator assertions cover finalization, fallback, exactly-once submission, Talk-session restart, quick toggles, and teardown. Audible playback and physical-device lifecycle/large-text verification are still pending. The earlier successful native trailing-word device report remains valid and should not be discarded.

**Restart contract clarification:** mute is retained across Talk stop/start and reconnect within the same app run. It is intentionally not persisted across quitting and relaunching the app. A full-app relaunch retaining mute is therefore **not** an acceptance requirement for this PR; the relevant retention check is restarting Talk without terminating the app.

### Requester real-device lifecycle recording — November 5

The requester supplied a 36-second iPhone recording and explicitly authorized use of the test-chat screen. These are **actual device screenshots, not mockups**. The recording does not display a build commit, so this is requester-supplied visual evidence, separate from the hash-verified kit v3 test run.

title: fix(zalouser): deliver received attachments as readable media
body:
Supersedes #159253, thanks @ceo633.
Closes #159249.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: files, photos, and videos received through Zalo Personal reach the agent as filenames and CDN links without readable attachments.

## User Impact

Authorized attachments reach the agent as stored media with their original document filenames. Failed downloads leave an attachment-unavailable notice alongside the message. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry recognized received attachments through Zalouser's existing normalizer and monitor into the shared media store and inbound context. Downloads run after sender and mention checks, enforce HTTPS and Zalo CDN hosts across redirects, retain private-network/MIME/size protections and deadlines, and honor monitor and ingress cancellation. Recheck sender and command access before downloading and before dispatch; retire newly staged files if access or cancellation rejects the turn.

Production grows by 105 lines because the handoff was missing. There is no dead or duplicate media path in this owner to remove without unrelated changes. The repair adds no transport abstraction, SDK capability, dependency, or configuration option. A separate 219-line regression allocation covers the new durable-ingress suite; the shared test budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Synthetic Testbox proof on base `9e59d23aff4d553dd264133d5efeffd10e359a40`: all five initial cases failed because no readable media was materialized; the same cases passed with the repair.
- The final inbound-media suite passes all 16 cases: document/photo/video bytes and MIME at agent input; filename preservation; access, mention, and ordinary-link exclusions; HTTPS, CDN host, private address, redirect, downgrade, and size rejection; revoked/cancelled staging cleanup while preserving a neighboring file. Test bodies take about 7 seconds; the final named-file run took 42.66 seconds including import/worker preparation.
- The existing group-gating, account-scope, and quote/normalization suites pass (36 cases). Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof.
- Touched-file formatting, syntax lint, and whitespace checks pass. Targeted typed lint reports zero warnings/errors and the Zalouser package typecheck passes on [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41785326306).
- Independent autoreview completed P0–P2 with no actionable findings against the complete local candidate and media/ingress owner contracts. Subsequent test-only corrections use the context builder's canonical empty media array and a void-returning setup hook.
- Follow-up CI repair replaces the inline attachment-record assertion with the existing SDK record parser, removing assertion-safety growth; an independent P0–P2 correction review is also scoped-clean.
- No contributor checkout or execution; no real Zalo credentials, messages, CDN requests, browser, or container proof. The listener and HTTP transport are synthetic; durable ingress, normalization, guarded downloading, media storage, and context building use production paths. Live-account interoperability is outside this proof.

Final head `09d73ac2bbba30845f04ea9731b8ffea8e5f87ca`: 48 checks pass, 58 are skipped, and none are pending or failed. [Linux CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41788003660) and [macOS CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41788003549) are green.

Related: #192442 (partial Browser repair; keep the issue open)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud-worker Browser construction failing with `Runtime config is not prepared` when the worker has no Gateway runtime config.

## User Impact

An admitted worker Browser can construct and use its attached bridge without borrowing host configuration. The separate capability-preparation, fallback transcript-base and reclaim reports remain unverified by this repair; this does not establish a release-wide cure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attached runtime already owns a restricted attach-only worker profile. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: worker GitHub access can lose the operator authority from its admitted run when later grant preparation no longer has the original caller context.

## User Impact

Admitted worker runs retain their original operator authority for GitHub access. Revocation still stops launch or refresh, and existing cleanup releases the retained authority. Missing authority is not promoted to synthetic authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass original admitted authority into the existing GitHub grant owner, which retains and revalidates it and composes its abort signal with the current turn. Keep grant lifecycle and cleanup with that owner.

## Evidence

### Retained authority and refresh
- Existing committed `worker-github-binding.authority-wire.test.ts` covers real admitted-request capture/release/retention, SQLite exact-turn binding, worker credential installation, production refresh dispatch and WorkerConnection delivery.
- Removing retention produces **2/2 failures after request completion**; the repaired combined suite passes **34/34**, with **2/2** passing through the registered runner. Real operator-role revocation and turn reassignment suppress subsequent credential delivery.
- The canonical test-inventory ordering is repaired; its affected selection suite passed **10/10**.

### Actual initial launch after public request completion
New committed [runtime test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a46198f6a0b32b19e18b78945b6a43ca62d9a7b4/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/worker-github-initial-launch.e2e.test.ts) passes **3/3** against a real built Gateway, public authenticated admission, production node invoke/workspace/bundle/supervisor owners, real WorkerConnection, and a real worker child:

1. **Allowed:** public `chat.send` ACK completes before the held noncredential preparation request resumes. `executeWorkerTurn` and the production launch deliver the initial credential; the worker creates its real `hosts.yml` profile and reaches the provider. The profile disappears after settlement.
2. **Original operator revoked:** a separate administrator uses public `users.setRole` while preparation is held. No credential-bearing launch, worker credential profile or provider request occurs for the original turn.
3. **Cancelled predecessor / legitimate successor:** public `chat.abort` settles the old turn without credential delivery; a legitimate successor receives its own binding, runs and cleans up.

There are no manufactured grants, admission mocks, manual token-frame sends, direct credential-installer calls or direct pairing-store writes. QA password plumbing uses the existing GatewayClient password contract, allowing documented trusted-proxy admission plus authenticated local administration without changing core auth or disabling guards.

### Source qualification and local gates

Their helper incorrectly drained the inherited Gateway lifeline even though the tests require natural exit before listening. The earlier one-line deficit on the proof checkout's older baseline does not persist against this PR's actual publication base.
- Fresh independent installed P0–P2 review is **scoped-clean** for the eight-file proof change with all 33 coupled source modules supplied. The later capture-helper correction has its own fresh **scoped-clean** review with complete fixture/caller/command/lifecycle context.
- The earlier CI native-PID observation defect was repaired and qualified in merged [#192539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192539). Current-head CI remains the separate broad landing gate.

### Limits
External GitHub HTTPS and model/provider responses are synthetic. The node test host executes production owners but is not a separately launched node CLI. This does not claim live GitHub, external model, cloud-worker or publication qualification. The preparation hold is before grant construction, not a prepared-retained-grant pre-send race; the existing retention/heartbeat tests provide that complementary authority-lifetime coverage.
