title: fix(codex): preserve worker-owned native authentication
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker-hosted Codex authentication being handed back to Gateway auth, and ensures current model authority is retained before worker initialization can execute a native auth command.

## User Impact

Workers keep their own native credentials. Normal Gateway model-availability resolution does not replace worker identity or block an otherwise valid worker turn. Explicit/forwarded Gateway profile choices and native supervision remain rejected. Model or placement revocation prevents the corresponding native effects. No configuration or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing worker-owned handoff for native-command runs, and retain model execution through the existing authority owner before initialization for every worker auth route. A resolved Gateway key can be availability data, not a request to use that account on the worker; the worker handoff never forwards that key.

A full shipped-runtime replay caught the earlier revision incorrectly rejecting that normal availability key. This revision repairs that integration failure rather than changing the fixture to hide it. The Linux composition observer also now reads children across all node tasks, preserving its native-process filter and cleanup assertions; reading only the main task missed subprocesses created by runtime worker threads.

## Evidence

### Actual built Gateway + paired node + native Codex

The repository's supported network-none runner built `qaRuntime` from the candidate and ran the existing full composition through real Gateway processes and authenticated node WebSockets:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  --isolated-image sha256:847f71bbb3f17fc1032d50d75bf6fb3fdcf188b16dff81f24667fe9ae9409e01 \
  --isolated-runtime=bun run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-node-app-server.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **Red:** the previous published implementation, with only the process-observer correction, built and reached actual `sessions.dispatch`, then rejected the normal availability key before worker auth. This was an execution failure, not setup failure. Source snapshot: `d68636b2dd9d070df0da735547f869ee904a59b89d5298b0d908c813f93e93b5`.
- **Green:** the corrected candidate passed **1/1 full composition test** (47.60 seconds test execution; 95.46 seconds Vitest run after the successful build). Source snapshot: `4291c8ce573583596adc030dd681bfda20995908ea056d26bd59e902ab84c034`.
- The test performs real worktree creation and worker dispatch, holds the actual native auth helper, observes worker-authenticated provider requests, starts and resumes the same native thread, reads the worker-owned thread store, and verifies persisted Gateway history and filesystem results.
- It aborts a real held command and joins process cleanup. While auth is pending, ordinary reassignment remains refused because workspace results are pending; changing the actual session permission from Full to Workspace stops the captured run, helper and native children before their auth timeout. Late release and a subsequent forbidden attempt produce no provider requests or filesystem result.
- Worker observations assert absence of Gateway/provider/forge credentials and runtime injection. The original assertions are retained; native children must stop before node shutdown.
- The selected pinned Bun executable was verified by the runner. Preflight used Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0 and matching Chromium revision 1248. Both runs reported container absence after completion; no live Gateway was changed.

The provider is deterministic loopback HTTP, not an external inference service. This proves the actual shipped Gateway/node/native-client composition, not cloud provisioning, live-provider behavior, or an upgrade.

### Focused regression and review

- Original native-command handoff failure reproduced against the repository baseline.
- Connection and environment siblings: **57/57 passed**. The worker matrix includes resolved Gateway availability keys and verifies no host login/handoff; explicit profile/supervision conflicts still reject.
- Actual native process/provider authority cases: **5/5 passed** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest.codex-worker-authority.config.ts --maxWorkers=1`. An availability key still results in only the synthetic worker bearer reaching the provider. Model-policy and placement revocation prevent auth/provider effects; an explicit Gateway profile opens no worker duplex.
- Selected-leaf types (`test/tsconfig.codex-worker-authority.json`), typed lint, formatting, diff and full-PR test-line gates passed. The shared baseline is unchanged.
- Fresh independent installed autoreview **P0–P2: scoped-clean**, covering the final delta with complete core auth producer, harness, transport and test context. Earlier reviews remain retained; the full runtime replay is additional executed evidence.
- The native binary used in the focused proof is Codex CLI 0.164.0, SHA-256 `b93f6811d3f653f0fb83be4050d857fb9abbb111dfa2ce160563327daff7f306`. Its inspected sibling auth-command source was pinned separately at `8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4`; no source-to-binary provenance equivalence is asserted.

title: fix(workers): honor profile setup-script opt-out
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a worker can run a setup script even though its selected profile disables setup scripts.

## User Impact

A profile's explicit setup-script opt-out applies during preparation and prepared-image startup, including repository checkout setup. Existing recipe-secret validation is unchanged. No migration or new setting is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the native profile policy take precedence over per-request setup authorization at both existing execution paths. Keep preparation and startup on the same policy.

## Evidence

- Fixed the hosted-review repository-checkout bypass: profile suppression is passed independently of caller setup permission. Profile false skips setup while allowing checkout; requested setup without current admin authority still rejects. Prepared startup applies the same policy.
- Documented the existing `settings.runSetupScript` behavior, including omitted/true semantics and its distinction from `settings.setup`. Removed the invalid undefined JSON-setting fixture.
- Production placement/startup and node workspace owners execute real Git subprocesses, HTTP checkpoint transfer and a setup script. The allowed case writes its result file; profile-disabled, non-admin and authority-revoked-before-command cases do not. Removing only the checkout repair makes the disabled case write that file: **1 failed / 32 passed**.
- Final owner/consumer suite: **50/50 passed**. Final isolated setup cases: **4/4 passed** after eliminating inherited fixture setup. Prepared lifecycle cases use actual subprocess/filesystem effects, including failure before activation.
- Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-intent.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-prepared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Direct changed-test-leaf compiler, typed lint/format/diff checks passed. Fresh installed autoreview P0–P2 and supplemental fixture-isolation review: **scoped-clean**. Separate allocation: 196 lines; shared baseline unchanged.
- The earlier owner-level proof used an explicit live authorization callback. The additional native proof below now covers public authenticated dispatch and actual managed Node CLI enrollment; it does not claim live-model completion.


## Native Runtime Proof

The committed `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/worker-setup-policy.e2e.test.ts` exercises a built Gateway, authenticated operator RPCs, actual managed Node CLI enrollment, native Git checkout, worker command execution, and real Podman filesystem/checkpoint effects. No production auth hooks or fabricated grants are used.

| Repository preparation | `prepare` effect, checkout succeeds | Checkout without setup | Checkout without setup | No setup; operation settles |

title: fix(worktrees): reserve capacity on PostgreSQL
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL-backed worktree creation fails when reserving capacity because its upsert references an ambiguous `owner` column.

## User Impact

Managed Git worktrees can be created and registered on PostgreSQL. Reservation renewal still requires the same owner; a replacement owner remains protected. SQLite behavior and persisted schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the target table's existing owner predicate. Allocation, leases, worker dispatch, and error propagation remain with their native owners. The new PostgreSQL suite is now included in the existing conformance runner's default targets and CI shards.

## Executed behavior evidence

The committed `capacity.postgres.test.ts` now calls **`ManagedWorktreeService.create`**, creates a real local Git repository, uses the real allocation/lease/capacity worker transport against **PostgreSQL 17.11**, reads the created checkout's `README.md`, and checks the persisted worktree registry. This case does not mock dispatch, database admission, SQL, Git, or filesystem effects. The suite owns teardown of its isolated database schemas, workers, state, and checkout.

The same final suite was executed twice, changing only the production conflict predicate for the negative control:

```text
Original predicate: .where("owner", "=", key)
FAIL creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)
FAIL admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)

Fixed predicate: .where("state_leases.owner", "=", key)
PASS creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation — 1195 ms
PASS admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation — 42 ms
Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
```

The second case separately proves renewal and refusal after reservation-owner replacement with real PostgreSQL; only that case substitutes the transport grant callback. Both cases failed for the intended SQL error on the control. Fixed source bytes were restored and verified afterward.

Reproduce with a disposable PostgreSQL database:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --list
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -- src/agents/worktrees/capacity.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Validation and limits

- Default conformance selection now includes this file. Existing target-inventory, disjoint-shard, listing, and argument-validation tests: **8 passed**. Their temporary fixture now declares its actual ESM package type instead of triggering an unexpected Node warning.
- Real PostgreSQL green run: **37.08 seconds wall**, including **29.7 seconds** of compiled-worker preparation; test bodies total about **1.24 seconds**. Negative control: **141.45 seconds wall**, including cold worker preparation. CI duration remains available on the current head's checks.
- Existing PostgreSQL/SQLite capacity sibling proof: **21 passed** on the original production fix; the production predicate is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Targeted agents-other and tooling test-type checks, typed lint (3 files), formatting, diff checks and staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh installed independent P0–P2 autoreview of this complete candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings.
- Full runtime/plugin/declaration build already passed with the original seven independent production fixes composed; this correction changes only regression selection, tests and allocation metadata. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.
- The **+85 test-line allocation** covers the two distinct PostgreSQL contracts and the one-line ESM fixture setup. The shared baseline is unchanged. No production API, schema, cache, or test-only seam is added.
- This is real production-owner/database/Git evidence, not a live cloud/model run. It makes no claim about worktree retirement: an exploratory `service.remove` call outside the CLI one-shot scope exposed a separate main-thread PostgreSQL admission refusal and was not included in the allocation claim.

## Public CLI → Gateway → PostgreSQL proof

Executed on 2026-11-04 against PR head 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, not just ManagedWorktreeService integration. The normal pnpm openclaw launcher built and ran the production CLI and two disposable, authenticated loopback Gateways. Both installations used fresh owned HOME/config/state directories and separate databases on PostgreSQL 17.11, with database.engine=postgres and the documented OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN env SecretRef. No production dispatch, Git, lease, capacity, or worker transport was mocked. No test admission override was installed.

The project fixture was a clean checkout of the existing PR commit; no fixture source commit was needed. Default worktree acceleration was left enabled, including its normal internal template cache.

### Exact public entrypoint

With the respective isolated config/state/DSN and loopback port selected, the commands were as below. Each gateway run stayed in its own supervised foreground process; health and creation were separate CLI invocations.

```bash
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-red   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json

pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-green   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json
```

**Red:** the same head with only the capacity predicate reverted from state_leases.owner to the original owner reference. Health passed; public creation exited1. The running Gateway recorded the worktrees.create RPC failing with:

```text
column reference "owner" is ambiguous: code=42702
```

The public list was empty, PostgreSQL contained zero worktree records, the requested checkout was absent, and no worktree leases remained. The uncertain-error receipt was reconciled before proceeding; no blind retry or offline fallback was used for creation.

**Green:** pristine 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, rebuilt by the normal launcher. Health and public creation both exited0. The returned id f1067054-e076-463f-be04-4a0911776531 appeared in the public list and the real PostgreSQL worktrees row, with matching path, branch and base ref. The physical checkout had HEAD 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, clean Git status, and README bytes matching the source (SHA256 368166ce96af9cf49729ef813f1ed5e93b04d26f7b3598c9c8721779d534cbda). No worktree leases remained after creation.

### Executing build binding

- Green native build: 2026.10.10-14674c64679e-2026-11-04T06-41-50.645Z; inputsClean=true.
- Green input signature: 59f1de5bc1851905aae4bc1c230680904ddafbd5b9e7ed817332e48e47b51046.
- Red input signature: 6cfe3aa07ce5ca33b9c4073e4212f410f7bfb57879120dfe04e58a5d1d959527; inputsClean=false solely for the one-line inverse patch.
- Both actual Gateway processes used the same pinned OpenClaw Bun binary, SHA256 0cef667e2f3fd465b6429904ed074381a679be379ec44fa42b5f460ed118b2b8. Serving process cwd, executable, build stamps and artifact hashes were captured.

### Cleanup and scope

Lossless cleanup correctly retained the unpushed synthetic branch. A separate online worktrees.remove --force RPC hit the PostgreSQL main-thread admission restriction; that issue was recorded, not hidden or patched into this change. After stopping the owned Gateway, the same public CLI in supported offline one-shot mode removed the checkout and retained its native safety snapshot/removal receipt. Verification found zero active PostgreSQL worktrees, no worktree leases, and the requested path absent. Both Gateways stopped cleanly; the PostgreSQL container and its anonymous volume were removed and all selected ports closed.

This is shipped CLI/Gateway entrypoint evidence for PostgreSQL worktree creation. It is not a live-model, cloud-provider, stress, or whole-lifecycle correctness claim. No PR/source code changes or extra test-policy changes were required for this proof.

title: fix(sessions): allow creation with invocation-time authority
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Keeps a prepared session-creation tool from freezing an early absence of authority into a permanent execution denial. The committed owner-level regression exercises construction before caller admission.

## User Impact

Authorized callers can create sessions after admission; revoked, changed, or absent authority still prevents creation. Tool definitions remain stable across turns. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Evaluate write authority at execution through the existing execution gate, then keep the existing live source/creator checks. This builds on the native session-creation owner and the repository-child inheritance already landed in #190843.

## Evidence

- Committed regression: `src/gateway/server.sessions-create-authority.product.test.ts`. It starts the production Gateway on isolated loopback state, builds the tool before caller admission, invokes through the production in-process dispatcher, then reads the created SQLite session row through the production accessor.
- The allowed idle session is persisted. Absent/read-only callers add no row. Revoking the original source or replacing its stored role while actual cwd resolution is awaited prevents creation and preserves the existing row.
- Exact baseline owner: the same regression fails because the allowed invocation returns `{ gated: true }`. Final candidate: **1/1 product test passes**, **12/12 consumer tests pass**. Prefix-stability proof on unchanged production source remains valid.
- Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions-create-authority.product.test.ts` and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-create-tool.test.ts`.
- Direct changed-leaf TypeScript, scoped lint/format/diff checks passed. Fresh full-slice installed autoreview **P0–P2: scoped-clean**. The dedicated test-line allocation is 233 lines; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- The authenticated-client fixture is synthetic. Authority capture, current-role checks, admission, dispatcher, creation and persistence are production owners. This tests idle creation, which needs no model call; it does not qualify WebSocket login or non-idle kickoff.

## Shipped-entry-point compatibility and authorization proof

The exact published source `4ffca1552e5ae42d0728a83b88f4a1284675860a` was built by the normal `pnpm openclaw --profile session-authority-green gateway run` owner into a disposable Gateway with its own state/config/home/workspace and loopback port. The source remained clean before and after execution. The external Responses fixture emitted only model protocol/tool-call packets; it did not construct tools, inject caller identity, grant authority, call a dispatcher, or write application state.

1. The normal authenticated public CLI created a non-main parent session, then ran `agent --agent main --session-id <parent> --message <explicit independent-session request> --json`. The model used the offered `tool_search` → `tool_describe` → `dispatch_action` interface to invoke `sessions_create`. The completed agent receipt reported four tool calls (including the nested `sessions_create`) and zero failures. A separate public `sessions.list` read returned exactly one target row labeled `session-authority-green-created`, with an operator-created session identity.
2. A separately authenticated documented `/hooks/agent` request asked for another independent session without an admitted operator. The same real model/tool-discovery path reached `sessions_create`; the tool reported an authority denial and no creation receipt. The subsequent public session list contained zero rows with the forbidden label, while retaining the allowed session.
3. Both task-owned services were terminated through their process owners; terminal results confirmed SIGTERM settlement, exact profile/model processes were absent, and both selected loopback ports were closed.

**Scope of the result:** this is actual CLI/Gateway/model-tool transport and persisted-session compatibility with a deterministic loopback model, not live external inference. The ordinary local-agent run also passed on the original constructor-time implementation; it is not a red reproduction of the late-admission defect. Source tracing confirms that ordinary path installs caller authority before catalog construction. The late-admission red/green evidence remains the committed production-owner regression described above. Non-idle kickoff and an externally reproduced late-caller worker flow are not claimed.

title: feat(beam): preserve live logical conversation handoff
body:
An authorized Beam publisher could open the Team link but could not compose, and repeated adoption created independent transcript copies. Beam now transfers ownership explicitly and retains one live logical conversation for Team and the source client.

Fixes #192520. Receiver merged as `7552558bfb389d57c760cc37a641bbed7a250175` from head `81953d01bb3c95706940a20b9e53e1b7882aa9fc` (tree `cea3dcd0491cf6b6d1d812a6c9d804c001329116`). The companion https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/356 subsequently merged as `4de04c55d02f57caea32176005c6a6c9517200da` from pinned head `b637385f21ab78ada03d87bba25e16aa9f192404`.

- Ordinary publication is a read-only snapshot. Only the authenticated original publisher can release its exact receiver generation with `beam handoff`. Release freezes source history and permanently retires source writes; archive or snapshot expiry cannot restore source ownership. Lost acknowledgments cannot recreate an expired publication.
- First continuation imports bounded untrusted history once. Durable plugin SQLite metadata retains the destination across concurrent requests, retry, restart, deletion and reopen. Exact creation tokens fence rollback/finalization; stale cleanup cannot clear a newer attempt. Reconciliation requires core-verified destination provenance. No schema or protocol version bump.
- Gateway owners authorize source access, destination creation/history and model selection. Destination aliases and provider-owned equivalent versions normalize against available models. An unavailable preference leaves the override unset for ordinary configured-default resolution. Available forbidden models remain forbidden. No credential, account selection or provider runtime session ID transfer.
- The companion uses its existing authenticated Gateway profile/device identity for read/follow-up. Query links resolve through a read-only owner; prefix links retain ambiguity discovery. UI continuation captures draft, attachments and ownership synchronously, fences deferred work and RPC results, and releases only its own unscoped sending state. Optional continuation work stays outside common chat boot preloads.

### Validation

[Final exact-head CI41793020965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793020965) succeeds, including all selected unit/browser/native, packaging, type/lint, prompt snapshot, Android and three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. Required `openclaw/ci-gate` passes. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192513#issuecomment-6622149780) has no findings or before-merge items.

- [Hosted bundle qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793020965/job/126451446846): chat1282633→1282788B (+155B within unchanged192B variance), requests20→20; startup90691B under90815B and new797172B under797395B. All22 locale payload pairs pass, largest ru143.1KiB under300KiB. No budget/preload/variance relaxation. Before publication, pinned-toolchain native archive builds measured153B saved; canonical precompression/comparison checks and34 focused tests passed (24 UI ownership,10 native SQLite store).
- [Joined pinned-client/Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793020965/job/126451448073) passes the complete scenario in33.858s: normal profile/device authentication, real HTTP publication, dropped release acknowledgment, destination first turn/default selection, client read/follow-up/idempotency, Gateway restart preserving session identity, late-source rejection and ordinary revocation with no additional inference. The shard exits0 after verified process cleanup. The provider is synthetic.
- Native persistence covers release generation, exact rollback/finalization after snapshot removal, archive-retained destination and source retirement. The new SQLite upgrade case seeds a pre-handoff owned row without generation/binding fields, proves list/read and nonmutating premature refusal, preserves owner/createdAt during original-publisher refresh, then releases and reopens one destination. Existing ownerless restrictions remain covered. [Reusable real-Gateway authority proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41782349000/job/126417014227) covers foreign publishers, forbidden models, actual post-import revocation, row/transcript rollback and authorized retry; those owners are unchanged.
- Three prompt JSON drifts were reproduced on exact base062d5d85481fca84c57014e7c3a128fc4386ea79 and [independent same-base CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41787264286/job/126433234494). title: fix(anthropic): Windows Claude turns fail with large tool allowlists
body:
Supersedes #156057, thanks @blazingphoenix7.
Related: #144792

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bundled Claude CLI turns on Windows fail to start when the admitted MCP tool list exceeds the Windows command-line limit.

## User Impact

Windows agents using OpenClaw-generated settings can retry startup with the same exact admitted tools, denials, permission mode, and restrictions. Commands that already fit retain their invocation without acquiring a temporary-file dependency. **Merge is blocked on native Claude validation described below.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Try the original invocation first. Only after Windows reports `ENAMETOOLONG`, place the admitted tool names and OpenClaw's path-independent restrictions in a private settings file owned by that child. The existing process owner rechecks live authority after the write; cleanup covers startup failures and child exit, including warm turns.

Only empty settings or the exact OpenClaw-generated restricted projection can relocate. Custom inline settings and settings paths keep their original error, because [moving caller-owned permission or sandbox paths can change their anchors](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#where-a-pattern-anchors). Tool, permission, sandbox, and execution boundaries are preserved.

## Evidence

- **Exact regression red on main:** [native Windows baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767148011), test-only commit `29fb561553c889b90e775667a4d91090f53bd9e2` on main `fa997337ede78046bc0e3e790ba452d06e34627b`. Both oversized settings forms fail in the real launcher with `ENAMETOOLONG` (`-4064`).
- **Replacement and siblings green:** [native Windows replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41766984009) of exact head `270d1143697a4f6b1853899299821167924b1148`: four named files, 53 passed, 11 skipped, 115.79 s wall. The eight regression cases total 961 ms and cover exact grants/denials, fitting commands, unsafe custom settings refusal, writes, retirement, retry failure, and child-owned cleanup. Windows exercises the real OS limit; Linux injects only that initial OS error before a real subprocess.
- **Real host-authority boundary:** [Windows authority probe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41774781014), [proof source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8da7e91a7b5cfd6a7e3bc272c52ff0f5500126b9/extensions/anthropic/cli-allowlist.authority-proof.test.ts). Production files are identical to the replacement head. The admitted-run owner permits Read and reads a synthetic file; undeclared Write is denied and creates no file. Closing real admission during the settings write prevents the retry child and removes the settings workspace. These two cases pass; the file as a whole is **not green**.
- **Remaining blocker:** in that same run, installed native Claude Code 2.1.280 reports its version, but the offline configuration probe times out before its loaded grant rules can be observed. Cleanup also reports `EPERM` on the isolated executable. The probe uses an explicitly synthetic startup token and a rejecting loopback endpoint, sends no model prompt, and uses no real model credentials. This failed setup does not establish a product defect or prove native permission enforcement. Native grant loading and cleanup remain unverified; merge and original-PR closure remain blocked on this validation gap.
- **Broad CI retains inherited failures:** [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767665905), attempt 2: 133 success, 24 skipped, four failed root jobs plus the downstream gate. `security-fast` succeeds. All three failing test files were replayed on clean main `919b0567dd1b5361e5c7f7e0b2c9f6ea6fe7b8bb` with the checksum-pinned Bun fork in [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41770371008): four failed, 32 passed, with identical signatures. Browser relay profile port/name drift resolves `false` instead of rejecting; QA kill/restart receives two records instead of an empty array; hooks CLI blank-parent-agent output returns the specific error instead of the expected generic prefix. These files and direct subjects are unchanged in the tested PR merge.
- **Existing test-line deficit:** CI reports a 20-line overage. The same checker fails on main `fa997337...` against its parent with that same 20-line deficit and +27 main test lines. The replacement adds exactly 180 test lines and exactly 180 allocation credit; it preserves the existing deficit. A default non-growing main check can pass while over budget, and is not claimed as failure proof. No baseline or excess allocation was added.
- Final local autoreview of the complete candidate is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Its earlier settings-anchor finding was fixed through exact canonical recognition. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Necessary production growth is 83 lines for serialization, the guarded retry, and cleanup; no equivalent dead code exists in this owner. The separate allocation records the 180 focused regression lines.
- Contributor source was read through GitHub view/diff only and was never checked out or executed. Heavy compilation and tests ran only in CI/Testbox. No CHANGELOG changes.

title: fix: show Gateway names for linked Slack mentions in Control UI

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI message bodies can show raw Slack mention IDs even after the referenced person has a verified Gateway profile link. Correct sender labels do not resolve inline references, and bot mentions must not be mistaken for the sender.

## User Impact

- Linked human references show the current Gateway display name using the existing viewer/session visibility policy.
- Unlinked people and bots use the Slack name already recorded in the message; unknown IDs, code, and messages without original account scope remain literal.
- Stored/model text, provider IDs, routing, authorization, and mention notifications are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native syntax and ID normalization in Slack’s pure mention adapter. The Gateway resolves the canonical channel/account/sender tuple and enriches only the admitted display copy. Native pages are enriched before final byte budgeting/encoding, preserving pagination and the webchat fast path. Live fanout asks each reader to reload its canonical view rather than broadcasting a shared person-name projection.

The existing Slack stripping behavior is moved unchanged into the same sibling adapter to satisfy the channel module’s line-cap ratchet. No new persistence, configuration option, or permission is introduced.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen; human co-author credit is retained in the commit. **Patrick requested landing this PR on 2026-11-04. Landing remains subject to the applicable review/proof gates and supported inherited-CI policy. No deployment is requested.**

**Red:** On baseline `57405d6f170a905c1056ae755ec20e259f893abf`, the linked-state RPC and real Gateway/Control UI browser regressions fail on the expected Gateway-name assertion. The serialized-page contract also fails because the original encoder discards the object graph before display enrichment. Setup failures were not counted as regression proof.

Focused Gateway suites passed 155 tests; live-publication/availability/guest suites passed 54. The full touched history/serialization pair was rerun after isolating its adapter fixture from extension runtime graphs. Slack channel and agent-tool prefix-stability suites pass. Core/extension/changed-test type checks, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet pass.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/slack-inline-identity.e2e.test.ts
```

Deterministic linked-state regression:

```sh

```

### Browser proof

The sender fixture is Patrick; the separate human target is `Gateway Alice`, the bot fallback is `Roboclaw`, and unknown/code IDs remain visible. title: fix(gateway): check Incognito chat leaves against the in-process transcript
body:
## Problem

Every Incognito chat send after the first one failed with `Error: Chat admission omitted its worker-prepared active path` and showed as **Not sent**. Stop failed the same way.

Incognito transcripts live in the Gateway's process-local session actor, which the database read workers cannot open. Admission and Stop compare the browser's `expectedLeafEntryId` against the chat's active path, and for Incognito chats nothing supplied that fact anymore. #174610 removed the in-process Incognito active-path read as "unreachable", but the Incognito admission branch still depended on it. The first message of a new Incognito chat still worked because it has no prior leaf.

## Fix

- `chat-send-session.ts` / `chat-send-active-leaf.ts`: for Incognito sends and Stop, read the active-path relation from the memory session actor (`readSessionTranscriptAnchorsAsync`), then run the existing `assertExpectedLeafActive` check. Durable sessions are unchanged.
- `session-actor-memory-history-anchors.ts`: memory anchor reads now report `activePathRelation` (exact / ancestor / off-path), matching the SQLite projection.
- `session-transcript-anchor-read.ts`: a missing memory transcript reports the empty-root relation, like the SQLite reader.

Accepted edge case (documented in code): the Incognito path read happens just before the entry snapshot. A reset is still rejected by the session-id fence. An append that lands between the two reads is a rare race that the user can retry.

## Evidence

- `chat-send-active-leaf.incognito.test.ts` (real `chat.send` handler, real memory storage): stale and earlier leaves are rejected with `active-leaf-changed` for sends and Stop, the exact leaf is accepted for Stop, and a session-fenced ancestor is admitted and dispatched. Red on base (generic error instead of `active-leaf-changed`), green with the fix.
- New `chat-incognito-send.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: a real built Gateway and Chromium. The test turns on Incognito, starts a session and sends two follow-ups, and every reply appears with no **Not sent**. On a base build it fails at the second reply; with the fix it passes.
- Related suites pass: projection rebuild, stop cascade, both transcript-anchor suites, `session-control.incognito`, `vitest-ui-e2e-config`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, run with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` because the full dead-export scan fails on `ui/.../systems-sidebar.tsx: systemKind`, which this PR doesn't touch. `tsgo:core` is clean.
- Local autoreview (P2): no findings.

## Not covered

A live run against real OpenAI showed that Incognito chats fail at the **model run** with `This account action requires a current authorized connection`. The failure is identical on base `main` without this change, and the same flow succeeds for a durable chat. It is a separate existing model-account authority issue and is not addressed here.

## Test cost

The dedicated 193-line allocation preserves the admission/Stop fence regressions and the real-Gateway Incognito follow-up flow. The shared baseline, production code, and existing assertions are unchanged. The staged test-line ratchet passes; the existing functional and CI evidence above is reused.

title: fix(ui): explain missing operator scopes in access errors
body:
## Summary

F3: preserve the Gateway’s existing missing-scope reason in Control UI permission copy, with plain-language next steps rather than raw scope identifiers.

- Read `MISSING_SCOPE` / `missingScope` through the existing Gateway client parser. Authorization, required scopes, grants, retry behavior, and technical error details are unchanged.
- One UI copy formatter covers generic missing-scope failures and existing feature-specific read-access messages (logs, usage, agents, model providers, scheduled tasks, context breakdown, and session history).
- Following Vyctor’s approved wording, display `operator.read` as “read access.” After inspecting `src/gateway/operator-scopes.ts` and `src/gateway/method-scopes.ts`, display `operator.write` as “write access” and `operator.admin` as “admin access.” Other scopes use “the required access,” never a guessed read-access label. Technical scopes remain in the original Gateway error details.
- Preserve “session history,” the distinction between sessions and conversation content, “admin,” curly apostrophes, and “Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}.” Explicit `UserFacingError` messages and unrelated errors retain their handling.

## Before → after

- `permission denied` / `missing scope: {scope}` → `Couldn’t complete this request. Ask an admin to grant {access}.`
- `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant operator.read.` → `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant read access.`
- Generic requests: `operator.write` → “write access”; `operator.admin` → “admin access”; any other scope → “the required access.”
- The initial F3 change also replaced `existing chat history` with `session history`.

- Fresh independent read-only review of the plain-language revision: **no actionable findings**. The reviewer inspected the scope owners, full changed formatter, and corresponding test diffs; no validation commands were run. Review run: `e66a07b4-c233-4fb2-aa2d-451af26ce776`.

---

## Problem

The composer chose the first quota group for a provider. With two accounts on the same provider, reversing the response changed which account's quota appeared. Model controls could also use a measured plan belonging to a different account.

## Solution

Carry the measured auth-profile identity through provider usage collection and the account-aware `models.authStatus` projection. Match that identity against the session's account selection before displaying quota or using a measured plan label. Share the exact-account join between the composer and model controls, and show **Quota account unknown** instead of guessing.

The profile identifier remains gated with account identity in `models.authStatus` and is removed from the public `usage.status` response.

## Impact

Quota selection no longer depends on provider response order. Model picker and default-model labels cannot borrow another account's measured plan. Profile account summaries retain their separate account-keyed source. There are no configuration, persistence, permission, dependency, or stylesheet changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI slash-command feedback uses inconsistent terms such as “active run,” title-case headings, and failure messages that lead with a diagnostic instead of a recovery action.

Commands use “reply,” “effort,” sentence-case headings, and actionable failure summaries. Diagnostics remain available in a separate paragraph. Slash tokens, command behavior, permissions, and redaction are unchanged.

| Before | After |

| Inject a message into the active run | Guide the agent’s current reply |
| Clear chat history | Clear this conversation |
| Available Commands | Available commands |
| Failed to get model info: … | Couldn’t load model details. Try again. + diagnostic paragraph |
| Prompt budget (last run) | Prompt budget (last reply) |
| Session capability is unavailable | Couldn’t access this session. Open another session and try again. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to the slash-command catalogs and moves the executor’s connection-change text into the English catalog. Updates quoted command feedback in the Chat documentation and all affected assertions. Retains the existing result contract rather than introducing another error-rendering owner.

title: feat(simlock): add owner-scoped mobile device tools
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Owners need agent-device UI automation on an existing Simlock gateway without exposing arbitrary commands or treating a shared fleet token as conversation-level device authority.

## User Impact

Adds an optional standalone Simlock tool-plugin source package (ClawHub distribution readiness is not yet established): read-only health/discovery, owned-lease status and observations; finite acquisition, explicit bounded renewal, UI actions, and explicit release that warns Simlock may wipe app data. Tools remain owner-only and subject to existing OpenClaw policy and live invocation authority. Endpoint and SecretRef examples are synthetic.

No host provisioning, rentals/billing, app installs, arbitrary shell/flags/reset, guest access system, hosting Gateway installation/restart, or npm release is included. Reopening retains the same owned lease/session rather than silently replacing a device.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses existing public plugin SDK contracts with version-2 tool factories; no core SDK expansion. Simlock remains the pool/TTL owner. Process-local receipts bind the host agent, session and incarnation to plugin-acquired scope. Cancelled/uncertain acquisitions are retained; proven undispatched failures retire safely. Explicit reconciliation of an unallocated receipt requires the pinned queue/TTL settlement bounds and fresh authoritative absence of both the lease and its pending requester. Release may wipe, so it is a separate explicitly destructive tool.

Contracts are source-pinned to Simlock `0aa6a58d0f84ed2f4409a669de5d54352f078b99` and minimum agent-device daemon `542fb77b324e522b121b18550307e457ba9be471` (RPC 2). Accessibility output is projected and infrastructure identifiers/credentials are withheld; screenshot bytes are not general app-content DLP. title: fix(doctor): allow slow original-state backups to finish
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes standalone Doctor abandoning an original-state capture at ten minutes on slow storage, before a verified recovery copy can finish.

Related: #192314. This takeover preserves Daniil Karpenko’s contribution and corrects the documented deadline.

## User Impact

Doctor allows up to twenty minutes for verified original capture. A managed Gateway may remain stopped for that additional capture time. Full verification, cancellation settlement, backup coverage, and repair-specific backups retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing single deadline and cancellation owner with a longer finite allowance. title: fix(plugins): install native dependencies when stage execution is denied
body:
Related: #193772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin installation rejecting a complete native dependency when a sandbox denies execution inside the writable install stage.

## User Impact

Staged native packages can pass completeness validation using filesystem metadata. Actual execution still requires existing runtime and OS authority. Missing or incomplete packages still receive one fresh-cache retry; persistent failure preserves the previous generation.

The old installer asks for `X_OK`, which can fail with `EPERM` even when staging filesystem operations are permitted. title: feat(ios): open matching chats from push notifications
body:
Related: #193113

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary iOS push notification opens the app but does not take someone to the chat the notification is about.

## User Impact

A push with an optional session destination can open that existing chat on the currently connected Gateway, after checking the current profile's access, without sending a message. Notifications without a destination keep their existing behavior. Missing, inaccessible, or wrong-Gateway destinations leave the current screen unchanged; taps do not automatically switch Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing `push.test` path and `openclaw nodes push --session <key>` rather than adding a general notification operation or arbitrary deep links. The Gateway resolves the destination and supplies its own identity. APNs sends revalidate through the existing session-read owner, and iOS resolves the destination on its current authenticated route before calling the existing `openChat` owner. Cold-launch handoff and reconnect use existing lifecycle owners, with duplicate-tap suppression and Watch/approval precedence preserved.

title: fix(update): name and retry busy files during backup capture
body:
Refs #193673. Builds on the diagnostic transport in #187927 by @wr-web (Wang Rui), with both existing Co-authored-by trailers preserved on all commits.

## Problem and behavior

A Windows backup can stop on a descriptor-read EBUSY without identifying the retained source file. The isolated probe now retries Windows EBUSY/EPERM twice, after 50 ms and 100 ms, closing the descriptor before waiting. Persistent failure names the source path and error code and refuses archive publication. Recovery logs a warning. EACCES and non-Windows errors do not retry.

Rebased onto main `225d2f7d4f18`. Main still lacks this busy-file handling; its 4,096-path batching, 10-second child deadline, recursive ETIMEDOUT splitting (#194239), timeout guidance (#193970), and backup snapshot changes (#194230/#194234) remain intact. Tests retain both timeout recovery and busy-file contracts. No source is silently skipped or guessed to be non-SQLite.

#195281 is potentially related, but its redacted package-update EBUSY report lacks the syscall/stack needed to establish the same cause. This fix must be present in the runtime performing backup capture; a staged candidate cannot repair an already-running older updater.

## Current-head evidence

Head `c34128c3d75425bc87928c234da35477905676f4`. This follow-up changes only one test-allocation scalar; source and tests remain identical to tested/reviewed parent `b9347326c65c`.

Linux [Crabbox/Testbox 42512351293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42512351293), with frozen candidate probe-file hashes matched and tests run serially under `timeout 180`:

| Named file | Result | Wrapper wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` | 12 passed, including main timeout recovery | 37.07s (cold worker compile) |
| `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` | 3 passed | 8.18s |
| `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.windows.test.ts` | 2 skipped on Linux | 7.73s |

The capture regression fails with main's probe modules on the missing path/code diagnostic and passes with the fix; capture uses the real isolated child and preserves the source/no-archive invariant. Six-file targeted lint passes remotely (2.93s). Dependency installation and shared worker compilation were confined to Testbox after local setup proved unavailable.

- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Local lint/test setup encountered stale linked dependencies; these were not repaired on the production Team host.
- Independent local Codex autoreview covered the complete frozen base-to-head delta and backup capture/snapshot callers at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. Source-only review.
- Allocation follow-up: 138 probe/capture lines + 223 native Windows lines = 361 literal LF lines. The original [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42514071205/job/128833652646) rejected 362 credits for 361 lines. The CI-equivalent temporary merge-index check against main `a5888561dd11`, using `--base origin/main --no-merge-base --staged`, now passes: `Test lines OK: 6585343; ceiling: 6585482; slack: 139.` Inherited debt is zero. Current-head [CI 42515751607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42515751607) is pending.

Prior-head [CI 42106962448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448) supplied genuine Windows range-lock recovery/refusal and a published-stable Linux upgrade/restore specimen for `8926dd997ae2`. Those are supporting prior evidence, not current-head Windows or upgrade proof. Current-head native Windows, build/typecheck, and upgrade coverage remain pending until the corresponding CI jobs pass. An automatic draft CI skip is not a green gate.

## Scope and limits

Production delta against main: +87/−20 in the two existing probe modules. Retained regression allocations (138 and 223 lines) cover child-I/O/archive refusal and native Windows lock lifecycle; the shared scalar is unchanged. The new tests protect observable retry bounds, accurate classification, named failure, preserved sources, and no incomplete archive publication.

This PR remains **DRAFT**. #187927 remains open.

title: fix: enable dictation for session-scoped guests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-scoped guests could send chat messages but could not dictate them. The microphone depended on operator-wide catalog/config access; recording and transcript delivery also required operator privileges.

## User Impact

Guests can dictate into chats they are authorized to write, including starting from the New Session composer. Transcripts remain editable drafts until explicitly sent. Voice settings and conversational Talk remain restricted; no broader guest role permissions or new configuration options are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse session authorization for a minimal transcription-readiness projection and transcription-only sessions. Keep provider/model overrides and full settings restricted.
- Bind recordings to the authorized session and originating connection. Retain that authority for the relay lifetime and recheck it before provider audio, finalization, readiness, and transcript delivery; revoke and clean up together.
- Carry the same live-authority check into the shared provider WebSocket transport. Recheck after asynchronous connection setup and at actual writes and graceful finalization, so queued/reconnected audio cannot outlive its authorization. Discard and revoked cleanup abort without invoking provider finalization. The callback is optional, preserving existing callers without it.
- Prepare a normal session for new-chat dictation and reuse it for the first send, rather than falling back to a shared session or creating a second chat.
- Preserve the prepared target and message idempotency key through interruption. Terminal timeout/error acknowledgments enter the existing persisted failed-message recovery path instead of being reported as accepted.
- Preserve typed speech-provider configuration and existing exports in catalog test mocks; adapt operator-only catalog tests to explicit read authority. Resolve the upstream provider-context import migration without changing the reviewed dictation behavior.

## Evidence

- Guest admission and UI regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix. Additional red/green proof covers provider audio after backing-session deletion, revoked relay finalization, and persisted initial-turn recovery.
- Real Gateway/provider-wire regression was red on `f9b01e4`: explicit discard sent `audio.done`, and reconnect-buffered audio reached the vendor after backing-session deletion. Both now pass, with authorized audio and normal finalization as positive controls and ordered socket-close barriers rather than sleep-based absence checks.

title: fix(install): keep installer fixtures off the npm registry
body:
Related: #187612 (production installer work stays separate). Requested by the test-health campaign parent ruling of 2026-11-05 17:32Z.

## What Problem This Solves

The canonical-checkout alias and configured-upgrade Doctor-failure unit fixtures queried the public npm registry while resolving Node engines. Registry availability and latency therefore affected otherwise local installer tests.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Installer unit tests use deterministic engine metadata while preserving the real installer control flow and existing assertions. **test-only; scripts/install.sh untouched**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing engine-row pattern: fixture shell `npm` functions return a fixed compatible engine range. Full-file tracing also found the nvm matrix executing ambient `/usr/bin/npm` through a fake Node executable; that fixture now supplies the same npm response. Unexpected non-`view` calls return failure.

All keeper assertions, watchdog synchronization, timeout-owner cases, and deadlines remain unchanged. Test lines remain exactly 3,679 (net 0); production lines net 0. The test-line baseline is unchanged. No new helper or production seam is introduced.

## Evidence

All six timing runs used only `pnpm test test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`, wrapped in `timeout 300`, sequentially. Each passed 228 tests with the existing Darwin-only skip.

| Run | Command wall (s) | Vitest duration (s) | Alias keeper (ms) | Doctor keeper (ms) |

Median command wall: **17.15 → 14.88 s**; Vitest duration: **15.74 → 13.41 s**; alias: **1,615 → 171 ms**; Doctor: **1,432 → 56 ms**. These are local observations, not a CI timing guarantee. The after measurements cover the final committed change, including the nvm fixture.

Historical scheduled [CI job 127375664967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42064636331/job/127375664967), at `bfbb6560585b1b7241a44a5202d927d093e776a8`, recorded **5.248 s** for the alias keeper and **5.051 s** for Doctor. Phase-1 tracing confirmed both called real `npm view openclaw@latest engines.node --fetch-timeout=5000 --fetch-retries=0` locally. Attribution of those original CI durations to registry timeouts remains unproven; ambient registry access is independently a hermeticity defect.

- Final whole-file `strace -f -e trace=execve,connect`: 5,092 `execve` calls, **zero ambient npm executions and zero IPv4/IPv6 connection attempts**; 228 passed, 1 skipped. Fixture npm executables remain in use where intended. Tracing adds overhead and is excluded from the timing table.
- Temporary mutation proof used scratch-only standalone installer copies. Removing canonicalization made **“keeps the full Git install on the canonical checkout after an alias is retargeted”** fail at its existing status assertion (received 1, expected 0). Swallowing the Doctor failure return made **“fails a configured upgrade without printing success when doctor fails”** fail at its existing status assertion (received 0, expected 9). title: fix(ui): converted sessions show import controls instead of native actions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Converted external conversations could still open the source catalog menu, including “Import to OpenClaw,” instead of normal native-session actions. This affected converted Beam rows under **Involving me** as well as other adopted catalogs.

## User Impact

Converted conversations retain their source grouping while offering normal native controls. Unconverted, view-only catalog conversations retain source controls. Native/source row replacement now closes the old menu owner and restores keyboard focus. No data migration, configuration, dependency, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the obsolete catalog-menu handoff from native display, renderer, and host contracts. Keep native and source menu ownership separate, including row cleanup and focus transfer. The coherent DOM lifecycle lives in a small sibling module because the existing renderer was at its file cap. Existing touch, keyboard, and lifecycle regressions are migrated rather than duplicated.

Against the base, production code grows by **1 net line**, maintained test code shrinks by **16 lines**, and the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Migrated desktop and touch regressions are **red on original base** `6d49ef1c4b364218f2470df9b069c7a1e5b020d0`: the source menu appears and the native menu is absent. Both are green with this change.
- **97 focused unit contracts passed**, including adoption/release, menu cleanup, focus restoration, and source-capability independence.
- **9 bundled-browser scenarios passed**: native desktop/touch/ContextMenu/Shift+F10 flows, Beam cold/pretty links, visitor access, native continuation, and paired-node source catalogs. Final one-worker command wall times were **12.18 seconds** for the unit group and **35.56 seconds** for the browser group. Per-file CI seconds are not yet available.
- Exact final-head scoped format, lint, core/UI type graph, UI controller, i18n, and dependency/patch guards passed. Staged test-line and pre-commit line-cap ratchets passed.
- The broader checker reports inherited changelog-attribution violations and unused exports `normalizeGoogleServiceTier` and `resolveScenarioConfigSteps`. Their source files are unchanged from the base; unrelated owners were not modified.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable issues after the lifecycle repair and extraction. Final-range local ClawSweeper completed with **no high/medium findings**.

**Accepted low advisory:** if a source binding is released while the native menu is open from a pinned duplicate, cleanup can dismiss that popup. This is a rare, visible, recoverable dismissal with no data loss or unintended action; keeping that popup open would add trigger-ownership coupling to the shared menu API. Users can reopen the menu.

Sanitized synthetic before/after screenshots are attached below and were inspected and shown in chat.

The separately reported fork wait-label and cross-viewer live-update symptoms are not claimed fixed by this PR. Their clean route/warm-navigation reproductions did not establish the affected client defect.

![Before: converted Beam row incorrectly offered import controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3e11775-4c0e-41c0-8e89-465d90d2f932)

![After: converted Beam row uses native session actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/987f7fcf-9b81-4a7e-8774-939b7d21ba8a)

title: fix(ios): keep New session options reachable at accessibility sizes
body:
Related: #193485

**Ready for maintainer review.** The validation gates below remain open; this status is not a claim of merge readiness.

## Contributor credit

Reported by @ellibbe in #193485. This work was requested by @PollyBot13, the linked human identity credited by the managed publication workflow.

## Work sessions

- [Original overview](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f02d78e0-e9b3-491b-9ed2-34702cfc3ce7)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6ad84dd9-6e11-4ed6-8635-14efe368e0b5)

## What Problem This Solves

At maximum accessibility text sizes, iOS Chat actions → New session options clips its heading, explanation and controls in a fixed medium-height presentation.

## User Impact

The change gives the iOS form vertical scrolling, uses a large sheet at accessibility sizes, and allows the Separate working copy label to wrap without reducing the selected font size. This PR is open for maintainer review. The basic OFF/no-keyboard matrix and the specifically tested normal-onboarding real-Gateway Cancel/OFF/ON and visible-keyboard cases are covered below. Full-suite, macOS app UI and broader qualification are not claimed complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iOS presentation owns its scroll container and adaptive detents; the shared form retains its macOS popover and existing creation/worktree logic. The shared toggle label can expand vertically. The temporary handoff checklist is removed and its remaining verification requirements are folded into this body.

The source is PollyBot13/openclaw at `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` (two commits atop `9f07ae4789dc727d992b61208ed06601633cb013`). The published integration preserves the three changed Swift files byte-for-byte and was applied directly atop old PR head `a159d658ca19a54658839cce9ad83bff13471aed`, without importing unrelated main changes. Contributor credit is retained.

### Reporter acknowledgement

**Thank you, @ellibbe**, for the [independent native red/green, default-size control, standard Watch-retaining builds and normal-onboarding ON/base-field Cancel trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6668182174). Your results are credited below and complement Engineering's proof.

The implementation is already included in this PR. **@PollyBot13 and Engineering own remaining verification and coordination.** Their isolated real-Gateway/disposable-workspace lane has now supplied the scoped effects and keyboard proof below. No additional proof is being requested from the reporter.

## Evidence

### Native layout evidence (inspected)

[Sanitized evidence and capture metadata](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) are hosted on a separate evidence-only commit, not in this product-code branch.

The inspected stills compare the same iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.2 at accessibility XXXL, Separate working copy OFF and keyboard hidden. The fixture agent has `workspaceGit=false`, so its working-copy toggle is disabled. Before shows the missing heading, truncated toggle label and clipped bottom actions; After shows the full title, explanation, wrapping label and both actions inside the large sheet.

**Before — production files at main `9f07ae4789dc727d992b61208ed06601633cb013`**

![Before: medium sheet at accessibility XXXL; heading is not visible, Separate working copy truncates, and bottom actions are clipped.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/main-iphone17-xxxl.png)

**After — captured layout commit `eef431bac6f8442085edcfc82c7a45dd8079bda2`**

![After: large sheet at the same text size shows New Thread, its explanation, the full toggle label, Cancel and Create Thread.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-iphone17-xxxl.png)

These are historical capture revisions, not a new run of the published head. Later source `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` removes the test-only production accessibility identifier and revises the regression while retaining the layout. Its three Swift blobs are identical to the published integration. Do not describe the earlier and later entire files as byte-identical.

Local Engineering reports that a manual Cancel tap dismissed the candidate sheet; the still does not depict that action or prove no thread/worktree was created. Neither image establishes Create Thread effects, working-copy ON, keyboard-visible behavior, other viewports, or an XCTest pass.

**The focused exact-source automated green is now accepted.** Engineering rebuilt the test target from task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` with Xcode 27.2 and ran `AdaptiveLayoutUITests.testNewSessionOptionsRemainReachableAtAccessibilitySize` on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.2 / accessibility XXXL at **20:50 CET on November 5, 2026**: **1/1 passed in 13.19 seconds**. Both affected production Swift files and the UI test file are byte-identical to live PR head `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`. [Durable focused XCTest proof and provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/3e8bb81bbb0f454df04ac1d7d3f7a8b74d8f7530/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).

The focused run verifies title/Cancel/Create Thread containment in the window, Cancel hittability, and dismissal after tapping Cancel. Its fixture is OFF/no keyboard; it does not exercise Create Thread or real Gateway/worktree effects. Public provenance and the screenshot were inspected and source equivalence was verified here; the Xcode execution was by Engineering, not rerun in this Team session.

Earlier iOS 26.5/27.2 automation-session stalls are historical attempts, not a current blanket inability to reach the form. An earlier `test-without-building` pass reused an older runner and is **excluded from exact-source proof**. The accepted result is the later rebuilt run only. Paired with the fresh original-main failure at 21:05 CET documented below, this now supplies a **matching focused automated red/green** for the iPhone 17 XXXL OFF/no-keyboard fixture scenario. It does not establish full-suite validation, real Gateway effects, or the complete viewport/ON/keyboard matrix. [Combined red/green and SE3 provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).

### Matching focused baseline-red and smaller-iPhone proof

[Durable red/green and SE3 evidence](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) records these additional Engineering runs on November 5, 2026:

The test **failed 1/1 on original behavior**: `New Thread title is not visible` at test line 48. The title was not hittable; Cancel began at `y=840.1` with height `44.2`, extending below the `874`-point window. This is a behavioral baseline failure, not a missing scroll-view identifier or a runner stall.
- The matching candidate green is the rebuilt **20:50 CET 1/1 pass** described above. Engineering reports restoring the candidate test/production files afterward and verifying its local worktree clean. The raw baseline result bundle and uncropped screenshot remain private; the published sanitized provenance records the failure. No Team-side Xcode rerun is claimed.
- **iPhone SE (3rd generation) candidate green, 21:11 CET:** the same exact-source focused test on iOS 27.2 / accessibility XXXL **passed 1/1 in 16.57 seconds**. In the `375×667`-point viewport, Cancel/Create Thread initially lay below the visible area (Cancel `y=696.5`, not initially hittable). The test scrolled until both action frames were contained and Cancel was hittable, tapped Cancel, and observed dismissal. This proves focused smaller-viewport **reachability by scrolling**, not that everything fits initially or that Create Thread was activated.
- The [SE3 initial screenshot](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-xcuitest-se3-xxxl-initial.png) was inspected. It shows the initial title, explanation and toggle with actions below the viewport; it is **not** a post-scroll or dismissal image. The post-scroll assertions and pass are recorded by Engineering's published provenance.
- These earlier Engineering runs alone establish OFF/no-keyboard fixture layout/cancellation, not real Gateway effects, production keyboard, full-suite or macOS UI validation. Additional default-size and independent Watch-retaining build proof is credited below; it is not retroactively attributed to these earlier runs.

### Attributed supplemental proof — Engineering

[Durable Engineering provenance, commands and sanitized images](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) records these runs on task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4`. The two production Swift blobs were independently compared with live head `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369` and match. The native executions below are Engineering reports, not Team-side reruns.

- **SE3/default text, OFF/no keyboard:** fresh Xcode 27.2 test on iPhone SE (3rd generation), iOS 27.2, light appearance, `375×667` points, at **21:33:18 CET**: **1/1 passed in 14.135 seconds**. Only the test-only category was temporarily changed to `UICTContentSizeCategoryL` and an extra pre-Cancel screenshot retained; no production code or fixture data changed. Title and both actions were contained **without scrolling**, and Cancel dismissed. The original test was restored and Engineering reports its worktree clean. The [default-size screenshot](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-se3-default.png) was inspected.
- **Native iOS typography:** rebuilt source-equivalent `OpenClawTypographyTests` **23/23 passed** on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.2 / Xcode 27.2; reported test duration **2.240 seconds**. This and the SE3/default run used the temporary generated **no-Watch project**. These results are not attributed to a standard Watch-retaining project.
- **Focused shared session actions:** macOS-hosted Swift package `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` **50/50 passed**, with Node 24 on PATH. This is targeted shared-package evidence, not a macOS app/popover UI pass or real-Gateway effect test.

<details>
<summary>Engineering command provenance and full-package failures</summary>

Sanitized command templates from the linked provenance use placeholders for private device IDs, executable paths and result directories; they were not executed by Team:

```sh
xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<owned-SE3-device>' \

  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<owned-iPhone17-device>' \

PATH="<Node24-bin>:$PATH" swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit \
```
