
Earlier full-package execution ran **2,492 tests with three failures**, all at `createdParentSessionKeys() == [nil]`:

- “new trigger starts fresh agent session without admin reset”
- “new trigger keeps selected global agent scope”
- “new trigger prefers explicit session agent over ambient agent”

Engineering's control restoring the changed shared production file to original main reproduced all three. This records baseline attribution, **not a full-suite pass**; raw result bundles remain private.

</details>

### Independent reporter proof — @ellibbe

[ellibbe's native-check comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6668182174) reports independent checks of the current implementation on **iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0 / Xcode 27.2 / Light/English**:

- Production files from parent `a159d658ca19` produce the behavioral red (“New Thread title is not visible”, **10.780 seconds**); current implementation passes containment, Cancel reachability and dismissal (**13.761 seconds**).
- The **default-size control passes in 13.473 seconds** on the same corrected binary. Combined with Engineering's SE3/default result and the existing XXXL cases, this covers the basic two-viewport, default/XXXL OFF/no-keyboard fixture matrix—not all production-flow configurations.
- **Both base and fix pass the standard app build with the Watch companion retained**, SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1, with no lint exception or Watch removal. This closes the PR-level “only a no-Watch build is proven” gap for the reporter's standard-build runs. It does not turn Engineering's narrowed-project tests into standard-project tests, nor prove a full suite, archive/release, macOS UI or Watch runtime behavior.
- A **normal-onboarding/WebSocket-fixture ON run** enables working copy, enters `main` in the base field, scrolls until both actions are inside the window and hittable, then cancels (**29.912 seconds**). Its fixture trace contains **no creation or chat-send request**. This is app/fixture client-boundary Cancel evidence, not real-Gateway creation/worktree verification.

The reporter used the accessibility method in an existing separate XCTest runner, retargeted to the explicit Debug bundle; this is not a claim of a full canonical repository test-target pass. The reporter's keyboard object existed during editing, but the retained stills **do not visibly show the software keyboard**. Do not close production-flow keyboard-visible qualification from that run. These are reporter-supplied executions, not executions by Team or local Engineering. The later Engineering real-Gateway keyboard run below is separate and does not change what the reporter's stills establish.

### Keyboard evidence — keep the fixture paths separate

Engineering also published an inspected [historical SYNTHETIC ON/visible-keyboard crop](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/synthetic-on-keyboard.png). A temporary transport stub / `workspaceGit=true` fixture was used with production layout code unchanged; fixture changes were restored. The crop shows the focused base field and both actions above a **visible software keyboard**; text entry and Cancel dismissal are reported separately from what the still alone shows.

This is **historical SYNTHETIC fixture-only layout evidence**. It is not the reporter's normal-onboarding flow, a real Gateway flow, an automated green/red, or production keyboard-visible qualification. The later real-Gateway assisted keyboard run below is distinct and now qualifies the specified normal-flow case; do not combine the historical fixture paths to manufacture that proof.

### Real native Gateway, persisted sessions and Git proof

[Engineering's pinned real-Gateway provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/86a5ac47d3b47af90fc95d01e548b3f8d63dda5e/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) records **normal-onboarding native app → real Gateway → persisted SQLite/session-owned Git worktree** checks, not screenshot transport or a WebSocket mock. The owned Gateway was built from task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4`; affected app production blobs match published head `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`. Environment: Xcode 27.2, iPhone 17 / iOS 27.2 / accessibility XXXL / light appearance. These runs still used the narrowed generated **no-Watch** iOS project; the independent standard Watch-retaining build above remains separately attributed.

- **Real Cancel — 21:42:01 CET, 1/1 passed in 27.684 seconds.** Normal onboarding connected to the owned loopback Gateway. After opening the form, Cancel dismissed it. Separate read-only SQLite snapshots before and after both showed **0 session heads, 0 session events and 0 worktrees**; Git retained only the original worktree. This closes the tested real-Gateway non-creation case, not just a client fixture trace.
- **Real OFF/ON Create — 21:45 CET, 1/1 passed in 45.949 seconds.** The temporary harness canceled once, created with working copy OFF, reopened the form, enabled ON, entered base `main`, and scrolled until Create was hittable **and fully contained** before activating it. Both successful modes dismissed the sheet. Separate backend readback found **three distinct persisted session identities and one managed worktree**: two OFF sessions (including one from the earlier partial attempt), and the successful ON session. The worktree has `owner_kind=session`, its `owner_id` matches that ON session, and `base_ref=main`. Independent Git readback found its HEAD equal to the disposable repository's main commit and its working tree clean. Private IDs/path mappings are retained by Engineering, not invented or exposed here.
- **First expanded attempt is not a full pass.** It persisted an OFF session, then stopped before ON activation because the harness had treated partial `isHittable` as enough and a full-containment assertion failed. Only the temporary harness was corrected to require containment as well as hittability; production code did not change. That partial OFF result is included in the totals, not hidden or counted as a complete run.

**Real ON/base-main with visible software keyboard — 21:47:29 CET, 1/1 passed in 63.429 seconds.** This was an assisted native journey: after entering the base field, the harness paused for 25 seconds and Engineering used **Device Hub → Device → Keyboard → Toggle Software Keyboard once**. It was not a fully unattended test. No app production code or host security setting was changed for the toggle.

The inspected native image shows `main` and both actions scrolled fully above the visibly displayed software keyboard. XCTest checked window containment, Create's hittable/enabled state and `Create.frame.maxY <= keyboard.frame.minY`, then activated Create and observed dismissal. Backend readback added **one session and one owned worktree**; its owner matches the new session, its requested base is main, and its HEAD independently equals main.

![Real normal-onboarding ON flow after scrolling: base field main, Cancel and Create Thread fully above the visible software keyboard. This run used one documented Device Hub keyboard toggle. ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/86a5ac47d3b47af90fc95d01e548b3f8d63dda5e/docs/pr-evidence/193600/real-gateway-on-visible-keyboard.png)

**Final accounting across all attempts: 4 persisted sessions / 2 session-owned worktrees**, including the partial OFF attempt. Both worktrees were verified against the disposable repository's main commit. No initial chat turn/model run was sent. The public provenance and image were inspected here; native executions and separate SQLite/Git observations were by Engineering, not rerun by Team.

Engineering reports final cleanup: original production/test sources restored and its test worktree clean, owned Gateway stopped, loopback listener absent, task app uninstalled. Credentials/state/Git data were disposable and isolated; production was untouched. Raw logs/result bundles remain private because onboarding included a task-only setup credential; no code/token or private environment path is embedded here.

These results close only the tested real Cancel/OFF/ON/backend effects and the iPhone 17 XXXL normal-flow visible-keyboard scenario with the documented assistance. They do not turn the committed layout regression into a full backend suite, retroactively make the first partial attempt pass, or establish full-suite, macOS app/popover UI, hardware-device or comprehensive VoiceOver coverage.

### Published-head checks

- Published head: `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`; tree: `f085a02112d52b7343fea7332e787074f454761b`; direct parent: old PR head `a159d658ca19a54658839cce9ad83bff13471aed`. Live GitHub and fetched Git objects verify the exact tree and PollyBot13 co-author trailer.
- The only task paths relative to that old head are the three reviewed Swift files plus deletion of `apps/ios/Tests/NewSessionAccessibility.md`. The published tree is identical to prepared candidate `a604622ab3873981ab007e3f2e1e4ffbaa6be8b6`; all three Swift blobs match reviewed task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4`. Whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh P0–P2 local Auto Review of the exact published head, with six complete source files as context: **scoped-clean, no findings**. This is code-review evidence, not native runtime proof.
- [Current-head checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600/checks) were observed as **5 successful and 58 skipped/neutral**, with no failed or active runs, all on `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`. The iOS build/UI/screenshot and macOS Swift jobs were skipped; those skips are not native validation. Earlier-head results are excluded; the completed current-head ClawSweeper review and author-side evidence reconciliation are linked below.
- Native Swift/Xcode tools are unavailable in this Team Linux sandbox; no native build or XCTest was run here. Team inspected the published provenance/images and source equivalence. Native executions remain attributed to Engineering or @ellibbe; unclaimed qualifications are listed below.

### ClawSweeper review reconciliation

[Completed ClawSweeper review of `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6663694967) lists **Before merge: None** and **Findings: None**. It requests no production-code patch. Its optional proof notes predate the later evidence; the following is the author-side reconciliation, not a new bot verdict or maintainer merge approval.

- **Missing automated baseline-red / optional red-green demonstration — addressed:** the same focused test, Xcode/device/runtime/category setup failed on original-main production files at 21:05 CET for the original title-visibility/clipped-action behavior, while rebuilt source-equivalent candidate passed at 20:50. This is not a missing test-only identifier failure. [Combined provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).
- **Smaller/default-size proof — addressed for the basic OFF/no-keyboard matrix:** SE3 XXXL passed with scrolling, SE3/default passed without scrolling, and @ellibbe independently supplied the iPhone 17/default control alongside the representative XXXL red/green. Sources, timings and narrow fixture/harness limits are recorded above. [Engineering proof](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md); [independent reporter proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6668182174).

It includes one documented Device Hub keyboard toggle during a 25-second pause, so it is qualified assisted proof, not a fully unattended or all-configuration claim. The reporter and historical synthetic cases remain separate. [Real proof](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/86a5ac47d3b47af90fc95d01e548b3f8d63dda5e/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).
- **Broader validation is not silently waived:** the tested real-Gateway and keyboard cases now have the explicit proof above. Full-suite attribution, macOS UI and broader/VoiceOver qualification remain distinct; no additional exhaustive matrix is invented from an unobserved defect. title: feat: reload plugins across active native conversations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent running `openclaw plugins reload <plugin> --wait` can wait on its own retained plugin generation. Multiple active conversations retaining the same generation make caller-only handoff insufficient.

## User Impact

`openclaw plugins reload <plugin> --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json` can hand off all supported retaining native conversations without asking the model to stop polling. The Gateway owns accepted maintenance independently of the CLI socket: an external CLI receives final JSON, while interrupted agent callers receive the actual outcome in the same conversation.

Force requires Gateway administration authority. It never discards live plugin leases or replays completed side effects. Ordinary Stop still cancels queued work; maintenance preserves durable queued inputs and their original requester. Failed activation or retirement keeps continuations fenced unless the lifecycle owner proves a healthy outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add the CLI/protocol force option through the existing reload reservation, publication and rollback owner. Non-force behavior and existing drain budgets remain unchanged.
- Capture exact retaining native-run continuations under each admitted original requester, with current-authority checks, session incarnation, queue custody and successor barriers. Unsupported runs fail before interruption.
- Give cooperative holders a short bounded grace, then use normal controller maintenance interruption and join subprocess plus actual plugin-call cleanup before allowing successors.
- Revalidate the maintenance administrator at physical interruption. Keep initiating-person and exact-run Stop ownership after the original RPC retires, retain private internal delivery, and preserve canonical Gateway binding for queued followups.
- Consume the canonical settled replacement outcome, including publication and recovery health. A committed activation failure must not resume conversations or claim rollback. Missing old rollback code must not block a successfully applied, healthy replacement.
- Scope is process-local only: no operation journal, startup recovery, schema migration, public operation observer or new queue. After a Gateway crash, inspect plugin state before retrying.

Designed and implemented from @jacobtomlinson’s approved multi-session reload plan.
## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/85b7d33e-fd16-4ea2-85ee-46951f9ab0e2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/353ee643-f438-4437-82e2-e5514304140f)

## Evidence

### Fresh dummy-plugin / real-Gateway proof

Conditions: isolated Linux Gateway launched through the normal `pnpm openclaw` guard, deterministic local Responses API fixture, real native and Code Mode tool execution, and actual CLI commands. The fixture never voluntarily completed retaining work before maintenance handoff. B/C held Node subprocesses with 200ms SIGTERM cleanup. In the force-control runs, D started while the target plugin was disabled, then the plugin was enabled before A/B/C started; D genuinely retained no selected instance. Merely hiding a tool does not establish that control. The non-force baseline instead had four retaining turns.

Sources: baseline `659d1c5bb3513f51b5ec0981a06909ed27c6bc15`; initial repair `bac8e5ac1103360717da35e449a8400f5da6ffab`; final repair `18661f5b89b35983eac9aa61d2862c10b55e8e9c` (same tree as this publication's metadata commit). Native/Code Mode and healthy-rollback rows ran on the initial repair; those unchanged paths are reused. The committed-activation fence and missing-old-source correction were exercised on final runtime bytes. Recorded runtime file hashes matched their corresponding committed source.

The dummy replacement registered this fault only in its new version:

```ts
api.on("gateway_start", async () => {
  throw new Error("POST_PUBLICATION_PROOF_REFUSAL");
});
```

Actual commands:

```text
openclaw plugins reload reload-proof --wait --accept-capabilities --json
openclaw plugins reload reload-proof --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json
```

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| Published non-force baseline, 12-second bounded observation | `phase=reloading`; 12 retained work items; A/B/C remained on original active runs; no continuation. Explicit Stop cleaned up afterward. This is not an infinite-time claim. |

title: feat(ios): reconcile unread app-icon badges (WIP)
body:
Related: #191489

## What Problem This Solves

iOS users have no app-icon unread reminder after dismissing a notification. **This is an explicitly partial/WIP draft, not a completed fix for #191489.**

## User Impact

This slice implements app-applied unread-session badge reconciliation on foreground, authenticated reconnect, session invalidations, accepted session mutations, and existing background wakes. It counts authorized unread conversations across agents, including manual unread, independently of sidebar pagination. Archived and execution-only subagent sessions are excluded; user-openable child conversations remain eligible.

**Automatic assistant-activity APNs wakes are still missing.** A disconnected phone is not yet woken by a newly completed assistant response. The accepted delivery limitation also remains: if iOS does not execute the app, its badge cannot update. Native compilation, simulator/device behavior, and real APNs acceptance are not verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse `deriveSessionUnread` through an optional `sessions.list` `unreadOnly` filter and existing exact `totalCount`; no separate unread-message counter or new unread store.
- Keep the badge a replaceable, authenticated current-scope projection. Account/route changes invalidate pending reads; privacy resets do not mark sessions read.
- Serialize OS badge setters separately from network reads so a privacy reset need not wait for an offline request. Keep APNs payloads badge-free: custom scope/revision fields cannot stop iOS from applying delayed `aps.badge` values.
- Keep `push.test` a transport diagnostic. No durable registration or permission changes are included.

### Maintainer design acceptance needed for the remaining wake path

Native APNs registrations currently contain node/transport identity, but no durable authenticated operator-profile binding. Pairing scopes alone cannot select disconnected recipients without risking an unrelated-profile activity broadcast. The existing web-push recipient-authority path has a profile binding; native registrations do not.

Proposed next step: extend the **existing APNs registration owner** with a binding established only from the authenticated operator/device, revalidate current pairing/profile/role/session visibility at the actual send boundary, and clear or replace the binding on unregister, unpair, or identity replacement. Then wire real assistant activity into an authorized badge-free invalidation/wake path. Do not broadcast to all registered iPhones or infer a profile from a display name.

This durable-data/authority-lifecycle design still needs recorded maintainer acceptance under the [storage-change checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes). This draft is the discussion and review checkpoint; it does not claim that acceptance has been granted.

## Evidence

Current published head: `75543e5e0e96265179d6da487b52d9402ffd24ac`; reviewed tree: `f9a10df3bfd3b139750c5a6e00e92975e5d25b5e`. The published tree matches the reviewed local candidate exactly. The exact PR merge base is `844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e`, confirmed by GitHub comparison. The target-main SHA / prior hosted-review base `c230ae5c3c4643476e5a6eddc3120260d043a86e` is distinct; it was not silently substituted for the local review base.

### Simplification and ownership

Applied **pr-simplify → cross-layer-pr-regression-review → Auto Review**. Scope stays with the existing authenticated operator connection and its authority generation. Removed the duplicate badge scope/route caches, gateway-identity and reaction-identity lookups, repeated cleanup/guard branches, and the private count-only response decoder. The canonical session-list response decoder is reused.

The small badge helper remains because it coalesces reads and serializes OS writes separately: a privacy reset must not wait for an offline network read, and an already-started OS setter must settle before the reset. Accepted-read transport invalidation and the existing foreground/reconnect/background hooks remain; no server-side unread counter or new registration state was introduced.

Compared with the full pre-simplification local candidate (tree `a0d763184e47f09d31f2cdbb669b75476ddb30bf`, including the retained roster test follow-up), production code is **59 lines smaller** and native tests are **one line smaller**, with an OS-setter failure case added. This is separate from the entire PR against its merge base: **381 added / 6 removed lines** across ten files. Excluding generated data/docs/allocation, production is +170/−4 lines and tests are +181/−0 lines. The necessary remaining growth implements the new query, native projection, and distinct boundary regressions.

### Executed checks and review

- The new real `sessions.list` handler regression was **red before implementation and green after canonical filtering and validator regeneration**. The retained follow-up also interleaves normal/unread queries and covers both ordinary and serialized/retained selection; canonical read/activity changes update totals without pagination or visibility leakage. This is Gateway boundary proof, not an icon demonstration.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.unread-count.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.filters.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **41 tests passed** across three files; 21.42 seconds total command time in the retained terminal-success log. The Gateway restarted after the run; its process exit receipt was lost, so no separate exit-code receipt is claimed for that run. CI seconds remain unavailable.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0.

- `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e --staged`, and whitespace checks — exit 0. Targeted TypeScript/docs formatting is unchanged and passing. The isolated 93-line allocation covers the RPC regression; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Read-only cross-layer review of the frozen candidate: no P0/P1 findings in the implemented Gateway → protocol → transport → connection lifecycle → OS-write path. Native execution gaps are retained below.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review**, local mode against the exact merge base, through P3: **scoped-clean**, exit 0, no findings across the complete simplified candidate. This is source review of the partial slice, not native compilation or completion of the original feature.

The [latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193491#issuecomment-6659144709), completed November 8 for head `75543e5e0e96265179d6da487b52d9402ffd24ac`, reports no definite introduced code findings but requires real production authority-to-native-effect evidence before merge. No Mac/device access, credentials, or paid allocation were borrowed. This PR remains a partial draft; the original implementation goal remains open.

### Native validation request

**Next owner/action:** a native validator with access to an existing authorized macOS lane should run the published commit `75543e5e0e96265179d6da487b52d9402ffd24ac` and attach the evidence below to this PR. ```bash

Confirm the actual checkout SHA. `--ref main` uses **main’s inline test selectors**, not the target branch’s workflow edits; current main omits `UnreadAppIconBadgeTests`. Explicitly select that suite on the qualified runner. A green job with zero matching tests, or a Node-only `build-artifacts` result, is not native proof.

<details>
<summary>Native build/test command on the prepared, dedicated runner (not yet executed)</summary>

```bash

HEAD_SHA=75543e5e0e96265179d6da487b52d9402ffd24ac

source scripts/lib/swift-toolchain.sh
```

## User Impact

Empty status sidebars no longer occupy space. Self-only conversations stay quiet during loading. Known participants remain visible when viewer lookup fails, and populated sections keep their conversation gutter while Details hydrates. Cached Processes reserves space only when its actual open callback is available; live-empty or denied results can retire the section. Cached process rows do not gain live control actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Section owners report presence and scoped availability instead of querying their own DOM. Rendering and pre-hydration reservation share admission policies for viewer identity, live/cached Outputs and Processes, Environment, Subagents, Automations, and published links. Lightweight Boolean selectors stay eager while rich projections and view rendering remain lazy. Existing scoped owner facts override initial cache forecasts without adding another inventory, identity owner, or process observer.

No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Evidence

- **192 tests passed across 15 focused suites**, preserving the prior regressions and adding cached-Processes pending→ready geometry, callback admission, and settled-empty/access retirement. title: fix(ui): make Goal shorthand composer reversible
body:
Contributor credit: @jacobtomlinson — authorized request and UX direction; credited as a commit co-author.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/70e5121f-0faa-435b-8510-efe302b46d70)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/a167119b-f494-4af6-98e4-f8002bc3e680)

## What Problem This Solves

Goal shorthand should use the same objective-only composer as an explicit creation starter: `/goal land it` should show only `land it`. Deleting that objective should restore command entry instead of leaving an empty Goal box stranded or immediately reentering it.

This supersedes the earlier raw-prefix iteration. It does not claim to reproduce the separately reported transcript text-loss cause.

## User Impact

- `/goal l` immediately enters Goal mode showing only `l`, without a visible command prefix.
- `/goal start` followed by a space opens an initially empty Goal box that remains available for typing; empty Enter does not submit or exit.
- Deleting the objective, or pressing Backspace/Delete in an already-empty command-origin Goal box, restores `/goal ` with the caret at the end.
- Valid subcommand prefixes and management actions retain command behavior. Picker creation and Goal editing retain literal-text semantics and do not exit merely because they become empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume command syntax at the existing composer/draft owner. An optional creation-only `fromCommand` marker enables empty restoration while the textbox and persisted draft contain the literal objective. Existing admission, cleanup, recovery, cancellation, and session owners remain authoritative. No timer, extra control, configuration option, or backend change is added.

## Evidence

- Corrective UI revision: **222 tests across eight focused files passed**, plus a passing production-bundle Chromium regression for activation, objective edits, empty restoration, completion/reentry, explicit empty creation, paste, reload, and literal Goal submission. The prior raw-prefix revision was red for the objective-only assertion.
- The follow-up consolidates the redundant admission test into the adjacent literal-objective table while preserving manual/command-origin, whitespace, intent, attachment, single-send and cleanup coverage: **47 admission tests passed**.
- Fresh scripts/UI-test types, targeted oxlint, oxfmt and whitespace checks passed. The Goal feature patch remains unchanged from reviewed head `52d0345`; current Main integration is separately qualified by fresh CI.
- Exact regression-line allocation is **221**, reduced from 231 after the ten-line test consolidation. The shared baseline is unchanged. The frozen-CI-corpus ratchet passed with **14 lines of prior slack retained**; the existing 11 passing ratchet-contract tests remain applicable.

### Authentic v2026.11.1 draft upgrade proof

**Four Chromium flows passed using the actual released UI as the legacy producer and the current production UI as the reader.** Each case preserves the same browser context and origin across the bundle switch; drafts are produced through released UI actions, not synthesized, rewritten, or copied.

| Released producer → current consumer | Verified outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary draft | Old/new reloads preserve exact text; normal submission has no Goal intent. |
| Manual Goal-start | Old/new reloads preserve literal `/goal clear`, whitespace and newline; submission carries the exact objective and Goal-start intent. |
| Manual Goal-edit → cancel | Old/new reloads preserve edit mode/text; cancellation restores the exact prior ordinary draft without a Goal update, including another reload. |
| Manual Goal-edit → submit | Submission retains the original Goal ID and exact literal objective; the acknowledged edit restores the prior ordinary draft. |

The official npm archive was checked against registry SHA-512 integrity and pinned SHA-256 `611282534d576e12f10b0ac5a1ac0d2825aac360637e92815a56eb71fb5a0301`. Release tag object `08d4ded27a1de5af3b60734f7673d4cb594efe78` resolves to `4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a`. The browser verifies real client version/build identity and loaded entry hashes. Reproduction driver: [`scripts/proof-control-ui-goal-upgrade.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7e278f0d62921618130680d642350fa6d13517ec/scripts/proof-control-ui-goal-upgrade.ts).

This is an authentic **browser-bundle/storage upgrade with a synthetic mock Gateway**, not a real Gateway/provider or full process upgrade. Native Gateway sockets and non-task-origin HTTP are blocked. The refresh guard is not disabled. Current UI source in the proof receipt is `52d0345`, whose product code is unchanged by this proof/test-only follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce from the repository root with a fresh output directory</summary>

```sh
mkdir -p .openclaw/tmp/goal-upgrade
git fetch --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head origin refs/tags/v2026.11.1
curl -fL https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw/-/openclaw-2026.11.1.tgz -o .openclaw/tmp/goal-upgrade/openclaw-2026.11.1.tgz
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-control-ui-goal-upgrade.ts --stable-tarball .openclaw/tmp/goal-upgrade/openclaw-2026.11.1.tgz --out .openclaw/tmp/goal-upgrade/reproduce-new
```

</details>

### Landing preparation and current CI

The paired diagnostics from the [previous performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42065703144/job/127380136250) show a **candidate-only** Chat boot JS gzip violation: **1,294,638 bytes** against **1,294,292 bytes**; the paired baseline has no violations. The step label `control-ui-performance-base` was not a baseline-failure verdict. This is not claimed as an inherited-failure exception. `pnpm test:ci-failed 193472 --run` completed and classified the performance failure as new, with no selected Vitest failures.

Current Main includes [#194135](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194135), the verified generated-name normalization/Chat boot byte-paydown repair with tighter budgets. That source was integrated at `a6b2e96ffd91f8a2d81564553b252a2c010fb7b2` without altering the Goal feature patch: its before/after stable patch ID is identical (`e8bfad2be0c0c4ce4c6652cc055f67b9d9586a0e`). No budget increase or unrelated repair was added by this PR.

The managed publisher produced current head **`0a9a9b43ebb1533491448205d16ec4f2f9d73b00`**. Its [fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42266332281) passes performance, all three UI shards, UI e2e, types/lint and security lanes. The remaining root failure is the test-line ratchet; the combined gates are red, not green. Native preparation records `github_pending`, not successful gate proof. Prior-head green results are not substituted for this revision.

The ratchet reports 6,550,939 test lines against ceiling 6,550,891: **48 lines over**, net PR delta **+221**. Actual captured Main `ce4260e0a5e81d0e9c1134c101e08fdd4b77cac2` has 6,550,718 lines against ceiling 6,550,670: the same **48-line deficit**. Recomputed source accounting exactly matches the tested merge. This PR adds precisely its existing 221-line allocation, preserving rather than creating the deficit. The scheduled-main comparison says “new” because its older matching scheduled job passed; direct captured-source attribution is retained separately. No scalar change, allocation padding, or unrelated test deletion was made to hide this inherited deficit.

The read-only native inherited-failure verifier **passed** for this exact head and failed run attempt, including tested-merge provenance, captured-source attribution, current-main security publisher, review requirements and effective writer capability. It qualified the bot's advertised **CI-only ruleset delegation**, not organization-admin authority. This is qualified exception evidence, not green CI or a merge receipt. Jacob's scoped landing instruction remains the authority; the parent maintainer workflow owns the final pinned squash action and revalidation.

### Visual evidence

The images retained below are labeled historical/current:

- Images 1–3 are historical captures from the superseded raw-prefix iteration.
- Images 4–5 show the accepted objective-only Goal box and empty restoration.
- Images 6–7 show the authentic v2026.11.1 persisted edit draft and current cancellation restoring its old ordinary draft.

Literal `/goal clear` inside the compatibility edit box is intentional objective text in an already-active manual edit, not shorthand activation. All captures use synthetic data. Direct GitHub attachment downloads returned HTTP 200 and matched inspected originals' SHA-256 hashes.

### Review and limits

Independent reviews found no actionable findings in the corrective product delta at `267ea838` and the allocation-only delta through `52d0345`. Jacob's requested [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193472#issuecomment-6658499844) completed on **`7e278f0d62921618130680d642350fa6d13517ec`** at 17:50 UTC on November 5 with **Findings: None**, accepting the authentic stable-draft compatibility proof; performance validation remained outstanding. No further automatic re-review comment was posted for the Main-only integration.

The three-file proof/test/allocation delta at **`7e278f0d62921618130680d642350fa6d13517ec` was independently reviewed with no actionable findings**. That review checked archive/tag integrity, actual released UI producers, preserved storage/origin, four-case request assertions, test consolidation and the exact 221-line allocation. It inspected source and the completed four-case receipt rather than rerunning Chromium. The Goal feature patch is unchanged by the subsequent Main-only integration; owned upstream drift adds optional chat attachment-context typing and a separate composer pane-rebinding regression, not Goal behavior.

These are agent reviews, not a claim of formal GitHub approval. Browser undo/redo proof covers objective edits after command consumption, not undo across consumption. No real Gateway/model/provider or full process-upgrade claim is made. The original transcript text-loss cause remains unreproduced. Jacob requested landing on November 6; merge remains gated on current-source preparation and required checks, and is reserved to the parent maintainer workflow.

title: fix: recover conversations after accidental session resets
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: accidentally choosing `/reset` clears the visible conversation with no recovery action in chat.

## User Impact

The latest recoverable manual reset now offers **Undo** in the existing Session reset divider, with confirmation. It restores earlier history and the next agent's context. Messages sent after the reset remain on another branch instead of being deleted or silently merged. Undo does not reverse tool actions or file changes.

Automatic or tail-preserving resets are not undoable. Active, queued, or unadopted input must settle before Undo; the operation does not cancel it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing rewind, transcript, and mutation owners rather than adding a recovery store. A deliberate leaf selection opens the requested reset window while ordinary stale controls remain fenced. Validated navigation records exactly which reset IDs were reopened; the planner consumes those facts, and later resets revoke them.

History and model-context projections share one complete navigation-field contract, so restoring the UI also restores the actual model request. Authority and the latest boundary are revalidated before mutation. No database table or migration is added.

## Evidence

### Current published raw-source-hash inventory repair

- Published head: `591578e4a775106f83f791bbc8f3e8a3b165f3e6`, tree-identical to approved source commit `80dbcf7d60a78c3da9ef7ee46388d78031c304b8`, with the exact Jacob coauthor trailer verified. Managed publication completed as `roboclaw-bot`; no main integration or PR merge was performed for this update. Its only source delta from prior published `912b13e7d0597099a05bf0352347d766e790b069` is **one added entry**, `en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts`, in the authoritative `sourceFiles` inventory in `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-catalog.ts`.
- The exact prior-head CI failure was reproduced locally before editing: `ui/src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts` → **includes every English dependency in the raw source-hash input** failed with the same reset-confirmation assertion (**1 failed, 43 unselected skipped**). The fragment was already consumed by the catalog composition and its modal; its complete raw bytes were missing from the maintained hash-input inventory. No test, collector, hash contract, snapshot or missing-file guard was weakened.
- After the one-line owner fix, **111 full consumer tests pass**: all **44 Vite-config/source-hash tests**, all **30 catalog tests**, and **37 catalog-verification/deadcode tests**. Scripts and UI type lanes, scoped owner lint, formatting and whitespace pass. These are **implementation-owner-run** results, not independent reviewer-run tests. No test source growth was added; the **853-line allocation is unchanged**.
- The same retained independent reviewer approved the frozen one-line artifact with **no findings**. The committed diff matches reviewed SHA-256 `af632061bb367b63843e4a68510f44578853fefeec25cfda03d0095f21533a59`; whole-checkout/index checks confirmed only that intended path and entry. This approval is limited to the inventory repair, not overall readiness, a performance waiver or a new runtime repair.
- Managed inspection at this updated head reports **open, unmerged, mergeable: false / dirty**. This did not prohibit the authorized branch publication; it does prevent a conflict-free/readiness claim. The reviewed upstream pin remains `9d8bbfbbaf162cda2f5cd620816b6ac8a8bd5d00`. New-head CI must establish its own outcome; **the prior-head run and performance measurements below are not CI evidence for this new head**. No automatic moving-main integration, performance experiment, Android retry or denied upgrade attempt was used to publish this one-line fix.

### Prior 912-head CI and integrated proof — historical scope

- The prior `912b13e7` tree matched reviewed integration `17345dd8af2c24640941d50385244c93021573c5`. Its branch integration restored normal CI eligibility; this was not a PR merge. The single generated-predicate conflict was resolved through canonical generation/check, while source/UI changes auto-merged.
- Exact prior-head [CI run 42132165125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125) **completed with failure**. Its aggregate selected three failing lanes: [UI source-hash job 127611975030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975030), repaired locally above; [Android access job 127611975286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975286), which failed while preparing the Emulator SDK ZIP with **Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel**, before Gradle or tests; and [performance job 127611974700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611974700). Android's setup failure is not product proof, a proven inherited defect or a passing run, and it was not retried. Baseline-ratchets job 127611974942 passed separately.
- The prior cloud performance annotation says **1264.7 KiB chat-boot gzip exceeds 1264.4 KiB**. These rounded values are not the exact local measurements below. A truncated check listing must not be interpreted as all green, and a Security Review target/workflow_run result is not a normal CI result for another head.
- Earlier integrated owner proof passed **368 core/tooling tests**, **90 affected UI tests**, **14 prefix-stability tests**, all five maintained type lanes, targeted core/scripts/root-test lint, formatting, source-line and whitespace gates. These retain their earlier source scope and were not all rerun for the one-line repair.
- The prior test-line checker passed **6,510,614 ≤ 6,510,672**, with **853** allocated regression lines. Earlier full core lint was not green: plugin-model-catalog (702) and supervisor (701) exceeded max-lines with files/config byte-identical to pinned upstream. No suppression or unrelated edit hid them. Complete integrated P2 autoreview returned two chunks with zero actionable findings; that review and the independent pipeline audit below are not passing CI or upgrade proof.

### Final symmetric local asset comparison — failing, independently audited

This measurement belongs to the **prior 912-source candidate**, compared with pinned 9d8; it was **not rerun after the one-line raw-source inventory repair**. Both source roots were prepared with their maintained native UI builders and metadata finalizers for the same **eight declared plugin UIs / 21 assets**, using **Node 26.12.1, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.3**, the same installed/remapped dependencies and fixed comparison build identity. The actual performance checker and cap were unchanged.

| Local profile | Chat-boot gzip | Requests | Against the 1,294,735 B cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pinned 9d8 baseline | 1,294,874 B | 20 | **139 B over** |
| Prior 912-source candidate | 1,295,475 B | 20 | **740 B over** |
| Candidate minus baseline | **+601 B** | 0 additional | Not a waiver |

Population records are byte-identical, including generations, normalized declarations and asset names; emitted plugin asset paths/revisions/printed sizes also match. Both have the same 1,751 mapped eager module IDs. The generated plugin-distribution carrier is **3,689 raw / 807 standalone-gzip bytes on both sides**. The preserved archive contains eight manifests, eight package identities and all 21 assets; the auditor verified all 21 recorded asset hashes. Individual module gzip estimates are not additive shipped-bundle attribution.

**Interpretation:** this is a failing symmetric **local** comparison: an independently over-cap local baseline plus a **601 B candidate increment**. It is neither wholly inherited nor a 740 B candidate-only regression. **It does not prove the cloud baseline failed**, identify the exact cloud byte gap, or establish a safe code cut. No asset cap, checker, integrity guard or inventory filter was relaxed.

#### Audit qualifications and recovery evidence

- Preparation used each root's maintained builder, real builder paths, ownership helper and metadata finalizer. The auditor found no argv impersonation or fabricated lease. **Per-root preparation ownership ends before population capture and direct Vite execution**; the adapter does not establish an uninterrupted lease through measurement. The implementation owner ran the recorded preparation/build stages serially, launched no intervening source/artifact writer, and retained clean-tree/diff-identity receipts. Equal emitted inventories corroborate this particular run, not a general concurrency guarantee.
- Baseline source came from the pinned Git archive with workspace-dependency remapping. Candidate measurement used the owned working checkout; its HEAD label alone is insufficient, so clean-tree receipts and equality with reviewed/published source are retained alongside the reports.
- The optional consumed-input signature failed because `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts` is **absent in the pinned baseline** but present in candidate: **897 bytes**, SHA-256 `2bdf7a36a70c0778e7767528c84c0524922b469e0c06f815090cafafe2a77637`. This is explicitly recorded absence, **not a successful signature check or filtering of missing inputs**. Resume built the baseline normally and ran the unchanged checker; setup failures are not product verdicts.
- CSS normalization used the baseline's own authored CSS and rewrote compression sidecars, not CSS source. Original packaged generations, manifests, hashes, reports, source-tree receipts and the task-only preparation/resume adapters remain in the implementation worktree's recovery evidence. The retained audit was read-only; it did not rerun builds, tests or cloud access.

Two bounded lazy-Undo prototypes saved **152 B** and **76 B** relative to the same candidate profile; their plugin asset rows matched the control. Neither closed the gate, and their additional asynchronous/ordinary-reset coupling was not justified. **Both were restored exactly; neither was committed or published.** No further justified narrow production cut was identified. Larger boot-performance work needs explicitly agreed scope rather than speculative refactoring or a cap waiver. The unresolved performance gate and separate operator-only compatibility proof remain blockers to readiness.

### Superseded asymmetric and historical measurements

The first 9d8 pair reported candidate **1,295,475 B** versus baseline **1,294,201 B** (+1,274 B), but used **21 plugin assets/eight plugins versus seven assets/three plugins**. Settings-only preparation built a subset while the producer consumed all existing completed distributions. The extra distributions were **not shown stale or corrupt** and were not removed. Therefore the entire earlier +1,274 B must not be attributed solely to Undo; the symmetric 139/601/740 accounting above supersedes that attribution.

The [older c531 performance gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517378885) reported **1,294,739 B**, four bytes over the unchanged cap. Historical d999 before/after copy-only measurements reported **1,295,147 → 1,294,950 B** (197 B less), raw **4,152,210 → 4,151,855 B**, 20 requests unchanged, and an older 215 B local overage. Those are historical results, not cross-base comparisons, cloud-equivalent measurements or passing evidence for this head.

### Prior source repair and test-allocation rationale

- Source `142914988afb9621516ad0089f2e14c85611c8e6` moved five **unchanged** reset-confirmation strings into the already-lazy modal's English fragment. Before/after snapshots proved complete `chat.board` and `chat.sessionReset` key/value identity; explicit catalog merges preserve both namespaces. Modal props, markup, lifecycle, recovery controllers and authority checks were unchanged by that copy-only repair.
- The [test-lines failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517379831) reproduced locally: required regressions added **851 net lines**, plus two catalog-consumer lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-reset-undo.txt` therefore records exactly **853 justified net regression-test lines**, as the fix workflow permits. They cover state/Gateway/model-context fencing, retained-history/UI confirmation, real-Gateway/upgrade-fixture proof and catalog ownership. **The shared scalar and shrink rules are unchanged by this PR. Retain this rationale in the squash body.**
- On that earlier tree, 39 UI tests, full catalog/wrapper closure, types, lint, format and line gates passed. All 30 changed-catalog tests passed with one worker in **9.49 s Vitest / 10.46 s wrapper**. These are historical local costs, not current CI estimates. The copy-only delta received a complete P2 pass with zero actionable findings; other earlier reviews retain their stated scopes, not exhaustive independent reproduction.
- Both hosted P2 findings were repaired: generated locale/translation-memory changes were removed under publisher ownership, and the catalog owner preserves eager reset keys alongside lazy Undo copy. Canonical generation/keyless baseline were run, not hand translations. No generated locale/translation-memory changes are shipped by this source PR.
- Earlier pinned proof passed the three CI consumer guard suites (**234 tests**), selected catalog regression (**1 passed, 29 unselected skipped**), owner suites (**104 tests in three shards**) and UI suites (**39 tests in four files**). The interrupted earlier full catalog attempt is not green.
- The [serial-owner gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325920) and [trusted wrapper import gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325315) reproduced; repairs passed 219 full guard tests and scoped review. Later [E2E inventory assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42098710378/job/127497159725) were repaired using independently declared expected sets, preserving inventory/sharding/phase/worker-cap/parallelism assertions and both provider-removal and reset-Undo cases. No ignore, snapshot waiver or guard weakening was introduced.
- An earlier broad changed-check exited 143 at its deadline amid repository I/O waits. Subsequent checks passed selected SQLite worker/dialect, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race and mock-factory gates on their selected snapshots. Historical results do not replace current-head CI.

### Released-data upgrade proof — BLOCKED

The opt-in fixture uses genuinely installed **OpenClaw 2026.11.1** and its dependencies outside the source checkout, avoiding candidate tsconfig alias contamination. It is designed to create released settings/transcript, stop and snapshot state, replace only the executable, then verify continuity, Undo, reload, next provider request and branch switching.

**No successful upgrade run is established.** The standalone-prefix repair resolved initial source-alias setup failures. The released Gateway subsequently started and created the session, but baseline `chat.send` was explicitly refused by the agent/subagent attribution boundary. The fixture exposes stdout and stderr to make the refusal visible.

This is authority-blocked, not passing compatibility proof or demonstrated migration breakage. **No alternate CLI, WebSocket, browser or CI retry, marker stripping or guard weakening was used.** Human/operator invocation or a boundary-owner-approved attributed fixture route is still required. This separate blocker does not justify bypassing security or declaring source readiness.

### Earlier behavior evidence

Regressions reproduced automatic/tail-reset eligibility, queued/unadopted input preservation, lost model-context navigation and nested-reset fencing. title: fix: cancel Telegram initialization during gateway shutdown
body:
Refs #193429

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram polling can hold gateway shutdown while bot initialization retries during a Telegram API outage.

## User Impact

The candidate forwards account shutdown cancellation into pending Telegram initialization, including grammY retry delays. Gateway restart/update shutdown shares this lifecycle, but an updater transaction has not been reproduced. Required CI is green; native shutdown and base-RED qualification remain explicit gaps for parent review before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The polling session already owns the account abort signal and awaits initialization before starting ingress. Forward that signal to `bot.init`, preserving initialization ordering and the existing error/retry/transport-cleanup owners. HTTP cancellation alone does not cancel grammY's retry sleep; the pinned [grammY implementation](https://github.com/grammyjs/grammy/blob/055a5a440f04d0b9fd5fd75a6d14dac4c2b83553/src/bot.ts#L306) accepts the signal for requests and retry delays.

The signature-derived assertion matches webhook startup. grammY1.46.0's Node declaration imports a legacy `abort-controller` signal type whose `dispatchEvent` signature differs from Node's; its initialization/API/retry code only reads `aborted` and uses abort event listeners. The direct typed call failed TS2345 with that pinned declaration. A precise adjacent `// SAFETY:` comment documents this compatibility; the final correction changes no runtime behavior or baseline policy.

Thanks to SoulSupremeNo1 for the report and proposed repair. No reporter patch/PR was linked when ownership was checked, so no reporter patch was reused. The issue's 2026.10.10 container timings remain attributed reporter evidence, not current-main proof.

## Evidence

- [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42027771342) completed **success** for head `ae84e9d471d27b733e3a643294d46038fd112640`; required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries report SUCCESS. The [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42027771342/job/127247027384), including assertion-safety, pass. No override or retry-for-green was used.
- [Hosted Telegram execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42027771342/job/127247028083): named real-grammY initialization retry-cancellation regression **PASS 5 ms**; polling **31/31** in **9.65 s**; monitor **10/10** in **4.22 s**. Includes initialized/error, restart/stop, transport cleanup, account isolation and token-release contracts. The job ran204s including setup/build.
- CI tested PR merge `555a55b616d175887e5ccdebb5254fe24823fac8`, whose parent is the exact candidate. Polling owner/regression and monitor test blobs match the candidate. This is hosted Linux execution evidence, **not base RED or native Gateway shutdown proof**.
- Fresh shared full-branch P0–P3 source review of `ec2e9b6328d21d39d7efb4022f529bee3a444706..ae84e9d471d27b733e3a643294d46038fd112640`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Host checks were limited to `node --check` syntax parsing and `git diff --check`; no local test/lint/build/install/package wrappers or product commands ran.
- Both authorized Testbox requests ([original](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42021123071), [resume](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42025140900)) returned queued and were stopped without a test payload. Native and Actions settlement were verified. No further Testbox attempt was made for the final correction.
- **Missing proof:** base `ec2e9b63` RED; native installed isolated current-main/candidate offline Telegram+warm-health shutdown timing/exit/transport-settlement comparison; macOS shutdown qualification; authenticated Telegram and updater-transaction reproduction. Do not claim the regression fixed solely from these candidate tests or old-release reporter timings.

Production change remains signal forwarding plus its invariant comment. The regression's unique60-line allocation covers the distinct initialization-backoff cancellation/cleanup boundary; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

title: fix(update): avoid repair self-fencing through custody aliases
body:
Refs #193401

## What Problem This Solves

Standalone update repair can refuse its own executor when current and legacy custody paths use different ancestor aliases for the same SQLite store.

## User Impact

Repair can acquire one executor lease for that shared store while continuing to refuse unrelated live owners, unsafe database leaves, and changed identities. The CLI running repair must contain this fix. The reporter's exact macOS topology remains unknown; this conditional regression does not establish their installation-specific root cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

Legacy discovery excluded only identical path strings, but database admission canonicalized ancestor aliases. The legacy fence then held the same installation key that the current executor tried to acquire with another owner.

Retain the current store's physical identity before awaited legacy discovery, deduplicate only a matching prepared parent/leaf path after validating that pin, and keep normal current-store acquisition authoritative. Fresh identity capture uses the prepared owner's path; earned receipts remain exact. Distinct stores keep legacy fences, and a busy legacy store leaves a missing current database uncreated.

## Evidence

- RED on `887a8a1108ea682fda92a63ebf16a2bd15b7a5b7`: both real standalone symlink-ancestor cases failed with `Another update executor owns this installation.` The existing legacy-parent control passed. A separate refusal regression caught eager creation of an absent current database before the final correction.
- GREEN on Linux Testbox: all six requested named files, 86 tests passed and one macOS-only test skipped. Same-spelling/distinct-store controls, live-owner byte/absence preservation, cancellation, exact release, lineage, and hardlink/replacement refusal remain covered.
- Built and checked a self-contained runtime package, installed it, and ran `update repair --yes --json` with isolated home/state and a symlinked temp ancestor. Exit 0, `coreUpdate: completed`, zero remaining custody rows or lock files. Overall status was `warning` for deliberately disabled plugins and deferred agent-path repair in the empty fixture.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and test-line ratchet passed. The dedicated 116-line regression allocation covers real executor admission and refusal preservation; the shared baseline is unchanged. The changed test file took 32.56 seconds including compiler preparation; its test bodies are subsecond. PR CI timing is pending.
- Shared autoreview (Codex), full candidate against the pinned base, P0–P3: scoped-clean after addressing the fresh-path spelling finding. The final review also includes the missing-current-file correction. No outstanding findings.

Refs #193157. This addresses misleading admission diagnostics; the reporter-specific macOS refusal remains unconfirmed, so this PR does not establish closure of the full report.

## Work sessions

## What Problem This Solves

title: fix(agents): preserve bounded operator authority across restart continuations
body:
## Summary

Preserve bounded operator authority through principal ingress, Gateway restart recovery, and scheduled continuations without treating a system turn as a new human owner input.

## Problem and solution

A live principal can lack handshake auth policy. Original recovery custody was then lost across restart, and protected calls or the first scheduled continuation could be denied despite the original authorization.

- Add an optional ingress-owner recovery hook and a principal recovery source. The MCP relay resolves the original audience and a canonical, persistent issuance UUID—not a timestamp or fabricated handshake.
- Normalize legacy grant rows once at the owning startup boundary. Preserve the UUID across restart; mint a different UUID for replacement consent even when its ID and millisecond timestamp are reused.
- Await recovery registration in the registered service startup, before startup recovery proceeds; do not wait for the external relay connection.
- Preserve recorded custody only for actual restart admission. Intersect original/current scope and model restrictions, checking original consent/access and current principal authority before effects.
- Share the complete existing person-ingress eligibility policy between live binding/RPC admission and restored authority: current effective trusted-proxy mode, configured roles, verified Cloudflare email/JWT headers, and canonical-email allowlist membership. Revalidate at restoration and protected effects, including transport-owned startup overrides; preserve HTTP/token/nonperson behavior and exact matching.
- Retry transient pre-execution restoration failures on the same one-shot. Do not replay started work or upgrade existing source-less jobs.
- Project verified admin eligibility only into supported control-plane admission. Preserve sender attribution, taint, policy, live checks, independently scoped session/portal/automation grants, and explicit-owner standing intents. Device/delegation ownership is not broadened.
- Declare create-time warnings in both closed RPC result variants and carry them through both UI consumers using existing notice/toast channels.

## Validation

- Exact immutable **0bfc2c7** real-model native SIGTERM/cold-start flow passed: original USER automatically resumed without new human ingress or manual marker writes; protected reads **1 original / 1 resumed / 1 FIRST recurring A**.
- The **same A** was denied on its next tick after revoking the exact original issuance UUID: **zero protected attempts/reads, agent starts or model stages after revocation**. The UUID survived cold restart. Both runner phases exited 0.
- Cleanup: **64,030 original source files unchanged; 1,038 writable files scanned, zero provider-key matches; all owned processes/services stopped**.
- MCP suite **179/179**, plus **6 focused issuance/migration/startup regressions**; extension production/test types and focused lint passed.
- Retained-owner and prompt-prefix **26/26**; core production and affected test types and focused lint passed. Unchanged hook owning suite **6/6** passed.
- Protocol strict validators **88/88**; cron UI mutations **38/38**; CI automation helper **14/14**; UI types and type-aware lint passed. Relevant regressions are red on prior producers/consumers and green with repairs; the baseline tree was restored exactly.
- Current **92b567b** person-policy proof: **34/34** continuation cases, **77/77** auth/live-ingress unit siblings, and **2/2** genuine person/principal integration siblings passed; production/test types and focused type-aware lint passed. Allowlist removal and person-mode disablement, both before cold restoration and after restoration/before effects, refuse with zero protected I/O. Deterministic prior-head replays exposed three protected reads in each negative case; transitions and live refusals are awaited. Original read/write fixture roles and source-less denial assertions are preserved.
- Actual latest-stable **2026.11.1 → D633** canonical Doctor **schema 27 → 40**, Gateway/device admission, protected read, session resolution and genuine legacy recovery passed. Automatic cross-version in-flight model resumption is **not** claimed: stable startup terminalized that pending claim.
- The first final-flow bootstrap attempt failed at the pre-scenario request-runtime/state-worker barrier, before MCP services. It is preserved as a failure, not counted as a pass. One unchanged-source/config/timeout/guard, same-state bootstrap retry completed the flow; no USER replay or production authority fix was used.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable findings. Official local committed-range review **0bfc2c7..92b567b** completed. Its earlier medium person-mode finding was reproduced and fixed. The remaining low spelling advisory is rejected because the old live person guard already exact-matched canonical profile emails against the allowlist; HTTP/header handshakes use a different source ingress and are unchanged. Earlier timestamp-compatibility and live-hook assertions were refuted by exact released sources, unchanged owning tests and producer paths.

### Regression cost

Normal allocation **1208 = 1008 + 108 + 92** exactly matches counted net regression growth; the scalar baseline is unchanged. The older unmodified integrated baseline already has **49** lines of over-ceiling debt, which this PR does not credit or hide. MCP full-suite wall time: **45.088s**; affected-file examples: matrix **3.961s**, issuance **9.511s**, service **2.042s**. Final person-policy continuation Vitest time: **225.81s**, mostly transformation; isolated auth file: **55 tests, 0.75s Vitest**. Current-head CI supplies broad proof; inherited-failure disposition requires actual evidence through the supported native route.

## Before / after UI proof

title: feat(notion): add shared memory and Skills integration
body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users need a supported connection to Notion’s announced shared-memory and native Skills workflow, without building a second memory backend or treating remote setup instructions as permission to import their data.

Context: [requested integration](https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2118138957229891670). The announcement’s short link resolves to its video; implementation requirements come from the [official setup guide](https://developers.notion.com/prompts/setup) (reviewed version 0.0.6, October 30, 2026), [MCP connection documentation](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp), and [technical memory/Skills reference](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/tools-skills-agents-reference).

## User Impact

Adds a disabled-by-default Notion plugin contributing the official hosted OAuth MCP connection and a `notion-shared-brain` workflow skill. Users explicitly enable it, sign in, and approve their import sources and destinations. No live installation, production configuration change, automatic import, remote Skill installation, or scheduled synchronization is performed.

The guide explains provenance, corrections and forget requests, native Skill package preservation, and remote-content/prompt-injection boundaries. Notion-managed memory is private to the connected user; the default OpenClaw MCP credential is shared with callers allowed to invoke it on that Gateway. This is not automatic multi-user identity isolation or a guarantee of permanent/cross-agent erasure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing owners: Notion owns remote memory and native Skills; OpenClaw owns MCP OAuth, discovery, transport, tool policy, and cleanup. The plugin has no custom client, credential store, memory database, hooks, or background service, and does not replace OpenClaw’s selected memory plugin. Explicit operator MCP overrides and disables retain precedence.

## Evidence

- **4 new production-boundary tests passed:** actual bundled manifest discovery, hosted OAuth configuration and attribution, real published workflow Skill, disabled-by-default/explicitly-disabled behavior, and operator replacement/disable precedence without duplicate connections. No owner-loader mocks.

- Scoped entrypoint and integration-test typechecks passed using the repository compiler runner and independently owned frozen-lockfile dependencies. Focused lint/format checks and `git diff --check` passed.

The isolated source-CLI smoke attempt was blocked by the managed host’s runtime-artifact publication guard/host-environment permission check; the guard was not bypassed and the live Gateway was not changed or restarted. The docs include an explicit account-authorized verification checklist. PR CI remains the broad integration gate.

title: chore(worktrees): distinguish provisioning copy waits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed worktree provisioning combines worker delivery, authority assertions, and filesystem copy waits in one interval, preventing useful attribution of a slow preparation.

Related: #191873, #192548, #193056. Adjacent fs-safe work remains owned by openclaw/fs-safe#1055; this PR does not duplicate it or change the dependency.

## User Impact

Diagnostics only: file selection, copy strategy, concurrency, timeouts, authority checks, cancellation and errors retain their existing behavior. This is not a latency fix or a claim about the cause of a reported stall.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing private terminal worker receipt with fixed numeric aggregates, projected into the existing preparation log/event: host roundtrip, worker elapsed, root/eligibility preflight, authority wait, inclusive `Root.copyIn` await, an explicitly approximate roundtrip residual, attempted/accepted file counts and logical source sizes.

Copy awaits include Root admission, native queueing, filesystem work and nested authority assertions; they are not native copy time and overlap authority wait. Existing lstats supply logical sizes without extra IO. Failed receipts retain partial timings; cancellation or worker loss without a delivered receipt retains only host roundtrip. No paths, contents, per-file events, config, public API or new log family.

## Evidence

- Current head: `3a2f5a9f22ca9d05c4d491db6deaff93430dc349`. [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41963169836) completed **SUCCESS: 33 successful / 29 skipped / zero failed jobs**. Both reported required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries are **SUCCESS**; the full check list has no failures or pending items. No gate waiver or unchanged-check rerun.

[Earlier direct-head proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41948540409) at `7659c9d8c` covers those owner cases under Node and Bun plus build-artifacts. Production files are unchanged by the final test-only repair.

The final commit preserves real singleton exports while retaining the existing fixture override; all four formerly failing host outcomes now pass. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview is **scoped-clean**, no findings. Normal hooks passed without bypass/bootstrap. Net PR test LF growth is **0**, with no assertions or cases removed.
- **Base-red verified under Node and Bun:** [baseline job 127000792450](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41952674246/job/127000792450) checks out `c0d0d4d550d88f9cdf4b631b55e863293d984cb3`, exactly the merge base plus the same service regression test. `service.provisioned.test.ts:184` fails on absent `copy.workerMs`, `copy.authorityWaitMs`, and `copy.sourceBytes: 41`; returned outcome and existing preparation phases match. title: improve(gateway): split current-session revalidation timings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Multi-second `chat.send` current-session revalidation timings do not distinguish source preparation, ordered admission, pre-read checks, and the history reader response. This is a maintainer-requested diagnostics enhancement; no latency cause or performance fix is claimed.

## User Impact

Existing chat-send timing details gain four request-local measurements under `detail.admission.current_session`: `source_prepare`, `ordered_admission`, `read_barrier`, and `history_reader`. No configuration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing async-local observer and phase helper at the ordered-reader owner. Keep admission observations separate from persistence observations. Admission, FIFO ordering, cache decisions, authority checks, errors, and dispatch behavior are unchanged.

`read_barrier` measures admitted host source checks and cache lookup before the reader call. `history_reader` measures the reader call through its response, including downstream database/pool/RPC waits; it is omitted on a retained-fact hit. These are elapsed host spans, not native SQL execution measurements or an exhaustive additive partition of revalidation. Only fixed phase labels and durations are added.

## Evidence

- Exact base `84097d630e263848e57a3aa98d47f789606a970d`: the final held-writer regression fails all four table cases at the missing timing-detail assertion (exit 1). Candidate: all 13 admission tests pass, including the existing lifecycle and revoked-caller assertions. The injected clock assigns 1000ms to ordered admission and 0ms to the other three spans; an empty-root leaf expectation requires the real history reader.
- Blacksmith Testbox focused proof: `chat-send-admission.reads.test.ts` (13 tests, 14.51s; wrapper 48.62s including worker preparation), `session-entry-read-ordered.test.ts` (20 tests, 18.45s), and `chat-send-diagnostics.test.ts` (11 tests, 2.11s). No production state or private transcript was read. No live model or production latency reproduction is claimed.
- Touched-file lint with `--type-check`, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Production net +25 lines; tests net -1 line. No test-budget or baseline exceptions. Broad proof and CI seconds belong to exact-head PR CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final local snapshot against the exact base, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no accepted actionable findings. Review used the frozen diff, owner source, and reported proof; the reviewer did not rerun tests.

Awaiting lead review; do not merge as part of this lane.

title: fix(plugins): preserve environment references when updates migrate settings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins update` replacing an authored environment reference with its resolved value when a replacement plugin moves the setting and core migration changes the plugin allowlist.

## User Impact

Moved settings retain references such as `${LISTENER_HOST}` in root config and single-owner `$include` files. Existing plugin config and installed-index records remain readable and updateable. Previously flattened literals stay literals because their original reference cannot safely be reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement plugin's selected manifest registry and IDs now accompany both authored/resolved replay views. Replay therefore uses the same candidate migration that moved the setting, even while the old package generation is still the persisted owner. Existing fingerprint checks, deferred-owner selection, backups, guarded publication, completion, and rollback remain in force. There is no new config option, schema, or cache.

The compatibility assertion now checks exact invocation count and selected config/plugin IDs without depending on absent optional fields. The existing include scenario exercises the moved reference too. Current main was merged without rebasing; its #193097 repair also resolves the original unrelated `check-lint-core-2` Promise-executor errors.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `7075e19cff8e3b02264dce5f3c14dbcec3c61caf` reproduces the exact raw-file `${LISTENER_HOST}` → `127.0.0.1` failure at the production update-command boundary on Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun. Package acquisition and Gateway transport are fixtures in this regression; persistence and migration are real. The affected owners/test are unchanged between that main and merged base `3816bcb3dea1879d055853fc070af78bc7737ab0`.
- **After:** all 46 tests pass on both runtimes across `plugins-update-command.migrations.integration.test.ts`, `channel-legacy-config-migrate.test.ts`, and `config-flow-steps.references.test.ts`, covering the original regression, include ownership, selected/non-channel owners, replacement installs, disabled/pending migrations, completion, and rollback. Node migration-file Vitest duration: 410.34s; two smaller files: 32.27s; total wrapper wall 575.64s. Bun: 226.80s and 29.50s; total wrapper wall 425.26s. The existing SQLite/publication matrix dominates runtime; no new cases were added.
- **Stored-data / real CLI:** a local synthetic npm registry supplied plugin 1.0.0 and 2.0.0. The built `plugins install`, `config validate`, `plugins update`, and `config get` commands loaded old `oldPort`/`oldHost` settings, migrated them, and returned `127.0.0.1` while raw root/include files retained `${LISTENER_HOST}`. Both the ordinary update/retry control (75.16s) and unmarked nonempty allowlist cases (54.58s) passed, preserving the include pointer, unrelated label, and authored policy. Restoring the synthetic state copy emitted a conservative source-snapshot cleanup warning; update/validation succeeded and no deletion bypass was used.
- **Live model:** the built `openclaw infer model run --local --model ollama/qwen2.5:7b` command loaded the updated included config and returned `listener-update-ok` via the shared local Ollama server (18.80s). This is direct CLI/provider proof, not a Gateway/agent-turn claim.
- **Review:** Codex branch autoreview against the pinned merged base, P0–P2, is scoped-clean on `9fcb3e85c450c0984f26b4b8c2ea04a4de3df272`.
- **Ratchets:** `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 3816bcb3dea1879d055853fc070af78bc7737ab0` and separate line-cap pass. Scoped format/lint, core types, Doctor and CLI test types, and `pnpm build` pass. The build took 931.31s on macOS, including full package declarations and UI assets; lint/type wall times include waiting for its artifact lock.
- **CI:** [run 41974756984](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41974756984) succeeded on exact head `9fcb3e85c450c0984f26b4b8c2ea04a4de3df272`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. No CI reruns or additional pushes were needed.
- **Size:** production +35/-5 (net +30), tests +6/-7 (net -1), docs +14. The production growth is the typed candidate selection forwarded through existing owners. No baseline/ceiling, allocation, dependency, or changelog changes.

Update behavior: the candidate plugin-update command needs the fix; older installed updaters need no new marker or protocol. Existing state is input to the same repair/publication owners; unresolved data migrations retain their inputs and existing Doctor guidance.
